Heading: PUTA chief steps down, says he was ‘pained by rumours’ - Indian Express
Content:
Industrialists who were thinking of getting their industrial plots converted to commercial ones have just four days left to file applications. The Chandigarh Administration may not extend the conversion policy any further beyond September 18. The earlier extension of six months, for the conversion of industrial plots to commercial plots, ends on Thursday.

Highly placed sources in the UT Administration said senior officials, in a recent meeting, decided not to grant any further extension to the conversion policy (Conversion of Land Use of Industrial Sites into Commercial Activity/Services in Industrial Area Phase-I and II, Chandigarh), as it may lead to "serious infrastructure deficiency" in the area.

"As such, the infrastructure in Industrial Area is not adequate to meet the needs of the ongoing commercial projects. If more industrial plots get converted to commercial ones, it would lead to serious infrastructure-related problems," said an official.

More than 47 industrial plots have already been converted to commercial complexes. While many shopping malls and multi-storey office complexes are under construction, a mall-cum-multiplex — Centra Mall — has already started functioning. With the area already coping with the lack of parking space, one of the major roadblocks in its development, and narrow roads, any more commercial project is going to choke it further.

As of Sunday, there are around 50 applications pending with the UT Administration, in which industrialists have expressed their willingness to get their industrial plots converted into commercial. "By paying the conversion fee, the industrialists can use their properties in a better manner and also enhance the value of the plot," said another senior official.

UT Home-cum-Finance Secretary Sanjay Kumar said: "I have called a meeting with the industries associations on September 15 where we will discuss these issues. There is no doubt that more commercial activities will increase pressure on the infrastructure and our effort will be to consolidate and provide for sufficient infrastructure. After the meeting, the Administration will firm up its view on a further extension. Any decision will be to strengthen partnership between the Administration and the industrialists for betterment and consolidation of adequate infrastructure."

The Administration had launched the conversion scheme in 2005, with a motive to spruce up the Industrial Area and develop it into a commercial hub. The plots measuring two kanals or above were made eligible for the change of land use from industrial to commercial on payment of certain charges. The industrialists, however, had been raising several issues from time to time for and against the clauses in the conversion policy.

Three years of conversion policy
2005:UT Administration formulated the policy for industrialists, giving them an option to convert industrial plots to commercial by paying a certain conversion fee.

September 18, 2007:A joint forum of the Industrialists' Association of Chandigarh, Federation of Small Scale Industries and Chamber of Chandigarh Industries made a representation to the UT Administration, seeking extension of the conversion policy for two more years. They got an extension of six months, till March 18, 2008.

February 1, 2008:Policy amended by doing away with the 15-year-old restriction on the sale and transfer of property. Though the Estate Office had objected to such an amendment, the finance department went ahead with the decision.

June 26:The UT Administrator assured to review the decision on allowing change of land use of plots measuring less than 2 kanals.

September 8:Another amendment made to the policy, according to which two or more adjoining industrial plots allotted under less than two kanals category could also be considered for conversion if after the amalgamation of these plots, with the permission of the competent authority, the measurement added up to 2 kanals or more.

Heading: Tigress found dead in Chhatbir zoo - Indian Express
Content:
Dr Ronki Ram, president of the Panjab University Teachers' Association, resigned from his post on Sunday. While PUTA members expressed shock over his step, Dr Ram said he was pained by the rumours that he had weakened the university's fight for a central status.

He announced the decision of his stepping down in a press statement, which irked most members of the association. "He (Dr Ram) should have maintained the dignity of office and acted sensibly. If he had such designs on his mind, he should have taken us into confidence. He has insulted both the association and its members," said a PUTA member, requesting anonymity.

For the last few days, many in the university had been targeting Dr Ram for "diluting" the radical stance of PUTA's struggle for a central university status.

Sources said he had deliberately changed his stand from a central university to a centrally-funded university. "It seems he has his own interest. Instead of leading the way for the team that has elected him its leader, he had come up with a solution which was completely his. Now that he has sensed the resentment brewing among the members, he put in his papers," said another PUTA member.

Ever since his election to the post of PUTA president, Dr Ram has courted one controversy or the other. It was alleged that he had divided the association into two groups. It was also felt that Dr Ram's decision to make PU a centrally-funded university did not have the support of other members.

Talking to Newsline, Dr Ram said he was unhappy with the rumours doing the round. "I am very much hurt. Instead of showing faith in me, my fellow members have formed a notion that I am acting in my interest. I have decided to step down."

Defending him, Professor Ashwani Kaul said Dr Ram was an honest leader and that his decision was right. "Anyone whose integrity is doubted will react in the same manner. Though I am shocked by his decision, I am not sure whether his resignation will be accepted. He has led the campaign for the central status and we will like him to continue with it. A decision on the matter will be taken in a meeting on Tuesday."

Heading: 6 months on, activity-based learning still on the anvil - Indian Express
Content:
A Royal Bengal tigress was found dead under mysterious circumstances at the Chhatbir Zoological Park on Sunday evening. Zoo sources said fighting with another inmate in the enclosure cost Shanti her life.

The role of the management has come under the scanner as it had reportedly deployed a few beldaars (daily-wagers) on duty at the tiger enclosure in place of regular zoo keepers.

The seven-year-old reportedly had a severe fight with another tiger around 3 pm. According to the sources, the two big cats got irritated while they were being captivated in their respective dens by a beldaar.

The unskilled worker was performing the job of a trained zoo keeper, due to which he could not control them, said a source. Shanti was a healthy tigress and had delivered four cubs twice.

The carcass of the Schedule I animal will undergo an autopsy on Monday. Not even a single official of the zoo, besides veterinary doctors, allegedly turned up at the spot. While Chief Wildlife Warden M P Rai said the matter had not been reported to him by any zoo official, field director Dharmendra Sharma could not be contacted for comments as his cell phone remained switched off.

Heading: Chandigarh to lock horns with Ludhiana in final - Indian Express
Content:
Here is another much-hyped proposal mooted by the UT Education department that has acquired the 'pending' status. More than half the session has passed, but the concept of activity-based learning proposed for Classes I and II in all government schools is yet to see the light of day.

Inspired by the concept running in around 38,000 schools in Tamil Nadu, it was said to be implemented in the UT from April this year. The system is still in the process of development at the State Institute of Education, Sector 32.

Activity-based learning promises to do away with school bags, by using practical study material, and examinations.

Even after visiting the schools in the Tamil Nadu capital where this concept is being used successfully and detailed discussions thereof, the work seems to be moving at a snail's pace. A 12-member team comprising teachers, technicians and experts went to Chennai on a 10-day trip in March this year. The visit was followed by discussion sessions and seminars to prepare the study material. The authorities admitted to the delay and said they were not sure when the system would be implemented.

"The computer designing and animation of the study material is taking time. Also, only two technical experts are working on one subject, which is making the process slow. Nothing can be said when the study material will be ready," says Surinder Singh Dahiya, Director, State Institute of Education.

The enthusiasm among the teachers when the proposal was mooted, too, seems to be dying due to the delay. "It has been months now since we have been hearing of activity-based learning for Class I and II. We have lost hope that the concept will be implemented in this session, as declared by the education department earlier this year," says the principal of a government school.

Proposals yet to see light of day
* Free computer education for all students of government schools from Class I to X
* Dress code for schoolteachers
* Accommodation for principals on the school premises
* Appointment of vice-principals
* No junk food in school canteens
* Use of playgrounds after school hours
* 'Read Chandigarh' concept to inculcate the habit of reading
* Laptop for principals
* Submission of fee and funds at e-sampark centres
* Director Public Instruction (Schools) S K Setia's taking over each school as principal on weekends, undertaking all duties, including cleaning of toilets

Heading: Ganguly likely to feature in JP Atray tourney - Indian Express
Content:
A Chandigarh batsman plays a shot during the Katoch Shield semifinal encounter against Ludhiana at Sector 16 Stadium in Chandigarh on Sunday. (Right) Chandigarh all-rounder Gaurav Gambhir has scored a total of 185 runs and scalped 12 wickets in the tournament. Newsline photos

Chandigarh will take on Ludhiana in the finals of Katoch Shield Championship after they were declared winner on the basis of first innings lead of 37 runs at Sector 16 Cricket Stadium on Sunday. Chandigarh which could not even make it to the semis last year must be hoping for the best this time around.

Chandigarh resumed from their overnight score of 260 for 6 and they added 149 more runs to finish at 409 runs in 166.2 overs due to the ninth wicket partnership of 106 runs between Gurinder Singh and Anupam Gambhir. Gurinder dominated the Mohali bowlers and made a pugnacious 81 runs with the help of 11 hits to the boundary. Gurinder also hit a well made half century with the help of five boundaries to set a target of 447 runs in 30 overs for Mohali. Varun Khanna was the most successful bowler for Mohali as he spun a web around the Chandigarh batsmen and his resilience was soon awarded as he returned back with a rich haul of six wickets from 68.2 overs that included 20 maiden overs. Mohali's run chase started on a disastrous note as they kept losing quick wickets to be left tottering at 72 for 5 in 21 overs. Sumit Ohri stood firm with a fighting knock of 25 runs. The match was, however, called off with no possibility of an outright result. Naresh Gogian claimed three wickets while Gaurav Gambhir bagged two wickets for Chandigarh.

Meanwhile, in the second match, defending champion Amritsar were humbled by Ludhiana by two wickets. Karan Goel and Ankur Kakkar emerged as the stars for Ludhiana as the duo was involved in 97 runs partnership for the fifth wicket. Karan Goel's well made 72 runs off 96 balls included seven boundaries and three towering sixes. Ankur Kakkar also played a captain's knock of 46 runs. For Amritsar, Sumit Sharma emerged as the most successful bowler with four wickets.

The final match between Chandigarh and Ludhiana will be played from September 16 to 19 at PCA Stadium, Mohali.

Brief Scores:
Chandigarh:409 for all in 166.2 overs (Gaurav Gambhir 121, Viswas Bhalla 97, Gurinder Singh 81, Anupam Gambhir 50, Varun Khanna 6 for 127);

Mohali (second innings): 72 for 5 in 21 overs (Sumit Ohri 25 no, Naresh Gogian 3 for 26, Gaurav Gambhir 3 for 25) beat

Ludhiana (second innings): 233 for 8 in 71.2 overs (Karan Goel 72, Ankur Kakkar 46, Gaurav Marwaha 29, Sumit Sharma 4 for 58).

Heading: Zirakpur all set to get one of region’s largest malls this Diwali - Indian Express
Content:
Old rivals Ganguly and Chappel might be seen together during the tournament

Top cricketers like former Indian skipper Sourav Ganguly, Yuvraj Singh, S Sreesanth, Virender Sehwag and Harbhajan Singh will be seen in action during the15th edition of All India J. P. Atray tournament, which will get underway from September 17 at the PCA Stadium, Mohali, Sector 16 Stadium, Chandigarh, DAV School, Sector 8, Chandigarh and St. John's School, Sector-26 and Cricket Stadium, Barwala. The tournament is the curtain raiser before start of the domestic season and is recognized by the Board of Control for Cricket in India.

According to Sushil Kapoor, organising secretary of the tournament, said that 17 top teams would compete in the tournament which will be played on league-cum- knock out basis. All matches will be of 50 overs each side and will be played under the ICC rules of one-day cricket. The teams will be divided into four pools and top team from each pool will qualify for the semi-finals.

The likely participating teams are last year's winners MRF, Chennai, runners-up St. Bank of Mysore-Bangalore, Punjab Cricket Club, BPCL, Mumbai, St. Bank of Hyderabad, HPCA Academy, ONGC-Delhi, Assam CA, Indian Oil Corp.-Mumbai, Moody ICL, MPCA XI, CM XI-Haryana, LIC Cricket Club, PCA Colts, RCA XI and India Cements Ltd,- Chennai.

The winners will get a purse of Rs.1.50 lakh, runners-up Rs.60,000, the third position Rs.30,000 and fourth position Rs.15,000. Arrangements have been finalised with Doordarshan, New Delhi for live telecast of the day/night final match 2.30 pm onwards which will be played at PCA Stadium, Mohali, on September 30.

Top drawer Indian players namely Niraj Patel, Sidharth Trivedi, Irfan Pathan, Suresh Raina, Naman Ojha, Md. Kaif, Rajat Bhatia, Hrisikesh Kanitkar for Air India, Wasim Jafar, Rohit Sharma, Chateswar Pujara, Rajesh Pawar, Ravikant Shukla, Pinal Shah for Indian Oil, Sreeshant for BPCL, Praveen Kumar, Virender Sehwag, Gautam Gambhir, Munaf Patel for ONGC, Daniel Manohar for State Bank of Hyderabad, Yuvraj Singh, Harbhajan Singh, M. Heading: Kharar MC polls: SAD-BJP combine makes a clean sweep - Indian Express
Content:
Offering a whole new experience in commercial and retail space to not only the residents of the tricity but also to those travelling from other states, the Paras Down Town Square in Zirakpur is all set to launch its operations by Diwali this year.

One of the largest malls in Punjab with the build up area of 3.5 lakh square feet, the much-awaited mall, being developed by Paras Buildtech Private Limited, has been fully constructed. The interiors have been done and the brand stores have placed their properties.

Located on the intersection of Delhi-Chandigarh-Shimla Highway, this will also prove a stopover point for commuters travelling on this highway. With a four-screen multiplex, Big Bazaar, Pantaloon anchor store, a food court and children entertainment centre spread over an area of more than 23,000 square feet, restaurants and business hotel with spa, gymnasium and a coffee shop, the mall will provide various services under one roof.

Rajinder Singh Takhar, Chief Operating Officer, Paras Build-Call said, "We had anticipated the demand of such a commercial and retail space a few years ago. "

The major brands already taken up space in the mall include Nike, Woodland, Provogue Jumbo Electronics, Madura Garments, Liberty and Reid and Taylor. The sprawling atrium forms the centre place of the mall. The parking aspect has been kept in mind with two-level basement parking.

Heading: For this coach, ‘spending time with my daughter is the most relaxing activity’ - Indian Express
Content:
The ruling Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) — Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) combine swept the Kharar Municipal Council (MC) elections, winning 10 out of the total 15 seats, on Sunday.

The opposition Congress, meanwhile, suffered a crushing defeat, losing 13 seats. Three seats went to Independent candidates. The win of the SAD-BJP that contested the Kharar MC elections jointly for the first time was just one seat short of a two-third majority.

The Congress had contested the MC polls on its party symbol, while the SAD-BJP had opted for the "Rising Sun" as their election symbol.

Charanjit Singh, Independent MLA from Chamkaur Sahib and MC president, had also supported the SAD-BJP combine.

The counting of the votes began just as soon as the polling ended, and the results were declared within half an hour. The official declaration of the results, however, was made by the Returning Officer at 9 pm.

The supporters of the victorious candidates, upon knowing the results, broke into jubilant celebrations, dancing on the beats of dhols and brass bands.

The first result was declared from Ward No. 15, where the SAD-BJP combine's Jai Bhagwan Singla defeated his rival Ratish Aggarwal of the Congress.

Capt Kanwaljit: Clear verdict against Cong
Expressing gratitude to the voters for the SAD-BJP win, Punjab Cooperation Minister and SAD general secretary Captain Kanwaljit Singh termed it a "clear verdict against Congress and its opportunist and misleading policies". He asked Balbir Sidhu, Congress MLA, Kharar, to resign. Captain Kanwaljit said the win had ushered in a new era of development and prosperity for Kharar.

Sidhu: Captain Kanwaljit should resign first
Responding to Captain Kanwaljit Singh's statement, Balbir Sidhu, Congress MLA, Kharar, said he would resign, only if Captain Kanwaljit and his son Jasjit Singh Bunny resigned first, owning responsibility for their party's defeat in the Zirakpur civic elections. Sidhu, however, said that wrong ticket allotments and alleged irregularities in the voters' lists had led to the defeat. He further accused the ruling alliance of resorting to 'unfair' means.

Heading: CN & Heard - Indian Express
Content:
Endurance, stamina and time-management are the virtues that Dr Gurmeet Singh follows. "I hit the ground at 5:30 everyday," says this sports coach, senior lecturer at the Department of Physical Education, Panjab University, and warden of Hostel Number 6, as he divides the group of 90 students into two for exercise. Lessons for the first group, comprising boys, starts between 5:30 am and 6:15 am. That done, it is the time to coach the girls.

"They practice a different regime every day. From weight training, running and yoga, they are made to do it all," says Gurmeet as he finishes off the session with 10 minutes of meditation. "Yoga, so that the students are ready to face the day with confidence," Dr Gurmeet reasons, as he leaves us to get ready.

Starting 9 am, it is time for a theory session on Biomechanics, which ends at 12:30 pm. Following this, he adorns the role of a warden from 1pm. Visiting the hostel, listening to the grievances by hostellers and checking the mess, he takes a short break and at 4pm, it is time to take charge as a coach. "From 4 pm to 5 pm in the evening, I hold sessions depending on the kind of sport the students are going to participate in. For the last four months I was busy coaching two international hockey players, Rajpal and Deepak," he says, while greeting the students of MPEd and BPEd for practical classes.

However busy the day might be, he manages two hours, between 6 pm and 8 pm for himself. "From playing badminton, football and volleyball to swimming, I do it all," he tells us.

Referring to the activity that keeps him relaxed, he says: "Spending time with my daughter Reet, relaxes me most."

It's only after 9:15 pm that Dr Gurmeet heads back to Hostel No 6 to check the rooms and the mess again.

Back at home, its time to get in touch with the world, and this he does by checking his mail.

"Whether it is replying to friends or preparing lectures for the next day, I make plans for the next day before going to bed," he says, while making the exercising schedule for the next day.

Heading: Telecom company to cough up Rs 2,000 - Indian Express
Content:
Street smart
No matter how irrelevant, the Enforcement Wing of the Municipal Corporation during its encroachment drives tends to pick up an assortment of stuff. From watercoolers to torn posters and utensils, the list is endless. Recently, the staff picked up three plastic chairs from outside a shop in the motor market. The roadside vendors, have meanwhile become smarter as they have started keeping torn posters or clothes outside for easy disposal. To prove their obedience, these vendors waste no second in handing over these cast offs to the MC staff. A penny saved is a penny earned !

For a noble cause
Extending help to the victims of the Bihar flood that devastated the state recently, Subhash Chander, Chairman of the Adhoc Front of the PGI Employees' Unions has donated his one week's salary (Rs 5,100) for the PM's relief fund. Lets hope some more Subhash Chanders come forward to help the needy.

Lights, Camera, Inaction
It's the college cameraman of MCMDAV College Principal Puneet Bedi, who seems to be her shadow wherever she goes. Recently Bedi went to the Panjab University accompanied by the cameraperson to meet the DSW on some issue pertaining to the college. Evidently obsessed by the principal, the cameraman kept flashing the camera and clicking her. When someone asked the reason behind the 'photoshoot', Bedi snubbed the cameraman and told him to stop clicking. "I am not that beautiful that you keep taking my pictures the entire day, smiled Bedi.

Manpower
Haryana Roadways is a perfect example of male domination at key positions among the public sector organizations. Ever since Haryana came into existence in 1966, there had been only one female bureaucrat heading the department. Satwanti Ahlawat was appointed for the post of General Manager, Haryana Roadways, Chandigarh. Not surprisingly, she held the additional charge as General Manager in the 90s only for about three months.

Painted black
"A good lawyer is one who knows the law and a smart lawyer is one who knows the Judge", a speaker at the General House of the Punjab and Haryana Bar Association said while addressing the gathering demanding introspection by black sheep among advocates who travel to the other side from the Bar.

Yeh dil maange more
Despite the fact that the financial condition of the Punjab government is in the doldrums, the menu card in the Punjab civil secretariat is improving. Gone are the days when the officers had to satisfy themselves with the traditional lassi. For, they have a new replacement, Diet coke. Moreover, in addition to the mini cheese samosas, for lunch, one can order chicken masala from the main canteen. Who cares for the expenses, its all courtesy Punjab government.

Heading: Among the winners are a couple, a five-time councillor - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Forum directed Tata Teleservices to pay Rs 2,000 to a complainant, as compensation for deficiency in services. The complainant, Rohtash Godara, a resident of Sector 7, had purchased a mobile at a cost of Rs 1,700. He had also paid an additional amount of Rs 500 as security for a new connection.

The complainant said he had opted for tariff plan and had a credit limit of Rs 2,500. He alleged that the outgoing facility of his phone was disrupted, on the ground that he had exceeded his credit limit of Rs 1,500. His credit limit, however, was Rs 2,500. He then moved the consumer forum.

In its reply, Tata Teleservices, said the credit limit of the complainant was Rs 2,500 initially, and was later revised to Rs 1,500.

The forum ruled: "This is an unfair trade practice adopted by the company to harass the complainant, which they cannot be permitted to continue."

Heading: Courier company to pay for not delivering rakhi in time - Indian Express
Content:
A couple was among the 15 newly-elected municipal councillors, who were voted for the Kharar Municipal Council on Sunday. Besides, Roshan Lal, was elected for the fifth consecutive time, while Jai Bhagwan Singla and Balwinder Kaur were elected to the council for the second time.

Anmong those who suffered losses were four councillors, all members of the outgoing council this year. Sukhwant Singh, councillor from Ward No. 8 and wife Paramjeet Kaur, from Ward No. 11 were the lone couple who had contested the elections. Sukhwant is the younger brother of Charanjit Singh, Chamkaur Sahib MLA. The couple had contested from the SAD-BJP combine.

Jai Bhagwan Singla, who was the vice-president of the outgoing council and Balwinder Kaur, who was a member, were elected from Ward No. 15 and 13, respectively, on the ticket of the SAD-BJP combine.

The prominent losers included Gurnam Singh from Ward No. 2, Jasveer Singh from Ward No. 8, Amrik Kaur and Gurdeep Kaur from Ward No. 10. Sher Kaur and Gurmukh Singh, too, who were members of the council in the previous term, also suffered a defeat.

Among the first-timers were 12 councillors.

Heading: Drama in Sec 18 as 100-yr-old tree axed - Indian Express
Content:
Holding a courier company responsible for causing mental and emotional harassment to the complainant after it failed to deliver a packet of rakhi, the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed DTDC couriers to pay Rs 100 as compensation.

The company has also been directed to refund the booking charges of Rs 25 which were paid at the time of booking the consignment. The company has also been directed to pay Rs 500 as the cost of litigation.

The complainant, Surinder Kaur, a resident of Sector 15, had sent a courier containing rakhi, to her brother in Amritsar. It was alleged that the courier was neither delivered to its destination nor was it returned back to the sender.

The courier company, in its reply, stated that they were still in search of the consignment. It also said that the terms and conditions were read over to the complainant at the time of the booking and they are liable to pay Rs 100 as damage.

The forum ruled that since the courier company has admitted that the consignment had been lost, it certainly amounts to an act of negligence and deficiency in service, due to which not only the complainant had suffered mentally, emotionally and physically, but the very purpose of the contract also stood frustrated and the desire of the complainant to send rakhi to her brother on Rakshabandhan could not be fulfilled.

Heading: Held guilty in inquiry, head constable kills self - Indian Express
Content:
High drama prevailed in Sector 18 when a 100-year-old kikar tree was axed by a woman resident on Sunday. She was, however, stopped by the police later, after strong opposition by the neighbours, and members of the Horticulture department.

Even as a case under Section 14 of the Punjab Capital Act was registered, the police were yet to arrest the women till the filing of this report.

Interestingly, the police do not even know the name of the accused, owner of house number 1530 in Sector 18.

"We will find the name of the woman tomorrow and then arrest her. She has been accused of illegally cutting the tree," said Sukhdev Singh Bhullar, SHO, Sector 19 police station.

The incident occurred at 11 am on Sunday when the woman was seen cutting the trees along with her domestic help.

While a kikar tree was axed, the servant also tried to axe a pipal and a neem tree. The neighbours cried foul and said the trees, with their heavy branches, were the attraction of the sector for years.

Later, the police took away the broken branches in a truck.

When the neighbours, including some lawyers, protested, the woman said she was only pruning the trees.

"She almost axed the pipal tree, while others were cut during the night, when no one noticed. They trees are about 100 years old," said Advocate Vishal Thakur, a resident of house number 1528.

The area residents said the woman is hardly seen in the house and lives somewhere else.

A case has been registered on the complaint of Krishan Pal Singh, SDE, Horticulture.

Heading: ‘Medical college’ to refund fee for duping student - Indian Express
Content:
A head constable posted as Malkhana Munshi at the Haryana MLA Hostel in Sector 3 allegedly committed suicide by shooting himself in the head with his service revolver late Saturday night.

Sukhbir Singh was found lying in a pool of blood inside his barrack. He was from the third battalion of the Haryana Armed Police (HAP) of Hisar.

In his suicide note, which the police recovered near his body, Sukhbir alleged he was taking the extreme step after Mam Chand, a CID Inspector in Hissar, wrongly held him guilty in a departmental inquiry. Following this, he had been demoted from an Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) to a head constable in the Haryana Police. Aggrieved, he decided to kill himself.

Har Shai Sharma, Station House Officer, Sector 3 police station, said the note will be sent to the Central Forensic Science Laboratory for confirmation of handwriting and the further course of action will be decided thereafter.

The police have, meanwhile, begun investigations under Section 174 CRPC. Sukhbir is survived by his wife and two sons.

Heading: ‘A new arms race is under way in Asia’ - Indian Express
Content:
Aspiring to become a doctor, Farah Latif, a resident of Jammu, had sought admission in a dental college in 1999 and deposited Rs 6.15 lakh for the four-year BDS course.

Little did she know that the college was unrecogonised and not affiliated to a university, as it had claimed in an advertisement.

Now, after nine years, the State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has upheld the order of the Mansa District Consumer Forum (passed in 2004) and directed the Khalsa Dental College and Hospital, Nangal Kalan, to refund the fee at the rate of nine per cent per annum.

A fraud case was already registered against them in 2001 and the managing director-cum-chairman, Dr Naginder Singh Harika, also faced imprisonment for two years in the case.

Latif had sought admission in academic year 1999-2000 against a management seat quota after depositing Rs 5 lakh as the admission fee. While she deposited this amount in November 1999, in February 2000 she was asked to deposit another Rs 75,000 as tuition fee and Rs 40,000 as hostel charges. In all, she had deposited Rs 6.15 lakh for the course.

After attending classes for about a year, the student realised that the college was not recogonised and she will not receive a degree. The student alleged that she had been personally assured by Harika's wife Sukhwant Kaur to wait for recognition, which she had said was likely soon.

It was alleged in the compliant that 20 precious months of the respondent were wasted and besides suffering huge financial loss, she also suffered mental and physical harassment.

The District Consumer Forum then directed the director to refund the fees along with compensation of Rs 2,000 with 14 per cent rate of interest.

The appeal was then filed against the order of the district forum.

The State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission observed that the student kept on waiting for the institute to get a recognition letter till she attended college for one year after which she went to Bangalore in August 2001.

On the basis of an advertisement published by the college in a newspaper, the commission observed that the college declared itself affiliated to Baba Farid University of Health Sciences, Faridkot, and that it was approved by the Government of India, Ministry of Health.

"The said order by the district forum does not suffer from any illegality and is upheld," said Justice S.N Aggarwal, President, State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Punjab.

The rate of interest was, however, lowered by the commission from 14 per cent, as ordered by the Mansa Consumer Forum, to 9 per cent.

Heading: ‘Perpetrators of violence do not deserve mercy, should be hanged’ - Indian Express
Content:
India's growing economy can easily sustain a 0.5 to 1 per cent hike in the defence budget over a period of three to five years, especially if the government reduces its expenditure on wasteful subsidies

Considering China's increased defence budget and its race to acquire submarines and aircraft to upgrade the forces along with developing the infrastructure, India now faces a threat from the communist state.

With India, Japan and Russia also investing heavily in defence, a new Asian arms race is under way. This year itself, China hiked its defence expenditure to 18 per cent, as compared to the previous years. This makes China's military spending second only to the US, whereas India has just increased it's spending by 5 per cent.

In monetary terms, China has allocated $59 billion as compared to $26.4 billion spent by India on its defence expenditure. Needless to say, it is a matter of concern for India. China's self-confidence and assertiveness has increased in line with the rapid growth of economy, ever since the introduction of market-oriented reforms in the 1970s.

This leads to us ask questions like: Where is China heading? Will it start a new regional order by taking advantage of the upper hand it has over its neighbors, both in terms of size and power?

Beijing fears that if the economic and trade relations between India and the United States intensify, it would be a great threat to China, and would mean the stronghold of USA over the region.

The change in China's policy of focusing on new generation military hardware started since the first Gulf War in 1991, for fear of a war anytime in the future. China's military planners know they cannot rely on their country's size as the only deterrent.

To counter this threat, India needs to modernise its military. We need to invest more on improving the logistics infrastructure along the Tibet border, on intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance systems for early warning and in generating land - and air-based firepower asymmetries to counter China's numerical superiority. We also need to raise and suitably equip four to six mountain strike divisions to carry the fight into the Chinese territory, if ever such a need arises. All of this, however, will require a large amount of capital investment.

India's growing economy can easily sustain a 0.5 to 1 per cent hike in the defence budget over a period of three to five years, especially if the government reduces the expenditure on wasteful subsidies.

In the past, it was China's alliance with Pakistan that worried India. We also have history as a proof of tensions between the two neighbours, which makes it all the more necessary to have a plan B of action, if ever such a need arises.

Heading: Four vehicles stolen from city in 36 hours - Indian Express
Content:
The recent terrorist attacks in the national capital have created ripples of fear across the nation. City residents, meanwhile, feel that concrete measures need to be taken in time to avoid such mishaps in future.

Newsline finds out

Kunal, chartered accountant

It was a complete act of gore. The barbarism, with which, the terrorists have once again targetted the innocent reflects upon the contempt they have for Indians. Keeping in view the rising incidents of terrorism in the country, the intelligence network needs to be updated. Also, those behind the attacks should be severely punished.

Dr Nandita Kakkar

Terrorists want to divide the country in the name of religion. The frequency with which such attacks are happening shows that India is on their hit list. The intelligence agencies need to become cautious. Also, the government should take strict action against the culprits.

Renu Sekhri, housewife

These people should not be tried under the court of law which is long and cumbersome. Since they have destroyed families, killed innocent people, they should be punished in an equally brutal manner. They should be hanged till death without being given an opportunity to defend themselves.

Anurag Bhateja, web designer

Yesterday's bomb blasts are worth condemning. We should not overlook it and let it pass off as another incident considering the frequency with which they are occurring. Indians have the habit of becoming used to things. But such incidents should be taken as a warning signal. The severest punishment should be reserved for these terrorists.

Dr Akshay Nayyar, dentist

There is no point lamenting over the blasts, now that they have happened. The perpetrators of violence do not deserve any mercy, they should be hanged.

Heading: Students to visit old age homes, says Education department - Indian Express
Content:
Nearly 700 vehicle thefts have been reported stolen from the city, since the beginning of this year. The city, meanwhile, has reported four incidents of vehicle thefts in the last 36 hours.

These include two Bolero jeeps and two Marutis. A Bolero, (CH 04-A-1236), was stolen from the residence of Satinder, a resident of Sector 38 (West) on Saturday night.

Sapinder Singh, a resident of Sector 47, meanwhile, reported that his Bolero (CH-04-0082) was stolen from outside his house on Friday night. Desbandhu Walia, another resident of Sector 47, said his Maruti (CH-01-V-8899) was stolen from the Madhya Marg parking on Friday.

Another Maruti, belonging to Rakesh Kumar, a resident of Sector 44, meanwhile, was stolen from his residence on Friday night.

Man crushed to death
An unidentified was crushed to death by a truck on Saturday night. The incident occurred near the Sector 39, 40, 55, 56 chowk. The man was rushed to the PGI, where he was declared dead on arrival. A case under Sections 279, 337, 304 A of the IPC has been registered against the accused, who has not been identified yet. ENS

Heading: Workshop held on scope in mobile space - Indian Express
Content:
The Education department has planned to launch a programme, involving senior citizens and city schools. Under the programme, the school authorities will be required to take students on a visit of the old age homes in Sector 15 and 17. The programme is being organised in association with Help Age India.

Sources said that the department had issued directions to schools regarding the same.

"The aged are an important part of the society and should not be neglected. We aim to make them feel special through this programme. If we are able to bring a smile on their faces, we will consider the programme a success," said S K Setia, Director Public Instructions (Schools).

He added that it is not mandatory for the schools to adhere to the programme. "We do not wish to impose anything. Such values and feelings come from within. Students can volunteer themselves," he said.

The school authorities will arrange regular visits to the old age homes on weekends, buses for which will be provided by Help Age India.

"It is a good step towards showing affection to the aged. They should not be deprived of respect and love, especially in the later part of life, when they need it the most," said Ravi Raj Kaur, Principal, Government Model Senior Secondary School, Sector 35.

Heading: Exams near, shortage of books worry students - Indian Express
Content:
"India is adding nearly 7 million mobile phone subscribers every month, which is equivalent to the total number of Switzerland's mobile subscriber base. There is a huge opportunity in the mobile domain in India," said Beat Brandle, CEO Mobile Solutions.

He was addressing a workshop on "Trends and Opportunities in Mobile Space" organised by the Chandigarh chapter of The Indus Entrepreneurs (TiE) today. Brandle is in India, on a visit to explore business opportunities .

Puneet Vatsayan, President, TiE said: " The workshop is the first in a series of business conferences, to mentor and guide the budding entrepreneurs, create synergies with different stakeholders in this evolving ecosystem for entrepreneurship, and drive growth in this region."

Heading: ‘God or not, there is a super power that governs world’ - Indian Express
Content:
Six months into the new session, students across the city are still grappling with the problem of shortage of textbooks. While the students are worried with the half-yearly exams round the corner, officials in the Education department say the NCERT has not been able to supply books on time.

The students of Classes VI to VIII have still not received the textbooks for Social Studies, including Geography, Civics and History.

Rajinder, a bookshop owner in Sector 22 said, "There has been a delay in the supply of books from the NCERT. We have received orders from different schools that do not have adequate books."

While some schools have received the books, others are waiting for their lot to arrive.

Rajesh Kumar, an SSA teacher says, "Students of my class were able to purchase the books only a few days ago as some booksellers that they approached had the stock. But the shortage cannot be ignored for long."

Seema Ranjan, a student at Government High School, Karsan, said: "The exams are next week and I still do not have the Social Studies books. I do not know what I will write in the exam."

Parents, meanwhile, say schools should scrap the half-yearly exam in view of the situation.

"It is not possible for students to prepare for the subject when they do not have the books. School authorities should defer the exams till the books are made available in the market," Pankaj Maja, a parent said.

Officials from the Education department say they have hastened the process to provide books to students. "We know that the students are facing a lot of problems due to the limited supply of books. Books will be available in a few days," an official said.

Heading: Ganesha gets safe farewell, Mumbai says no to terror - Indian Express
Content:
The question about the existence of God has always been my favourite topic. What amazes me is that since times immemorial, ever since the birth of mankind, we have had questions raised about the almighty, the ultimate force that is god.

Of late, I have observed that the young, who have reservations about god and faith, have given a different name to the phenomena: spirituality.

I am neither an atheist, nor do I blindly believe in God. I, however, believe that there is a superpower, which governs everything. Whatever happens on this planet is manoeuvred by another force, which is much higher and exalted than we can ever comprehend.

The force, by many, is called God. I have had discussions with my friends who say that spirituality and the almighty are two different domains. They argue that when you worship God, you follow various rituals and customs, without even knowing their real purpose. But when you turn spiritual, you connect yourself with God on a different plane.

It is to do with self-awakening, rather than pleasing a particular god, or the proponents of a faith.

I feel, in all this discussion about God and spirituality, what matters is faith. For me, the almighty is my faith, which keeps me going, even in the worst circumstances. I have the faith that someone is guiding and protecting me.

But I do not visit temples or mosques to thank him. I do pray, but it is more a meditation, as it has a calming effect on me and guides me towards my purpose in life.

If I am discharging my duties honestly, I think I am worshipping God, for I believe that all of us have a purpose in life, which has been laid for us by no other body than God. If I do that properly, I have achieved God.

Heading: After Delhi’s dustbin bombs, each bin manned - Indian Express
Content:
* Day after serial blasts in capital, lakhs throng immersion points amid unprecedented security
* Relief for thousands of policemen, civic staff and volunteers overseeing day's proceedings

Ultimately, it was Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh who echoed the sentiments of the city's law and order establishment and of the average Mumbaiite alike: "Thank you," Deshmukh said at Girgaum Chowpatty, where 15 lakh people gathered to watch as thousands of Ganesha idols made their way to the sea on Anant Chaturdashi Sunday.

"No amount of human effort can manage such a large sea of people. I would like to thank the city, and all Mumbaikars and mandal organisers for showing such solidarity. They have followed all the security rules and made the day a success¿ It is a befitting answer to the terrorists."

With serial bomb blasts rocking the national capital on the eve of Mumbai's big day, security at Girgaum Chowpatty and 83 other Ganpati immersion points was reviewed overnight and stepped up further: The number of high ranking police officials and security guards at the VIP dais at Girgaum was increased; big potted plants that were part of the décor were removed; 50 security guards manned each major immersion area, up from the earlier 30; senior police officials at each major spot were increased from five to eight; while the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) had set up five CCTV cameras and three rotating cameras at Girgaum pandal, the Mumbai police had its own CCTV cameras; even the number of ambulances was increased from five to eight at Girgaum Chowpatty.

There were also two helicopters alongside the rescue boats on standby.

"This year, around 900 VIPs are expected to visit the seafront to witness the immersion proceedings. Maximum security has been taken to ensure that the day goes off smoothly," said Additional Municipal Commissioner Mahadeo Sangle.

Deputy Chief Minister R R Patil visited all the main immersion points to take stock of security.

To the credit of the Mumbai Police's Traffic Department, traffic was mostly smooth, thanks to some detailed planning and management. Parts of arterial roads leading to immersion points were strictly out of bounds for non-Ganesha traffic during the peak evening hours.. Also, after a long night of tense nakabandis, the city's traffic policemen were back on the streets on Sunday morning, readying for the immersion rush.

"Traffic management is all about an alert eye for detail and keen observation," said Deputy Commissioner of Police (Traffic) Harish Baijal, who was himself on the rounds of the city through the day. "Maintaining a balance between pedestrian traffic and vehicular movement is essential, ensuring that no parked vehicles on the road delay any procession is also a priority."

At Juhu beach, one of the four main immersion points, there were 200 policemen as well as 20 policemen in plainclothes, from the state Anti-Terrorism Squad.

The Bomb Detection and Disposal Squad (BDDS) of the Mumbai Police made repeated visits too, and sniffer dogs checked every corner of the area.

Deputy Commissioner of Police (Zone 3) Niket Kaushik said: "Following yesterday's act, we have deployed two teams of the BDDS. Till last year we just had one squad manning the area. This year, as the Mumbai Police does not want to take any chances, the BDDS will take repeated rounds till the final immersion is over."

Policemen in plainclothes also mingled with the crowd to keep a check on any suspicious people, objects or activity. "Till last year, focus was on crowd control. However, keeping in mind security threats, we have shifted our focus to alertness," said Kaushik.

CCTVs had been installed at secret locations at Juhu beach too, as they were at other immersion spots, said Kaushik.

"Keeping in mind the heightened security situation, we have installed 15 flood lights and 25 search lights in Juhu," said Assistant Municipal Commissioner of K-West ward, Anil Khoje.

* By 8 pm on Anant Chaturdashi, 23,484 idols were immersed at the 84 immersion spots in the city.

* Of these, 21,960 were household idols and 1,524 were large idols being bid adieu by Sarvajanik Ganesh Mandals.

* Of the household idols, 724 were immersed in the 20 artificial lakes set up in the city

* Ham Radio operators registered 27 lost-and-found cases including a dozen children and over 10 senior citizens at main immersion point Girgaum Chowpatty, of which 22 were solved by 8 pm.

* There were 21 cases of registered injuries at Girgaum Chowpatty, most of them treated on the spot.

* An ambulance had to be called when the frame of an idol fell, injuring three persons

Heading: At Agripada, a lasting Ganpati tradition continues in sensitive times - Indian Express
Content:
The innocuous green dustbins dotting the city were top priority for the city's civic administration on Sundya morning, hours after similar dustbins were used to hide bombs in the capital.

As an immediate measure, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation on Sunday decided to ensure that each and every dustbin in the city ¿ there are a few thousand ¿ are manned through immersion day. Conservancy staff workers were roped in immediately.

Significantly, the large pot-shaped 'nirmalya kalash' the urn for floral offerings, were also closely watched over by volunteers and guards.

Additional Municipal Commissioner (City) R A Rajeev said civic officials had been in consultation with the police top brass soon after the New Delhi serial explosions. "Accordingly, it was decided that at least one conservancy worker will man every dustbin in the city," he said. Earlier, after bicycles were used in blasts at Bangalore, Jaipur and Ahmedabad, the civic body passed a resolution making licensing and registration compulsory for cycle-owners. That move is now awaiting the municipal commissioner and state government's final nod.

At the 150 urns placed at the city's 84 immersion spots to collect nirmalya, devotees were also requested to empty their plastic bags and only dispose of their contents. "Each and every bag will be checked and only then its contents allowed to be put in the urn," said Additional Municipal Commissioner Mahadeo Sangle.

Heading: Ganapati visarjan attracts tourists from UK, Thailand - Indian Express
Content:
Lalbaugcha Raja idol procession halts for two minutes opposite Hindustani Masjid, welcomed by Hindus and Muslims together

It all started over two decades ago, when slogan-shouting Hindus accompanied by loud music led their Ganpati deity into localities offering namaaz. So, at a time when the polarisation of communities is once again in the spotlight, the genuine amity at the annual pit-stop of the Lalbaugcha Raja at minority-dominated Agripada during the holy month of Ramzan was a sight to witness.

"Our Muslim brothers have been coming to welcome the lord at Byculla for over more than 20 years," said Lalbaugcha Raja mandal president Sunil Joshi. As the idol makes its way from Lalbaug to Girgaum Chowpatty, it makes a series of scheduled halts en route to immersion, Agripada being one.

On Sunday, around 100 policemen and a Special Reserve Police Force battalion stood guard at this most sensitive spot. And, as has been the tradition, Lalbaugcha Raja was garlanded during his two-minute halt right opposite Byculla's Hindustani Masjid, by Hindus with Muslims standing alongside.

With idol worship banned in Islam, members of the community who participated in Hindu festivals were often isolated. "The practice was in existence a long time back, but now the masjid does not participate nor pays any money," said Altaf Patel, general secretary of the Hindusani Masjid, who himself is a part of the committee and remains present onstage when the Ganesha idol comes visiting.

Former MLA Madhu Chavan is among those ensuring that everyone gathers at the time of the procession. "We have been doing this for years and both communities participate," he said.

Before Ganeshotsav begins, trustees of the mosque and the Lalbaugcha Raja mandal meet to ensure that the arrival of the procession in Nagpada and Agripada does not clash with namaaz timings. "If the procession reaches here by 6 pm or before that, it stops until namaaz is complete," said one of the trustees.

M R Borana of Sandeep Cloth Center says the tradition of garlanding Lalbaugcha Raja at Agripada began in the late 1970s.

"The atmosphere was heated due to regular communal clashes and then the Bhiwandi riots. It was then that both communities decided to come together through the Mohalla committee," Borana said.

Heading: Immersion Sidelights - Indian Express
Content:
"Aatankwaad se nahi darenge, Ganapati bappa moraya karenge"(We will not get scared by terrorism, we will continue praising the elephant God). That was the slogan on the lips of the thousands of people who were present at Juhu on Sunday to witness Ganpati visarjan.

For 28-year-old graphic designer, Craig Lewisohn from London, this was indeed was a unique spectacle. "Nothing like this happens in my country. Back home I have never seen such a huge sea of people uniting for a common cause," says Craig. Craig came to India two months back and ever since he landed in Mumbai, he was waiting to witness the visarjan. "Forget the religious angle, this festival has also got a social value. I have read a bit on Indian history and as far as I know, this festival was started by a leader called Lokmanya Tilak to unite Indians against the Company," he says as locals ask him to click their pictures.

Quiz him on the security issues that are dominating the country and he says, visibly unperturbed, "Terror attacks can happen in any large gathering, and as far as I know after yesterday's attack in the capital, security in the city has been heightened. In any case, terror attacks should not play a spoilsport, this is a festival and one should celebrate it with utmost gaiety." Indeed the crowds present at the visarjan displayed the same sentiment. Locals and foreigners said that if people started living in fear that would be the ultimate win for terrorists.

John Lewingston, who came from Washington with his wife and son in June, says, "I came to India with my family three months ago. I had always wanted to see this festival and did not wish to miss this opportunity." John is no stranger to terror attacks and understands the need for heightened security. Adds John, "Unfortunately we live in times of bomb blasts and terror attacks. I lost more than 200 friends and relatives in the 7/11 attacks. But that has not stopped me from going to large gatherings." For people like him it is all about living without any paranoia. He admits that today he is more open to being checked and cross-checked for security reasons.

Juhu also saw a group from Thailand which was present at the beach to shoot a documentary about the festival. Surawoot Maikan, a television anchor who doubles up as a documentary film maker whenever he gets an out-of-the-box idea informs, "In Thailand too people worship the elephant god but here the celebrations are done on a huge scale, I wanted to know how Indians celebrate and worship the festival." Apart from the many foreigners for whom the festival was a spectacle, Juhu also saw locals from all communities coming together for the festival. 22-year-old Hassan Quereshi came all the way from Pune with his group of friends to catch a glimpse of the festival. "I had heard about the festival so many times and seen it on TV. However it was my utmost wish to come to the city and see the festivities first hand. So yesterday night I boarded the last bus from Pune to be here," says Quereshi.

Heading: Andheri-Dahisar belt high on property demand: Report - Indian Express
Content:
Hungry Kya?
The serpentine queue formed in front of a small stall at Girgaum Chowpatty on Sunday was not for immersing the elephant-headed god but comprised devotees and visitors waiting to quench hunger pangs. Ramesh A Manipuri's stall has been distributing free vada pavs to the milling crowds that visit the beach on Anant Chaturdashi for the past eight years. This year, there was an addition-packets of farsan and biscuits.

"We earn and make money the entire year, so why not spend one day just giving back?" asks Ramesh, who distributed 2,500 vada pavs last year. Ramesh says his friends celebrate the Ganesh festival with great fervour and then contribute towards his initiative.

While his stall is located a few metres away, it remains closed on immersion day. This year, Manipuri had 6,000 vada pavs to give away, 40 kg of farsan, and 200 kg of biscuits.

An interesting footnote: Manipuri is a native of Haryana.

The Loudest Sena
The hub of the visarjan celebrations, Lalbaug, played host to a political battle with a difference. The Shiv Sena and the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena may not see eye to eye on a regular basis, but at the Lalbaug junction, the two political parties had set up stages on opposite sides of the road, complete with DJs and huge loudspeakers. One MNS activist, tongue-in-cheek, warned the rival Sena to turn down the volume. "It is adding to noise pollution. Sena leaders are requested to keep the noise under control," he said, even as his own camp's DJ blasted remixed bhajans at full decibel.

No Entry
The media, especially television channels who had geared up for the grand finale at Girgaum Chowpatty and had been promised a vantage point at the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation's dais, were turned away at the last minute. The pandal, usually shared by dignitaries and mediapersons, was out of bounds for press owing to security concerns. Electronic media houses' OB vans were also removed from the beachfront late Saturday night and had to later scrounge for space on the congested main road and.

Marathi manoos
Municipal Commissioner Jairaj Phatak arrived dressed in traditional Mahrashtrian attire to bid adeiu to the elephant-headed god. With a colourful red peshwa pagdi and white bandhgala, the IAS officer looked every bit the Marathi manoos at the VIP pandal. "For the last 116 years, Mumbai has been celebrating the Ganesh festival. This year too we are celebrating the festival with equal enthusiasm," he said. "Ganpati is a reigning god for Hindus, but for the Marathi manoos he is the main deity and we seek his blessings and strength," he said.

Green volunteers
While garbage may hold no value for many, it earns 58 year-old Vijaya Rajan Shetty her daily bread. And during Ganpati visarjan it earns her Rs 80. Shetty, a Karnataka native but a Mumbaiite by birth, has been coming to the Girgaum Chowpati for the past seven years with 10-15 other women. "We are all from Goregaon's Santosh Nagar and have been a part of the Forum of Recyclers Community and Environment (FORCE) for the past seven years. While on other days we collect garbage from buildings on Napean Sea Road, we come here every visarjan," said Shetty. On other dyas, they sell scrap that they sort to earn their living, but immersion day brings some ready cash too. Asked whether they have tried any other job Shetty's friend Sulochana Perimal Gounder quipped, "For 20 years we have done only this and for 20 more years to come, this is our fate. We don't know any other skill except for sorting and collecting garbage."

(contributed by Swatee Kher, Shweta Desai and Riya Kartha)

Heading: Advanced IVF centre inaugurated by President - Indian Express
Content:
At a time when a slowdown has hit the realty sector in Mumbai, a market study report called Makaan IQ has shown that demand for properties both on sale and rent is the highest in the Andheri-Dahisar belt.

The study reveals that despite the belt witnessing a 16% drop in demand over the four month period, April and July 2008, it still commands a demand that is double than that of prime areas of Central Mumbai such Dadar-Lower Parel and three times the demand in South west area of Bandra-Santacruz. The report carried by a portal by the same name analyses the property trends in both sale and rental markets between April and July this year. It shows that demand has nose-dived by 8% to 20% all over Mumbai in the last four months. It states that besides the Andheri-Dahisar belt, the property hotspots are Navi Mumbai, Thane and Central Mumbai, all together accounting for 65% of the demand in Mumbai. The demand for rental properties is maximum in Andheri-Dahisar (28%), followed by Navi Mumbai (17%) and Central Mumbai (13%).

Aditya Verma, business head for Makaan.com says, "Places between Andheri and Dahisar are preferred by professionals migrating to Mumbai since the area provides budget homes with close proximity to multiplexes, malls, pubs, shopping centers and schools. Another factor that has boosted the demand for homes here is the shifting of offices from town to Andheri, Goregaon, Andheri-Kurla road and Malad."

Another finding in the study reveals the demand supply imbalance in the city. Eighty per cent of the demand is for properties below Rs 75 lakh. However, with most developers eager to get into the lucrative luxury homes segment, the supply of houses below 75 lakh is merely 64%.

Verma explains that this is the reason why Central Mumbai has supply in excess of demand despite several residential projects coming up over the last few years.

"Areas like Lower Parel cater to homes for the luxury segment for which the demand is very limited," adds Verma.

Drop in demand from April to July 2008
South Mumbai:-14%
Central Mumbai: -17%
Bandra-Santacruz: -14%
Andheri-Dahisar: -16%
Virar: -20%
Harbour: -17%
Navi Mumbai: -8%
Thane: -16%

Heading: Tech innovation centre at IITB - Indian Express
Content:
The advanced DY Patil Fertility Centre along with a new medical college building was recently inaugurated by the President Pratibha Patil in Navi Mumbai.

This centre has started in association with the Bloom IVF fertility care clinics. Bloom IVF is also in the process of starting an advanced fertility care centre in association with the Fortis group at the La Femme Hospital in New Delhi.

The unit is focusing on increasing the success rates of patients who come for the first time to access IVF facility as well as patients who fail multiple times by using this facility, said Dr Nandita Palshetkar, Consultant Gynecologist and infertility specialist at the centre. These patients can be treated with a variety of techniques such as Assisted Laser Hatching, a combination of day 2 and day 5 embryo transfers also called 'Sequential Transfers', and an introduction of a new freezing technique called vitrification. The DY Patil Fertility Centre will also focus on trying to help poor patients who want to access these services. "We believe in helping infertile patients irrespective of their financial background and without compromising on the results," said Dr Palshetkar.

Heading: Riding The Tome Truck - Indian Express
Content: Technological entrepreneurship at the Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay (IITB) is set to receive a boost with the establishment of the Rahul Bajaj Technology Innovation Centre on its campus. The centre will not just house the 17 start ups incubated at the Society for Innovation and Entrepreneurship (SINE),  an 'umbrella for promotion for entrepreneurship' at the IITB, but is also expected to nurture over 50 companies once its set up. According to Ashok Misra, director, IITB, the technology centre would comprise a six to seven floored building with two of its floors reserved for a rotating exhibition showcasing the technological developments at IITB. "Through this exhibition, people will be able to see the excitement of innovation by the IITians," said Ashok Misra.

Heading: Dipped Clean - Indian Express
Content:
The Mumbai Metropolitan Region has barely a dozen big bookstores. Of 35 districts in the state, 22 have no bookstores at all. In 30 districts, there are no bookstores stocking titles in English.
With 10 trucks converted into mobile bookstores, Granthayan becomes the first to make English and Marathi titles available at a toll-free number

Books may be man's best friends, but the relationship grows only when one is able to find the book. For Mumbaities, that search just got simplified for anybody armed with the title of the book and its publisher's name. A new city-based venture Granthayan now offers to bring the book to your doorstep through mobile book shops. You can place an order by telephone, from anywhere in the state, at no extra cost.

"Publishers and book sellers are not changing with changing times. Why would a person travel a distance to procure books to read? Books are not an essential commodity that people cannot live without," says Pankaj Kurulkar, the 46-year-old chief executive officer of Granthayan.

More significantly, Granthayan is one of the very few places where book lovers can access English and Marathi titles under one roof.

Kurulkar feels that easy availability is the only hurdle between people and books. "The literacy rate is increasing and so is the need for books. Granthayan is the result of my wish to overcome the hurdle that readers face in trying to locate a book."

An electronics engineer, Kurulkar voluntarily shut down his successful I-T firm in 2005 to pursue his long time desire of being a full time writer. That's when he realised how pathetic the publishing and distribution system was in India. "I could see the flaws in the system and I thought I could remedy this," says Kurulkar. Granthayan is the result of eight months of planning. "I decided to sell books in a different manner," Kurulkar says.

Books can now be procured after a quick browse at the Granthayan mobile books stores, one of which was inaugurated by Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh at Mantralaya on August 27 this year.

"We have purchased 10 trucks and converted them into mobile books shops which would be constantly touring the state," says Kurulkar. Besides having the capacity to store and display 20,000 books, each Granthayan truck is a state-of-the-art space, equipped with a computerised sales counter and GPS.

The vehicle's satellite link relays various data regarding the books shop, such as position of the vehicle on a map, whether it is stationary or in motion, sales of books along with their titles, authors' names and publishers, in real time. Besides, Kurulkar can also check the position of each vehicle's fuel tank from the comfort of his office at Mahim, he explains, showing on his laptop the position of one of the mobile stores, currently at Wai, in Satara district.

The popularity of the mobile book shops can be gauged by the fact on the very first day, Granthayan became the top vendor of Marathi titles, selling over 1,000 books in a day.

The mobile book stores also host hour-long cultural activities on Saturdays. "Eminent people engage the crowd with short story recitations, poetry, comedy, psychiatry and counselling. Besides it would also be a platform for local artistes to showcase their talents," says Kurulkar.

He has already set himself targets of growth – 100 mobile book shops in a year and 1,000 in three years, covering a majority of the states in the country.

To order books in English and Marathi, call the toll free number 1800 209 8074.

To avail this facility, one has to place an order worth a minimum of Rs 250. The books will be delivered at your doorstep at no extra cost.

Heading: History society turns 125, to expand reach - Indian Express
Content:
From segregation of nirmalya to sweeping on the morning after, thousands of civic staff will be helped by volunteers

With the Ganesh Chaturthi, arguably Mumbai's most popular festival, coming to an end, several groups of concerned citizens are preparing to tackle the after-effects of the festivities — flowers and coconuts strewn on the beach along with garbage, litter left behind by the revellers and rotting food leftovers.

Now, in a joint initiative by the Clean Mumbai Foundation, the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai, the Brihanmumbai Sarvajanik Ganesh Utsav Samanvay Samiti and United Way, citizens are planning to segregate floral offerings — called nirmalya — along with accompanying plastic bags and other miscellaneous items and collect them from the various Ganesha mandals. Launched before immersion day, the idea was to hold back flowers and other miscellaneous items from being dumped into the sea while idols are being immersed.

"Nirmalya consists of flowers, garlands, coconuts, accessories to decorate the deity and other miscellaneous things that are offered during worship. For the past few years, Mumbai's Ganpati festival revellers and the BMC staff have initiated the separation of festival flowers that are put into the 'Nirmalya Kalash' instead of disposing the flowers directly in the sea," said Kunti Oza from the Clean Mumbai Foundation. "Our scheme involves the various Ganesh mandals, to separate the Nirmalya in three different bags when they are close to the immersion site. They will be responsible for handing over these Nirmalya bags to the nearby BMC staff who in turn will deposit the Nirmalya collected into trucks categorized for flowers, plastics and miscellaneous. In this way we shall strive to prevent all the Nirmalya going into the sea and also save the big efforts of the BMC staff from doing it manually, as is the case currently," Oza added.

"I live on Juhu Beach. Every day, for the last twenty years, I go for a walk on the beach in the evening. Normally this is a beautiful experience for me. However, for the last seven or eight years there are two times in the year when this experience is anything but beautiful. One is at the onset of the monsoon and the other is at the Ganesh Utsav festival. For days, we have remnants of pujas strewn all along the beach," said actor Soni Razdan.

While this one initiative received immense support from corporate groups and prominent citizens of Mumbai including various mandals, another simultaneous initiative was by students of various colleges who signed up as volunteers to help BMC staff with the entire process.

The Rotaract Club of Narsee Monjee College (RCNM), functioning under the parent body of Rotary Club of Bombay West has been involved in the process since 2004.

This Monday will see the team of 50 to 60 volunteers gathering at 7.30 am at Juhu beach Beach, spending the next three hours collecting waste from the immersion process.

While the remains of idols will be immersed in the sea once again, all the other waste will be gathered and given to the BMC for recycling.

The team had handed over almost 156 kg of waste to the BMC last year.

"We believe that keeping all the good things that nature has endowed us with as pristine as they were meant to be is a responsibility that all of us must share. Last year, we were dirty, tired and perspiring after the drive but the amazing feeling that overcame us looking at the beach which had debris strewn around just a few hours back, all clean with sparkling yellow sand made all the efforts totally worth it," said Naushita Jaising, a member of RCNM.

Also cleaning up Juhu beach will be volunteers of Indian Development Foundation in collaboration with Podar International School, Santacruz (W). NSS Volunteers from Vivek College of Commerce will also be joining the team.

Heading: Green Wheels - Indian Express
Content:
As the Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS) turns 125 years old on Monday, a 20-minute film will be screened depicting its journey through these years and its work in the field of nature conservation.

Having started as a suggestion when eight citizens of Mumbai first met on September 15 at the Bhau Daji Lad Museum at the Jijabai Bhosle Udyan at Byculla, BNHS is now India 's premier and foremost non-governmental organisation working in nature conservation, and the only voluntary organisation in the country to have sustained a tradition of scientific research, education as well as conservation activities.

On Monday, a book titled Loke Wan Tho's Birdswill also be released by Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh. A compilation of black and white photographs of birds, the pictures are the work of Loke Wan Tho, a friend and benefactor of the society.

Apart from working towards making key decision-makers in corporate firms and financial institutions aware of the need to work towards ecological security, the BNHS also plans to launch an awareness programme to make people aware of the need to conserve natural resources.

Among its future plans, the BNHS proposes to have Permanent Field Research Stations in all four zones of the country, to aid the society to work more effectively at the local level and in collaboration with local agencies and state governments.

Heading: Selection trials for international carrom tournaments held - Indian Express
Content:
This 17-year-old college student has started Cycle-e-thon, a club of people who believe bicycles are the answer to fuel prices and global warming

While the tension surrounding global warming continues to simmer with environmentalists and scientists yet to stumble upon a solution, 17 year-old Mulund resident Yagnesh Katira has begun a local experiment to counter a global concern. Katira, who feels that cycles are the answer to the challenge of bringing down pollution levels, has started 'Cycle-e-thon' — an eco-club of people who share his passion for cycling.

With a vision to make the city's streets bicycle-friendly, Cycle-e-thon's members have also begun an awareness campaign locally.

"It would always irk me that people would prefer to go by their car or hail an auto rickshaw even if they had to go just a few kilometers away. As I gradually began reading more about global warming concerns and the rise in fuel prices, I realised that cycling could be the solution to all these problems," says Katira. A light study schedule during his Class 11 aided Katira to devote his time to conceptualising Cycle-e-thon, back in 2006. Under the aegis of the Mulund Parents Association, after Cycle-e-thon had become a reality, the next step before Katira was to mobilise members.

"The first initiative by the club was to organise a cycle rally to disseminate its message. Cycles as a mode of transport are most popular among children and we roped in schoolchildren — they were the immediate target group to be roped in for the rally," says Katira who had personally approached principals of various schools in Mulund seeking their support.

Four schools participated and the rally won Cycle-e-thon many admirers. In 2007, the club organised its second rally which saw 300 cyclists participating.

This year Katira decided to involve the government in his endeavour and has started a signature campaign demanding cycle lanes and cycle stations to boost the use of cycles among citizens. "People feel awkward to be seen on a cycle and feel that a car is a symbol of prestige. However infrastructural development is necessary to change these attitudes. Parents are hesitant to let their children use bicycles as they fear the bad roads with no dedicated lanes for cyclists and rashly driven vehicles would turn them into accident casualties. Hence we decided to voice our complaints and our demands to the Minister for Public Works through a signature campaign," says Katira.

The signature campaign with 2,300 signatures from students, cycle enthusiasts as well as school officials was recently sent to Minister for Public Works Anil Deshmukh and the Municipal Commissioner of Mumbai.

"While our demands were acknowledged and commended, the officials however confessed that the lane-planning would require detailed planning. They asked us to conduct workshops to generate awareness about the benefits of cycling and we are presently speaking to some schools about it," says Katira, who however confessed that balancing his studies and his passion is a tough job. "I am presently juggling my first year of college and chartered accountancy. But these can't sabotage my plans for a third rally," he adds.

Heading: UNESCO invites tribal rights activist to Paris - Indian Express
Content:
Eight slicers selected to represent India in the 12th SAARC Carrom Tournament, 5th International Carrom Federation Cup

Eight national and international level slicers were selected to represent India in the 12th South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) Carrom Tournament and the 5th International Carrom Federation Cup, after the completion of the selection trials on Sunday.

While the SAARC tournament will be held in Sri Lanka, the 5th International Carrom Federation Cup will be held in Vadodara from October 11 to 19.

Twelve players from all over the country participated in the trials, which were held at Urmi school. Out of these only eight qualified for the tournaments. In the men's category, Ashok Prakash Gaekwad from Maharashtra ranked first in the competition, followed by B Radhakrishnan and M Natarajan from Tamil Nadu and Yogesh Pardeshi from Maharashtra. Pardeshi is also the reigning world champion.

In the women's category, Rashmi Kumari from Bihar ranked first, followed by I. Ilavazhakhi from Tamil Nadu, P Nirmala from Andhra Pradesh and G Revathy from Tamil Nadu. Ilavazhakhi is the current women's world carrom champion. Both Pardeshi and Ilavazhakhi won the men's and women's title respectively in the 2008 World Carrom Championship in France.

"My confidence level has increased after this selection tournament. Now, I am preparing for the international tournament, which will require intense practice," said Rashmi Kumari from Bihar, who is working with BSNL.

The selection competition in Vadodara was organised by the All India Carrom Federation in association with the Gujarat State Carrom Association.

All the eight SAARC countries — India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Nepal, Maldives, Bhutan, and Afghanistan, will participate in the SAARC tournament.

Countries including USA, UK, Germany, Switzerland, France Italy, Japan, Korea, The Netherlands, Sweden, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, India, Malaysia, Maldives, Nepal and Bangladesh will participate in the Federation Cup.

At present, there are 30 countries all over the world playing the game. Out of these, 23 are affiliated members of the International Carrom Federation, London (UK).

Heading: Contractor beaten up over faulty construction - Indian Express
Content:
Devy to help chart out plans for policies for indigenous languages in India

Vadodara-based tribal rights activist and Sahitya Akademi Award winner Ganesh Devy has been invited by the UNESCO executive board in Paris to discuss issues relating to the framing of policies on indigenous languages of the world.

Devy will join the conference in Paris on September 23 and will give a presentation on the 90 indigenous languages of India, the scriptures of which need to be preserved for their continued existence.

Devy, who runs an NGO working for Denotified Nomadic Tribes, said: "There are nearly 1,600 indigenous languages in India, and 90 of these are spoken by more than 10,000 people….The languages reflect the richness of their culture and tradition that have been developed over the ages. They can be retained only if the scriptures of those languages are preserved properly."

Devy informed that at present, there are only 21 indigenous languages that receive government patronage according to the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India. These languages are promoted in schools and colleges.

Heading: Violence erupts in Fatehpura, spreads to Yakutpura - Indian Express
Content:
