The residents of the tenements built under the Gajapura Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) beat up a contractor of a private company over faulty construction in Akota on Sunday. Apart from the contractor, Chandrakant Patel, four security guards were also beaten up.

In a complaint lodged with the J.P. Road police station, Patel said that he was assaulted by a group of unidentified persons who claimed that they were residents of the colony. The group also threatened to kill him if his company did not carry out the necessary repairs.

Inspector A M Patel of J P Road police said that following the heavy showers on Saturday night, water entered many houses occupied by Below Poverty Line (BPL) families because of faulty construction. This angered the residents of the area. Moreover, eyewitnesses said a courtyard collapsed due to water seepage injuring some of the residents.

Patel stated in his complaint that he was sleeping when a group of unidentified persons came inside Priyanka Constructions, his office, and started threatening the security guards. However, police said that they are yet to arrest any resident from the area.

Heading: Gujarat a model of growth: Modi - Indian Express
Content:
Violence erupted in the communally sensitive area of Fatehpura, late evening on Sunday, when Hindus and Muslims clashed during the visarjan procession. As per unconfirmed reports, three persons were injured in the clashes that broke out at the Fatehpura Char Rasta in the walled city area. It later spread to Yakutpura and Nagarwada areas in the city, too.

The mob set fire to a a few crackers and damaged a police vehicle. Police had to do lathicharge and lob at least five teargas shells to disperse the irate mob. While there was no official confirmation, eyewitnesses said that even petrol bombs were hurled during the clash.

Deputy Commissioner of Police, North, Gangandeep Gambhir was injured when mobsters started pelting stones at policemen.

To avoid further problems, police blocked the roads leading to Fatehpura and Yakutpura. The immersion processions were also diverted towards the less problematic areas.

Heavy rains, however, played the saviour's role by dispersing the mob.

Police said that the actual cause of the riot is yet to be ascertained. "It seems some revellers coming back from the visarjan started taunting people from the other community. The opposing party reacted instantly and stone pelting started," they said.

Vadodara Police Commissioner Rakesh Asthana told Newsline, "The situation is well under our control. The remaining procession would pass off peacefully."

Heading: Congress kickstarts Gujarat Nirman Yatra - Indian Express
Content:
Gujarat has turned public partnership into a movement in the development process and thus came up a model of growth for other states, Chief Minister Narendra Modi told a gathering of the Federation of Karnataka Chambers of Commerce and Industries in Bangalore. Modi said Gujarat had made development take a paradigm shift by changing its direction to public welfare.

Addressing more than 400 industrialists and business management experts, Modi said that Gujarat was being showcased across the country as the model for growth and development. He said that in the changed times, when the definition of development has undergone transformation, competition was imperative for survival. Gujarat has achieved new parameters of growth by bringing in a qualitative change in the country's economic and social conditions through its slogan of "India's progress lies in Gujarat's progress".

He criticised the Congress and the Left for failing to achieve desired results through their socialist strategies. According to him, development model of the 21st century must be in the interest of the general public. "We have changed altogether the earlier model of state-dependent growth as adopted by past regimes and turned it into a public participation-based development mode…this has shown wonderful results in Gujarat," he said.

This, he said, saw emergence of the concepts of forensic science university, defence university, energy management university, petroleum university and children's university. He underlined success of attempts to link human development with special economic zone, special investment regions, dedicated freight corridors, and port- based global trade and using them as conduit for bridging the rural-urban gap.

Growth should also include strides in having healthy children, fight against malnutrition, sanitation, higher human development index and girls education. He said that though Gujarat and Maharashtra had their RTO checkposts across the road on the state borders, there was a vast difference in their collections. "This proves the effective recovery with a transparent mechanism by Gujarat," he said.

Heading: Metre down: City auto-rickshaws take commuters for a ride - Indian Express
Content:
Party lambasts Modi government, lauds efforts of the UPA rule in the Centre

Flagging off the Gujarat Nirman Yatra on its Vadodara leg, AICC (All India Congress Committee) secretary P Sudhakar Reddy criticised Chief Minister Narendra Modi for the statement he made in wake of the serial blasts in Delhi.

"Modi says he had advised the Prime Minister, but he has no answer to how state intelligence failed during the Ahmedabad blasts," Reddy said. Terrorism and communalism must be fought together, but the Bharatiya Janata Party and Sangh Parivar are exploiting the situation, he added.

"The arrests post-Ahmedabad blasts happened due to the cooperation of other state police and Central Intelligence," he said.

Giving details about the plans Congress has for the Nirman Yatra, Reddy said Gujarat Congress intends to reach out to the villages to propagate and publicise the achievements and schemes of UPA government.

The AICC secretary said that the UPA government has generously allocated funds to Gujarat for various schemes. "We are now demanding a white paper on various state government schemes in Gujarat," he said.

Meanwhile, Congress state president Siddharth Patel flagged off the Yatra in Ahmedabad (West) and said that true development of the state is when the common man gets the basic amenities necessary for survival.

Congress leader Shaktisinh Gohil also lambasted the state government and said that even though the Centre has given grants amounting to crores of rupees for development work, the state government has failed to utilise it.

Heading: Appeal to Centre not to pass Bill - Indian Express
Content:
Doctored fare metres not approved by the Regional Transport Office are being rampantly used to fleece passengers

Auto-rickshaws in the city are having a gala time fleecing hapless passengers with non-approved and often tampered fare metres.

The RTO (Regional Transport Office) has been denying clearance to round (Yankee) fare metres for years now, yet they are being used in the city.

On an average, around 500 round (Yankee) metres are sold every month in the city. As per the Regional Transport Office (RTO) rulebook, only flag metres are to be used in auto-rickshaws, yet most of the auto-rickshaws do not use them. Some drivers reason that local passengers insist on using the round metre instead of the flag metre.

Gagjibhai Parmar is an auto-driver operating on the Vastrapur-Satellite-SG Highway route. He explained: "The flag metre requires around Rs 3,000 whereas the non-approved round metre costs only around Rs 500. A flag metre is essential during vehicle clearance by the RTO. We can easily hire one for a single day for as little as a hundred rupees. Rs 3,000 for a metre is a costly affair for us."

There are several shops in the walled city areas of Ahmedabad were Yankee metres are manufactured and repaired. Raipur, Gheeghata, Mirzapur are the major areas were such metres are easily available. "In the past, Yankee metres used to come from Bangalore and cost around Rs 500. But now, we manufacture these metres locally and only order a few parts from outside," said Shyam Prasad (name changed), a Yankee metre manufacturer in Gheeghata area.

Kiran Singh (name changed) is a Yankee metre manufacturer and repairer in the Raipur area.

He said: "I am into this business for several years now. Neither the state government nor the RTO can do anything, as they themselves are corrupt."

While using round metre is a common practice, it comes down heavily on the commuter's pocket. While most commuters believe that the flag metre is a costly affair, as it is automatic and keeps on ticking even when the vehicle is stationary at a traffic signal, the fact that most of the round metres are tampered is little known.

Anil Gaekwad is another driver who confessed to resorting to metre tampering. "Sabhi gol metre mein log yahi karte hain. Metre ka her-pher to city mein karvana bahut aasan hai. (Every driver does a little bit of tampering. It can be easily done in the city area)," he said.

The Gujarat Auto Rickshaw Drivers Action Committee president, Ashok Punjabi, recently went to the Regional Transport Officer with a proposal to either not have metres at all, or put a check on the shuttle system (where many passengers share an auto and pay a fixed fare without going by the metre).

"It's true that many drivers take a flag metre on rent to get an RTO approval, but the shuttle system is ruining the business of the drivers who sweat it out without indulging in tampering. They then tend to turn to Yankee metres. In fact, both drivers and passengers have still not adjusted with the flag metres," he said.

He added: "As of now, there are around 82,000 auto-rickshaws in the, but only five per cent use flag metres."

When contacted, A B Gor, the Regional Transport Officer, Ahmedabad, said that he is yet to receive any public complaint about the matter. Also, no auto-rickshaw has been booked for not having a flag metre. At present, 45,000 CNG auto-rickshaws are registered with the RTO.

"Though we have been very strict in approving the vehicles, auto-drivers seem to have flouted the rules. Every day, 20-25 chalans are issued to auto-drivers who do not have flag metres," he said.

About the local manufacture of Yankee metres, Gor expressed ignorance about it. "If we receive any complaint about any such unit, we will surely take strict legal action against them," he said.

However, when asked about the course of action they will take to tackle the issue, Gor said: "We will now have to keep records and details of each flag metre. We will cancel the permits after issuing a notice in case the auto drivers fail to comply."

Heading: No threat to Australia tour: BCCI - Indian Express
Content:
Police are the biggest organised gang of criminals, says lawyer quoting an Allahabad High Court judgment

Speakers at an anti-GUJCOC rally organised here on Saturday asked the central government not to accept the demand of Chief Minister Narendra Modi for passing the GUJCOC (Gujarat Control of Organised Crime) Bill, 2003, maintaining that it was a draconian piece of legislation.

Addressing the gathering at Sardar Baug, leading advocate Mahesh Bhatt said unrestricted power could not be given to police as senior police officials, including IPS officers such as D G Vanzara and Dinesh M N, had been allegedly found misusing powers for staging false encounters.

Quoting an Allahabad High Court judgement of Justice Anand Narayan Mulla, Bhatt described police as the "biggest organised gang of criminals" and said unrestrained power given to them would not be in the interest of society. GUJCOC Bill, which contained provisions empowering police without any restrictions, should not be passed by the Centre, he demanded.

"Crime and terrorism can never be controlled by the law. Despite the existence of POTA, the attack on Parliament did take place in New Delhi. Similarly, Akshardham temple in Gandhinagar was attacked. POTA could not stop such attacks," said Bhatt.

Representative of Jan Sangharsh Manch (JSM) and advocate Mukul Sinha said Modi's justification for asking for GUJCOC Bill in relation to the trial of the accused of July 26 serial blasts was hollow and misleading since even if the President gave assent to the Bill, then too the law would not be applicable to the July 26 blast incident because no criminal law could be enforced retrospectively.

Others who spoke on the occasion included activist Ibrahim Sheikh, Iqbal Mirza, Anmrish Patel and Shamsuddin Peerzada.

Organisations that took part in the demonstrations included Jan Sangharsh Manch, New Socialist Movement, Jamaat-e-Islami, Aman Samuday, Jamaat-e-Ulema, Bharatiya Muslim Mahila Samiti, Aman Samuday and Ahmedabad Muslim Women Association.

Heading: Vadodara records 47 mm rainfall this weekend - Indian Express
Content:
The Indian Cricket Board on Sunday asserted that the serial blasts in Delhi will have no bearing on Australia's Test tour of India, which would go ahead as scheduled.

After the Capital was rocked by a series of five blasts on Saturday evening, Cricket Australia (CA) said it was considering the option of sending a security team to India before taking a call on the four-Test tour next month.

BCCI secretary Niranjan Shah, however, asserted there was no threat to the tour. "I have not heard about any communication from Australia and I don't think there will be any change in the tour schedule," Shah said.

"I hope Australia understands our position. The situation is normal and the Australian tour to India will go as per schedule," he said.

On CA's plan to send a security team to India, Shah said, "If there are any concerns, a security team will come. I don't think the Australian team will have any problem in coming to India."

Heading: ‘Last spell of monsoon in next 48 hrs’ - Indian Express
Content:
Rains lashed central Gujarat with Vadodara recording 30.2 mm rainfall on Saturday and 16.8 mm rainfall on Sunday.

The city will witness heavy rainfall in the next 12 hours, predicted officers at the Meteorological Department.

In Kheda district, Kathla (918mm), Kapadvanj (911mm), Mahuda (817 mm) and Kheda (698 mm) recorded the highest amount of rainfall through the weekend. Across Anand district, most areas on Sunday remained dry except for Umreth with 3 mm rainfall and Tarapur with 5 mm rainfall. Saturday recorded moderately heavy rainfall in Anand with Petlad (628 mm), Khambat (580mm) and Sojitra (532 mm) receiving the highest amount of rains.

No major cases of waterlogging were reported from central Gujarat. However at 1.30 am, a tempo carrying goods from Pavagard and going towards Surat skidded at Jamva Bridge. Two persons were injured in the incident.

Heading: 4 revellers meet watery grave during visarjan - Indian Express
Content:
With the monsoon just a fortnight shy of completing its annual June to September journey, the recent rainfall in most parts of the state may well be one of the final bursts for this season, say officials at the Meteorological Department.

The rain-laden winds lashing out over most of south Gujarat, Saurashtra and Kutch, and also parts of north and central Gujarat, are expected to engulf most parts of the state with heavy to very heavy showers within the next 48 hours, according to the latest forecast released by the Indian Meteorological Department (IMD).

An IMD officer said: "Satellite pictures show dense clouds covering coastal Gujarat, Saurashtra and Kutch. In the next 48 hours, they will travel further and cover the rest of Gujarat. So, while rainfall will gradually decrease over south Gujarat, Saurashtra and Kutch, it will increase over the rest of the state."

The rains this time had to traverse less, coming from a spate of torrential activity over the Arabian Sea, instead of taking the more conventional route of crossing the country from over the Bay of Bengal.

For the state that has been witnessing dense but scattered showers this year, this late gust of rain winds has come at just the right time for the standing kharif crop.

Dr K A Thakkar, director, board of education, Sardar Krushinagar Dantiwada Agricultural University said: "These showers are very timely for the standing crop and were the need of the hour. However, very heavy cyclonic rainfall at this stage may damage standing crops as well. There have been showers like the one yesterday. The farmers would not want more of it."

According to the IMD officer, the main difference between the monsoon season this year and the previous year is the scattered rainfall pattern. An officer said: "This year, rainfall has been very scattered. Last year witnessed the golden monsoon, which was very evenly distributed."

Though the exact study of rainfall pattern this year vis-à-vis the previous year is still to be completed, the IMD had predicted normal monsoon over the western region that includes Gujarat.

Heading: Statues at traffic circles to make way for BRTS - Indian Express
Content:
The festival of Lord Ganesha was marred by four incidents of death by drowning and a minor incident of violence near Mohan Cinema in Asarva area in Shahibaug, on the last day of the ten-day festival on Sunday. While two persons sustained minor injuries in the scuffle that broke out in Asarva, overall, the event passed off peacefully amid tight police bandobast across the city.

The victims are believed to be revellers who may have drowned during immersion, police said. Till reports came in, the victims were yet to be identified although four cases of accidental deaths have been already registered with the police.

According to Inspector J N Parmar of Shahibuag police, an altercation ensued between two groups of revellers from Bapunagar and Mohan Cinema areas respectively, over a trivial issue. Cops on duty, however, intervened and controlled the situation. "Two persons were injured and are under treatment at the V S Hospital," Parmar added. Earlier, Ahmedabad Fire and Emergency Services (AFES) personnel had on Sunday afternoon, fished out four bodies — three from Sabarmati River near Vasna Barrage, Paladi and Jamalpur, and one from the Kharikat canal in Ayodhya Nagar.

Heading: Pakistan captures 16 Indian fishermen with three boats - Indian Express
Content:
While some statues will be removed and relocated, the huge roundabouts guarding other statues will be redesigned and shortened in consultation with the traffic department

The statue of Sardar Patel at the well-known Sardar Patel diamond market in Bapunagar will no longer be a regular sight for Amdavadis. For, the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC) Standing Committee has decided to remove the statues of eminent personalities from traffic circles across the city to ensure smooth passage of traffic and make way for the ambitious Bus Rapid Transit System (BRTS) project.

At a meeting with other senior officials, the Standing Committee announced that all the existing statues that restrict traffic will be relocated to appropriate areas.

"We need to change a lot of things before the BRTS is launched in the city. We will need wider roads. The circles and statues on the roads distract the traffic flow. The statues lead to local problems in the city, as there are a lots of emotions and political importance attached to them," said Asit Vora, Chairman of the Standing Committee, AMC.

While some statues will be removed and relocated, the huge roundabouts guarding other statues will be redesigned and shortened in consultation with the traffic department.

The statue of Sardar Patel in the diamond market will now be shifted to Vijay Char Rasta. The Jivranjani Circle, which has a statue of Rani Lakshmi Bai (Jhansi ki Rani), will be shortened. Work is also underway at the Ellis Bridge Circle, which has a statue of Swami Vivekanand. The much-debated statue of Dindayal Upadhyay will now be installed in the triangular island formed at Kankaria.

"We will remove the statues after the consent of the concerned political authorities. We are not doing this to hurt the sentiments of the people. With new infrastructure projects coming up, our city's infrastructure will change. Statues of eminent personalities, like the statue of Indira Gandhi at Ropalee will be removed only with the consent of the Congress," said Manubhia Kathrotia, Chairman of Roads and Building Committee of AMC.

There are 41 traffic circles in Ahmedabad out of which some have statues. The Traffic Police (Planning) believes that the roundabouts in the city are sensitive areas where anything ranging from minor traffic issues to serious accidents can take place.

"The bigger circles in the city lead to traffic congestion. The big circles can also result in mishaps. The statues do not create problems if the circles surrounding them are small. We have always been ready to shorten the circles so that the drivers can drive safely in such areas," said Kishorsinh Ghelda, Inspector (Traffic).

AMC officials said that in future the statues will be installed only at the corners of the roads or at places where the traffic flow will not be obstructed. Statues will be placed in these areas only after the consent of the AMC Standing Committee and Traffic Police.

Heading: 4 unclaimed bodies found in city - Indian Express
Content:
Pakistan Marine Security Agency (PMSA) captured 16 Indian fishermen and three boats off the coast of Jakhau in the Arabian Sea on Saturday night. While the boat owners are all from Porbandar, the captured fishermen are from various parts of Gujarat.

According to Manish Lodhari, president of the Gujarat Cell of the National Fish Forum, the total number of boats and Indian fishermen captured by Pakistan in the last two years now stands at 372 and 392 respectively.

"We came to know from our sources in Pakistan this morning that three boats were captured by Pakistani authorities near Jakhau in the Arabian Sea. The boats are named Amivarsha Rajsinhasan, and Saptasahi. Amivarsha is owned by Babu Vija Macch of Porbandar. There were six crew members on the boat including its tandel (captain) at the time of capture. Naranbhai Lodhari of Porbandar owns Rajsinhasan. It had a crew of five. Saptasahi is owned by Syambhai Kotia. It too, had a crew of five at the time of capture," said Lodhari. He further said that some of the fishermen belong to Vanakbori in Diu, Valsad.

When contacted, Porbandar District Collector M B Parmar said: "I am waiting for a confirmation from the Coast Guard."

Meanwhile, the Porbandar Coast Guard Commandant and District Operational Officer, K L Arun, has confirmed the news. "We are investigating the matter," he said.

Heading: Delhi blasts end a Gujarat dream - Indian Express
Content:
Four unclaimed bodies have been recovered from different parts of the city in the last 48 hours.

Around 9.45 am on September 13, an unidentified body was found in the compound of the RMO, Civil Hospital at Shahibaug. A case has been registered with the Shahibhag police station.

The same day, around 4.45 pm, Sabarmati police found the body of one Raghunath Bareva near the Jawahar Chowk Municipal School. As per the police, the man died of health reasons. Two more unclaimed bodies were found by Ellisbridge police on September 14. One of them was recovered from the Sabarmati River near Rahima Slum at 7.25 am. As per the police, the deceased was about 30 years of age.

Another body was recovered from the Sabarmati near the PTC College Road at 11.15 am. The dead person was aged about 40. Police are investigating the deaths.

Heading: Gujarat ATS may soon leave for Delhi - Indian Express
Content:
Harshad Vishaka, a resident of Anand Lok Society in Nizampura, never thought that his daughter, Kamini's dream of working in the national Capital would actually lead to her end. A computer engineer from Vadodara, Kamini, 24, was killed in the serial blasts that rocked New Delhi on Saturday, when one of the bombs exploded in Central Park in Connaught Palace.

Kamini, who recently finished her engineering from MSU Faculty of Engineering and Technology went to the Capital looking for a job. On Saturday, she and her friend Kashyap Rawat, who is in a critical condition at the Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, had gone to take a stroll in the Central Park after giving a job interview in the Federal Bank.

Kamini's family, comprising her father, a younger brother and sister, has now left for the national capital to bring back her remains. Kamini's mother passed away a few years ago while Kamini and her siblings were still studying.

Meanwhile, Rawat's relatives are at the Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital. A resident of Officer's Enclave in Salatwada area, Ravat and Kamini were classmates and had applied to the Federal Bank for a job.

Heading: Adieu, the lord of business - Indian Express
Content:
The Gujarat Police announced on Sunday that it may send a special team of the state Anti Terrorist Squad (ATS) to New Delhi soon, a day after five serial blasts rocked the national Capital.

The police also said that they are in constant touch with their counterparts in New Delhi and may leave for the Capital soon.

"We are in touch with the Delhi ATS and are keeping a close watch on the developments there. If required, a special team of ATS will be sent to New Delhi soon," said Ajay Tomar, chief of Gujarat ATS.

Meanwhile, Gujarat Chief Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday declared in Bangalore that he had warned Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and National Security Adviser, M K Narayan, about the terrorists' plan to attack New Delhi.

Modi had earlier told mediapersons in Bangalore that the interrogation of the accused in the Ahmedabad serial blasts had revealed that the Students Islamic Movement of India (SIMI) was also planning to strike the Capital and that the plan may be executed soon.

The Delhi serial blasts that left 24 dead are being linked to the July 26 serial blasts in Ahmedabad.

"This is particularly because of the similarity in the modus operandi, the explosives and the timers used in the two cases. It is quite possible that the Delhi blasts may be the handiwork of some of the accused wanted by us in connection with the July 26 Ahmedabad blasts," said a top state police officer.

Meanwhile, sources in the Police Bhavan told Newsline that a team of Delhi ATS will be arriving in Ahmedabad soon.

Heading: There wasn’t any time to lose, they were holding a ticking bomb - Indian Express
Content:
Cries of "Ganapati Bappa Morya" reverberated through the Sabarmati banks, as thousands of Amdavadis thronged to bid farewell to Lord Ganesha on Sunday, on the eve of Anant Chaturdashi.

The ten-day festival of Ganesh Chaturthi came to an end amid great pomp and revelry in the city. The heavy rains in the state and the serial blasts in the national capital could not mar the spirit of the people as festivities continued on the visarjan day. Ganapati idols of different sizes were seen afloat. Some of the idols had interestingly styled Ganesha as Lord Krishna, Lord Ram, Hanuman and even Sai Baba.

All this created a unique spectacle and attracted thousands of people to the immersion.

Preparations for visarjan had begun in the afternoon. Roads across the city were packed with trucks carrying Ganesha idols to the Sabarmati. People taking part in the processions swayed to the tunes of music.

Some people from the Sabarmati neighbourhood helped visitors immerse the idols in the river by ferrying them in their boats in return for a token amount.

"Ten years ago, we had brought home our first Ganesha idol. Ever since, we have been coming here very year. We gave away the entire amount we had received during the aarti — from the visitors at our place to this boatman who helped us immerse our idol," said Nitesh Oza, system manager of Saath.

The city of Ahmedabad has 2,000 Ganesh mandals, out of which 800 are big. This time, there were about 90 big Ganesha idols in the city. Some of the famous mandals like the ones at Bhadrakali, Maninagar, Amrewadi, Khokara, Isanpur and the eastern side of Ahmedabad, had grand celebrations throughout the festival.

"Because of the blasts, this time we did not organise cultural programmes unlike the previous years. The amount that we collect every year during the festival goes to people who need money for education, medical fees or to perform the last rites of the dead," said Parag Naik, coordinator of Shiv Shakti Yuvak Mandal.

In Surat, over 22,000 Ganesha idols came for visarjan even as police maintained strict vigil.

Fire brigade personnel, electricity officials and swimmers were present at 32 ovaras. CCTV systems were fixed at different ovaras and routes. The ceremony passed off peacefully here.

In Vadodara, situation once again went out of control in the communally sensitive Fatehpura, Yakutpura and Nagarwada areas of the walled city. The mob torched a few shops in Yakutpura even as the police tried to quell violence by lathicharge and teargas shells.

To avoid further problems, police blocked the road leading to Fatehpura and Yakutpura. The immersion processions were also diverted towards the less problematic areas.

Heavy rains, however, played the saviour's role by dispersing the mob.

Meanwhile, a man died while watching the proverbial spectacle at the Sur Sagar Lake in the evening. Raopura police said that Girish Machhi (27) drowned in the lake near the Padmavati Shopping Centre.

According to the Fire Department personnel, Macchi, a resident of Dabhoi had come to see the immersion of Lord Ganesha when he slipped from a railing and fell into the lake. Police said that the part of the lake he fell into is deep. Macchi was taken to the SSG Hospital where he breathed his last.

Heading: Security between blasts - Indian Express
Content:
Saturday, 7 pm. In a span of half-hour, all five blasts of the day had already taken place — Ghaffar Market, Barakhamba Road, Central Park and GK's M Block Market.

The police had been put on alert. The buzz was that there were more bombs hidden in the city.

At Connaught place, a four-member team of policemen had been put on the job.

Assistant Sub-Inspector Mahender Pal Singh, Head Constable PN Subhash and constables Suresh Kumar and Praveen Kumar, who were on duty at Regal Cinema, had been asked to go to the Central Park.

But before that, they decided to check the area they were stationed at. And within minutes, a suspicious polybag was detected in an NDMC dustbin outside the Regal Cinema.

"All four of us gathered to look at it. The first thing we decided to do was to ask all shopkeepers to down shutters," said Constable Suresh Kumar, who had been posted at Connaught Place for the last one year.

They opened the polybag. Inside, there was a canister, with wires attached to it and a small watch. The dial showed 12.07 am. "We became sure that it was a bomb."

The next step was not so simple. "We did not know what to do but we knew that we have to do something, as there was still a huge crowd in the vicinity," said Constable Kumar.

There was no time to call in the bomb squad. The decision had to be immediate.

"I had undergone training to defuse bombs soon after I joined the force in 1994," said Kumar, "at the moment I had only one concern, keeping the crowd safe."

Taking a long breath, they gingerly extracted the contraption. Pulling out the wires to deactivate the circuit, ASI Singh stamped on the watch to break it and make doubly sure that the timer was disabled. The remnants were put in a gunny bag and buried for the time being.

Soon after, the senior officers at the Connaught Place police station were duly informed and the National Security Guards personnel and Bomb Disposal Squad officials arrived.

Shakil Ahmed, who has a garment shop in the area and was a witness to the incident said: "It was unbelievable. They showed exemplary courage and saved many lives."

"I just want to thank my training officer," said Kumar.

Heading: Bargaining for Rs 20 landed them in hospital - Indian Express
Content:
Yet another red alert has been sounded following Saturday's blasts. But while security looks spot-on at the moment, will it last? Newsline takes stock of the situation since Sarojini Nagar blasts of 2005:

* Police was to install CCTV cameras and metal detectors in big markets. But none were in place at Sarojini Nagar and Lajpat Nagar till end of 2007. The residents and market associations had to raise funds for them.

* 27 cameras installed in Sarojini Nagar this July. Today, none work. Police blames it on a fallout with the company awarded the contract.

* Following a red alert, use of metal detectors is enforced. But it is discontinued within months.

* Frisking made mandatory at entry points to Sarojini Nagar market, but practice discontinued soon. Policemen sent on other beats. In July, market association employed private security guards.

* In Walled City, in front of Jama Masjid's Gate No 1, two metal detectors installed at the entry to the market. But they are unmanned. Cars, bicycles and motorbikes pass through the space between the two metal detectors.

Heading: Gelatin sticks in bombs, CCTVs of little use - Indian Express
Content:
In moments of tragedy, some lives can hang in balance — for as less as Rs 20.

Autodriver Karuna Singh, his left leg in a cast today, found this out the hard way when the bomb went off near the Barakhamba metro station on Saturday evening. He had spent two minutes — enough in this case — arguing with a prospective woman passenger who wanted to pay him Rs 20 less that what he had initially charged. They were both injured in the blast, his passenger critically.

Singh was trailing the road in front of the station around 6.30 pm looking for passengers. Near the garbage bin, in which the bomb had been kept, a middle-aged woman flagged him down. "She was in a hurry and asked me to drop her at Jagriti Enclave, Anand Vihar. She asked me what I would charge. I said Rs 80, but she bargained for Rs 60. We were arguing when the bomb went off to our left," Singh said, adding, "If I had agreed to Rs 60, we would have been off and reached Mandi House, far from the blast."

Singh, from Karawal Nagar, is a regular on Barakhamba. "Yesterday I was tired and looking for the day's last passenger when the woman approached me," Singh said. His left leg was pierced with shrapnel, shattering the bones. But he was concerned about the woman. "She was thrown on the road, bleeding heavily. I don't remember anything after that," Singh said.

Heading: He doesn’t know his daughters are dead - Indian Express
Content:
The key financer and conspirator of the 29/10 Delhi Blasts Tariq Dar had told his boss across the border Abu Al Qama that he has chosen targets where CCTVs have not been installed. But this time, the bombers could boast that despite CCTVs, they managed to fox the police. Karol Bagh was one of the first markets to have CCTV cameras. Its sophisticated network of 28 cameras had helped police solve a jewellery heist in 2006. But at Gaffar Market, which saw the maximum casualty, the CCTV was at least 100 metres from the spot. The camera was not working, the wires were cut and there was no footage of any sort. At the Central Park, no CCTV has been installed. At Barakhamba Road too, the CCTV, meant for traffic, was of little help. "We are studying the footage, although the camera was trained on the intersection and not on the terror site," said Joint Commissioner (Traffic), SN Shrivastava. The only footage of some value comes from Greater Kailash. "We have got a few shots of the cycle on which the bomb was kept," said a senior police officer. But the pictures are very hazy and it will be no mean feat to decipher them.

NEW BOMBS
Also, for the first time in Delhi, terrorists have used gelatin sticks to make the explosives. This was common to the explosives used in Bangalore and Ahmedabad blasts and signifies the hand of Indian Mujahideen. Gelatin sticks are highly effective as they create a hard push on the shrapnel, metal pieces and ball bearings in the bomb. The metal pieces and ball bearings pierce through the bodies of victims and cause maximum damage. Apart from gelatine sticks, all eight bombs contained ammonium nitrate (as seen in past blasts), a small analogue watch (of Prince Company) used as timer with small wires attacked to the detonators, said a police officer. The bombs were packed in small wooden boxes, were about 10 cms in size and of C shape. Similar C-shape bombs were found in Ahmedabad and Jaipur. They were kept in black polythene garbage bags.

METRO ON SCANNER
With blasts in the vicinity of the metro, Delhi government took note of metro's vulnerability to terror strikes. The CM has summoned DMRC's managing director E Sreedharan and commissioner Y S Dadwal for an urgent meeting on Monday. "We want to ensure that nothing untoward happens in Delhi Metro, which is Delhi's pride," said a senior Delhi government official.

LIFE RESUMES
Normal life, meanwhile, resumed despite the debris, police barricades and heavy presence of the media at the markets that bore the brunt of the blast. But there was hardly any shopper till late evening. At Karol Bagh's Ghaffar Market, most shopkeepers kept their shutters down. At Barakhama Road, media vans dominated the scene. Many had gathered to witness the spot.The Central Park, too, had been shut down by the police.

Heading: Police detain NGO head, family awaits his return - Indian Express
Content:
Rama Nadipat, 48, lies listless on his bed in the Orthopaedics ward at Ram Manohar Lohia (RML) Hospital with a fractured left arm and chest injuries. He refuses food, begging for news of his wife and two daughters, Pooja and Santosh.

Nurses and doctors cannot bear to tell him that his daughters are dead, fearing his condition will sink.

"Please tell me where my wife and two daughters are. Doctors told me they are in this hospital itself. Please take me to see them," he pleads.

A resident of Gali No. 42 in Karol Bagh, the site of one of Saturday's serial bomb blasts, Rama's life was shattered in a matter of minutes.

"My wife Krishna, and daughters Santosh and Pooja, were at home when the blast went off. The next thing I remember is waking up here," he says through tear-strained eyes.

Against the advice of the doctors, Rama ventured out of the Orthopaedics ward on the fourth floor around 2.30 am on Saturday night.

Inconsolable and determined to find his family, he limped around the hospital in a blood-stained hospital gown. "We convinced him to go back to the ward but please help find his family," said Rashid Khan who was there for the treatment of his brother Zahir injured at the same blast site.

Morning brought confirmed news of the death.

Rama's 17-year-old daughter Pooja was dead by the time she was taken to Lady Hardinge Medical College, "It's best not to tell him at the moment as his condition too could deteriorate," says the nurse at the ward.

His 22-year-old daughter succumbed to injuries late on Sunday evening. She too was admitted to the Intensive Care Unit at RML. "She was bought here with critical brain damage. Her skull was broken and parts of her brain got dislodged. We conducted extensive surgeries and put her on ventilator," the doctor-in-charge told Newsline.

Rama's wife is in the post operative theatre. She has just had abdominal surgery, is still unconscious and unaware of the fate of her family.

Rama says, "My daughters mean the world to me, and I bought them up like sons. Please find Pooja and Santosh. Please tell doctors I just want to see them. I will eat only after I have seen them," he cries.

At the blast site, Newsline tracked Rama's sister Kishan Devi who is unaware of the whereabouts or the family. "I know that Rama and Krishna are in RML but I do not know where the girls are," she said. She said Santosh was married, although her husband was nowhere to be found. "Pooja too was to be married soon, I don't know what has happened to them," she says. Amid the terror, it is perhaps the confusion and the uncertainty that is adding to the woes of this family.

Heading: Picking up the pieces - Indian Express
Content:
Abdul Rashid Agwan, the 55-year-old director of a non-government organisation was picked up by the Delhi police on Sunday noon for interrogation.

Agwan operates the NGO Universal Knowledge Trust from his home in Shaheen Bagh near Okhla. This association, established more than a year ago, arranges scholarships for bright students and is committed to promoting knowledge among the backward sections of society, Agwan's son Rafiq told Newsline. He said: "My father holds seminars and discussions on contemporary issues. His organisation also publishes."

Around 12 noon on Sunday, a few armed men came for Agwan, asking family members not to intervene. "They said they were the police," Rafiq said, adding that other family members — his mother Afia, and brother Taufiq — were also at home when Agwan was taken away.

The men did not introduce themselves and were harsh with the family, he said. Neither has the police returned the family's calls, or told them when Agwan would be released.

Queries with the police on Agwan drew a blank. Delhi Police's public relations officer Rajan Bhagat said: "I don't have any information on detainees. Our teams however are out, gathering information on Saturday's blasts."

Police sources said the main focus is on members of the Students Islamic Movement of India or SIMI, who might be active in the Capital. An officer said, "We shall question all people who we think can offer us leads. The police of neighbouring states have also been alerted to conduct raids on anyone suspicious."

Heading: After endless wait, relief and sorrow - Indian Express
Content:
The human cost of the blasts was high. Newsline takes a look at those who lived

Love story ends in the beginning
They were young, one from the cool climes of Pauri-Garhwal and the other from Vadodara, the city of royals. And they had a lot to look forward to. Marriage, for instance. But fate had it otherwise. Twenty-four-year-old Kamini, an engineer from the National Institute of Technology, Jaipur, was in Delhi with fiancé Rawat Kashyap, an engineer from the same institute. She had come to take a banking exam, said Kashyap's friend and colleague at Hero Honda, Akhilesh. A stroll in the Central Park proved fatal for the young woman, while 27-year-old Kashyap's neck was lacerated by shrapnel. In intensive care at Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, he awaits surgery. His father Satendra Singh was allowed to see his son only once on Sunday morning. Kamini's body, meanwhile, is being flown to Vadodara for the last rites.

All for a song
After a visit to the Hanuman Mandir on Baba Kharak Singh Marg, Shama Goel and Neha Sharma were lounging on the grass in Central Park, listening to music. When Neha (22), was ready to leave the park, her 20-year-old colleague wanted to hear one last song. The two — employees of Angel Broking Ltd — were hit the next moment by shrapnels. When she saw Shama was too hurt to walk, Neha, grievously injured herself, ran for help. Shama is now on ventilator support. Neha needs to be operated upon. Her relatives had to conceal the seriousness of her condition from her ailing parents. Her mother, a heart patient, had fainted on Saturday night on hearing about the blasts. Her father suffers from asthma. Their colleagues are keeping vigil at the Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital.

What's in a name?
For 26-year-old Raju, it was a day like any other. Except that he was driving a hearse full of the bodies of blast victims to the Lady Hardinge Hospital for postmortem. The Bhai Dayal Singh Charitable Trust ferries and cremates 15 to 16 bodies free on a regular day. This Sunday, their vans are busier. Till noon, they had delivered eight bodies to the hospital from the mortuary of the Ram Manohar Singh Lohia Hospital. Two Sikh men, dressed in crisp white kurta-pajamas, who appeared to be in charge, were loading five bodies on to a truck. Asked what were the names of the deceased, one of them said, "hum sirf kaam karte hain, naam nahi lete".

Heading: Five-yr-old’s close brush with terror - Indian Express
Content:
At one hospital, a long wait ends in part relief, part dismay when friends and relatives finally get to know of the fate of two women injured in the Ghaffar Market blasts.

Both will survive, but one with just one leg and the other possibly with one eye, and certainly with a face scarred for life.

At another hospital, two friends mourn the death of a third and worry about a fourth, who is unconscious. They also worry how they can contact the family of the friend they have lost; all they know is that he hailed from UP.

At a third hospital, a brother spends the night looking for a sister, who had gone shopping at Connaught Place. By the time news arrives that she is safe, it is morning; he has gone through a wait he would remember for the rest of his life.

For those uncertain about what has happened to friends and relatives, the wait can be no less agonising than the trauma the injured will face.

One such group spends eight hours at Ganga Ram Hospital, refusing to leave till they know for sure what will happen to Promila Gulati and her daughter-in-law Sonia.

Sonia's husband finally brings the news: his mother and wife are both badly hurt but alive. Yet the tearful family hugs each other, relieved that both women are alive.

Dr S B Byotra later confirms it, "The mother-in-law has lost a leg and the daughter-in-law's face is swollen. Until tomorrow we can't say whether or not she has lost an eye."

Promila (61) and Sonia (31), residents of Kirti Nagar, had gone shopping to Ghaffar Market. They were close to the bomb that exploded.

Sonia, who joined a recent job at Delhi University, has a three-year-old daughter, Gaurika. She was at home when her mother and grandmother went shopping.

At Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, Satish Singh lies unconscious in the neurosurgery ward. His oblivion is offset by the worries of his two friends.

They have suffered minor injuries but lost another friend, Arun Kumar. Now, they wonder how they can contact Arun's family in Azamgarh, UP.

The four friends were shopping at Palika Bazar when the blasts hit them. Arun Kumar was dead by the time he was taken to the hospital; no one knows his family.

"All we know is that Arun (27) was a resident of UP. We are trying to get in touch," a hospital employee says.

Satish, injured in the head, has lost sight in one eye. "I was chatting with Satish minutes before the blast," says brother-in-law Anoop Singh.

At Lady Hardinge Hospital, N Sochoba looks for his sister, who had gone shopping to Connaught Place. He also searches at Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, again without result.

It takes all night before N Monalisa finaly calls up her brother to say she is alive; she spent the night at a friend's home but could not contact Sochoba since her mobile battery had gone dead.

Brother and sister are from Manipur and staying in Delhi, he as a student, she as an employee with the HCL call centre in Noida. Sochoba describes what he went through: "I and two friends, Leonardo and Iggu, first went to RML Hospital, where we were told to check at Lady Hardinge and then come back. We went there, failed to find her name on the list and then went back to RML."

Neither hospital could provide news and calls on Monalisa's cell failed to connect. It was 6 am when a friend called to say that Monalisa was at her home. Monalisa had gone there because she was scared after the blasts, but couldn't contact her brother because her battery was dead, she said.

Heading: Post-blasts, Ramzan bazaar loses spark - Indian Express
Content:
Five-and-a-half-year-old Sudarshana, Khushi to her parents Shweta and Sri Rang Jha, looked around in the trauma centre at Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital (RML), at the bodies and the open wounds, taking in the atmosphere of pain. The only child around, she sat beside her parents, who had been injured at Central Park, Connaught Place, when a bomb went off on Saturday evening and watched the blood trickle from her mother's hip and her father's legs. And she began to cry.

"She was fine before we came to the hospital. She even tried to console me, but later, she herself was inconsolable," says Shweta.

Forty-five minutes ago, Khushi had been eating strawberry icecream — her favourite. The family was enjoying a rare outing, when a terrible sound rent the air. A sharp sensation on the right side of her hip made Shweta turn around. Behind her, a woman fell to the ground.

At first Shweta thought Jha was unhurt, but shrapnel had punctured his leg in places. "Those who were seated suffered injuries on their faces and upper bodies. Fortunately, we were not that close to the impact zone. People behind us were mostly dead and the ones ahead were unhurt," says Jha, 35.

A constable arrived at the scene and was hailing an autorickshaw, when a young man offered to ferry the couple and the child to the nearest hospital in his Indica.

At RML, the couple was promptly administered injections and painkillers, and by 12:30 in the night, headed back home in Dwarka sub-city, where Jha and Shweta teach Human Resource Management at the Apeejay School of Management. They have to go back to hospital on Wednesday to get the embedded shrapnel removed surgically, but they are not complaining. They cannot forget scenes of terror at the trauma centre, where most other patients were fighting for their lives.

Heading: Scars, trauma remain for 2005 blast survivors - Indian Express
Content:
The stalls were weighed down with food items and shopkeepers looked ahead to a busy Ramzan night. The iftaar went on as usual. The news of the blasts took time to spread in Old Delhi.

"People hardly watch TV during Ramzan, and around iftaar time they were busy with the preparations," said Nooruzzama, a shopkeeper in the busy market of Chitli Qabar. "Here the news spread by word of mouth."

Within a few hours, however, the effect of the blasts was palpable in the bazaar. "This is a place where customers come from Okhla, Seelampur, and places quite far away," adds another shopkeeper Rehmat Ali.

"After people watched news of the blasts on TV, they chose to stay at home," said Ali. The bazaar around the stairs of the Jama Masjid, though all lit up, was empty in a new hours.

"Look at the stairs," Haji Mian Fayazuddin pointed to the almost deserted stairs of Jama Masjid on Saturday night, usually throbbing with life during Ramzan. "Sannataa hai."

Shopkeepers were also waiting for 'instructions' from the police.

Mehtab Bhai Zari Wala, president of the Bazaar Chitli Qabar Shopkeepers' Association, says, "Soon, calls will start coming from the thana about keeping extra vigil."

Another resident of Lal Quan has asked his wife not to go to the market near Jama Masjid. "Pavement-dwellers were asked to go away. I have asked my family to stay at home," said Mehtaab Ahmed.

With the Indian Mujahideen claiming responsibility, people fear the area might be tense. "In the streets, there is no tension now," says Mehtab Bhai. "Par jab zehen mein galat message jaata hai, usse halaat kharaab hotey hain."

Mehtab Bhai, however, does not think the market will affected in the coming days. "Unlike earlier, when a murder would create terror for a week, these days people remain tense only for a very short while. Then, everything gets normal. Nobody bothers."

Heading: BMW hits, injures two on KG Marg - Indian Express
Content:
DTC driver Kuldeep Singh has been glued to the television set since Saturday evening after five blasts rocked the Capital. He can't view the gory visuals of the blasts, but words are enough to remind him of his drive close to the Kalkaji bus stand in the Outer Mudrika route when he spotted a bomb and carried it to safety himself before it exploded in his face, blinding him for life.

Saturday's blasts have come as a rude shock for the 2005 Diwali blast victims, who are still struggling to pick up the threads of their lives and move on. "Neither the police nor the government have kept their promises. The police said they have arrested five people and we thought no more terror strikes would happen. The government had also promised me Rs 3 lakh as compensation but none came," a dejected Kuldeep Singh says at his one-bedroom house in DTC colony. Although he earns his bread as a vehicle examiner at Shadipur Depot, he goes to work only for attendance, since he cannot do anything.

"How many more are going to lose their sons, husbands and daughters in these kinds of blasts? If it can happen in Connaught Place and GK, which are areas under high vigilance, then it can happen just about anywhere. I have lost faith in the police," Saleena Dass says.

Dass had lost her son Michael, daughter-in-law Bubbli and grandson Alwin in the blasts three years ago. Dass (59) and her husband Bhagwan Dass (62) are bringing up their granddaughter Manisha. The entire family had gone shopping at Sarojini Nagar when the blast occurred on October 29, 2005.

And as a horrible coincidence, Dass's friend lost his brother in Saturday's blast. "I have to rush to the hospital, they have found his body," Dass says. The elderly couple are bringing up Manisha on their meagre savings. No compensation has arrived from the government for the death of Michael, since he was listed as missing.

At Shyam Juice Corner — the spot where the Sarojini Nagar blast happened — which was open on Sunday, there were hardly any customers. Three years ago, shop owner Deshraj had gone through the trauma of viewing the remains of his own brother Lal Chand, who had been ripped apart by the bomb. "Life moved on after that and things had just come back to normal. But with yesterday's bomb blasts, it is again the same scare and the same empty markets," said Deshraj. As the news of the bomb blast spread at 6.30 pm on Saturday, Deshraj once again rushed to down the shutters, while the market emptied out with alacrity.

Not far from Sarojini Nagar, Indu Poddar and her husband Vinod Poddar are limping back to life. In 2005, the couple lost their seven-year-old son and Vinod, his right leg. Just a fortnight ago, he had resumed work at the Supreme Court where he works as a court attendant, after being fitted with an artificial limb. "I am scared every time any of our family members steps out of the house. We hate going to markets or even socialising. Our lives have changed forever," Indu Poddar says.

Heading: Man, help held for Lado Sarai murder - Indian Express
Content:
Barely three days after the BMW accident on the BRT corridor in Lajpat Nagar that killed Anuj Chauhan, another BMW was involved in an accident on Kasturba Gandhi Marg on Sunday. The car, which was not speeding, hit a bike at a busy intersection close to Max Mueller Bhavan and injured two people.

A complaint has been registered at the Parliament Street police station and the driver of the car has been detained.

The owner, Varun Malhotra (24), helped the police take the victims to a hospital after the accident. Speaking to the media, he said, "We were not speeding, and the traffic light at the crossing was not working."

Tarun (26), who was driving, has sustained minor injuries, while his wife Anita (23) who was riding pillion, sustained injuries on the head, neck and back. She is currently admitted at the Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital.

Malhotra's driver Rupesh was driving the car (DL4CNA1290). Malhotra is a resident of Rajouri Garden. A case has been registered under Sections 337 and 279 of the IPC, the District Commissioner of Police said.

Tarun and Anita are residents of Durgapuri Chowk in the Trans-Yamuna area.

Heading: Two sisters from Jharkhand allege rape by placement agents in S Delhi - Indian Express
Content:
South District police has arrested P K Khuntia of Lado Sarai and his domestic help Aman Seth on charges of involvement in the murder of his wife Rekha on September 11.

Aman had made a PCR call on Thursday about 10 am and informed the police about having discovered Rekha's body inside her office-cum-residence at Lado Sarai. He told the police he had found Rekha's body on the floor after he returned from grocery shopping.

During investigation, police grew suspicious of Aman's role, as several expensive items were found missing from the house. Upon sustained interrogation, Aman broke down and confessed that Khuntia wanted his wife murdered as he suspected her of having 'relations' with her clients and friends. He had persuaded Aman to join the plan and promised him Rs 5 lakh. Aman had then entered the bedroom of the victim, where she was sleeping with her son, and slit her throat with a kitchen knife.

Heading: Weekend that was their last - Indian Express
Content:
Two sisters from Jharkhand were allegedly gangraped by two placement agency brokers recently. The incident has been reported from Kotla Mubarakpur area of South district where two cousins, both minors, approached the police with a complaint that two men, Sandeep and Raj, who had brought them to Delhi from Jharkhand, allegedly gangraped them. Police sources said, on the basis of the sisters' complaint, an FIR (218/08) was registered at the Kotla Mubarak police station.

"The sisters came to us on September 8 with the complaint that Sandeep and Raj had gangraped them in their office and threatened them with dire consequences if they tell anyone," said police sources.

Even three days after the FIR was registered, no arrest has been made. "As the accused have been identified, we have formed teams of police officers and sent them to different spots for raids," said the investigating officer of the case.

During investigations it emerged that Sandeep and Raj had brought these girls to the Capital first in 2005. "Sandeep and Raj used to call the victims to the Capital when they had jobs for them," a senior police officer said. "This time the sisters came to Delhi in June as they were summoned by the two. However, they failed to get jobs."

The placement agents did not allow them to return to Jharkhand and kept promising them jobs. "Last week, the accused allegedly gangraped them repeatedly and threatened them with dire consquences if they informed us," said police sources.

Sandeep and Raj who used to run their own placement agency till last year closed their office due to lack of funds and operated through old contacts. They used to bring their old known maids from Jharkhand, Orissa and other states and offer them jobs in Delhi on commission basis, sources added.

The sisters were handed over to family members who took them to Jharkhand after registration of the case. "Soon after they approached us their medical examination was done which confirmed rape," investigating officer added.

Heading: Idol Talk - Indian Express
Content:
Manoj Kr Singh, 16
Manoj had come from Patna for a holiday with his cousin Virendra and aunt Sangeeta Singh. He was staying with his aunt in Mayur Vihar and they had stopped at Ghaffar Market to shop for necessities. They had almost reached their car in the parking lot, when all three were injured in the blast.
"There were mangled bodies right in front of our car. Only after they were removed could we manage to pull out our car and head for a hospital. If only we had left a little earlier, this would not have happened," Sangeeta said, as she waited outside the ICU around 2.30 am, while her son completed formalities for the handing over of the body to the police for autopsy.
Manoj had succumbed to internal injuries around 1.30 am. "His parents are on their way," she said. Sangeeta too, sustained injuries on her hand.

Subrata Mondal, 21
Subrata Mondal (21) had gone to buy a mobile phone from Ghaffar Market with a friend.
Sanjay, his brother, is in a state of shock. "When I was first called to the Lady Hardinge Hospital morgue to identify my brother, I did see a body similar to Subrata's but couldn't identify it. I did not want to believe that my little brother, whom I spoke to just an hour ago over the phone, was dead," Sanjay says.
Subrata's face was could not be identified. Ball bearings packed into the bomb had left a hole in his forehead. When Sanjay demanded to see the body, he saw injuries all over it. While Subrata was brought dead to Lady Hardinge, his friend Sheebu Bag was taken to Dr Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital in a critical state.
After a postmortem, Subrata's body was taken to his brother's house in Usmanpur, where the rest of his family, including his mother, sister and brother-in-law, was waiting. He was cremated at the Nigambodh Ghat crematorium at 5:30 pm.
The family is originally from Domjur in Howrah and Subrata had come to Delhi to work as a craftsman at a jewellery factory. He lived in a small room with twenty others from West Bengal in the Chail Puri Gali in Chandni Chowk's Kinari Bazaar.

Rajni Gupta, 42
Rajni's 16-year-old son had been unusually obstinate last afternoon as he demanded that she drop her plan to visit her parents' place in Karol Bagh. But duty-bound Rajni, a 42-year-old homemaker and mother of two, had to see her paralysed mother and arrange for a maid, to keep her company round-the-clock.
She arrived at 2.30 pm, ensured her parents had lunch, shared pleasantries with neighbours, discussed which agency she could hire a maid from and rushed to the nearby Ghaffar Market to buy cushion covers for home.
Ritu Monga, her neighbour, who saw 'Pinky' (Rajni's nickname) taking her last steps away from home, recounted how "Pinky wanted to settle the issue of hiring a maid to look after her mother. We had a chat and she said she had to rush back home after some shopping, so she left."
"Few minutes later we could feel the impact of an explosion and I knew in an instant our daughter was caught in it."
Rajni was declared dead on arrival at Ganga Ram Hospital as she had succumbed to head injuries right at the spot. Being in close proximity to the bomb, Rajni was killed in the impact.

Babita Negi, 22
"Babita is gone. She is not coming back," wailed the grandmother of Babita Negi, 22, who died in the bomb blast at Karol Bagh on Saturday. Sitting at the doorway of Babita's house at Jawahar Market, she wept over the death of her granddaughter as relatives milled around. Inside, the mother weeps and refuses to come out.
Babita would have been alive had she listened to her mother and visited her grandmother in Tilak Nagar instead of going shopping, say relatives.
"At the last moment, Babita's friend called her up and asked her to accompany her for shopping to Ghaffar Market. Babita agreed," says Ramesh Beniwal, a close relative. While Babita died, her friend survived. "Splinters pierced her friend's shoulder. As Babita was standing in front, she died in the impact of the blast," he said.
Babita was the eldest child of the household with a younger brother and sister. Poonam, the younger sister, is 19 while the brother is 15. "Her father, Ram Chandra Singh, in government service, has not returned home," says Ramesh before breaking down.

Heading: Talking point with gaurav chopra - Indian Express
Content:
Do you have a musical background?
No, I have not got any training in music. If I sing, people would run away. But I love listening to ghazals, old Hindi movie songs as well as the recent Bollywood numbers. I often buy CDs of the songs I enjoy.

What prompted you to be a judge of Indian Idol 4?
My mother-in-law is a huge fan of Indian Idol. When I got the offer, she insisted that I accept it.

Have you followed the show earlier?
I don't watch television much. But I have seen some episodes of Indian Idol along with my mother-in-law.

All other three judges of the show-Javed Akhtar, Kailash Kher and Annu Malek-are associated with music. What's your role as a judge?
I will be commenting on whether a contestant has the X-factor. I would also be giving my extra two bits on the contestant's potential in singing. I am not the kind of person to fight, but I will definitely not hesitate to give my opinion.

Who according to you is X-factor?
There is a misconception that 'X-factor' is linked to the physical appearance. For me, it is not appearance but that one extra quality or characteristic that stands out from the rest. It is not necessary that an extrovert would stand out. Even an introverts have the ability to impress. I was suggesting that the contestants need not undergo a complete makeover. They are best as their natural selves.

Amongst the earlier Indian Idol winners, who is your favourite?
Though I saw very little of Indian Idol 3, I felt Prashant Tamang was the most deserving .

During the elimination rounds, which city did you think had potential winners?
It is a very difficult question to answer, but I feel there were some talented participants from Gwalior and Ludhiana. But I must say, the girls across the country are really great this time. I hope, for a change, one of them would walk away with the title.

What was the toughest thing to do as judge?
Saying 'no' to a participant was the toughest. I felt sad, but we had to eliminate those who couldn't sing at all. As an actor, I am used to having scripts. Initially, it was scary not having one. By now, I am very comfortable.

You said earlier, that you are not going to do films as your priority is your son.
Yes, I am still not ready to return to Bollywood as my son is just three years old and movies involve 24X7 devotion. Judging a show doesn't really demand so much of my time and I can manage both. I also do plays whenever something interesting comes up.

What about assisting your husband Goldie Behl in his projects?
His projects are his babies. During his labour pains (troubles), I take care of him which I am doing right now.

Heading: Honestly speaking - Indian Express
Content:
The actor talks about his career so far and his upcoming English movie

You have won the All Time Achievers Award recently. How has your career shaped since your first serial Lavanya in 2003?
I was fortunate to settle in the industry so quickly—seven serials in three years. I never thought I would be an actor. It was only after Grasim Mr India where I reached the final rounds that I started getting offers and then there was no looking back. After acting in Lavanya, Saara Aakash and Dil Kya Chahta Hai by end of 2005, I took a break. Very soon I was lucky to get the opportunity to work with Edward Zwick in his movie—Blood Diamond.

Which serial has given you the most creative satisfaction?
The lead role in Aisa Desh Hai Mera, which ran for eight months, was the best. It was not only because I enjoyed playing the role, but the whole environment on the sets was great and hence I felt like giving my best shot. I shared a good rapport with the director and also learnt a lot from veteran actors like Kirron Kher, Kanwaljit and Benjamin Gilani who were part of the serial.

Two movies and seven serials till date; so what's next?
I am not in a hurry to take on many projects, as I am currently doing one serial, Left Right Left, and taking part in Zara Nach Ke Dikha. I will also be seen in an English movie—The Killing Moon. The movie is a blend of action, romance and humour. As for Bollywood, I am getting offers, but I've not yet made up my mind. I am happy with television right now.

You and Narayani Shastri make a good pair on screen. How come you are competing against each other on Zara Nach Ke Dikha?
I didn't know that Narayani was in the show when I signed it. We are best friends off screen and we share a very healthy competition in this show. There are no mean tricks between us. We appreciate each other's good performance.

What are your expectations from this show? Do you think the boys will win it this time?
So far, the boys have won the maximum votes and our performance is being appreciated. So we definitely stand a chance to win.

Heading: Chatter box - Indian Express
Content:
The Moment of Truth

Star World

Wednesday, 10 pm

Rating****

What's it about?

Sometimes when asked a difficult personal question, a little lie doesn't hurt. Unless you're on the game show The Moment of Truth, and you are caught by a lie detector. The challenge is simple - answer 21 increasingly personal questions honestly, as determined by a polygraph, and win up to $500,000. Prior to playing, participants are strapped to a lie detector and asked a series of questions by a polygraph expert, who records their answers. Questions range from simple ones like Will you feed a dog instead of a homeless man to more difficult ones like Were you in love with your ex boyfriend on your wedding day and have you had sexual relations after marriage? At any time, between the polygraph and the televised game, participants can change their answers or walk away from the competition.

Who's in it?

Host Mark L Walberg is the hard taskmaster on the show. He administers the questions already answered by contestants previous to the show's taping. The prize to be won is $500,000, but what we all want to know is if it will be worth it?

What's hot?

The first season of the game show was very successful, but the second season that is currently being aired on TV has lived up to the potential of its relationship-destroying promise. The contestant on last week's episode, Lauren, decided to answer every question. Does she steal from work? Yes. Was she in love with someone else on her wedding day? Yes. Has she ever cheated on her husband? Yes! At this point, she'd accrued $100,000. But then, in what will likely be remembered as one of the all-time greatest moments in reality-show history, she lost everything on a throwaway question (turns out she doesn't actually believe that she's a good person), thus rendering her marriage-ruining confessions totally pointless. It is this uncertainty and shock value that is the highlight of the show.

What's not?

This is the only game show where participants know both the questions and the answers before they begin to play, which takes away the realness from the show. The show also has too much melodrama in it, with camera panning overhead before the right answer is announced. The female's voice making the True or False announcement with long pauses is especially annoying. The touchier questions on the show are especially revealing because participants reveal their answers in front of spouses, relatives and friends, hanging on every word and you really feel for the participants.

Should you be watching it?

For the Indian audience, this is a complete culture shock. But for those who dare to watch it are going to enjoy an hour-long package of entertainment.

Heading: Bag it - Indian Express
Content:
Debojit's Woes
Tempers are fraying faster in the Bigg Boss house these days. The latest fracas is between Debojit Saha and Raja Choudhury over some cigarettes. It seems that the inmates are already mad at Debo for holding out on ciggies and instead doling out long lectures whenever anyone asks him for one. So it must've seemed like payback when he went into the smoking zone to demand a puff himself, and ended up with a lecture from Raja. Poor Debojit couldn't react, but later in the day he instructed everyone to look for his pack of smokes which had apparently gone missing. One wonders what new drama will unfold in the house.

Shivani incognito
SHIVANI Gosain was in for a shock at the launch party of the new show Rubi on 9X. Shivani, who plays Chandni Bhabi in the show, usually dresses up in traditional clothes when she's in character. However, when she turned up at the party looking chic in an indo-western dress, none of her co-stars recognised her. It was only when the director recognised her that the others realised who she is. Shivani says, "I realised that I must be so convincing in my role that no one imagined that I have another side to me." That must have been quite a compliment, indeed.

Blogger Manav
INDIAN celebdom blogroll just got longer. Actor Manav Gohil has started his own blog in order to reach out to his global fan base and keep them updated about his life, even as he gets busier and busier with his professional commitments. He was apparently inspired by a Canadian fan who persuaded him to start blogging and thus stay in regular touch with his fans. Manav has just finished shooting for his Bollywood debut, Dharmesh Darshan's Bhanvraa, the love bee stings, which is slated for release by the end of this year.

Heading: Arranging Love - Indian Express
Content:
Income Tax Department officials conducted raids at all outlets of fast-food chain — Hot Millions — and residences of its owners on Wednesday. The raids, at two houses of Rajbir Singh — one of the owners of Hot Millions — in Sector 9 and Sector 6, Panchkula, carried on till late night.

The scrutiny of documents, property-related papers, bank passbooks, gold, vehicles and cash was still on at the time of filing of this report.

The earnings and sale documents of outlets in Mohali, Dharampur, North Park, AB's at Madhya Marg, Sector 26 and three outlets in Sector 17, including the Salad Bar, are also under scrutiny.

Also, another team of I-T officials raided the house and office of Chandigarh-based builder, Prem Lal Midha, today. Midha is constructing flats in Derabassi and is involved in numerous real-estate dealings.

Sources said I-T officials have recovered agreements of land deals worth crores of rupees executed in favour of Midha or executed by him. "The builder has been asked to explain his source of income. In case he fails to furnish a satisfactory reply, the I-T department may levy a heavy penalty on him for tax evasion," said the source.

Sources said notices had been served earlier to both Singh and Midha giving them an opportunity to declare their assets and file income tax returns accordingly.

"The preliminary scrutiny of seized documents indicate tax evasion amounting to lakhs of rupees. Details can be given only after completing scrutiny of their assets, bank accounts, income and tax returns," said a senior I-T official.

Heading: It’s a Doggie Dog World - Indian Express
Content:
Anita Jain gets candid about the husband hunt and about her memoir Marrying Anita

Several failed attempts at finding a suitable boy to marry led journalist Anita Jain to write Marrying Anita (Penguin, Rs 450)— a completely honest and reflective memoir that's already raised eyebrows in book circles around the world.

Sitting at Oxford Bookstore, Jain sips her cold coffee and pointedly tells me that the book is definitely not chick-lit. "Principally, it is a memoir. Every second book in the West is a memoir but nobody in India writes memoirs unless they're public figures," states Jain, 35, who embarked on a "grand experiment to merge the memoir with the travelogue". The experiment has been successful, reviews in the West have been favourable but things might be different in India, Jain feels. "People here are uncomfortable with talking or writing about loneliness. While the West is interested in the whole phenomenon of Arranged Marriage, here the focus of the book has been my honesty," she says.

Jain began writing about her own dating-courtship experiences when she figured out that the New York City romance scene had failed her completely, and after much thought, she boarded a plane for New Delhi giving herself a year to find a husband. As her search for the 'One' became tougher than ever before, Jain found that she was succumbing to the shaadi.com route and even then, things weren't working out.

"Men are basically the same everywhere," states Jain a tad philosophically. "There's as much sexual freedom here as there is abroad," adds Jain.

In 2005, when she came to the capital, the landscape had changed completely to malls, call centre glass offices, new clubs, pubs and jobs. Jain found herself meeting an entirely different community of people who made up the New India. "Nobody talks about the people who've made a journey from the interiors of India to come and work in Delhi. They're in the fringes, ignored and underestimated by the South Delhi social circles. But they're the ones who're responsible for the increase in the GDP every year," says Jain who has consciously given them a voice in her memoir. The book delves into the inter-play of Old and New India and contains a sharp critique of the rigid class structure in North India, while Jain shifts from one situation to another in her never-ending search for a husband.

Jain refuses to comment on her current relationship status. She's not writing another book in a hurry but she is definitely staying back in the country. "This is an exciting time to be India, so much is happening. There are no set rules for anything and it's a great place to find something wonderful to do," says Jain who would like to move to Mumbai soon and try her hand at film production. There, maybe she will get lucky finding that very elusive husband.

Heading: Boss of the Course - Indian Express
Content: Who better to deliver tips on beauty and wellness than the lady who started the size zero phenomenon, Kareena Kapoor. Clad in an indistinguishable green outfit, Kapoor dropped into the Capital to unveil a new wellness spa, the Lambency Chandan Sparsh Spa in Greater Kailash II. And she expressed her appreciation of the treatments offered there, "The slimming equipment here is non invasive. Personally, I love yoga and I've controlled my weight by turning vegetarian. I encourage you to do the same," she smiled. Kapoor appeared pale and worn out; "I was shooting till 2 a.m last night and caught the early morning flight to Delhi," she said. On the movie front, Kapoor has had some disappointments of late what with the debacle of her last release, Tashan. But now, Kapoor will lend her voice to an animation film Roadside Romeo, about a spoilt dog roaming Mumbai streets. And as boyfriend Saif Ali Khan is lending his voice to the film as well, Kapoor can't stop smiling. "I am looking forward to do an animation character. It is nice to know how people associate your voice with a particular character. Since Saif is with me in this project, it's even better," smiled Kapoor. With her 28th birthday round the corner (September 21), Kapoor claims she will be busy shooting for Raju Hirani's upcoming 3 idiots, for which she will be shooting in Ladakh. "I don't intend celebrating my birthday with Saif since I will be shooting with Aamir Khan for my upcoming film," she added. It is also rumoured that Soha Ali Khan will be designing jewellery for Kapoor's birthday. A fact the actress considers too personal to be discussed.

Heading: Silver Lining - Indian Express
Content: The next time you're trying to cut a natty figure playing golf, you can head to the newly opened Hugo Boss store at DLF Emporio Mall, which has just launched its new line, Boss Green, catering to golfers. The collection boasts of chic quilted jackets, pullovers in plaid colours, khakis and flannel trousers with French pockets— in bold colours and figure-hugging fits. So what if they're more suited to the St Andrews course? "Golf as a sport is garnering a lot of attention. So we decide to launch a mix of retro chic and funky designs with slimmer cuts," says Harish Chandra, Country manager of Hugo Boss, India. Keep a look out for the nylon rain cape paired with a matching hat. Mumbai, meanwhile, gears up for Boss Orange, an entirely different line that still manages to look decadently cool. The collection will be available by end of September and begins at Rs 5000.

Heading: Light It Up - Indian Express
Content: The four-member experimental hard rock band from Pune, Silver, is basking in their victory of the country's longest running rock competition Independence Rock. As a part of their five-city tour, this group of 20-somethings performed a set at Café Morrison on Thursday evening that had a mix of their originals and a cover like AC/DC's Big gun.
