"We are an experimental band and love to incorporate sounds of every genre including the Indian and western classical  as well as jazz. It feels nice to play to a variety of an audience across cities, and it helps getting an honest feedback," says Rishi Rai, bassist of the band, which was the Indian representation at this year's Asian Beat—a South Asian rock competition for amateur band—held in Taiwan, among bands from Indonesia, Malaysia and Hong Kong. "Interacting with musicians from different countries broadens your horizons not just about music but about its dynamics as well," says Rai, who was most impressed with the band from Malaysia that belted out a hard rock act in their traditional costume. Although next on their list is recording an album, Rai confirms that they'll wait till a good record deal comes by.

Heading: Things looking bright for Bagan, others have a catch-up job to do - Indian Express
Content: At designer home accessories store, Candle & Bloom (C&B), that's just opened at Crown Interiorz Mall, Faridabad, candles have gathered a new found opulence. A three-piece candle set (pic) weighing 800-1000 kg is priced at an astounding Rs four lakhs. "We've used imported paraffin wax and cotton wicks for these in-house manufactured candles decorated with golden glitter on top of it," says Saif Shah Nawaz, Managing Director C & B. While there are other home decorative accessories like fragranced essential oils, artificial flower arrangements, stoneware ceramics and metal art ware available as well, the candle set priced this at staggering figure has been the highlight of the flagship store.

Heading: Move over Sourav as Saurav makes waves - Indian Express
Content:
On the face of it, the Calcutta Football League (CFL) is a meaningless tournament for the clubs and the players who have their sights firmly set on the I-League and the Federation Cup.

In hindsight, it's an opportunity for the youngsters who want to make a mark in big-time football.

Mohun Bagan kept faith in youth and bagged a double whammy. Not only did they win the Premier Division title but also saw their youngsters mature fast and get ready for the bigger challenge. Credit goes to their coach Karim Bencherifa.

Skipper Baichung Bhutia barely took part in the CFL. Injuries rendered other senior players hors de combat midway through the league. The Moroccan didn't flinch. He made the game enjoyable for his wards. The relationship grew on mutual respect.

The coach turned a group of greenhorns to potential match-winners. This is his biggest contribution.

Bagan now have the advantage to go into the I-League with their back-up line ready and the seniors fit and fine. Perfect build-up for a big tournament.

Bencherifa came to Kolkata with a big reputation and bigger salary. He had all the pressure in the world to deliver. He didn't disappoint. This is the precise reason why he edges past George Telegraph's Raghu Nandy to be the top coach of this CFL.

Nandy impressed one and all with his constructive football. His boys played to win even against the big teams. With some luck they would have made a few more upsets. Still a fourth place and a chance to play the I-League qualifiers is good enough a reward for a team that started with its stake very low. The Indian Football Association (IFA) must ensure that Nandy's expertise is utilised.

Mohammedan Sporting too deserve special mention. After a long time, they are a force to reckon with. With Mike Okoro and Theodore Sunday upfront, they probably had the most potent attack. The two packed a punch. "They pushed us to limit. That helped raise our game," Bencherifa was all praise for the black-and-white brigade.

I-League, however, is a different ball game altogether, and Sabbir Ali has a job at hand ahead of the tournament. He must strike a balance between attack and defence. Else, it will be tough for them to keep the momentum going.

East Bengal looked a disjointed lot. Throughout the tournament, coach Manoranjan Bhattacharya lamented over the unavailability of his frontline players who were busy playing for India. Unlike Bencherifa, he failed to motivate the reserve bench to stand up and get counted. His replacement Stanley Rozario, completely new to the pressure and demands of Kolkata football, has his task cut out. That he shares a very good rapport with the likes of Sunil Chhetri, Renedy Singh, Surkumar Singh and other India team players is a definite positive. It should be now or never for the red-and-golds.

Apart from the Big Three, Chirag United would be the other Kolkata club to play in the I-League. They have moved in the right direction by appointing Subrata Bhattacharya as their coach. But they need some quality players to be better than the also-rans.

As for the players, Jose Barreto continues to impress. He guided the juniors on the field and off it. In crisis, he showed the way. In success, he kept a low profile. He is the best player of this CFL by a long chalk.

The emerging player award can go to George midfielder Subho Kumar. He has the skill to rattle any defence. Does he have the fitness and temperament to move into a higher level? Time will tell.

Match officials would like to forget this CFL. Players and club officials turned the heat on them at the drop of a hat. Biplab Poddar, Sunanda Bose, Rathin Mukherjee learnt it the hard way how hazardous things could be on a football ground. The IFA, which continues to work in its own amateurish way, was too weak to offer any protection.

Heading: War Zone - Indian Express
Content:
National squash champion Saurav Ghosal wins his biggest ever international title in France

At a time when Sourav Ganguly is beginning to fade away into the background, sports enthusiasts in Kolkata seem to have found a new hero to look up to — the cricketer icon's namesake, India's squash sensation Saurav Ghosal.

Riding high on his impeccable form over the past few months, 22-year-old Ghosal today went on to clinch the biggest title in his international career. The Kolkata-born youngster, who stays in England, scored a pulsating victory in the final of the inaugural Ornano International Open in Bordeaux, France. The No 1 Indian player beat third seed Davide Bianchetti in the final of the $15,000 PSA Tour squash event today.

The sixth-seeded Ghosal shocked Italian Bianchetti 11-6, 11-6, 9-11, 11-9 in the finals to secure the fourth and the biggest PSA Tour title of his career.

"I entered my name in the tournament because I wanted to see France, a place I have never been to. I didn't care about the draw. I knew I was facing some really tough players but I have been playing pretty okay for a while," Ghosal said.

"To win such a big tournament after beating players who are ranked above me is certainly very special. All the hard work that I have put in is finally paying off," the young gun said. The win in the final was the 22-year-old's third successive upset in the event.

The reigning national champion made his breakthrough in the quarter-finals when he toppled the tournament's top seed Renan Lavigne in four games, dashing hopes of the local success in the high-profile event. And then in the semi-finals, Ghosal overcame fifth-seeded Egyptian Amr Swelim in a thrilling five-gamer.

Celebrating his sixth appearance in a PSA Tour final, the four-time national champion from India faced third seed Bianchetti, who is ranked 30th in the world and is a seasoned campaigner of 18 final appearances. Ghosal and Bianchetti last met in June 2006 but Ghosal lost 1-3 in that match.

"I was better prepared and I had the speed advantage. Davide is not the fastest on the court and I used my speed well. But he raised the bar in the third game when I was too excited," Ghosal said.

"The fourth game was also very tight, but I just remained calm and managed to pull it off. I am very happy because it is a good build-up to the World Open next month," he explained.

Ghosal credited his improved fitness and game to experienced British coach Malcolm Wilstrop, who has been with him for the past three years. "My game is better now, and so is my fitness. I am play a more attacking game now and placing has improved. The credit for this goes to Malcolm. He has been with me and we have trained really hard," he said.

Heading: Fine blend - Indian Express
Content:
Shona Urvashi's Saas Bahu aur Sensex, with the distinction of being the first official film to be distributed by Warner Brothers in India, is all set to explore the stock market the woman's way

Another name added to the thinly populated list of women directors in India, Shona Urvashi with her soon-to-release flick, Saas Bahu aur Sensex, ventures into that genre of filmmaking, which relatively remains unexplored by the Bollywood directors at large. And what else could be more supportive to sail into uncharted waters than an international name such as Warner Brothers! So there she is with her experimental venture, an urban comedy drama consisting of an eclectic mix of fresh faces and a not-so-typically-Bollywood-like theme — stock market and women.

In the city for the premiere of the film, Urvashi, who also is an alumni of city's Wadia college, shares what prompted her to bring two such things together which, in real life are supposedly poles apart — women and sensex.

Providing a kaleidoscope view of modern India, the film step by step documents the process of women being inclined towards stock market. "The common notion is that women and numbers don't go together. I break this perception with my film. Here is what we have, something beyond the Saas bahu image which is so synonymous to the image of women in our country today," elaborates Urvashi.

Her main objective being the portrayal of the transition of the contemporary Indian society, Urvashi, in due course of doing so, also lays bare the factors why women, especially homemakers completely lack interest in the stock markets.

"When Richard Fox on behalf of Warner Brothers approached me to direct a film which will be a romantic comedy, I did not give it a second thought. This is what I always wanted to do. To create something that inspires but in a light way. The inspiration should come as effortlessly and as practically as it can, sans heavy words, philosophies and ideologies. This is how I make a film and that is how you will find Saas bahu… too," says Urvashi whose directorial debut, Chupke Se, also a comedy, made the audience sit up to notice her talent. The film too inspires women to take the charge and invites them to be a part of the very progressive economy of the country.

Intricately woven together with the central characters are other characters that form an inextricable part of the storyline. Nevertheless the presence of so many characters does not appear to clutter the show. "The storyline demands a long starcast and even if one character is missing, it creates a deep void. This is because I have tried my best to make the film look real and in real life you are surrounded by people. I picked up faces that were intresting but yet had that small town look to them. I did not want my characters to have the caricature feel," says Urvashi.

With no touchstone to test if in the entertainment-driven market such a film would gather an audience, this one sure seems to be trailblazer and perhaps there would be more to follow suit.

Heading: Music of the Barred Land - Indian Express
Content:
Rituparno Ghosh on The Last Lear and his reasons for taking Amitabh Bachchan for the movie

What inspired you to do The Last Lear?
I grew up seeing Utpal Dutt's Bengali play—Aajker Shahjahan and I,ve loved it since my school days.I was inspired by the storyline of the play, which revolves around a veteran Shakespearean actor—Harish Mishra played by Amitabh Bachchan, who is wooed by a movie director (Arjun Rampal) to act in his first film. The film explores Shakespeare's influence on the actor's life.

Is it a tribute to Utpal Dutt? Do you think he has got his dues?
He was one of the finest actors Indian cinema had. Unfortunately as a playwright, his identity did not go beyond West Bengal. He has done a lot of Shakespearean plays. I wanted the nation to realise his talent as a playwright. Hence I made this film. It is also sheer co-incidence that Amitabh Bachchan's first movie had Utpal Dutt in it.

Is the movie's title, The Last Lear, inspired by the great play?
The name is not linked to the play but Bachchan's ironic old man image of the character.

When a great script and storyline could make castmovie a blockbuster, why take big stars like Bachchan and Preity Zinta?
I chose Bachchan as his personality reflects the character and fits the role perfectly. I don't make movies eyeing box-office success.

This is your first movie with Bachchan. How was the experience?
His understanding of the entire environment was extremely fascinating and the moment he entered the sets, he made everyone very comfortable, adjusting beautifully with the rest of the crew.

Why did the movie take this long to release considering it was made last year?
My producers planned it this way. The movie did the rounds of the festivals. Now that my job is over, I am looking at the project objectively. If I had seen it when it was made, then I would have looked at the project with a critical eye. So in a way, it is good that I am distant from the movie at this moment.

What challenges did you face while adapting a play into a film?
I didn't face any difficulties since I have made movies based on novels.

Are you apprehensive about the recent controversies around the release of movies in multiplexes in Mumbai?
It is a very impulsive reaction, and I wouldn't wish movies to get undue publicity from any kind of cause or issue and vice versa.

Tell us about your next project Sunglasses starring Jaya Bachchan.
It is in the post-production stage now and that's all I can give away at the moment.

Heading: Suspected thief lynched in Howrah - Indian Express
Content:
It's around 3 pm at the Sa Re Ga Ma studio on Jessore Road. There's the usual hustle bustle typical to a recording scene. Eight artists, huddled in one corner choose to strain their vocal chords even during the lunch break, hoping to get the notes right on the mike. They have been at it since early morning, but their faces betray not a sign of exhaustion. Playfully taunting each other's singing skills, the group remains engrossed in their task. Maybe because, it is not just their first tryst with the mike professionally, but also their first brush with the no-nonsense air that usually hangs heavy inside a recording studio. Between the half-lights of their cells in various prisons across the state and the chill of a sleek music studio, lies a difference of a world. A difference, that these prisoners have finally managed to face, with a little help from the greatest leveller of all times — music.

Jagat Sarkar, one from the group trying to record their version of Tagore's renowned dance drama Balmiki Pratibha, calls himself a 'bathroom singer'. "I have always loved music. I used to pick up the strains of Bhatiyali and Palli Geeti very easily. But this is the first time I am singing Rabindrasangeet," says Sarkar, who hails from Bali. This would be a far cry from his early days in the prison where he was always chided for his passion for music. Rabindrasangeet is easily not a hit with inmates and except for people like Sarkar who knew a little country music, the younger inmates were usually Bollywood addicts.

The initiative, to include the inmates in a creative production, was taken by B D Sharma, IG (Prison) and danseuse Alokananda Roy. In fact, to encourage the inmates, Sharma himself lent his voice to the character of Balmiki. "The idea was to sensitise people, including the prison staff, to the inmates, who mostly regret their crimes now. That is why we decided to include the prison staff and their family members in the production. This way they would learn to respect the prisoners' sentiments," says Sharma.

Like the rest of the cast, Sharma himself had to practice regularly to perfect himself. A sense of camaraderie has developed between Sharma, the prison staff and the inmates in course of the project, admits the IG. Several from the team will also participate in the stage adaptation of Tagore's dance drama. The performance will involve around 50 inmates, both men and women.

Ranjit Das and Steven are among the younger members of the team. Given a choice they would listen to Kumar Sanu, happily giving Tagore a miss. But over the last two weeks, when they have been practicing their bits, they reveal to have understood the feeling that goes behind most of Tagore's compositions. "With his transformation from a dacoit to a saint, Balmiki's life has made an interesting example for us. To infuse soul in the songs we had to understand his emotional journey," says Das. Dancer Roy hopes, "There is no single Balmiki in this production. Rather the sinner-turned-saint is a paradigm that most of these men will end up identifying with at the end of the production."

Tagore himself directed the first production of the dance drama and he would certainly have approved of the present production team. The audio CD will be released in November this year during on the eve of their stage performance. The proceeds will go to the welfare fund set up for the prisoners' families.

Heading: Inactive Green Police make authorities see red - Indian Express
Content:
An unidentified youth was lynched by locals of Q Road in Howrah early on Sunday morning after they suspected him to be thief. Although a case of unnatural death has been filed, no arrests have been made so far, said police.

Police said that the night guards, all residents of the area, saw four men consuming alcohol under a water tank late in the night.

There had been several cases of theft in houses and small factories in the area over the last few days. The night guards suspected the four men were thieves, who had committed the robberies.

When the guards confronted them, three of them managed to flee. One youth, however, could not run away. He hid near a pond, but the guards cordoned off the area.

When day broke, locals saw the youth half submerged in the water. The youth was forced out of the water and was beaten up by the guards and the locals with his hands and legs tied up.

After thrashing the youth for over an hour, the locals fled the scene thinking that he was dead. The youth lay there for more than four hours battling for life, before the police arrived.

It took the police more than four hours to take the body to hospital where the youth was declared dead on arrival.

Police said that the identity of the deceased could not be ascertained.

"The deceased is around 28 years of age. We have not been able to identify him. We are also looking into the allegation that the youth was involved in the series of robberies in the area recently," said an officer of the Bali police station.

Heading: Congress urges CPM to follow the agreement - Indian Express
Content:
The much-hyped Green Police project, a joint venture of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) and the Kolkata police, is facing criticism from various quarters because the very purpose of deploying nearly 500 volunteers of the Green force seems to have been defeated.

The force, named Green Police by Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee, is supposed to check civic and environmental offences such as putting up of hoardings on trees, illegal cutting of trees, filling up of ponds and violation of traffic rules.

For this, the state has employed green volunteers, who are paid Rs 89 as daily wages and they are assigned work for four to five hours a day.

The salary of 500 volunteers is borne by the civic body and the volunteers are supposed to be trained by the Kolkata Police.

A civic official said the KMC has already spent Rs 20 lakh over the project. The green policemen, however, are rarely seen on duty.

A group of them can only be seen at major crossings such as Esplanade, Dalhousie Square and Park Street, though there is hardly any need for nearly a dozen Green volunteers at a crossing, where traffic police is also deployed.

The green force is never seen at several high accident-prone crossings like Shyambazar, Ultadanga, Gariahat, Gol Park and Park Circus seven-point crossing.

Deputy Commissioner (traffic) Dilip Banerjee said, "There are 244 green policemen in my department who are deployed at 30 major crossings in the city. Rest of them are assigned other jobs."

Asked about their absence at several crossings, he said, "They are supposed to be present at all major crossings. I cannot say why they are not available at some crossings."  

Sushil Sharma, MMiC (environment) said, "I have never received any complaint from the Green Police regarding unauthorised filling up of ponds."

In fact, the civic police volunteers have never reported or prevented any illegal activity. Rampant cutting of trees for commercial purpose at Jatin Das Park and on the Eastern Metropolitan bypass has gone unchecked, marking major instances of the failure of the Green Police.

Faiaz Ahmed Khan, MMiC (parks and squares and parking) said: "The civic police is supposed to provide us information on illegal felling of trees but so far they have not come up with a single complaint. There have been several instances of illegal parking. But nothing is reported to us by the green volunteers." Same is the case with illegal hoardings dotting the city.

A senior civic official said: "The green policemen are not properly trained. Several hoardings can be seen on trees in the city. If civic offences like this keep on happening, what is the use of deploying this special force."

Heading: No no Noddy, children tell the latest toon show in Kolkata - Indian Express
Content:
West Bengal Pradesh Congress Committee president Priya Ranjan Dasmunsi asked the state government to implement the agreement it had signed with the Opposition on Singur.

"It will be most undemocratic and an act of betrayal if the state government fails to honour the agreement," said Dasmunsi on Sunday.

The Union Minister for Information and Broadcasting expressed regret that the Congress was neither invited to the talks at the Raj Bhavan nor was consulted on this issue.

In a related development, the Singur Krishi Jomi Raksha Committee held a meeting at the Trinamool Bhavan and analysed the package offered by the state government to Singur farmers.

"By announcing the package, the state government has acted in an unethical and undemocratic manner. You make a commitment before the Governor but you yourself flout it," said one of the members of the committee.

Mamata Banerjee is now revamping the Trinamool Yuba Congress to take on Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI), the youth wing of the CPM, that has launched a campaign against the Trinamool Congress. "Didi will set up a committee to revamp the organisation so that it can counter the DYFI," said a Trinamool Congress leader.

Preparations are underway in Singur to gather a huge crowd for the Krishi Jomi Raksha Committee rally on September 16, which will be addressed by Mamata Banerjee.

Heading: CM appeals to Mamata for talks - Indian Express
Content:
The popular animated series says Make way for Noddy, and as the name goes, the cute wooden boy makes children stay glued to the television sets when he arrives on screen. The boy from Toyland, however, had a bumpy ride in real life, when he arrived in Kolkata in his red and yellow car on Sunday.

The musical show of the Noddy series — Noddy and the Treasure Map Adventure — got a lukewarm response from children in Kolkata, a city known for its literary tradition. Celebrated children's author Enid Blyton created Noddy, the much-loved cartoon character, in 1949. Since then, the Noddy series has been widely read by children across the world.

On Sunday, it was the first Noddy Live Show in Kolkata — the fourth city on the itinerary after Mumbai, Delhi and Bangalore. The first show saw less than one-fourth of the seats occupied in an auditorium having a capacity for 2,000 people. While the shows have run to packed houses in the other three cities, the organisers were clearly left disappointed with the turnout in Kolkata.

The organisers — a joint venture group of Delhi-based JBC (Just Because Its Children) and the Australian Millennium Entertainment International (MEI) had invested a sum of Rs 3.5 crore for the four-city tour in India.

The ticket was priced at Rs 300 for the audience in Kolkata. With the first show of the day coming a cropper, the organisers appealed to the audience to send out messages to their friends and relatives to come and watch the show.

"We had expected a good turnout for which we had booked this huge auditorium in the Science City. We are not sure if we could hold a show in Kolkata again as it may not be economically feasible," said Kavita Bedi, Managing Director (Indian Operations) of JBC-MEI.

The cast of the show was from Australia and Singapore and the show featured Noddy's friends like Tessie Bear, Big Ears, the law enforcing Mr Plod and the goblins — Sly and Gobbo. "I have been reading Noddy since I was in Class I. My favourite character is Mr Plod," said Shivika Shah, a Class IV student of the Modern High School.

"Lack of awareness about the show could be reason behind this low turnout. The steep price of tickets could also be a deterrent," said Debabrata Dutta, an employee of an IT firm who had come with his five-year-old daughter to watch Noddy.

Heading: New package leaves farmers confused - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee once again appealed to Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee to sit for talks to resolve the Singur impasse. He was addressing a gathering of SFI members in Burdwan on Sunday.

Bhattacharjee reiterated the need for immediate resumption of work at the Tata's Nano plant. "We need this project for the benefit of Bengal. I urge the Opposition to sit with me for talks. I am ready to sit for talks any day, even tomorrow if they want it," he said.

He added: "I don't want any tussle. I want a solution. We need to work together for development of the state. We need investment for creating jobs. Our youth need employment and we have to cater to their demands."

Bhattacharjee spoke about his new compensation package for the affected farmers in Singur and urged the Opposition to join hands with the government to resolve the crisis.

He said: "When I went to the Governor's place to have a discussion with Trinamool chief Mamata Banerjee, many people asked me why I did so. But I said I did not want the image of West Bengal to be tarnished. We need industry. If Tatas leave West Bengal that will affect the credibility of the state. To prevent such situation, I am ready to speak with Banerjee again."

The meeting was organised by SFI and DYFI leaders.

Heading: CPM go all out to woo Singur farmers - Indian Express
Content:
With confusion surrounding the recent compensation package announced by the state government for Singur farmers, the farming community is unable to comprehend its components. Basudeb Das, a resident of Beraberi village, said: "We do not know what the government is actually offering through this package. We expect somebody from the government explain to us everything."

Das had one-and-a-half acre land in the project area but had not accepted the compensation for the land that was acquired for the project. "This government has no credibility. I was a staunch supporter of the CPM but they snatched my land," he said.

Similar sentiment was echoed by other Beraberi farmers, who held a rally protesting against the package on Sunday.

Madan Das said: "The package is confusing. We cannot even understand whether it's fair or not. We will not stop our protest till everything becomes clear to us." He also had one-and-a-half acre land inside the project area and had not accepted the compensation.

In a related development, the Krishi Jomi Raksha Committee led by Trinamool Congress carried out a procession on Sunday that started at Beraberi and ended at Sanapara. Rabindranath Bhattacharya, Singur MLA and one of the members of the 4-member committee that was set up by the government to settle the land issue, was present at the rally.

He said: " We asked the government to return the land that is lying unused within the factory but they turned down our demand." Expressing his dissatisfaction with the new package, he said, "This package offers nothing. This is not something we have been fighting for the last three years."

A group of farmers at village Joymollah, however, was all praise for the package.

Madhusudan Santra, whose eight kottahs of land was acquired, said, "It's the best package that we could have got. Nowhere in the world has such package been offered to farmers. I hope all those who did not

receive compensation should accept this package." Santra is among those farmers and construction workers, who have been sitting at a dharna in support of the Tata factory near Joymollah village.

Meanwhile, CPM state secretary and Left Front chairman Biman Bose urged all farmers of Singur to accept the fresh rehabilitation package and join hands in the implementation of the Nano project.

He praised the state government for the new package and said it will benefit farmers, landless agricultural labourers and other people of Singur.

Heading: Railway police deploy flying squads to patrol  Metro platforms - Indian Express
Content:
Hours after the Left Front government announced a special package for farmers in Singur unhappy with the forcible acquisition of their lands for Tatas' Nano project, the CPM is leaving no stone unturned to woo the disgruntled farmers.

Local CPM leaders and party workers conducted a day-long campaign in villages around Singur — Beraberi, Khaserberi, Singherberi, Joymolla, Gopalnagar, all known to be strongholds of the Trinamool Congress controlled Singur Krishi Jomi Raksha Committee (SKJRC) — to ensure a good turnout at Left Front's rally on Monday.

CPM leaders claimed that a section of farmers, who had been opposing the Left Front over the last two years, has accepted the fresh package proposed by the state government.

Agricultural labourers and sharecroppers are also happy with the new proposal as "it takes care of their interests", claimed CPM leaders.

Dibakar Das, CPM Hooghly district committee member, said several farmers, who had left the CPM camp following the land acquisition in Singur, have decided to attend the Front's rally.

Many of them have even participated in a dharna on Saturday that was organised by farmers demanding immediate resumption of work at the Nano factory, Das said.

"We hope that the thousands of people from Singur, who were misled by the Trinamool Congress, will attend tomorrow's rally. The Trinamool Congress has started losing ground at Singur," claimed Das. Local DYFI supporters and women belonging to Paschim Banga Ganatantric Mahila Samity participated in the campaign and urged the agitating farmers to accept the fresh compensation package announced by the state government.

The SKJRC, on the other hand, took out a rally from Beraberi village in Singur to keep its support base intact. They organised a rally at Beraberi, a village known to be the epicentre of the anti-land acquisition stir in Singur, and urged people not

to fall into the "trap laid by the CPM by accepting the package."

"We have told the people of Singur that Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee has betrayed Trinamool chief Mamata Banerjee by flouting the agreement that was signed at the Raj Bhavan in the presence of the Governor last Sunday. The people of Singur are convinced by our argument. Our support base remains intact. Not a single SKJRC supporter will join the Left Front rally tomorrow," claimed Manik Das, a senior SKJRC member.

Heading: Miles away from Delhi, Domjur family scarred by Saturday’s blasts - Indian Express
Content:
Coaches and platforms of Metro railway, which have been lying unmanned, will now be patrolled by flying squads of security personnel. Each squad will comprise four to five RPF personnel besides one metro rail personnel, and will have two or three stations under its jurisdiction.

The team will board the first station and disembark on reaching the third. After this, they will take the return train. For 17 stations, there will be five flying squads. "This will ensure that all the trains and stations are covered," said a senior official of the Metro Railway.

A day after the Delhi blasts, senior officials of both the Eastern Railway and Metro authorities held an emergency meeting.

In the suburban EMU section, sniffer dogs will be pressed into service to monitor all the coaches including sleeper coaches. Until now, sniffer dogs were only deployed for AC and general coaches.

The number of entry and exit points will be kept to the bare minimum in both the Sealdah and Howrah stations to ensure proper monitoring of commuters.

Car and bicycle parking lots will now be under strict vigilance. The authorities are even thinking of hiking up the charges at the parking lots to discourage parking.

Heading: Delhi blast ripples in city, security on its toes - Indian Express
Content:
Twenty-three-year old Subrata Mondal had gone to Karol Bagh in New Delhi on September 13 to buy a cellphone for his mother so that he could frequently speak to her. Little did he know what fate had in store for him when he arrived in the area. Minutes later, he was ripped apart by the explosion.

Mondal, a resident of Maitypara in Domjur area of Howrah, had been working as a goldsmith in Delhi for the last seven years. His elder brother Sanjay owns a shop at Karol Bagh.

A few days ago, his mother, who still lives in their ancestral home in Domjur, lost the cell phone he had given her. The phone was a prized possession for her, as it was the only means of communication between her and Mondal, who visited home only once a year.

Realising he had not spoken to his mother in a long time, Mondal took a half day's leave from work and went to Karol Bagh to buy a new handset for his mother.

"He had bought the phone and was about to catch an auto back to his Shastri Park residence when the blast occurred," said Ira Mete, Mondal's sister-in-law.

The news of his death reached his family in Domjur around 4:30 am on Sunday. Sanjay called up a neighbour in Kolkata and informed him about Mondal's death.

"The neighbour told me about his death but I decided not to tell his mother. She was told that Subrata was sick and had to be admitted to a hospital," said Kushodhar Mondal, the victim's uncle.

Though it was beyond their means, relatives pooled in money and one of them took Mondal's mother to Delhi by air this morning.

"Though we had not told her, she understood that something bad had happened to her younger son. She kept on crying and asked us repeatedly if we were hiding something from her," said Nobokumar Mondal, another uncle of Mondal.

The news has shattered Mondal's relatives, who had high hopes on him. "We do not have any children. He was like a son to us. I had dreams that Subrata would look after us when we were old and not able to work anymore. Look what has happened," said an inconsolable Nobokumar, clutching Subrata's picture close to his heart.

Blast has a victim in Singur too
KOLKATA: Shibu Bagh, a 28-year-old youth from Singur, was injured in Saturday's blast in Gaffar Market in Delhi. Hailing from a farmer family, Shibu is battling for his life at the Ram Monohar Lohia Hospital in New Delhi. One of his hands was blown up in the explosion. Shibu had gone to Karol Bagh in New Delhi nearly two years ago to work in a jewellery shop, and was walking along a road near the market when the blast took place. Shibu's employer informed his family at Chowkhandipota village near Singur over telephone on Saturday night that Shibu was admitted to the RML Hospital in a critical condition with severe burn injuries. The victim's brother, who works as an agricultural labourer, rushed to Delhi on Sunday morning. His family members said Shibu was scheduled to come home next month.
— ENS

Heading: Tata Motors lauds CM’s effort, Mamata sticks to her guns - Indian Express
Content:
The blasts that ripped apart the national capital on Saturday have sent panic bells ringing in Kolkata as well.

Following the Delhi blasts, the Kolkata Police officials are not ready to take any chances with the security arrangements. With Durga Puja around the corner, the have braced themselves up to provide a safe festive experience to the people.

Police Commissioner Gautam Mohan Chakrabarti, made rounds of the various malls of the city on Sunday evening to oversee the security arrangements.

An alert has been sounded in Kolkata after the Delhi blasts and security at vital installations has been beefed up. Police are, however, worried about the security in the marketplaces, as Saturday's blast in Delhi and the ones in Jaipur had taken place in busy market areas.

Although Kolkata is not on the list of terrorist organisations and there is no specific threat to the city, the officials are on their toes, scanning through the malls and market areas, given the fact that Puja shopping has picked up over the last few days.

"Most of the malls have their own security personnel. Though there are some shortcomings, like retired police personnel being recruited as guards, the malls are trying their best to meet the security standards stipulated by us," said Vineet Goel, DC (Headquarters).

He added that DCs of the five divisions are making regular rounds and special teams have been constituted for making random security checks.

"These teams will move around the city and conduct sudden checks. Plain-clothed policemen have been asked to make rounds of busy markets," said Goel.

"People should also co-operate with us. If anyone sees any suspicious object lying unattended, he/she should immediately inform the nearest police booth," he said.

Heading: Man found laying sewerage pipe without nod - Indian Express
Content:
Tata Motors on Sunday came out in support of Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee whose offer of a fresh package for farmers whose land was taken has been rejected by Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee. In a press statement issued by the company, the Tatas appreciated the package offered by the state Government and said it was hopeful that the initiatives would generate favourable response from the farmers, creating a positive atmosphere in Singur.

The statement comes at a time when Banerjee has already rejected the fresh rehabilitation proposal. The Left Front is organising a rally in favour of the Nano factory at Singur on Monday and a counter rally is scheuled to be held by the Singur Krishi Jomi Raksha Committee near the plant on the following day.

In the statement issued by Tata Motors spokesperson from Mumbai on Sunday, the company said: "Tata Motors appreciates and supports the recent initiatives of the Government of West Bengal for the residents of Singur area where it had acquired land for Tata Motors' Nano project."

The statement also re-confirmed the company's objective of setting up the Nano factory in Bengal.

"Tata Motors decided to set up its Nano plant at Singur to play an active role in the re-industrialisation process of the state of West Bengal and make a contribution to the economic development of the region," the statement said.

It also stated that Nano factory is also aimed at providing direct and indirect employment opportunities for the people of Bengal and the company is keen to participate in the overall community development in Singur. The statement also highlighted that Tata Motors is hopeful that farmers will accept the fresh package and thus a congenial atmosphere will be created. "Tata Motors hopes that these initiatives will evoke a positive response from the residents of Singur and that all stakeholders will contribute to create a congenial environment conducive to the long-term sustained operations of an industrial enterprise," the statement added.

On September 12, Bhattacharjee proposed fresh initiatives for Singur, including a fresh rehab package for the affected farmers. The proposal stated that 70 acres of land would be returned from within the project area, all dispossessed farmers both willing and unwilling get an extra 50 per cent of the compensation, 300 days wage for unrecorded bargadars and wage labourers, government jobs to each of the family with in a year, community development by way of setting up schools, roads, hospitals in villages surrounding the project area and other benefits. The offer was rejected by Mamata Banerjee.

On Sunday, the Krishi Jomi Raksha Committee held a rally at Beraberi which was addressed by Trinamool Congress MP Mukul Roy and TMC legislator from Singur Rabindranath Bhattacharya. "This is not something we have been fighting for," he said.

Heading: 6 fresh cases of suspected dengue - Indian Express
Content:
A man was found trying to lay sewerage pipe without permission from the authorities in the market opposite Nav Durga Mata Mandir in Sarabha Nagar on Saturday. He allegedly had an MC official's nod to undertake the digging work.

Area residents brought the matter to the notice of area councillor Amrit Varsha Rampal, who informed senior MC officials.

According to information, it was around midnight when a few residents noticed the digging activity on in the market area. The accused owns a shop in the area.

"I got the complaint that somebody was illegally trying to lay a sewerage pipe in the nearby sewerage line. I informed the joint commissioner of the MC about the matter. Thereafter, the officials intervened and stalled the work," said Rampal.

She said the person who was trying to dig out the concrete ground to make way for the pipe alongside the road said that an MC official had allowed him to take the connection into the nearby sewerage pipe. "When asked, the person named an MC official and said that he had the permission to undertake the work," the councillor said.

However, when asked, the MC official VK Mahajan, said that he had not given any permission to anybody and added that it was not even in his authority to do so.

"I may have met this person, but I have not allowed him to undertake any digging work. It is not even in my capacity to grant such permissions," he said.

On the other hand, the councillor said, "The person was carrying out the work in the cover of the dark which proves that this was being done without any proper authorisation. But I have asked the higher MC officials to take the matter seriously as such connections usually lead to choked sewerage pipes."

Heading: Starting today, MC to crack down on all illegal structures, hoardings in city - Indian Express
Content:
Suspected cases rise to 75; 4 patients report to DMC while GTB Hospital and Oswal admit one case each

As many as six fresh cases of suspected dengue have been reported in different city hospitals since Saturday. The number of suspected cases, according to the Health department, has risen to 75 while 14 cases have been confirmed in the district.

While four patients were admitted to the Dayanand Medical College and Hospital (DMCH), Guru Teg Bahadur Hospital and MD Oswal Cancer Hospital admitted one patient each.

In the last 24 hours, it is learnt, the DMCH has admitted various patients suffering from suspected dengue in its emergency ward.

The hospital has admitted 114 cases so far and 56 of them are from the district.

Health officials, however, said there was no need to panic as the situation was not alarming.

"It is not out of control if we find about 100 cases in a population of 30 lakh in the district," an official said.

Deputy Speaker, Punjab Legislative Assembly , Satpal Gosain, meanwhile, visited the Civil Hospital on Sunday and announced that the hospital had been recommended to be converted into a 200-bed facility.

The Deputy Speaker interacted with the patients and listened to their problems. Speaking on the occasion, he said: "The city needs a bigger hospital. I have recommended to the Chief Minister and the Health Minister to make the Civil Hospital a 200- bed facility."

At present, the hospital has 100 beds. "We want the hospital to cater to the public in a better way,"he said.

Heading: 5 months on, 10,000 teachers work without salaries - Indian Express
Content:
Beginning Monday, the Ludhiana Municipal Corporation will embark upon one of its much needed projects. If everything goes as MC has planned, encroachments on the city roads will be a thing of the past. Under a separate plan, the corporation has also planned to remove illegal hoardings across the city.

Giving details, B S Ghuman, Commissioner, Ludhiana Municipal Corporation, said, "Our thrust will be to remove encroachments dotting the city roads. I have asked tehbazaari wing to initiate the drive with the Ferozepur Road." Ghuman added, "The road will be cleared of all rehris and other illegal structures soon."

When asked about the illegal hoardings that simply clog the green belt running parallel to the Ferozepur Road, Ghuman said, "These hoardings make the city ugly. However, for removing hoardings, we are devising a separate plan that will be ready within the next two days."

Ghuman added, "After Ferozepur Road, we will target the Gill Road and so on."

Though the ambitious plan will roll out from Monday yet the contentious issue of illegal hoardings remains unsolved. It has been learnt that after the advertising mafia had made it tough for the LMC officials to bring down illegal hoardings, it is now the religious bodies and the politicians, who are making the task more difficult. What more with the festival and wedding season approaching these mammoth size hoardings are mushrooming all across the city.

A senior official of the LMC on condition of anonymity said, "Putting up a hoarding has become very easy these days. All one has to do is stick a picture of either some God or politicians and stick it to the poles. No one can then remove it. If we try and remove a hoarding which has a picture of God, that sect will gun for our blood and in case the hoarding is of some politician, he will get angry with us. Religious sects and political parties do not want to pay to MC and then put up a hoarding."

Heading: ‘We need to give better living conditions to migrant population’ - Indian Express
Content:
The wait of the teachers and staff working in government-aided private schools for their salaries of the last five months refuses to end.

It is more than a year now since 10,000 government school teachers have not got their salaries in time.

The teachers last received their salaries in March. Government-Aided Private Schools Principals' Association President and N M Jain School Principal O P Arora said, "It is getting impossible to manage without salaries. The aided schools get 95 per ent grant from the state government while 5 per cent is given by the school managing committee of the respective school. Many teachers have taken personal loans or are borrowing money from their near and dear ones. The school management had arranged one month's salary of teachers which was about Rs 4.50 lakh. But it is not possible to churn out such an amount every month."

R S Model Senior Secondary School Principal M L Kalra said, "There are many schools where the school management cannot even afford one month's salary. One can imagine the difficulty being faced by teachers."

Around 7,000 computer science teachers employed in government schools are also sailing in the same boat. Gurvinder Singh, President, Computer Teachers' Union said, "We are fed up of delayed release of salaries. Neither the government is regularising us nor releasing our dues in time. We held a state-level protest today at Jalandhar and also stopped Amritsar-bound Shatabdai for about an hour at Rama-Mandi."

Commenting on the issue, Computer Teachers Union Ludhiana-2 Block President Ranjan Bhanot said, "It has been a year since we have been getting our salaries only four times a year. My wife and I are both computer teachers and it is very difficult to meet the daily expenses."

Heading: Ready to assist India in the war on terror, says US - Indian Express
Content:
Dr RS Grewal is the district epidemiologist who took charge earlier this year, only to find the city under the incessant dangers of disease outbreaks, mainly in areas inhabited by the migrants. He shares with Sameer Kumar Sharma his concerns as the district epidemiologist and tries to provide with some concrete answers to the health problems ailing the city.

Why is it that diseases like gastroenteritis have been striking the city every year now for the past decade?
It is because the water supply in the areas inhabited by the migrant population is not only faulty but poses health risks for residents. One only needs to visit the areas in order to gauge the gravity of the situation there. The joints of the water supply pipes are leaking, illegal connections are abound. Therefore, sewerage water at such points gets mixed up in the water supply pipes. The result is apparent: diseases.

In the event of a disease outbreak, what is your role as a district epidemiologist?
The Health department's role entails looking after the treatment of patients and creating public awareness about the disease among the residents. It is not the responsibility of the department as far as poor quality of water being supplied to the households is concerned.

How can such water-borne diseases be tackled?
We can only take samples and inform the authorities concerned to rectify the problem. But there is only one permanent solution; the potable water should be safe. It is sad that even after 60 years of independence, when we are talking about economic boom, thinking of mission for going to the moon, the potable water supply is still very bad.

Which are the areas that fall prey to the diseases in the city?
Localities of Giaspura, Dhandari and Sherpur are the areas which house industrial units and where the migrants reside. It is in these vehras the basic problem lie. The children eat and drink in the kind of environment which is so bad that if people from the posh localities are to live there for a single day, they would most probably succumb to the ill-effects of unhygienic conditions.

These people tend to develop strong immunity so, therefore, the death rate is still low or there would have been many deaths. But I do not understand why we cannot have better places for migrants, who form the workforce in industries, something like quarters for them, rather than 'vehras' where they live in pathetic unsanitary conditions.

But aren't the people also to blame for the unsanitary conditions they live in?
Yes, very much. Their participation in improving the conditions is next to nil. People are still indifferent towards diseases such as dengue, which we hear about every day. They take very less initiative to even clean up the stagnant water collections in their own houses, not to talk of the adjoining areas.

Heading: Security beefed up in Kolkata - Indian Express
Content:
The United States has said it is ready to assist India in the war on terror after serial blasts rocked New Delhi, underscoring that such macabre acts only united those committed to peaceful and democratic society.

"We are ready to assist the Indian government in its ongoing fight to eliminate the scourge of terrorism," State Department spokesman Sean McCormack has said in a statement.

He said the tragedy serves as a reminder that "terrorism did not deter, but unites those committed to peaceful and political means as the guarantor of a free, democratic and prosperous society".

The spokesman condemned the terrorist attacks on September 13 in New Delhi and extended sympathy to the families of those killed and injured in the blasts.

Heading: Hunt begins all over again: SIMI links - Indian Express
Content:
Security has been beefed up in all public places and vital installations here following the serial blasts in Delhi although the metropolis has not received any specific threat, police said.

"Security has been beefed up and all owners of malls and multiplexes advised to reorganise their security systems as per rules and standards set by Kolkata Police," Deputy Commissioner of Police (Headquarters) Vineet Kumar Goyal said.

"Special teams have been formed to supervise the security system of the city and people are requested to call police on toll free numbers 100 and 1090 for information and any kind of assistance," Goyal said.

Heading: Vital leads in Delhi blasts: SIMI activist key suspect - Indian Express
Content:
A day after serial blasts left at least 21 dead and nearly 100 injured, Delhi limped back to normalcy while police, looking for leads, were said to be questioning two persons who had been detained. Police Commissioner Y S Dadwal said they had come across "vital clues" which would help them track down perpetrators of the blasts who police suspect belong to the Indian Mujahideen-SIMI network.

Abdus Subhan Qureshi alias Tauqeer, who remains at large and is wanted by police in Gujarat for his alleged role in the Ahmedabad bombings, is emerging as one of the main suspects in the Delhi blasts too.

Sources said police and Central security agencies were looking for three SIMI sympathisers — Abu Zair, Danish and Aftab — who apparently arranged a safehouse in Delhi for Abu Bashar, arrested from Azamgarh in UP after the Ahmedabad blasts. Bashar, police sources said, stayed in Delhi from July 24 to 26.

Bashar told his interrogators that Zair, 23, was his younger brother who worked as a parking attendant near the Jama Masjid police chowki in the Walled City. Security agencies are not sure whether Zair is involved in SIMI activities but say he can help identify his brother's SIMI associates in Delhi. Investigators believe that the Delhi bombing was a desperate bid by remnants of the SIMI to assert its identity after most who made the organisation's top leadership were rounded up.

Mool Chand, the driver of the auto-rickshaw involved in the Gaffar Market blast that claimed 18 lives, has described the bomber as a 25-year-old, fair-complexioned man who had hired his vehicle from outside Imperial Hotel on Janpath to take him to Patel Nagar. Mool Chand told security agencies that the man told him to take a detour to Ajmal Khan Road, the busiest shopping district in west Delhi, because "he wanted to buy something". Since the police did not allow Mool Chand to park the auto-rickshaw on Ajmal Khan Road, the man got off near the Saraswati Marg-Gurudwara Road intersection at Gaffar Market. The man asked Mool Chand to take care of his bag and got off. Within minutes, the bomb went off.

Sources said an all-out effort was being made to nab remnants of the SIMI top brass. Those who remain at large include Subhan Qureshi alias Tauqeer of Mumbai, Ikram of Madhya Pradesh, Mohammed Ali Musa from MP, Qayamuddin and Akram aka Abu Faisal, a Unani medicine student from Mumbai. These names have been culled from the interrogation reports of Safdar Nagori, Qamaruddin Nagori, Sajid Mansuri, Abu Bashar and Shahbaz — they are all under custody and were part of the critical SIMI meeting at Castle Rock near Hubli in April 2007.

The hunt for Subhan Qureshi alias Tauqeer had taken Gujarat police to Nanded in Maharashtra but Shahbaz told Rajasthan police that Tauqeer could be in Karnataka as the organisation had a sound network there.

One pointer to the desperation in the SIMI ranks following the arrest of its top brass is the fact that the Indian Mujahideen mail was signed by the media centre. According to Shahbaz Hussain, accused in the Jaipur blasts, anyone in the SIMI media centre could sign the mail — from the contents of the mail sent this time, it appears that it was not written by any of its top leaders.

Security agencies suspect not more than five persons were used for the Delhi bombings. The desperation showed in the manner the bombs were placed — in dustbins. The one bomb that turned to be most destructive was the Ghaffar Market device which was apparently ticking as the bomber travelled from Janpath to Ajmal Khan Road.

As in Jaipur and Gujarat, the bomb-makers had used ammonium nitrate, shrapnels, detonators and ball bearings in the Delhi bombs. Gelatin sticks were also used.

"From Greater Kailash, we have taken CCTV footage of three hours before the blasts and it is being scanned," the sources said. Teams from Jaipur and Mumbai police also reached Delhi today to join the probe.

The two teenaged balloon-sellers, who found two bombs which were later defused, have been taken to the Crime Records Bureau and sketches of two suspects are being made with the help of the description the boys provided.

Heading: Delhi blasts: Probe indicates little role of locals - Indian Express
Content:
A suspected SIMI activist based in Mumbai emerged on Sunday as a key suspect along with three from Azamgarh in Uttar Pradesh in connection with the Delhi serial blasts that left 24 persons dead as police detained six persons and claimed to have obtained "vital leads".

Amid indications that the Delhi terror attack had a similarity with the Ahmedabad blasts in July, Delhi Police spokesman Rajan Bhagat said "we have got vital leads" but declined to give details saying "we will solve the case soon".

Sketches of suspected bombers were being drawn by the Delhi Police with the help of five eye-witnesses including a teenage balloon seller, who claimed to have seen them placing packets in the dustbins at Central Park in Connaught Place.

Sources in the investigating agencies said two people were picked from the walled city and two more from Okhla. The suspects with reported links with banned SIMI were being probed by joint teams of central security agencies and police.

While two more were also being quizzed, two others detained from Barakhamba Road have been released, they said.

Initial probe pointed to a group belonging to Western Uttar Pradesh behind the five coordinated blasts at Ghaffar Market in Karol Bagh, Connaught Place and Greater Kailash.

Police teams have been sent to neighbouring UP and Rajasthan.

Sources said the role of Mumbai-resident Mohammed Subhan Quereshi alias Tauqeer, a suspected SIMI activist, was being probed. Police believe that he could have hacked the WiFI system in Mumbai to send the terror e-mail to media houses.

Sources said that Qureshi is believed to have visited the National Capital two weeks back and the two persons detained from Okhla would provide leads about him. Qureshi has been named as an accused in various terror attacks since 2003.

Sources also said strong similarities were found between the Delhi blasts and the serial explosions in Ahmedabad on July 26 that left 53 dead.

Heading: Four security personnel killed in JK gun battle - Indian Express
Content:
As investigations behind Saturday's serial bomb Blasts in Delhi gained some momentum on Sunday with the detention of a few suspects, initial indications pointed to a lack of any major local involvement in the attacks.

Investigators probing the incident believe that the attack was carried out mostly by people from the outside with involvement of locals, most probably, being limited to arranging for accommodation and logistical support for the terrorists, sources said.

They said the police had detained about seven-eight people so far, including a few from neighbouring Haryana and Uttar Pradesh. But there are indications that the Terror module behind Saturday's blasts had its base in western India with links in the cities of Mumbai, Indore or Ahmedabad. The fact that the email sent by Indian Mujahideen was traced to Mumbai and also references in the mail to a few scarcely reported raids in some areas of Mumbai has also given credence to this theory.

Another crucial lead the investigators are said to be working on is the stark similarity in the nature of explosives used in the blasts in Delhi and Ahmedabad. With both Ahmedabad and Delhi blasts being believed to be carried out by the same module, this has given rise to suspicion that the explosives expert of this module is not among those who have been arrested by the Gujarat Police in connection with the Ahmedabad blasts, the source said.

The explosives used in Delhi were exactly similar to the ones used in Ahmedabad blasts about two months back. The manner in which they were packed, the C-shaped boxes they were kept in, even the carpentry of the box, all point to the same group behind their assembling.

The investigators are banking heavily on the footage from the four CCTV cameras at Greater Kailash market. The sources said video footage in three of these were clear and would be crucial in identifying the people who placed the bombs. The fourth camera was said to be malfunctioning.

Heading: HC stays custodial interrogation of Amarinder - Indian Express
Content:
Four security personnel were killed and one injured in a gun battle with militants in Poonch district of Jammu and Kashmir.

Acting on a tip-off, army troops and police launched a joint cordon and search operation in Tarawali forest belt in Surankote on Sunday night, Sub Divisional Police Officer (SDPO) of Surankote, Parbeet Singh said.

During the operation militants started firing to which the security personnel retaliated, Singh said.

Four security personnel, including two army jawans have been killed and one injured in the encounter which is still going on, he said.

The slain army personnel have been identified as Vishnu and Jurnail Singh. Two cops killed in the encounter are identified as Maqbool Shah and Mohmmad Maroof.

The injured army jawan is identified as Om Prakash.

"No militant has been killed so far in the encounter," he added.

Heading: Bomb scare in Connaught Place triggers panic - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab and Haryana High Court on Monday stayed the custodial interrogation of former Chief Minister Amarinder Singh in a graft case registered by the Vigilance Bureau following his expulsion from the state assembly last week.

A division bench comprising Justices Adarsh Goel and Ajay Tewari, which had last week reserved its judgment on Singh's plea seeking a stay in the case and on his expulsion from the House, also issued notices to the Punjab Assembly through its Secretary and directed him to file the reply on or before October 31.

The bench directed 66-year-old Singh to file a rejoinder on or before November 15 and admitted the case for final hearing on December one before a regular division bench.

However, the court allowed the Vigilance Bureau to carry on with its investigation into the case registered against the Congress leader and seven others in connection with irregularities in the Amritsar land deal.

Singh had moved the High Court last week challenging the Assembly's September 10 decision to strip him of his membership and declaring his Patiala seat vacant after a House Committee indicted him and three others in the case.

The Committee charged them with releasing 32.10 acres of Improvement Trust, Amritsar land for development by private colonisers in violation of rules following a complaint by a senior Congress leader Bir Devinder Singh, who had raised the issue in the House during Singh's tenure as Chief Minister between 2002 and 2007.

Besides Singh, former Local Bodies Minister Jagjit Singh, former Amritsar Improvement Trust (AIT) Chairman Jugal Kishore Sharma, two employees of AIT and two builders have been named in the FIR registered in Mohali. Singh left for the UK for medical treatment following a court permission a day after the case was registered against him.

Heading: 'Indian Mujahideen striking cities for publicity' - Indian Express
Content:
Panic was triggered in the heart of the national capital on Monday after police received an anonymous call threatening to blow up a multi-storeyed building which later turned out to be a hoax.

Police received a call at around 8:15 am that explosives were placed at New Delhi House building on Barakhamba road, a stone's throw away from the spot where a bomb exploded on Saturday evening.

The call was declared a hoax, a senior police official said. The 12-storeyed building houses several offices, those of Punjab Indian Bank and several travel agencies, where around 1,000 people report for work everyday.

People were evacuated as bomb disposal squads were rushed to the spot. The building was searched but no explosives were found, the official said.

A large number of office-goers were seen standing around the busy Barakhamba road intersection.

Police have received at least five hoax bomb calls so far since the Saturday blasts in the national capital which claimed over 20 lives.

On Saturday night, two calls were received that bombs had been placed in Merina Hotel and on Parliament Street.

Two more calls were received from Madhuban Chowk and Paschim Vihar yesterday but searches did not yield anything.

Police have received about 70 bomb hoax calls this year.

Heading: BMW sting ops: SC declines to stay HC order against advocates - Indian Express
Content:
Indian Mujahideen, a relatively new group which has claimed responsibility for most of the recent strikes across the country including Saturday's serial blasts in the capital, is targeting important places for media attention, security experts said.

Former Intelligence Bureau Chief A K Doval felt the group is targeting major cities, mainly "capitals", because it wants "global media attraction.

"They (Mujahideen members) want to terrorise people and terrorism thrives on publicity. So, they target such areas from where they would get maximum media attention," Doval said.

The militant group first emerged on the national front when it send an e-mail to some media groups on November 23 last year, minutes before bombs exploded in buildings of three trial courts in Uttar Pradesh, including one at capital Lucknow.

Echoing Doval's views, former RAW Secretary A S Dulat said the motive is to gain publicity.

"Smaller cities will not provide them so much publicity as these larger, politically important cities," Dulat said.

Doval said "in case of small cities, there is always a hreat of being identified, but in bigger ones, you can go unnoticed".

While Dulat was of the opinion that the larger motive s "propaganda publicity" rather than killing people, Doval felt that even low-intensity bombs can kill a number of people if planted in high density population areas and the explosion is triggered at peak hours.

Dulat added that the material used to prepare low-intensity bombs and was easily available in local markets.

Heading: Vacant seat after OBC quota implementation to go to general category - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court on Monday refused to stay a Delhi High Court order barring advocates R K Anand and I U Khan from practising for four months after they were "caught" in the BMW sting operation case.

A bench of Justices B N Agrawal and G S Singhvi also refused to pass any direction on the High Court's verdict stripping them of their senior advocate status.

The apex Court posted for hearing on Monday the appeal of the two lawyers against the High Court judgement.

The High Court had given its verdict after taking on May 31 last year suo motu cognisance of the NDTV sting operation showing Anand, in collusion with Khan, allegedly offering money to witness Sunil Kulkarni to depose in favour of the defence in the BMW case.

Heading: 'False' relatives cashing in on Delhi serial blasts - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court on Monday ruled that seats remaining vacant after implementation of the 27 per cent quota under a Parliament-enacted legislation would go to students of the 'general' category.

"There is no no confusion about our judgement that seats which remain vacant after the implementation of the 27 per cent quota will go to the general category," a bench headed by Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan said.

The bench had on April 10 upheld the validity of the Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admissions) Act.

Heading: Mgmt students should study factors behind terrorism: Kalam - Indian Express
Content:
For some, the serial bomb blasts in the capital seems to be a perfect way of trying to mint money and gain cheap publicity.

As reporters scurry around for relatives of blast victims, many have come forward with false claims to say that their kith and kin have been killed or severely injured hoping to get a share of the compensation.

Some can be later seen smiling minutes after yelling and beating their chests in front of the cameras.

In Karol Bagh, Beadonpura one of the serial blast sites, a group of men and women including children are huddled together on the pavements ready to give TV sound bytes.

Though on Sunday, some members had claimed that they were one big extended family staying together with seven of their family tragically killed in the blast, surprisingly today, the number of deceased family members climbed to 12.

"Yesterday we lost seven. Today four more have died," said Jeevan Ram along with a lady who spoke the most.

On continued discussion it was later found out that the seven killed were not from one family but from four different families and the entire group actually belonged to a common Rajasthani village and community - Nadibadh Samaj.

The group later said most of those present had come from Punjab, West Bengal and Haryana after getting to know about the blast.

"Our 12 people died here and the government is doing nothing. We have been supporters of the government but we are not being helped. Temporary relief should be immediately given to the victim's family along with pucca houses," said a visibly agitated Dashrath from Haryana who had come to the capital on Sunday.

When contacted, hospital authorities said that no blasts victims had died on Monday.

Heading: Sonia holds meeting on internal security, Patil absent - Indian Express
Content:
In the wake of terrorist attacks in the capital and other parts of the country, former President APJ Abdul Kalam on Monday asked management students to study the factors behind scourge and launch a national campaign against the menace.

Speaking at the convocation function of FORE School of Management in New Delhi, Kalam said management students could take up a study and go into details of the factors behind the extremist acts.

"You can take a lead role and create leadership required to address the issue," he said.

Kalam also favoured launching a national campaign for eradication of poverty to sensitise the public against terrorism. He stressed on equitable growth in the country so that people of all sections get the benefit of it.

On Sunday Kalam had advocated a unified intelligence agency and stringent laws to handle terrorism. He had said the security agencies should be armed with latest technology.

He said development of rural sector and small and medium scale industries were key to the progress of the country.

About 180 students were awarded diplomas and degrees on the occasion. Institute's director Seema Sanghi presented a brief account about the B-school.

Heading: 'BJP has turned Karnataka into Gujarat of South' - Indian Express
Content:
Congress President Sonia Gandhi on Monday reviewed the country's internal security situation with senior party leaders but significantly Home Minister Shivraj Patil, who is under attack from various quarters over the handling of terrorism, was conspicuous by his absence.

External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee, Defence Minister A K Antony, Digvijay Singh, Margaret Alva and the Congress president's political secretary Ahmed Patel were present at the meeting, sources said.

The meeting discussed the Delhi blasts and the situation arising out of it. The internal security situation of the country came up for review, they said.

There was no explanation why Patil, whose ministry is directly in-charge of security of Delhi, was not present at the meeting.

Party spokesman Abhishek Manu Singhvi speculation over Patil saying review of situations at the government and party levels were part of governance and stories in the media were pure speculation.

Patil is under all-round attack over his ministry's handling of internal security. Some senior leaders of the Congress are also said to be critical of the minister, whose attention to sartorial preferences even during the night of Saturday blasts have been attacked.

Heading: Lalu slams Home Ministry over handling of terrorism - Indian Express
Content:
Former Prime Minister H D Deve Gowda on Monday alleged that minorities were at the receiving end of Sangh Parivar 'fanatics' in Karnataka and charged ruling BJP with attempting to turn the state into the "Gujarat of south".

"Chief Minister B S Yeddyurappa has lived upto his promise that he would implement a 'Gujarat Model' in the state", he said in his caustic remarks a day after some churches were attacked allegedly by pro-Hindu groups in the state.

"Karnataka has today emerged as the worst terror and communal hub among all the southern states," the JD(S) leader told reporters in Bangalore.

"The violence in Tiptur and the attacks on churches in Davangere, Dakshina Kannada, Udupi and Mangalore are manifestations of the manner in which the Sangh Parivar organisations are fast spreading their tentacles across the state and turning it into a Gujarat of the south," he said.

Targeting senior BJP leader L K Advani, Gowda said he was shocked to find that BJP's prime ministerial candidate did not express any concern over the situation in the state.

"Has the mask of secularism that the octogenarian Advani was trying to wear by describing Pakistan founder Muhammad Ali Jinnah as secular, terming the demolition of Babri Masjid as a 'black day' and paying obeisance at the Ajmer Dargah come off, as he gets into a 'must win' mode in his hurry to occupy 7, Race Course Road?" he asked.

Gowda sought the immediate resignation of state Home Minister V S Acharya owning moral responsibility for the "spate of violence against minorities".

Heading: Governors' meet to discuss terror - Indian Express
Content:
Home Minister Shivraj Patil on Monday came under pressure after a key UPA constituent and a Cabinet colleague attacked the handling of terrorism and demanded an urgent meeting of the Cabinet and all political parties to discuss the issue.

RJD chief and Railway Minister Lalu Prasad, who met Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and the Congress president after Delhi blasts earlier in the day and discussed the situation in the wake of serial Delhi blasts on Saturday that claimed 24 lives, however, did not take Patil's name directly.

"A special Cabinet meeting should be called to discuss threadbare issues arising out of the blasts in Delhi," he told reporters in New Delhi adding the Prime Minister assured him that he would call a meeting in a couple of days.

He said UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi should also call an all-party meeting to debate the issue of terrorism.

Prasad blamed intelligence failure for the Delhi blasts, saying inputs from the IB are always "vague".

Asked about Patil's statements after every blast, the Railway Minister said, "Do I contradict whatever you say".

The RJD chief demanded constitution of a special task force to deal with terrorism-related cases.

Attacking the intelligence agencies, Prasad said the Delhi blasts were a result of intelligence failure. "The Intelligence Bureau inputs are always vague and should be more specific," he added.

"A mechanism should be evolved to tackle such situation," Prasad said.

"After bomb blasts we remain alert for a day or two only whereas the alertness should be a continuous process. There should not be any slackness in maintaining vigil all the time," Prasad said.

However, Prasad refused to blame any particular organisation for the Delhi blasts. Let us not indulge in blame game without proof."

He said innocents should not be harassed in the name of investigation but only the guilty should be punished.

About the need for any stringent laws to tackle the terror menace, he said, "No law can prevent human bombs. There was a POTA when Parliament was attacked. So just passing laws is not the solution in such cases."

He said there should be accountability fixed on the part of bureaucracy. "Because it is the bureaucracy which will ensure the proper operationalisation of the law."

Heading: Khairlanji: 8 held guilty for killing Dalit family - Indian Express
Content:
Close on the heels of the Delhi serial blasts, President Pratibha Patil will take stock of the internal security situation of the country with Governors of all states at a two-day conference beginning in New Delhi on Tuesday.

The focus of the conference, which will also be participated by Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and senior Cabinet Ministers, is to discuss threadbare the internal security environment of the country with special reference to Left-wing extremism and insurgency.

The steps taken for police modernisation, the security scenario along the international borders and related issues, various aspects of bilateral relations with India's neighbouring countries will also come up for discussions, official sources said.

The meeting bears significance in view of the fact that it comes just three days after the Delhi serial blasts, which so far claimed 24 lives, and weeks after Amarnath land row.

Issues relating to climate change and sustainable development in India's context, the Indian agricultural scenario and food security, current economic situation and strategy for price stability will be discussed at the two-day conference.

Heading: Investigations on right track, sketches being fine tuned: Delhi police - Indian Express
Content:
Eight persons accused of killing four members of a Dalit family have been held guilty in the Khairlanji murder case by a sessions court in Bhandara.

Ad hoc sessions and district court judge S S Cass on Monday Binjewar, Sakru Binjewar, Shatrughan Dhande, Vishwanath Dhande, Ramu Dhande, Jagdish Mandlekar, Prabhakar Mandlekar and Shishpal Dhande guilty under various sections of the IPC.

Three other accused - Mahipal Dhande, Dharampal Dhande and Purushottam Titarmare were acquitted.

The court found no evidence against these three accused.

The court could not find any evidence against them under the prevention of atrocities on Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe Act 1989.

However, the court deferred the pronouncement of the quantum of the sentence today, but has agreed to resume hearing in the case from September 20.

Four persons of a Dalit family - Surekha Bhaiyalal Bhotmange, her daughter Priyanka and sons - Sudhir and Roshan were killed on September 29, 2006 over a land dispute by the accused in Khairlanji village.

Surekha's husband and the only surviving member of the family, Bhaiyalal, had managed to flee the spot.

he four were mercilessly beaten to death and their bodies were thrown into a canal in the village, prosecution had alleged. The killings had evoked violent reactions across the state and drew flak from all quarters including the state assembly and Parliament.

Bowing to mounting pressure, the state authorities had handed over the case to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and its Chennai unit was entrusted with the task.
