"By play of words, you cannot get away with the court's order. By putting the word provisional, are you not going against the court's order?" asked the three-member bench, underlining that the government has to seek the mandatory nod from the court before it proceeds with the process.

"File an affidavit and then seek a modification of the court's order," said the bench as Additional Solicitor General (ASG) P P Malhotra stood up assuring that all basic services have been provided in these colonies.

The ASG's brief submission came as Malik pointed to the full-page ads by the Delhi government promising residents of these colonies to come and collect their provisional certificates.

"A rally was scheduled at the Ramlila Grounds for the purpose but has been deferred in view of the bomb blasts on Saturday," the counsel informed, showing the advertisement, which appeared in national dailies. Justice Pasayat quipped, "The certificate may be provisional, but the blasts were final."

Meanwhile, the Court also directed the DDA to place before the court all documents relating to the 37 new amendments, proposed in the Masterplan Delhi (MPD) 2021.

"Whether you invited suggestions, what were the reasons for bringing those amendments, suggestions considered and those which were not with reasons, place all the documents," ordered the bench as it remarked, "we want to know whether it was an application of mind or plain formality."

This was directed after amicus curiae Ranjit Kumar asked whether these amendments can be allowed, when the city is already crumbling.

"Why do we want to add more people and allow them to die in the serial blasts like Saturday," counsel submitted referring to the serial blasts that took place last week.

Heading: Smart cards for pavement traders, dustbins to be checked - Indian Express
Content:
Vilakshan Jha
On Monday, two days after the blast, Ranju got back her smile when she heard the voice of her husband Vilakshan Jha, who suffered serious injuries in the blast. Lying on his bed at Jessa Ram hospital, 36-year-old Jha, who worked at Gaffar Market, on Monday talked to his wife for a few minutes.

"I feel fortunate that my husband is fine. I was terrified after hearing the news. But it seems the God was on my side," said Ranju.

Raj Kumar Chauhan
It was an ordinary day for 30-year-old Raj Kumar Chauhan, a resident of Yamuna Vihar, when he travelled to Karol Bagh to collect money from a customer. The blast left serious injuries in his left hand and he now lies in Jessa Ram Hospital with 14 stitches. "It has taken two days for doctors to stop the bleeding. But he will still have to be here for a while before he recuperates," said Daulat Ram, father of the victim. Chauhan's father was accompanied by his wife, Rajni and six-year-old son Aditya.

Mahavir Singh
"Could you please speak a little louder." Thirty five-year-old Mahavir Singh has managed to survive. But his biggest fear is his hearing impairment might be permanent. The Singh family suffered a double blow as Mahavir's nephew Sanjay was also grievously hurt in the Gaffar Market blast on Saturday evening. Both have now been discharged from Lady Hardinge Medical College (LHMC). Mahavir was back at work — manning the mobile accessories shop in the narrow lanes of Gali No 3 in Karol Bagh on Monday. He was shopping for mobile accessories in Gaffar Market on Saturday evening when the bomb went off.

Nephew Sanjay suffered shrapnel injuries in his left leg. The sound of the blast damaged both his eardrums. "I am lucky to have survived. Thinking about my family's plight without me sends a shiver down my spine," said Mahavir. He is the family's only breadwinner.

Raju Shao
The promise of a job and a better future brought Raju from Darbhanga district in Bihar to the Capital last week. Raju (18) was loitering around Gali no 42 in Gaffar Market when the bomb went off. He suffered serious burn injuries in his legs and a splinter pierced his right arm, injuring him critically. Post two operations, he lies recuperating in the orthopaedic ward. "I went numb for a few minutes after the blast. All I could see was bodies lying around me," Raju says. My brother Ram Babu and two doctors from the orthopedic unit, Dr Mahima and Dr Charu, donated blood and saved my life," he says.

Shahid
A mobile store owner in Kabir Nagar, Shahid had just closed his shop and was going towards the MCD parking block when the autorickshaw parked a few meters away exploded. Splinters and ball bearings pierced his body. "I heard a deafening sound and saw the person standing next to me collapse," he says. When Shahid regained consciousness, he found himself in the surgery ward of LHMC. "Maine us din Roza rakha tha shayad isliye Allah ne mujhe bacha liya," he says.

Mohd Nahid
A resident of J J Colony in Bavana, Nahid had been standing outside his shop in Gali no. 42, Gaffar Market, when the blast occurred.

He was heading back home when his friends asked him leave after Iftar. "He was standing outside when I heard the deafening sound of the blast. I rushed out of my shop and saw that he had been injured," says Ahmed Mustafa, Nahid's friend who rushed him to Lady Hardinge. Nahid suffered serious leg and back injuries.

A resident of Bihar, Nahid's parents are in their native village.

Harsh Sahay
A native of Rajasthan, Harsh, has been living in Gaffar Market area with his wife, a son and two daughters. He had been standing outside his house in Gali no. 42 when the blast occurred.

"I saw people running and ran towards my house. Someone pushed me. I fell on the ground and lost consciousness," he says. His left arm was seriously injured in the blast.

Wife Natthi and three children were in the house and hence, were saved. "These are just bad times we all have to face. So many people have lost lives, what purpose does it serve?" he says. His younger son, a daily labourer, is the only earning member in the family.

Heading: No reprieve for Anand, Khan - Indian Express
Content:
After the twin blasts in Connaught Place on Saturday shook the city, the New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) has decided to issue smart cards to all tehbazari shopkeepers setting shop on pavements in the markets.

Tehbazari licences are to be reviewed by all civic agencies, as mandated by the Supreme Court. NDMC's chief spokesperson, Anand Tiwari, said all licence-holders will be issued smart cards which cannot be duplicated and will contain all necessary information of the licensee.

"We usually keep carrying out regular drives to check licences, but this has been a policy decision taken to avoid keeping steady vigil," he said.

The agency will also launch a drive to remove unlicensed vendors from pavements of markets like Janpath, Sarojini Nagar and CP.

The health department has also decided to set up teams to check all dustbins and dhalaos in New Delhi area, every day.

According to the Medical Officer of Health, Dr P K Sharma, all supervisors in the area have been officially instructed to check dustbins and dhalaos every morning and evening, besides keeping a regular vigil and submit reports regularly to him.

While all of New Delhi has been divided into 14 circle areas for the collection of garbage, there are about 1,100 small dustbins in residential pockets, and 1,000 big dustbins (similar to the ones in which the bombs exploded) in commercial spots.

There are around 333 dhalaos where garbage trucks collect garbage dumped by rag pickers.

Sharma said, "We have a good network of ragpickers and safai karmcharis who carry out door-to-door collection in the area. We have now asked our circle officers to tap them and if possible stay in touch with them to keep vigil on suspicious activities."

Over 200 ragpickers have been put on the door-to-door collection scheme of colonies like Kaka Nagar, Rabindra Nagar and Bharti Nagar to collect garbage directly from homes.

Heading: People avoid main markets - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court, on Monday, declined reprieve to senior advocates R K Anand and I U Khan, who had approached the apex court after the Delhi High Court barred the two from practice for four months. The senior defence lawyer, along with the senior prosecution lawyer, were found guilty of criminal contempt of court.

The bench comprising, Justices B N Agrawal and G S Singhvi, that took up the appeal filed by the senior advocate for hearing, however, refused to stay the impugned judgment dated September.

While posting the appeal for further directions on September 22, 2008, the bench silenced those assailing the HC's judgment on the ground that it exceeded its powers in debarring lawyers and recommending for stripping of their senior designation.

The SC observed, "The court was competent and the bar council has no role."

"The designation of senior is given by the Full Court. It is for the Full Court bench now to decide," the judges said, adjourning the matter for a week.

Both Anand and Khan had challenged the judgment, which found them guilty of causing obstruction in the administration of justice by the BMW sting operation case.

The HC gave its verdict after it took on May 31, 2007, suo motu cognisance of the NDTV sting operation showing Anand, in collusion with Khan, allegedly offering money to witness Sunil Kulkarni to depose in favour of the defence in the case.

Heading: Police look for terror mongers among the injured, dead - Indian Express
Content:
After the serial blast that rocked Delhi on Saturday on Monday, Delhiites saw a new morning when stores in the markets were open and traders busy at work. Yet, the bustle was missing. On Sunday, most of the market was closed. On Monday all markets were open, but the crowds were still thin.

In Connaught Place (CP), shopkeepers waiting for customers to fill the shops and pavements, were a disappointed lot. Some vendors said, "We take permission from the police to open shop. But what can we do if there aren't enough people venturing out into the markets?"

The blasts have had an impact in Palika Bazaar which shoppers are avoiding, and the crowd is much less than on any weekday.

One of the oldest shopkeepers Ashok Grover said, "I've been working for 25 years and traders stand to lose because people are too scared to go to public places."

Heading: An unlikely football tale - Indian Express
Content:
Failing to get any clues about Saturday blasts suspects, the Delhi Police are also working on another line to identify terrorists who planted the bombs.

A dedicated team has been formed to identifying the victims, dead and injured, of the blasts. This team will focus on those who have not been identified yet.

Sources say among the dead, there might also be the bodies of the blast suspects. "Many victims are still unidentified after blasts and their families failed to recognise them. There are possibilities that the unidentified bodies might even be of the suspects," said an official.

This is similar to what happened in the 2005 serial blasts in Delhi in which three bodies could not be identified. The Special Cell had even sent the skull of an unidentified body to a Kolkata forensic lab for identification.

Cops tried to get the structure of face prepared. The body has not been identified till now. The body was reportedly found from Cheh Tooti Chowk at Paharganj. Only the Kolkata lab has the facility to recreate the structure of the face matching with the body.

Three bodies found on October 29, 2005, which could not be identified, were of middle aged males.

"It is hard to establish that they were suspects but if portraits described by eyewitnesses matches the lab portrait, then it gives some hope," added the source.

In the Paharganj and Sarojini blasts, 61 persons were killed.

After these three bodies could not be identified, some families including that of 13-year-old Shayan Mukharjee from Kalighat, Ramjivan's brother Ram Kishore from UP and the family of one Michael John had made several rounds of hospitals to know whether they were their dear ones but they got no clear information.

The team working on identification of victims is trying to know whether all injured or dead person's families have given correct addresses and information.

The victim's background would be checked without bothering them, said a source. "If someone suspicious is found then he would be interrogated," added the source.

Heading: Goa tainted by overage allegations - Indian Express
Content:
Orissa's Sundargarh district has a penchant for producing hockey players — be it the Tirkeys or the likes of Lajraus Barla and Subhodra Pradhan. So for Sankho Marandi and Bhada Tudu, the goal-scorers for Orissa against NCC (North East Region) on Monday at the Ambedkar Stadium, football had an unlikely temptation as hockey is bigger than cricket in this north-western town of Orissa.

Students of Town High School, the duo led their side to a 4-0 victory scoring a brace each to ensure a quarter-final berth in this year's Subroto Cup — bettering last year's ousting at the qualification stages.

The sob story of Indian footballers cuts through the faces of the Orissa footballers, and Sankho and Bhada claiming no exception, but this team presents another picture too.

"The boys are poor; 80 per cent of Orissa's population comprises the backward classes, but the government has done an excellent job in providing them with basic facilities. They stay together at Sundargarh Sports Hostel, where the expenses are provided by the state government. The selection process starts from the panchayat level and 22 boys are selected from 12-14 years of age. They stay in the academy till they reach Xth standard. After that there's a senior hostel facility in Cuttack, where the players are picked on the basis of their consistency during these years," says coach Surendranath Padhy, dismissing the lack of resources as an excuse.

The footballers too, seem to have opened a new chapter at the academy. "We practice for five hours a day. In between we study too. I got 58 per cent marks in my exams," says Sankho, whose parents work under a small contractor on the outskirts of Sundergarh. The tract of land they own is smaller than a garden.

While Bhada considers playing cricket as a pastime, Sankho thinks it's boring. Even when they play the gentleman's game, they play it with abandoned hockey sticks and balls. Coach Surendranath Padhy, though, readily dismisses the existence of the game in his part of the world, saying, "Hockey is the biggest sport in Sundargarh. Cricket is nowhere close. 80 per cent of the boys play hockey while the rest are into athletics or football. At our academy we have 52 students playing hockey, athletics and football only."

If this wasn't encouragement enough for the would-be footballers, they are set to receive a hike in their daily stipend, according to the coach. Bhada's face presents a reluctant smile on the announcement as he ended up spending half of the stipend from last year's Subroto Cup on some relatives' treatment. With the rest, he bought two pairs of practice shoes and a couple of track suits. And this year, he would have more reasons to keep it up,as the prize money in all categories has been doubled.

Heading: Rashid eyes another victory - Indian Express
Content:
Spectators lined the stands of the Ambedkar Stadium for the quarter-final league match between Goa and NCC (Bengal and Sikkim) of the Subroto Cup. But the 2-0 victory for the NCC team didn't reflect the expected competition as the Goans escaped a bigger loss. Goa coach Sebastiao Noronha blamed the absence of key players Marshall Fernandez and Sameer Arjun Pendenkar for the result, who were left out after failing medical tests. Sebastio lashed out at the organisers, accusing them of lack of transparency.

"Marshall and Sameer are our senior players. But this year, the organisers didn't allow them to play saying they were overage. I have brought medical certificates and reports from Goa that are proof enough. A bigger proof is these players' participation in the U-14 category of Subroto Cup 2005. The organisers stopped the boys seconds before kick-off. The team list is submitted almost a couple of hours before the match," said Sebastio.

Arijit Ghosh, secretary of the Subroto Mukherjee Sports Education Society, said that all the teams were made aware of the medical check-ups going into the matches which would overrule any other medical report carried by the team management. "This year we have a panel of three doctors, including a radiologist, and this has been employed to counter such cases. We also have a set of preliminary assessments failing which a player is subjected to the next set of assessments. These two players (Marshall and Sameer) from Goa failed both the stages and hence were not allowed participation. This applies to every player and we don't have any interest in denying any of the youngsters. As far as transparency is concerned, I can give him (Sebastio) the reports any time he wants it. The management was informed about the discrepancy through a letter long before the match. In such cases, their participation in 2005's u-14 category doesn't count as they might have been a few days short of the age cap," said Ghosh.

Interestingly, as many as seven players were ousted from the Goa U-14 team last year due to overage allegations while two players from the U-17 category failed the tests. "They came prepared this time with all the reports and certificates. This year we have three specialists. So there's nothing more we can do to crosscheck," added Ghosh.

Heading: Trials for youth games - Indian Express
Content:
Rashid Kumar's flawless displays on the gold course will once again be the cynosure of all eyes as the LG Amateur Golf Tour moves on to the sixth leg of the season.

Rashid would be hoping for another win this week to consolidate his position on the Order of Merit list. Halfway into the season, Gagan Verma is leading the list but with a long way to go, the race to the top is still wide open and a number of players are still in contention.

More than a hundred golfers are registered for the pre-qualifying rounds, but since most of the top forty in the order of merit list are playing this week, only 50 golfers could make it to the main draw. Play was suspended due to persistent showers in the afternoon and the field has been pruned based on player scores over nine holes.

The course is in prime condition after playing host to the professionals last week where the cut fell at six over par. The winning score this week is expected to be around five-under, a low score for an amateur tournament, but with the fairways being soft and the greens not as fast they would be expected, five-under appears to be a good winning score.

Heading: Police fumble with names, ‘probe on’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Athletics Federation of India will conduct events for youngsters during the trial for the Games at Balewadi Stadium, Pune, between September 19 and 21. These trials will form the basis of the final selection of athletes for participation in the Youth Commonwealth Games to be held in Pune between October 12 and 18.

The events for which trials will be conducted are: 100m, 200m, 400m, 800m, 1500m, 5000m/3000m, 110mH(m) /100mH(w), long jump, triple jump, high jump, pole vault, discus, javelin throw, hammer, shot put, 4x100m relay, 4x400m relay.

Heading: Alert ragpickers rewarded, kept off media glare for ‘security reasons’ - Indian Express
Content:
Though the Delhi Police have not been able to put together a tangible file on Saturday's serial blasts in the Capital, investigators in other cities have come up with four names — Raqeeb, Mujib, Mohammad Afridi and Shah Alam — who they think might have had a hand. All four are from western Uttar Pradesh.

Three names are also floating in Delhi: Abu Zar, Danish and Aftab. Several police teams have raided various places in the Capital, Muzaffarnagar, Baraut, Baghpat, Azamgarh, Faridabad and Ghaziabad to look for these men. It is learnt 13 people are in detention all over, being quizzed about Abu Zar, suspected Delhi blast mastermind Subhan and one Qayamuddin, who has recently emerged as a possible suspect in the Ahmedabad blasts.

However, Joint Commissioner (Special Cell) Karnal Singh refused to comment. "Investigations are on," he said.

Police Commissioner Y S Dadwal was positively gruff. "This is not a cricket match that I have to keep up a commentary," he told Newsline.

On Saturday, right after the blasts, Dadwal had said the police were "close to cracking the case since officers had vital clues".

Karnal Singh said the police were looking at any clue that might lead to the Indian Mujahideen since this group had signed on the mails sent after the Ahmedabad, Jaipur, Hyderabad and Delhi blasts. The content of all mails was similar.

A senior police officer said: "Abu Bashar, arrested by the Gujarat Police, was in Delhi before his arrest. So were Subhan and Qayamuddin. We suspect nearly 10 people planted bombs in Delhi."

A Delhi team is also closely monitoring Bashar's interrogation.

Sketches not clear
Though the police had made rudimentary sketches of the suspects — with inputs from eyewitnesses, including autodriver Moolchand — these couldn't be released till Monday evening. "Still not clear," said Karnal Singh. All eyewitnesses have reportedly said the suspects were men in their 20s. The police is also planning security for eyewitnesses.

2000 mobile numbers under watch
The Special Cell has reportedly put nearly 2,000 mobile numbers under surveillance since it feels blast suspects had called each other up before and after the attack. They are also trying to find out who called other cities, Mumbai and some in Uttar Pradesh. These 2,000 numbers have been randomly selected, an officer said.

Heading: Bomb disposal squad story: full dress, only rehearsal - Indian Express
Content:
Delhi Police's new 'special officers', the ragpickers who gave information about live bombs at three spots on Saturday evening, did not turn up in front of the media on Monday due to "security reasons".

They, along with other bravehearts both in police and public, were to be rewarded by Delhi Police Commissioner Y S Dadwal at the Police Headquarters in the function.

"The ragpickers cannot be presented in front of camera due to security reasons," Delhi Police spokesperson Rajan Bhagat said. "But they, along with others, were rewarded at the Commissioner's office today."

Among those present at the event were the officers who disposed off bombs at Regal Cinema in Connaught Place and Children's Park, India Gate: Suresh Kumar, Praveen, P N Subhash, Ashok Kumar and Joginder Singh.

Subhash, who diffused the bomb along with beat colleagues Suresh and Praveen at Regal, said, "A local vendor, Kundan Singh, came running to us around 6.30 pm — he was screaming like there was no tomorrow, saying a bomb had been found in a dustbin near the theatre.

"We rushed there and asked the public first to vacate the place at the earliest, without creating further panic. We didn't have any option — calling in bomb disposal squad could have been too late — so we went ahead and diffused it ourselves."

Suresh Kumar said, "We were taught the basics of it during training; we used that knowledge."

Ashok Kumar and Joginder took care of the bomb found at Children's Park. Joginder said, "A ragpicker told us about the bomb in a dustbin. We immediately took it to a vacant place." Constable Kumar added, "During classes at training we were told about defusing bombs in emergency cases. That came handy on Saturday."

Members of GK-I Market Association were also rewarded for the alacrity they showed after the twin blasts in the market. Rajender Sharda, president of GK-I Traders' Welfare Association, said, "We cordoned off the area immediately after the blasts, and everyone else around helped us."

Heading: Released, detainees say quizzed on SIMI, Bashar and 9/11 - Indian Express
Content:
Crumbling stairs in the backyard of Parliament Street police station lead to the one-room Bomb Disposal Squad's (BDS) office. With its jurisdiction running into three police districts, the squad has an additional room where all the sophisticated equipment is kept, along with a cot for its staff to stretch their legs.

Delhi Police has four such BDS, one for each police range and one for the Crime Branch, and nearly 70 officials in the specialised squad. But, on Saturday evening, the onus of disposing off the three live bombs fell on NSG teams. And Delhi Police's BDS officials? They stood as onlookers.

"We have the capacity to dispose off bombs but when sophisticated and trained teams from NSG and Army are available, it is better to use their expertise," Delhi Police spokesperson Rajan Bhagat said.

So, at the end of the day, the police squad merely detects bombs. "We have been told clearly to inform the NSG and Army teams if the bombs are too sophisticated," a senior BDS officer said. "We have to ensure safety by using sand bags and bomb blankets till they arrive."

The NSG team is stationed at Samalkha, the Army Engineering Corps team at Delhi Cantonment.

The BDS, though, is not short of sophisticated electronic devices. Among these are the non-linear junction detector — the latest addition in its arsenal — used to detect all electronic devices containing semi-conductors and bi-metallic junctions. Then there are radio transmitters, power amplified microphones, electronic timers and so on.

The BDS also has explosive vapour detectors — automatic hand-held devices that read vapour released by any object to ascertain the kind of explosive. Other equipment include X-ray machines, deep search metal detectors, bomb blankets, bomb suits and tool kits.

Heading: Teen’s kin say RML doctors ‘failed to see’ pellets in body - Indian Express
Content:
Any tentative lead that might have prompted the police's Special Cell to detain three men on Sunday morning had fizzled out by late evening when officers released them, one even offering to drop home 'suspect' Abdul Rashid Agwan.

For ten hours, these men — NGO director Agwan from Shaheen Bagh, young publisher Adnan from Jamia Nagar and another unidentified man from Okhla Vihar — were grilled at the Special Cell office in Lodhi Colony.

During this time, they faced a range of questions from whether they knew Ahmedabad blast mastermind Abu Bashar, any member of SIMI and if their recent travel trips had taken them to Bangalore, Jaipur or Ahmedabad.

Newsline caught up with Agwan and Adnan Fahad on Monday to learn what the officers had asked. Adnan, 28, was not at home when the police arrived at his door in Abul Fazal Enclave around 10.30 am on Sunday. His wife called him with the news. "I rushed home to find several officers in plainclothes waiting at the parking lot, another six were in my hall," Adnan said.

The officers did not identify themselves and escorted him to a car. The cavalcade of six cars then stopped at Agwan's house from where they went to Okhla Vihar. "We were all in different cars. At the police office, we were also put in separate cabins. I had no idea it was in connection with Saturday's serial blasts," Adnan said.

The police first wanted to know about his work — he has a printing and publishing company at Daryaganj. After that, they sprung a few names on him — Hamil Parvez, Abdul Rashid, Abu Bashar and Abu Zayed. Did he know them?

Sources said this is standard procedure if the police want to catch someone off-guard. They first ramble fictitious names, in this case perhaps Hamil Parvez, and then slip out the name of a suspected terrorist.

Adnan was also asked if he had recently been to any of the cities where serial blasts took place or whether he had any links with the SIMI. He was also posed a few questions on America's twin tower attacks. Finally, he was asked where he was on Saturday evening, Adnan told Newsline. "Around 10.30 pm, I was made to sign a few papers without reading them. I was released soon after," Adnan said.

Fifty-five-year old Agwan's story is similar. "I was picked up by six officers around noon. My interrogators told me they had specific information that I was not home on Saturday between 6 and 7 pm. I told them I was entertaining scientist friends in my house at that time. The police kept on at it till I gave them my friends' numbers to cross-check," Agwan said.

He was then asked about Abu Bashar. He did not know Bashar, Agwan told them, nor did he know any SIMI activist. Agwan also informed them he was a member of Jamat-e-Islami-e-Hind. "I was questioned about the organisation. They wanted to know the profiles of members and the topics of our discussions," he said. "It was all very pointless. One cop offered to drop me home," Agwan said.

Heading: Sarojini blast survivor hits Ground Zero again: to help victims - Indian Express
Content:
Barely lit, the winding staircase leads to a small room of a three-storey building in Shakti Nagar: this is where the Manrals live. The shelter costs the family Rs 2,000 every month and Basanti Devi is anxious how they would manage to pay the rent, with daughter Nisha in hospital following Saturday's blast at Gaffar Market.

"Nisha was our only earning member, and I don't know what we will do when the landlord comes calling later this month," Basanti Devi says. The 19-year-old, the third of her six children, worked in ICICI Bank and had gone to Gaffar Market with friend Babita on Saturday.

Babita died in the blast.

With husband Madan Singh still recovering from the severe heart attack he suffered recently, Basanti Devi says a small "negligence" in attending to Nisha's injury at RML Hospital made matters worse for the family.

The family says RML doctors overlooked metal pallets stuck in Nisha's shoulder and discharged her after stitching the wounds. Cousin Kalpana, who brought her home on Saturday, says Nisha could not sleep the whole night — "she was howling in pain."

They took her to RML on Sunday, and X-rays showed the pellet still lodged inside. "She underwent operation today," Kalpana says, "but I am sure she would not have suffered so much if they had detected the metal on the first day itself."

Irate, Kalpana says she tried to point out the "negligence" to hospital authorities, but "they were just not ready to accept responsibility — they even said Nisha was not treated at RML."

Chief Medical Officer S K Sharma says, "Nisha did not have our slip when she came complaining of pain yesterday."

Sources in the hospital, meanwhile, say the CMO has called an internal meeting to inquire the case, and also another related to Akhilesh Kumar who returned for further treatment.

"My daughter has stitches on her shoulder and neck — she is bedridden. And despite being her mother, I am thinking about the rent," Basanti Devi says. "At an age when other girls are studying and having fun, my daughter is looking after all of us."

Heading: The hunt is on! - Indian Express
Content:
Having been saved by a fraction when blasts rocked Sarojini Nagar market in October 2005, Ashok Randhawa, 46, is in the frontline, helping victims of Saturday's blasts. With a team of 15 volunteers who are ready to donate blood whenever required, Randhawa has as good as camped outside RML Hospital: he visits the patients once a day, and provides their relatives with drinking water bottles, tea and food.

"Besides other friends, my closest friend Lalit, of Shyam Juice Corner, died in the 2005 blast," he says. "I witnessed death from just a fraction away," says the garment shopowner.

On Saturday evening, Randhawa, president of Sarojini Nagar Mini Market Traders' Association, was collecting money from fellow shopkeepers for Bihar flood victims. "We planned to collect at least Rs 5 lakh," he says. But the effort had to be stopped midway, for news of the first blast at Karol Bagh had trickled in by then. "We carried on collecting money, only to realise in a while that Delhi was once again the target of serial blasts."

Randhawa then had only one aim, and run he did, all the way to RML Hospital.

VINAY Gautam could not judge the age of the screaming victim thrust into his arms moments after he ran to the blast spot on Barakhabha Road. "I could not tell how old she was — all I saw was blood on her from head to toe.

"She murmured something. But I could not make sense of it," says the 25-year-old intern with the local news channel Total TV. "I got hold of her hand to help her stand and asked another man to help the woman — I was unable to lift her."

No time to think, that evening he did what his heart told his brain: he left the woman in black at a police vehicle and ran back to help others.

"There were seven or eight bodies, all maimed, and I carried five of them…. There was an old man, dead.

"I saw a woman in her 40s falling off an auto-rickshaw due to the blast's impact." Gautam took her to the police vehicle, and returned to help the auto driver, later identified as one Karuna Singh. Reflecting, two days on, he says, "I don't think I did anything exceptional. I did what every human being should do in such time of crisis."

Heading: What is Op art ? - Indian Express
Content: Fiama Di Wills has launched the 'Fiama Di Wills Beautiful Face 2008 Hunt'. The contest will provide an opportunity to aspiring models across the country to represent India in the International Elite Model Look contest to be held in China in November 2008. In addition, the winner of the contest becomes the Fiama Beautiful Face 2008 and gets an opportunity to be in Fiama di Wills ads. Deepika Padukone, Fiama Di Wills Brand ambassador for its range of soaps and shower gels formally launched the contest. From all the entries received, 15 girls will be short-listed and taken for grooming to New Delhi at the Elite Model School. The contestants will then go on to compete in the final round of the Elite Model Look India Hunt 2008 which will be held at the Wills Lifestyle India Fashion Week from October 15 to 19 in Delhi.  According to Sushma Puri, CEO, Elite Model Management India, "The contestants will get an opportunity of a lifetime to participate in the International Elite Model Look contest where models are selected from approximately 50 countries. The winner of each national final goes on to participate in the international final event which is held over 10 days. A jury of models, world renowned photographers and other professionals from the industry select the winners. The 15 international finalists receive a two year guaranteed modeling contract from Elite". One can log on to www.elitemodelsindia.com for participating in the contest.

Heading: Double Trouble - Indian Express
Content:
Getting a friend at art school once joked that Op art is Pop with the P fallen off. We tend to link these two movements because of their similar sounding names, but actually the two are separated by almost 20 years. Op is the abbreviation for Optical Illusion and Pop of course stands for Popular Culture.

While the former movement was an offshoot of the German Bauhaus constructivist theories perpetrated by Walter Gropius in 1933, the latter emerged in Britain in the 1950s as a response to mass media and mass culture. The principle of Op art is to induce an illusion of movement and vibration, swelling or warping through the use of pure geometric forms. Pop art is tackled head-on with the breaking down of the artist as a 'talented genius' and embraced mediums like the comic book and banal kitschy elements of everyday life. It was a response that opposed the elitism of High Art. Art critics like John Berger and Lawrence Alloway have interesting takes on pop art, which arguably looked less like art and more like mass produced media images.

Op art, on the other hand, was not an opposition of high art or culture; it is a more playful and purely visual, and in fact upholds some of the tenets of high art. For example, Minimalist Frank Stella was a prominent artist whose work has been cited as Op Art. To understand the subtitles of figure and ground which Op art plays with, there is an assumption of a certain 'intellectual' quality that is a pre-requisite for enjoying Op Art.

One could argue, however, that the unstoppable forces of popular culture did subsume some of the illusionary visual patterns of Op Art into the Flower Power and the Hippie Movement. Many design schools took off on Bridget Riley's paintings and made it part of fabric and soft furniture design. Riley, a British-born artist, was hugely popular during the 1950s when she began her iconic black-and-white squares that were said to induce giddiness and sea-sickness in viewers. It produced sensations similar to hallucinogenic drugs and on an intellectual level tied up with the anxieties expressed by writers like Aldous Huxley—the angst of a future driven by science and technology that could either be beneficial or detrimental for mankind.

Demystify art, e-mail georgina.maddox@expressindia.com

Heading: Full Throttle - Indian Express
Content:
Season six of MTV Roadies promises many more twists, and twice as much of Raghu Ram as well

If you found one Raghu Ram a bit hard to take on MTV's Roadies, there's some bad news in store. On the sixth season of the dramatic adventure reality show Raghu's identical twin Rajeev Laxman will join him to create even more hell for the contestants. "Every year we take the show to another level. This time we have upped the stakes even further," smiles Raghu, the irreverent boss of the Roadies, and Associate VP, MTV shows. With the number of roadies increased to 20 and the prize money doubled to Rs 10 lakhs, contestants are in for hell Down Under with difficult tasks on the deadly terrains of Austalia and biting observations and sheer wrath from the Raghu-Rajeev duo.

Rajeev— who has been part of the casting process of the Roadies for the last four years— agreed to even turn bald for the show on Raghu's insistence. Hard to tell the two apart, Rajeev will now be introduced to the viewers for the first time. "Roadies is not just about the money. It's a badge that makes people discover a side to them that they didn't even know of," adds Rajeev, who appears to be almost as aggressive as his twin. "Actually I'm more violent and Raghu is more aggressive," smiles Rajeev wickedly. "But we use these characteristics only to push the buttons of the contestants to get their reaction."

But what really prompted them to bring the twist of the twins? "Over the past years people have started observing my behavioral pattern. So essentially, now with both of us appearing on the show, the contestants will not know who they are dealing with," adds Raghu with a smile.

While it's the curses and abuses by Raghu that have made contestants quake with fear and seethe in anger in the past, some of the past roadies have overcome it all and even found alternative careers in the course of it. While Rannvijay, Bani J and Ayushmann all became VJs on the channel, others like Ashutosh Kaushik went on to participate in Big Boss and Shambhavi Sharma has been roped in for a Suniel Shetty movie.

However, MTV Roadies— the only Indian format to be licensed abroad by the ARY Pakistan— will journey through every place from Great Barrier Reef to the Great Outback this year. "It's a scientific fact that there are more ways of dying of natural causes in Australia than anywhere else in the world," quips Ashish Patil, GM, MTV India. While their parameters to zero in on the tasks include dangerous topography, Patil agrees imbibing the local culture is as important. While there might be the Roadies Cheat Code DVD available in the market to crack the auditions, Raghu still warns, "Fakes not allowed. I don't like people who plan. You need to be real and we'll take it from there."

If you thought it was Raghu walking in to twist things at Splitsvilla, MTV's reality show about love, here's a trivia —it was Rajeev. Expect the unexpected.

Heading: West Side Story - Indian Express
Content:
The Johnnie Walker F1 party on Sunday night ran high on fashion and to a full house

Fun, fast and furious. It can either be a Formula One race or an equally high-paced fashion show. Don't agree? Well, then you clearly missed the Johnnie Walker Formula One party that saw the city raise a toast to fashion and fast action. Hosted at The Taj, the show brought in the rather good looking Vodafone McLaren Mercedes MP4/22 show car which hogged centrestage on the ramp. The evening also saw the unveiling of the much-awaited Johnnie Walker Formula One inspired fashion line put together by fashion guru Manish Arora.

The evening first saw the city's select few (that seemed to be quite many in number) down some drinks and nibble on gossip and starters. The actual fashion show rolled out when the celebrity guest Mahima Chaudhary, who made the most of her trip to Chandigarh, walked in looking rather dishy in a black number. Once the clock touched ten, the lights dimmed and the guests got to see a show reel of Formula One and Johnnie Walker's delectable range of Scotch. All the while the tempo of the music was a mix of Formula One - very fast and edgy. The show reels done with, model and emcee Divya Jaitely stepped on stage and got the crowds animated with her trivia questions and some free gifts, all of which were duly lapped up. Then came in Diageo India's managing director Asif Adil who raised a formal toast and finally got the show to begin. What began on stage was a visual psychedelic treat. Leading runway faces like Tina Chatwal, Laxmi Rana, Manasvi Mamgai, Joey Mathews, Nayonika Chatterjee, Indrani Das Gupta, Sonalika Sahay...sporting blonde and ash coloured wigs complete with full-bling makeup, wearing black spandex tights teamed up with equally shimmering tunics and Tees walked out. The clothes were anything but pret with the Johnnie Walker insignia all over them in gold. The highlight however was the music and the fast pace of the show that finally wrapped up with Mahima coming on stage to bid adieu.

All in all, a neat package.

Heading: Present Reaction - Indian Express
Content:
A slew of fashion shows across the world see Indian designers headed west

With the New York Fashion Week getting over on Friday and the London Fashion Week starting this week, the fashion season has kicked off across the globe with a bang. Big events like the Paris Fashion Week are scheduled for the end of the month. If that's keeping the likes of Anamika Khanna, Manish Arora and Rajesh Pratap Singh busy, there's more happening over the next couple of weeks to keep everyone on their toes. Here's a lowdown on who is headed where in the world from the Indian contingent:

Ravi Bajaj
In his career spanning well over a decade, designer Ravi Bajaj has always kept well away from the Indian fashion weeks. However, it seems Bajaj is more than game to put up a show abroad. The Delhi designer will be showcasing eight collections comprising 65 ensembles at a show at Los Angeles' swanky Hilton Hotel today. With a bunch of American models and a guest list of about 250, Bajaj is all set to give his NRI clients a taste of home-grown fashion with his latest coup: a poncho sari. "For many NRIs, the sari is something immensely attractive though they cannot wear it properly. I have taken that into account for this collection," he says. Post the show in LA, Bajaj will then head to Dubai and Jakarta over the next six weeks for further shows and exhibitions.

Renu Tandon
Come October and Delhi designer Renu Tandon will head to Dubai for her maiden appearance at the Dubai Fashion Week scheduled between October 5-9. Tandon has been invited by Dubai-based fashion boutique, Mumbai Se, to showcase her label Mynah. The designer known for her high-bling quotient is quite popular with the NRIs and had recently been invited to Singapore for an exhibition by the local Sindhi Association. In Dubai, though, her show on October 7 would be sponsored by the company Red Sea Housing Services.

Rina Dhaka
Her beach collection with its abbreviated bikini tops and patchwork thongs had created a furore at a desi fashion week appearance a couple of years back, but Delhi designer Rina Dhaka has mellowed down since. This season, Dhaka is headed for London Fashion Week to take part in the exhibition there. The exhibition, LFW's official showcase of talents from across the world has over 210 designers participating.

Samant Chauhan
A young designer, Chauhan has already carved a niche for himself in the industry. After an outing at the London Fashion Week last season he will now be seen at the Ethical Fashion Show in Paris, promoting fair trade practices and eco-friendly materials. Then there's the Tranoi Fair in Paris before he turns homeward for the India Fashion Week. His new collection will see his take on indigenous fabric.

Heading: Act Apart - Indian Express
Content:
Meet 11-year-olds from the city who can make their own robots and do the programming too!

What do kids do when they get bored of their toys? Buy new ones, right? Wrong! Srijan Gupta and Aditya Puranik model out their own. A black-line tracer becomes a ball picker, a robot meant to travel on a smooth surface transforms into tough-terrain robot and in this case tools take the shape of a robot that can hit three cans placed in three different directions with utmost ease. A robot, the mechanics of which has made them the only team from Chandigarh to succeed at the India Robot Olympiad '08 and be invited to the World Robot Olympiad '08, which will be held at Yokohama, Japan.

"Assigned as a part of our project in St John's High School, our mentor Parminder Malik helped us create it," smiles Srijan, as he shows us the programming techniques on the laptop and tells us that their team won the runner-up prize in the primary school category. Made with LEGO Mindstorms kit, "this has touch and light sensors, sound sensor and ultrasonic sensor," Aditya tells us that from deciding the number of motors required for the robot to connecting the input and output devices, they have done it all. "The 32-bit command center is used in a manner to give maximum utility," they chorus displaying the use of drag-and-drop interface and configuring the objects.

The robot took the boys about two months to reach its final completion. "We did not sleep for many nights," say these engineers in the making, as they talk about the about 32 options they had thought of and created. "After conceptualization, we took into consideration all the terrains that it can go on and the constraints," says Aditya, as he astonishes all with his calculations and reasoning. But for them, it's just about having fun. "While last year we only participated in the World Robot Olympiad held in Taiwan, this year we will win it too." Whoever said youngsters these days are uselessly whiling away time on gaming and computers, needs to meet them!

Heading: Chandigarh tops again in per capita income - Indian Express
Content:
An increasing number of city colleges are inviting experts on campus to polish students' extra curricular skills

It's a rat race. One college starts a trend and the others follow. But for this one, they say, "it's just the need of the hour". One that is beneficial, both to the college and the students. "We get the goodwill while the students get the much needed skill set," smiles Puneet Bedi, principal of MCM College, as she takes us to the auditorium where Amita Shabdeesh, a theatre artist, is helping the students prepare a play 'Jis Pind Ka Koi Naam Nahi'. "A professional, Shabdeesh helps them learn the art in a perfect way," Bedi says, as we all turn to see Ridhima Puri, a BA final year student's act. Her voice deep, eyes filled with grief and legs shivering, she enacts her part and Deepika Duggal, a second year student takes on from there. "Coaching has been on for about one and a half months," chips in Shabdeesh, who has held classes in GCG 11 and Khalsa College, Ludhiana, in the past.

Elsewhere Michael, a Boogie Woogie winner, teaches the tricks of the dance floor to the students of University Institute of Applied Management Sciences (UIAMS). "Slide, step and move," we hear him as we enter the old UIET building (the slotted place for practice) and follow the music. The room is buzzing with about 20 young faces. Rahul Rishi, a freshers turns and tells us, "We got money for preparations sanctioned from the University authorities." Here, from Salsa, Bollywood to Punjabi dance, they learnt it all for the freshers party.

While, colleges and the university make events an excuse to groom their products, "The real cause is to develop them into all-rounders," chirps Ashok Garg, incharge of cultural affairs at DAV College, who is set to make his students participate in all the 42 events in the PU Zonal Youth and Heritage Festival to be held from October 21 to 24 at GC-46. The will to win, he agrees, is a major criteria, "but over and above is the endeavour to teach the students subjects we don't even have," he says.

Surinder Khan, a music expert, is busy honing the skills of students in Shabad, group singing, ghazal, folk songs, classical music vocal at DAV College. The college is also on the lookout for someone for the fine arts section to train the students in still life, landscaping and clay modelling.

At Government College, Sector 46, the focus is on Bhangra and Gidda. "It's an opportunity for the students to move away from studies and computers and do some physical activity," chips in Dr Sahib Singh, organizing secretary of the Youth Festival. Paramjit Tewari, former Dean Students Welfare (Women), too agrees. "It's an opportunity for those who want to become professionals in streams other than their subjects. And besides, it's good for their mental health and wholesome grooming that multi-national companies need today." Why even the girls' hostel at PU got a professional karate trainer? Need we say more!

Heading: Direct railway link to Baddi likely - Indian Express
Content:
Chandigarh has once again bagged the top position in the country as far as the per capita income is concerned. While Goa clinches the second position, Haryana has slipped to the sixth spot. The constantly increasing per capita income of Chandigarh has multiplied about 2.5 times in the last eight years.

While the average per capita income of Chandigarh was Rs 44,502 in 2000, it has increased to Rs 1,10,676 in 2008, as per the quick estimates collected by the UT Economics and Statistics department.

The Directorate of Economics and Statistics (Statistical Cell) brought out the facts in the 'annual statistics of state domestic product/per capita income', measured both at current and constant prices.

Raji P Shrivastava, Special Secretary, Finance, and Director, Economics and Statistics, released the publication on Monday.

The statistics uphold the belief that Chandigarh is a city that has firmly moved away from the primary sector in terms of occupation. The Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) of the city has the highest component of tertiary sector — around 78.09 per cent at constant prices — since 1999-2000, with 75.91 per cent in the year under review (2008).

Industries or the manufacturing sector, called 'secondary sector', has contributed around 20.69 per cent since 1999-2000, with 23.54 per cent in the review year at constant prices.

The contribution of the primary sector — agriculture and allied activities — has been quite low in Chandigarh since 1999-2000 and it has gone down further. All thanks to the change of land use and rampant urbanisation, the contribution of this sector, which was only 1.22 per cent in 1999-2000 has slipped further to 0.55 per cent in 2007-08 at constant prices.

The GSDP has shown a growth of 12.94 per cent during the last year and 244.17 per cent since 1999-2000 at constant prices.

The per capita income of Chandigarh was the highest in the country in 2006-07 both in terms of current and constant prices.

The latest estimates prepared and published by the Directorate of Economics and Statistics, UT, are for the year 2005-06 (Provisional), 2006-07 (Quick) and 2007-08 (Advance).

Heading: Fish mortality in Sukhna cause for worry - Indian Express
Content:
New line aims to facilitate movement of industrial goods; work to start in 2009

The Northern Railways has proposed a rail link to the industrial town of Baddi in Himachal Pradesh from Chandigarh. The direct link promises to provide a mass rapid transport system and facilitate the movement of industrial goods.

Estimated to cost Rs 750.81 crore, the 33.75-kilometre link will have six railway stations — Chandigarh, Saketri, Khuda Ali Sher, Kasauli (Punjab), Khokara Nawahnagar (Haryana) and Baddi — en route. Saketri and Khokara Nawahnagar will be the halt stations while Khuda Ali Sher and Kasauli will be the crossing stations.

The railway authorities have already conducted the final location survey to check the feasibility of this new line. The project alignment will entail 11 major bridges, 27 minor bridges, two road over-bridges, eight road under-bridges and nine tunnels.

"This new line has been proposed after proper economic, feasibility and land surveys," said Chief Public Relation Officer Rajiv Saxena.

"Since Baddi is emerging as an important industrial town in Himachal, the new rail link was the need of the hour. It will connect the town to all other major destinations of the country, which will help in the movement of industrial products and raw material," he added.

There was an in-principal approval for this link in the Rail Budget 2007-08.

Union Minister for Railways Lalu Prasad had declared that all such proposals were to be considered on the highest priority.

Under the expansion plans of the Northern Railways, work on the project will start from April 2009. Officials said a detailed estimate for the project was being worked out, after which the procedure for acquisition of land would be initiated.


he schedule of trains, which had been diverted or cancelled due to the re-modelling work under way at the New Delhi Railway Station, has been restored. 'Non-interlocking' work at the New Delhi station had resulted in temporary cancellation, diversion, change of origin and destination stations of many trains from September 5. While the Kalka Shatabdi Express was back to its old schedule from September 13, the Jan Shatabdi Express and other trains — Himalayan Queen, Paschim Express, Kerala Sampark Kranti and Unchahar Express — too would follow their original route from Tuesday, officials said.
