Heading: The rising Suraj-milk vendor to a successful businessman - Indian Express
Content:
Around 15 dead fish were found floating in the Sukhna waters on Monday morning, causing concern about the safety of aquatic life in the lake. Preliminary investigations have revealed that the fish could have died because of deposition of sand in their gills.

The dead fish were removed and their samples sent to the Department of Zoology, Panjab University, for tests. Water samples were also collected by the Chandigarh Pollution Control Committee.

Prof M S Johal from the department said: "I have analysed the samples. The fish died a day earlier. Investigation shows sand deposited in their gills cut off the supply of oxygen, which led to asphyxiation. During the rainy season, silt deposits increase in the lake."

He added that since the number of dead fish was not very high it could not be termed as mass mortality. "The fish could be physiologically weak, which led to their death. Regular monitoring of water and aquatic life is essential. Sampling should be done at fixed intervals to ensure there is nothing that adversely affects the water," said Prof Johal.

Water samples are being tested to check for the presence of heavy metals or toxic substances.

Deputy Conservator of Forests Ishwar Singh said: "There were no signs of any injury on the bodies of the dead fish. They appeared quite healthy. Fish tend to die during the rainy season. Tests are being conducted to ensure that the water in the lake is free of polluting agents. The report is expected in the next two to three days."

According to Dr Kawaldeep Kaur, Dean, Fisheries, Panjab Agricultural University, fish tend to die if organic content in the water is more and toxic gases are released. "At times, there is a sudden change in the temperature of water. It is necessary to test the quality of water to know the exact causes that led to the deaths," she said.

Heading: Little security in place, is Chandigarh the next target? - Indian Express
Content:
The village of Shahkot in Punjab is reverberating with the tales of a milkman, whose unflinching determination saw him transform a life of penury into prosperity.

Milk vendor Sandeep Arora alias Suraj, a matriculate, is now the proud owner of a chain of artificial jewellery stores located in the most upmarket shopping areas of the country.

The list — ten in Chandigarh, and one each in Guwahati, Shimla, Bathinda, Panipat, Amritsar and Patiala — goes on. So, what is next for this milkman with the 'Midas touch'? Suraj has got one store each booked at the Shalimar Mall, The Bella Vista Shopping mall in Panchkula and at the Paras Down Town at Zirakpur.

"It was a long nerve-racking and stressful journey which I had to undergo to be where I am today," says Suraj, maintaining that there is no shortcut to success.

"It was in 1994, when frustrated by the monotonous and mundane routine of selling milk, I decided to shift to Chandigarh where my elder brother used to work. With inadequate education, I failed to get a job and started selling lemonade outside the Sector 17 bus stand," adds Suraj.

This job too did not give him much satisfaction. "I would stitch chiffon rubber bands and sell them from a footpath in Sector 22," he recalls.

Admitting to a slow start, Suraj says: "The business soon started showing an upward trend and finally I decided to take a shop on rent."

For him, childhood was not about playing with toys. "I used to get up early in the morning and sell milk throughout the day. Worst were the days when I would go to bed at two and get up at five and had to go without meals," recalls Suraj.

All his pains disappeared the day he went home from Chandigarh and gave the keys of his shop to his mother. "I told her that we now own a shop in the same area where I used to sit on the footpath," beams an emotional Suraj.

According to Suraj, what turned things around for him was a call from the Fun Republic to put up a stall on Baisakhi Mela. "After the success of that stall, I was offered a permanent place at the mall. There was no looking back then," he says.

"My parents have faced many hardships and now I want to provide them with everything. I aspire to spread my business all around the country," adds Suraj, revealing his three-word mantra for success — Mother, Honesty and God.

Heading: Father gets life term for raping minor daughter - Indian Express
Content:
As the nation is on a virtual alert post the recent serial blasts in Delhi, authorities in Chandigarh are doing little to suggest of any pre-emptive measures. The railway station, bus stands and airport in the city look as penetrable as ever with little sense of security.

At the airport, the checking procedure only consists of frisking done at the entry point of the main terminal and that also just to ensure that the passenger is carrying an air ticket. There is no extra checking or scanning of the luggage at the airport. When asked about the security situation after the blasts, Airport Director Sunil Dutt said, "We are on alert,"— where and how only the authorities know.

The situation at the railway station and ISBT-Sector 17 and 43 is worse. Neither is any security staff deputed at these places nor is there a check on abandoned luggage. "Seeing the attitude of the authorities leaves us shocked. There is no checking at the entry point of the railway station. The only checking is done in the train and that too only in Shatabdi, which is more of a casual routine," said a passenger at the railway station.

Passengers at the ISBT-17 and 43 shared similar views. "Seeing the lax attitude of the authorities, it seems nothing has happened. We were expecting at least a couple of security men on patrol at the bus stand," said an elderly couple waiting for a bus at ISBT, Sector 17.

Another commuter added that even the Volvo considered to be one of the safest conveyances, lacks proper checking of luggage. It is a safety concern for the public that needs to be addressed immediately."

BJP seeks more security
The Chandigarh unit of BJP has urged the Union Home Ministry to take immediate steps for ensuring safety and security of residents in view of the terror threats and serial blasts.In a statement issued on Monday, president of the Chandigarh unit Kamla Sharma and former MP Satya Pal Jain stressed that despite numerous warnings of terror attacks in Delhi, the Centre did not take adequate steps in time.

"The government should not repeat the mistake and act in time to prevent such mishaps in future," she said. The leaders added that crime in the city is escalating. There has been an increase in the number of thefts, snatchings and murder cases. A delegation of BJP will meet the UT Administrator on Tuesday and submit a memorandum listing their concerns.

Heading: Cash at judge’s door: Ravinder deserves no relief, says HC bar - Indian Express
Content:
A local court on Monday awarded life imprisonment to a father who allegedly raped his 15-year-old daughter repeatedly. Gajjan Singh, the accused, was sentenced under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC).

"There can never be more graver and heinous a crime than a father being charged of raping his own daughter. It is a loathsome sin and an unpardonable act," the verdict said.

"When the perpetrator of the crime is the father against his own daughter, it is more graver than the rarest of the rare," noted Additional District and Sessions Judge Raj Shekhar Attri.

The minor girl has also been granted protection under Section 357 (3) of the IPC under which the father is also entitled to give her a compensation of Rs 1 lakh.

Besides, the UT Administration, through its home secretary, has also been directed to bear the educational and boarding charges of the girl until she is a major. The girl will continue to stay at the Nari Niketan.

The court also observed that it would now be difficult for the girl to stay with her stepmother, Laxmi, whom she accused of being a partner in the crime. The court has, however, acquitted Laxmi.

On Monday, the girl just wanted her tormentor to be sentenced. Having faced enough trauma at a tender age, the girl said she received justice today. "I want to study further and become an IAS officer," she said.

Flatly denying the allegations, meanwhile, the accused said his brothers had falsely implicated him for they want to grab his property. Awaiting sentence, he continued to lash allegations against his daughter and claimed innocence.

A resident of Khuda Ali Sher, Gajjan was married to one Nasib, the victim's mother. After Nasib died, Gajjan allegedly raped the victim repeatedly. The victim's uncle noted her plight in 2006 and reported the matter to the police. A case of rape was then registered.

Heading: Conversion policy not to be extended: UT Administration - Indian Express
Content:
The Bar Association of the Punjab and Haryana High Court has, as expected, moved an application demanding permission to intervene in the anticipatory bail application demanded by Ravinder Singh, co-accused in the judge bribery case.

The bail application is slated to come up for hearing on Tuesday in the court of Justice A N Jindal.

The court had directed the CBI to allow the presence of a counsel in case Ravinder surrenders. The CBI was also asked to not use third degree torture against him. The High Court Bar had expressed its strong resentment against the order of the single judge.

To voice its protest and contest the anticipatory bail demanded by Ravinder, the Bar has filed the application. Advocate Anupam Gupta will represent the Bar, as unanimously decided by it in its General House.

In the strongly worded application, Gupta has submitted "no allegation or accusation of torture, forget third degree torture, has been made by one who has been arrested and interrogated so far in the case, whether against the Chandigarh Police or the CBI, and the investigation has been conducted in an absolutely lawful and bona fide manner. It is evident that 'apprehension' voiced on behalf of the accused is a false alarm that deserves no credence whatsoever". The application further reads that this so called apprehension is an obvious red herring, clearly intended to deflect the attention of the court away from Ravinder's own criminal involvement and culpability as also the sheer brazenness with which he has continued to abscond and evade the clutches of the law.

"It lies in the mouth of such an absconder, who earlier corrupted the judicial system and now defies it, to speak of 'surrender' and to seek safeguards from this court to that end", Gupta has submitted.

Advocating custodial interrogation of Ravinder, the application reads that the process is absolutely imperative and indispensable and the grant of anticipatory bail to him, with or without conditions, will gravely impair and frustrate the investigation.

Ravinder, the kingpin of the corruption scandal and a highly connected, influential and resourceful person, has been absconding ever since the registration of the case by the Chandigarh Police on August 16. Holding that he deserves no relief from the court, the application further reads: "Apart from all other considerations, the very fact that Ravinder has remained willfully and continuously at large, defying all efforts and attempts to apprehend him firstly by the Chandigarh Police and now by the CBI, clearly disentitles to him any relief whatsoever from this court."

The Bar has also vehemently challenged the direction of the court in which it has been ordered that if Ravinder surrenders, his counsel will be directed to remain present in the court.

Heading: Hong Kong firm to expand research base in city - Indian Express
Content:
The conversion policy for the industrial area Phase-I and II is all set to be closed on September 18. This is keeping in mind the serious infrastructure-related problems, which are likely to choke the area, if anymore industrial plots are converted. The consensus was reached in a meeting of the Administration's top brass and representatives of various industrialists' associations.

While top officials were firm on not giving any extension to the Conversion Policy after September 18, sources said that the representatives of industrialists associations too sounded affirmative on the decision.

"As far as the fate of the pending applications is concerned, those will be processed but no more applications regarding conversion will be entertained after September 18. Of course, for the other industrialists, certain need-based changes can be allowed, depending upon the policy. We have roped in CII and PHD Chambers to prepare a detailed plan on the infrastructure development in the Industrial Area," said one of the senior UT Administration officials.

More than 47 industrial plots have already been converted to commercial complexes. With the area already coping with the lack of parking space, one of the major roadblocks in its development, and narrow roads, new commercial project will choke it further.

Regional Director of the Confederation of Indian Industries Charu Mathur, said: "The Chandigarh Administration must commensurate infrastructure with the development of the industrial area. The basic amenities including water, power, sanitation, parking and others should be provided in abundance, before further developing the area."

Chairman of the Chandigarh Industries and Traders Federation Jarnail Singh said that the Administration is confused about the policy. "They keep on changing the policy whenever an association raises objections on a particular issue. There has to be a clear policy outlined for those having 10 marla plots or one kanal plots."

Meanwhile, president of the Chandigarh Industrial Association MPS Chawla welcomed the decision to call a meeting of the representatives of the various associations. "We hope that a favourable decision will be taken."

Pawan Kumar Aggarwal, the president of the Industries Association of Chandigarh, said: "We request the Chandigarh Administration to have a transparent, uniform policy without frequent changes with retrospective. We also suggest resolving all the pending issues while deliberating with the representatives of the association."

On agenda
Transfer of plots: The Admn may allow transfer of lease hold plots to the GPA holders by fixing a reasonable price

changes in bylaws: For the development and expansion of industry, it may be allowed to increase in the ground coverage with 2 FAR at the existing compounding fee for the units.

Power Supply: The applications are pending for the extension of load and new connections for more than two years.

Sub-way connectivity to improve the movement and reduce the traffic congestion

Heading: Management institute to refund Rs 21,000 to ‘dissatisfied’ student - Indian Express
Content:
The Hong Kong-based provider of value added services and gaming platforms — Goldfinch Mobile Solutions — has expanded its Research & Development (R&D) base in India, making the Chandigarh IT Park its hub. The company, having operations in Malaysia and Indonesia, plans to invest nearly US $ 1.5 million into its operations across South-East Asia this year.

The new R&D centre in Chandigarh will focus on developing applications based on multiplayer gaming techniques on mobiles, mobile advertising and forming communities for gaming.

"We are bringing gaming to India in partnership with Ozura. A complete integrated Gaming Engine known as FunlogiX will be provided to the Indians. We will be targetting to launch these services for GSM and CDMA networks, besides DTH and IPTV as well," said Newton Bubber, CEO of Goldfinch.

The other R&D Centre in Singapore is engaged in evolving applications for Interactive Voice Response (IVR) services for mobile, web and WAP.

Newton said: "Research is also going on in Singapore for a new roaming service — My Alerts. This will help in informing a selected set of people through self-generated messages about the location of the person while travelling. It is expected to be launched in the international market in December."

Mobile advertising is another segment which Goldfinch is exploring. The company is in talks with Nokia to introduce advertising campaigns through IVR and WAP.

Heading: 5 fresh cases of dengue reported in Panchkula - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Redressal Forum has directed a management institute to refund Rs 21,000 taken as tuition fee from a student for providing insufficient services.

The complainant, Seema Saggu, a resident of Sector 15, stated that she got admission in the MBA Course at ICFAI, Hyderabad, by depositing Rs 14,500 through a credit card in June, 2007.

She stated she also paid Rs 6,500 besides handing over 16 post-dated cheques for clearance of the balance fee.

The complainant alleged that "dissatisfied" with the insufficient services rendered by the institute, she approached the programme coordinator in Chandigarh through email for discontinuation of the course.

The authorities forced her to honour all the post-dated cheques given to them at the time of the admission. After she stopped the payment, she was sent a legal notice.

The institute denied all allegations and said no such email was ever received. They also said that the fee was not refundable as per their terms and conditions.

The forum said that it has already been held in a plethora of judgments that institutions, while rendering no service, cannot seek any consideration.

It added that the fee is only to be charged for the services rendered and the charging of fee for the services, which are yet to be rendered, are totally unethical and unscrupulous.

Heading: No students’ polls in MCM DAV this year - Indian Express
Content: Five fresh cases of suspected dengue were reported from the General Hospital in Panchkula, taking the toll to 11. On Saturday, a 42-year-old resident of Sector 14, Panchanand Pandey, succummed to dengue at PGI. While three of the eleven cases are confirmed, the others are suspected cases. Sources said while the two cases have been reported from Sector, three were from Sector 21.

Heading: PUTA refuses to accept president’s resignation - Indian Express
Content:
Taking a serious view of the protests by the students of MCM DAV College, a joint committee was constituted on Monday, which decided to scrap this year's students' elections.

The committee comprised Raji P Shrivastava, Director Higher Education and Professor R C Sobti, Vice-Chancellor, Panjab University, among others who visited the college and heard the demands of the college authorities as well as the protesting students.

Other members of the committee included Professor Promila Kaushal, Principal of Government College for Girls, Sector 11, Professor KS Saluja, Principal, Government College, Sector 46, Jagdish Arora, Registrar, Education, UT Administration, Professor V S Jaswal, Department of Laws and VS Thakur, Assisitant Controller, Accounts, UT Administration.

After having a detailed discussion with the students and the college authorities, the committee verified the nomination papers of Himani Walia and Geeta Tariyar.

The committee found that while the papers submitted by Himani fulfilled the eligibility criterion for contesting the elections, those submitted by Geeta did not.

"The college has rightly cancelled Geeta's nomination for the post of president as she does not have the required attendance. While the criterion makes at least 75 per cent attendance mandatory, she has attended only 54 percent of the lectures. This is in violation of the Lyngdoh guidelines," said Shrivastava.

The committee also found that the issue of elections was blown out of proportion by the students as they involved outsiders as well.

"The involvement of a political party as well as an NGO added fuel to fire and complicated the matter. Moreover, we have found that there were some internal grievances that were brewing for a while and the elections became an excuse to vent them out," Shrivastava said.

After much deliberation, the committee decided not to hold any elections to any office of the student council in the college this year.

"After the youth festival gets over on September 26, there will be an autumn break followed by Dussera holidays. After the holidays, the students will have their mid-term exams till October. Since it will be too late to conduct elections in November, we have decided not to have them this year in the college's interest," stated Shrivastava.

In its findings, the committee also concluded that Principal Puneet Bedi's role was biased.

"We have prima facie evidence that Bedi's role was partisan. In fact, students have also alleged unjust treatment and discrimination on her part. If this is proved, we will form an advisory committee to look into the allegations against the principal. The students have also demanded her to be more approachable and address their problems more compassionately which has already been conveyed to her," added Shrivastava.

Heading: Senate polls: Professors’ constituency records 90 per cent turnout - Indian Express
Content:
Members of the PUTA executive body decided today not to accept the resignation of Dr Ronki Ram, President of PUTA. They also requested Dr Ram to take back his resignation in the interest of the university.

The members were unanimous in their decision to reject his resignation and consider him as the Association's leader. The association will present his case in the general body meeting to be held tomorrow.

Talking to Newsline, Professor Ashwani Kaul, Secretary, PUTA said that Dr Ram will continue to be the leader in the agitation for central status for the university.

"He is an honest man who is concerned about the varsity's welfare. We do not want him to step down and in fact we need him to lead us. Though he is very much hurt with the allegations levelled against him, we are sure he will support our decision," said Professor Kaul.

While PUTA members expressed shock over the step taken by him, Dr Ram said that he was pained by the rumours that were doing the rounds that he had weakened the university's fight for central status.

For the last few days, Dr Ram was being targetted for diluting the radical stance of PUTA's struggle for central status. Sources claimed that he had deliberately changed his stand and had asked for 'centrally funded university status'. His decision of stepping down from the post came in the form of a press statement issued on Sunday.

Heading: Students protest outside V-C office against new merit list for UILS - Indian Express
Content:
Polling for Senate elections for the Professors' constituency was held at the Panjab University on Monday, with five professors from various departments in the fray. The results will be declared on Wednesday.

The Open House held on Thursday, a flop show with only a few professors turning up, however failed to affect the voter turnout with over 90 per cent votes cast today at the polling held in two phases.

Even as a large number of supporters gathered at the University Auditorium to cast their votes, polling went off peacefully. While most of the votes were cast during the morning phase, some voters came in the afternoon to exercise their franchise. Over 200 votes were polled today including votes from the University Centre based in Hoshiarpur and Muktsar.

Talking to Newsline, Professor V K Mahajan, one of the contestants from the Arts faculty said, "Elections have always been unpredictable. Though I am hopeful of a win keeping in view the support I have from my patrons, yet I am keeping my fingers crossed."

Another candidate Professor N K Ojha said, "I have faith in my ability. The rest will be clear once the results are out on Wednesday."

Of the five candidates contesting the Senate elections, two are from the Arts faculty and the rest belong to the Science faculty. Professor V K Mahajan and Professor N K Ojha represent the Arts faculty and those contesting on behalf of the Science faculty include Professor Rupinder Tiwari, Professor A S Ahluwalia and Professor K P Singh.

Heading: ‘Youngsters are blindly aping the western culture’ - Indian Express
Content:
Nearly 50 students staged a protest on Monday outside the residence of Vice-Chancellor against the counselling to be held for student admissions to the University Institute of Legal Studies. The students protested against the new merit list made by the Syndicate, which takes into consideration only the marks scored by students in the Class XII exams.

The students alleged that in the previous merit list, the university considered the marks scored in the entrance exams as well as the marks scored in the Class XII exams. "The University has made a new merit list and ignored students who were in the waiting list. This is a sheer harassment. The University is denying admission to those who deserve it," said Sanjeev, an applicant waiting for counselling.

The students also expressed their unhappiness against the University's decision to convert the vacant seats falling under the SC/ST category to General category and reject the conversion of the same under the OBC category.

"The University had invited applications from OBC and SC/ST students for admissions to the course. After the counselling, they decided to leave the seats under the OBC category vacant while filling the SC/ST seats with the General students," said Akhil, another student.

He added, "For the counselling involving general students, they did not inform anybody and made a new merit list instead of considering those in the waiting list."

Heading: ‘The alarm bell on global warming has already started ringing’ - Indian Express
Content:
Much has been said and written about how the youth today is far removed from the values that make a good human being. While the elders continue to fret over the loss of values and morals among the young, they, on the other hand, are treading on a path, unaware of the consequences.

The Page 3 culture, which has become the hallmark of this generation, is being adopted by almost everyone.

In their bid to be counted among the 'in' crowd, youngsters have failed to see the good and the bad of this phenomenon. They consider it 'cool' to be seen at the most happening parties in the city. At parties like these, alcohol flows freely and all inhibitions are shed. Unfortunately, we are bracing this culture with open arms.

The generation Y seems to have lost respect for elders. They are blindly aping the western culture where elders are considered to be the interfering radical. Massive cultural erosion is corrupting the innocent minds of the young. They seemed to have lost sanctity for all relationships and are leading a self-conceited life.

The young brigade lives for itself and throws everything else to the wind.

For them, life is a huge party and in their bid to party hard, they are, unconsciously ruining their life. No matter how much the parents try to ward them off the bad track, the peer pressure is so much that they succumb to it and follow the herd mentality.

Parents can play a pivotal role in grooming their child. They should imbibe string cultural values in their children so that they do not succumb to temptations and follow the path of virtue and lead a happy life.

Heading: Janata market to get 369 concrete booths - Indian Express
Content:
India is among the top four emitters of carbon dioxide in the world, the others being America, China and Indonesia. If this continues unabated, the result will be very damaging for the climate of the region," said Dr K D Sharma, Geography professor, Panjab University. He was speaking at the seminar on 'Global warming and its impact on Indian Climate', organised by the Department of Public Administration, Panjab University in association with the regional chapter of the Indian Institute of Public Administration.

Dr Sharma said that according to climate models, the earth's temperature will increase by 13.5 degree Celsius by 2010, which will have a devastating impact on the vegetation as well as human health. "It should be kept in mind that climate changes do not consider political or administrative boundaries or differentiate between different sections of the society."

He also mentioned the reasons responsible for climate change. "Human activity is the main driving force behind the climate change over the last 50 years. The increase in temperature will mean melting of more ice-caps, rise in sea levels and water shortage. Various species of animals are also at the risk of extinction if there is a rise in temperature," stated Dr Sharma.

He also warned that the alarm bells had already started ringing and instead of waiting for some natural disaster to happen, we should take preventive measures. "The best way to control global warming is to plant as many trees as possible. The more green the surroundings, the better it is for everyone," he suggested.

Heading: Lobbying begins for the top post - Indian Express
Content:
Finally, the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (GMADA) has decided to allot concrete booths to 369 persons, who had lost their "illegal" kiosks in a major fire on June 1, 2007, at the Janata Rehri Market in Phase 3B1 in Mohali.

All 377 kiosks in the market were wiped out in the fire and since then the displaced kiosk owners are awaiting allotment of booths, which had been deferred several times in the past few months.

Speaking to Newsline, GMADA Chief Administrator Vivek Partap Singh on Monday said the allotments will be made through a draw of lots on September 23 at PUDA Bhawan in Sector 62.

GMADA Estate Officer Sukhjeet Pal Singh said that of the total 377 claimants, 369 were found eligible. The remaining 8 claims were rejected on grounds such as more than one claimant from a single family.

Earlier, GMADA had deferred indefinitely the draw of lots fixed to allot 322 booths on July 18 following fresh instructions from Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal to include the names of all 377 claimants in the list of allotments through draw of lots.

It was on the persistence of Area Councillor Harman Preet Singh Prince, who had sought Punjab Cooperation Minister Capt Kanwaljit Singh's help to persuade CM Parkash Singh Badal to ask the GMADA to allot booths to all claimants.

Prince had argued that when the CM had already given Rs 25,000 compensation to all 377 claimants, how can GMADA deny giving them a booth?

Later, Badal had decided that where the names of husband, wife and their minor children were separately included in the list of claimants for booths, only a single booth will be allotted in such cases.

However, all other claimants, whether they are siblings or major children of their parents, who have rolled in their names separately in the list, will be allotted separate booths.

While the GMADA had already built 130 booths, which will be immediately allotted following the draw of lots, the remaining booths will be built in due course of time, sources said.

It was also contemplated that in case the shopkeepers insist for early booths, they can be given the earmarked sites, where they can build their booths on their own. A final decision on the matter will be taken once the draw of lots is conducted on September 23, sources added.

Heading: Residents irked as taps run muddy water in Mohali - Indian Express
Content:
Immediately after the declaration of the results of the Kharar Municipal Council, the winner camps geared up for the next obvious step — the selection of the candidate for the post of president.

Though the ruling Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD)-Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) combine, which made a clean sweep in the polls, has not announced any name so far, lobbying for the post has already begun. This has also brought to the fore the factionalism within the winners.

As per the state government's notification, the president of civic body has to be elected within 14 days of the election. With this, the time for horse-trading has also decreased considerably, making it a matter of concern for the prospective candidates eyeing the top job.

The candidates considered strong contenders for the post include the SAD's Gurprem Singh from Ward 4 and Sukhwant Singh, brother of Chamkaur Sahib MLA Charanjit Singh, from Ward 8. Besides, the names of Roshan Lal from Ward 9, who became the senior most councilor after being elected for the fifth consecutive time, Jai Bhagwan Singla from Ward 15, who was the vice-president of the previous MC house, and Balwinder Kaur, who was elected for the second consecutive time from Ward 13, were also doing the rounds.

While Gurprem enjoys the patronage of Punjab Cooperation Minister Captain Kanwaljit Singh, Charanjit was pursuing the case of Sukhwant as his wife Paramjit Kaur also won from Ward 11 to make them the first and only councillor couple in Kharar.

Though none of the leaders or councillors are ready to divulge the ongoing parleys, reliable sources revealed that an offer of Rs 20 lakh each was being made to the elected councillors for securing their vote for the MC top post's election.

While Charanjit had joined hands with the SAD-BJP combine to contest the civic polls, the MC presidential election was expected to have changed scenario. Besides wooing three Independent councillors, those from the ruling alliance camp were also being contacted to form a majority group for electing the new city chief.

Meanwhile, all the factions are pushing the case of their respective candidates while the candidates themselves are making efforts to muster the support of the elected members. The top leadership of the ruling alliance, however, wants to nominate their choice for the top post.

It is reliably learnt that on the first day of their election, the councillors remained occupied in receiving several offers in cash and kind from different quarters. But, "wait and watch" has been the mantra so far.

Heading: Tigress death: Worker suspended, probe ordered - Indian Express
Content:
The residents of Phase X, on Monday, complained of receiving muddy water over the last several days.

The Citizens' Welfare Council threatened to launch a mass agitation if the authorities concerned failed to ensure regular and adequate supply of clean and safe drinking water to the area. Council press secretary Ranjivan Singh said it had lodged repeated complaints with the concerned officials about muddy, irregular and inadequate supply of water but to no avail.

"Powercuts and maintenance works was the answer of the authorities to our complaints," alleged Singh, while adding that the residents were exposed to the risk of waterborne and other diseases due to the consumption of dirty and unsafe water.

Heading: 3 killed, over a dozen hurt in separate mishaps - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab Wildlife department has ordered a department inquiry against Beldaar Ramkaran and put him under suspension on Monday, a day after the Royal Bengal Tigress Shanti died following a clash with another inmate, tiger Paras.

As the alleged negligence on part of the beldaar cost Shanti her life, the postmortem report confirmed that severe injuries were the cause of the death.

Zoo sources said the Ramkaran left the duty without locking the den of Paras on Sunday afternoon. During the time of flesh feeding to Shanti, who was on display with three more junior tigers, Paras came out of his den and attacked her. The bloody fight ended with Shanti's death.

Veterinary doctors Nirmaljit Singh and Rajkumar conducted the postmortem on the dead cat on Monday before burning its carcass. The report stated that Shanti died of excessive bleeding from the main vein of the neck.

Heading: Ward 15 records highest 86.88% voter turnout - Indian Express
Content:
Three persons were killed and over a dozen injured in separate road mishaps on the Kharar-Ropar stretch of National Highway 21 and on the Kharar-Ludhiana stretch of National Highway 95 in the past 24 hours.

Amrik Singh, the driver of a truck canter, was killed while over a dozen bus passengers were injured when a recklessly driven bus of the Himachal Road Transport Corporation rammed into a truck parked on the roadside near Padiala village. Truck driver Harpal told police that Amrik had stopped to help him replace his punctured tyre when the speeding bus rammed into their parked truck, leaving Amrik dead.

In another accident, an unidentified motorcyclist was killed when an unknown vehicle hit him and fled near Daonmajra late on Sunday night. Sapinder Singh of Sill Batta village was killed when another unknown vehicle crushed him and fled away near his village. The local police have booked the drivers of the killer vehicles and initiated further investigations.

Heading: ‘Let us remove encroachment and save our heritage’ - Indian Express
Content:
Lowest 65.94% votes polled in Ward 10

24 of total 69 contestants fail to get even 10% votes

The highest voter turnout of 86.88 per cent in Sunday's Kharar Municipal Council (MC) general elections was recorded in Ward 15 while Ward 10 polled the lowest 65.94 per cent votes.

Overall, a 76.99 per cent voter turnout was registered with 23,000 of the total 29,873 electorates exercising their franchise to elect their 15 civic representatives.

Analysis of the election result figures revealed that 24 of the total 69 candidates failed to even get 10 per cent of the total valid votes polled.

The maximum of such contestants were from Ward 1. Two Independents, Jaspal Singh from Ward 2 and Sanjeev Sharma from Ward 7, created a record of sorts by securing just 7 votes each from 1,185 and 1,675 valid votes polled in their respective constituencies.

Kamal Kishore of the Congress polled the maximum 1,077 votes from Ward 7, followed by the SAD-BJP combine's Himmat Singh, who secured 1,016 votes of the total 1,814 votes polled in Ward 3. They were the only two winners who secured over 1,000 votes.

SAD-BJP combine's Gurprem Singh from Ward 4 recorded the maximum winning margin of 682 votes. He polled 888 of the total 1,314 polled votes against 206 votes secured by his nearest Independent candidate Ravi Kant.

The toughest contest was in Ward 2 where the winning margin was of just 4 votes. Here, Independent candidate Kuldeep Singh won by securing 495 votes against 491 votes polled by his nearest rival Gurnam Singh. Both were former municipal councillors.

Heading: ‘Lack of coordination’ to delay widening of Pinjore-Kalka road - Indian Express
Content:
It was on September 3 that I visited a famous building designed by Le Corbusier, the Punjab Civil Secretariat, which is now being occupied by Haryana as well in the ratio 60: 40.

I have been seeing this building since 1961 when I came to Chandigarh to pursue a degree course in Architecture at the Chandigarh College of Architecture (CCA).

The building with its proportions, its Roof Garden and the external features with an imposing façade has mesmerised all.

This time, however, when I saw the building from the Chandigarh Club, I was disturbed by the sight of its façade.

The balconies provided to give shelter from rain and heat has been covered with different materials varying from aluminum frame glazing to wooden frame glazing, iron frame glazing to canvas, fiber sheet to broken furniture and even with torn curtain cloth.

The solution to this alarming problem is not difficult. If we architects decide jointly or otherwise, we can avert this visual calamity without any enforcement bulldozers.

It appears we are not contented with the space provided to us in our offices and are not grateful to be given an office accommodation in this state-of-the-art building of international repute with which the name of master architect Le Corbusier is attached.

On one hand we are trying to preserve the building where Corbusier once worked to design Chandigarh and on the other we are blinded to the fact that these buildings are being misused.

There has been a surge of campaigns in Chandigarh — 'Save Chandigarh', 'Preserve Chandigarh Heritage' — by INTACH and other voluntary organisations. These campaigns will go a long way in helping us save our heritage, our city and its buildings.

We need to go out of our air-conditioned premises and see where the damage is being done and persuade the people to exercise caution before a major damage is done.

I urge everyone who is genuinely concerned with Corbusier and his buildings to see the Punjab and Haryana Civil Secretariat from the angle I saw it recently.

Let us just remove these encroachments ourselves and save aour heritage.

Heading: Western Command, 61 years on and still going strong - Indian Express
Content:
This is a perfect example of sheer lack of coordination between the various civic departments in the town.

While the numerous electricity poles and lines on the Pinjore-Kalka highway were recently shifted, a communication gap, it seems, is likely to delay the widening of the Pinjore-Kalka road.

The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) project director claims that they have neither received any proposal to widen this stretch nor a written application for the same.

Officials of the district administration, in turn, say that the Haryana PWD (B and R) department has been requested to take up the matter with the NHAI.

"The work to shift the electricity poles and lines on the Pinjore patch was completed about three-four days ago. Five transformers and the 11-KW low-tension (LT) lines on the patch have been shifted. Around 40 new poles have been put up on the extreme ends of the road for the same," said a senior official of the Uttar Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam (UHBVN) on condition of anonymity. Now that electricity poles have been shifted, the widening work can easily be carried out, it was added.

Colonel K P Sharma, Project Director, NHAI, however, said: "Till date, we have not received anything in writing from the Panchkula Administration regarding the widening of the road. We have, in fact, told the authorities that there was never a proposal to widen that part of the road."

Contradictions about the project, meanwhile, are strong. On one hand, Panchkula DC Rajender Kataria claims the road would be widened, either by the State PWD (B and R) or by the NHAI, PWD (B and R) Financial Commissioner K K Jalal said the state cannot go ahead with the widening till the Pinjore-Kalka highway is with the NHAI.

The highway is expected to be handed over to the state after two and a half years when the Zirakpur-Parwanoo four-laning project will be completed. Kataria said, "We have asked the Haryana PWD (B and R) to take up the matter with the NHAI to widen the road. If they do not agree, the state will itself go ahead with the project."

Talking to Newsline, K K Jalal said: "We do agree that the widening of the Pinjore-Kalka road was never on the agenda of either the NHAI or of the PWD (B and R). The state department also cannot widen the road till the time the highway is with the NHAI. But as the Panchkula administration now wants the widening to be done, we would take up the matter with the NHAI."

Col K P Sharma, NHAI:"There was never a proposal to widen the road. We have not received anything in writing from the District Administration for the same."

Rajender Kataria, Panchkula DC:"The state PWD (B and R) will take up the issue with the NHAI. If the NHAI refuses, then the state PWD (B and R) will go ahead with the project."

K K Jalal, Financial Commissioner, PWD (B and R)
"Due to the ongoing project of Zirakpur-Parwanoo four-laning, the maintenance of Pinjore-Kalka highway has been handed over to the NHAI for two and a half years. As the highway is with the NHAI, the State PWD (B and R) cannot go ahead with the widening of the road.

Heading: Robbers gang busted with arrest of one,  claim police - Indian Express
Content:
To commemorate the 61st anniversary of the raising of the Headquarters' Western Command on September 15, a memorial-cum-wreath laying ceremony was held at Chandimandir on Monday. Lt General T K Sapru, GOC-in-C, Western Command, laid wreath to pay tributes to the martyrs at "Veer Smriti", the command War Memorial. Senior Officers, Officers, JCOs and jawans were present on the occasion.

Lt General Sapru assured that the path shown by the veterans will be the guiding force for all future ventures. The celebrations included variety entertainment programmes and Barakhana for the troops.

History recalled
Western Command is the largest operational Command of the Indian Army. Raised on September 15, 1947 with its Headquarters at Delhi, it was then called Delhi and East Punjab Command. It was re-designated as Western Command in January 1948. Six years later, the HQ of the Command moved to Shimla. After the Indo-Pak Conflict of 1971, the Northern Command, with its Headquarters at Udhampur, was carved out of it to assume operational responsibility of Jammu and Kashmir. Headquarters' Western Command eventually moved to its present location at Chandimandir in 1985.In 2005, consequent to the raising of South Western Command, the areas of responsibility of the Command were readjusted. At present, the Western Command guards the heartland of the country including parts of J&K.

Achievements enlisted
The Western Command has participated in all the wars since Independence and was instrumental in effectively blunting the Pakistani aggression in 1947, 1965 and 1971.

During the period when militancy was at its peak in Punjab, the Western Command rendered service in combating militancy and restoring normalcy and faith of civilians in the democratically elected Government. Besides controlling militancy, the valiant troops of the Western Command did a commendable job in helping the civil administration in conducting peaceful elections during 1992. They also helped the people of Punjab, Haryana and Himachal Pradesh by rescuing marooned people in areas devastated by unprecedented floods in 1993 and 2005 and are presently involved in the flood-affected areas of Bihar and Punjab. The Command also provided timely medical aid to the cyclone-hit areas of Myanmar this year.

Feather in the cap
Ever since Independence, the Western Command troops have won 11 PVCs and 113 MVCs as gallantry awards for their services.

Financial conference held at Western Command
The Financial Co-ordination conference of the Western Command was held on Monday at its headquarters in Chandimandir to "achieve common objectives to bring out professionalism and proficiency and also to enhance the customer satisfaction level." The issues deliberated upon ranged from monitoring of expenditure, audit objections, submission of acccounts by army units, e-payment scenario to the recently introduced pension scheme. Lt Gen T K Sapru, General Officer Command-in-Chief, Western Command chaired the conference. Senior army officers from the Western Command and Defence Accounts department were present on the occasion.

Heading: Highway projects: HC asks Haryana chief secy to appear on next hearing - Indian Express
Content:
The Rupnagar police claimed to have busted a gang of robbers involved in incidents of petrol pump looting after arresting one of its alleged members on Monday.

Panna, a resident of Roshan colony Rajpura, has confessed to his involvement and the other accomplices in looting petrol pumps at Kurali, Bhago Majra and Darauli (Nangal) on August 15, claimed Rupnagar SSP R N Dhoke.

The SSP said that during interrogation Panna also revealed the name of one Bittu, a resident of Shahbad Markanda (Haryana), Banti of Roshan colony Rajpura and two other persons.

It was after some unidentified persons looted Rs 1.84 lakh on August 15 from a salesman at a petrol pump owned by Daljit and company in the Bhago Majra village that a special police team was formed under the supervision of Rupnagar DSP Amarpreet Singh to nab the accused, added Dhoke,

He said the police had also recovered a black Scorpio (UA07-7475) used in the crime from Moti Nagar Market in the Industrial area in Ludhiana.

Heading: Coal shortage, snags hit power plants in state - Indian Express
Content:
Shortage of coal and regular snags at thermal power plants are restricting generation of power in the state, which is already suffering from shortage of power supply. Even with all the power plants working at full capacity, the state is able to muster 750 lakh units against the actual capacity of 850 MW. And now with coal shortage and malfunctioning of some units, the power crisis has worsened further.

Talking to The Indian Express, Sanjiv Kaushal, managing director of the Haryana Power Generation Corporation Limited (HPGCL), said the shortage of coal for power plants has been a long-standing problem. The situation has worsened now due to floods in Bihar and other parts of the country, he said.

Kaushal denied the coal stocks at Yamunanagar power plant had reached the critical point. "There is no need to panic. We have seven days of coal stock at Yamunanagar for the Sir Chhotu Ram thermal power plant there. At Panipat too, we have four to six days of coal stock left and the same is true for the Faridabad plant,'' he claimed.

Kaushal said the state government has taken up the matter of coal shortage with the Central coal ministry which has promised all help. "The Central Electricity Authority has advised us to keep a coal reserve of at least 25 days to be able to deal with any shortfall. It will take at least 2-3 months for us to tide over the problem if we manage to get regular coal supply,'' he added.

About the 300 MW unit of the Yamunanagar power plant that had to be closed down last week due to the breaking out of a fire, he said the unit was likely to be started later this week. The first unit of Panipat thermal power plant, which was out of order, is being repaired, he said.

Meanwhile, in order to ensure a minimum of six-hour power supply to agricultural tubewells daily, the Uttar Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam has decided to revise the power regulatory measures with immediate effect.

A spokesman of the nigam said that in view of the grid frequency, outages of the generating units supplying power to the northern grid and other technical parameters, it has been decided to impose load restrictions on industrial and independent industrial feeders from 5 am to 7 am and 5 pm to 12 midnight. At least 10 per cent of normal load will be allowed for lighting purpose.

The tubewell consumers of Panchkula, Ambala, Yamuna Nagar, Kurukshetra, Kaithal, Panipat, Rohtak, Jhajjar, Jind and Sonepat will get power in two groups during day and night in different time slots. It will be ensured that electricity is supplied to public water works for a minimum of one hour each in the morning and evening, he said.

Heading: UHBVN introduces voluntary disclosure scheme - Indian Express
Content:
The ana Education Department is considering a proposal by the Haryana State Child Welfare Council to set up 423 education centres in the state. The council has also forwarded a project to the Centre to impart vocational training to women.

This was revealed at the inaugural function of the second state-level five-day camp organised by the Haryana State Child Welfare Council in Ambala today. As many as 110 children from various districts of Haryana are participating in the camp. Inaugurating the camp, vice-president of the council, Asha Hooda, wife of Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda, said children should not be confined to bookish knowledge only, but ample opportunity should be provided to them for their overall development.She also gave away prizes to all the children particiapeting in the camp.

Honourary secretary of the council, Manju Gupta, apprised those present about the various activities of the council.

Heading: HAFED launches new varieties of cattlefeed - Indian Express
Content:
Keeping in view the persistent demand by the public and feedback received from the field offices, the Uttar Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam has decided to introduce the voluntary disclosure of load scheme for domestic, non-domestic, agricultural tubewell and industrial consumers with immediate effect.

The scheme will remain open till October 31 and no penalties will be charged from the applicants for regularisation of unauthorised load, a spokesman said here today. The procedure of regularisation of unauthorised load has been simplified for the convenience of consumers, he said

For regularisation of domestic and non domestic load, the applicants would be required to submit the Application & Agreement Form. There will be no need of submitting the Term and Conditions forms or affidavits. However, the applicant would give an undertaking that he will abide by all the terms and conditions of the power supply.

For regularisation of extended load upto an extension of 20 KW of load, there will be no need to submit the test report. The extended load would be regularised after getting the necessary certificates. They will be required to deposit the consumption security, fixed connection charges etc. and the extended load shall be considered as regularised immediately.

The unauthorised load of AP tubewell consumers will also be regularised on receiving the application and agreement form.

The extension of load will be regularised with the existing system. However, if the existing system cannot take up the additional load, the Nigam would augment the system. In case, the capacity is not available with the feeding sub station, the applicant would be asked to remove the unauthorised load.

Referring to the procedure of regularisation of load of industrial consumers, he said that the applicants would be required to submit the A&A form, test report, advance consumption security and service connection charges for the extended load.In case of High Tension consumers, the consumer shall submit revised contract demand undertaking. The extension of load shall be regularised with the existing system if it can take up the extended load, the spokesman added

Heading: Ghumantu samiti demands plots - Indian Express
Content:
With the commissioning of the new ultra-modern cattlefeed plant with increased capacity at Rohtak, HAFED has come out with a number of new products, including HAFED Navjat feed, Sarvshakti feed, Pashudhan feed, Sampuran feed and Sareshth feed for the benefit of dairy farmers.

A spokesman of HAFED said that Navjat Feed was suitable for calves, Sarvshakti feed for post-calving and Pashudhan Feed was a special feed for buffaloes. Similarly, Sampuran Feed was suitable during last stage of pregnancy and HAFED Sreshth Feed was most suitable for high milk yielding animals, especially cross-bred cows.

The formulation of newly-introduced cattle feed would go a long way in addressing the problem of farmers and would increase productivity and lactation period, besides helping in solving the problems of repeat bleeding and reducing inter-calving period, which would reduce the milk production cost and treatment cost. This would bring higher realisation of milk for the farmers and thereby increase their income.

The good quality of feed would further strengthen the belief of the farmers in the new balanced system of feeding.The spokesman said that development and availability of proper cattle feed would lure the farmers to adopt dairying as their subsidiary occupation, besides agriculture, for improving their economic condition and also reducing the risk-factor, which is unavoidable in agriculture, he said.

Heading: Students get a taste of hospitality in Kufri - Indian Express
Content: The Bhartiya Ghumantu Beghar Sangharsh Samiti has demanded 100 plots of land free from the Haryana government. A delegation of the Sangharsh Samiti, led by national president Pushpender Kaur, organised a rally here on Monday to put forward their demands to the government.

Heading: State opens doors for private sector in medical education - Indian Express
Content:
In a move, designed to expose school children to the state's hospitality sector, at least 40 children from Shimla's leading schools, participated in a workshop at the Institute of Hotel Management, Kufri.

State's Secretary Tourism, Manisha Nanda, engaged the institute's faculty and students to learn techniques of cooking, besides making them aware of the career avenues in the hospitality sector, including hostels, airlines .

The students prepared different food items led by Gurjeet Singh, a faculty member. Speaking on the occasion Nanda, the brain behind involving school children, said the state, being a tourist destination, is trying some unconventional methods of promoting tourism. "Home-stay tourism scheme is one such innovative method and offers a complete package of hospitality, culture, art, handicraft and service industry. Inviting children to the institute is a beginning to popularise this sector as career option," she said.

She said the new Indian institute of hotel management has already been sanctioned by the Centre for Hamirpur and a food craft institute at Dharamshala has also been cleared. Hospitality sector is the only sector which has witnessed an impressive 21 per cent growth as well as opened new avenues for the youths. Certificates were given to the students, who participated in the workshop.

Director of the institute D. Mukherjee announced that effort will be made to involve more schools and also organise other activities at the campus.

Heading: Files of abolished Tribunal make space in High Court - Indian Express
Content:
The state government today selected SREI-Astron Hospital and Healthcare Consultants for making an assessment about requirement of medical colleges and also hospitals, which will be attached to the medical colleges to come up in the private sector.

With this, the government has opened its door to the private sector's entry to medical education and healthcare sector. The state's Principal Secretary (Health) Deepak Shanan said the government has finalised the proposal to engage consultants for setting up new medical colleges and attached hospitals, offering super-specialties.

Most of these projects, attracting investments to the tune of several crores, will change the entire medical education and health care scenario in the state. These projects will come up in the rural areas away from Shimla.

Till now, Himachal Pradesh has two government sector medical colleges with attached hospitals at Shimla and Tanda (Kangra). Five new medical colleges, three of these in the districts of Mandi, Hamirpur and Solan, are proposed in the private sector.

Though the locals have opposed the proposal for a private sector medical college at Mandi, the BJP government is looking at the advantages of setting up a private medical college with a fee structure decided by the government, and 50 seats reserved for Himachalis.

"We are committed to complete the college in a time," said Health Minister Rajeev Bindal. The minister said the BJP government is keen to see the new institutions in public-private partnership, and provide people with the best possible medical facilities within the state.

The consultants engaged by the government will undertake a detailed assessment of the existing health infrastructure in the areas where the new medical colleges are proposed and suggest upgrade of the facilities.

The consultants will also study the exact requirements of infrastructure for setting-up medical colleges and mechanism for running the health care facilities in the hospitals, which will be attached to the private colleges.

"The role of consultants will be important in getting MCI clearance and also meeting their requirements, both in the colleges and hospitals," said Shanan.

The consultant has been asked to complete the study by this year end and submit the report to the government by January for a follow-up action.

After receiving the report the government will invite bids from the groups keen for setting-up new colleges and hospitals.

Heading: Armyman arrested for murder - Indian Express
Content:
With Himachal Pradesh Assembly passing a bill, relating to transfer of all pending cases and records of decided cases of recently abolished Administrative Tribunal to state High Court, those struggling for justice may have to wait for sometime.

The immediate issue, which the state's General Administration Department (GAD) has to resolve is providing additional space to the High Court for keeping the records and files, numbering over 24,000.

The High Court has already asked for handing over at least one floor of the Directorate of the Industries complex.

The Directorate of Industries, built in mid-eighties, is one of few buildings which the departments had built in the town.

Being close to the High Court, this two-storied complex became the first choice after the government abolished the Tribunal.

A portion of the industries department was earlier used by the state's Advocate General, before it was moved to a separate building close to the High court.

The Tribunal functioned from an independent complex few yards away from the State Secretariat.

The government so far has not taken any decision on utilisation of the Tribunal complex but decision to hand over a major part of the industries department's complex to the High Court has already been taken.

When contacted, Secretary GAD, Diljeet Dogra said the modalities on shifting of the Tribunal records, including "live files" are being worked out with the High Court.

"We are studying the requirement of the space and also the volume of the Tribunal files. The government will provide sufficient space for the keeping the files and other records," he said.

In the industries department there is an atmosphere of uncertainty over the vacation of the complex or a part of it.

"Even if a part of the department moves out, some working problems will crop-up. During the past five years, the industries department has been the centreof attention. More than Rs 27,000 crore investment is already committed,"said an official.

Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal said after abolition of the Tribunal, the High Court's role has become more important. The government would ensure that functioning of the High Court is not affected and justice is delivered.

High Court's Registrar General V.K.Sharma said, "Issue of transfer of Tribunal cases is under active consideration. Once the matter is settled between the government and High Court, the cases will get shifted for regular hearing."

Heading: In Rural Development Minister’s village, residents pine for clean potable water - Indian Express
Content:
Two Armymen and their accomplice allegedly killed a taxi driver after kidnapping him last year.

The accused include Baljit Singh, alias Balli, and Amritpal Singh, alias Kala, both Armymen and Fatehgarh Churian residents, and Bhinder Singh, alias Lucky, of Gidderbaha. Both Bhinder and

Balli were on a one-month leave when they committed the crime. Bhinder was arrested a few days ago and he spilled the beans during interrogation.

Notably, Vikas Kumar of Kishanpura had complained on October 2, 2007, that some unidentified persons had hired his taxi and then kidnapped the driver, Rakesh Kumar. A kidnapping case was registered and on October 9, 2007, police arrested Baljit and Amritpal, who were driving the taxi without number-plate.

But the police did not interrogate them properly. They did not even ask them from where they took the numberless taxi. Later, both managed to get bail and are now absconding.

Now, with the arrest of Bhinder, police have started backslapping themselves. Bhinder has confessed that the trio had killed the taxi driver after strangulating him and snatched his mobile phone and purse before throwing his body into the Sutlej.

SSP Pawan Rai said Bhinder and Baljit were with two Rashtriya Rifles and 119 Engineers Battalion, Chandimandir, respectively.

Heading: Virk makes first court appearance - Indian Express
Content:
Each day in the life of young Baljit Kaur, a resident of Brahmpura village in Tarn Taran—the home of Rural Development and Panchayat Minister Ranjit Singh Brahmpura—begins with search for potable water.

She sometimes scours the whole village for clean water, as the supply that she gets at home is unfit for consumption. "The water is of deep yellow colour and unfit even for animals," she says.

Her neighbour, Bhajan Kaur, says getting clean drinking water in this hamlet was next to impossible.

Residents in over 20 villages in Tarn Taran district are forced to consume contaminated water. Several cases of jaundice have been reported in the recent past. Besides, the supply from hand pumps and government taps too is highly polluted.

The villages that are badly affected include the minister's village Brahmpura, Sangatpura, Ranian Wala, Mohanpura, Bhattal, Raal Chaal, Dhun Dhaike, besides several areas in and around Patti and Chohla Sahib.

Deputy Commissioner Khushi Ram has sought a report from the Health Department and the BDPO.

Sources say lack of proper sewerage disposal system results in contamination. While the health authorities are clueless about the real reason behind the contamination, the residents attribute it to the same level of toilets and water supply bores. "The bores for the hand pumps are at almost the same level as the toilet pits. The dirty water mixes with the potable one," says Daljit Singh Brahmpura, sarpanch of the village.

Bakhshish Singh, a resident of the area, says development has eluded the place for the past over 60 years. "The Panchayat Minister has never bothered to address the problems of the people," he says.

Rakesh Nayyar, a resident of Chohla Sahib, says the 10 ponds of dirty water (chhappars) which run through the township are a source of water contamination. "The ponds have not been cleaned for ages," he says.

Civil Surgeon Dr Amrit Kaur says the department was distributing chlorine tablets among people, besides advising them to consume boiled water.

However, minister Brahmpura says there was a water sanitation scheme worth crores under which the World Bank pays 90 per cent of the cost, while 10 per cent is borne by the villages. "It is up to the village panchayats to approach us for it. So far, we have not received any application," he says.

Heading: VB set up special team; Jagjit, Jugal untraceable - Indian Express
Content:
Sit's plea for NBWs dismissed

Former Punjab DGP Sarbdeep Singh Virk on Monday appeared before a special court in Mohali. This was his first court appearance in a corruption, disproportionate assets and criminal case registered by the Vigilance Bureau on September 8, 2007.

Assisted by his counsels, he argued against the plea moved by the one-member Special Investigation Team (SIT), comprising Patiala SSP SK Asthana, to seek non-bailable arrest warrants against him. Coming down heavily upon the SIT, Virk submitted that Asthana was trying to obtain NBWs by being "overenthusiastic and without understanding the legal complications".

Notably, on the last date of hearing on September 1, the SIT had moved a plea, seeking NBWs against Virk, while submitting that he was neither cooperating with the investigation team nor appearing before the trial court despite serving of summons. Responding to a notice issued on SIT's plea, Virk had moved the court seeking directions to restrain the probe team from evaluating or assessing his property and his house in Sector 27, Chandigarh. Special Judge SK Garg ordered to dismiss the SIT plea, as it became infructuous with Virk's appearance.

Asthana, however, stressed for issuance of search warrants to evaluate Virk's property. Virk also moved a plea seeking exemption from personal appearance in the court, citing "ill health" as a reason. The court has fixed September 30 for taking decision on both the pleas.

Meanwhile, the SIT today again swooped on Virk's house in Sector 27, but found it locked.

Heading: Vocational courses not updated in 20 yrs - Indian Express
Content:
'SIT will also question Bir Devinder, BR Bajaj and former AIT head Ratna'

The Vigilance Bureau has formed a three-member Special Investigation Team (SIT) to probe the Amritsar Improvement Trust scam in which former chief minister Amarinder Singh and five others were recently booked.

Meanwhile, sources said Chaudhary Jagjit Singh, former local bodies minister and an accused in this scam, has gone underground.

The three-member team comprises Joint Director (Crime), Vigilance Bureau, Inderjit Singh Randhawal; SP (Economic Offences Wing) Chaman Lal and SP (Flying Squad-I)Paramjit Khaira. The team, which would be headed by Randhawa, will submit the report to the Speaker within two months.

Jugal Kishore, former chairman of the Amritsar Improvement Trust, is also untraceable.

Besides, there is also no clue of the owner of Veer Enclave, the property being developed on the disputed land.

"The special team will question the accused as well as other people who gave their statements before the special Vidhan Sabha committee. These include senior Congress leader Bir Devinder Singh, senior IAS officer BR Bajaj and former AIT chairperson Ratna," said an official.

The SIT would also examine as to whether the government had any authority or not to exempt 32.1 acres. An officer said, "The SIT will look into the bank accounts and other transactions to check the possibility of money having exchanged hands. There is a possibility that more people are involved."

Heading: Poll bugle echoes at Chhapaar Mela - Indian Express
Content:
Vocational courses were started in various Punjab schools two decades ago to help students earn a living after they leave the institution.

However, in the past 20 years, the government has not upgraded the courses, most of which are running on papers only.

Besides, the government hardly releases grants to run the courses.

In 1986-87, vocational courses were started in hundreds of schools of Punjab, including 35 in Jalandhar district. Vocational training in furniture making, typing, shorthand, knitting, nursing, weaving, radio and TV repair, tailoring, leather and sports good making, carpentry, commercial art and agro business was provided to the students from Class VIII to XII.

Under the National Education Policy of the country, the Centre provided grant for purchase of machinery for running the courses.

However, today there are no takers for the vocational courses. Reason: the government neither provided grants nor staff; at present, there are only 10 per cent teachers for these courses. Besides, the curriculum has not been updated for decades and most of the courses do not draw interest.

To top it all, post of the District Vocational Officer has been lying vacant for the last 10 years.

A vocational education teacher said earlier, an annual grant in the range of Rs 2,500 and Rs 5,000 used to come for every trade. However, this meagre grant was stopped a few years ago.

The machinery meant for various trades is either gathering dust or has been damaged.

When contacted, District Education Officer (Secondary) Harinder Sahni said in the past 20 years, courses have neither been upgraded nor changed as per the changing needs, for instance typing and shorthand should have been replaced by computer training.

He said he had never received a grant for these courses. He, however, added that in some schools the courses have been doing well.

Heading: NRI singer serves notice on Himesh - Indian Express
Content:
With Lok Sabha elections on mind, the political parties turned no stone unturned to draw the first blood from their opponents at the religious Chhapaar Mela here.

While the ruling SAD (B) said they would raise the issue of inadequate MSP for paddy in the Lok Sabha in the next session, opposition Congress said they would apprise the Centre of the misuse of Central funds by the state government.

SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal said, "The MSP of Rs 850 for paddy announced by the Centre is not adequate. It is much below than what was recommended by the Commission for Agriculture Costs and Prices (CACP). The CACP had recommended Rs 1,000. The SAD will raise this issue in the coming session of Parliament."

Attacking former chief minister Capt Amarinder Singh, Sukhbir said he had fled abroad after "looting" the state. "When Capt Amarinder got Vigilance cases registered against us, we did not run away, but faced them bravely. We have not slapped the cases on him, but these had cropped up during his tenure. In fact, the Ludhiana City Centre case inquiry was marked by Amarinder himself. And members of his party had deposed against him before the Vidhan Sabha committee in the Amritsar land scam," Sukhbir said.

Earlier, speaking to the media, Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal condemned the Congress for levelling allegations of rigging in the Moga MC elections. "Had there been rigging, they (Congress) should have complained to the Election Commission," Badal said.

Meanwhile, at the Congress stage, leader of opposition Rajinder Kaur Bhattal accused the state government of misusing the Central funds, including Rs 1,643 crore given for flood relief. "We will prepare a detailed report about the misuse and send it to the Centre so that action can be initiated against the Badal government," she said.

Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee (PPCC) president Mohinder Singh Kaypee, when questioned about the unseating of Capt Amarinder Singh from state assembly, said, "The matter is now in court, which will take a decision."

While at the SAD stage, many senior SAD leaders were present, only few leaders could be seen at the Congress venue. At the SAD venue, the prominent leaders included Capt Kanwaljit Singh, Balwinder Singh Bhunder, Ludhiana MP Sharanjit Singh Dhillon, Jagdev Singh Talwandi, Mahesh Inder Singh Grewal and Harish Rai Dhanda. At the Congress stage, besides Bhattal and Kaypee, AICC spokesperson Manish Tewari, former minister Partap Singh Bajwa, former PPCC president Shamsher Singh Dullo, former MP Jagmeet Singh Brar and Kila Raipur MLA Jassi Khangura were present.

Meanwhile, at the Lok Bhalai Party (LBP) stage, president Balwant Singh Ramoowalia said while all the other parties were fighting for their share of power, his party was into social service.

Heading: SAD-BJP sweeps Moga MC poll - Indian Express
Content:
An NRI Punjabi singer, Kulwinder Kally, served a legal notice on famous lyrist Sameer and music composer, singer and actor Himesh Reshammiya for allegedlly stealing his composition.

The singer has sought a compensation of Rs 5 crore. Kally said his song 'Soniye je tere nal daga main kumawn rab kare main mar janwan' from the music album 'Sham Wali Gaddi' was released five years ago. He said if he was not given credit in the film posters and music album within 15 days from issuance of the notice, he would start legal proceedings against the accused .

Heading: Ferozepur cops nab Bangla national on charges of spying - Indian Express
Content:
The SAD-BJP alliance has bagged 26 out of the 31 seats in the Moga MC elections, which were held on Sunday. In the elections marred by violence, four seats went to Independents, while in ward number 4, repolling has been scheduled for Tuesday.

The SAD contested 21 seats and the BJP 10; both lost two seats each.

Baljinder Singh Brar, son of former minister Tota Singh, is set to be chosen the president of the municipal council. Brar was elected unopposed from ward number 1.

Tota Singh and his son Baljinder assured the residents sewerage and water supply facilities and also promised to upgrade the nagar council to a municipal corporation.

Tota Singh, who was in charge of the party's poll campaign, condemned the violence and said that none of his partymen were involved. He also expressed regret at the manhandling of mediapersons.

Meanwhile, the SAD has won nine seats in Badhni Kalan, out of the total 11. Polling at ward numbers 2 and 6 was deferred by the district electoral officer following incidents of booth-capturing. Congress leaders, including MLAs, Darshan Singh Brar and Ajit Singh Shant, had demanded repoll in all the wards, but the electoral officer ordered it at only two. In these wards, votes polled were reportedly more than the total votes listed.

Case registered against an Independent
Moga:After day-long consultations with senior police officers, the police finally registered a case against two close relatives of Independent candidate Surinder Singh Goga and 25-30 unidentified persons on charges of attempt to murder and deterring police officials from performing their duty. The case was registered on the complaint by SAD candidate Gulvinder Singh Bawa. Gulvinder alleged that when he was standing at the polling station on Sunday morning, Baljinder approached him with a revolver and asked him to leave the polling station. When he refused to leave, he fired two shots at him but he escaped unhurt. He also alleged the accused and his associates assaulted the polling staff. No arrests have yet been made. Interestingly, as per eyewitnesses, a large number of supporters of the SAD candidate, armed with lathis and iron rods, had arrived at the polling station and assaulted the Independent candidate, his son and brother. When contacted, senior police officers, including the SSP, said police were not informed about the assault on Surrinder Singh and his son till today. Sources said the father-son duo was taken to Jalandharhospital.

Heading: 250 examined at free medical camp  held by CMC - Indian Express
Content:
The local police claimed to have nabbed a 20-year-old Bangladeshi resident on charges of spying.

SSP Dinesh Partap Singh said Akbar Ali was staying in Ferozepur Cantonment for over two months now and was caught while roaming around the Hussainiwala Bridge.

Notably, Ferozepur Cantonment is one of the largest Army bases in this part of the country and a high-security area.

The SSP said, "We were tipped that Md Akbar Ali was trying to gather information about the Army installations and strength in Ferozepur Cantonment. When our police party, led by Inspector Sarbjeet Singh, caught him, he revealed his names as Mohammad Akbar Hussain, a resident of Fanni district in Bangladesh."

The SSP said, "Our preliminary investigation reveals that Ali had entered India through the Tripura border. He stayed in Delhi for some time before coming to Ferozepur. He worked as a daily-wager in Delhi as well as Ferozepur."

He said, "During his stay here, he tried to develop contacts with people in the Cantonment and was preparing for a 'mission'. On searching him, we found a pocket dairy that contained certain telephone numbers of Bangladesh and Pakistan. He told us about one of his links in Bangladesh to whom he was supposed to pass on the information."

The police said Ali has disclosed that his primary task was to collect information about Army, its strength and weapons and pass it on to his masters in Pakistan and Bangladesh. The SSP has urged the public to inform the police about any suspicious-looking person.

Meanwhile, the police have stepped up vigil in the area.

Heading: I will use Atray tournament to make a comeback: Ganguly - Indian Express
Content:
About 250 patients suffering from various ailments were examined at a free medical and dental camp organised by CMCH at Mata Kaushalya Devi Pahwa Charitable Hospital, Hambran. Medicines were also distributed free-of-cost to the patients.

Medical teams from Surgery, OB and Gynaecology, Paediatrics, Orthopedics, Eye, Medicine, ENT and Dental departments examined the patients at the camp.

The free camp was in continuation of a series of the camps organised by CMC to serve the poor and needy in the society and to provide the best health-care in the rural areas.
