Giving more details about the camp, the Director, Dr AGT, Deputy Director, Dr Kim Mammen, said, "It has always been our endeavor to reach out to the masses and offer quality health-care. CMC has been organising such camps from time to time and will continue to do so in future also."

Dr Sunil Singh, principle, Medical College, CMC, and Dr Kanwal Masih, Medical Superintendent, hoped that maximum number of people would avail the benefit of the free camps. He further added, "This free camp is part of CMC's endeavor towards good health among the people of the region."

Heading: KB DAV bags gold, silver in roller skating - Indian Express
Content:
Former Indian skipper Sourav Ganguly is still harbouring hopes of making a comeback to the Indian Test side and will use the local J P Atray Memorial cricket tournament as an opportunity to gather some form and make his case. The tournament gets underway from September 17 and Ganguly will play for the city-based Life Insurance Cricket Club.

"I will land in Chandigarh on Thursday and our first match is on Friday," Ganguly told Newsline from Kolkata, "We would have two more league matches and I will try my best to use this opportunity to make a comeback. I haven't given up hopes of making it to the Test team against Australia and will fight for it."

After being dropped from the Irani Cup Rest of India squad there has been speculation on Ganguly's career having come to an end with some even hoping for the southpaw to announce his retirement. However, Ganguly's decision to play in the Atray tournament would have surprised many.

It is also interesting to note that the tricity had brought luck to Ganguly on an earlier occassion too. When he was dropped from the Indian team in 2006,

Ganguly made a comeback with selection in the team for the Test series in South Africa, days after having played a Ranji Trophy match at the PCA Stadium in Mohali. Ganguly would hope for a repeat this time too.

Heading: PAU students union lists out its demands - Indian Express
Content:
The roller hockey team of KB DAV Sector 7 claimed the first and second position in the sixth Bhawan Hawk Roller Skating Carnival held from September 13 to 14 at Bhartiya Vidya Bhawan, Sector 27. The team A comprising of Manjit Singh, Utkarsh Bhardwaj, Sachin Sharma, Rohit Bajaj, Brijesh, Harjun and Harsh claimed Gold in above 16 years category while Shivam, Vipin Kumar, Karan Lamba, Peeyush, Bhavdeep Singh, Himank, Aashish, Jatin, Deepanshu and Gaurav bagged the silver.

In the individual category, KB DAV-7 claimed seven gold, three silver and two bronze medals in Rink Race-I, Rink Race-II and Road Race.

Shiv, Gargi to lead
Shiv Charan Madan and Gargi Thakur of Mount Carmel School, Sector 47 will lead the Chandigarh boys and girls team for the 11th Sub-junior National Sepak Takraw Championship to be held from September 18 to 21 at Hyderabad. The players attended coaching camp at Mount Carmel School who were selected during the Chandigarh Sub-Junior State Championship.

Team: Boys: Shiv Charan Madan, Siddhant Verma, Pranshul Gautam (Mt. Carmel-47), Akshay Dhawan, Siddharth Khanna (St. Joseph's-44)

Girls: Gargi Thakur, Riya, Mandeep Kaur (Mt. Carmel-47), Swati, Pooja (GMSSS-20)

Officials: Priyanka & Shivani (Girls)

Ranbir Kaushik & Baljinder Singh Banwait (Boys)

Ball badminton championship from Sept 29

ST Joseph's Senior Secondary School, Sector 44 under the aegis of Chandigarh Ball Badminton Association (CBBA) will hold the 14th Chandigarh Sub-Junior State Ball Badminton Championship for boys and girls on September 29 and 30 at the school's grounds.

Interested players can send their entries to Baljinder Singh Banwait, general secretary, CBBA before September 25. The City team will be selected for the 28th Sub-Junior National Ball Badminton Championship to be held from October 4 to 7 on the basis of their performance in the championship. Players born on or after 01-01-1994 are eligible to take part in the Championship.

Heading: Seminar on bloodless surgery organised - Indian Express
Content:
After announcing a new president, Punjab Agricultural University Students Association is now doing what it is best at. Listing out their demands that range from raising of new walls that pose inconvenience to water shortage on campus. Interestingly, this is not for the first time this list of demands is being submitted to the Director Students Welfare. The list is just the same as it has been for over the previous years.

Gurpreet Singh Brar, the newly appointed PAUSA president, who took over from Amandeep Singh recently after the latter left for the foreign shores, says, "Walls, especially the one put up between hostel number 1 and 2, is posing a lot of problem. The students who used to walk down to their lecture rooms now have to take a detour because of this wall. Moreover students' interaction has also been curbed." This wall had been raised to avoid scuffles between the residents of both the hostels.

Another issue that the students feel is nothing less than mental trauma is the problem of water shortage. The students claim, "Due to power cuts, water supply has also been affected acutely. Thus we have to head for our morning baths early or we miss out. The university needs to do something about resolving water woes too."

Heading: Dr T.S. Anand presents paper at international seminar - Indian Express
Content:
A seminar on hemostasis (reducing the amount of blood loss during surgery) was organised by SPS Apollo Hospitals in collaboration with Pfizer Ltd Mumbai. Dr Shalini Menon, Medical Research Department (MRD), Pfizer Mumbai, described their ongoing research of a medication that reduced the need for blood transfusions.

This will have tremendous benefits like reduction in recovery time, stay at the hospital, cost and complications.

According to Dr Prafull K Arya, Senior Consultant, GI Surgery, the surgery inevitably led to bleeding, and hemostasis aims at reducing the amount of blood loss and the need for transfusion as well as preventing rebleeding, and the need for repeat surgery.

According to Dr Menon, there is strong emerging evidence that the patients who need transfusion during or after surgery have chances of post-operative infections.

According to Dr Navneet K Chaudhary, a renowned laparoscopic surgeon, in foreign countries many surgeons have successfully practiced bloodless surgery for years, and researchers are conducting several clinical trials of drugs and blood substitutes that may make transfusions obsolete.

Heading: Chandigarh eves to face Amritsar in final - Indian Express
Content:
Dr T.S. Anand, faculty member at Guru Nanak Dev Engineering College, presented a research paper in an international seminar on "Representation of women in contemporary literature" organised in Agra.

Dr K.C. Tripathy, Vice-Chancellor, B.R. Ambedkar University, inaugurated the seminar while Dr Jane E Schukowsky, former executive director, United States Educational Foundation in India, presided over the inaugural session.

In all, 60 research papers were presented by scholars drawn from various institutes of higher learning. Dr T.S. Anand also chaired a paper-reading session.

Heading: Kaint invited for eco meet - Indian Express
Content:
Riding high on a 4 wicket haul by Radhika Bhutani Chandigarh defeated Patiala comprehensively by 10 wickets to cruise into the final of the Punjab Women Inter-District Cricket Tournament (u-19) in a match held in Patiala on Monday.

Earlier Chandigarh won the toss and elected to bowl first on a docile track at Dhruv Pandove Cricket Stadium. There decision proved right as the Patiala girls kept losing wickets at regular intervals and could not sustain for the stipulated 50 overs. Patiala were bundled out for 97 runs in the allotted in 40.2 overs. For Patiala Robin was the only batsman who managed a decent 24 runs as the others succumbed before Radhika Bhutani's deadly spell who claimed 4 wickets in her spell of 10 overs.

In reply the Chandigarh opening pair of Shivani and Akriti remained unbeaten and scored 41 and 25 runs respectively, as their team managed 98 without loss in 29.1 overs.

The first semi final match was played today at Jalandhar between Jalandhar and Amritsar.

In second semi-final, led by Monica Mehra's all-round show (30 not out, 5 for 27) Amritsar defeated Jalandhar by 9-wickets.

The final will be played between Chandigarh and Amritsar at GNPS-36 in Chandigarh on September 17.

Brief Scores:

Patiala: 97 all out in 40.2 overs (Robin 24 and Radhika 4 for 19).

lost to Chandigarh:98 for 0 in 29.1 overs (Shivani 41 no and Akriti 25)

Jalandhar:103 for all in 29 overs (Rewa Arora 54, Asha 16, Monica Mehra 5 for 27, Anjali 2 for 18) lost to Amritsar: 104 for 1 in 22 overs (Renu Verma 18, Monica 30 not out, Navdeep 21 not out, Bubita 1 for 27)

Heading: Bounced cheque lands trader in jail - Indian Express
Content:
Eminent agricultural economist, Dr Gursharan Singh Kainth, Director, GAD Institute of Development Studies, Amritsar, has been invited to participate in the annual conference of the International Forum for Ecology and Health slated to be held from December 1 to 5. The theme of the IEF-2008 is "Ecohealth: Healthy environment and healthy people." The conference will be hosted by National Institute of Public Health of Mexico in collaboration with International Development Research Centre (IDRC) Canada; and Pan American Health organization.

At the IEF-2008, Dr Kainth will present his research paper on "Environmental awareness among school teachers of Indian Punjab." The research study is based on the data collected from 2,500 teachers belonging to Majha region of Punjab.

Though there exists environmental awareness among teachers, but the awareness level of science teachers was much more as compared to the art teachers. Likewise, the science teachers are more aware of the management of waste material as compared to arts teachers. Higher level of awareness among science teachers is due to the exposure, the study says.

Heading: ‘We will realise dream of Panchayati Raj’ - Indian Express
Content:
The court of Charanjit Arora, Judicial Magistrate, Ludhiana, has sentenced Vinod Kumar, a local businessman, to one-and-a-half year imprisonment in a bounced cheque case.

The court has also directed Vinod Kumar, proprietor of M/s J K W Exports, to pay a compensation of Rs 150,000 to the complainant.

Sukhdev Raj Jain, the proprietor of M/s Sukhdev Raj Jain and Co of Ghas Mandi, Ludhiana, filed a complaint and submitted that Vinod Kumar of Kalyan Nagar, Ludhiana, had approached him for a loan of Rs 2 lakh on June 13 who issued a cheque for Rs 2 lakh for August 17, 2005. It was assured that the cheque would be encashed on its presentation.

But to his utter surprise, when the cheque was presented for encashment, the same was dishonoured by the banker of accused with remarks "Exceeds Arrangements" vide memo dated August 18, 2005. Thereafter, a legal notice was served upon the accused, requesting him to make the payment of dishonored cheque. But he failed to do so, added the complainant.

On the other hand, the accused pleaded innocence and claimed false implication. He said the cheque had been handed over to the complainant only by way of security. In defence, he also examined Kamaljit Kaur, senior tax assistant from Income Tax Office.

After hearing the arguments of both sides, the Judicial Magistrate, Charanjit Arora held that it was established that the cheque had been issued for discharging the liability raised due to taking a loan from complainant. Pronouncing the verdict, the judge held that the prosecution had successfully proved the guilt of accused who had been sentenced accordingly.

Heading: ‘Let’s go’ rally held in city - Indian Express
Content:
Paramjit Singh Walia was made the chairman of the district unit of the All-India Congress Committee Rajiv Gandhi Panchayat Raj Sanghathan at a meeting held at Basant Resorts here today. The meeting was chaired by the chairman of the Punjab unit of the Sanghathan, Jagtar Singh Burj, where general secretary Rajesh Rudhra and spokesperson Kimti Rawal were also present.

Addressing the conference, Rudhra said that through this organisation, Rahul Gandhi was going to fulfill the dream of Mahatama Gandhi and Rajiv Gandhi of Panchayati Raj. A total of 10 lakh workers — honest, loyal and dedicated with clean credentials — will fan out to accomplish the task, said Rudhra

The sanghathan is aiming to tap 70% of voters in the villages. A state-level conference will also be held soon which will be presided over by Rahul Gandhi, he added

Addressing the mediapersons, the chairman, Jagtar Singh said the organisation would endeavour to strengthen the panchayats and panchayat judiciary so that they did not have to grope for justice. Panchayat Raj is such a mechanism through which a simple man can enjoy the powers of the government, he explained.

Through this organisation, training will be given to the panches and sarpanches, so that they know their rights thereby creating awareness among the people of the villages.

Heading: 41st Engineers’s Day celebrated at GNDEC - Indian Express
Content:
Alto Let's go Rally was organised at Ludhiana on Sunday to create driving awareness among the users of Alto car to get the best mileage out of their cars.

The purpose of the rally, being organised by Maruti Suzuki India Ltd in all major cities of India, is not to finish in the shortest possible time, but to get the maximum possible mileage out of their Alto car by driving safely in the city conditions. Speed is not the test, but extracting the maximum mileage is the goal of the participants of the rally.

The response received by the rally in the city was overwhelming with total 52 participants along with their family taking the total number to 156. Maximum mileage recorded in the rally was 39.2 km per litre by Rakesh Kumar. The average mileage recorded by all was 23.8 km per litre.

The three contestants obtaining the highest mileage were honoured by Ankur Sharma, Regional Manager, Maruti Suzuki India Ltd, with attractive prizes like air conditioner, home theatre and micro wave oven. The award ceremony was held at Hotel Majestic Park Plaza and ended with a gala lunch function for the participants and their families.

Heading: BCET college students shine - Indian Express
Content:
41st Engineers' Day was celebrated at Guru Nanak Dev Engineering College here on Monday. The chief guest on this occasion was Dr S.K. Sondi, Ex-Dean, Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana, while the function was presided over by Dr M.S. Saini, principal, GNDEC.

Section chairman IIE, Ludhiana chapter, Surinder Singh, explained the importance of the day and said that it was celebrated in the memory of Sir M Visvesvaraya, father of engineering in India. He was honoured with Bharat Rattan for his contribution to the engineering field.

A.S. Pandher, retired chief engineer, Irrigation Department, who was the guest of honour on the day, said that the Institution of Engineers had chosen this year as "Planet Earth Year" and UNO also has declared 2008 as International Year of Planet Earth.

Puneet Pal Singh Cheema gave a talk on "Climate change and water" which provided a message, "How the melting of glacier and other issues are causing high sea levels" which it is one of the major environmental issues today. Dr Jagbir Singh gave a talk on mega cities and explained how they were needed for our urban future. This is causing changes in India in the form of intensified heat waves and extreme temperature range in some areas.

Dr S.B. Singh, Ex-Principal, GNDEC, M.N. Sharma, Chief Engineer, Ludhiana Municipal Corporation, Balbir Singh, Ex-Chief Engineer, Irrigation Department, Dr H.S. Rai, Professor and Head, Civil Engineering Department, Dr J.N. Jha, Professor and Dean (Consultancy), Prof Kanwaljit Singh, Head of Electronics and Communication Engineering Department, Prof Nirmal Singh Grewal, Dean (Students and Welfare), Col Gusum, Secretary, Institute of Engineers, Ludhiana Chapter, B.B. Goyal, LMC, Ludhiana, S.K. Salaria, LMC, Ludhiana, K.S. Gill, Harinder Singh, Dr B.S. Walia of Civil Engineering Department were present on the occasion.

Heading: Follow PAU-advised farm practices, V-C tells farmers - Indian Express
Content:
"The students of Bhutta College of Engineering and Technology (BCET) brought laurels to the institute by securing excellent marks in the MBA (4th semester) examination held by Punjab Technical University in May 2008", said Dr R.S. Gupta, Director, BCET, in a press note issued here today.

Ninety five per cent students bagged first division and 53 pc passed with honours (more than 70 pc marks). Khush Kamal Kaur bagged the first position in the college be securing 89% marks, Harjeet Kaur got second position with 87 pc marks, and Gurpreet Kaur secured the third position with 84.3 pc marks and was closely followed by Manpreet Kaur who got fourth position with 84 pc marks.

Johny Garch and Balbiri Singh Garcha, members of management and Dr R.S. Gupta, Director, BCET, congratulated the members of faculty and students for their excellent performance.

International Peace Day celebrated
NSS units of SDP College for Women celebrated international Peace Day under the guidance of programme officers B. Ahuja, Raugang Sood and Ramneek. NSS volunteers presented poems and speeches on the theme of world peace on the occasion. Aarti, Meenakshi, Manisha, Veena and Lovely presented self-composed poems and conveyed the message of international peace.

Compositions by Rachna, Shikha, Squnta, Madhu, Hemlata, Babita, Jaswinder, Shikha and Vimmy were the star-attraction. Officiating principal Veena Gian Singh Mann while addressing the volunteers on the occasion urged them to use their skills for promoting communal harmony, universal brotherhood and international peace. The celebration was followed by career counselling presentation by a team from Viva Tour and Travel Institute.

Heading: CM blames UPA govt for ills facing nation - Indian Express
Content:
A regional Kisan Mela was organised by the Punjab Agricultural University at Krishi Vigyan Kendra, Rauni, on Monday.

PAU Vice-Chancellor Dr Manjit Singh Kang, who inaugurated the mela, said that agriculture was passing through ecological and economic constraints and there was a need to bolster farmers' income through allied ventures and diversification of agriculture. He said that need-based technology for water conservation and maintaining soil health was being developed. He mentioned that farmers, by using tensiometer for scheduling irrigation and leaf colour chart, for applying nitrogen to paddy judiciously, have been able to translate expert advice in their fields. He said that the university had laid emphasis on developing technologies with a focus on natural resource conservation. He advised farmers to use natural resources prudently.

Dr Kang said that the PAU had evolved a number of recommendations for management of region-specific problems and that it is keeping in view the specific requirement of small farmers while developing package of practices for different crops. He said that the farmers should maintain a rapport with farm experts.

He shared that PAU was promoting the influx of students from rural areas to agricultural and home science programmes so that after obtaining education, they could serve the cause of agriculture. He said that water table was a serious problem in Punjab, especially in central Punjab and that the prevailing agro-climatic conditions permitted growing of fruit crops and some vegetable crops for which production technologies had been recommended. He said that PAU scientists were always at the service of farmers. He suggested farmers to regularly participate in Kisan Melas of PAU and to develop habit of reading farm literature brought out by PAU.

Heading: MC razes illegal structures in Feroze Gandhi market - Indian Express
Content:
Clearly getting into poll mode, Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal today blamed the directionless policies of the Congress-led UPA Government at the Centre for problems of poverty, illiteracy and poor pace of development in the country.

Addressing a huge political conference of SAD at the historic Chhappar Mela at Chappar, today, Badal said that the Congress in particularly had always adopted anti-Punjab policies, which had caused a severe damage to the economy of the state.

The Chief Minister while lambasting the Union government for adopting discriminatory approach towards Punjab farmers, who had baled the country out of the severe food crisis by contributing around 60 per cent in the national food pool. He said that it was a cruel joke on the farmers that the Central government had fixed Rs 850 per quintal as MSP for paddy in the coming season, which was even much below Rs 1,000 per qtl recommended by Agriculture Price Commission.

He said that to ensure the acceleration of speedy development and prosperity of the state, a like-minded government must be installed at the Centre by throwing out the UPA government in the coming Lok Sabha elections. Unfolding the plans of his government for the all-round development and welfare, Badal asserted that each and every promise made during the elections with the people would be fulfilled. He informed that a crash programme had been launched at a cost of Rs 3,540 crore for the repair and strengthening of 5300 kms roads in the state. He said that all the major highways in the state were being developed into six or four laned at a cost of Rs 3,035 crore under a special programme.

He said that his government was committed for the improvement in the education system in the rural areas and one Adarash Model School was being set up in each constituency, where the education facilities would be provided at par with the reputed Punjabi schools.

Sukhbir Singh Badal, President, SAD, while addressing the conference said that the Congress, which ruled the country most of the time during 60 years after independence, had completely ruined the economy and development process in the country. Ridiculing the false challenges/threats of Capt Amarinder Singh former Chief Minister, Badal said that he was a coward, who fled abroad instead of facing the legal process in the corruption cases registered against him. He asked how much time he could spend in the foreign countries to evade the process of law for his misdeeds? He said that one day he will have to face the punishment for the of large-scale corruption and atrocities committed during his misrule.

Referring to the development plans of SAD Govt, he said that the power sector was the main priority and asserted that during the next four years, power projects of 8000 to 9000 MW capacity were being executed approximately at a cost of Rs 50,000 crore in private sector and the state would definitely be a power-surplus state.

Among others who addressed the conference were Jagdev Singh Talwandi, Senior Akali Leader, Charanjit Singh Atwal, Deputy Speaker Lok Sabha, Capt Kanwaljit Singh, Cooperative Minister, Hira Singh Gabria Jails Minster, Harish Rai Dhanda, Bikramjit Singh Khalsa (both CPS), Balwinder Singh Bhunder Ex-Minster, Jagjiwan Singh Khirnia, Darshan Singh Shivalik, Iqbal Singh Jhunda (all MLAs), Manpreet Ayali Chairman ZP, Santa Singh Umedpuri district President SAD Rural, Jagdish Singh Garcha Ex- Minister, Ranjit Talwandi and Inder Iqbal Singh Atwal.

Heading: Powercuts, diesel scarcity make life miserable - Indian Express
Content:
The Tehbazari branch of the Municipal Corporation today conducted a drive to remove illegal encroachments in the city. The team first demolished a few hutments near the Feroze Gandhi market and later moved towards the Mini Secretariat, where they faced stiff resistance. This was the tenth time in the past two months when the team had gone to the complex to remove encroachments. The team entered into a heated argument with the shopkeepers. The episode continued for about half an hour and later the stalls of typists, dhaba owners, driving licence agents and many others were removed. Most of these stalls were back again after an hour.

Later, the team went towards the Bharat Nagar chowk, where they demolished stairs and ramp of many showrooms including Saligram and Omparkash - a furniture store, Gujral Tyres, MRF Tyres, Ludhiana Eggmart, amongst others. The team finally reached the Canara Bank to demolish their stairs, but the bank staff argued taking a plea that they are a public sector department and hence should be given more time.

The team gave them one-week to clear the illegal construction site.

Heading: No syllabus and datesheet, 185 teachers shun exam - Indian Express
Content:
The city is reeling under severe power crisis. Six hours of powercuts coupled with shortage of diesel to run generators has made the life of city residents miserable.

Most of the city's petrol pumps are running short of diesel thus making residents run from one petrol pump to the other to fetch the fuel.

Petrol pump dealers, too, have stated that there has been an increase in the demand of the fuel by about 20 per cent, which has further widened the gap between demand and supply.

Meanwhile, the Punjab State Electricity Board (PSEB) officials have stated that the power situation in the state will continue for a month.

The city faces powercuts for one hour in the morning and five hours at a stretch in the afternoon. Gulshan Kumar, a resident of the Pakhowal Road, while talking to Newsline, said, "I had to go to five different petrol pumps to get diesel. Pumps located near railway crossing on the Pakhowal Road, Canal Road, pumps in Dugri denied the fuel. Finally, I got some fuel from a petrol pump near Verka milk plant and that too after standing in a long queue for over an hour."

JP Khanna, President, Petrol Pump Dealers' Association, said, "Being an industrial city, the demand-supply gap in the city has widened."

Meanwhile, PSEB officials have revealed that their hydel share has been reduced by about 140 MW due to slow melting of glaciers.

Apart from 6 hours power cuts, city residents also face technical snags due to which power cuts in many areas stretch to more than 10 hours.

Heading: Ayurvedic dept to get regular officers in 14 districts - Indian Express
Content:
Boycott: Certificate of Teaching English exam was held under the Sarv Shiksha Abhiyan

A Majority of the 442 schoolteachers of different schools in the district, who were to take the exam for the 'Certificate of Teaching English' in the city, boycotted the examination today.

The exam was held under the Sarv Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA).

The teachers protested that they had neither received any syllabus nor were informed about the dates of the four exams. Shaheed-e-Azam Sukhdev Thapar Government Girls' Senior Secondary School, Bharat Nagar, was the centre of the exam.

Joint Front of 17 Bodies of Teachers member Pyara Singh Dhillon said it was two years ago that schools were asked to send the list of the teachers of social studies who also teach English. It was decided that these teachers would be imparted certificates of teaching English by holding the exams under SSA.

Speaking on behalf of the teachers, Dhillon said, "As many as 185 teachers boycotted the exam and registered their protest with us today. Only 15 teachers took the exam."

A teacher contended, "We are all trained graduate teachers. The exam is of lower standard as we have already studied and passed what they have included in the test."

Another teacher, who also boycotted the exam, said, "We neither received the syllabus for these four exams that they are holding nor did they ever send us the schedule of the exam. It was only yesterday that we were informed about the exam."

Many of them said they were informed about the test when they reached their respective schools this morning. "We were told that the exam would be held at 12 pm while it was to start at 3 pm," a teacher said.

Heading: PAU agri business students roll out plan to get jobs - Indian Express
Content:
For the first time in the last six years, the Ayurvedic department will have regular District Ayurvedic and Unani Officers for the 14 districts in the state.

The move is expected to give boost to the department which has long been clamouring for better promotional benefits and facilities to deliver the best in the Indian System of Medicine (ISM).

According to an order passed by the department on September 12, as many as 14 officers have been promoted to the rank of regular District Ayurvedic and Unani Officer. Until now, the officers who were discharging their duty at the district level were doing it in the capacity of Drawing and Disbursing Officers (DDO).

At present, there are only two regular District Ayurvedic Officers in the state and the order has been awaited for a long time to appoint regular District Ayurvedic Officers.

Ayurvedic department Joint Director Dr Inderjit confirmed that 14 districts will soon have regular district ayurvedic and unani officers. "We have sent the orders to the different districts and all these officers will take the charge in a couple of days," he said.

Those who have been promoted as District Ayurvedic and Unani Officer include Dr Sham Sunder at Amritsar, Dr Madan Lal at Jalandhar, Dr Satpal Khanna at Bathinda, Dr Kuldeep Singh at Mansa, Dr Gokul Chand at Sangrur, Dr Ram Pratap at Patiala, Dr Vishwamitra at Fatehgarh Sahib, Dr Raj Kumar Popli at Ferozepur, Dr Kamal Kishore at Faridkot, Dr Keval Krishan Sehgal at Hoshiarpur, Dr Mohammad Iqlakh (Unani) at Kapurthala, Dr Rajinder Kumar Sangar at Ropar and Dr Bakshish Singh at Ludhiana.

Commenting on the decision of the department, former Ayurvedic officer Dr Jawahar Dheer said, "It is definitely a welcome change in the department. Though officers like me retired without any promotional benefits for want of this decision, it is now going to boost the morale of the ayurvedic officers in different districts of the state."

The latest development to promote 14 officers of the department to the rank of District Ayurvedic and

Unani Officer has come after the decision to install ISM Wings and AYUSH speciality clinics in seven districts of the state.

Heading: Rains fail to provide relief in two Kutch talukas - Indian Express
Content:
While on-campus interviews may be one way to find placement in companies, the 20-odd students of the Department of Agri Business, College of Basic Sciences and Humanities have devised a novel way not only to secure new avenues for placement but also for an hands-on training in rural marketing.

According to Dr Ramandeep Singh, who teaches rural marketing, "Nearly 300 companies dealing mainly in agriculture will visit the university for two days during the Kissan Mela. This is just the right kind of exposure our students need. I have asked the agri business as well as MBA students to prepare consumer preference questionnaires to be filled by the farmers thronging the mela. This will help us in gauging what kind of services farmers need and this information can in turn be shared with the companies."

Dr Singh added, "The basic idea is to get in touch with the masses. For this, teams have been constituted and each team will be collecting data. I am hopeful that at least 150out of 300 companies will benefit from our data. This in turn will open up a lot of job avenues for our students."

Poonamdeep Cheema, a final-year student of agri business who has been entrusted with the task of co-ordinating with the teams, said, "Our paper work is ready. We will enlighten farmers about the services being provided by companies. In the next step, we will take a feedback from the farmers whether they are satisfied with the services or they require any changes.

Cheema adds, "The exercise will be beneficial for both students and the corporate sector. The companies in turn will get a human resource data. And farmers get to voice their opinion to the corporate world."

Heading: Heavy rains just not enough to quench Rajkot residents’ thirst - Indian Express
Content:
The latest spell of rains has not been enough to assuage the drinking water woes, especially of the milch animals in the Abadasa and Lakhapat talukas of Kutch.

"The rains have not been enough to meet the drinking water requirements of our animals," said Satish Thackar, sarpanch of Nalia.

Vishwanath Joshi, a leading social worker and local journalist of Lakhapat said that while the farmers in his taluka were happy, the maldharis were worried because the dams and ponds in the taluka have not received much water.

Resident Deputy Collector Mahesh Dave said that the rains have definitely brought the much needed succour to the state. Abadasa and Lakhapat talukas have not been as lucky as the other 8 talukas, but they still have received generous showers, Dave said.

Heading: Violence in Dangs: Fear of cops makes youths hide in forest - Indian Express
Content:
RMC fails to make proper utilisation of surplus water in Nyari-I and Nyari-II dams

Drinking water crisis in the district continues to persist notwithstanding good rains in the last three days. Although Nyari-I and Nyari-II dams have a water surplus, the Rajkot Municipal Corporation (RMC) has failed to provide drinking water in the city.

When contacted, N H Waghela, Former city Engineer and RMC Advisor on water issues said: "We have received good rains in this last spell. Our Nyari and Aji dams, which had hit the rock bottom last month, now have ample water. Nevertheless, we are not in a position to supply drinking water daily to the residents."

He added: "We need 360 lakh gallons of water everyday. We can draw 100 lakh gallons from Bhadar, 100 lakh gallons from Nyari-I and Nyari-II and 80 lakh gallons from Narmada. Even after that, a deficit of 80 lakh gallons will remain. If we draw water from the Aji Dam, then water in the dam will last for only four months. If more rains replenish the water stock at Aji, we will definitely think about daily supply."

The entire district has received ample rains in the last 48 hours. The fresh rains have come as a lifesaver for the crops in the region.

One drowns in Nyari River
A man met with a watery grave when a car carrying three people was sucked into the flooded Nyari River near Dholra village on the outskirts of Rajkot city on Sunday evening. NRI businessman Raghvir Rughani (65) was drowned while the other two persons succeeded in coming out alive. Fire brigade personnel recovered the body after several hours of search on Monday afternoon.

Heading: Two killed as boat capsises;four Junagadh villages marooned - Indian Express
Content:
Nandand Peda village in Dang district holds quite a barren look these days. Youths of this only minority-dominated village of the district are hiding from the police fearing an attack from them.

The sense of fear follows Thursday's incident in which cops had arrested a truck driver of the village claiming that he was involved in illegal transportation of cattle to the slaughterhouses of Malegaon, Maharashtra. Angry villagers had retaliated by pelting stones at police personnel and severely injuring Ahwa police sub-inspector A T Borse.

Fearing an attack from the angry cops, villagers hid in the forest areas leaving the entire village empty. Protesting against the attack on police, the Vishwa Hindu Parishad has declared Dangs bandh on Tuesday. Later in the afternoon, VHP members will take out a rally from Vaghai village to Ahwa in Dang and hand over a memorandum to the district collector of Ahwa seeking strict action against the people of Nandand Peda village.

On Sunday, police arrested six people from different villages allegedly involved in assaulting cops. They are Gulab Wani, Gulab Bhest, Majid Wani, Moiyuddin Naik, Gulam Shaikh and Hafezi Yusuf.

Karim Shaikh, a resident of Nandand Peda village, said: "Police came to our village on Thursday night and started beating up women and the elderly. The scared youths escaped from the village."

VHP president of Dangs, Gaman Gangude, said: "We condemn the assault on police. The residents of Nandand Peda village are supplying cattle to the slaughterhouses of Malegaon. The accused should be caught and punished."

Range IG Shivanand Jha said: "The situation in Nandand Peda village is peaceful. I am unaware of the Dang Bandh declared by the VHP."

Heading: Surat textile labourer beaten to death by neighbour - Indian Express
Content:
Over 1,000 villagers evacuated after overflowing Uben river enters low-lying villages

At least 1,000 people were evacuated from four villages in Junagadh district following heavy rains on Monday. In a separate incident, two persons, including a seven-year-old child, died when a small fish off the Mangarol coast on Monday.

The floodwaters of Uben river entered the low-lying areas of Majewadi, Kerala, Valasimadi and Choki villages. The villagers have been shifted to safer areas.

Meanwhile, Anwar Allarakha (35) and a seven-year-old child drowned in the sea when the boat they were travelling in capsized near Sheriyaj-bara off Mangarol coast.

With the rivers already swollen, seven dams in the district, including Hasnapur, Aambajal, Dharafad, Ozat 1 and 2, Ozat (Shapur) and Ozat (Vanthali), are overflowing. The sluice gates of many dams have also opened.

According to a district flood control official, all the 14 talukas of Junagadh district received an average of three to eight inches of

rainfall. In the last 24 hours Keshod received 200 mm of rainfall, Una 167 mm, Visavadar and Kodinar 165 mm each, Junagadh 140 mm, Vanthali 136 mm, Talala 135 mm,

Mandarada 130 mm, Maliya 121 mm, Manawadar 111 mm, Veraval 87 mm, Mangarol 85 mm, Sutrapada 75 mm and Bhesan 75 mm.

Heading: Three drown asST bus plunges into river; 19 injured and seven still missing - Indian Express
Content:
A 25-year-old textile labourer was beaten to death by his neighbour over a minor issue on Sunday night. The police have launched a manhunt for the accused.

According to the police, some six days back, Padam Pradhan, (24) a resident of Patelnagar, in Bhestan, returned home from work only to find his neighbour Bhaya Bishnoi and his friends gambling outside the main door of his house.

An angry Pradhan then asked Bishnoi not to gamble in front of his door, which led to an altercation between the two.

Later, Bishnoi hatched a plan to teach him a lesson. On Sunday, when Pradhan was returning home from work, Bishnoi intercepted him near the Bhestan railway crossing and repeatedly hit him with sticks, causing severe head injury.

His body was found by some passers-by, who informed the police. A diary found on his body carried his elder brother, Pratap Pradhan's address. He was summoned to identify the body.

Investigations led to the revelation that the deceased had had a conflict with Bishnoi. Pratap then lodged a complaint with the Pandesara police station in this connection. Pandesara police inspector D M Brahambhatt said, "We have launched a search operation and have even looked for Bishnoi at his relative's place."

Heading: Mastermind’s Man Friday leaves a trail of destruction - Indian Express
Content:
When the bus was some 20 km short of Junagadh, it plunged into the flooded river while crossing a bridge

Three persons including a senior forest official died on the spot while 19 others were injured when the State Transport bus they were travelling in fell into river Uben near Junagadh on Sunday night. Seven other persons are reportedly missing. The incident occurred on the Junagadh-Rajkot highway, between Juni-Sankli and Pipalawa village — some 20 km from Junagadh.

According to unconfirmed reports, there were some 29 passengers travelling in the bus. While three have died and 19 seriously injured, nobody knows the whereabouts of the other seven passengers, who have either drowned or perhaps alighted at an earlier destination. The injured, including the bus driver and conductor, have been admitted in the Junagadh Civil Hospital.

The three who have died in the accident have been identified as Devabhai Parmar, Thakorbhai Thaker, and And Ogha Parbat. It is learnt that Parmar was a senior forest official posted at Ahmedabad, while Thaker was a journalist associated with a local daily.

According to Junagadh ST depot official, bus no. GJ 18 V 449 that plies on the Junagadh-Unjha route had left Junagadh at around 11.30 pm on Sunday night. When the bus was some 20 km short of Junagadh, it plunged into the flooded river while crossing a bridge.

Heading: Police remand of July 26 blast accused extended by 24 hours - Indian Express
Content:
He is an explosive expert and carries a veritable bomb in his depraved mind. Meet Qayamuddin Sarfiddin Kapadia, suspected to be one of the main conspirators of the recent blasts in Delhi. He is also wanted by the Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) in connection with the serial blasts that rocked Ahmedabad on July 26. DCB officials have reasons to believe that he stayed in Ahmedabad for over a month prior to the blasts and held meetings to plan the terror attacks.

DCB officials said Qayamuddin is a fundamentalist and possesses good knowledge of explosives. He is believed to have played a vital role in the training camps organised by the banned outfit, Students Islamic Movement of India (SIMI) at various places across India. He has been evading arrest ever since the Madhya Pradesh police came to arrest him following the arrest of SIMI idealogue Safdar Nagori in March this year.

Qayamuddin lived with his family at Bagechistiya Vadi, Taiwada, Kumbharwada in Vadodara city and ran a business of rubber stamps before he disappeared from the city. Police officers investigating the Ahmedabad blasts case say that even Qayamuddin's family members have no news of him and nor have they been able to contact him in the recent past. He had been once earlier arrested for stabbing a person.

DCB officials believe that Qayamuddin is a close aide of Abdul Subhan alias Tauqeer, the mastermind of July 26 Ahmedabad blasts and one of the co-conspirators of the Mumbai Train Blasts. He had put up with Tauqeer in a rented house in Vatva area of Ahmedabad to plan and execute the July 26 blasts.

He had been given the responsibility of planting the bombs in Ahmedabad and Surat and was the one who had purchased the bicycles used in the blasts and also selected the youths who had planted the bombs.

Police sources said that Sajid Mansuri, another core member of the SIMI module of the Ahmedabad Blasts, had introduced Qayamuddin to Tanvir Pathan — who has been arrested by the Surat police for his role in the Ahmedabad blasts. It is believed that Tanvir provided logistical support to Qayamuddin for planting bombs in Surat.

Heading: Attack on Christian institutions condemned - Indian Express
Content:
The accused, including alleged mastermind ABU Bashar, are in custody for the past 28 days

Metropolitan magistrate G M Patel on Monday extended the police remand of the 10 persons accused of planting bombs in Khadia and Raipur Chakla areas of Ahmedabad on July 26, by another 24 hours.

Among those whose police custody has been extended are Mufti Abu Basher, reported to be one of the masterminds, Sajid Mansuri and Shamsuddin Sheikh. They have been in police custody for the past 28 days.

The magistrate rejected the plea made by defence advocate I M Munshi, who sought that the statements of the accused be recorded either in the magistrate chamber or by the defence advocate in absence of police to find out if they had been subjected to mental or physical torture during custody.

In his plea, Munshi argued that the accused would not be able to furnish the correct details in presence of police personnel.

Meanwhile, Shamsuddin's wife Zahidabanu filed an affidavit before the magistrate seeking directions for medical treatment of her husband. It has, however, been rejected. She had contended that her husband had been kept in unauthorised detention for several days before the police declared his arrest. She pleaded that her husband required urgent medical treatment, as he had been physically and mentally abused in police custody.

In her submission, she said that the police had called her husband on August 1, August 2 and then on August 4 for recording his statements. On all the three occasions, he was released after his statements were recorded. However, he was not released after police called him on August 8.

On August 14, police declared that Shamsuddin had been arrested.

Heading: I-T dept searches Bhuj developers’ group - Indian Express
Content:
Prashant, a centre for human rights, justice and peace, has condemned the recent attack by Sangh Parivar on Christians and their institutions in Mangalore and the surrounding areas of Karnataka.

In a statement issued on Monday, Director of Prashant, Fr Cedric Prakash, said: "They have assaulted innocent and peace-loving people, vandalised property, desecrated places of worship and created terror everywhere. Such behaviour is totally unacceptable in civil society and all of us need to hang our heads in shame." He said that above all, the partisan role that the police and the district administration played deserves severe condemnation.

It is also understood that at some places, police refused to file FIRs or register complaints, he said adding that these were reprehensible acts not expected from those supposed to protect the lives and property of people.

"The attacks in Karnataka by these fascist, fundamentalist and anti-national forces, follow exactly the same pattern as that in Orissa, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Gujarat. These affiliates of the BJP take law and order into their own hands in total connivance with the state administration. In fact, the chief minister and the home minister of Karnataka have gone on record to give their followers a clean chit inspite of documentary evidence to prove otherwise," he said.

Demanding immediate ban on Sangh Parivar affiliates, he demanded that the central government should monitor the Karnataka situation very closely and if the scenario failed to improve, it would warrant the dismissal of the state government and the imposition of President's Rule.

He asked people in general to protest these heinous acts of destroying the diversity and secular fabric of the country.

Heading: Bus rapid system to give AMTS the kiss of life - Indian Express
Content:
Investigating wing of the Income-Tax (I-T) department began an extensive search and seizure operation on several premises of a prominent group of real estate agents and developers in Bhuj on Monday.

A total of 29 places, including the groups' business and residential premises were covered in the operation, I-T officials said.

About 200 officials, including the local police personnel, were involved in the operation. Alongwith a large number of incriminating documents that indicate the groups' unaccounted affairs, the I-T sleuths have also seized their bank accounts and lockers. "The seized documents are presently being analysed and the actual amount of evasion can be established in a day or two," a top I-T officer said.

Heading: GU ready with its wishlist as date for UGC team’s visit draws close - Indian Express
Content:
AMTS could generate revenue by operating on feeder routes of BRTS at major points like Akhbarnagar, Shivranjani cross, Ankur and Vasna

Introduction of the Bus Rapid Transit System (BRTS) in the city is likely to revive the ailing Ahmedabad Municipal Transport Service (AMTS).

The AMTS incurs monthly losses to the tune of Rs 5 crore. For years, the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC) has been compensating for these losses. Though the introduction of BRTS will shrink the network of AMTS, it will also give the Service a chance to reach new areas and make up for its lost revenue generation.

Sources in AMTS said that BRTS may provide new business to AMTS. For, because of the introduction of a limited number of buses on BRTS, AMTS will have a chance to improve upon its service quality and add more buses on its routes.

"While the current requirement of Ahmedabad's five million population is 1,500 buses, only 800 are plying on city roads. Even if we presume that BRTS will have 100 buses in the initial phase, it means that at least 600 buses are still needed to meet the demand," said a senior AMTS official.

Deputy municipal commissioner in charge of AMTS, T G Jhalawadia, said: "The AMTS will have a wonderful business opportunity as the operator of feeder routes of BRTS at major points like Akhbarnagar, Shivranjani cross, Ankur and Vasna."

He said that the first phase of BRTS will be launched in November end.

"AMTS can generate great revenues by taking commuters to BRTS stops," he added.

However, it must be noted that AMTS's revival itself depends on the success of BRTS, which will be accepted by commuters only if its fares are similar to AMTS fares.

Heading: IIM-A students to get lesson in managing carbon footprints - Indian Express
Content:
Varsity to demand more teachers, better laboratories and better infrastructure when the XI Plan panel visits campus on Sept 19-20

More teachers, better labs, laptops and better infrastructure form the Gujarat University's (GU) wishlist as the University Grants Commission's XI Plan Expert Visiting Committee will be in the varsity on September 19 and 20 to assess its Eleventh Finance Plan requirement and review the Tenth Finance Plan.

Prof T N Kapoor, Former V-C of Panjan University, Chandigarh, C K Capahi, Member Secretary of the Committee and L M Jain, Officer for the Committee will visit GU.

These committees are sent at the beginning of every plan period to evaluate the performance/ implementation of previous plans and assess the financial requirement of the university for the next plan.

Reports from various departments point out that 30-40 per cent posts are lying vacant. There is also a need of financial support for the development of infrastructure and exemption plans of their departments.

The report submitted by the Physical Education Department mentions that, there is scarcity of lecturers in their department. They feel that there is an urgent need to appoint three lecturers. Head of the Department (HOD), HN Desai told Newsline, "We need a laboratory and more books for the students."

Chairperson of Women's Development Cell (WDC), Ranjana Harish, added: "To make the department more efficient, we need assistant office staff. It is not possible to carry out activities without them. More funds should be allocated for the infrastructure development and for promotional activities. A proposal has been sent to the authorities in this regard."

Report submitted by the School of Languages indicates that since 1968, no expansion plans have been undertaken by the university. Moreover, around 40 per cent posts are vacant in the departments running under the School. Director of the School of Languages, Vasant Bhatt, said that a new department of comparative studies, drama, and translation needs to be formed immediately.

Bhatt added that around 60 per cent students in the department are from the reserved category and their pronunciation is not up to the mark. So, to improve on their skills, a remedial center is a must.

The report submitted by the School of Law shows that till date they have had limited access to the software related to law studies. The department also lacks computers and a proper lab.

School of Social Sciences has asked for laptops and desktop computers for their faculties and to fill the 35 per cent posts that lie vacant.

School of Commerce has specifically made demands for funds to buy new books, journals and upgradation of their library.

The authorities of the Gujarat University were not available for comment.

Heading: Relatives create ruckus in hospital after death of three-year-old - Indian Express
Content:
The premier institute launches carbon finance course to fulfill the needs of the growing market

The Indian Institute of Management-Ahmedabad (IIM-A) has launched a course on carbon finance to train budding managers in the various aspects of Global Warming and carbon emission.

Prof P R Shukla, one of the designers of the course, said that the aim of the course is to sensitise and prepare future managers about the emerging market as well as its implications both in scientific and business terms.

"The carbon industry is amongst the fastest growing markets across the globe. By 2012, the volume of the carbon market is projected to be only second to that of global oil and gas market," said Prof Shukla.

Jointly designed by Prof Shukla and one of his IIM-A colleagues, the course has attracted 126 5th term PGP students, including 13 students from the European Union.

While IIM-A is the first institution to introduce such a course in India, there are a very few institutes which offer something similar at the international level, said Prof Shukla. Global carbon expert Ram Babu, who is also the Managing Director of Cantor CO2e, a London-based company, said: "While there exists a huge and expanding market for carbon, there is also a shortage of expertise in the sector. By 2012, the volume of carbon trade across the globe is expected to touch 100 billion dollars and India will play a major role in this scenario."

"Over the last year, India earned about 200 million dollars in the trade. The volume can only increase in the coming years," he said, adding that by 2012, India can expect to earn about 15 billion dollars from the sector.

"Under this situation, a Carbon Finance course introduced by a premier institute like IIM-A will go a long way in addressing the human resource crisis in the area," Babu said. Pratki Vaid, a student of the course, said: "This is an exciting course. It prepares us for some real entrepreneurial ventures. We have a lot of guest speakers from the industry itself, which is really helpful when it comes to getting practical and relevant insight into the subject."

Heading: Playing Cupid dooms man as wife and daughter deliver him to death - Indian Express
Content:
Family accuses doctors of negligence in treatment of boy suffering from bronchial infection

Death of a three-year-old boy during treatment at Shardaben Hospital led to a furore on Monday when his family accused the hospital staff of negligence in treatment. After receiving the news, the boy's family and relatives attacked the hospital, damaged furniture and assaulted the staff, including professor and head of the Paediatric Department Dr Jaishree Mehta.

Hospital superintendent Dr Nimesh Pandya later said that no one was injured in the attack and no police complaint was lodged in this case.

K R Joshi, manager of the hospital, said the staff was not responsible for the boy's death, as he was already in a critical condition when he was brought to the hospital at around 7 am on Monday.

According to hospital authorities, the boy, Alkam, was suffering from bronchial infection. But his family was reluctant to get him admitted to the hospital and asked the doctors for an OPD treatment.

"We tried to convince them that the boy's condition was critical and he needed proper indoor treatment instead of the OPD treatment. The family finally agreed to get the boy admitted. However, the boy developed convulsions during treatment and died after a while," said doctors.

Dr Pandya said that this led Alkam's relatives to believe that the hospital staff showed negligence in treating him. Soon after, they started smashing furniture, breaking glasses and attacking the staff, he said.

Doctors are upset at the way the relatives misbehaved with them. Later, Rakhial AMC councilor Taufiq Khan Pathan visited the hospital and pacified the restive staff and doctors.

Heading: Govt fumbles for ‘power’ as wind energy is left untapped - Indian Express
Content:
A man was allegedly killed by his wife and daughter at Kathwada village near Odhav in Ahmedabad district on Sunday. The two accused were arrested on Monday afternoon after the Odhav police took custody of the body from the nearby Kambha village, when the accused were about to perform the last rites.

According to Odhav police, Govind Rathod (48) was allegedly clubbed to death by his wife Nirmala (41) and daughter Hetal (18) at their residence in Indira Vasahat in Kathawad village. The incident occurred around 1 pm on Sunday. Preliminary investigation revealed that the accused were unhappy with the engagement of Hetal that Govind had fixed with a boy from Bilasia village.

"The mother and daughter were unhappy with the engagement fixed by Govind. Their differences often resulted in quarrels. On Sunday, it turned fatal for Govind when the mother-daughter duo clubbed Govind to death," said Inspector V J Raval.

Police say that Nirmala and Hetal, in an attempt to cover up the murder, took the body to Nirmala's ancestral village, Kambha. Meanwhile, it were the neighbours who informed the police about the murder.

Based on a complaint filed by Ramesh Jadav, a neighbour of the Rathods, Odhav police arrested Nirmala and Hetal under IPC 302 and 114 on charge of murder. The role of other family members including Nimala's brother would be examined during the investigation, police said.

Heading: Vandalism blurs party lines: FIR against BJP MLA’s nephew, Cong leader’s brother - Indian Express
Content:
The recent entry of India's flagship energy company—Oil and Natural Gas Corporation — into the wind power sector with the commissioning of its first-ever 50 MW wind power plant in Kutch, has raised some questions about the "not-so-transparent" and unregulated wind farm sector in Gujarat.

India, with 8754 MW of installed wind power capacity, is one of the leading nations in the category. It now plans to add another 10,000 MW during the 11th Five Year Plan. But what is surprising is that this is the first time an energy company has shown interest in the wind energy sector which otherwise has been dominated by investors like hospitality companies, spinning mills, temple trusts, cricketers and even film stars till now.

The scenario appears all the more hazy in the state of Gujarat that has about 1252.9 MW of installed wind power as per March 2008 figures. It may be mentioned here that the Gujarat government had announced its Wind Power Policy on June 13, 2007 with an intention to promote clean and green energy to reduce carbon dioxide emissions. But the wind farm energy experience has not been pleasant so far.

The fiscal and financial incentives provided by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Government of India, which include concessions such as 80 per cent accelerated depreciation in the first year, concessions in custom duty on specified items, excise duty exemption, sales tax exemption and income tax holiday for 10 years are already attracting investors. Also, the Gujarat government's policy has virtually made entry into the wind energy business a lucrative affair, as within one year of its commissioning the power plant can become free of cost.

The Wind Power Policy 2007 of Gujarat includes incentives for Wind Turbine Generators for a period of 20 years, provision for wheeling of electricity at a 4 per cent charge, provision to sell power to any entity at higher prices i.e. third party sale, exemption from electricity duty and demand cut to the extent of 30 per cent and even raising the rate of sale of power to GUVNL to Rs 3.37 per unit.

Although MNRE introduced a scheme recently with provisions to give Rs 0.50 per unit of wind power generated, in addition to the tariffs fixed by the state electricity boards, all the above listed incentives, both at the Central and state levels are being offered on the capital investment done and not on the real power generated.

Another important point to be noted is that these sops and tax bonanzas do not differentiate between different plant load factors (PLF), which is a measure of average capacity utilisation of a power plant. As per the data supplied by MNRE, the PLF in Gujarat is 7.8 per cent, way below the national average of 15 per cent and far too low than the global average of 25 per cent. No substantial effort to increase the efficiency of wind power plants adds to the notion that investment and not generation is the focus in wind energy business.

Even the Renewable Portfolio Standard, which means obligation on the electricity suppliers to produce a specified fraction of their electricity from renewable energy sources, is as low as 2 per cent in Gujarat. This has virtually restricted the green energy growth in the state. Also, the major increase in installed wind energy can be directly linked to the provisions of Kyoto Protocol.

Heading: DCB arrests two more for July 26 blasts - Indian Express
Content:
One accused of damaging police chowki, the other of shouting provocative slogans during visarjan

Vadodara police lodged a formal complaint on Monday against one Sangram Patel, the nephew of Raopura MLA Yogesh Patel (BJP), and others for damaging the Raopura police chowki on September14. The accused were seeking the release of one Raju Pawar, who was arrested for refusing to obey police orders to wind up the Ganesh Visarjan rituals by 7.30 pm.

In another incident, a complaint was lodged against former Congress councillor Sangita Varkhade's brother for shouting provocative slogans in Fatehpura during the Ganesh Visarjan on Sunday.

Meanwhile, Yogesh Patel has disowned Sangram Patel as his nephew, and said Sangram only lives in the same neighbourhood but is not related to him.

Both Patel and the Congress have washed their hands off the case.

The police complaint names Sangram Patel, who runs a mobile phone shop, Dipak Patel, Minesh Pandya, Jignesh Patel, Nimesh Patel and Himanshu Bhatt as leaders of a mob of about 35.

"Sangram first damaged the sign-board of the police chowki and then asked the officials to release his friend, Rajesh Pawar. When he was asked not to interfere with the law, he slapped Head Constable Pradip Janardan twice and snatched away his pen. He also abused the other cops present. They hurled the office furniture on the road and even threw out official documents," said the investigating officer, S B Raolji.

In the other case, the FIR names the brother (name not known to police) of Congress councillor Sangita Varkhade, and one Gopal Sharma of Gopaldas ni galli, for shouting provocative slogans in Fatehpura where the communal clashes took place.

According to police, at around 10.15 pm, the duo made provocative gestures and shouted slogans inciting the mob to riot.

Member of the Opposition in Vadodara Municipal Corporation, Chirag Zaveri told Newsline, "Varkhade was a councillor and a Congress party worker once. Today, she is neither."

Heading: Violent trail: 1 killed, 7 injured in police firing - Indian Express
Content:
Names another three persons who could be involved in the crime

The Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) on Monday arrested two more persons from the city in connection with the July 26 serial blasts.

With this, the total number of arrests in the case has reached 21. The DCB has also announced the names of three persons wanted in the case, who could also be involved in the serial blasts in Delhi. It has been announced that those providing information to nab the accused will be rewarded.

The two arrested are Umar Kala Kabira alias Ashok (38) of Shabnam Duplex behind Memon Hall in Juhapura, and Salim Jamal Sipahi alias Umar (38) from Gujarat Housing Board Colony near Garib Nagar Cross Roads in Bapunagar. Kabira is a newly converted Muslim. DCB officials believe that some other persons who had converted to Islam along with him may also be involved in the planning or execution of the blast conspiracy.

Announcing the arrests, DCP Abhay Chudasama said: "Umar Kabira had arranged for the illegal SIMI meetings at his residence, whereas Salim Sipahi is an expert bomb maker who was present in all the meetings in Ahmedabad for the planning of the blasts."

He added: "Sipahi had learnt to make different types of bombs at the age of 15. He has trained SIMI members in Ahmedabad, Surat and Vadodara. The pipe bomb, which was recovered by DCB from the house of Usman Agarbattiwala, was made by him," he said.

The three other persons wanted by the DCB for involvement in the Delhi serial blasts are Abdul Raziq Mansuri alias Mohammed Ismail from Al-Aman Flats in Gomtipur, Muzib Sheikh from Gulzar Park Society in Juhapura and Alamzeb Afridi from New Ashiyana Society in Juhapura. According to DCB officials, Mansuri does embroidery work and was given the task of purchasing bicycles and planting bombs at various places in Ahmedabad. He had also attended the terrorist training camp organised by SIMI leaders in Kerala in December 2007. He is also accused of instigating the local youths for jihad and taking part in all the meetings of SIMI leaders to plan out the July 26 blasts.Muzib is a skilled polisher of imitation jewellery and is accused of taking part in the terror training camp organised by SIMI leaders near Halol in January 2008. He also took part in all the clandestine meetings in Ahmedabad.

Afridi is unemployed from Juhapura who allegedly took terror training at the camp organised in Halol and was present in all the SIMI meetings planning the blasts. Afridi is accused of playing a key role in purchasing and planting the bicycle bombs in Ahmedabad.

Talking to mediapersons, Chudasama said the involvement of the three along with Abdul Qureshi alias Tauqeer and Qayamuddin Kapadiya is under scanner for their role in the Delhi serial blasts.

Heading: HC orders action against Howrah dist officials - Indian Express
Content:
Unruly mob resorted to looting, arson, claim cops; curfew imposed in Fatehpura

One person died and seven others were injured when the Vadodara police opened fire on an unruly mob in Fatehpura locality on Monday, following the violence that broke out in the area during the Ganesh Visarjan on Sunday evening. Curfew has been imposed in the area ever since.

Vadodara Police Commissioner Rakesh Asthana said that the decision to fire at the rioters was taken instantly, as the mob resorted to looting and arson.

Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) officers nabbed one Rajesh alias Raju Pawar late on Sunday night for not winding up the Ganesh Visarjan ceremony by 7.30 pm, as the situation in the area had already become tense after miscreants torched two shops in neighbouring Yakutpura.

According to the residents, stone pelting started after Pawar's supporters had gathered in Fatehpura Char Rasta. Police said three shops below a temple were torched in the morning by the rioters. A jewellery shop was also looted, said eyewitnesses.

DCB officials said rioting began immediately after Pawar was arrested on Sunday night. Three shops in the Champaner Gate area below a mosque were burnt down including a laari (hand-cart). "We have arrested Rajesh Pawar for not following police orders," said K D Pandya.

On Monday morning, a group of youngsters from the area went to the police station to protest against the arrest of Pawar. Residents, both Hindus and Muslims, said additional force sent to bring the rioting under control reached late.

Rioting had taken place even on Sunday night in Yakutpura where three shops were torched. Eyewitnesses said it was prayer time for the Muslims fasting in the Holy month of Ramzan, when some of the drunken revellers going towards the Sursagar Lake for the Visarjan began jeering at them. This resulted in stone pelting.

"Almost immediately, the men, armed with sticks, doused one of the shops with kerosene and torched it until the police came," said an eyewitness on condition of anonymity.

Shocked kin of riot victim ask: Why?
Junaid Hussain (25) was shot dead by the police on Sunday night. His family has one question for the police: "Why did they aim at his chest and not his legs?"

Father of a 10-month-old boy, Junaid had stepped out of his Fatehpura house thinking it was just another incident of stone pelting: a common occurrence in the walled city area. What he did not know, however, was that he would fall victim to police bullets.

Junaid's brother, Javed, said at the mortuary in the SSG Hospital that he never imagined a police firing would take place in Fatehpura. "He was not among the rioters," said Javed.

Junaid was an employee of the Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation. He had come out thinking he would leave for work immediately after the stone pelting stops, said Javed. "We had asked him to wait, but it was too late. They could have fired at his legs," said Javed, adding that Junaid was hit on the chest and shoulders.

Meanwhile, SSG Hospital is yet to release the dead, as the autopsy is pending. "We have been waiting for the last five hours for the doctors to complete the post-mortem," said Javed. Junaid was married a year and a half ago.

Pawar, a known history sheeter
Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) officials, who had arrested Rajesh Pawar on Sunday night, told Newsline that Pawar is a known history sheeter.

"Rajesh Pawar is a known history sheeter in the area. Several cases of betting are pending against him," said Inspector K D Pandya.

Interestingly, he is also the organiser of the Maratha Putra Ganesh Puja Mandal.

Pawar's supporters, however, maintained that he is not involved, as he was busy with the Visarjan preparation on Sunday evening. Sources say that every time during Visarjan, Pawar would offer prayers in the Dargah at the Champaner Gate in the city.

Locals say that Pawar has a large following among the youth of the area, who are ready to do anything for him.

Seven injured and one dead brought to SSG Hospital at 12:30 pm on Monday
* Junaid Shaikh (25) died after being hit by two bullets on the left side on his chest.
* Maqbool Shaikh (23) seriously injured after a bullet hit his back
* Shahrukh Mansuri (15) hit by a bullet on left hand
* Ijaj Shaikh (21) received bullet injuries on the right hand
* Moshin Saiyad (23) received bullet injuries on the left hand side of body
* Mohammad Panwala (39) received bullet injuries on the left hand side of his body
* Shoaib Mansuri (20) cut his feet with glass shards
* Mohammad Rafiq Abdul Hamid (38) received bullet injuries on the left side of his body

Heading: Met warns of heavy rains - Indian Express
Content:
The Calcutta High Court directed the Howrah district magistrate on Monday to initiate proceedings against the state's director of Panchayat and the sabhadhipati of the Howrah Zila Parishad.

The direction came in response to a writ petition filed by Dinabandhu Mondal, a resident of Koshmallick village alleging that the two had misappropriated funds meant for development.

The panchayat and rural development department, the petition had stated, had sanctioned Rs 50 lakh for building roads.

Justice Kalyan Jyoti Sengupta also directed the Block Development Officer of Amta Block II to start a criminal and a civil case against the sabhapati of the block and the panchayat pradhan of Koshmallick village.

Heading: Enteric strikes 350 in Jadavpur, KMC to withdraw health camp - Indian Express
Content:
Heavy rainfall is likely to lash Gangetic West Bengal and isolated places in coastal Orissa over the next 48 hours as a result of a low-pressure area that has developed over northwest Bay of Bengal.

"It is a well marked low-pressure area that is likely to intensify in the next 48 hours," said LR Meena, deputy director-general of the Alipore Met office.

A warning has been issued to trawlers and fishermen along the coasts and they have been asked not to venture into the seas for the next 24 hours. According to the warning, strong east to southeasterly winds with a speed exceeding 45 km per hour and generally rough seas are likely along and off the West Bengal coast.

The Met has predicted a cloudy sky for tomorrow with one or two spells of rain or thundershowers. The maximum and minimum temperatures will be around 32°C and 27°C respectively.

Heading: Early morning accident leaves kids orphaned - Indian Express
Content:
The enteric outbreak in Ward 101 of Jadavpur entered its sixth day on Monday. On Sunday, 28 enteric-affected people were registered at the Jadavpur health camp. With 15 more being reported on Monday, the enteric count has crossed 350 in the area.

The Kolkata Municipal Corporation, however, is considering to dismantle the health camp that it had earlier set up in the locality. Local councillor Chandana Ghosh Dastidar said: "Since the situation is improving, we are thinking of withdrawing the camp. A final decision will be taken after today's review meeting."

The water supply tankers of the KMC will not be sent to the area after the health camp pulls out.

The locals, however, are not happy with the decision. Affected people, especially poor, are regularly coming to the camp for treatment and are being referred to various hospitals. On Sunday, three people were admitted in hospitals and another two were admitted on Monday.

"We will request the local councilor to run the camp for a few more days. People are still coming to the camp for medicines. They will be affected if the camp is withdrawn," said a ward committee member.

The water samples collected from the area have been tested twice by the water supply department of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation. Since the samples were not found contaminated, the civic body declared that the water is fit for use. Dastidar said: "The water of the area was chlorinated five days ago. Tests have also found the water to be safe. So we have asked the locals to use the water."

The enteric outbreak was caused by contaminated water in the area that followed a breach in the drinking water supply pipeline, when the Kolkata Environment Improvement Project (KEIP) workers were carrying out the drainage and sewerage upgradation work.

Heading: 26 yrs on, HC offers hope to job seeker - Indian Express
Content:
When she said goodbye to her parents early on Monday morning, little did 12-year-old Saswati Roy know that it was the last time she and her 15-year-old brother, Ashish, would see them alive.

Shyamal Kumar Roy (40) and his wife Anjali (30), died when their motorcycle was hit by a truck near Khanna cinema at the Raja Direndra Street in north Kolkata at 5.30 am.

The couple were residents of Salt Lake sector-III.

The trailer had collided with a lorry and toppled, hitting the motorcycle which was heading towards the Khanna cinema crossing.

Bimalesh Kumar, the lorry helper also died. Though both vehicles have been seized, the drivers are absconding, the police said.

"A case has been registered under Section 279, 304A and 427," said an officer of the Burtolla police station.

Roy, an East Guard Traffic Constable and his wife were on their way to shop for clothes for her business, which supplemented the family income.

"My parents would go early in the morning to buy the clothes that mom would sell. Like any other day, my mother woke me and my brother and asked us to eat breakfast before sitting down to study," said Saswati.

The children were waiting for their parents to come back and get them ready for school. Instead, they were informed of the tragedy by the neighbours who, after receiving the news at 6 am, have been at the Roy residence. The couple's son studies in Class IX in Bidhan Nagar Municipal School and Saswati is a student of Begam Rakshia Shriti Rastriya Balika Vidyalay.

Heading: For a change, Padma hilsa flood city markets - Indian Express
Content:
Justice Sadhan Kumar Gupta of the Calcutta High Court on Monday directed the chairman of the district primary school council of North 24 Parganas to hand over an appointment letter to Tapas Kumar Hari within four weeks.

Hari had applied for the post of a primary school teacher on compassionate grounds after the death of his elder brother in 1982. Hari was a 21-year-old then. His brother Dipak was a primary school teacher at the time of his death.

A few days ago, Hari had filed a writ petition in the High Court. His counsel, Anjan Bhattacharya, moved the plea that Hari had submitted a representation to the chairman of the council four times in the last 26 years but the chairman did not respond. Justice Gupta also directed the school council to examine whether Hari had the necessary qualifications when he had applied for the post.

Heading: Industry gives a shot in the arm to Buddha - Indian Express
Content:
Good news for hilsa-loving Bengalis. A record quantity of hilsa from Bangladesh hit the Kolkata markets on Monday, just ahead of the Viswakarma Puja on Wednesday.

Thirty-five truckloads of hilsa reached Petrapol border in North 24 Parganas early morning and were dispatched straight to the Sealdah wholesale market. Some early birds wanting to lap up the delicious fish from Bangladesh were already waiting at the markets, when the trucks arrived.

With the festive season just around the corner, city markets are witnessing an increase in the demand for the fish. Traders said the scarcity of hilsa was reported in the markets in the last ten days, pushing up the prices. The wholesale price has been ranging between Rs 150 to Rs 180 kg this year.

With fish arriving from Bangladesh, Kolkata traders said over 102 tonnes of hilsa will soon flood the state markets.

Atul Das, president of Hilsa Fresh Fish Importers Association, said, "We are expecting more fish to arrive in the next few days. That will pull the prices down during the Pujas." He, however, added: "By the time hilsa reaches Kolkata markets, the price can touch up to Rs 400 per kg, making it unaffordable for most households."

The association is also looking at the cheaper options of importing hilsa. "To import fish from Myanmar, we pay 35 per cent import duty. We have appealed to the state fisheries department to waive the duty. If that happens, hilsa will be available in the markets at Rs 150 to Rs 200 per kg," said Das. There is also speculation about the weight of hilsa this year. Retail dealers claimed that the average weight of the fish was 700 to 900 grams, much less than the normal weight of 1,000 to 1,200 grams.

Heading: Farmers to get new package when plant reopens - Indian Express
Content:
Even as Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee is struggling to come out of the Singur imbroglio, various industrialists have come to his succour.

A week after industrialist L N Mittal had said Singur was a stray case, the Jai Balaji group assured the chief minister that their Purulia steel project was very much on track and work for the plant will start in November. The group is setting up a steel plant at Raghunathpur in Purulia. Aditya Jajodia, the Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) of the company and Joint Managing Director Rajiv Jajodia met the chief minister on Monday.

Aditya said: "Singur is an isolated case. It will not hamper the investment in West Bengal. In 2006, violence was reported in Kalinganagar, Orissa but that did not affect the investment in that state. We assured the chief minister that our Purulia project was very much on."

The group is setting up a 5 million tonne integrated steel plant, a 3 million tonne cement manufacturing unit and a 1,215 MW captive power plant over 3,800 acres at Raghunathpur.

The company has already received 800 acres from the West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation and it hopes to get another 1,200 acres by November. "Once we get the land, we will start work and we expect to finish the first phase of the project within three years," said the CMD.
