He also said the company will offer employment to at least one member of each of the families, who have lost their land for the project. "The project is expected to offer jobs to nearly 8,000 people," said Aditya.

Heading: Now, Writers’ Buildings in line of Mamata’s fire - Indian Express
Content:
Even though Left Front chairman Biman Bose exhorted farmers to collect their cheques and additional compensation on Monday's rally in Singur, the state government can pay up only after Tatas resume work there.

Mentioning a recent advertisement published by the state government in the newspapers, a government official pointed out that it "makes it clear that unless normalcy is restored in the area and Tata Motors resumes the work, there is no point in giving out the compensation package."

Subrata Gupta, Managing Director of West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation (WBIDC), told The Indian Express: "Unless all the farmers, whose land was acquired, accept the package, the additional amount announced two days ago cannot be disbursed."

Since most of the money that could not be disbursed earlier is still with the district magistrate of Hooghly, the farmers who did not take the money earlier can come forward now and collect it, he added.

The WBIDC had paid Rs 120 crore for the 997 acres acquired for the plant. Of this, Rs 29 crore is yet to be disbursed.

During a meeting with Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee, Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee had proposed the new package that offered several benefits, including anadditional 50 per cent of the price of the land to all the farmers, whose land was acquired in Singur.

Trinamool sources, however, said the leaders were in a dilemma about whether the package will be welcomed by the farmers.

Heading: East-West corridor project runs into hurdle - Indian Express
Content:
Trinamool chief Mamata Banerjee has threatened to sit on a dharna inside the Writers' Buildings if the state government does not punish the persons responsible for the September 11 violence reported in the Writers' Buildings.

On Monday, state government employees owing allegiance to the Opposition parties organised a rally, during which Trinamool MP Mukul Roy read out a message sent by Banerjee.  It said, "If the government does not take any action against the employees, I will lead an agitation at the Writers' Buildings." The last time Banerjee had sat for a dharna inside the Writers' Buildings in front of then chief minister Jyoti Basu's chamber was in 1993.

While the Kolkata police has lodged FIRs against four employees of the Writers' Buildings, who were involved in the violent demonstration, the state government has also sent show-cause notices to eight employees, including those four.

To inculcate discipline among employees of the Writers' Buildings, the state government issued a circular on Monday making attendance at 10 am mandatory.

Home Secretary Asok Mohan Chakrabarti said the government would take disciplinary action against the employees if their responses were not satisfactory. He also admitted that the employees lacked discipline.

As the deadline for submitting the replies expired on Monday, the employees sought more time to file their responses. "We have requested the state government for an extension of 10 days," said Sanket Chakrabarti, Writers Building unit secretary of state government employees federation (unified).

Heading: Mamata all set to renew attacks at Singur rally - Indian Express
Content:
The experiences with land acquisition in Singur and Nandigram have forced the state government to tread cautiously. The Left government has decided to do away with the railway stations on the much-hyped East-West Metro Corridor project rather than to venture into any fresh land acquisition controversy.

In the second board meeting of the Kolkata Metro Railway Corporation (KMRC), the recently-constituted body to implement the project, the Left government proposed to scrap the plans of setting up a central station at the Bowbazar Crossing. It has been proposed that the station at Bowbazar will be the junction connecting the East-West Metro Corridor with the existing North-South one.

M Ramachandran, the secretary of the Union Ministry of Urban development, said: "The area is congested and it may be difficult to acquire land for the station." He further said: "The state government has suggested whether the station can be dispensed of altogether. But no final decision has been taken in this regard and the matter will be taken up in the next board meeting." He was speaking to media at the sidelines of a seminar on urban development organised by the Merchant Chamber of Commerce.

The Bowbazar station already finds mention in the Detailed Project Report (DPR). The DPR has to be changed if the station is scrapped, said Ramachandran. The distance between metro stations on the route has already been specified. Doing away with a station will increase the distance between the preceding station and the next station. We have to see whether it is feasible or not," said the secretary.

Earlier, transport minister Subhas Chakraborty had claimed that there was no political resistance to the issue and work on the project was going on smoothly.

The project, however, is already facing resistance from the local traders. In the last four months, the 300-year-old furniture market on the B B Ganguly Street at the Bowbazar crossing has witnessed dwindling sales. As the word spread about shops being pulled down to make way for the Metro corridor project, the steady flow of customers has come down to a mere trickle.

Though only 14 of the 88 shops in the furniture market will be relocated, these shops are extremely popular and have been the landmarks of the market. The relocation will affect the identity of the market and we will lose our customers, said a trader.

Heading: Winds of change at LF Singur rally - Indian Express
Content:
After Singur, the next battleground in the war between Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee and Mamata Banerjee is going to be the Chief Minister's own backyard, Writers' Buildings.

With the Kolkata police lodging FIRs against four employees of Writers' Buildings who were involved in a violent demonstration there on September 11 and Home Secretary Asok Mohan Chakrabarti sending show-cause notices to eight of them, Mamata has sprung to their defence.

On Monday, at a rally of state government employees owing allegiance to Opposition parties, Trinamool MP Mukul Roy read out a message by Mamata: "If the Government takes any action against these employees, I will myself lead the agitation at Writers' Buildings."

If that happens, it would be a historic event. The last time Mamata came inside Writers' Buildings and sat for a dharna was in 1993, and then it was Jyoti Basu who was the target of her ire.

In a move to tighten discipline among employees at the Writers' Buildings, the state Government also issued a circular today making attendance at 10 am mandatory. The employees have sought another 10 days to reply to the show-cause issued by the Government.

Heading: BJP yet to decide on alliance - Indian Express
Content:
With a massive rally at Club Maidan, the Left Front marked a happy return to Singur today after two years as farmers who have been opposed to the Tata plant indicated that they were willing to accept the Government's new compensation package.

Left Front chairman Biman Bose announced that compensation cheques were "ready" with the district magistrate, and urged everyone to collect them before September 22.

The Left Front last held a rally in Singur in November 2006. Later, as the CPI(M) was targeted by allies over land acquisition for the Tata Nano factory, and Mamata Banerjee joined the protestors, the LF kept away.

The latest package by Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee — offering 70 acres within the plant site and a 50 per cent hike in compensation — seems to have done the trick. Among those convinced is Anar Banu Begum, a resident of Joymollah and one of the 2,150 who had refused to accept the compensation for their land. She was present at the LF rally.

"Even if I get back my land from inside the project area, farming is no more possible there," she said today. "I have heard I will not be able to re-sell it. So I have decided to collect compensation at the earliest." Anar Banu's 2.3 acres were acquired by the Government in September 2006.

Joydeb Das, a resident of Beraberi Purbapara, whose 8 bighas of land were acquired, was also rethinking his options. "Initially we were thinking of taking the compensation money. But after the murder of Tapasi Malik, we changed our mind. But now we are rethinking our decision as this may be the last chance of getting the money. The compensation is also not bad," he said.

The rally was held around 2 km from the Nano site, and the LF had managed a substantial crowd with people from five South Bengal districts brought in. With the crowd pouring out, a few thousand jostled to enter the grounds.

"You will get 50 per cent extra for your land," Bose told the people, flanked by Forward Bloc state secretary Ashok Ghosh, who had earlier held a meeting at Singur against forcible land acquisition. "You can buy land nearby and start farming with the money. Or if you wish, you can start some project. Your family members will also get jobs."

The widow of Susen Santra, who committed suicide reportedly after he heard that the Tatas were leaving Singur, was called on stage and given a cheque of Rs 25,000.

Bose explained that the Chief Minister had done all he could to convince the Opposition, but in vain. "The land which is being demanded back, which is kept for the ancillary units, cannot be given back. The Tatas will not be able to function if that happens. We should understand that Nano, the Rs 1 lakh car, is not only important for Bengal but the whole world. The car will be marketed to foreign countries priced at $2500. We should all try to join hands for the project, which will bring prestige to Singur," he added.

Apart from the Forward Bloc's Ghosh, the RSP's Kshiti Goswami and the CPI's Manjukumar Majumder also lauded the package today. "The Singur farmers are not our enemy... We fully support the Chief

Minister who went to Raj Bhavan five times to solve the issue peacefully. We are still open to a peaceful dialogue. I appeal to Mamata Banerjee to resist from violence," said Ghosh.

Heading: Samajwadi youth-wing campaigns against govt - Indian Express
Content:
Amid differences in the party over forging an alliance with the Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD), Rajnath Singh, national president of BJP, said no final decision was taken as yet.

"A decision in this connection will be taken by the Central Parliamentary Board of the party. It will be finalised only after a discussion with the leaders of the state unit," said Singh. 

Many in the party — state president Ramapati Ram Tripathi, legislator Om Prakash Singh, national vice-president Kalyan Singh, national general secretary Vinay Katiyar and Rajya Sabha MP Kalraj Mishra — have strongly opposed any alliance with the RLD.

 Singh was in Bahraich on Monday to address a Vijay Sankalp rally held by the state unit of the party. Once again Kalyan and Kalraj gave the rally a miss, although all senior state leaders were present.

Not missing the opportunity, Singh took a dig at UPA's policies on terrorism as well as the government's role in the Amarnath and Ram Setu issue. He said these issues would be the poll planks of the party with a new tone and tenor.

Blaming the Centre to have been indulging in appeasement politics on the issue of terrorism, Singh said BJP was the only party capable of curbing terrorism. Once voted to power, the first thing that BJP would do is to hang Afzal Guru, said Singh.

At the same time, he demanded an inquiry into violent activities that have occurred in Orissa and Gujarat.

On the Amarnath issue, Singh said that the UPA government had bowed in front of the separatists, but the public of Jammu gave a befitting reply.

"If the BJP was in power, it would have hanged all those who were flashing the Pakistani flag and shouting pro-Pakistan slogans," said the party national president. As for those political outfits, which were waving the Pakistani flag, Singh demanded the Election Commission to de-recognise them.

Heading: Irrigation department seeks more time - Indian Express
Content:
To strengthen the Samajwadi Party (SP), its student wing, Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha (SCS), launched a week-long student awareness campaign in universities and colleges across the state on Monday.

During the campaign, the Sabha members will discuss the various student-friendly measures initiated by the Mulayam Singh Yadav government, which have been discontinued by the Mayawati government. 

Akhilesh Yadav, the national convener of SP's youth affairs, said: "The SP government had introduced schemes like allowances for unemployed youths and Kanya Vidhya Dhan Yojna to provide education to girls. But the Mayawati government has discontinued these programmes."

He said during the awareness week, party's youth wing will meet students in colleges and universities. The party will also urge students to join the SCS ranks. 

 "On September 25, Sabha members will stage demonstrations and protest against anti-youth policies of the BSP government. We will also demand the holding of elections for students' unions and reintroduction of schemes for youth welfare," Yadav said.

The SP leader also raised the issue of nonfunctional student bodies in various colleges. "In 2007, the ruling party had banned the students' union elections in the state. Though the ban was lifted after protests, the government is delaying the announcement of polls," he added.

Taking a dig at the money spent by the Mayawati government on the construction of memorials, Yadav said, "Instead of taking steps for the welfare of students and setting up new universities, the BSP is wasting money on park and memorials."

The Student Federation of India (SFI) has criticised the campaign stating that a political party should not impose its agenda on students' bodies. Piyush Mishra, a SFI leader of the Lucknow University, said: "The Mulayam government worked a lot for the welfare of students but anti-social activities in student politics was at a record high in his regime."

 Akhil Bhartiya Vidhyarthi Parishad (ABVP) has also disapproved of the campaign. ABVP leader Ranvijay said: "There should be a difference between the agendas of a political party and its student wing. But Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha is following the agenda of the Samjwadi Party for attracting the students."

Heading: Apex court stays HC order for CBI probe - Indian Express
Content:
The state irrigation department needs another year to complete the Uttar Pradesh Water Sector Restructuring Scheme (UPWSRS). The project is being funded by the World Bank and its first phase was to be over by 2007.

State Irrigation Minister Nasimuddin Siddiqui said: "The scheme was introduced in 2002. Though we need an extension of another year to complete the first phase, our pace in the last one year was faster." The minister said this while inaugurating a web portal on the UPWSRS in Lucknow on Monday.

The Rs 6,000-crore project aims to strengthen the canal system in the state with the introduction of latest technology and has been divided in four stages. The first phase, with a budget of Rs 25 crore, will focus on the Sharda canal system in Sultanpur, Jagdishpur, Rai Bareilly, Pratapgarh and Jaunpur. The drought-affected Bundelkhand area, Barabanki district and Gomti Ganga basin will be included in the second phase at a cost of Rs 2,000 crore.

If the department had completed the work in time, the situation in the drought- hit areas would have been better. Siddiqui, however, said: "Except this year, Bundelkhand has remained dry for the last five years. We will include the area in the second phase of the scheme."

The UPWSRS portal will provide important information to farmers on water availability in a particular area. Farmers can also post their online queries on message boards. The users can get latest updates through SMS.

Manjeet Singh, Principal Secretary of the Irrigation department, said: "We need to regularly update the website so that it can help various stakeholders."

World Bank official Havier Juleta said: "By providing crucial information to the farmers, the portal will help in the effective utilisation of resources. We hope the system will be in place by January next year connecting nearly 400 offices in the state."

On the occasion, the irrigation minister also launched a magazine, Paani, for the benefit of farmers.

Heading: Door-to-door polio drive begins - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court stayed an Allahabad High Court direction for a CBI probe into the UP police recruitment scam on Monday, which had taken place during Mulayam Singh Yadav's regime.

The order came after the Centre expressed its inability to allow the premier investigating agency to probe the matter.

A Bench of Justices C K Thakker and D K Jain in an interim order while staying the direction issued notices to the UP government and Amit Kumar Shukla, petitioner before the High Court, to file their responses to the Centre's claim.

The direction by the Bench comes as a major blow to Chief Minister Mayawati, as it was her government that had pushed for a CBI probe after she came to power, when the scam was detected. Mayawati had set up a high-level inquiry committee that had found that recruitments were not only done for monetary and political considerations but also sexual favours were sought in return from some female recruits before appointing them in the police force. Over 15,000 recruits have already been sacked by the state government.

The interim order of staying the CBI probe came on an appeal filed by the Centre challenging February 4, 2008 order of the High Court to the CBI to conduct investigations into the scam, where names of several top politicians and police officials had cropped up.

The CBI probe was ordered on a petition filed by an aggrieved candidate, Amit Kumar Shukla, who contended that an independent probe was essential as one Additional DGP, two IGs, 16 DIGs, one SSP, 33 Additional SPs 77 DSPs were allegedly involved in the racket.

He had submitted that it would not be possible for the state police to conduct a free and fair probe.

Challenging the HC's order, Solicitor General G E Vahanvati said the CBI would not be in a position to take up the probe as it was preoccupied with various other investigations.

Heading: Juvenile undertrial dies of Hepatitis B - Indian Express
Content:
After the most virulent polio virus — wildpolio P1 — resurfaced in central Uttar Pradesh for the first time this year, health officials on Monday began the statewide house to house Pulse Polio drive.

Alarmed by the prospect of the virus spreading to the state capital, the state health officials, alongwith World Health Organisation (WHO) officials, reviewed the immunisation status at Malihabad block in the state capital, neighbouring Sandila block of Hardoi. The first P1 case of central Uttar Pradesh was recently reported from Sandila block itself.

The purpose of this campaign is to ensure 100 per cent coverage of the block.

None of the children till the age group of five should miss the present pulse polio round — which includes the distribution of Monovalent Oral Polio Vaccine to combat the Type 1 (MoPV1) virus.

"The P1 case from Sandila has made it clear that P1 virus has entered central UP again. But now our aim is to stop the spread of this virus to the state capital," said Dr A K Shukla, the Chief Medical Officer (CMO) of Lucknow.

The officials of the WHO, meanwhile, have intensified surveillance in the Malihabad block. The CMO undertook a separate review of the immunisation status in the block on the first day of the drive. "We cannot afford to take this block lightly. Thus, I have decided to review the immunisation status of the block after each day of the drive. This will also motivate the ground level health workers in the area," added Shukla.

Around a week ago, 18-month-old Sonu was found infected with the wild P1 virus in the Sandila block. This child did not have any history of travelling, thus indicating that the virus had infected the child in Hardoi itself.

Heading: On village roads, gram pradhans on driving seat - Indian Express
Content:
A young prisoner lodged in Faizabad Juvenile Jail, who was suffering from Hepatitis B, died late on Sunday night at Lucknow's CSMMU hospital.

Waseem (14), a co-accused in a theft case, was brought to the Faizabad Juvenile jail six months earlier. A few weeks ago, he contracted Hepatitis B.

The family has alleged that the boy was mistreated in jail and the officials had not provided proper treatment during his illness.

District Probation Officer Mukul Maitrey confirmed that the cause of death was Hepatitis B, and said the body will be handed over to the family members after the postmortem.

The Additional Superintendent of Faizabad Juvenile jail, A P Dubey said the police arrested Waseem and he was sent to jail on April 8.

He had fever from September 1 and was being treated at Shri Ram Hospital in Ayodhya. On September 11, he was admitted to the Faizabad district hospital and moved to Lucknow' CSMMU on September 12, where he died late on Sunday night.

His mother, Roshan Jahan, told The Indian Express that a week ago, her son had complained to her about being ill-treated by the jail administration officials.

"My son was ill for a long time. When I met him a week ago he was not able to talk properly and when I complained to the jail authorities, they only banned me from meeting him," she said.

According to Nirupam Mishra, member of Juvenile Court board, over two dozen juvenile prisoners lodged in the jail are suspected to be suffering from Hepatitis B, to which the jail authorities are turning a blind eye.

Dubey, however, denied the allegations.

Heading: Suicide in lock-up, three policemen suspended - Indian Express
Content:
Soon getting a road constructed under the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojna (PMGSY) scheme will become an easy task.

In a review meeting of the Rural Housing Board, it was decided that the construction of roads could now be recommended by the gram pradhans.

The gram pradhans can directly send their proposals to the Uttar Pradesh Rural Roads Agency or recommend them as a part of the district plan.

All this with the aim to strengthen the network of roads in the state as well as to prevent siphoning of funds released under the PMGSY scheme.

Earlier, the proposals were sent either through the MP, MLA or the Block Development Officer (BDO)."We have heard a lot of complaints regarding the misuse of funds and the quality of the roads being constructed," said a senior officer of the agency.

"There have been demands for more roads. But since the BDO does not recommend them, people are unable to take the benefit of the scheme," added the officer.

With the aim to ensure transparency, a committee comprising gram pradhan, panchayat members and a local will also be setup to check the quality of the roads constructed. They will be formed at the block levels, headed by the Chief Development Officer at the district level.

Heading: Dropping teaching for research, UPTU decides to start new fellowship - Indian Express
Content:
A day after a 26-year-old youth allegedly committed suicide in police lock-up, three policemen, including in-charge of Panchdeora police station in Hardoi, have been suspended for negligence.

A letter has also been shot off to the Uttar Pradesh Home Guard department to take action against the two homeguards present at the time of the incident.

On Sunday morning, the police had arrested Maghai, a resident of Chak village, over a murder that had taken place on Wendesday. Maghai was brought to the police station and he was kept in the lock-up for interrogation. At 4 pm, when a policeman went to see Maghai, he found him hanging. A scarf was wrapped around his neck. The body was immediately sent for postmortem.

"It is a clear case of suicide. The postmortem report of Maghai states that death occured due to hanging. No injury marks have been reported in the report," said Superintendent of Police, Hardoi, Pradeep Chand.

He added that it is still not clear why Maghai took such a drastic step. The three officers who were suspended are — Panchdeora police station in-charge Narendra Dev Pathak, Head Constable Kotwal Singh and Constable Ram Asrey.

Heading: Woman officer suspended for beating up girl - Indian Express
Content:
With engineering graduates not showing much interest in the Teacher Fellowship Scheme, the Uttar Pradesh Technical University (UPTU) has decided to abandon the scheme for a new Research Fellowship Scheme from 2009.

The in-principle decision of the Academic Council will soon be tabled before the Executive Council for final approval. The new scheme is expected to produce quality researchers who would be free to either continue research or opt for teaching.

Professor Prem Vrat, UPTU Vice-Chancellor, said in 2007-08, over 100 applications were received for Teacher Fellowship Scheme. Eight candidates were selected of whom four finally joined as lecturer.

"In this session, only 26 candidates have been shortlisted. Considering this a poor turnout, the university has decided to close the scheme," Prem Vrat said.

The scheme had been introduced three years ago to motivate engineering students to take up teaching as a profession. The qualification required was a BTech with distinction or First Class postgraduate degree in any stream of engineering out of Electronics, Computer Science, Information Technology and Mechanical Engineering, said an official of the UPTU.

Explaining the poor response to the fellowship scheme, the VC said: "It has been noticed that the students are not interested in teaching. Instead, they prefer a job after completing the course or want to go for research."

"Research Fellowship Scheme would prepare good researchers in the field of engineering," Prem Vrat said. For this, a NET qualified engineering graduate or an MTech with a First Division will be eligible. But the honorarium of Rs 20,000 per month which was allocated for the earlier scheme, will now be reduced to Rs 10,000. "The selected candidates will join research projects in engineering colleges across the state," he said.

Heading: Maya sanctions Rs 8.65 lakh for Bihar flood victims - Indian Express
Content: In wake of Sunday's incident, in which a woman police constable openly thrashed a girl in Hazratganj, SSP Akhil Kumar on Monday suspended her. He also disbanded the entire women's wing of his much-hyped Goonda Daman Dal (GDD). Constable Savitri Giri — a member of GDD's women's wing — allegedly beat up Vandana Shaurya, who was returning from Saharaganj with a relative on Sunday night. Giri took them for a rowdy couple, "creating a nuisance"  by holding hands.

Heading: Count on MNS to fill potholes - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister Mayawati has sanctioned an additional help of Rs 8.65 lakh from CM's fund to provide relief to the flood victims of Bihar.

The amount has been contributed by the members of UP IAS Association and other government employees and officers. On her visit to Bihar earlier, Mayawati had given Rs 11.16 crore for the relief of the flood victims.

Heading: Crackdown on medical waste plant raises a stink - Indian Express
Content:
While workers of Ganesh mandals take a break after the hectic 10-day festival, MNS members have set out to fill up the potholes made by Ganesh mandals for erecting pandals. The city MNS unit has decided to live up to its promise of filling these potholes at its own expense on selective roads. MNS city chief Prakash Dhore said party workers would start filling the potholes from Tuesday "to fulfil their promise".

PMC authorities and office-bearers including Mayor Rajlaxmi Bhosale and Municipal Commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi had appealed to Ganesh mandals not to dig roads while erecting their pandals and prevent the city from getting defaced ahead of the Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG) to be held in October.

The MNS leader in the PMC, Ravindra Dhangekar, had come out in defence of the Ganesh mandals and asked the PMC to let the Ganesh mandals go ahead with digging. The MNS had assured the PMC that it was ready to fill in the potholes at its own expense. Dhore said, "We are going to embark on our work from Tuesday onwards. We don't want common citizens and traders to suffer. We have decided to do the patch-up work only at the major roads and junctions like Laxmi Road, Kumthekar Road, Nana Peth, Bhawani Peth, and other Peth areas. We will hire a vehicle to carry the material and party-workers."

He added, "Since we cannot tar the roads, we will fill the potholes with cement concrete. We will not seek help from anybody including the civic administration; we will do it on our own."

Civic road department chief Vivek Kharwadkar welcomed the step and said, "Even though any organisation is welcome to contribute this way, it first needs to seek permission from the civic authorities to ensure that they follow the work as per the minimum standards required. This will also enable us to check whether they have really followed the work."

Corporator Kishor Shinde said, "If the civic authorities carry out the work, it is well and good. If they don't, our party workers will start the work. Last year we had done the same, but had to leave it in the middle as the PMC later told us that it was ready to fill the roads."

Heading: Vice-chairman of bank charged with rape - Indian Express
Content:
Used syringes, needles, bandages, body parts pile up at city hospitals, with no place to dump the waste in

It was a crackdown on a racket involved in the disposal of spray cans, but it is hospitals that are suffering — and stinking.

Following a blast at the biomedical waste plant on the premises of Kailash crematorium, it emerged that deodorant cans were illegally being disposed of there and the Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) then shut down the plant.

As a result, syringes, needles, blood-soaked cotton swabs, bandages, body parts - every other form of medical waste - started piling up at hospitals. With no alternative facility in the city, the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) had no option but to request the Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation (PCMC) to collect and dispose of the waste. The waste was eventually removed, but after two days.

A total of 530 hospitals, nine blood banks, 115 pathological laboratories and 250 dispensaries and clinics generate around 1,200 kg of biomedical waste everyday. So far a private firm, Sun Enviro Limited, had been collecting it from 250 points in the city.

"Following the blast four days ago, we decided to shut down the facility," says P K Mirashe, Regional Officer for Pune. The PMC was told to make alternative arrangements. The waste was collected on Sunday after city hospitals had piled it up for two days.

J Ravindranath, Director of Poona Hospital and member of the Association of Hospitals in Pune, told Newsline, "The waste was collected after two days, but today since morning no one has come and the waste is piling up again. We are running from pillar to post so that we can have the waste disposed of day by day. It is not wise to accumulate such waste for more than two days."

Hospital authorities are looking at various alternative avenues, while the PMC has urged the PCMC to dispose their waste and temporarily hired the services of Passco Environment Solutions Limited. Pradeep Mulay, director of Passco, confirmed that he got a letter from the PMC on Monday, but rued that the company would be able to collect only 400 kg of waste from Pune.

"The biomedical waste generated in the PCMC area is nearly 550 kg daily and the incinerator set up at YCM Hospital at Chinchwad can take an extra load of 400 kg," he said. Dr P S Dhaigude, Chief Medical Officer of PMC, said they were working out alternative arrangements and even sent the waste to the facility at Talegaon.

Heading: How does our city develop? You suggest, govt will listen - Indian Express
Content:
Prabhu Jodhwani, vice-chairman of Seva Vikas Cooperative Bank, Pimpri, has been booked on charges of raping a woman in need of a loan on August 17. The woman lodged a complaint with the Pimpri police station on Sunday evening.

Jodhwani, who has been booked under Sections 376, 328, 506(1) and 507 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), has not been arrested yet.

The police said that the woman, who is 32, needed a loan and approached the Seva Vikas bank in Pimpri to ask about its loan schemes. She met Jodhwani there.

Between 6.30 pm and 10 pm on August 17, the woman and Jodhwani met near the octroi post at Hinjewadi. Police said that Jodhwani tricked the woman into taking a soft drink, which he had mixed with sedatives.

Following this, he asked her to accompany her in his car. Minutes later, the woman fell unconscious and Jodhwani raped her while she was semi-conscious, the police added.

Jodhwani then allegedly told the woman that he had clicked nude pictures of her and threatened to send them to everyone through MMS if she complained to the police. He also said that he would kill her if she complained to anybody, the police added. Police Sub-Inspector S S Patil said that when the woman was asked why she had complained almost a month after the alleged raped, she replied, "I was scared I would lose my respect in front of everybody. I dared not register a complaint with the police but finally mustered the courage."

Patil said that during investigations, it was found that the woman had waited for some days before filing the complaint because she thought that Jodhwani would return her photographs. But he did not do so — even after promising to return her photographs on two occasions, the police said. Patil said that Jodhwani has not been arrested so far. The woman has been sent for medical tests at Yeshwantrao Chavan Memorial Hospital, Pimpri.

Heading: Faster, Higher, Stronger - Indian Express
Content:
The development plan for the 23 merged villages will now be open to public scrutiny. To bring in more transparency in the process, the state government on Monday said it would seek objections and suggestions from the public for the changes in the draft development plan for Baner-Balewadi.

"A notification will be issued," a government official said. Citizens can now register their remarks on all the proposed changes in the draft DP.

The decision was taken after some people had raised apprehensions about the changes the state government had made in the draft, he said. The public would now be able to find out for themselves the exact changes being proposed, he said. Notifications for substantial changes under Section 22 (A) of the MRTP Act, 1949, will soon be issued.

The maps of the draft DP with proposed changes will be available in the office of the deputy director, Town Planning Office, and also at the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC).

Maps will be available for the public from Friday and two months' time would be given for registering objections and suggestions, officials said. The state government has divided 23 villages into 10 units with a plan to finalise one unit at a time. It approved the first unit of Baner-Balewadi with some changes in January.

Former Union minister Mohan Dharia, PMC standing committee chairman Shyam Deshpande and environmentalists had alleged the state government had altered the proposed Green DP for Baner-Balewadi.

All activists and representatives of various non-governmental organisations (NGO) have come under one roof, called the Green Pune Movement, and have decided to file a public interest litigation (PIL) challenging the government move.

Heading: MCCIA to hold course in effective management of financial resources - Indian Express
Content:
28 hours, 15 minutes:Peaceful, hassle-free

AMID tight security in the backdrop of the serial blasts in Delhi and despite some dampeners, one of these rain, the Ganesh immersion procession ended in 28 hours 15 minutes — two hours less than it took last year — and far faster than in the last few years.

There were rumours of possible terror attacks but the city overcame such fears as devotees ended their celebrations on a high and came out stronger, encouraged to do even better next time.

There were some sour notes, though. The police lathicharged the crowd after a few mandals tried to delay the proceedings in protest against a directive to shut down loudspeakers after midnight. Also, at least four people drowned. And there were the terror rumours.

The procession was flagged off at 10.30 am on Sunday by Mayor Rajlaxmi Bhosale, who performed the aarti of Kasba Ganpati, the presiding deity of the city. It ended by 2.45 pm on Monday. The Mayor and Guardian Minister Ajit Pawar garlanded the deity and felicitated mandal heads at Alka Chowk

The procession was delayed for some time on Tilak Road. Mandals continued to play loudspeakers; police forced many to stop, leading to a delay till the police used a mild lathicharge, forcing processionists to move faster.

There was a mild lathicharge on Laxmi Road, too. A few mandals also burst crackers despite the police's appeal. However, most co-operated, the police said.

Terror rumours
Panic spread briefly among revelers following rumours that the police had received information about a terror plan to carry out attacks during the procession. Some senior police officers initially confirmed the report; the news was even flashed on a few television channels. One channel reported that Pune police had received an anonymous letter with information on planned attacks at important immersion sites.

A police officer, too, told The Indian Express that they had received "specific information". However, they later conceded it had all been rumours.

Police Commissioner Satyapal Singh, who was monitoring security, told reporters that everything was under control and advised citizens against believing in rumours.

Four youths drown
Three youths drowned in a canal near Dias Plot in Market Yard while trying to immerse an idol on Sunday. Naresh Sitaram Mavkal (24), Rahul Raghunath Jindal (21) and Rajesh Sharnappa Jarmandi (25) were from Solapur.

Police said the three had entered the canal and been carried away by the current. The fire brigade recovered the body of Naresh on Monday; the others have not been found. The search started late because the police were informed in the evening.

In the river Indrayani, Ratankumar Nizamchandra Das (22) of Bangerwadi in Lonavala drowned while trying to immerse an idol on Monday afternoon.

Swimmer missing
In a possible accident not related directly to immersion, 30-year-old Mahesh Zambre of Aranyeshwar Sahkarnagar disappeared after he went swimming in the Indrayani from Baba Bhide Bridge at Deccan Gymkhana on Monday. Police fear he has drowned and are looking for his body. A body was fished out of a canal near Empress Garden; it is yet to be identified.

The Maharashtra State Board of Secondary and Higher Secondary Education (MSBSHSE) has declared that class X and class XII exams for repeaters will commence on September 18. It is the last chance for the students appearing for the exam based on old syllabus.

The MSBSHSE has issued a press note in this regard saying, "Written exam for class 10 will be conducted from September 18 to 27 and for class 12 from September 18 to October 10." As many as 81,643 students will appear for SSC, while 54,032 students will appear for HSC exams.

"The exam for repeaters is usually conducted in October. But due to commonwealth youth games and Deewali holidays, the dates of exams are preponed," says the press note.

The students appearing for the exam based on old syllabus will have a last chance. If they fail to get through, they will have to appear for the exam in March, which will be based on the new syllabus.

The students appearing for the exams based on new syllabus will have to give 20 marks oral exams for languages. Orals and grade exams for class 10 and 12 will be conducted from September 11 to Sept 17.

Heading: Professor’s book explores diverse face of sex work in India - Indian Express
Content:
The salaries of nearly 16,000 people employed in the sugar industry in non-permanent category across the state are yet to be brought up to wage board levels as talks held at the sugar commiserate in Pune between the sugar cooperatives and labour associations failed to yield any result.

At present only permanent and semi permanent employees get wage board packages. Various unions have been fighting to get the rest of the employees coming under casual, temporary, contract, daily wages, and other categories to get "equal payment" if they the work the same as permanent employees.

While both parties have agreed that equal work should get equal pay, the timeline for the payment is yet to be worked out. Labour associations have now pinned their hopes on a scheduled meeting with Union Agricultural Minister Sharad Pawar in the third week of September to arbitrate the matter.

"We have agreed in principal that all workers should get equal pay if they are doing the same work, but we want to implement it over four years. It will cost us Rs 350 crore more. We have recommended that each year the worker be given a 25 percent increment, so that at the end of four years, their pay is equal to the permanent workers," said Prakash Naiknavare, Managing Director, Maharashtra State Co-operatives Sugar Factories Federation Limited.

"All of us have accepted in principal that workers should get equal pay for equal work, the only matter of dispute is when. The labour associations want us to disburse the money immediately, we want to do it over four years," Naiknavare said. Since the talks held under the tripartite committee between the state, cooperative companies, and the employee labour associations broke down in 2006, the members decided that they would accept the decision of Sharad Pawar.

In 2006, the tripartite committee accepted a 15 per cent wage increment for permanent and semi-permanent workers. "If a "temperory" wire man does the same work as a "permanent" wire man why should he not get the same pay," said Babanrao Pawar, general secretary, Maharashtra State National Sugar Workers Federation and member of a tripartite committee.

"In the last 15 years, the sugar cooperatives have taken to hiring temporary workers and undertake highly skilled work but pay them very poorly. They should be getting around Rs 215, according to the wage board, but companies do not pay them more than Rs 50," said Pawar.

"We will tell the union minister that legally the wage board stipulates that the workers have right to equal pay for equal work under the wage board," he added

Heading: ‘Eco-friendly’ festival gets thumbs up - Indian Express
Content:
Exploring the profile of sex work and how diverse it is across India, an economics professor at the University of Pune, Rohini Sahni, has penned a 400 page book —Prostitution and Beyond: An analysis of Sex work in India.

Sahni believes her book will take the reader beyond the clichéd definition of a sex worker. "For many, the impressions of a sex worker are most unrealistic. Chastised as much by self as by society, her portrayal is a sheer mockery of reality.

Sahni says, "It is very difficult to estimate the number of sex workers and which state has the highest number of sex workers etc. So my focus is on the profile of sex work in India.''

For Sahni, several questions are unanswered pertaining to the economics of remittances that the prostitute creates and sustains as long as she can earn, the artist in her who preserved a wealth of music and dance in the past. Should her association with the society be viewed merely as a high risk group in the transmission of AIDS? What are the underlying value systems at work that highlight only the negative aspects, while not acknowledging the possibility of anything positive about her?

So, more than nine experts -- including senior scientist with National AIDS Research Institute Dr Sanjay Mehendale, Gayatri Chatterjee from Film and Television Institute of India and others from the ctiy and across the country —feature in the book addressing the issues like feminist discourse, ethnographic studies, socio, economic, legal, health frameworks and cultural reflections.

The book is divided into four sections, each concerned with different issues around which research on sex work in India has got segregated.

Sahni is also a post doctoral student in UoP's department of economics. V Kalyan Shankar, and Hemant Apte, president of the Late Professor Yamato Kawakami Foundation, an NGO working for women, edited the book published by Sage Publications in July this year.

Heading: Music to God’s ears - Indian Express
Content:
The most talked about romantic pair of primetime daily soap, Kis desh mein hai mera dil on Pune, the city where they spent their carefree college days

Even though it's been five years now since Harshad Chopda left Pune, he still has vivid recollections of the lanes in the city, which he treaded as an engineering student. Chopda who brought romance back to the silver screen with Additi Gupta, just after Kasautii's love birds signed off shares, "I have had the most wonderful time here. A large chunk of my student life owes its fun loving moments to the city. I can remember how we used to roam the FC road. Carefree as we were at that time we used to have a blast once college used to get over."

Where Chopda was the student of Modern College of Engineering, Additi Gupta who pairs opposite Chopda as Heer was pursuing her graduation in apparel designing at Symbiosis. Seven months back when she left Pune to step into the small screen world, she did not realise she will miss her Pune life so much. "When I came to Mumbai, I already had the Pune culture and climate infused in me. I missed hanging out at A1's where we got our most cherished respite, A1's milk shake," she reminisces.

If to Gupta it was A1's milk shake which was a respite, to Chopda who avoided cooking, it was Nandu's paranthas that kept him going. "The taste has left its indelible traces on my salivary glands. I still haven't tasted anything like that. For five years now I have missed it like hell," shares Chopda who was crowned with the title of the Best beta at the Star Pariwaar Awards last year.

Chopda was passionate about acting since his college days. " I participated in the plays and talent hunts conducted in the college. Acting was my first love and it did not happen to me just like that. I had to sacrifice my engineering career for that," shares he. But for Gupta, acting just happened like that. "To be very honest I never had acting on my mind and acting as career was out of question. It was in Symbiosis only that I was spotted by Ekta Kapoor's associate Pooja. I was apprehensive about getting into this industry but then I thought why not give it a shot," shares Gupta whose portrayal of the idealistic, coy and the girl next door character of Heer has made her win hearts everywhere.

Still a very fresh face to the industry, Gupta manages to leave a mark. " People don't care to know about my real name. They call me Heer and completely ignore the fact that Heer and Additi are two totally different individuals," shares Gupta.

Only 20, Gupta had to leave her graduation mid-way to for the daily soap. "This profession demands 100 per cent from you, especially when it comes to time. You have to give all your time to it," shares Gupta who now plans to stick to the industry for the years to come.

Currently working for Kis Des..., the pair however does not have anything lined up for the coming years. "Even if you are working for one serial, it is very time consuming. You can't afford to work on other projects," they says almost in unison.

With the Star Pariwaar's award for the best romantic pair up their sleeves, the duo surely has reasons to stick on and make a mark in the glamour world.

Heading: Small Talk - Indian Express
Content:
Big waist clinchers have little secrets that have made them an irreplaceable part of girls' wardrobes

Whether you're donning an elegant tunic or slithering into a dress from the latest rock-n-roll trend, an extra essential that has hit the fashion scene and has been drawing all the attention at the party scenes these days, is a big waist clincher. Commonly known as empire belts (as they are buckled on the empire waist), these clinchers are more than a mere fashionable accessory. If the little bloat around your waist, peeping from your favourite dress plays spoilsport to your party and makes you conscious every time, here's a little secret! Fasten this 'cheat belt' to bury the monster.

"Empire belts are bold and funky. They are the most flaunting accessory these days and look great over tunics and maxi-style dresses," says fashion designer Nimrita Lalwani.

Taking a cue from high-end fashion designers to budget-friendly stores, the big waist clinchers accentuating the empire silhouette are not only the wardrobe essentials for celebrities, but are also being espoused in college fashion these days.

"It is a pick of the day. Trendy clothes are liked by woman of all ages. Belts make you look dressed and add finesse to you attire. Moreover, they can add style to any plain clothing. One can balance a delicately ruffled dress with a substantial wide belt," says Lalwani. "As dresses are the indispensable fashion wear this season, take your pick and accentuate your middle with a stunning wide belt to make heads turn. But make sure you choose the right size according to your figure," she advises.

"Belts provide a uniform finish to your body as it makes the torso appear in line with broad shoulders. If your upper torso is relatively slimmer than the lower, a thin or broad belt worn on the empire line with flared tops, tunics and dresses can do wonders," says fashion designer and stylist, Kush Agarwal of KushAgarwal, of LavKush Boutique in Camp.

"The belt is like a finishing accessory to any outfit. When empire belts are clinched to elegant evening gowns or a chic short tunics, they add just the right feminine touch to the attires," says Agarwal.

The assorted variety of clinches made in elegant leather or fancy quilts, bejeweled with sequence, push-button buckles and studded belts come in the range of Rs 350-1200, depending on the material and the embellishments and are quite the neatest accesory to adorn the closet of the urban chic this season. Buckle up then.

Heading: ‘Google, Yahoo tie hurts competition’ - Indian Express
Content:
European Union antitrust watchdogs are looking into a planned deal between Internet giants Google Inc and Yahoo Inc to share some advertising revenue.

"In mid-July, we decided to open a preliminary investigation on our own initiative into potential effects of the Google-Yahoo agreement on competition in the European Economic Area (EEA) market," said Jonathan Todd, a spokesman for European Competition Commissioner Neelie Kroes.

Under terms of the deal, first announced in June, Google will supply Yahoo with advertising services to run alongside Yahoo's own Web search system.

Google and Yahoo said the deal would only be in effect in the United States and Canada, but the World Association of Newspapers said it would hurt Yahoo's ability to compete against Google in the future and called on EU antitrust authorities to scrutinize it.

The Newspaper Association of America, which is part of the World Association of Newspapers, distanced itself from the call for EU scrutiny.

"I would like to clarify that the NAA Board of Directors has taken no position on the proposed advertising partnership between Google and Yahoo," Chief Executive John Sturm said in a statement.

Commission spokesman Todd said there was no deadline for the investigation in Brussels.

The probe is similar to one in Washington, where the US Justice Department is also looking into whether a commercial tie-up between the two companies, which together have 80 per cent of the market, would violate antitrust law.

Google and Yahoo said that they would cooperate with the Brussels probe.

"Yahoo has been and will continue to work with the relevant regulatory agencies to provide officials with the necessary information about this business agreement, which we believe will strengthen competition in search and make advertisements more relevant for our users," the company said in a statement.

Google agreed.

"The agreement is limited in scope to Yahoo's US and Canadian websites, and it will not have any significant effect on Europe. We are, of course, cooperating with the commission and are confident that they will reach the same conclusion," said Google spokesman Adam Kovacevich.

The EEA comprises the EU and some neighboring countries.

Companies ruled to be in breach of the EU's competition rules can face fines of up to 10 per cent of their global revenues.

Heading: Cops fumble with names, 'probe on' - Indian Express
Content:
A deal by Google Inc and Yahoo Inc to share some advertising revenue will mean less money for newspapers and weaken Yahoo in the long run, the World Association of Newspapers said on Monday.

The group, which represents 18,000 publications worldwide, criticized a deal struck in June in which Google will supply Yahoo with advertising services to run alongside Yahoo's own Web search system. Together the two companies have more than 80 per cent of the search market.

"Competition between both these two search companies has provided a necessary check to any potential market abuses, and has helped to ensure that publishers and content generators are capable of earning an equitable and fair return on their content," the group said in a statement.

"W.A.N. strenuously opposes Google's attempt to take over a portion of Yahoo's content advertising and syndicated search business," the newspaper group said.

The newspaper association expressed concern the deal was announced as publishers battled Google over copyright issues.

The group also argued that "with respect to paid search ads, the deal can be perceived as an agreement to fix prices."

Google usually charges between 20 and 35 per cent more than Yahoo on average, the group said, citing a study that found that "prices on Yahoo will increase by an average of 22 per cent under the deal."

Although Google and Yahoo said the deal would only be in effect in the United States and Canada, the World Association of Newspapers said it would hurt Yahoo's effort to compete vigorously against Google and give Google a valuable window into Yahoo's ad business.

"The proposed deal will fatally weaken Yahoo as a competitor (to Google)," said the newspaper group, in calling on European antitrust authorities to scrutinize it.

Heading: India to assist family of Andhra student killed in US - Indian Express
Content:
Though the Delhi Police have not been able to put together a tangible file on Saturday's serial Blasts in the Capital, investigators in other cities have come up with four names — Raqeeb, Mujib, Mohammad Afridi and Shah Alam — who they think might have had a hand. All four are from western Uttar Pradesh.

Three names are also floating in Delhi: Abu Zar, Danish and Aftab. Several police teams have raided various places in the Capital, Muzaffarnagar, Baraut, Baghpat, Azamgarh, Faridabad and Ghaziabad to look for these men. It is learnt 13 people are in detention all over, being quizzed about Abu Zar, suspected Delhi blast mastermind Subhan and one Qayamuddin, who has recently emerged as a possible suspect in the Ahmedabad blasts.

However, Joint Commissioner (Special Cell) Karnal Singh refused to comment. "Investigations are on," he said.

Police Commissioner Y S Dadwal was positively gruff. "This is not a Cricket match that I have to keep up a commentary," he told Newsline.

On Saturday, right after the blasts, Dadwal had said the police were "close to cracking the case since officers had vital clues".

Karnal Singh said the police were looking at any clue that might lead to the Indian Mujahideen since this group had signed on the mails sent after the Ahmedabad, Jaipur, Hyderabad and Delhi blasts. The content of all mails was similar.

A senior police officer said: "Abu Bashar, arrested by the Gujarat Police, was in Delhi before his arrest. So were Subhan and Qayamuddin. We suspect nearly 10 people planted bombs in Delhi."

A Delhi team is also closely monitoring Bashar's interrogation.

Sketches not clear

Though the police had made rudimentary sketches of the suspects — with inputs from eyewitnesses, including autodriver Moolchand — these couldn't be released till Monday evening. "Still not clear," said Karnal Singh. All eyewitnesses have reportedly said the suspects were men in their 20s. The police is also planning security for eyewitnesses.

2000 mobile numbers under watch

The Special Cell has reportedly put nearly 2,000 mobile numbers under surveillance since it feels blast suspects had called each other up before and after the attack. They are also trying to find out who called other cities, Mumbai and some in Uttar Pradesh. These 2,000 numbers have been randomly selected, an officer said.

Heading: HC asks mother to live with daughter, son-in-law - Indian Express
Content:
India has said it will provide assistance to the family of a student from Andhra Pradesh, who was killed in Chicago and extend all possible help to expedite her remains to the native country.

"The Embassy of India is aware of the tragic situation and the Consulate General of India in Chicago has been instructed to extend all possible assistance to expedite the remains of Sowmya to India," a senior official of the Indian embassy said.

"We are in touch with the sister of the diseased, the university and law enforcement officials," the official said.

The body of Soumya Reddy (23), a post-graduation student at Southern Illinois University, was found in a car in Missouri with gunshot wounds on Saturday, making it the fourth such incident when a student from the state was killed in the US in last ten months.

Heading: Mob kills cop, torch police station in Orissa - Indian Express
Content:
The Bombay High Court on Monday asked a woman to stay with her daughter and son-in-law, in a bid to save the daughter's marriage.

Division bench of Justice B H Marlapalle and D B Bhosale earlier persuaded the husband to resume living with the wife for their handicapped son's sake.

The husband, S Mashelkar, obtained divorce from wife on the ground of mental cruelty two years ago. The wife, however, challenged it before High Court.

The couple has a five-year-old son, who suffers from hearing and speech impairment.

When case came to the High Court, court asked the husband if he was willing to live with the divorced wife, at least for a few months, so that court may decide on child's custody issue. Wife is currently living in husband's rented flat.

Mashelkar said he was willing to give it a try. Court then asked wife's mother to move in with the couple, so as to help their rapprochement.

Court also asked husband to approach the court immediately if there was any trouble from wife's side.

The court directed that the child be examined by doctors and a report be filed in the court in six weeks. After that court will pass order regarding his treatment and the custody.

Heading: Terrorists scaring people with everyday objects? - Indian Express
Content:
Armed attackers on Tuesday shot dead a police constable and set fire to a police station in Orissa's riot-hit Kandhamal district.

The spurt in violence has led to heavy force deployment in the area.

A large number of attackers armed with country-made guns and crude weapons gunned down a constable and set ablaze the police station at Gochapada early this morning, Director General of Police Gopal Nanda said.

Other policemen present at the police station, located about 36 km from district headquarters town of Phulbani, seemed to have fled into the forest as they were heavily outnumbered by the attackers, he said.

Kandhamal District Collector Krishan Kumar said the mob comprised about 500 people who were carrying fire arms and other weapons.

Additional security forces have been deployed in the area in the wake of the incident in the sensitive district which has been witnessing violence for the last three weeks, both the DGP and the district collector said.

Police sources said the mob was demanding release of a man held by the security personnel but local residents felt that the attack was retaliatory action of the police firing at Kurtamgarh in Tumudibandh area on September 13.

The roads leading to Gochapada had been blocked by logs and boulders which were being cleared to facilitate the movement of forces, the sources said.

The state police chief said it was not the first instance of a police station being attacked and torched as similar incidents had taken place during the riots that had rocked Kandhamal district in December 2007.

Heading: Terror spilling over to India from neighbours: Antony - Indian Express
Content:
It seems psychologists have a different way of interpreting the mindsets of terrorists - three days after the blasts that rocked the national capital, they have come up with what appears to be a 'scaring' theory.

According to them, the use of tiffin boxes, bins and bicycles to plant bombs actually points to the terrorists' mindsets of scaring people with objects of everyday use.

"The tiffin box is used to carry food by everyone, be it a peon or a professor or a CEO of a company. When one sees images of bombs ripping apart these objects, a deep sense of fear sets in," psychologist Dr Aruna Broota said.

In the aftermath of such blast incidents, one may also experience the post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD).

"A person may undergo serious trauma and fear psychosis after he experiences an accident or a tragedy and he then becomes a recluse and abstains from returning to his normal life. A terrorist's mindset is to scare people. Its like you look for food and you get a bomb," Broota explained.

While Saturday's blasts in New Delhi saw garbage bins being used at Central Park and Barakhamba Road in the city's main shopping hub to plant bombs, the market at Greater Kailash saw bicycles as the bomb holders.

Agreed Virender Kumar, who volunteered to help blast victims at LNJP hospital: "Nowadays, whenever I see a garbage bin, a tiffin box or a bicycle parked at a desolate place, the first thing that crosses my mind is explosions and terror."

Another leading doctor corroborated the theory. "These items like tiffin boxes, bicycles and bins obviously are used to evade suspicion but they also propagate fear. The next time he comes across an object associated with the trauma he reacts hysterically," psychiatrist Samir Parikh said.

Even former Intelligence Bureau (IB) official M K Dhar accepted the interpretation.

"The person, at times, may have hallucinations out of a particular phobia that varies from person to person. Terror minds use such objects to place bombs as they are the safest options and do not invite suspicion," he said.

Heading: Bail of accused in BMW accident cancelled - Indian Express
Content:
Two days after serial bomb blasts shook the national capital, Defence Minister A K Antony said terrorists have sanctuaries in neighbouring countries that are used as bases to carry out attacks in India.

In a reference to Pakistan, the minister expressed concern that terrorism 'spills over' to India from neighbouring countries and said the fear of nuclear proliferation had compelled India to be on eternal guard.

"A large number of non-state armed groups have sanctuaries in our neighbouring states who use these bases and resources to carry out acts of terrorism across India. The combination of these and other issues such as nuclear weapons proliferation compel us to be on constant vigil and preparedness to defend our vital interests and values," Antony said at the inaugural lecture of a seminar on 'Force Projection' in the Capital.

While Antony did not directly blame Pakistan for Saturday's serial bombing, he said countries in the neighbourhood that were themselves affected with terrorism were a serious cause of concern.

"We have unsettled territorial disputes with our largest neighbours. Some of them are seriously afflicted by terrorism, itself a cause for our concern as a neighbour. This is further aggravated when that terrorism spills over into India, through state sponsorship or otherwise," the minister said.

He added that the 'real threats' to international security came from states that avoid interdependence from neighbours and outfits like the LTTE and Taliban.

On increased tensions along the Line of Control, Antony said the next few months would be crucial as infiltration bids were expected to increase. The minister, who returned from his maiden visit to the US last week, reiterated that terrorists were getting support from Pakistan and the Armed Forces had been told to remain more vigilant in wake of the recent increase in infiltration attempts.

"The recent firing along the LoC is an attempt of infiltration by militants and Armed Forces are keeping a vigil. By and large, we have been able to defeat these attempts of the militants. The coming few months are crucial and we have to be more alert. The Armed Forces have been asked to be more vigilant," Antony said, speaking to reporters at the sidelines of the seminar.

Heading: No point staying on if leadership not with me: Patil - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi High Court on Tuesday said the offence of Utsav Bhasin, accused of mowing down a person with a BMW car on September 11, is non-bailable and issued a notice to the city police on a petition seeking cancellation of bail granted to him.

Delhi police submitted before Justice Veena Birbal that additional charges under Section 304 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) have been framed against Bhasin after the death of victim, Anuj Singh, a BPO employee, who succumbed to his injuries on September 12.

The court, after hearing the contention, said police can take appropriate action as the offence is non-bailable.

"You (Police) can always arrest him (Bhasin). It a non-bailable offence. The respondent (Bhasin) can approach the court for bail," Justice Birbal said while asking the police and the accused to file their replies on the petition filed by Rajender Singh, the father of the deceased.

Singh had approached the High Court seeking its direction to cancel Bhasin's bail alleging that he might tamper with evidence.

Police had already seized the Bhasin's passport on the direction of the Delhi High Court.

Heading: Women seek release of bomb blast prisoners in Coimbatore - Indian Express
Content:
Under pressure to quit over his handling of internal security, Home Minister Shivraj Patil has said that he will go if the Congress leadership wants him to step down.

"If the leadership is not with me there is no point of staying here. I am not in much demand. I am here just because of them (leadership).

"I have no group either. It's only that the leadership supports me that I continue to stay here," he was quoted as saying in a TV channel.

The Home Minister took exception to the criticism over his changing clothes thrice while appearing before the media on Saturday after the Delhi blasts and said, "you criticise his policies, you don't criticise his clothes".

Patil said, "suppose I don't use abusive language. I live in a clean, neat manner. If I don't get angry with the people. If I keep my cool when it is necessary to keep cool when such incidents happen, you find fault with me. And if they are doing it, do you expect me to reply to that kind of criticism against me".

The Home Minister further said, "I will leave it to the people to judge. You judge yourself. Is this the correct way of criticising a politician. You criticise his policies, you don't criticise his clothes".

Heading: BMW Case: Bhasin may go the Nanda way - Indian Express
Content:
A group of Muslim women staged a demonstration in Coimbatore, demanding remission and early release of their near and dear ones, undergoing imprisonment in connection with 1998 Coimbatore serial blast cases and completed nearly 10 years term, Police said 12 women, led by Mobina, daughter of S A Basha, a key accused in the serial blasts case and sentenced for life, raised slogans in support of their demand.

Though the prisoners charged under Explosives and Arms acts were not entitled for remission and release in tune with the Government order in the wake of Birth centenary of Annadurai, they could a least be released on 'humanitarian grounds,' they said.

After shouting slogans for a while near Red Cross Building, the women dispersed, police said.

Heading: Situation remains tense in Mangalore - Indian Express
Content:
Utsav Bhasin, a 19-year-old man accused of killing a person with a BMW car, has been booked under a stringent legal provision -- similar to the one under which Sanjeev Nanda was convicted, Delhi police told the High court on Tuesday.

The city police informed the court that it had imposed the stringent Section 304 of IPC (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) against Bhasin after the accident victim, succumbed to his injuries on September 12. An offence under this section is nonbailable.

"We have amended the FIR and have added Section 304 against the accused. Now it is for the trial court to decide under which section he is to be prosecuted," counsel appearing for the city police submitted before Justice Veena Birbal.

The court then asked the police to take appropriate action against the accused.

"You (Police) can always arrest him (Bhasin). It a non-bailable offence. The respondent (Bhasin) can approach the court for bail," Justice Birbal said while asking the police and the accused to file their replies on the petition filed by Rajender Singh, the father of the deceased seeking cancellation of Bhasin's bail granted by police.

Advocate Vinod Tyagi, appearing for Singh contended that the accused, who is a son of a Haryana industrialist, is trying to influence witnesses and pleaded that he should be restrained from moving out of Delhi.

Bhasin, however, refuted the allegation and said that he cannot fly out of the country as his passport has already been seized by the police.

"I am not going to escape from the system and I would appear before the police whenever required by the investigating agency," advocate Ramesh Gupta, appearing for Bhasin said.

Heading: Set up federal agency to deal with terror: Moily panel - Indian Express
Content:
The situation continued to remain tense but under control in the troubled areas of Mangalore where violence erupted after attacks on churches and prayer halls by suspected Hindu activists, police said on Tuesday.

A bandh called by 'Sriram Sena' to protest stabbing of one of its activists on Monday evoked good response in the area as most of the shops, business establishments, schools and colleges remained closed on Tuesday, the police added.

Police are maintaining tight vigil in all the areas and over 50 suspected Bajrang Dal activists have been arrested in connection with the attack in the three districts of Dakshina Kannada, Udupi and Chikmagalur.

On Monday, hundreds of Christians took to streets in parts of Mangalore and Bantwal protesting Sunday's attack on churches and prayer houses over alleged forcible conversions by Missionaries, a charge denied by the Bishop of Mangalore.

Heading: Cong might field Sanjay Dutt for Lucknow Lok Sabha seat - Indian Express
Content:
The second Administrative Reforms Commission (ARC) on Tuesday recommended comprehensive anti-terror legislations and establishment of a federal agency to investigate terrorist acts in the country.

In its eighth report, the ARC has also said no person accused of an offence punishable under the National Security Act (NSA) should be released on bail.

Releasing the report, ARC Chairman M Veerappa Moily said that the commission was of the view that a federal agency was necessary to investigate terrorist offences.

"The Administrative Reforms Commission recommends comprehensive anti-terror legislations," he said.

The Commission also recommended that special fast track courts should be set up for trial of terrorism-related cases.

Measures should also be taken to block flow of funds for financing terrorist activities, he added.

Heading: 'Form national commission to detect anti-national group' - Indian Express
Content:
Setting the stage for the biggest electoral drama of country to unfold in Uttar Pradesh – the hotbed of Indian politics, Congress seems all set to give the Lucknow Lok Sabha seat hustings a Bollywood colour.

"Names of Sanjay Dutt, Govinda and Shabana Azmi are there in the list of probables for the prestigious Lucknow seat, represented by BJP stalwart A B Vajpayee," party sources said in Lucknow.

Congress had earlier planned to field former Union minister of state for steel Akhilesh Das from the Lucknow seat but he switched loyalties to BSP and will be contesting from the said seat on the party ticket.

In view of possible alliance with Samajwadi Party, Congress wants to ensure that the seat is bagged by their candidate and for this it has zeroed in on three high profile names -- Sanjay Dutt, Shabana Azmi and Govinda, he said.

"Samajwadi party is also staking its claim on the seat, but we will try to have this seat in our quota," he said.

Heading: I planted bombs, claims a drunkard; cools his heels in jail - Indian Express
Content:
Union Minister Ram Vilas Paswan, whose Lok Janshakti Party backed lifting of the ban on SIMI suspected to be behind recent terror attacks, demanded the setting up of a national commission to identify "anti-national" organisations.

"A national commission has to be formed immediately to identify the organisations which are anti-national whether it is the SIMI or any other unit", Paswan said in Guwahati.

Asked to comment on his views on the SIMI, the union minister for fertilizers and chemicals said that commission should identify the "anti-national" elements, irrespective of their name and prescribe their ban.

"I am not identifying any particular organisation but anyone found indulging in anti-national activities should be banned", he said.

On large-scale infiltration from Bangladesh to the north eastern region and other parts of country, he said a proper cut off date has to be decided on to deport the infiltrators.

"To avoid any controversy or confusion, an acceptable cut off date should be decided, after which who have come from Bangladesh should be detected and deported", Paswan said.

Heading: Delhi blasts: Police release sketches of suspects - Indian Express
Content:
A Najafgarh resident had to spend a night in police station. Reason, for claiming responsibility for Saturday's serial blasts in the Capital and that too in an inebriated state.

Surender Pal's share of woes began on Monday night when he telephoned a CBI inspector and started inquiring about one Vinod and refused to listen to repeated requests that the phone did not belong to the person he was asking for.

"I will blast you with a bomb," Pal is alleged to have told the inspector prompting him to lodge a complaint with the Police control room.

Police immediately got in touch with central security agencies to locate the number which was traced to Pal in Najafgarh in South West Delhi.

The local police station was asked to take details about Pal. The policemen then got in touch with Pal and asked him as to why he was threatening people with bomb blasts.

Pal again claimed that he had already detonated five on Saturday and would do it again. He was immediately picked up from his house in a drunken state and kept in Police station before being shifted to R K Puram for further questioning.

In the morning, after recovering from the influence of alcohol, Pal realised where he had landed himself and pleaded for mercy. He was released after being kept in detention for a whole day.

In another incident, a woman apparently jealous of her husband's second wife informed the police that a 'militant' was visiting her home. A police team was promptly despatched but to its surprise found that the visitor was a distant relative of husband's second wife. The first wife was later given a stern warning by the police.

Heading: I’m again requesting Buddha to quit smoking: Ramadoss - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi police on Tuesday released five sketches of three persons suspected to have planted the bombs in the national capital on Saturday.

One of the sketches was that of the person who purportedly planted the bomb in Ghaffar market in Karol Bagh, while two sketches each were of the two men who placed the bombs near a building in Barakhamba road.

"We appeal to the people to inform police if they happen to find those resembling to these sketches. Informer's identity will be kept secret," Delhi police spokesperson Rajan Bhagat said.

The sketches were prepared with the help of at least five eye-witnesses, who claimed to have seen 'planting of bombs' in Ghaffar market and Barakhamba Road.

The eye-witnesses, including a teenaged balloon seller, who saw suspected persons placing packets in dustbin at Central Park and Barakhamba Road were called to the Police Headquarters on Sunday to assist them in making sketches.

Besides the teenaged boy, a father-son duo who sells breadrolls at Barakhamba Road were also among those called to the headquarters.

Heading: Oil slips to USD 91.79 a barrel - Indian Express
Content:
Amid reports of West Bengal losing millions of dollars in international aid due to its Chief Minister's smoking habit, Union Health Minister Anbumani Ramadoss on Tuesday 'issued fresh advice to him to kick the butt'.

"I have already requested him (Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharya) to quit smoking and I do so again," Ramadoss said.

He said the Health Ministry has sent letters to all the state governments asking them to enforce the smoke-free work places ban from October 2.

"The West Bengal Chief Minister has done a marvelous job as far as getting investments to the state is concerned and has worked hard to make the state better in all respects," he said.

West Bengal has the highest number of smokers 71 per cent of men smokes cigarette in the state.

According to reports, the CM's smoking habits have made the state lose out to millions of dollars in international aid.

Within the last six months, the Bloomberg Initiative To Reduce Tobacco Use had rejected application for grant to West Bengal many times.

Heading: Rupee falls to its lowest since Aug 2006 - Indian Express
Content:
Oil tumbled over 4 per cent to a seven-month low on Tuesday, in free fall for a second day as Lehman Brothers' collapse made investors ditch oil for safe-haven assets, and on fears the credit crisis will hurt the real economy.

Reports that Hurricane Ike caused minor damage to US oil platforms and refineries also weighed on prices, adding to the previous session's more than $5 fall and almost 37-per cent decline from its peak above $147 in mid-July.
