The Ministry of Defence spokesperson, Lt Colonel S D Goswami, identified the deceased as Sepoy Bishan and Sepoy Jarnail Singh of the 16 Rashtriya Rifles. He added that one Army personnel, Om Parkash, also received bullet injuries and was shifted to a hospital. Saini identified the SPOs as Maqbool Hussain Shah and Mohammad Maroof.

"We had been tipped off about the presence of a group of unidentified militants hiding in Tarawali forest in Surankote area of Poonch district. A joint team of Special Operation Group of the state police, local police and Army personnel laid a cordon around the hideout this morning," Saini added. The DIG did not confirm the identity of the militants and their outfit, but sources said they belonged to Lashkar-e-Toiba (LeT). "The operation will continue till we flush out the militants," the DIG said, adding that so far there's no report of any casualty on the militants' side.

Heading: Shiv Sena in damage-control mode, replaces trade union leader - Indian Express
Content:
With a massive rally at Club Maidan, the Left Front marked a happy return to Singur today after two years as farmers who have been opposed to the Tata plant indicated that they were willing to accept the Government's new compensation package.

Left Front chairman Biman Bose announced that compensation cheques were "ready" with the district magistrate, and urged everyone to collect them before September 22.

The Left Front last held a rally in Singur in November 2006. Later, as the CPI(M) was targeted by allies over land acquisition for the Tata Nano factory, and Mamata Banerjee joined the protestors, the LF kept away.

The latest package by Chief Minister Buddadeb Bhattacharjee — offering 70 acres within the plant site and a 50 per cent hike in compensation — seems to have done the trick. Among those convinced is Anar Banu Begum, a resident of Joymollah and one of the 2,150 who had refused to accept the compensation for their land. She was present at the LF rally.

"Even if I get back my land from inside the project area, farming is no more possible there," she said today. "I have heard I will not be able to re-sell it. So I have decided to collect compensation at the earliest." Anar Banu's 2.3 acres were acquired by the Government in September 2006.

Joydeb Das, a resident of Beraberi Purbapara, whose 8 bighas of land were acquired, was also rethinking his options. "Initially we were thinking of taking the compensation money. But after the murder of Tapasi Malik, we changed our mind. But now we are rethinking our decision as this may be the last chance of getting the money. The compensation is also not bad," he said.

The rally was held around 2 km from the Nano site, and the LF had managed a substantial crowd with people from five South Bengal districts brought in. With the crowd pouring out, a few thousand jostled to enter the grounds.

"You will get 50 per cent extra for your land," Bose told the people, flanked by Forward Bloc state secretary Ashok Ghosh, who had earlier held a meeting at Singur against forcible land acquisition. "You can buy land nearby and start farming with the money. Or if you wish, you can start some project. Your family members will also get jobs."

The widow of Susen Santra, who committed suicide reportedly after he heard that the Tatas were leaving Singur, was called on stage and given a cheque of Rs 25,000.

Bose explained that the Chief Minister had done all he could to convince the Opposition, but in vain. "The land which is being demanded back, which is kept for the ancillary units, cannot be given back. The Tatas will not be able to function if that happens. We should understand that Nano, the Rs 1 lakh car, is not only important for Bengal but the whole world. The car will be marketed to foreign countries priced at $2500. We should all try to join hands for the project, which will bring prestige to Singur," he added.

Apart from the Forward Bloc's Ghosh, the RSP's Kshiti Goswami and the CPI's Manjukumar Majumder also lauded the package today. "The Singur farmers are not our enemy... We fully support the Chief Minister who went to Raj Bhavan five times to solve the issue peacefully. We are still open to a peaceful dialogue. I appeal to Mamata Banerjee to resist from violence," said Ghosh.

Heading: Plan panel task force chief says Kosi rehabilitation beyond Govt’s ability - Indian Express
Content:
With trade unions controlled by Maharashtra Revenue Minister Narayan Rane and MNS Chief Raj Thackeray making inroads into its domains in Mumbai, the Shiv Sena is feeling threatened from its own former stalwarts.

Both Rane and Raj have made important gains in the Sena-controlled civil aviation and hotel sectors. As a damage-control measure, party executive president Uddhav Thackeray has divested Bharatiya Kamgar Sena general secretary Kiran Pawaskar of the charge of trade unions in the aviation sector and appointed Bharatiya Kamgar Sena secretary Vinayak Raut in his place. Pawaskar's performance in other areas too is also under observation.

"He was not vigilant enough," sources in the Sena said while confirming the change. According to them, Pawaskar not only showed a certain lethargy, but also failed to respond when the leadership, acting on tip-offs coming from loyal elements in the trade unions, told him to check the attempts being made by elements close to Raj and Rane to gain control of unions in Khambatta Airlines company, airport duty-free shops, Oberoi Hotel, Leela Penta Hotel and Lilawati Hospital.

Sources said Pawaskar kept reassuring the party leaders that his hold over them was intact while the ground situation was totally different. He confessed having been overtaken by events only when the other side went one up. The Sena has since been working overtime to retrieve the situation and has succeeded to some extent.

Heading: Official claims Soren wants to grab his house - Indian Express
Content:
Saying that rehabilitation and reconstruction work in flood ravaged Bihar was beyond the ability of both the Centre and state, chairman of the Special Task Force (STF) on Bihar under the Planning Commission S C Jha on Monday urged the Prime Minister to seek help from international financial institutions like the World Bank (WB) and Asian Development Bank (ADB).

Concerned that the work to plug the breach in Kosi's embankment had still not begun, Jha blamed technical teams of both the Centre and state and urged them to act urgently as the worse was yet to come. "By now the breach should have been plugged. It's very sad that so far work has not even started. The technical teams should realise that it is an emergency situation. If the breach is not plugged then further devastation can take place," Jha said.

"The technical teams should stop talking and start work. There is complete lack of coordination between the Centre and state. My engineer is ready with a plan to plug the breach but his authority is being questioned," said an angry Jha, adding that he would write to the Prime Minister and hold a meeting with the Union Water Resources Minister.

Terming the Rs 9,000-crore demand of the Nitish Kumar Government for rehabilitation and reconstruction as "paltry" and a "hastily" prepared estimate, Jha said his on-the-spot assessment showed that at least Rs 25-30 thousand crore was needed for a reasonable work. "The damage is immense. Nothing less than Rs 25-30 thousand crore was needed and that was beyond the ability of the Centre or state. So, we should seek assistance from the WB and ADB who are keen to help," Jha, who has worked with the ADB earlier, said.

Jha said rehabilitation of the displaced masses and reconstruction of damaged infrastructure was a Herculean task and thereby assistance of all should be sought. "People here are unable to imagine the damage. It's more than tsunami. Large tracts of land will turn arid. A big population will have nothing left to feed them," Jha underlined.

He said he had even spoken to banks like the SBI to come up with an innovative plan to help in the rehabilitation process. "Normal plans will not help. Banks will have to formulate something innovative and they have assured to do so," Jha said.

Lauding the Kumar Government's efforts to extend succour to flood victims, Jha advised the state to use the tragedy as an opportunity to build a new Bihar by declaring the flood-hit areas as Special Development Zones and seek funds from all directions.

Heading: 1 more dead, toll 28 - Indian Express
Content:
Two days ago, Director (Human Resources) Anjani Kumar Srivastava and five others were served eviction notice by the district administration. They were asked to vacate a land that reportedly belongs to tribals and cannot be sold to or purchased by non-tribals. On Monday, Srivastava and his wife Ranjana alleged that their land has been sold by the claimant to Rupi, wife of Chief Minister Shibu Soren.

Srivastava said, "We have been living here for 50 years and now the administration, under pressure from the Sorens, wants us to vacate it." They also furnished photocopies of land records to substantiate their allegations. Rupi has not denied the charges so far.

Besides Srivastava, Rambriksh Singh, Kriti Bhushan Singh, Jaynarayan Mandal, Vasudev Ahir and Santosh Lal have been directed by the Circle officer to vacate land/ house before sunset on Monday. "In case they do not abide by the order within 48 hours, they would be evicted and their land would be restored to rightful owners," stated the order passed by Circle Officer Asid Ekram on September 13. Ekram's order was a sequel to the order passed by the Schedule Area Regulation (SAR) court's magistrate, Devanish Kido. The SAR court had based its order on Chotanagpur Tenancy Act 1908 that prohibits sale and purchase of tribal land to non-tribals. Invoking the Act, Kido had asked these six persons to vacate tribal land so that the property could be restored to the bonafide owners.

In 1959, Srivastava had bought four kathas of land from a tribal, Sukra Oraon. He got the land transferred in his name and built a double-storey house on it. In 2005, one Soma Oraon, claiming to be a descendent of Sukra, filed a petition alleging that Srivastava had illegally purchased the land. Srivasatva has alleged that while the case was still sub judice, Soma had sold the land to Rupi.

Heading: Ban on Deendar Anjuman upheld - Indian Express
Content: Vikas Anand, a 22-year-old banker died at RML Hospital on Monday, taking the death toll in Saturday's serial blasts to 28. Injured in the Central Park blast, doctors said Anand did not regain consciousness. He worked with IDBI Bank. "He died of septicemia, caused due to multiple injuries," hospital chief medical officer Dr S K Sharma said.

Heading: UP recruitment scam: HC order put on hold - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court on Monday upheld the Centre's decision to ban Deendar Anjuman, a Muslim outfit in southern India, for carrying out anti-national activities.

"Your professed activities may be something but your general activities are different," a Bench, headed by Justice Arijit Pasayat, observed while dismissing a petition by Deendar Anjuman challenging the decision of a Special Tribunal justifying the ban.

A tribunal, headed by Justice Mukul Mudgal of the Delhi High Court, on February 27 had upheld the Government's fourth notification extending the ban on the outfit accused of attacking churches to foment Hindu-Christian animosity.

The Bench noted the findings of the tribunal that the organisation was actively involved in anti-national and anti-religious activities in Goa, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra.

The Karnataka-based organisation started in 1924 and was banned for the first time in 2001for two years after it was accused of engineering blasts in various cities in south India. Since then, the Centre has been extending the ban every two years and the last notification issued on August 29, 2007 was the fourth ban imposed on the outfit.

The organisation had filed an appeal submitting that there was no fresh evidence to show that it was involved in anti-national activities and many people from other religious communities had deposed in its favour.

Heading: Cong broke my heart: Amar Singh - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court on Monday stayed an Allahabad High Court direction for a CBI probe into the UP police recruitment scam, which had allegedly taken place during Mulayam Singh Yadav's regime, after the Centre expressed its inability to allow the premier investigating agency to probe the matter.

A Bench of Justices C K Thakker and D K Jain in an interim order while staying the direction issued notices to the UP Government and Amit Kumar Shukla, petitioner before the High Court, to file their responses to the Centre's claim.

The direction by the Bench comes as a major blow for Chief Minister Mayawati, as it was her government that had pushed for a CBI probe after she came to power, when the scam was unearthed. Mayawati had set up a high-level inquiry committee that had found that recruitments were not only done for monetary and political considerations but also sexual favours were sought in return from some female recruits before appointing them in the police force. Over 15,000 recruits have already been sacked by the state Government.

The interim order of staying the CBI probe came on an appeal filed by the Union Government challenging February 4, 2008 order of the High Court to the CBI to conduct investigations into the scam, where names of several top politicians and police officials had cropped up. The CBI probe was ordered on a petition filed by one aggrieved candidate, Amit Kumar Shukla, who contended that an independent probe was essential as one Additional DGP, two IGs, 16 DIGs, one SSP, 33 Additional SPs 77 DSPs were allegedly involved in the racket. He had submitted that it would not be possible for the state police to conduct a free and fair probe.

Challenging the HC's order, Solicitor General G E Vahanvati said that the CBI would not be in a position to take up the probe as it was preoccupied with various other investigations.

Heading: Vacant OBC seats to go to general category: SC - Indian Express
Content:
Terming the defection of four Samajwadi Party MLAs as "betrayal" on the part of Congress, the party general secretary Amar Singh said on Monday that the party has broken his heart.

"Congress Party has betryaed us by engineering defection of four MLAs of our party. They have not only broken my party, but also my heart," Singh said while addressing a tribal convention ahead of assembly polls in Madhya Pradesh. " We wanted to fight against communal forces with the Congress, but now no alliance will be forged with it and the SP will field its candidates on its own in all the 230 seats in MP," Singh said. However, he said he is a "Kshatriya" and will abide by his committment to Sonia Gandhi.

Heading: Nitish-Prachanda meeting today - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court on Monday said that seats remaining vacant after the implementation of 27 per cent OBC quota in educational institutions like IITs and IIMs will go to general category candidates and it would be "desirable" not to have huge difference in cut-off marks. However, it accorded an opportunity to the Union Government to come clear on the anomaly and confusion being created in the process during admissions.

"In case, some seats remain vacant after due implementation of the reservation for OBCs, it would go to the general category," said Justice Arijit Pasayat, part of the Constitution Bench headed by Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan.

The five-judge Bench was hearing an application by anti-quota petitioners seeking a "clarification" on two aspects arising from the April 10, 2008 OBC quota judgment. On Monday, the court heard the application filed by P V Indiresan, a former IIT director, and Arjun Nath, a professor, who had asked the court to clarify two aspects — filling up vacancies in reserved category and cut-off marks for reserved candidates.

Responding to senior advocate K K Venugopal's submission that every single vacant seat is "a wastage" of opportunity for meritorious students belonging to the general category, Justice Pasayat observed that "this (wasting of seats) cannot be allowed. It will go back to the general category."

Heading: Prachanda says ties with India crucial - Indian Express
Content:
In the backdrop of the breach in embankment of Kosi in Nepal, Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar is scheduled to meet Prachanda on Tuesday at a luncheon meeting hosted by JD(U) MP and president of India-Nepal Parliamentary Forum Sharad Yadav at his residence. Kumar reached New Delhi on Monday.

Kumar had wanted the Centre to formally invite him to meet the Prime Minister of Nepal to discuss management of rivers originating from Nepal that cause annual floods in Bihar. After his meeting with Prime Minister Manmohan Singh recently, Kumar had said he was keen to meet Prachanda and would be happy if the Centre extended him an opportunity.

Sources said the Chief Minister, however, would use the brief meeting on Tuesday to stress how building high dams and reservoirs over rivers originating in Nepal would be beneficial for both the countries. Kumar earlier had impressed over a high level Nepalese delegation in Patna that Nepal could use the rivers to produce power and transform its economy while it will save Bihar from floods.

Heading: Terror spilling over to India from Pak: Antony - Indian Express
Content:
Nepal's Prime Minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal "Prachanda" on Monday sought to allay apprehensions in New Delhi by saying that Kathmandu's relations with New Delhi vis-a-vis Beijing can't be compared. He said there were historical ties with India which were crucial.

Prachanda, who is on a three-day tour of India, is expected to discuss reviewing the 1950 Friendship Treaty with India as well as the 1954 Kosi agreement.

While delivering an address at a joint business meeting organised by CII, FICCI and Assocham, the Nepal's Prime Minister said, "I think that due to our historical, cultural and geographical relations, due to our whole tradition of inter-dependence, the relation with India is crucial and vital, although we also want to develop a relation with China, but it cannot be compared right now, no questions of comparison."

On Monday, he held talks with Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, besides meeting External Affairs minister Pranab Mukherjee, Congress president Sonia Gandhi, Leader of Opposition L K Advani, President Pratibha Patil and Vice-President Hamid Ansari.

Commenting on hydel power projects, he said was in favour of "big projects". There is a proposal for a big dam on the Kosi river, which has been on the table for decades between New Delhi and Nepal's Foreign Ministry. "We would like to start afresh... big projects should be undertaken, not petty projects in the hydropower sector," Prachanda said.

He also sought to remove the fears of Indian businesses in Nepal. "We will do all we can to ensure industrial security in Nepal. The Government of Nepal remains committed to adopt every possible measure to provide investors necessary security."

Meanwhile, president of Nepal Film Producers Association Ashok Sharma, who has produced 10 movies and is now part of a 40-member business delegation with Prachanda, said, "We want to produce joint-venture movies with Bollywood and offer picturesque locations in Nepal for shooting of Hindi movies." Sharma, who puts the Nepal film industry at Rs 20 crore per year with about 30 releases, added, "There are similarities in culture and language, and we share a common history. We are here to explore possibilities of movies with Indian and Nepal actors and technicians."

Heading: Fuel supply assurance: India expects clarity in Burns testimony - Indian Express
Content:
Two days after serial bomb blasts shook the national capital, Defence Minister A K Antony said terrorists have sanctuaries in neighboring countries that are used as bases to carry out attacks in India.

In a reference to Pakistan, the minister expressed concern that terrorism 'spills over' to India from neighbouring countries and said the fear of nuclear proliferation had compelled India to be on eternal guard.

"A large number of non-state armed groups have sanctuaries in our neighbouring states who use these bases and resources to carry out acts of terrorism across India. The combination of these and other issues such as nuclear weapons proliferation compel us to be on constant vigil and preparedness to defend our vital interests and values," Antony said at the inaugural lecture of a seminar on 'Force Projection' in the Capital.

While Antony did not directly blame Pakistan for Saturday's serial bombing, he said countries in the neighbourhood that were themselves affected with terrorism were a serious cause of concern.

"We have unsettled territorial disputes with our largest neighbours. Some of them are seriously afflicted by terrorism, itself a cause for our concern as a neighbour. This is further aggravated when that terrorism spills over into India, through state sponsorship or otherwise," the minister said.

He added that the 'real threats' to international security came from states that avoid interdependence from neighbours and outfits like the LTTE and Taliban.

On increased tensions along the Line of Control, Antony said the next few months would be crucial as infiltration bids were expected to increase. The minister, who returned from his maiden visit to the US last week, reiterated that terrorists were getting support from Pakistan and the Armed Forces had been told to remain more vigilant in wake of the recent increase in infiltration attempts.

"The recent firing along the LoC is an attempt of infiltration by militants and Armed Forces are keeping a vigil. By and large, we have been able to defeat these attempts of the militants. The coming few months are crucial and we have to be more alert. The Armed Forces have been asked to be more vigilant," Antony said, speaking to reporters at the sidelines of the seminar.

Heading: Police give clean chit to JD(U) MLA - Indian Express
Content:
Having stepped up pressure on the US over qualifying fuel supply assurances as a political and not a legal commitment, India will be watching closely for corrective action when Under Secretary of State for Political Affairs William Burns delivers his testimony before the US Senate Foreign Relations Committee on Thursday.

Interestingly, a State Department fact sheet on the Indo-US nuclear initiative, dated September 12, two days after the agreement was submitted to the Congress along with the presidential determinations, described the 123 Agreement as providing a "legal framework" for civil nuclear cooperation with the US. The same day, few hours earlier, India had issued a statement that it would consider the agreement to be a "legal document" once it enters into force. New Delhi has since maintained that there cannot be selective interpretation to certain portions of an agreement.

"On September 10, 2008, the President submitted the 123 Agreement to the Congress for its review and approval. This agreement would provide the legal framework for the US to engage in civil nuclear cooperation with this key strategic partner. President Bush has made the requisite determinations on India's progress on a number of commitments it made in the 2005 Joint Statement, as provided for under the Hyde Act and the Atomic Energy Act. We believe the 123 Agreement package is consistent with the requirements Congress set out with strong bipartisan support in its passage of the Hyde Act in 2006, and we look forward to continue our work with the Congress to bring the agreement into force," said the State Department in the fact sheet prepared by its Bureau of South and Central Asian affairs.

It's learnt that India is expecting further clarity in Burns' testimony, which will kickstart the process. India has made it clear that it would not accept any dilution to the 123 Agreement and has conveyed that differing interpretations on an issue such as fuel supply assurance, which is vital to the Indo-US civil nuclear initiative, was not acceptable and needs correction. More so, India had pointed out that it was US President George W Bush who personally endorsed this demand on March 1-2, 2006, when he was here on a visit despite stiff resistance among sections of US bureaucracy.

While India does not see the issue snowball into a major impediment yet, it feels that such differing interpretations could end up forcing Indian entities to avoid sourcing nuclear material from US companies in the future. Armed with the NSG waiver, India is all set to sign a nuclear cooperation agreement with France during Singh's visit on September 30. An agreement with Russia will happen in December.

Heading: CSIR to produce cheap drugs for TB, malaria - Indian Express
Content:
Two days after the police in Munger registered a complaint against Kharagpur JD(U) MLA Anant Kumar Satyarthi for thrashing an old woman to death in village Pokharia on Saturday, the police on Monday said that the case had little substance, as the post-mortem report did not support "the murder theory".

Eighty-year-old Runa Devi, a resident of Pokharia village under Kharagpur police station, used to supply milk at Satyarthi's house and had gone to ask for her dues of Rs 8,000 from Satyarthi. He allegedly asked his supporters to beat up the old woman. After her death, Runa Devi's family lodged a complaint against Satyarthi and three members of his family.

Munger Superintendent of Police Shalin told The Indian Express: "So far, investigation does not support the murder theory." Post-mortem report indicated natural death, he said, adding, "As we have not got any strong evidence against him, there is not enough ground to press the case."

A Kharagpur police officer said: "As the matter concerned an MLA, we registered the case. In normal circumstances, we would not have lodged the case."

Heading: 8 held guilty for Khairlanji murders, 3 out - Indian Express
Content:
In a path-breaking initiative that has the potential to revolutionalise the drug manufacturing sector, the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) on Monday launched its Open Source Drug Discovery (OSDD) programme with the aim of finding a cheap medicine for tuberculosis.

The main objective of the initiative is to produce effective and cheap drugs for diseases like tuberculosis and malaria, which mainly afflict people in developing countries like India, through an alternative process that cannot be patented.

The inspiration for an open source mechanism in drug discovery has come from the success of similar models in software, the most famous being the World Wide Web and Linux operating system, and in biotechnology, where the Human Genome Sequencing Project has come up on the same concept.

CSIR Director-General Samir Kumar Brahmachari — the force behind the project — said very little research was being carried out by big pharmaceutical companies for producing drugs countering diseases like TB or malaria because of their relatively smaller markets, mainly confined to the developing countries. With average R&D costs rising to at least US$ 1 billion for every new drug, the pharmaceutical companies prefer to concentrate their energies on the discovery of big-ticket drugs like those for AIDS and cancer. Additionally, any new drug discovered by these companies is protected by patents, which makes it expensive for people in developing countries.

The OSDD was an attempt to find an answer to these problems, Brahmachari said. Any drug discovered through the open source route would be made generic as soon as discovered. He pointed out that no major advancement in the treatment of TB had taken place in the last half a century. Not more than 1 per cent of the newly developed drugs are for tropical diseases such as TB, malaria, lymphatic filariasis or dengue.

"The normal patent model of drug discovery has failed to produce medicines for diseases that are widely prevalent in countries like India. The open source initiative is therefore a revolutionary concept and could not have come at a better time," Science and Technology minister Kapil Sibal said.

As the first step, the CSIR has set up a website www.osdd.net which will act as a global platform for scientists and researchers to pool in their research and resources. It is hoped that the website will lead to collaborative sharing of know-how for the entire spectrum of processes in drug discovery — ranging from identification of drug-able non-toxic targets, in-vitrio and in-vivo validation, in-silico screening of small molecules, lead optimisation, pre-clinical toxicity and clinical trials.

Brahmachari said the initiative had been receiving a very encouraging response from scientists, researchers and others working in the field of drug research. He said a number of international donor agencies and philanthropic bodies expressed interest in providing the necessary funds for making this project a succes.

Heading: Bio-fuel drive loses steam - Indian Express
Content:
In a major setback to the prosecution, a fast-track court at Bhandara said there was no evidence that the Khairlanji murders were a result of a criminal conspiracy hatched out of caste hatred. The court, however, convicted eight of the eleven accused for murder and acquitted the remaining three for want of evidence.

Four members of a Dalit family — Bhaiyyalal Bhotmange's wife and three children — from Khairlanji village in eastern Vidarbha were killed on September 29, 2006 after wife Surekha and daughter Priyanka helped the police identify the nine assailants of one Siddhartha Gajbhiye of Dhusala village during an identification parade.

The assailants, who were arrested and released on bail the very same day, visited Bhotmange's house, dragged Surekha out stripped her and battered her to death. While Priyanka, 17, was pulled out of the cowshed and killed in a similar fashion, her two brothers were also killed later. Although there were allegations of rape, medical tests had ruled against it.

"There is nothing before this court to prove that the incident occurred out of caste animosity. Even Bhaiyyalal's FIR doesn't mention it. One of the eye-witnesses Suresh Khandate had also said there was no caste animosity," said Additional Ad-hoc Sessions Judge S S Das.

"There is neither anything to prove that there was a criminal conspiracy to kill the four persons. It was only after Surekha set her cattle-shed afire to deter them that the accused killed all the four. There is also no evidence of outraging modesty of the women. Though the women had been stripped there is no evidence who had done so," he added.

The judge, however, held Gopal Sakru Binjewar, Sakru Bijewar, Shatrughna Dhande, Vishwanath Dhande, Ramu Dhande, Jagdish Mandlekar, Prabhakar Mandlekar and Shishupal Dhande guilty under various sections of the IPC. Three persons — Mahipal and Dharampal Dhande and Purushottam Titarmare ¿ were acquitted.

The persons were held guilty under sections 148 (unlawful assembly), 149 (rioting), 201 (disposing of dead bodies/disappearance of evidence) and 302 (murder).

The quantum of sentence would be announced at a later date. However, the judge has set September 20 as the next date of hearing following a submission by Special Public Prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam who raised a legal point.

"I am not satisfied. I think the three acquitted persons should also have been convicted. And there was a caste hatred against us in the village. After studying the final judgment, I will decide what to do next," said Bhaiyyalal following the verdict.

Heading: Odyssey on the wing - Indian Express
Content:
Diesel nahi ab khaadi se; diesel milega badi se (no more diesel from the Gulf; get diesel from our own field)" — that was Chief Minister Raman Singh's slogan to promote bio-fuel in the state. He had also announced that he would use only pure bio-fuel in his official vehicle.

Many government agencies, NGOs and others joined the propaganda, and huge funds were spent on planting 40 crore saplings of Jatropha Curcus, locally known as 'Ratanjyot', on over 1.55 lakh hectares of barren or fallow land during the last three years.

Even before these plants began bearing fruit, Singh stopped using bio-fuel in his official car as he now travels in a bullet-proof vehicle which, officials say, requires petrol or diesel.

As of now, no data about actual survival of saplings and production of seeds is available. Many farmers, who planted Jatropha, are in a fix as trees did not bear fruit at many places.

In tribal Kanker and Rajnandgaon districts, a large number of children fell ill after consuming fruits of Jatropha last year, leading to protests. However, the authorities called these 'isolated incidents' but imposed a ban on planting of Ratanjyot saplings near schools.

Problems persisted even at the places where Jatropha plants bore fruits. Various departments, panchayat bodies and other agencies which planted bio-fuel plants on government land in almost all the districts are still waiting for guidelines regarding collection and sale of Jatropha seeds and extraction of bio-fuel from it.

While the state's bio-fuel programme has failed to achieve the desired result, the state Government claims it could not be expedited without the Central assistance, a national policy on bio-fuel and clear instructions from the Ministry of Environment and Forests regarding planting of Jatropha on degraded forest land.

"Till now, work under bio-fuel programme has been carried out from the state's funds and funds available under National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA)," said S K Shukla, executive director, State Bio-fuel Development Authority, adding steps such as providing subsidies to farmers for taking up Jatropha plantation on barren land could not be taken up at state-level for want of a national policy.

Shukla said the state had already signed MOUs with Indian Oil Corporation and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited for forming a joint venture company with Chhattisgarh State Renewable Energy Development Agency to start commercial production. "Efforts are being made to go for commercial production of bio-diesel by 2010," he added.

Officials claim the state has got tremendous potential for bio-fuel promotion because of the availability of substantial government-owned fallow land, degraded forest land in addition to large tracts of vacant railway land which could be utilised for Jatropha plantation.

The state Government had declared a support price of Rs 650 per quintal and Rs 600 for Karanj seed and Rs 18 per litre of Jatropha and Karanj oil. However, the farmers did not turn up to sell these products at the primary forest cooperative societies of the state Minor Forest Produce Corporation. "It's because the farmers fetched much better prices for their produce in the open market," a Government spokesman claimed.

Heading: Science vs law - Indian Express
Content:
It all started in winter last year, when Czech and Indian scientists decided to solve the puzzle of the journey of two black storks — large red-billed fish-eating birds — that visited India annually during the course of their winter migration.

In December 2007, a team of five, including Czech ornithologist Lubomir Peske, three bird lovers from the Czech Republic and Dr Girish Jathar from Bombay Natural History Society zeroed in on little-known Akola in Maharashtra (near Nagpur) where the birds were found. "We tagged a juvenile and an adult at a local reservoir called Macchi Talao," Jathar says.

The tracking of these two radio-tagged black storks, which migrate individually to India from Palaearctic regions (around Siberia), has found that the foreign migrants cover up to 700 km, at altitudes ranging between 3,000-5,000 feet every day. Interestingly, they seem to prefer small freshwater ponds and reservoirs that dot the country, as opposed to visiting protected birding sites or even major rivers, thus illustrating the importance of even minor waterbodies in global ecology. Following satellite telemetry signals, it was eventually found that while the juvenile was shot over Kabul on April 13, the adult is safe in Tikenlik in Tarim basin in China.

This study has its roots in a Czech experiment, which first aimed at tracking migratory birds visiting the Czech Republic. "We followed black storks from the Czech Republic first. Our country lies on a divide; some of the storks fly west, others towards the east, both ending up in Africa. Knowing the situation in Europe, we moved towards studying the separate eastern stork populations, which begin migrating from Siberia. These birds flew to India in the winters. We had problems with tagging in Siberia so we decided to "invert" our method and begin in India," ornithologist Lubomir Peske told The Indian Express.

The relatively unknown Macchi Talao itself tells a story. "In our study we found that storks, which migrate individually over long distances and not in flocks, prefer small local waterbodies. These are areas that no one would usually look in. But when we had to start the project, we did so in Akola and that is where the storks actually landed," Jathar says.

The scientists also found that the storks would fly as high as 5,000 feet in order to map the area and find better feeding sources. "The storks would soar in the afternoon to find new spots. It would explore and effectively 'map' the area mentally and then move towards a new feeding ground," he adds.

And the journey to find that perfect place to settle is nothing short of heroic. The adult stork moved 3,100 km in 4.5 months between December 20 to April 16, crossing two mountain ranges in central and northern India — the Satpura and Karakoram ranges respectively.

As the scientist traced its circuitous journey, they found it travelled from Akola to Latur area, in south-east Maharashtra and from there on to adjoining Andhra Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, parallel to the Satpuras. Upon crossing the Satpura mountains, it returned to Aurangabad, Maharashtra. Then it crossed Malegaon and the Satpura mountains again. Further north, it flew near Indore and followed a route from Agra- Haryana- Jammu, crossing the Karakoram mountain range. In April, it reached northwest China's Tarim basin, and settled on a lake at Tikenlik.

Interestingly, the juvenile, which travelled 1,985 km, took a similar path, but refrained from crossing the Karakoram ranges, opting instead to fly over Pakistan and Afghanistan. From Akola, it went to Amravati before crossing the Satpura mountains. From near Gwalior, it moved towards Agra, Delhi and then Jalandhar, continuing its journey towards Peshawar and Islamabad in Pakistan. Unfortunately, as it was passing through Afghanistan, it was shot dead at Charikar near Kabul.

However, the extensive migration routes and their zigzag pattern hold a warning, the scientists say. For while India has many stopping places for these birds, over-fishing by humans and shrinking waterbodies may be a reason why the storks moved around so much. "My first impression is that black storks travel during winter much more than other birds studied. This movement could be related to poorer food supply and the fast rate at which water bodies are drying up. The storks do not feed along rivers but mostly use small water bodies for fishing. These are also areas where people fish," Peske says.

Fact File

• Among storks, the black stork has the largest breeding range. A large, striking bird, almost one metre in height, it is distinguished by a black body, red bill and legs and a white underbelly. They are monogamous and migrate individually.

• The western population, originating from Europe, crosses the Mediterranean Sea to migrate in the winters to Africa. They are known to land in both the eastern and western sides of the continent below the Sahara desert. The eastern population, originating from Siberia, migrates to India.

• Owing to the large breeding range, black storks are protected under the Agreement on the Conservation of African-Eurasian Migratory Waterbirds (AEWA), which gives the birds protection through their migratory routes. However the black stork is often hunted down.

• Black storks need a lot of water and eat fish, as well as crustaceans, shrimps and insects

Heading: Need to review counter-terrorism strategies: IB head - Indian Express
Content:
The arrest and conviction of Czech entomologists Dr Petr Svacha and Emil Kucera for collecting insect specimens without prior government authorisation from the Darjeeling forest area has virtually pitted the scientific community in India against the lawmakers. Ever since 2002, when the stringent Biological Diversity Act, 2002, was enacted, scientists have been railing against its provisions which, they claim, are stymying research while aiming at conservation.

The arrest of the Czech entomologists on June 22 turned out to be the flashpoint for scientists both at home and abroad. Notwithstanding the existing Indian laws on biodiversity conservation, they chorused support for the Czechs, saying their stature as scientists should be enough for them to be let off the hook. In effect, the Czechs came to represent all that was wrong with the biodiversity conservation policy in the country.

The Darjeeling district forest department, however, threw the rulebook at them, finding them guilty of biopiracy for commercial gain through violation of several sections of the Wildlife Protection Act and the Biological Diversity Act. After nearly three months of incarceration, on September 10, the Chief Judicial Magistrate of Darjeeling sentenced Kucera to three years' simple imprisonment under each Act, to run concurrently, and fined him Rs 60,000 while granting him bail. Svacha, however, was let off after being fined Rs 20,000.

The disparity in the sentences has surprised the Czech Ambassador and the entomologists. Following their release from the Darjeeling district jail, The Indian Express tracked them down to the Traveller's Inn in Darjeeling town. Although relieved to be released from their incarceration, both were decidedly unenthusiastic about talking to the media.

While Kucera, 51, said he spoke very little English, Svacha, 52, said he found the entire fiasco to be "absurd". "We don't need to say anything, ask your Indian scientists. They are furious with the law. The (Biodiversity) Act is absurd as well, and so are the different sentences we have been handed for the same offence. As far as we were concerned, we were outside the boundaries of the Singalila National Park, and so we've not violated any laws. Consequently, we did not need any permits to collect specimens there. Grazing and tree-felling were going on there, which is not allowed in a National Park."

The CJM court's judgment noted that Svacha's reputation as an entomologist of international repute and his educational qualifications were kept in mind while handing him a lighter conviction, said defence counsel Taranga Pandit. ''We have one month to appeal against Kucera's sentence in the Darjeeling District and Sessions Court. Till the appeal comes up for hearing, he has bail and he can't leave Darjeeling. Svacha's passport will be with the CJM's court for one month, should the prosecution wish to appeal against the sentence.''

The judgment also terms Svacha a ''victim of circumstances''. Utpal Nag, assistant wildlife warden (wildlife 1 division) who participated in the investigation, told The Indian Express the suspicion rested on Kucera. ''Our findings indicate that this is Kucera's third visit to the Singalila area since 1999. Each time, his passport number was different. At the time of his arrest, he had a working website which offered to send specimens by post. The website has shut down since then. On none of the occasions did he have the requisite permits.''

''It is quite unbelievable that someone visiting the country since nearly a decade doesn't know English. How can it be possible that they're unaware of the rules and regulations? We confiscated nearly 2,300 specimens of beetles, butterflies, moths in larva and pupa stages from them. Some were dead, some alive, some dormant. The same has been sent to the Zoological Survey of India in Kolkata. They've not managed to identify all the specimens, but they sent a list of those they could. One of them is an endangered species under Part II of Schedule II of the Wildlife Protection Act. They also had preservatives and food for the insects,'' added Nag.

Forest Ranger Arvinden Lepcha, who effected the arrest, said the Czechs had moved into the area on June 13. "They stayed from June 13-16 at Hotel Goperna in Rimbick, around 50 km from Darjeeling town. They did not register with the hotel using their passports, as foreigners are required to do. According to the hotel owner, they said they'd complete the formalities at the time of checking out. On June 17, they moved up to higher-altitude areas bordering the National Park, where they collected specimens till June 21. Upon receiving intelligence of their activities, we located them at Hotel Goperna."

Lepcha said the arrest took nearly two hours to effect. "They were staying in room numbers 3 and 4 on the first floor. I went with four other wildlife officers. When we confronted them, Svacha looked nervous, and said he had no idea that he was violating laws. We also found that they had de-barked and drilled nearly 20 trees to collect specimens. The Silver Firs have been partially damaged. They had so many specimens it took us four days to sort them."

However, a senior forestry department official, on condition of anonymity, said the boundaries between the revenue land area, forest area and protected area was not clearly demarcated and even intermingled at several spots.

Assistant Public Prosecutor Govind Chettri, who appeared on behalf of the Government, said he was yet to get a copy of the judgment. "Forest officials, on receipt of information about illegal wildlife hunting, confronted the Czechs who failed to produce requisite documents. On completion of inquiry, they were found to be violating Sections 9, 27, 29, 35, 39, 49, 49 (b) and 51 of the Wildlife Protection Act, and Section 3 of the National Biodiversity Act, punishable under Section 55. The court has found them guilty. Once we read the judgment copy, we will decide on appealing against the ruling."

Interestingly, most of the support received by the Czechs, including an online campaign signed by nearly 1,000 scientists from all over the world, and submitted to the Prime Minister's Office mentions only Svacha. Kucera remains unknown. According to Priyadarsanan Dharma Rajan, Fellow Scientist with the Ashoka Trust for Research in Ecology and the Environment (ATREE) in Bangalore, Kucera is more of an "enthusiast" who "collects insect specimens and sends them to taxonomists on demand".

"Although I have never worked with Svacha, he emailed me saying Kucera has, as a supplier of specimen, nearly 100 species named after him as he has discovered them during his collection trips to various places. Svacha, however, is a renowned entomologist. He is known for his research on the long-horned beetle. That he is probably the only scientist in the world working on beetle larvae as well makes him unique," he said.

A day after his release on September 8, Svacha wrote to Dharma Rajan, stating: "We are of course disappointed, but the decision is so one-sided and ignoring facts and numerous lies and cheats of the foresters, that we strongly suspect it is a result of a behind-the-stage agreement -- the prosecutors are "government" and cannot lose. By the way, the judge accepted even the accusations according to the Biodiversity Act, although, as you said, the foresters are not the appropriate party to employ it. He simply dismissed all objections by saying that formal imperfections cannot stand in the way of applying law. Thus, we suspect that at this stage we were bound to lose, whoever our lawyers would be. Let's wait for the result of Wednesday's written submission (to the same court and same judge). Otherwise, of course, we will appeal."

On September 13, in an email to Dharma Rajan, Dr Max Barclay, head curator (Coleoptera) of the Museum of Natural History, London, defended Kucera, saying "I think that the court does not understand that there is such a thing as an innocent amateur enthusiast, who collects and studies insects not for a job, but just for the love of and interest in entomology. Amateur naturalists have for a long time made an important contribution to science (famous examples include Charles Darwin, Alfred Russel Wallace, Jean-Henri Fabre, Gerald Durrell!). There are today many keen amateurs, especially in eastern Europe, where hobbies like this developed during the communist period when people were restricted in what they could do, but natural history hobbies were acceptable. I fear that because he is not paid to do entomology, the courts suspect he must be doing it for some 'sinister' reason."

Wildlife Protection Act 

Sections 9, 27, 29, 35, 39, 49, 49 (b) and 51, under which both Czechs were charged, prohibit destruction, exploitation or removal of any wildlife including forest produce from a sanctuary except under and in accordance with a permit granted by the Chief Wildlife Warden.

The Act, however, provides for grazing or movement of livestock permitted under Clause (d) of the Section 33 for people living in and around the sanctuary. It also states that offences committed in relation to any animal specified in Schedule I or Part II of Schedule II shall be punishable with imprisonment of three-seven years and a fine not less than Rs 10,000. In addition, it states that all wildlife in sanctuaries is government property, and no person shall, without the previous permission in writing of the Chief Wildlife Warden or the authorised officer, acquire, possess, transfer to any person by way of gift, sale or otherwise, or destroy or damage such government property.

 

Biological Diversity Act, 2002

After the Convention on Biological Diversity was adopted by the UN in June 1992, the contracting countries were required to integrate consideration of conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity into relevant legal procedures, programmes and policies. The Biological Diversity Act was passed by Parliament in 2002.

Section 3 states that anyone not a citizen of India or an NRI shall not without previous approval of the National Biodiversity Authority obtain any biological resource occurring in India or knowledge associated thereto for research or for commercial utilisation or for bio-survey and bio-utilisation. Persons found contravening the provisions of Section 3, Section 4, or Section 6 shall be punishable with imprisonment upto five years, or with fine which may extend to Rs 10 lakh.

Who Are They?

•Dr Petr Svacha is currently a research worker with the Institute of Entomology, attached to the Department of Ecology and Conservation Biology. He has several published papers in German and English. His research interests are holometabolan larvae, coleoptera, insect phylogeny.

• Emil Kucera is said to be a forestry expert, and reportedly has several insect species named after him according to his associate Svacha. However, during communication with Indian scientists after the arrest of the duo, Svacha's Institute director Jan Sula had said he had no idea of Kucera's scientific and academic background or the nature of his work.

Heading: ‘Why did you go to Delhi?’ - Indian Express
Content:
With the intelligence-gathering mechanism coming under pressure in the wake of repeated serial blasts in various Indian cities, Intelligence Bureau Director P C Haldar on Monday called for a complete review of the counter-terrorism strategies.

Speaking at a seminar of police chiefs from countries in the Asia-Pacific region, two days after the Delhi serial blasts, Haldar said that in the fast changing paradigm of terror, terrorists remained invisible and exhibited a cross-national spread, spawning intricate networks, with the Internet being used as a force multiplier and a resource base for terror cells. He said the counter-terrorism strategy required a dynamic and uniform response conforming to national systems.

The seminar was attended by representatives from a number of countries, including Afghanistan and Pakistan. Sources said while there was no discussion on the recent Delhi bomb blasts, the delegates spent a considerable time analysing the terror network in the region.

President of French National Crime Commission Alain Bauer stressed the need for strengthening the basic structure of the judiciary, police and society for tackling terror. He pointed out that in addition to sharing compiled data on terrorist outfits, cooperation between countries should extend to timely exchange of actionable intelligence.

Heading: Tauqeer ‘aide’, he has been missing since Nagori arrest - Indian Express
Content: Watigam's 36-hour wait ended on Monday as an ambulance finally made its way to the remote village, 112 km from Srinagar, carrying the body of Mohammad Qasim Parray who died in the Delhi serial blasts. The village was once the hotbed of militancy, and Qasim went to the Capital to escape the violence and find work. With death finding him there, his 70-year-old mother Rehamti asked this on seeing his body.

Heading: 3 Gujarat wanted linked to Delhi blasts - Indian Express
Content:
Qayamuddin Sarfiddin Kapadiya, who is suspected to have been one of the main conspirators of the recent Delhi serial blasts, is also wanted by the Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) in connection with the serial blasts that rocked the city on July 26.

According to DCB officials, Qayamuddin lived with his family at Bagechistiya Vadi in Vadodara city till he went missing. His whereabouts are not known since the Madhya Pradesh police came to Vadodara looking for him after the arrest of SIMI leader Safdar Nagori in March this year. Investigating officers in the Ahmedabad blasts case, who have quizzed his family, say they claim to have no idea of where he is.

Before Qayamuddin went missing, he was in the business of making rubber stamps. He was once arrested by the Vadodara police on the charge of causing grievous injury to a person with a knife. His brother runs a tyre shop in the walled city area of Vadodara.

According to DCB officials, Qayamuddin is a close aide of Abdul Subhan alias Tauqeer, the mastermind of the July 26 Ahmedabad attack who is also believed to be a conspirator in the Mumbai train blasts. Police suspect he may even have stayed along with Tauqeer at a rented house in the Vatva area of Ahmedabad for the planning of the July 26 blasts.

Qayamuddin is believed to have been given the responsibility of planting the bombs in Ahmedabad and Surat. He allegedly arranged for the bicycles and selected the youths who would place the bombs.

DCB officials believe Qayamuddin has a good knowledge of explosives.

Sajid Mansuri, another core member of the SIMI module alleged to be behind the Ahmedabad blasts, is believed to have introduced Qayamuddin to Tanvir Pathan, who was arrested by the Surat police in connection with the recovery of bombs and explosives in the city.

Heading: Re 1 rice: Anna’s dream fulfilled, says Karunanidhi - Indian Express
Content:
The Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) on Monday picked up two more persons from the city in connection with the July 26 serial blasts, taking the total number of arrests in the case to 21.

The DCB also announced the names of three others, apart from Abdul Subhan Qureshi alias Tauqeer and Qayamuddin Kapadiya, who are wanted and who could be involved in the September 13 Delhi serial blasts.

The two arrested were identified as Umar Kala Kabira alias Ashok (38), a resident of Shabnam Duplex, behind Memon Hall in Juhapura, and Salim Jamal Sipahi alias Umar (38), from the Gujarat Housing Board Colony near the Garib Nagar crossroads in Bapunagar.

Kabira recently convered to Muslim and DCB officials believe that some other persons who converted to Islam along with him could be involved in the planning or execution of the blasts.

Announcing the arrests following the interrogation of 19 accused who are under police remand, Deputy Commissioner of Police Abhay Chudasama said: "Umar Kabira had arranged the illegal meetings of SIMI at his residence, whereas Salim Sipahi is an expert bomb-maker who was present at all the meetings of SIMI in Ahmedabad for the planning of the blasts."

According to Chudasama, Sipahi learnt to make different types of bombs at the age of 15 and also trained SIMI members in Ahmedabad, Surat and Vadodara. "The pipe-bomb which was recovered by the DCB from the house of Usman Agarbattiwala, one of the arrested persons, was made by him," the DCP said.

The three others wanted by the DCB apart from Tauqeer and Qayamuddin include Abdul Raziq Mansuri, alias Mohammed Ismail, from Al-Aman Flats in Gomtipur, Muzib Shaikh from the Gulzar Park Society in Juhapura and Alamzeb Afridi from the New Ashiyana Society in Juhapura.

According to DCB officials, Mansuri — who does embroidery work at his residence — was given the specific task of purchasing bicycles for the blasts and planting them at various places in Ahmedabad city. He is believed to have taken training at a camp organised by SIMI leaders in Kerala in December 2007. He is also accused of instigating local youths for jehad and taking part in all the meetings of SIMI leaders to plan the July 26 blasts.

Muzib Shaikh, a skilled polisher of imitation jewellery, is believed to have been present at a training camp organised by SIMI leaders near Halol in January 2008. The DCB said he attended SIMI meetings in Ahmedabad.

Alamzeb Afridi is an unemployed youth from Juhapura area who allegedly also participated in the Halol camp and the meetings held to plan Ahmedabad blasts. He is accused of playing a key role in the purchasing and planting the bombs in Ahmedabad.

The DCB announced a reward for anyone providing information on the five persons wanted in the case.

Heading: Sun TV claims case filed with ‘malicious’ intention - Indian Express
Content:
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M Karunanidhi on Monday launched the Re 1 per kg rice scheme for ration card holders through PDS shops here to commemorate DMK founder C N Annadurai's birth centenary.

Launching the scheme, which has received flak from opposition quarters, Karunanidhi said, "Even if God comes and implements welfare schemes there will be some shortcomings." The CM sought the co-operation of all political parties for the smooth implementation of the scheme, under which 20 kg of rice would be provided to card holders at a price of Re 1 per kg, instead of the previous price of Rs 2 per kg.The scheme would benefit 1.86 crore cardholders and would cost an extra sum of Rs 400 crore per year to the state exchequer.

Heading: No HC stay, 1,405 life convicts set free - Indian Express
Content:
Sun TV on Monday alleged that the case filed against it by Tamil daily Dinamalar was done with malicious intention, and charged the police with bias for filing a case based on the complaint.

In his letter to the investigating officer of Central Crime Branch (CCB) of Chennai Police, Sun TV Managing Editor 'Murasoli' Selvam said that while various media reported on the daily carrying a cartoon of prophet Mohammed and the agitation by Muslims outside Dinamalar offices in Vellore and Chennai , a complaint had been preferred only against Sun TV. "This shows the malicious intention of the complainant, (R Parthiba Rajan, News Editor, Dinamalar)," he said. Police had also acted in 'haste' to file a case, he added.

The summoning of Sun TV's News Editor, Raja, had been done with "some intentions", he said adding reports suggested Raja had been summoned since he was in-charge of news. "How can one person be in-charge of a particular news item," Selvam asked.

Heading: Another Andhra student killed in US - Indian Express
Content:
With the Madras High Court declining to stay the Tamil Nadu Government's order granting them remission, as many as 1,405 life convicts were released on Monday from various prisons in the state commemorating the birth centenary of C N Annadurai, founder of the ruling DMK and former Tamil Nadu Chief Minister. A total of 117 life convicts, including six women, were set free from the Puzhal prison. Those released were given cash assistance and other utility machines like sewing machines to start afresh.

Speaking at the occasion, DGP (Prisons) R Nataraj advised the convicts never to show up again at the prison even to visit acquaintances. The state government last week had decided to release life convicts who had completed seven years (five years for those above 60) in prison. The move had hit a roadblock when Janata Party president Subramanian Swamy moved the HC on Tuesday challenging the decision.

The First Bench, comprising Chief Justice A K Ganguly and Justice F M Ibrahim Kalifullah, in a special hearing at the former's residence, said that the prisoners be released subject to the conditions imposed in the bond they have to execute on their premature release. The court has also directed the government to recall the prematurely released persons if Swamy won the case, the hearing of which has been posted to October 30.

Heading: Centre chalks out progress roadmap, N-E CMs say first give better roads - Indian Express
Content:
The midnight call was devastating for the Reddy family in the quiet neighbourhood of Padmarao Nagar in Hyderabad. "Her professor called to inform that Soumya was fatally shot yesterday. He had no more information. I just cannot believe it," an inconsolable Rajesh Reddy, brother of Soumya Reddy, a medical student who was shot dead in Illinois, said on Monday.

"Soumya had gone to the US last July to pursue MS after completing her MBBS from Hyderabad University. She was doing MS at Southern Illinois University, Edwardsville. We haven't seen her for 14 months," Rajesh says.

For Soumya's mother, Hemlata Reddy, this is the second time that her world came crashing down. A few years ago she lost her husband.

The Reddys migrated from their native Muniyal village in Kadam Mandal of Adilabad district several years ago. They settled in Padmarao Nagar near Gandhi Hospital, Mushirabad. While Soumya's brother Rajesh is working in a private company, her elder sister Shailaja is married.

"We really don't know what happened. Do you know anything? How and who killed her?" Rajesh asks. "Except her professors we don't know anyone whom we can call and find out what really happened," he says. The family has no idea whom to get in touch with either in the Government or in Illinois.

Soumya was apparently shot dead by an unidentified person on Saturday. There is no confirmation yet on whether the incident occurred in Illinois where she was staying or in Chicago.

There was some confusion when the police passed on the information to Adilabad district police about a student hailing from Muniyal village being shot in Chicago. That information was based on the place of birth mentioned in Soumya Reddy's identity card and personal file.

However, the family was eventually traced to Hyderabad where they have been living for several years.

With the Andhra Assembly taking up a vote of confidence against Speaker Suresh Reddy, none of the ministers or MLAs could take up the matter with officials in the US.

Soumya is the fourth student from Andhra killed in the US in the past two years. Last December, two students from Hyderabad — Kiran Kumar and Chandra Sekhar — were killed in Louisiana University while Akkaladevi Srinivas (29) of Karimnagar, who was pursuing his MD in Internal Medicine from Mercy Hospital in Scranton Town, Pennsylvania, was found murdered on March 4.

Heading: UP women’s panel a BSP family affair - Indian Express
Content:
Union Minister for Development of Northeastern Region (DoNER) Mani Shankar Aiyar may be talking about a roadmap for the rapid economic development of the region. But what chief ministers and governments of different states of the region immediately look for are better roads and connectivity.

This became evident when even as Aiyar was trying to elaborately deal with the roadmap for development, at least one Chief Minister — Okram Ibobi Singh of Manipur — said the urgent need was to develop the existing roads and make them pliable.

"The condition of NH 39, which is Manipur's lifeline, is not up to our satisfaction. When I ask corporates to invest in my state, the first thing they ask me is about road connectivity. I have been pressing the Centre for long to improve NH 39 and make it a four-lane highway. Otherwise investors will never come," Singh said at the chief ministers' conclave held as part of the fourth North East Business Summit organised by DoNER in collaboration with the Indian Chamber of Commerce.

In fact, NH 39, that runs from Numaligarh in Assam through Nagaland into Manipur and ends at Moreh on the Indo-Myanmar border, remains closed, either due to strikes and law and order problems or due to landslide and other natural calamities for nearly one-third of the year. It was only last month that it remained cut off near Kohima for about a week due to heavy landslides.

Ibobi Singh also pleaded with the Centre to open a bus service from Imphal to Yangon and Mandalay through Moreh. "Once this bus route is opened, it will attract a lot of business," he added.

The Manipur Chief Minister also asked for immediate withdrawal of the Restricted Area Permit (RAP) and Protected Area Permit (PAP), two restrictions that have been there since the late 19th century as part of the British policy of keeping the hills of the Northeast insulated from 'outside' influence.

Mizoram Chief Minister Zoramthanga wanted reopening of roads between his state and Myanmar, Malaysia, Thailand and Singapore. "Road links to Yangon in Myanmar, and to countries beyond like Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand can usher in massive development in Mizoram because those places are closer to our state that mainland India," said Zoramthanga, whose speech was read out by his Industry Minister S Ramawai.

Assam Industry and Commerce Minister Pradyut Bordoloi on the other hand wanted the Stilwell Road between Ledo in Assam and Kunming in China to be reopened in order to accelerate economic growth in the region.

Heading: Land in sight for drowning AIG Inc - Indian Express
Content:
Family takes precedence over 'samaj' when it comes to appointing members to the Uttar Pradesh State Women's Commission. Mayawati's Government has packed the Commission with relatives of Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) workers and district-level office bearers.

The 16 district members, appointed for a period of one year, get an honorarium of Rs 25,000 per month. And while the guidelines of the Commission stipulate that members should be women of repute who are actively involved in social work, all these office bearers happen to be the wives, sisters or daughters-in-law of BSP leaders or workers, with some even directly involved with the party.

Interestingly, even the top officials of the Commission who have completed a year in office, including the chairperson and the vice-chairpersons, are connected to the BSP. Chairperson Abha Agnihotri is the sibling of Satish Chandra Mishra, BSP national general secretary, while one of the vice-chairpersons, Namrata Pathak, is the wife of BSP MLA Brijesh Pathak. The second vice-chairperson, Sunita Devi, is also a member of the BSP.

The other members have similarly 'distinguished' associations:

• Meerut's Savitri Lal is the wife of BAMCEF's divisional coordinator Jamman Lal.

• The father-in-law of Rekha from Kaushambhi, Harilal Baudh, is the district president of the BSP.

• The husband of Geeta Gautam of Muzaffarnagar, Rishipal Gautam, has been an active BSP worker.

• Bijnore's Suman Lata is the wife of Sarjeet Singh, BSP divisional president.

• Sharda Bhaskar from Etah, along with her husband Bhaskar, is an active BAMCEF worker.

• Geeta Singh, member from Firozabad, is the wife of BSP district coordinator, Murari Singh.

• Rampur's Jagdevi, like her husband Bankelal, has been a BSP worker since 1996.

• Durgesh Nandini from Basti, is a party worker while her husband, Udai Bhan, has also joined the BSP recently.

• Aligarh's Sunita Singh and her husband, Lakshman Singh, are both attached to the BSP as 'pramukh karyakarta'. Aligarh's second member, Meena Shammi, is known to be one of the most firebrand party workers in the district and is often responsible for bringing in droves of people to Lucknow for rallies.

• Gayatri Rajbhar from Ghazipur, the youngest member of the Commission, has sung Bhojpuri songs in praise of Mayawati and the party. She is a zila panchayat member and her brother Nagina Rajbhar is also associated with the BSP.

When asked about the credentials of district members with BSP links, Abha Agnihotri said that they had been elected by the Chief Minister herself.

"The nominations were sent to her and she has personally approved the list. They may be associated with the party but these women have surely shown some inclination towards social work," she said.

Regarding the honorarium, Agnihotri said that it had been decided after a recent amendment, as it helps members meet expenses because they have to deal with cases at the district level themselves and are responsible for organising various programmes.

Heading: Lehman may put its India holdings on the block - Indian Express
Content:
American International Group (AIG) Inc will be allowed to use $20 billion of assets held by its subsidiaries to provide cash needed for the troubled insurer to stay in business, New York Gov. David Paterson said Monday.

The move comes as AIG continues to review its operations and discuss alternatives with outside parties, reportedly including Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway Inc., to improve its business amid concern the world's largest insurer could need up to $40 billion to shore up its balance sheet.

Paterson asked New York state insurance regulators to essentially allow AIG to provide a bridge loan to itself. The governor has also asked the head of New York's insurance department to talk with federal regulators about providing an additional bridge loan to AIG. "AIG still remains financially sound," Paterson said.

The move will allow AIG to use those assets as collateral to borrow cash to fund its day-to-day operations, Paterson explained. AIG has been battered over the past year by billions of dollars of losses tied to deterioration in the mortgage and credit markets. Shares of AIG — once the world's most valuable insurer by market value — fell $5.82, or 47.9 per cent, to $6.32 in afternoon trading. They had been down as much as 71 per cent to $3.50 before Paterson's comments.

Heading: BoA rescues Merrill Lynch for $50 billion - Indian Express
Content:
In the last two years, Lehman Brothers has invested around Rs 1,200 crore in stocks of various Indian companies as a foreign institutional investor (FII). Between 2005 and now, the investment bank had also invested some Rs 4,400 crore as private equity.

With its global losses mounting, within the past month the bank offloaded shares worth Rs 400 crore in several Indian companies, including Amtek Auto, Amtek India, Cranes Software International, NIIT Ltd, Northgate Technologies, Prajay Engineers Syndicate, Fedders Llyod, Masterk, and Triveni Engineering.

"The sell-off was a clear signal that the company was desperate to liquidate its assets and get whatever price it could at that point of time," says a market analyst. The firm is also learnt to be looking for buyers for its real-estate investment division. In fact, most of its private equity exposure was in the real estate sector, including in firms like Unitech, DLF Assets, Future Capital, DB Realty.

According to CMIE and other sources, Lehman Brothers' move to file for bankruptcy in New York on Monday wiped out more than Rs 2,000 crore from the market valuation of those Indian companies in which the US financial major had made investments through the stock markets. Agency reports say the bank recorded a loss of more than Rs 50 crore on Monday on its investments in India. Experts say if it had not offloaded its entire stake in these companies, losses on Indian exposure would have been much higher.

Heading: Six days of agony, fear and failure - Indian Express
Content:
Bank of America on Monday began adding another slice to its growing financial services empire, buying Merrill Lynch in a $50 billion deal that would create a bank that offers everything from fixed-income trading to credit card lending. It will rival Citigroup Inc., the biggest US bank in terms of assets.

Bank of America Corp. said early Monday it would acquire Merrill Lynch in an all-stock transaction that should lift the uncertainty shrouding the investment bank since the start of the credit crisis over a year ago.

Charlotte, North Carolina-based Bank of America has the most deposits of any US bank, while Merrill Lynch & Co. Inc. is the world's largest and most widely recognised brokerage. The acquisition of Merrill "creates the premier financial company in the world", Bank of America Chairman and CEO Ken Lewis said during a joint press conference with Merrill's chief executive, John Thain.

Under terms of the transaction, which came together in less than 48 hours, Bank of America would exchange 0.8595 shares of Bank of America common stock for each Merrill Lynch common share. The deal values Merrill at $29 a share based on Bank of America's Friday closing price of $33.74. That represents a 70 per cent premium over Merrill's Friday closing price of $17.05, but well below what the brokerage firm was worth at its peak in early 2007, when its shares traded above $98.

Merrill's shares surged $4.44, or 26 per cent, to $21.49 in late morning trading Monday. Shares of Bank of America dropped $4.80, or 14.2 per cent, to $28.94. Merrill's stock had languished further last week as ailing Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc. raced to find to a buyer.

Bank of America said its buyout is expected to close in the first quarter of 2009. The deal been approved by directors of both companies and is subject to shareholder votes at both companies and standard regulatory approvals, the bank said. Under the agreement, three directors of Merrill Lynch will join the Bank of America Board of Directors.

Strategically, most industry analysts are saying it's a good fit. If the deal goes according to plan, Bank of America will be able to offer Merrill's retail brokerage services to its huge customer base.
