Filmmaker Krishnendu Bose angles his camera at the Yamuna and sees a vision of the future. "This will be Delhi's hippest address. On the flood plains of the Yamuna will rise a Manhattan of the future, with undulating series of high-rise buildings and the best condominiums that money can buy," he says, referring to the state's urban blueprint. The ribbon of the Yamuna and its 22-km-stretch flood plains form the integral part of the 47-year-old documaker's new film, Delhi: Work in Progress.

Bose's camera doesn't stop roving; he travels with it to the other extreme of Delhi's landscape — at Bhawana, 40 km away on the Haryana border, where evicted slum dwellers have been "dumped". He takes it to a series of urban planners who paint fantastical pictures of the future, to social experts who sound warning notes and perches him atop flyovers that look out onto depleting tree cover.

"The film is a Dilliwalla's tribute to the only city he can call home," says Bose. His shelves are lined with trophies — his last film Tiger, the Death Chronicle won an award at Montana in May — but Delhi: Work in Progress, he stresses, is straight from the heart and documents the Capital's rapid transformation into "what politicians call a world-class city" and the cost of development. "At Bhawana, I was frightened by the level of anger. Around 2,000 people were moved to the jungle from their slum in Vikaspuri. They lost their jobs, have no sanitation and there's only darkness at the end of the tunnel," he says. The anger of the displaced runs through the film — and it espouses Bose's fear that soon the city could see a social backlash by the displaced. "They form 70 per cent of the population who are getting increasingly frustrated by the day," he says.

The 38-minute film, made over a period of one year on a budget of Rs 3 lakh that was largely met by the WWF, progresses as a linear narrative on a series of issues ranging from civic values to Delhi's couldn't-care-less attitude. For the students who watched the movie, the effect was scary. "Delhi: Work in Progress started as a five-minute campaign film on tree-felling in the Capital. I had no idea it would end up as a horror movie instead," says the filmmaker.

Delhi: Work In Progress will be screened at IIC at 6.30 pm today. Contact: 24619431

Heading: Quiz Master - Indian Express
Content:
CHAPTER THREE: Ghosh performing with his band at the launch of the album

"We don't call them songs, we call them journeys," says Gautam Ghosh, as he introduces his band Gautam Ghosh Collective and his kind of music to the eager crowd at Blues, Connaught Place. Performing at the launch of their third album 3!!!, the three-member band proved that live, impromptu world music could be as popular as rock or pop.

Juggling between a dramatic progression on the keyboard one moment and tribal instruments or temple chimes the next, the multi-instrumentalist connected a chord with the cheering crowd. His first journey (not a song, mind you) was a tribute to Joe Zawinul, whom Ghosh calls the "father of world music that we know today", with varied vocal improvisations embellished by the rich sound of the soprano saxophone played by Vikas Gautam. Giving instant, eclectic beats was Siddhart Das on the drums and percussion. And as the evening progressed, GGC left no genre unexplored, experimenting on the spot with funk, jazz, reggae and rock and all that lies between.

"We believe in producing music 'alive', that is why all our acts are unrehearsed and unplanned and our numbers don't follow the conventional verse-chorus pattern. The same holds true for our album 3!!!, which is a recording of our concert in August and consists of 10 journeys," says Ghosh.

Heading: DPS Society doing injustice to ‘brand DPS’: Khurshid - Indian Express
Content:
Vikas Swarup on Slumdog Millionaire, the adaptation of his debut novel Q & A, winning the People's Choice Award at the Toronto International Film Festival

Slumdog Millionaire, British filmmaker Danny Boyle's movie based on Indian diplomat Vikas Swarup's debut novel Q & A, has won the People's Choice Award at the just concluded Toronto International Film Festival. And in Pretoria, Swarup has a million-dollar smile — his picaresque through urban India has not only wowed the audience in Canada but is also set to close the forthcoming London Film Festival. "I guess everybody loves a good fable. In fact, Simon Beaufoy (who adapted the novel) told me that it was the element of Dickensian drama that drew him to the book in the first place," says Swarup, now India's deputy high commissioner to South Africa, over the telephone.

The film, which revolves around the tale of a poor Dharavi waiter who wins the Indian version of Who Wants to be a Millionaire and who has to explain how he knew the answer to each question, is set to make its debut in India in November. It has a largely Indian cast — NRI Dev Patel playing the protagonist Jamal, Anil Kapoor as the quizmaster, and model Frieda Pinto and actor Irrfan Khan in other important roles. Even though Swarup has yet to see Boyle's adaptation of his novel,

he is convinced that the director of Trainspotting and 28 Days Later would have done justice to it. "I have watched all his movies and I was certain that his own unique style will bring a completion to the craft. It was him and Simon's mastery over the script that made me sign the contract in the first place. I am sure it deserves every bit of the adulation it is getting," he says.

In fact, it was the involvement of Boyle and Beaufoy, who had earlier written The Full Monty, that made it easy for Swarup to accept the creative changes. "In any such adaptation, you can either accept the change or reject it. I knew they had retained the framework of the novel and I saw both the first and second drafts of the script since I had the creative rights. It would have been cinematically boring to have retained all the 12 questions and answers. I trusted their creative vision and now, I am waiting to see the DVD which Danny has promised he will send," he says.

Heading: Flat run ends, DDA a winner - Indian Express
Content:
Instead of just selling its name and mint money, institution should open doors for franchise schools, says expelled member

Expelled by the DPS Society for pointing out its "irregularities", its former president Salman Khurshid says the governing body for 11 Delhi Public Schools, and another 119 franchisee institutions, says "brand DPS" began to go off track with the franchise scheme.

The Congress leader, who moved the Delhi High Court following his expulsion on September 1, was the DPS Society president from 1993 to 2004. "It worked well when DPS began the franchise system in the 1960s with public sector units such BHEL and others. But the problem started when DPS went to the private sector," Khurshid told Newsline.

Parents, he said, line up for DPS going by the institution's name and reputation but the franchisee schools are "DPS only by name; they aren't actually DPS". To begin with, Khurshid said, the Society should "open its doors" to franchise schools and make them stakeholders.

Khurshid said he took up the cudgels on behalf of franchise schools after DPS Society's recent decision to hike charges for lending its brand. Till now, the schools had to pay Rs 5 lakh upfront to DPS Society for inking the deal, and another Rs 5 lakh as annual charges.

According to Khurshid's petition in High Court, the Society now plans to raise both amounts to Rs 25 lakh.

"I wrote to all 140 schools — they (franchise schools) were being short-changed by DPS Society. They had every right to be part of the society — a preserve till date of only 11 schools."

The DPS Society's rules make it clear that the elite league "reserves the right to decide about further extension and also the right to change management fee payable¿ to DPS Society." At present, only 11 schools and their principals, besides illustrious names such as Planning Commission Deputy Chairman Montek Singh Ahluwalia and author Khushwant Sigh among others, are its members.

DPS Society chairman Ashok Chandra refused to comment on the issue since it is sub-judice.

'Big fraud'
But principal of a franchise DPS called it a "big fraud": "I have to answer parents who admitted their children in our school only because it is a 'DPS'. But when DPS Society suddenly asks me to cough up 25 lakh for initial registration and Rs 25 lakh as annual charges, and says this guarantees the DPS name for my school is for just nine months, it is a big fraud I am forced to commit against students and parents who trust us and the DPS brand.

"If DPS Society suddenly withdraws its name off my school, can you imagine what it will mean to hundreds of students enrolled here?"

Another principal said though the franchise schools are "DPS to everyone in the city, the fact is they are not DPS. And the DPS Society ensures this is never forgotten."

But another principal of a prominent DPS said the model has worked just fine. "It is a unique way of taking DPS's standards to other cities but not as clones," the principal said. "DPS franchise schools, as some term them, developed keeping in mind local needs: school fees and recruiting teachers locally among other steps. But DPS Society ensures that standards are maintained and the academic quality is good.

"That is why there is a clause that allows DPS to withdraw its name from a school if standards are not maintained."

Khurshid's petition in HC:
"This is violation of the Delhi School Education Act and CBSE Affiliation Bylaws and misrepresentation to the public that franchise schools are DPS schools. Outside India, DPS has sold its name and logo to schools run by profit-making businesses in clear violation of laws — DPS Kuwait was recently sold for reportedly Rs 200 crore.

"All principals of DPS schools in Delhi have been given responsibility of up to 10 franchise schools and paid additional amounts for this."

DPS: Going back in time
* In 1941 began Church High School, in President's Estate
* It relocated with the new name — Delhi Public School — to Mathura Road in 1949
* The school initially operated in tents, under principal K C Khanna and vice-principal Din Dayal.
* DPS, RK Puram, began in 1972

Heading: CM meets top cop, Metro chief to review security - Indian Express
Content:
5,010 houses, 8.64 lakh forms sold, 3,12000 applications submitted Rs 8.64 crore generated just through the sale of forms

The mad rush for the DDA Housing Scheme '08 finally came to an end on Tuesday as people all over the Capital made a dash to submit their forms in the eleventh hour. While the DDA's housing schemes have always been well received, the last one in 2006 received 1.9 lakh forms for 3,000 houses. However, the scheme this year has seen overwhelming interest in a sliding real estate market.

"I know the odds of my name coming up in a draw are unlikely, but I had to try. Where else can you get a house for Rs 14 to 15 lakh these days?" asked Anuj Salwah, who was racing against the deadline to ensure his form is submitted.

The DDA is yet to tally the number of forms submitted, but many applicants said they had trouble filling up forms as instructions were unclear and hence they had to buy them again. Vijay Goyal, chief manager of SBI, said,"Nearly 600 loans for the DDA scheme have been provided from INA branch. Almost 8000 people came forward to submit their forms here."

Subhash Chandra Srivastava, Chief Manager, Central Bank of India, said," Around 700 loans for DDA housing scheme have been provided to people from INA branch and around 5000 forms were submitted here."

Heading: Medical officer made SOS call, doctor performed surgeries through the night - Indian Express
Content:
Following Saturday serial blasts, Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit conducted a review of the law and order situation in the Capital at the Cabinet meeting held on Tuesday morning. Delhi Police Commissioner Y S Dadwal and DMRC chief E Sreedharan also attended the meeting.

With the government battling Opposition's allegations of failure on the law and order front in the Assembly election year, sources said that Dadwal and Sreedharan were invited to ask if the Delhi government could provide any assistance in checking the terror threat in the Capital.

Dadwal reportedly highlighted the fact that the Delhi Police is short by at least 40,000 police personnel trained in tackling similar terror threats. Dikshit has promised to write to the Home Ministry asking for more people to be inducted in the Delhi Police and also impart special training to them. Dadwal also said that while there are only 60 control rooms for contacting PCR vans in the city at present, there will be at least 30 more added to the list to manage PCR calls better.

DMRC chief E Sreedharan said the DMRC has been imparting regular training to its employees on management and vigilance.

Accommodation for construction site workers

With Delhi witnessing a sudden construction boom and a lack of accommodation for labourers, the government has decided to implement a scheme for providing temporary accommodation to construction labourers that will funded by the Labour Welfare Board, Delhi government and the private construction company. Called "holding areas", the tentative sites identified by the government are — Jhatikara, Aya Nagar, Dera Mandi and Saddatpurthe.

Don't discriminate against children in compensation: NCPCR
The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) on Tuesday asked the government to provide "equal or more" compensation to children injured in the Delhi blasts as compared to adults. "The government should take special care of children admitted in hospitals," said NCPCR member, Sandhya Bajaj. Commission chairperson Shanta Sinha would write a letter to the Delhi Government putting forward these demands, she said.

Heading: Clamour for compensation: Injured back at hospitals - Indian Express
Content:
For Dr Rana M Rajneesh, it was a routine round at the Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital on Saturday when one of his relatives called to inquire about his well-being. "When I heard that Delhi was hit by serial blasts at Barakhambha Road, Central Park and Greater Kailash, I initially thought the victims would be taken to LNJP Hospital," says Dr Rana, who performed at least four major operations on blast victims after the Saturday blasts.

"But when I saw the victims being brought to RML, I immediately asked the sisters to open all the operation theatres and be ready," says the surgeon.

Dr Rana has trained with a US team and is certified in dealing with injuries from weapons of mass destruction. He has also trained in disaster management.

When he was posted at LNJP Hospital, he was called in to operate upon bomb blast victims of the Jama Masjid blasts.

"It was a 'do or die' situation. We needed to take quick decisions as there was a whole queue of trauma patients outside, waiting for emergency operations," says Dr Rana.

From 9.30 pm to 6 am on Sunday, Dr Rana performed four major operations back-to-back. It took his team five-and-a-half hours to operate upon Shailesh Kumar, who was bleeding profusely. "His liver and lungs were damaged. A splinter measuring 2.5 by 1.5 inches was extracted from his body. His condition is now stable," said Dr Rana. He also operated upon Jamyang, Akhilesh and Krishna — the other critically injured patients.

Dr S K Sharma
The past 72 hours are a blur for Dr S K Sharma, Casualty Medical Officer at Dr Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, caught as he was between patients crying for help, VIP visits and media frenzy. On Saturday evening, when the bomb went off at Ghaffar market, Sharma was at Karol Bagh, shopping with his wife and children.

Between 6 and 7 pm, RML Hospital received over 70 patients —most of them grievously injured.

After sending his family back home, Sharma headed to the hospital. After the Karol Bagh blast, people started running towards the Metro station, while Sharma called the hospital and informed the authorities about a possible blast. "People initially thought it was cylinder blast. However, the nature of injuries on the victims did not suggest that. I called the police post at RML telling them that four or five cases of injuries might come in," said Sharma.

Even at 6.20 pm, more than 10 minutes after the Karol Bagh blast, the police post at RML Hospital had no information. "I saw the report on TV in a shop in Karol Bagh and told them to keep wheel chairs and trolleys ready. Four of our emergency OTs were ready to receive patients," he added. His tip-off gave the hospital staff vital time to pool in their resources. Within 15 minutes, department heads of various branches of medicine had gathered at the hospital. Blood bank requirement was assessed and arranged for, 25 beds in the disaster ward were readied, and when patients started pouring in, his staff was as prepared as they could possibly have been.

Heading: HC moots proposal to use traffic fines for prompt compensation to accident victims - Indian Express
Content:
Three days after the blasts, the hospitals are handling not just injured victims, but also the ones who want their names incorporated in the list of injured to make them eligible for the compensation of Rs 50,000. There are victims who allege hospital authorities discharged them after first-aid.

"People are now showing up with bandages saying they were discharged in a hurry and not looked after properly. But they do not understand it was an emergency situation. There are people who lost their lives. Some needed immediate surgery to save their lives," said a senior doctor at Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital.

Bipin Rawal, who contacted Newsline to share his grievances, said he was discharged after first aid, but then went back to the hospital alleging he had injuries that were not detected then. "I was given first aid and asked to go home. But the wound on my shoulder started bleeding profusely when I was in the auto," said Rawal, who now wants his name in the list of injured patients with the Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital. He also complains the hospital did not have competent doctors, and that a junior dentist gave him first aid.

The hospital's Chief Medical Officer Dr S K Sharma said a lot of such patients are now surfacing, demanding compensation for the so-called 'shoddy' treatment that they got. "But they need to get their case verified by the police. Rawal does not even have the initial slip that the hospital gives while discharging patients, and has been showing the medical prescription of a private practitioner, which does not count here," he said.

Rawal says he had to go to a private doctor in Dwarka and get his wound operated upon. Doctors found splinters in his body and he now has a 2.5-inch deep hole in his shoulder. He was in RML today, trying to confront the doctors on their 'negligence' but was turned away.

"I want to know why a government hospital cannot give the same treatment that a private hospital can?" asks Rawal, who says he has been advised complete bed rest for the next one month.

Bipin's father Shyamlal Rawal said they now want their names in the list of victims injured in the blast to seek the compensation of Rs 50,000.

After the blasts on September 13, the Delhi government had announced a compensation of Rs 5 lakh to the next of kin of each of those killed and Rs 50,000 to the injured in the serial bombings. It was also announced that the cost of all medical treatment in government and private hospitals would be borne by Delhi government.

"Rs 5,000 will be given to victims with minor injuries, while Rs 50,000 will be given to victims with major injuries. This will be certified by the hospital regarding the nature of injuries," informed Vinay Kumar, Additional Divisional Commissioner of Delhi.

Heading: Govt flat in Lodhi Road caves in, well underneath - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi High Court on Tuesday sought the opinion of the Delhi Government and the Centre to form a "substantial" corpus fund towards which traffic fine amounts can be deposited to be used as a source of immediate compensation to road victims and their families.

"The case of Delhi is particular. Here the police comes under the supervision of the Centre. So kindly verify if the amounts collected as traffic challans comes to you (Centre) or to the State Treasury," a Bench of Chief Justice A P Shah and Justice S Muralidhar directed Additional Solicitor General P P Malhotra, who appeared for the Centre.

The court's resolve on Tuesday to devise this "welfare measure", meant to be timely succour for road victims immediately after an accident, was firmed up when amicus curaie and senior advocate Kailash Vasdev read out the Delhi Government statistics on road accidents from October 2007 to July 31, 2008.

"In about seven months, the figures say, 1,167 persons were killed and 3,804 others injured in accidents. The figures will cross over 2,000 by the end of this year," submitted Vasdev.

To this the Bench reacted that the number of accidents would require a "substantial" amount in the corpus fund. "If Rs 1 lakh is allotted to each accident victim as immediate solatium, then as per the government figures, we will need at least Rs 50 to 60 crore in total," said the court.

"If the proposal comes through, a vehicle owner will have to give an undertaking to deposit the amount (which will be fixed by the court) in the corpus fund. So far, vehicle owners had to take only third party insurance in case of accidents.This move is a pre-emptive step to provide instant relief to road victims, who otherwise have are left with no choice but enter into a long litigation with the insurance companies for compensation," said Vasdev.

Heading: Missing after blasts, hawker returns home - Indian Express
Content:
The floor of a ground floor flat at the Lodhi Road government apartments complex caved in on Tuesday evening. When the owners called in the Central Public Works Department (CPWD), the workers found an old well under the building, much to the shock of the owners.

The floor of house number 2139 of the complex caved in. While the Residents Welfare Association (RWA) of the south wing of the apartments decided to forward a complaint to senior officials, they alleged the CPWD officials present on the spot asked to them to "hush up" the matter.

Joginder Singh, the Vice President of the RWA, said, "The officials tried to convince the owners to keep the matter down. They assured quick repair work in return."

The flats had been constructed by the CPWD in 1983.

Heading: Relief to 13 cops in fake encounter case - Indian Express
Content:
Missing after the serial blasts on Saturday, one man returned home and a missing report was registered at the Karol Bagh PS in another case. Major hospitals in Delhi now say the unclaimed and unidentified bodies of Saturday's blasts have been claimed by relatives. Yet, there are a few unfortunate ones who have still not been able to trace family members.

Hemlata (25), a resident of Okhla, says her husband Dilip (25) had gone to Gaffar Market at 12 pm on Saturday, but never returned. "I have checked all major hospitals, but he is untraceable," says an inconsolable Hemlata.

Dilip sells watches in Okhla, and had gone to Gaffar Market to buy his stock. Hemlata has been doing the rounds of police stations to file her complaint.

Another victim is Manir Alam, who came looking for his 19-year-old nephew Farooq. Farooq worked as a motor mechanic at Gaffar Market till a month ago. On Saturday he had gone shopping to Gaffar, after which he went untraceable.

"I have left a message for his family in Bihar. Since they live in a village, Farooq's family will get the news only tomorrow," says Alam.

For some, it was relief after endless anxiety. After scanning dead bodies at all hospital mortuaries, 28-year-old Rani, was finally reunited with her missing husband, Mukesh Kumar.

Mukesh, 37, who sells painkiller ointments in buses for a living, had told his wife he would be visiting Gaffar Market to buy a birthday present for their 10-year-old daughter Bharti. Fortunately, Mukesh did not.

Mukesh's phone had stopped working and he had fainted on the bus. "The bus dropped him at Nangloi and he was so sick that he couldn't even get up," Rani said.

Mukesh has already said sorry to his wife a hundred times over for what she has been through.

Heading: ‘Those who did this have no respect for Ramzan’ - Indian Express
Content:
In a temporary relief to 13 policemen summoned by a magistrate in connection with a fake encounter, a sessions court has stalled the execution of the order after the Delhi government opposed the direction.

Additional Sessions Judge B R Kedia had also issued a notice to the CBI for October 17, seeking its response on the government's move.

Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Sanjeev Jain had on August 6 sought the presence of the policemen, including two sub-inspectors, after noting that the six-year-old act appeared to be a clear case of criminal conspiracy and murder.

On January 11, 2002, a Delhi Police special staff team led by sub-inspector Vinay Tyagi conducted a raid at the house of Rupender alias Upender at Pandav Nagar in East Delhi and allegedly killed him.

The CBI had registered a case against the accused in March 2003 but the agency had filed the closure report in the case for the want of a sanction from the Lt Governor.

Heading: Karol Bagh: site of mourning - Indian Express
Content:
Like any of the relatives of the bomb blast, Mohammed Rashid, 32, is always around his younger brother, Nahid, 25. Fasting for Ramzan, Rashid's schedule in the emergency wing of Lady Hardinge Medical College includes his daily rituals and prayers. During Iftar, Rashid takes a quick break, rushing to Aliya Mosque on Minto Road that is closest to the hospital. He cannot even go five times a day, as he has to be near his brother.

"Those who carried out the blasts were targeting everybody, including Muslims," he says. "Those who did this have no respect for Ramzan. Terrorists behind the blasts are sullying the reputation of Muslims," he says.

"Ramzan is a time for meditation and deep introspection, fasting and spiritual rest. I fast all day but cannot rest at all. I run to the mosque for the Taravi and then come back as soon as possible. In between, I rush to get medication," he says.

Ahmed Mustafa, a trader based in the Beadon Nagar blast site, is also a blast survivor. He runs shop number 114. Nahid was in shop number 113 when the blast took place in the market. Mustafa is unhurt. But he has joined Rashid's vigil at the hospital, even though it means his regular Ramzan schedule is disturbed. He comes often to meet Nahid, and for Iftar follows Rashid to Minto Road.

Nahid, unlike his older brother, has no beard, nor does he wear a cap. Cleanshaven, he does not seem to believe in symbolism. "It is all about personal choice and the atmosphere you live in," says Rashid.

Life has changed forever for the close-knit family. "Nahid couldn't keep his Ramzan this year. But for the next six months, he will be unable to get up, to go to work. It's a year lost to us all," Rashid says. Faith, however, helps him carry on.

Heading: MCD supply glut makes medicines rot, alleges Congress - Indian Express
Content:
At Karol Bagh, it seems just like another day till you walk up to the place where the CNG auto rickshaw had blown up on Saturday killing nearly 12 people. The usual hustle-bustle in the rest of the market is replaced here by yellow barricades and policemen.

The mourners sit in a corner. One can still hear some cries occasionally but most faces are devoid of expression. The presence of the door frame metal detectors (DFMD) does not seem to be making much of a difference, as people do not bother to pass through. The DFMDs were not working for three hours from 11 am onwards due to a powercut.

Kuldeep Singh, a septuagenarian living in Karol Bagh, has been coming to the site every day since the blast to arrange food and water for families of victims. T Edward, Sub-Inspector (Ministerial) with the CRPF has offered to support the education of a five-year-old girl, Simran, whose mother is battling for her life in Jessa Ram Hospital. Her father died in the blasts.

Raju Amilal, with his team, associated with Nasha Mukti Abhiyan, an NGO has been arranging food, water and medicines.

Heading: Arrest BMW crash driver if need be, says HC - Indian Express
Content:
With dengue cases in Delhi touching 245 on Tuesday, the BJP-led civic body came in for sharp criticism from the Opposition over alleged "misuse" of funds to buy medicines.

The Opposition claims the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) bought medicines in excess. The result: unused, many drugs are past their expiry date. They alleged MCD has some 80,000 kilogrammes of unused medicine lying in its godown.

"The Delhi government had sanctioned Rs 22 crore for initiating (all kinds of) measures to combat dengue. But the MCD spent a huge part of that on medicines, many of which are past expiry date," former city mayor Farhad Suri said.

Leader of the House Subhash Arya refuted the charges.

A councillor from Nizamuddin, Suri said the civic body bought stocks of the drug 'Temiphos' "in much larger quantity than required". The drug is sprinkled in places with stagnant water, like water cooler and flowerpots etc, to prevent breeding of mosquito. Suri said the medicine is used "only up to October, so there was no justification in buying them in bulk".

Leader of Opposition Jai Kishan Sharma said chlorine tablets and 'Promiphos' are also well past their expiry dates. "How can the civic agency distribute medicines beyond their expiry date?" he asked.

The Opposition had raised the issue at a House meeting earlier. But claiming that the civic body paid no attention, they will now take their complaint to Lieutenant Governor Tejendra Khanna.

To make matters worse for the municipality, 2,500 Dengue Breed Checkers (DBCs) are on a strike for the last 10 days seeking regularisation of jobs. They have also threatened to go on a relay hunger strike from Wednesday.

"These DBCs have not been paid for the last eight months," Suri said. "They do not have identity cards to carry out checks and are not properly equipped with dippers, torches or stationery."

House leader Arya said, "The lot of medicines that we have right now expires in February. The amount of medicines being quoted (as having expired) is part of what was left over two years ago."

Arya had, however, accepted the charges at House meeting earlier — he had then called for an inquiry.

Meanwhile, he said the DBCs cannot be regularised. "There is no provision under law for that," he said. "We have a new batch of 450 DBCs deployed to make up for the gap."

Heading: Though money in pocket, Garhi studio still waits to expand - Indian Express
Content:
Five days after management student Utsav Bhasin, 21, allegedly rammed his BMW on two youths, which left one dead on Saturday, the police today told the High Court that it had framed a non-bailable charge under IPC Section 304: culpabale homicide not amounting to murder.

Bhasin is accused of hitting Anuj Aditya Chauhan, 25, and friend Mrigank Srivastava — Chauhan, riding pillion on Srivastava's bike, succumbed to injuries at AIIMS on Saturday.

Arrested day after the accident, Bhasin secured bail within hours since the police had booked him only for rash driving and endangering human life by causing "grievous hurt". If found guilty under these provisions of IPC, Bhasin would have faced a maximum of two years in jail. Now, though, the maximum imprisonment can be up to 10 years under Section 304 IPC — the same charges under which Sanjeev Nanda was booked.

"We have amended the FIR and added Section 304 against the accused. Now it is for the trial court to decide under which section he is to be prosecuted," the Delhi Police's counsel submitted before Justice Veena Birbal.

The court, in turn told the police that they can "always arrest him (Bhasin) — it is a non-bailable offence. The respondent (Bhasin) can approach the court for bail."

The High Court has already sought a response from police and the accused on a petition filed by victim's father Rajender Singh, seeking cancellation of Bhasin's bail.

Bhasin moved the court of Additional Sessions Judge Brijesh Garg for advance bail hours after the hearing at High Court.

His counsel Ramesh Gupta told the court, "There is no need to arrest the accused because all procedural formalities, including his medical tests, have already been carried out by police."

ASJ Ravinder Kaur will take up Bhasin's application on Wednesday.

The victim's father, meanwhile, said "We are satisfied with the court's intervention. We are hoping for justice — both from the courts and the police."

Heading: Super skip raises the bar for Nagaland - Indian Express
Content:
Managed by the Lalit Kala Akademi, the Garhi Artists Studio was primed for a makeover four years ago.

The money was sanctioned, the plan laid out and announced, gladdening the heart of artists already working here, and filling those with hope who have stood in the long queue outside waiting for a room.

However, when it came to execution, the file landed at the bottom of the pile of priorities.

"The government had allotted Rs 4 crore for the studio's expansion and renovation in 2004. It had also agreed to provide Rs 1 crore every subsequent year," said artist M K Puri who was on the Akademi's executive board when the project was cleared.

But the green patch marked out for the new studios inside the complex is yet to see any construction. "We had even finalised the architect — A R Ramanathan. But last year Akademi secretary Sudhakar Sharma informed us the management needed to reconsider a few things," Puri said.

Present chairman Ashok Vajpeyi, who came into office in April, said: "The expansion is on the agenda. We will go ahead after consultation with the artists who already have a studio in Garhi."

Artist Kishore Chakraborty said less space is not the only problem here. He looked at the grinder he uses to work on his sculptures. "The machines are too old, and the maintenance is poor," he said.

Not too long ago, he was part of a group of artists who had complained against the Akademi's plan to revise studio fees.

The management in June suggested that the rental for an old shared studio be increased to Rs 2,250 from Rs 1,050 and to Rs 500 from Rs 100 for a community painting studio.

The artists met Vajpeyi for a review of the hike. Artist Tapan Bhowmik said the chairman also asked them to list their other complaints. "Essential facilities are lacking here. We need to improve the parking area, provide garbage bins, erect a central light tower in the complex, upgrade canteen facilities and give clean water," Bhowmik read out from the list.

Artist Jagdish Chander also complained that the art gallery in the complex had been converted to an office.

Heading: Abhinav leads after Day One - Indian Express
Content:
Rokozhakho of Modern High School, Kohima, boasts of the rare experience of having made three Subroto Cup appearances, making the Nagaland u-17 captain the unanimous choice for leading his young team mates. Among his team mates, Hukavi, Mezhiilhoukho, Beri Kokon and Michael have all played in last year's edition. Rokozhakho is distinctly the shortest figure in the Nagaland team, one of the factors his coach Ropfumeyase rues after they lost 2-1 to Army Boys in a close contest at the Ambedkar Stadium on Tuesday.

But what sets the skipper apart from his towering team mates is his flexibility. "He can play as right out, left out, center forward, left half, right half. "He can play at any position other than the goalkeeper. That really sets him apart from the rest of the players. We keep on changing his position according to the combinations we have," says the coach.

"The most important thing we have learnt is to find an alternative to tackle the height deficiency of the team. We lost today's match because we failed to convert the aerial balls. Over the years we have worked on making the boys stronger which in turn has translated into better control on the field play," says Ropfumeyase.

Rokozhakho took the field as a defender against the Army Boys team as one of their key defenders missed out with an injury. Unfortunately for Nagaland on Tuesday, the plan didn't quite work, as they looked weak in the midfield and striking line, frittering away promising moves.

The IXth standard student, though, has made a few choices for himself and just like his favourite Frank Lampard, loves the role of a playmaker.

"I love playing as a midfielder. I have been playing in that position throughout the tournament. Today I had to push myself back as one of our major players was unavailable," says Rokozhakho.

While his taller team mates speak of learning everything from the coach, Rokozhakho elaborates. "We don't have such grass-covered grounds in Kohima or Dimapur," he says.

For Rokozhakho, the learning process will continue to build his experience for the next cap. This is his last appearance in the Subroto Cup as he turns 17 next year.

Heading: Preparations for Youth Games underway - Indian Express
Content:
Abhinav Lohan carded the best round on day one of the LG Golden Greens amateur tournament with a five-under 67 to charge ahead of the field. Abhinav shot the lone under par round of the day, with the second best score being five strokes behind at even par. Six players were tied for second place, including Rashid Khan and Abhishek Jha. LG Order of Merit list leader Gagan Verma failed to make an impact on the opening day, a score of two-over leaving him at tied 12th place.

Abhinav got off to a blistering start with a score of five-under after the completion of the front nine. But an average back nine meant he had to settle for a final score of 67.

L Selvadurai shone through to card the second best round of the day — an even par 72. But Selvadurai would have to put in another good round on Wednesday to pull ahead of the crowd, as there are many others tied for second place alongside him, including Rashid Khan. Rashid started off in fine fashion but on the par-3 eighth, his game unraveled. What followed was a tee shot into the bunker, a poor bunker shot, a flyer from the rough and a three putt. A sedate back nine meant that he finished even par for the day.

Scores
1. Abhinav Lohan (67); 2. Rudresh Sharma, L. Selvadurai, Abhishek Jha, Rashid Khan, Karan Vasudeva, Moin Malak (72); 8. Rakesh Kumar, Rahul Bajaj, H.S. Kang, Havaldar Jahangir (73)

Heading: No need to study impact before increasing FSI, State tells High Court - Indian Express
Content:
If one were to pop down to the Capital's tennis centre at the DLTA Complex these days, the sights and sounds emanating from the area betray furious preparations for the 2010 Commonwealth Games. But as the dust settles, a group of youngsters can be seen unperturbed by the noisiness of it all.

The Youth Commonwealth Games in Pune are less than a month away, and with Akhtar Ali and Nitin Kirtane presiding over the camp currently underway, there's a lot of work to be done.

Four boys and four girls would form the final teams for the competition. Tuesday was the second day of the camp, and former Davis Cupper Akhtar Ali admitted fitness would be the main concern if Indians had to hold their own against opponents from Australia, New Zealand and Canada.

"We are making these children practice for four hours in the morning, where the focus is on the technical skills, mainly tennis practice. There is another session devoted solely to fitness in the evenings. The physical aspect of the game is very important," said Ali.

"This is a very good experience for the kids. There will be another camp in Pune just before the Games begin. There will be good competition for us since countries like Australia, New Zealand will be there,"said Kirtane. "There are no big junior tournaments at that time, so I think the countries will send their best teams," added Ali.

Akash Wagh, Sudanwa Sitaram, Ronak Manuja, Karunuday Singh and Vijayant Malik are the boys currently up for selection. The girls include Kyra Shroff, Poojashree Venkatesh, Rushmi Teltumbde and Tanvi Shah. Sonia Dayal and Kelsey Sundaram were also called for the camp, but were unable tomake it due to tournament commitments.

Junior Davis Cup
Mexico hosts the Junior Davis Cup from September 23-28, and the Indian squad's team members, minus Yuki Bhambri, are gearing up for the 17-team competition. Yuki is training in the United States, and will join the team directly in Mexico. Saurabh Singh and SV Abhishek are the other members in the squad.

Heading: Civic body not happy with contractors, to use jet-patchers for filling potholes on city roads - Indian Express
Content:
The state government on Tuesday told the Bombay High Court that the government did not feel it was necessary to carry out any impact study before they decided to increase the Floor Space Index (FSI) in the suburbs of Mumbai.  

Advocate General Ravi Kadam, told the court on Tuesday that no independent study was necessary before the FSI was increased following a query by the division bench of Chief Justice Swatanter Kumar and Justice V M Kanade.

The court was hearing two Public Interest Litigations filed by Tardeo resident, Amit Maru and a Kurla resident challenging the state government's decision to increase the Floor Space Index (FSI) in the suburbs. The petitioners contended that the increase in FSI will lead to uncontrolled construction and strain on infrastructure. Opposing their contentions Kadam had argued that the so called strain on infrastructure was not backed by any study. This prompted the division bench to ask whether the Government had carried out any "impact study" before taking the decision.

Kadam said that when Transfer of Development Rights (TDR) scheme was brought in, there were several committees, including the one headed by former chief secretary Dinesh Afzalpurkar, which said that city can bear additional construction. Under TDR, land-owners who surrender land for development project get extra FSI, which they can use or sell elsewhere. Kadam said that since the issue of strain on infrastructure due to additional FSI had already been examined when TDR was introduced, no fresh study was needed this time.

However, the petitioners have contended that while TDR gave extra FSI to only a few land-owners and builders, the present increase in FSI can be availed of by any land-owner or housing society in the suburb.

In July, the counsel for the petitioners had told the court that only 20 percent of the 19 crore square feet of FSI under the TDR has been used till date. They argued that that the government is in fact "creating another city" which means that the "character" of the development plan is changed.

Kadam told the court that the revenue from this can be used for infrastructure and development projects. Kadam had earlier told the court that the state government notification on increasing FSI in the suburbs from 1 to 1.33 will benefit the entire city and only the TDR lobby will be affected by it. According to the petitioners the notification suffers from at least 10 different alleged violations in the decision making process over the FSI hike.

Heading: Pharmacy students urge MU to lower pass percentage - Indian Express
Content:
After experimenting with the South African patented carboncor technology this monsoon, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has moved on to a new gadget to fill potholes on the city roads. Not satisfied with the manual work, the civic body has embarked on mechanised filling of potholes to finish the job in less than 15 minutes with the help of a machine called jet-patchers. The contractor system for filling the roads will be a history, if these machines prove their worth.

Costing around Rs 72 lakh each, these machines will soon replace the contractors who are blamed by citizens and corporators for their shoddy and inefficient work during the monsoon, said civic officials. Accodring to them, there will be three such machines which will be used for filling potholes and trenches. "After the purchase of three such machines, there will be little need for the contractors to carry out the work. If necessary, we will order more machines," said Additional Municipal Commissioner R A Rajeev.

The civic body this year had appointed 24 contractors, one for each ward. These contractors were responsible for filling potholes and other road repairs till 2010. "We will take a decision on the contractor system in a month's time. If the machines are effective, we can do away with contractors," he said.

When asked about the carboncor cold mix technology— its use was made compulsory for the contractors of all the 24 wards to fill the potholes— Rajeev said the civic administration was considering its further use. "The machines should be able to do fill the potholes effectively. But, if manual repair is needed, we can make use of carboncor technology. We're also considering the use of a Canadian material matrix," Rajeev said. One year from now, the contractors of the machine— US made CRafco spray injection patcher-Airstream TM —- will be responsible for filling the potholes on the city roads and maintenance of the machines. After a year, civic labourers will be trained to fill the potholes using the machines. A demonstration on how to use the machine was conducted outside the civic headquarters in CST,

Heading: Now, customers can trace their parcels online at WR website - Indian Express
Content:
Bachelor of Pharmacy (B Pharma) students from colleges across the city have written to the University of Mumbai to lower pass percentage and increase number of ATKT (Allowed To Keep Term) subjects in the B Pharma examination. As many as 200 students will meet university officials and put forth the issue during a academic council meeting to be held later this week.

The students urged the university to lower the pass percentage from 50 per cent to 40 per cent and increase the number of ATKT subjects from 3 to 4.

Pravin Khedekar of the Samtawadi Chaatrabharati, a students' union said, "We also want the university to give students who fail in the final examination another chance by conducting an exam in October so that such students do not lose an entire academic year."

"The ATKT exam is conducted in November, but results are published only in February. Unless we get the results,we won't be able to appear for the internal examination that is held in December. Invariably, we end losing a year," said a B Pharma student. Another student said, "Pharmacy students have to appear for exams in 12 subjects a year."

"It's very difficult to pass all the papers and get promoted to the next class, " she said.

Heading: Teachers across state to observe ‘demands day’ tomorrow, stage protest and dharnas - Indian Express
Content:
In a bid to provide customers with greater facilities, the Western Railway (WR) has opened its website, www.fois.indiarail.gov. in, to the customers. Customers can now trace information about their parcels booked on goods train through the website.

While earlier this website was accessible only to railway personnel, now even the customers can access it. The site makes it possible for officials at the headquarters and stations to gather information regarding a train's journey time and the number of extra hours spent at good sheds to unload the material.

Shyam Sunder Gupta, Chief Public Relation officer, WR said, "This site brought about a lot of revolution in goods train operation. It enables us to know the reasons why a goods train is running late. The loopholes were removed because of the site. Now, customers can access the information."

Gupta added, "This facility will be of great use for the customers who book goods through Indian Railways. Now they are saved of the trouble of personally visiting the stations/good sheds to inquire about their goods. Major beneficiaries would be oil companies, cement companies, FCI, fertilizer companies, steel companies, etc."

This website tracks the movement of each rake right from its origin to its destination. The website is backed by a very strong information collection system and is linked with Freight Operations Information System (FOIS). FOIS and the website, both developed by Centre for Railway Information System (CRIS) are linked to the terminals at various stations. The information is keyed in at these terminals on real time basis and immediately updated on the website.

A customer who has booked a parcel has to just key in a few details such as invoice number, date of booking etc.

The customer can get the location of the parcel booked by him. FOIS also offers important information to the operating officers of railways to enable them make vital managerial decisions for improving operational efficiency.

Heading: Fake journo arrested for assaulting, intimidating woman - Indian Express
Content:
The Maharashtra Shikshak Sanghatana Samanvay Samiti (MSSSS), along with eight different organisations under it, will be observing Teachers' Demands Day on September 18 all over Maharashtra.

Teachers from kindergarten to the post-graduate level will stage protests around the state. In other parts of the state, teachers will stage dharnas in front of the collectors' offices, and in Nasik, teachers will protest in 15 different Talukas.

The MSSSS is protesting the proposals by the Government of Maharashtra which it termed as anti-teachers. "For the first time, there will be protests in Maharashtra on the same day. There is a nine-point charter of issues, which we are protesting," said K K Theckedath, co-convenor of the MSSSS.

Among the MSSSS demands is a revamp of the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, which they believe is not transparent enough. "Forty crore rupees have been allotted from the World Bank and the Central Government for the scheme, but the money is spent only for the heck of it," said Theckedath.

They are also opposing the new amendment that is being proposed to the Maharashtra Private School Employees Service Rules. "Even if a teacher receives a gift for his or her wedding, they have to inform the management.They are planning to increase the term of probation from two to five years. Moreover the teachers' appointments are becoming more contract-based,"he said.

Besides, the MSSSS is demanding the implementation of the Sixth Pay Commission, with a separate pay panel for primary teachers.

Theckedath said that this is the first time that state-wide co-ordination has been planned.

"In three months, after the elections, we will focus on pay scales, and if the need be, we will call for a more intense strike," he added.

Heading: CR appeals to public to help Bihar flood victims - Indian Express
Content:
The Oshiwara police arrested a man on Sunday for trying to sexually assault a woman and for intimidating her with a gun.

The accused Nirajan Choudhary (40) was arrested by the officers of Oshiwara police station while on visarjan bandobast.

According to the police, they were alerted when the victim ( a housemaid) started screaming for help from Choudhary's car while they were driving on the Andheri-Link road. Senior police inspector, Oshiwara police station, Kiran Sonone, said, "When we intercepted the car, the accused, a resident of Shivaji Nagar Thane, said he was a freelance photo-journalist and he also had a red 'PRESS' sticker on the back window of his car, a Maruti 800. However no media organisation has claimed any affiliation to him. He has been charged with threatening, intimidation and illegal possession of arms as his gun was also found out to be illegal. He is in police custody till September 17."

He added, "From what we have gathered so far, Choudhury had met the victim 3-5 months ago in a market in Lokhandwala where she worked as a domestic help." Sonone said, "They were friendly and he used to take her out. Then on Anant Chaturdashi he called her out to meet and tried to sexually assault her and threatened her with a gun when she resisted," he added.

Heading: Vigilant citizens only answer to terror: Police Commissioner - Indian Express
Content:
Central Railway has made an appeal to the public to send relief material for flood victims in Bihar. Central Railway has already dispatched 2,982 packets carrying medicines, clothes and other necessary things to be distributed among the victims, this month.

According to the railway authorities, relief material can be dispatched to Bihar from three stations — CSTM, Lokmanya Tilak Terminus and Kalyan station. S Mudgerikar, Chief Public officer, Central Railway, said, "We have put banners on all these three stations and near the parcel house seeking support from people to help the victims. A team of officials has been deputed to guide the people who want to donate relief material."

Packets of clothes, medicines, bed sheets, tarpaulins, water bottles, utensils, grains, pulses among other things have been sent to Bihar. The relief material has been sent to several districts of Bihar including Purania, Samastipur, Katiyar, Sahrsa, Bhagalpur and Rajendra nagar. "But these materials are being sent directly to the district collector of that district," said an official from CR.

Heading: Corporators put brakes on BMC parking rate hike plan - Indian Express
Content:
Surveillance will be upgraded when Mega City Policing project is implemented, says Hasan Gafoor while launching 24-hour helpline for alert Mumbaikars

Looking to the police for answers after leaving a WiFi Internet connection unsecure and susceptible to being hacked is "asking for a bit too much", warned Mumbai Police Commissioner Hasan Gafoor on Tuesday, at the launch of an alertness campaign aimed at Mumbaikars.

"It's like looking to the police when you leave your key in the ignition, and your vehicle gets stolen. It's a bit too much to ask for. People must secure their WiFi connections on their own," said Gafoor, at the launch of the 'Alert Mumbaikar' campaign at the Mumbai Police Gymkhana at Marine Drive on Tuesday evening.

Gafoor added that the ambitious Mega City Policing project could go a long way in combating terror, as it entails an upgrade of existing resources.

"The project is in the last stages of completion, and would be effective in combating terrorism. Under this project, surveillance across the city would improve through the use of new technology. Other available resources, such as vehicles and communications, would also be supplemented with new and better additions," said Gafoor.

In a press conference attended by actor Shahid Kapoor, the Mumbai Police on Tuesday tied up with mobile phone service provider Idea Cellular to launch the 'Alert Mumbaikar' campaign in the wake of the Bangalore, Ahmedabad and Delhi blasts. As part of the campaign, a free 24-hour 'Idea Safe Mumbai Helpline' number 9702100100 was also launched for citizens to report anything suspicious to the police.

"Mumbai has always been a terror target as it is the financial capital of the country. Prevention is better than any cure, and therefore we urge all citizens to be alert and vigilant, and to report anything suspicious to us. That is why we are launching the Alert Mumbaikar campaign, so that citizens and the police can jointly combat terrorism," said Gafoor.

As part of the campaign, citizens will be urged to be vigilant through posters and stickers pasted across the city at malls, bus stops, on buses, taxis and trains, at movie theatres and at religious places.

According to figures provided by the Mumbai Police, a total of 497 people have died and 2,053 injured in blasts that have taken place in city since 1988. Of  586 terror arrests made in Maharashtra in this period, 396 have been made from Mumbai. In a survey conducted by the Mumbai Police a month ago, 79 per cent of Mumbaikars were aware of the terror threat looming over the city, while only 3 per cent were actually alert and bothered to remain watchful.

"I am proud to be a part of this campaign. I think the police are asking citizens to do something very simple, and I don't think it's asking for too much. I think it's time for all of us to take some responsibility for what has been happening," said Kapoor.

Heading: MNS man asks state rights - Indian Express
Content:
Civic body directed to raise parking space, likely to develop 150 multi-storeyed and underground parking lots

As the country's financial capital faces an annual vehicle population growth of more than 6 per cent and grapples with an acute parking space shortage, the city's corporators have shot down a Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) proposal to hike parking rates. The elected representatives have directed the civic body to refrain from charging Mumbai car commuters increased fees and, instead, create more parking space.

Mumbai, where an average of 400 new vehicles get registered every day, currently has the lowest parking rates — Rs 5/hour for cars and Re 1/hr for two-wheelers — among the country's metros. In a move aimed at discouraging people from bringing private vehicles into commercial business areas, the BMC had proposed a four-fold rise in parking charges.

It would have been the first such hike in 12 years. The last increase in parking charges was made in 1996, fixed then by the Bombay High Court.

While the Parking Policy, a blueprint for coping with the increasing traffic and parking problems, was approved by group leaders from all political parties, the proposal to raise rates was shot down at last month's meeting of leaders of various groups within the BMC.

"What is the need to charge more fees when we do not have adequate parking space? First we should provide citizens enough parking space... only then should we think of levying penalties," opined Sena leader Ravindra Waikar. "Citizens should be given more facilities instead of just burdening them with taxes every time," he added.

Echoing the same view, BJP leader Bhalchandra Shirsat said that it would be unfair to raise parking rates. "The (proposed) hike was exorbitant, with no extra facilities for commuters. It does not make sense for the BMC to earn revenue like this. When multi-storeyed and mechanised lots are ready, people themselves will be willing to pay an extra price. Only then will it be right to increase the rates."

Acting on the corporators' directions, the BMC has set on a task of developing 150 multi-storeyed and underground parking lots in the city on public-private and BOOT initiative.

However, civic officials are upset that their parking rate hike proposal has been shot down. "The elections are close by and politicians fear that raising the rates will backfire," remarked a senior civic official.

Transport planner Ashok Datar termed the corporators' reaction "unfortunate". "In the absence of a congestion tax and with heavy subsidies on fuel, the least effort to regulate traffic would have been to increase parking rates. The best way to regulate the traffic system in the city is to increase the price of parking."

Another transport expert, Sudhir Badami, said that the rejection of the proposal would send a a wrong signal to the public. "It gives a wrong impression... that the BMC wants to shift from a policy of effective public transport to encouraging private use of vehicles. This is not a right indication, as the city will invite more cars — and congestion."

Heading: Susairaj denied bail - Indian Express
Content:
'An officer in charge of law & order is himself provoking people and creating a volatile atmosphere'

A Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) worker has filed a complaint with the Maharashtra State Human Rights Commission (MSHRC) and sought action against Joint Police Commissioner K L Prasad for the controversial statements he made at a recent press conference.

In a letter sent to the MSHRC on September 12, MNS worker and Goregaon resident Anil Chitale said that while watching television news on September 10, "I was surprised to hear Maharasthra Police Joint Police Commissioner K L Prasad's statements in an interview about the MNS protests. Prasad had said, 'Raj Thackeray usne ye bola hai, political dhang se, koi bhhicheez, kuch bhi bolte rehta hai, but definitely koi bhi admi kanoon ka bighadne ki koshish karenge, us samay police usko achche dhang se samadh dena aur usko pratiband karma — yeh city koi baap ka property nahi hai".

The MNS worker said that these statements reminded him of another interview given by Prasad — on February 12 — which too was "careless and hampered peace and tranquility in the city". In that interview Prasad had said, "Koi bhi admi kanoon hath mein liya, uska hath pair tod dalenge."

Chitale said in his letter that it is shocking to see an officer in charge of law and order himself make such statements in interviews. Prasad's statements amount to violations of the basic fundamental rights entitled to him by the Constitution. "Is it not our fundamental right to be a member of an organisation and protest democratically?" he asked.

He added, "Should officials entrusted with safeguarding the rights entrusted in the Constitution be violating those rights? This officer is without any reason provoking people, creating a volatile atmosphere and violating the same rights."

Referring to State Home Minister R R Patil's objections to the statements made by the officer, Chitale sought a thorough investigation into the matter and orders for appropriate action against Prasad.

Heading: Peon gets year’s jail sentence for taking Rs 20 bribe - Indian Express
Content:
The sessions court on Tuesday rejected the bail application filed by actor Maria Susairaj, co-accused in the Neeraj Grover murder case.

Additional Sessions Judge S T Mahajan rejected the bail plea observing that there was prima facie evidence of Susairaj's involvement in the murder along with her naval officer boyfriend Emile Jerome Mathew. This is the second application moved by Susairaj, who is pleading not guilty for murder.

The court also rejected defence's plea of making Susairaj an accused only in the part pertaining to the destruction of evidence. The defence had argued that the murder was not pre-mediated since Susairaj had called Jerome 20 times on May 6, the night of the incident, pleading him to come to Mumbai.

The judge also observed that Susairaj's conduct was dubious and hence her participation in both the murder and destruction of evidence can well be assumed at this stage of trial. Susairaj's lawyers, G Kannur and Ponda, now plan to approach the Bombay High Court challenging the sessions court order.

While the defence had maintained that there was no conspiracy theory in the case, Public Prosecutor R V Kini argued that Susairaj was angry with Grover after he failed to get her a role in TV serials and movies.

Susairaj's counsel Harshad Ponda had argued that if the murder was pre-mediated then Susairaj would have called Jerome to Mumbai earlier and not at the last moment.

Heading: Lots in a name as Mumbai soccer clubs ape the sublime to the stupefying - Indian Express
Content:
A Class IV employee of the state government employed as a peon with the Regional Transport Office (RTO) at Mumbai Central office was sentenced to one year's rigorous imprisonment by a special anti-corruption court on Tuesday for demanding and accepting a bribe of Rs 20 from an RTO agent.  

According to the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) officials the complainant Raju Kakad, an RTO agent, had on May 20, 2002 approached the RTO office for issuance of two number badges for taxi drivers. However, the then assistant RTO Mathew Yohana, who died during the pendency of the trial, demanded a bribe of Rs 400 from him for issuing the badges. He also directed Kakad to pay the amount to his peon Nandkumar Shinde (43), and to also give him Rs 20 separately as his share.

Kakad subsequently lodged a complaint with the ACB, after which a trap was laid the next day at the RTO office, and the officials arrested Shinde and Yohana red-handed while accepting the Rs 420 graft.

During the trial public prosecutor V Desai examined three witnesses of which the complainant turned hostile. The other two witness were panch witnesses who were present at the time of the trap. Desai argued in court that there was substantial evidence before the court that Shinde was hand in glove with the deceased assistant RTO officer. He also argued that the defense of the accused that the amount accepted was a fees was not true as no such evidence was put forth before the court.

Accordingly, the court accepting the prosecution arguments convicted Shinde to one year's imprisonment and imposed a fine of Rs 2,000 on him.

Heading: Domestic help among two arrested for Santacruz double murders - Indian Express
Content:
Football fans in Europe can merely dream of that unlikely country-club showdown between Romania and Arsenal but at the St Xavier's ground, Parel, it's an annual affair. But before shocked queries about dates and tickets come flooding in, one small clarification: Don't expect to find a Mutu, a Gallas on field or Aresne Wenger on the sidelines since on show will be some amateurs with modest skills fighting for the city's fourth division football league title.

Call it a serious lack of imagination or the overwhelming influence of European football, when it comes to naming, the inspiration for lower division Mumbai District Football Association clubs is generally imported. A number of teams with the famous 'United' suffix and one with a prefix 'Athletico' reflect the exaggerated aspirations of football teams inclined to think big. Manchester might be miles away from Laxminagar or Chembur and light years ahead in terms of the game's tradition but somehow the English soccer hub and the city's suburbs find themselves 'United'.

Even famous nicknames of clubs are diligently adopted. Manchester United fans call themselves the Red Devils, while Arsenal faithfuls are the Gunners. The inspiration behind the Red Devils who play in the MDFA Division V league is anybody's guess. Athletico Mumbai — apparently Madrid too has a team with a similar sounding name — shows that the Spanish League too has its fans base in the city.

Besides these Euro-inspired teams, the MDFA lower division draw throws up more team names that range from the obvious, stupefying to some downright comical. Nails United, for instance. Club manager Ramesh, however, explains that the name has nothing to do with the human anatomy and that the team strongly believes in 'nailing' the opposition. But what about a club named 'Gatofield'? Skipper Aditya throws light on the issue. "Well, it's quite simple actually. The 'field' in our name comes from the team Chesterfield that plays Division 1 in England, while 'Gato' comes from the energy drink Gatorade," he says.

There are other unique names that regularly figure on local sports pages of newspapers but are quite self-explanatory. Sport has always been linked with the uncontrollable powers of nature like fortune and luck and teams like Lucky Utd, Lucky Boys, Believers and Miracles certainly seem to project a more hopeful sentiment rather than a confident one. For others, modesty doesn't seem to be a virtue as teams like Super Boys, Chedda Nagar Soccer Prodigies and Little Masters hope to skyrocket to higher divisions. Bravado too is a much flaunted trait with Colaba No Fears United giving the impression that they wouldn't sigh away from any tough tackle.

A few contests on field sound more like video game battles than serious soccer matches. Falcons vs Spartans isn't a blast-from-the-past kind of gaming duel but an outdoor activity between two average, well-behaved soccer teams. Names like these may be a delight for a headline-writer with a penchant for puns. And even if you forget the quality of play, on paper there is never a dull moment in the MDFA lower division.

Heading: BMC orders inquiry into road cave-in tragedy - Indian Express
Content:
Cops say accused had planned the entire operation in advance and accordingly sent servant to victims' house

A day after the gruesome murder of an elderly woman and her grandson in Santacruz, the police on Tuesday arrested two persons including the victim's domestic help.

Ushaben Parikh (74) and her 12-year-old grandson Harsh were killed after a robbery in their flat in Shobhna building at Tilak road on Monday.

The Santacruz police picked up Parikhs' servant Ajay Singh Dhanbahadur (19) and Yadhu Singh (20), a watchman, from Ghatkopar and Vile Parle respectively at around 3:30 am. The police have also recovered a part of the stolen materials, including a few watches. Two more people are said to be involved in the murder and the robbery but are yet to be apprehended. All the four suspects are Nepali and the two absconding accused are also said to be watchmen. "The entire operation seems to be preplanned," said Additional Commissioner of Police (West Region) Archana Tyagi. "Ajay was employed at the Parikhs' house only a week ago, though he had been in Mumbai for the past five years and used to work as a cable operator," she added.

"All the four accused knew each other and according to Ajay and Yadhu, they owed money to someone for a piece of land they had bought in Nepal. They then planned and sent Ajay to the Parikhs' house as a servant. On the day of the incident, Ajay let the other three into the building in the morning and hid them on the terrace. When he saw that Harsh's mother had left, he called them down. They then tied Ushaben up and strangled her with a pillow. Later, they went into Harsh's room where he was playing on the computer. They tied him up also to muffle his protest and took him to the bathroom and strangulated him. After the crime they intended to flee to Katmandu" Tyagi said. When asked whether the accused had past criminal records, she said, "We are still investigating into this. But since they made use of household things like sheets to bind and strangle their victims, maybe they have some experience."

"We made three teams to trace the culprits. In the last year, many similar crimes have occurred where servants have murdered senior citizens and made away with money. In all these cases the servants were not registered or photographed. We request people to do the same as a preventive measure," Tyagi said.

Heading: Business rivalry: Cable operator attacked - Indian Express
Content:
A day after, a road at the Jacob Circle caved in, claiming three lives, clueless Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) ordered a probe to identify the reason for the cavity. A leakage in the main sewerage lines caused by the soil erosion led to the weakening of the road surface, which subsequently caved in when a truck passed on it.

The decision was taken in a meeting chaired by Municipal Commissioner Jairaj Phatak on Tuesday. Deputy Municipal Commissioner (vigilance) will conduct the inquiry, said civic officials.

"We do not know the exact reason for the cavity. We don't have any idea whether it was because of the leakage or the road was weak," said said Additional Municipal Commissioner (city) R A Rajeev. "It was a major accident and we need to find out the exact reason for the cavity on the road," he said.

However, the police have registered a case against the contractor who laid the road and written a letter to the BMC to provide details about the contractor. When contacted, Senior Police Inspector Ravindra Khandagale of the Agripada police station said, "Our enquiries have shown that the accident was probably a result of negligence of the contractor and we have registered a case of causing death by negligence against him. The contractor has not been identified so far and we are seeking the civic body's help."

The BMC, however, is yet to take any action against the contractor. "Any decision regarding action against the contractor will be taken only after the inquiry report is submitted," said Rajeev.

The incident occurred at 1 pm on Monday, when the road failed to bear the weight of a truck carrying bamboos. Following the incident, the police detained the driver of the truck for enquiry, but are ruling out his fault in the incident.

Since the cavity is large, civic officials said it will take some time to repair the road. Fixing of the sewerage line leakages will also take some time, officials said. "The patch in the sewerage line has been temporarily filled and repair work should be completed in three-four days," said Rajeev.

Compensation for victims' families
The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) announced compensation for the three persons who died in the incident. " A compensation of Rs 1 lakh each will be provided to the families of deceased," Rajee said. It is for the first time that the civic body is giving compensation to the dead, as giving financial aid to the victims comes under the purview of the state government.

Heading: Four months on, body of woman lies unclaimed at JJ Hospital morgue - Indian Express
Content:
A feud between two local cable operators in Ghatkopar was taken to streets on Monday morning, when a gang of goons attacked Kripali Jawalkar— one of the cable operators in the area— on Tuesday. Jawalkar sustained severe injuries on her hand and alleged that her rival cable operator in the area had sent the goons to attack her. Following the incident, Jawalkar filed a complaint with the Vikhroli police station.

The police have booked the accused identified as Vimal Balbhim Nagane, Sharad Nagane, Balbhim Aryan Nagane and Manibai Gonde for attempt to murder. "I was attacked when I was on my way to Mulund. I sustained injury on my wrist," said Jawalkar.

According to Jawalkar, she had complained to the Collector about an illegal cable service that was run by the accused in the area. "Following this, they developed grudge against me. They run an illegal cable service business. But, I have taken all the necessary permissions to run a cable service network and pay taxes regularly," said Jawalkar. When contacted, the Vikhroli police said, "It's a case of cross complaints as both the parties allege that the other was running an illegal business."

"Cases have been registered against both the complainants and accused ," said Police Sub-inspector Nitin Vijaykar who is investigating the case.

Heading: TC arrested for taking money from commuter - Indian Express
Content:
According to police, it's a case of murder

Four months after a partially decomposed body of a woman was found in a sack in Vikhroli, the body lies unclaimed at the J J Hospital morgue with the police suspecting it to be a murder case. Though the police have tried to trace her identity across Mumbai, Navi Mumbai and Thane regions, their efforts have not yet succeeded. On April 20, the Vikhroli police had found a sack with a partially decomposed, headless body of a woman near the highway at Kanjurgaon. The skull and some other remains were found a few feet away.

"It is undoubtedly a murder case as the woman was severely assaulted and her spinal cord was totally broken. The head was found a few feet away from her body and her arms were also severed," said Police Inspector P P Kirdat. He added, "Once we find out her background, the motive behind the murder can be ascertained."

The police officials claim that they have met nearly 200 people so far to find out the woman's identity. "In the past few months, 168 women have been reported missing from Mumbai, Navi Mumbai, Thane city and district areas. We have met most of the complainants in these cases. However, none of the complainants recognized the body," said head constable B B Dighe.

The police also found a beaded chain with an amulet usually worn by Nepali women or those from Karnataka beside the body of the woman.

The officials are now waiting for the body to be entirely decomposed as advised by the doctors at the JJ Hospital's anatomy section. "Only after the decomposition process is complete, the doctors will be able to ascertain the cause of the death. They have told us that some more details could emerge after the decomposition," said Kirdat.

Heading: Taking stock - Indian Express
Content:
A woman ticket checker (TC) was caught red handed by vigilance officials of Central railway (CR) at the Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus (CST), while taking money from a commuter who was allegedly travelling without a ticket. The TC was caught while the CR's vigilance officers were carrying out checks to monitor cash being paid to railway officials and other cases of corruption at the station.

Sangita Singh, was posted as a TC at Dadar station. However, on Tuesday, Singh was on replacement duty at CSTM. When she saw a lady with two children travelling without a ticket, she demanded Rs 762 from her. The lady paid her Rs 700. An official on condition of anonymity said, "As Ms Singh realised that the vigilance staff was watching her, she returned Rs 400 to that lady and then made a receipt of Rs 260 but tore it. When vigilance officer, SR Tripathi, came to her, the remaining Rs 40 was also not with her." Vigilance officers have recorded her statement. Singh accepted that she purchased bottles of milk from a railway shop and gave the amount of Rs 40 to the shopkeeper.

Railway sources said, "The victim is a homely lady. As she did not know the rules and regulations, she was going to purchase ticket from the booking window near the administrative building, using platform number 1. Meanwhile she was caught by the TC. Actually in these circumstances, there was no intention to defraud. The TC should have helped her purchase the ticket. Most of the TCs do not follow the rules. And in this case, the TC herself was trapped by vigilance officers."

S Mudgerikar, chief public relations officer, Central railway, said, "She  was caught by vigilance officers. Vigilance department conducts regular preventive checks. Further investigations will be conducted in this case."

Heading: Wide angle - Indian Express
Content:
Rituparno Ghosh on The Last Lear and his reasons for casting Amitabh Bachchan for the movie

What inspired you to do The Last Lear?
I grew up seeing Utpal Dutt's Bengali play—Aajker Shahjahan and I've loved it since my school days. I was inspired by the storyline of the play, which revolves around a veteran Shakespearean actor—Harish Mishra played by Amitabh Bachchan, who is wooed by a movie director (Arjun Rampal) to act in his first film. The film explores Shakespeare's influence on the actor's life.

Is it a tribute to Utpal Dutt? Do you think he has got his dues?
He was one of the finest actors Indian cinema had. Unfortunately as a playwright, his identity did not go beyond West Bengal. He has done a lot of Shakespearean plays. I wanted the nation to realise his talent as a playwright. Hence I made this film. It is also sheer co-incidence that Amitabh Bachchan's first movie had Utpal Dutt in it.

Is the movie's title, The Last Lear, inspired by the great play?
The name is not linked to the play but Bachchan's ironic old man image of the character.

When a great script and storyline could make castmovie a blockbuster, why take big stars like Bachchan and Preity Zinta?
I chose Bachchan as his personality reflects the character and fits the role perfectly. I don't make movies eyeing box-office success.

This is your first movie with Bachchan. How was the experience?
His understanding of the entire environment was extremely fascinating and the moment he entered the sets, he made everyone very comfortable, adjusting beautifully with the rest of the crew.
