Why did the movie take this long to release considering it was made last year?
My producers planned it this way. The movie did the rounds of the festivals. Now that my job is over, I am looking at the project objectively. If I had seen it when it was made, then I would have looked at the project with a critical eye. So in a way, it is good that I am distant from the movie at this moment.

What challenges did you face while adapting a play into a film?
I didn't face any difficulties since I have made movies based on novels.

Are you apprehensive about the recent controversies around the release of movies in multiplexes in Mumbai?
It is a very impulsive reaction, and I wouldn't wish movies to get undue publicity from any kind of cause or issue and vice versa.

Tell us about your next project Sunglasses starring Jaya Bachchan.
It is in the post-production stage now and that's all I can give away at the moment.

Heading: CNG for city before CYG takes off - Indian Express
Content:
Dehu Road resident procures card for Rs 2,000 from Nigdi rationing office; officials call it fake but probe is ordered

If you are in Pune, you can apaprently get a ration card issued even in the name of the Chief Minister and his family members. Sanjay Jayram Dhutadmal, a resident of Dehu Road, is the "proud owner" of one such ration card purportedly issued by the rationing office at Nigdi, last month. Dhutadmal claims that he procured the ration card in the name of the chief minister by paying Rs 2,000 and without any hassles.

Officials at the rationing office in Nigdi however say they never issued the ration card and it was not genuine. While Dhutadmal and the officials trade charges, one thing is certain, the divisional commissionerate here has swung into action: to find out whether a bogus ration card racket flourishes in the city.

The matter came to light on Tuesday when Dhutadmal, who calls himself a civic activist, approached Divisional Commissioner Nitin Kareer seeking action against the authorities at the rationing office for allegedly issuing a ration card by "accepting a bribe." Kareer has initiated an inquiry into the matter.

"We will conduct a proper investigation into the case. Those found guility will be punished," Kareer said. "There is also a possibility that Dhutadmal might have prepared a bogus ration card in the name of chief minister from somewhere else. If Dhutadmal is found to be the culprit, it will help us in exposing bogus ration card racket."

Dhutadmal said that he got the ration card in the name of the chief mininster in a bid to prove that corruption exists at the rationing office.

"My ration card had become old and was in a bad shape. So I went to the zonal rationing office "A" division at Nigdi on August 7 for obtaining a duplicate ration card. The employees there asked me to bring an affidavit. I told them that affidavit was required only if the ration card was lost. Since I wanted a duplicate ration card on submission of the older one, the affidavit was not required. But the officials refused to heed my pleas," Dhutadmal said.

"A few persons outside the office were murmuring that ration cards are issued without submitting any documents and by paying money to the authorities. Then I decided to expose this racket. ," he added.

" On August 9, I requested zonal rationing office Vaishali Waghmare to give a ration card urgently. She called assistant zonal officer A N More and asked him to give me a ration card. They asked me to pay Rs 2000 and provide the names of my family members and myself and the address for the ration card. I purposely gave the names of Chief Minister Vilas Dagduji Deshumukh, his wife Vaishali and sons Amit, Ritesh and Bunti on a Nigdi-Pradhikaran address," he alleged.

"Since I paid the money, the authorities did not ask for any documents. They issued the ration card carrying the names of Chief Minister and his family members," he added.

When contacted, Waghmare said, "We have not issued any ration card to Dhutadmal. We have

also filed a complaint application against him at Nigdi police station on September 1 for preparing a bogus ration card in the name of Chief Minister."

His subordinate, More, also said that allegation made by Dhutadmal are baseless. "Dhutadmal has got some bogus ration card and now he is blackmailing me," said More. The issue of bogus ration card is not new to the city. Even the Pakistani spy Sayeed Desai, who was arrested in Pune, had a fake

ration card.

Heading: Baner-Balewadi DP: Changes few and far - Indian Express
Content:
Army hurdle over, natural gas by first week of October

Pune is all set to get piped Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) in time for the Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG).

With the Army having given clearance for the Dehu Road stretch of the pipeline project, Gas Authority of India Limited (GAIL) and Maharashtra Natural Gas Limited (MNGL) are hopeful that 50 city buses would be able to run on CNG by October, as scheduled.

"We are optimistic that CNG would be available by the first week of October," said Shama Sunder, managing director, MNGL. Fifty CNG buses were proposed for the CYG in tune with the Games' theme of going green.

Pune is tapping into the existing main CNG pipeline from Dahej (Gujarat) to the Dabhol project-Ratnagiri, at Panvel. GAIL is constructing the 66 km stretch from Panvel to Pune, which is complete except for a stretch in defence premises at the Ordinance Factory in Dehu Road. The Army had raised doubts about the viability of the pipeline due to safety concerns.

But on Tuesday, Pune sub area commander Brig R J Sharma said all concerns had been taken care of. "The issue was resolved more than a week ago. There were some objections with regard to the safety of the pipeline, but that has been solved," he said.

A senior GAIL officer said the work on the pipeline had resumed. "We expect the work to be finished unless rains interfere," he said.

Even if the pipeline work is held up, Pune Mahanagar Parivahan Mahamandal Limited (PMPML) is certain of CNG supply. "It was decided at a meeting last week that our distributors, Maharashtra Natural Gas Limited (MNGL), would transport CNG via cylinders, if the pipeline is not laid in time. Either ways, CNG buses would run in time for CYG," said PMPML chairman and managing director S B Patil.

According to the officer from GAIL, CNG has been procured in cylinder using other means of transport in areas where pipeline facility is unavailable. "But it will be more expensive. The commercial aspects like who will bear the additional cost will have to be discussed between the parties involved," he said.

Once the pipeline is complete, buses would be expected to come to MNGL's Chinchwad mother station for fuel. However, six CNG pumps have been identified across the city, but they will not be operational by October. They would be functional only in next year, an MNGL officer said.

The CNG equipped buses is being supplied by Ashok Leyland and will be available by the first week of October, Patil said. The Gas Authority of India Limited (GAIL) and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) have formed a joint venture company, MNGL, to distribute CNG in the state.

Heading: Take cash from us, buy uniforms: PMC to students - Indian Express
Content:
Half of the 44 modifications fall in non-substantial category, and will be brought for public scrutiny: Govt

Even as objections and suggestions have been sought on the modifications in the development plan (DP) for Baner-Balewadi, the state government has claimed that around half of the 44 modifications fall in non-substantial category and would be brought for public scrutiny along with those substantial ones. However, various organisations that raised the issue have rejected the state government claim, arguing that the modifications are substantial.

There are a total of 44 modifications in the Unit One of the DP for Baner-Balewadi and the review meeting called before publishing the notification for seeking objections and suggestions has enlisted that 20 of them are non-substantial changes while a few fall in both substantial as well as non-substantial categories.

"The state government is suppose to seek objections and suggestions for the substantial changes in the DP for Baner-Balewadi, but the same would be done for non-substantial modifications to make the entire process transparent," official sources said.

Going by the applied criteria, the modifications of more than 10 per cent of land in reservation is termed as "substantial" while less than that falls in non-substantial category.

"Thus, there is less than 10 per cent of changes in most of the 44 modifications made by the state government," officials said, adding, the citizens would themselves get to know about them after the maps are made available for seeking objections and suggestions. The maps will be made available at the Deputy Director, Town Planning office and also at Pune Municipal Corporation headquarters.

The idea behind putting all the modifications for seeking objections and suggestions is to bring in more transparency in the finalisation of DP, he said.

Aneeta Beninger, executive director, Centre for Development Studies and Activities, rejected the state government claim, saying there have been substantial modifications to convert huge land for residential purpose.

"The state government modifications are substantial and the truth will emerge after the maps are made available for public," she said.

Civic officials justified the modifications by the state government, saying that there are no substantial changes and whatever changes have been made are in keeping with the requirement of the area.

The PMC has no role to play in the future process, officials said. "It would only convey the suggestions and objections of the public to the state government."

The civic body had sent the draft DP of 23 villages to state government for final approval. The state government decided to divide it into ten units and began the approval process in January this year by approving the Unit One for Baner-Balewadi with modifications.

Heading: 74 years on, new dawn at Prabhat Talkies: Call and book your seat - Indian Express
Content:
Admitting that there have been irregularities in the purchase of the school uniforms and other school material, the Pune Municipal Corporation finally decided to give cash amount in the form of demand drafts or cheques to civic school children for purchasing the school uniforms on their own this year. The civic administration also decided to initiate a departmental inquiry against the education officer of the school board, Sudhakar Tambe, as he has been found "responsible" for these irregularities.

Municipal Commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi and additional commissioner Machhindranath Devnikar told this to mediapersons on Tuesday. Following complaints regarding the irregularities, the PMC had appointed an inquiry committee headed by deputy commissioner Suraj Mandhare, gave its recommendations to commissioner. The PMC has decided to take action as per the committee recommendations.

Pardeshi said, "The committee has found that there have been irregularities in the purchase of uniforms and other items. It has also been found that the school board has also violated the necessary tender procedures. Therefore, we have taken a decision to scrap the whole tender procedure for the current year."

"However, starting the tender procedure all over again would mean that students would not be able to get the uniforms in time, as the re-tendering procedure would take another 4 to 6 months. Therefore, as far as three items including school uniforms, shoes and socks, are concerned, we have decided to give students cash amount instead to buy that. This cash will be in the form of demand drafts or cheques, will be given to the school authorities," Pardeshi said adding, "These payments would be made in two installments. While the first installment would be sixty per cent of the total amount, the remaining forty per cent amount would only be made, once the students produce evidence that they have really purchased the uniforms as per the specifications."

Clarifying that the PMC has not yet taken any action against the education officer, Devnikar said, "A departmental inquiry will be initiated against the education officer. We will also write to the state education department as well as the Urban Development department, which will decide, what further action should be taken against the education officer. Regarding the other members of the school board involved in this, a report would be tabled in the general body meeting, which will take a decision."

On the purchase of other school material, including note-books and slates, they said, "Since these items have already been purchased and distributed amongst the school children, the prices of these items would be tallied to check whether they are as per the wholesale market rates, and accordingly the contractor would receive payments."

The committee has also recommended appointment of a committee with accountant and other experts on it, who would handle the tender procedures for the school board in future.

Heading: Technical hitch blocks rollout of 70 new academic courses - Indian Express
Content:
For the last 25 years, the theatre has screened only Marathi movies of which Maherchi Sadi ran for a consecutive 100 weeks

Prabhat Talkies, one of the oldest theatres in the city at Appa Balwant Chowk in Shaniwar Peth, which is still housed in the same structure built 74 years ago, has now stepped into a new mode with introduction of telephone booking for its customers. Interestingly, the theatre where the tickets are still in the range of Rs 20 to 40, telephone booking is not going to burden the customer with any extra charge.

Prabaht Talkies is completing 74 years on September 21. On the occasion of stepping into 75 th year, the theatre has come up with the new scheme. "The customer will have to purchase a card for Rs 150 for availing telephone booking facility. The card will have a password that the customer will have to reveal while booking ticket telephonically," said Vivek Damle, director, Prabhat Theatres Private Limited.

"The card is usable for lifetime and there will be no extra charge while booking tickets. The owner will also have a choice to transfer the card into spouse's or descendant's name," he added. The owners of the theatre are also planning to renovate the theatre by making it air-conditioned and changing interiors.

The place where Prabaht Talkies stands has a historical importance. Up to 1926, there was a wada owned by Sardar Kibe. It used to house office and press of one of the oldest newspapers of Maharashtra, "Daily Dnyanprakash." On May 25, 1926, the wada was ravaged by a fire. In 1934, Kibes, owners of the land built Kibe Laxmi Theatre here.

The famous Prabhat Film Company and its distributors Famous Pictures took over the management in the same year and from then it became Prabhat Talkies. The theatre had a "cry box" for babies and their mothers so that the crying babies could not distract the other viewers. The cry box was a talk of town then.

Low ticket rates is another feature of the theatre. Presently, when the multiplexes and other single screen theatres in the city are charging anything between Rs 60 to Rs 200, the maximum ticket rate for balcony for a regular show in Prabaht Talkies is not more than Rs 40. "We are not at all planning to increase the rates in near future," said Damle. The theatre has a seating capacity of 894.

The theatre has so far shown over 900 Hindi, Marathi and English films. The first film it screened was "Love Me Tonight" on August 21, 1934. For the last 25 years, the theatre has screened only Marathi movies of which "Maherchi Sadi" ran for consecutive 100 weeks in the theatre. It was a record. As many as 43 films celebrated silver jubilee stay at the theatre, the latest one being a Marathi movie "Kadachit."

"Presently, we can show 12 to 15 Marathi films in a year that use to run successfully. There is not a single occasion in the last 74 years, where a show had to be cancelled because of least number of viewers," said Damle. Damle also mentioned that the company was planning to publish a handbook on the history of the theatre.

Anniversary stamp
The Prabhat Theatres Private Limited had applied to the government for publishing a stamp on the occasion of entering into 75 th year. "So far we have not got any response from the government. We are not going to push it again as we think that the government should recognise the importance of the history of such places on their own," said Damle.

Heading: Cops: immersion points to be increased - Indian Express
Content:
As many as 49 colleges in the district that were given permission to start around 70 courses by the state government may find it tough to get going in this academic year. As the nod for these courses came only in August, none of these colleges would be able to fulfill the criterion of completing 90 working days in the term ending October 31.

The state government has given permission to these colleges to start MBA, MCM, BBA, BFT, MCA and some post-graduate diploma courses in management after August 1. While some of these colleges are already affiliated to the University of Pune, many others are still to get affiliation.

According to a circular issued by the university, the first term for most of the courses concludes on October 31. "It is mandatory to complete 90 working days for the first term as per the guidelines in an ordinance issued by the university. As the courses have been given permission after August 1, the criterion would not be fulfilled if the courses get started this academic year," said a member of senate of the UoP.

He said the issue was discussed in the sub-committee of academic council and the sub-committee had decided not give permission to these courses for this academic year. "As it is difficult to complete 90 working days in this term, the sub-committee had decided not to give a go ahead to the courses this year," he said.

However, the sub-committee is not the final authority to cancel the permission for the new courses to the colleges.

Although it is clear that the colleges would be unable to complete 90 working days in the term, the university has set up local inquiry committees to verify the same.

"The committees will decide whether the courses could be started from this academic year or not," said Pandit Vidyasagar, director, board of colleges and university development.

The local committees are set up every year and are given the responsibility of inspecting infrastructure, faculty strength and other related aspects in the colleges.

These committees make recommendations about giving affiliation or permission to start new courses. Incidentally, the sub-committee of academic council had passed a resolution last week to not send these committees to these colleges as it was clear that the colleges would be unable to complete 90 days in the first term.

Heading: Symposium on biotech in plant disease management - Indian Express
Content:
Enthused by this year's early completion of the Ganesh immersion procession, the city police have planned to increase the number of immersion points from next year and suggest route diversions to Ganesh mandals so that the procession time is reduced by five hours.

The police have proposed two more roads for the immersion processions. Henceforth, they will pass from Shastri Road to Dandekar bridge and the immersion procession will end near the bridge at Poona hospital. Likewise, Ganesh processions will also take the route of Jangli Maharaj Road to Wadarwadi to Dnyaneshwar Paduka Chowk and end at new Ganesh immersion point suggested by the police.

This year, a lot of Ganesh mandals cooperated with us and followed the guidelines told to them. But a few did not cooperate as per our expectations," said police commissioner Satyapal Singh.

"We also got calls warning us about threats to security during the Ganesh immersion procession. We also received information from sources regarding security issues," Singh said.When asked how people cooperated with the police during the procession, Singh said, "Because of the efforts taken by the police, people are alert now. We thank the people of Pune for being alert and informing us whenever they suspected anything" Joint Commissioner Ranjendra Sonavne said that this year, the immersion procession was over within twenty-five hours and the police could also reduce procession time of various mandals.

According to Singh, the police have taken action against some people and mandals which flouted rules." This year, police had employed camerapersons at various roads in the city to record the immersion procession. Singh said the police would study the data recorded, which would help them to manage crowds better in future.

Suggestions
*Two more roads proposed for immersion procession
*Route modifications will be suggested to mandals

Heading: UNEP’s special programme to create awareness on ozone depletion - Indian Express
Content:
A National symposium on 'Biotechnology in plant disease management for sustainable crop protection' will be held at the Agharkar Research Institute on September 17 and 18.

The symposium is organised jointly by the MACS' Agharkar Research Institute and Indian Phytopathological Society.

The symposium aims at bringing together relevant information on some of the aspects of biotechnology in relation to sustained crop protection through management of plant diseases and pests.

It will focus on the biological approaches to major crop diseases and pests - biodiversity, taxonomy and conservation of plant pathogens, plant associated microbes for biotechnology applications, biocontrol of plant diseases and insect pests and enhanced crop productivity through biotechnology (mycorrhiza, PGP bacteria, biofertilizers etc.)

The symposium will be inaugurated by Dr TM Manjunath, Consultant, Agri-Biotechnology and IPM and Former Director, Monsanto Research Centre, Bengaluru.

The symposium will also have talks by eminent speakers like Dr C Manoharachary, Dr RK Verma, Dr DV Singh, Dr K Acharya, Dr RN Kharwar, Dr SK Singh, Dr LV Gangawane, Dr RV Vyas, Dr MV Deshpande, Dr Pratibha Sharma and Dr Absar Ahmad.

Heading: Symantec to strengthen sales network; focus more on data loss prevention - Indian Express
Content:
The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and Pune Zilla Parishad Secondary School Section will hold a special programme to celebrate the International Day for the Preservation of Ozone Layer on Wednesday.

An educational tool for creating awareness about Ozone depletion and climate change among students will be launched on the occasion.

The UNEP had already created an educational tool for the primary students. It consists of a story in which a character named Ozzy tells the story of Ozone depletion and climate change. It has already been translated into Marathi, Hindi, Urdu and Bengali. The tool is available in the form of books and CDs.

"The new tool is for the students of secondary level," said Vineeta Apte, reviewer of the UNEP's educational tool. "It is in English, but we are planning to translate it to other regional languages if we get co-sponsor," she said.

"The new tool is also easy to understand in which Ozzy, the central character meets his girlfriend Zoe. The idea is to make the subjects like ozone depletion and climate change understandable for school children," added Apte. She said that the UNEP was trying to spread the message on climate change across the world and wanted to educate school children about it. "The same programme will be arranged in Mumbai too on Tuesday," said Apte.

The programme will be conducted at the New English School, Ramanbaug, where principals of various schools in the city will be present.

Prakash Parab, district secondary education officer and R Gopichandran of Centre for Environment Education, Ahmedabad will be chief guests.

Heading: ‘We’ll strike if quota system for diesel supply not removed’ - Indian Express
Content:
Symantec Software India Private Limited, providing security, storage and systems management solutions is focusing on increasing its sales in the country, particularly in the Data Loss Prevention (DLP) segment — the security solution for organisations.

Michael Wolfe, vice president, DLP solutions, Symantec said a dedicated team of employees had been assigned to carry out the sales operations in the country. He said customer data loss was a major threat that Indian companies want to prevent. "In India it is seen that customer data is more important than the employee data since there are lot of Indian companies that handle it,'' he added.

Symantec has now six products, Vontu-Network Discover, Network Protect, Endpoint Discover, Endpoint Prevent, Network Monitor, and Network Prevent to address the security concerns of organisations.

Wolfe, co-founder of Vontu, said data loss is the biggest security issue as it involves organisations' critical information assets. "Data loss is not just an IT problem, it is a business issue. Still young, more organisations are now turning to DLP since they understand value proposition," he said.

In India, organisations from the IT, finance, and health are opting for the DLP solution and Symantec estimates to increase the volume of sales in the coming days.

Some of the features of Vontu is to prevent employees from copying source code to USB device, scan laptops and prioritise encryption efforts, find product design documents, prevent employees from burning DVDs and use automated on-screen notifications to educate employees on the need to protect confidential data.

Heading: Bank of Maharashtra announces three new schemes - Indian Express
Content:
No other city in the country has a quota system for diesel supply, said Pune district Petrol Dealers Association president Baba Dhumal. The association has threatened a two-day fuel strike if no action is taken in the next eight days.

"We have written to all the three major oil companies, the district Collectorate and the union ministry but we have not heard from them. All petrol pumps here are reporting a shortage in diesel supply," he said.

With the fall of price for crude oil in the International market, a member of the association said that the three companies ought to be able to increase the diesel supply.

"In the last month, the price of a barrel crude oil has fallen substantially. Oil companies can remove the quota system and increase the supply now," said a member of the association. Meanwhile, fuel shortage continued to haunt commuters at Samarth petrol pump in Bhosari. This pump on the Pune Nashik Highway catering to commuters from PCMC and Bhosari heading towards Nashik needs about 20,000 litres of diesel in a day. Of late, they have been putting up a board saying 'no fuel'.

"We get only 10,000 litres a day, which gets finished between 7 am and 11 pm," said the owner. The petrol dealers' association said that the supply was normal. "The pump owner might have finished off his quota in advance, because of which he is facing a shortage. It is true that there has been a chronic gap between demand and supply in the past few months," said a member of the association. Two weeks ago, the Loni terminal, which is the node for all fuel supply to the city, developed a technical snag, which resulted in some delay in procuring diesel to the city. However, since June-July, diesel has been on ration across Pune and Pimpri Chinchwad - one reason being the high international crude oil prices, which saw a decline only this month.

Heading: Hooligans on the prowl in Kalyaninagar:  damage 15 cars, cops make no arrests - Indian Express
Content:
The Bank of Maharashtra on Tuesday announced three new schemes, including Mahasaraswati Scheme for minors, on its 74th Foundation Day.

"A special scheme inculcating saving habits among minors was launched for those who have attained the age of ten years and above. The student should open a savings account and an account in Mahasaraswati, which will enable them to get the benefit of free International Visa ATM-cum-Debit Card," Allen C A Pereira, Chairman and Managing Director, Bank of Maharashtra, said in a press conference.

The Mahasaraswati account can be opened in monthly installment with minimum of Rs 50 and Rs 100 in rural and urban area respectively and deposit in multiple of Rs 10 thereafter for minimum period of 36 months and maximum period of 120 months. The scheme shall carry rate of interest as that of regular term deposit scheme.

The main benefit of the scheme is that the investor will be preferred customer for the educational loan scheme to meet any of their future needs of funds for their higher education with concession. The minor account holder will also be entitled for the free accident insurance cover of Rs 50,000 for every year till the maturity of the deposit.

The bank also launched Drive-in Banking facility that provides free valet parking facility at its main branch in Pune and the valued customers of any branch of the bank in Pune can undertake their banking transactions at the Pune main branch.

The bank has also started Internet banking, SMS banking and phone banking facility for its customers. For the NRI customers, the bank launched the Maha-Bharati-NRI Services that would focus on increasing its NRI deposit base by providing quality service.

Heading: Lifetime achievement award for Dajikaka Gadgil of PNG - Indian Express
Content:
The residents of Kalyaninagar are worried about the rising incidents of hooliganism in the area. On the night of September 13 hooligans spray painted around 15 cars causing damage of around Rs 5000 to each car.

The citizens had filed complaints at Ramwadi police chowky, which comes under the jurisdiction of Yerawada Police Station. While Yerawada police confirmed receiving the complaints, no one has been arrested in the case so far.

"The incident happened in the night between 11 pm and 5 am. Around 15 cars in the area were spray painted with some slogans," said a citizen.

The incidents took place at street no. 12, 13 and 14. The cars were parked outside the apartments.

"The apartments don't have enough parking space and the citizens have to park their vehicles on road. Hooligans took advantage of it," said another citizen. He also added that the apartments did not have watchmen to guard vehicles.

The citizens also said that the incidents of hooliganism were increasing in the area.

"The area needs a proper patrolling as the incidents like petrol as well as vehicle thefts are on rise," they said.

Heading: CYG to celebrate ‘sustainable transport week’ - Indian Express
Content:
Dajikaka Gadgil, one of the founders of P N Gadgil & Co, has been awarded 'Lifetime achievement in the field of bullion trade' by The Bombay bullion Association Limited. The award has been bestowned on Dajikaka for his contribution in the field of bullion trade, the promotion of the associate dealers in general and the Bombay bullion association in particular. PNG has recently opened a branch in California, USA.

"The stature of the 175-year-old PNG brand stands tall on the firm foundation of trust, built over the years by Dajikaka. His vision led PNG jewelers to Pune half a century ago and the rest is history. Today PNG shares a beautiful bond of love and trust with the Puneites. Dajikaka has been on the forefront throughout this progress," said a press release.

Heading: Combating Pancreatic cancer - Indian Express
Content:
Four days after the blast at Pune Municipal Corporation's (PMC) biomedical waste disposal plant in Kailash crematorium premises, Municipal Commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi said the corporation has asked Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) approved Passco Environment Solutions Limited to operate the plant.

The incinerator will start functioning from Wednesday. The PMC disposed the hospital waste generated on September 12 and 13 at Pimpri-Chinchwad plant. "However the capacity of the plant is falling short of 800 kg. Therefore, we had requested the MPCB to permit us to assign Passco Environment Solutions Limited to temporarily run the incinerator in Pune," said PMC additional commissioner Machhindranath Devniker.

Meanwhile, leader of opposition Vikas Mathkari has criticised the PMC for not lodging a police complaint against the contractor Sunil Singhania for misusing PMC resources. "The illegal godown that stocked aerosol cans is barely five feet away from the crematorium run on diesel. Also, the first contract with Image India Limited in 2000 was done on stamp paper. However, in 2006, the company changed its name to Sun Enviro Management Private Limited and the contract was done on plain paper. The changes between the two contracts were not put before the standing committee or the general body for approval," he said in a press meet.

Mathkari added that he has proofs that industrial waste from Avon Products Limited in Bhiwandi and six other companies was being disposed off at this incinerator. He further alleged that the plant was not being run at the mandatory temperature of 850 degree Celsius and the partially burnt waste was directly let out in the river. Mathkari has demanded that the PMC should immediately file a complaint against the contractor of the plant. Pardeshi has issued orders to terminate the contract with Sunil Singhania following Singhania's arrest.

Heading: Health Corner - Indian Express
Content:
A website on pancreatic cancer promises more awareness and aims to put a check on the rising incidence of this form of cancer in India

Pancreatic Cancer is ranked fifth in the cause of cancer related deaths in USA and is seen in increasing numbers at tertiary cancer centres in India.

To combat the threat by spreading awareness, Asia'a first website that informs about pancreatic and peri ampullary cancer — www.pancreaticcancerindia.com — has been launched. It aims at providing a comprehensive platform and building awareness on pancreatic cancer and periampullary tumours among patients, care givers and health care professionals.

This website will provide a novel forum to patients and the pancreatic cancer medical community in India. This will enable pancreatologists, oncologists, general practitioners, radiologists, pathologists, palliative specialists, nurses, patients and families to interact freely with each other about their concerns. It will also provide them up-to-date and locally relevant information on various aspects of pancreatic and peri-ampullary cancer.

Dr K A Dinshaw, director, Tata Memorial Centre, launched the website.

Pancreaticcancerindia.com is the brain child of pancreatic cancer specialists from the Tata Memorial Hospital, Mumbai and Sir Gangaram Hospital, New Delhi. Dr Shailesh V Shrikhande, Dr Sudeep Gupta and Dr Umesh Mahantshetty, from the Tata Memorial Hospital and Dr Shyam Aggarwal and Dr Adarsh Chaudhary, from Sir Gangaram Hospital are multidisciplinary specialists in Oncology and belong to different regions of India but share a keen common interest in research and management of pancreatic cancer.

Dr Shrikhande, associate professor and consultant surgeon, Gastrointestinal and Hepato-Biliary-Pancreatic Surgery, Tata Memorial Hospital said, "The annual pancreatic cancer load of India is likely to increase in the near future because of the increase in older population. The situation calls for a need of multicentric studies, more systematic approach to document outcomes at all levels and identify potentially preventable risk factors associated with pancreatic cancer in India."

"There is a need for improving knowledge and awareness of this disease among healthcare professionals and general population. This website will bridge this void in our country. With the availability of advanced technology in India, our effort is to create awareness towards significantly improving the treatment outcomes, the doctors said.

"The pattern of pancreatic cancer is different in our country. This is most likely the result of demographic structure of our population that is still predominately young. There is a lack of palliative and end-life-support to the patients, which is very important in a fatal disease like this," says Dr Shyam Aggarwal, hon. senior consultant and chairman, Department of Medical Oncology, Sir Gangaram Hospital.

The website has started its journey as an information and interaction resource. The information will include diagnosis, staging, surgery, chemotherapy, radiation therapy, palliative care, nursing issues, targeted therapies, clinical trials, translational and basic research. There will be sections dedicated to patient and professionals.

Heading: Cold & clue - Indian Express

Back to yogic ways

According to researchers, regular consumption of the formulation is set to offer positive results within a span of a fortnight. Heading: Jigrr visits MMCC - Indian Express
Content:
Home remedies and a little precaution will keep your children away from cold and cough that are so common these days

With yet another spell of monsoon, children are again prone to cold related ailments. However, certain precautions and care at home can avoid further snag. City doctors recommend different measures to aid a child recover.

"Warm water with honey is the best preparation. However there are three types of colds — dry cough, wet cough and cough with chest congestion. For dry cough use suppressants like codeine, dextrometharphan. In case of chest congestion and associated whizzing we recommend broncho dilator and salbutamol and if it is wet cough then the best way to remove the expectorant is light chest tapping. The patient should also be kept away from dust, smoke, pollen and other allergic elements," says Dr Pramod Jog, professor of pediatrics at DY Patil Medical College.

Dr Jayant Naurange, pediatric, says, "Precaution is anyday better than cure. In the first place, an enclosed area should be avoided. Keep the child dry and warm. It is very important that the child is examined before being medicated and should be given a decongestant medicine during the initial stages. Pseudo ethidrine and anti cold preparations are recommended. Parents can wait up to three days and if minor sneezing is observed then medication might not be needed. However if there is fast breathing, vomiting or even slight fever they should immediately consult the doctor."

Dr Avinash Bhondwe president of Indian Medical Association, Pune branch suggests that cold, in any case takes at least seven days to cure completely.

"The most important thing is a balanced diet. Cold drinks, foods with preservatives, curd should be avoided and hot soup and fresh food should be given. Steam inhalation is important along with hot fomentation during cold. The child should also be kept away from cold air and congested areas. However if the child is not showing symptoms of fever, cough or restlessness it is not at all necessary to consult a doctor. Basic measures and care should cure the child," he adds.

Heading: Inter-dist badminton tournament - Indian Express
Content:
In view of the inter-school PSAA touch rugby tournament, which is scheduled to be held in January 2009, a rugby PT clinic will be organised from mid October. Since most kids are unfamiliar with the basic rules of rugby, PT clinics will be organised to teach them the tactics and strategies of the sport.

Selected coaches will be instructed by Surhud Khare, an International Rugby Board (IRB) level one coach, Swapneel Khare, President of Khare's Football and Rugby Academy (KFANDRA) and by members of the Pune District Rugby and Football Association (PDRFA). They will in turn conduct camps in the selected schools and teach the kids, the basics of rugby. The clinic will include an intensive lecture on the ins and outs of the sport through the Audio Visual medium. The coaches will also speak about the Rugby Ready Programme which elucidates the safety and ethos of this sport. This programme will show the kids the difference between fitness in rugby and fitness in other sports and the importance of technique, tackling and mental toughness.

The equipment and material for these clinics will be provided KFANDRA and the PDRFA. "The kids will not be expected to pay any fee, thanks to the financial backing of Kai Taraporevala," said Khare. Kai Taraporevala is the co-founder of India Advisory Partners (IAP), a Mumbai and London-based corporate finance advisory group committed to helping international companies in India. He is an active member of the INSEAD's rugby team and also a sponsor of rugby in India.

"Also providing invaluable advice is David Wiggins-ex India and British army coach and a keen follower of Pune Rugby," Khare said. For now, these clinics are scheduled to take place in three schools - Vikhe Patil, St. Vincent's and Anglo Urdu School, with the help of the coaches of these schools, Ashok Gunjal, Wilson Andrews and Majid Shaikh. Khare will supervise the work of the instructors.

A major boost coming from this tournament is that each participating player will be registered with the Indian Rugby Football Union (IRFU) and the Western Indian Rugby

Football Union (WIRFU) database. The IRFU is working on a national insurance policy for all registered players. They would then be covered for any major injury in the future. With this, the burden of medical expense will be lifted off the parents' shoulders. Expressing his desire for the process to run smoothly, Khare said, "It is about time that the image of rugby as a dangerous sport is erased. It is a tough sport and requires high standards of fitness and strength but it also teaches courage, discipline, morals and camaraderie."

"These are values we should look at inculcating in all our school kids. We must keep in mind that touch rugby is nothing but a step towards contact rugby," he added.

Heading: Terror translated: Agarbattiwala scripted Mumbai plot in Gujarati - Indian Express
Content:
The community holds nearly 35-40 % share in India's equity market

The mayhem in the global and domestic markets has scared away even the most die-hard investor — the Gujaratis.

The investor community in Gujarat seems to have vanished. The bravehearts who are still there in the market are trading, and not investing.

According to an estimate, the Gujarati investor has 35-40 per cent share in the equity markets in India. Considering this, Gujaratis have taken the blow of Hurricane Lehman on their chin. Interestingly, despite sound domestic fundamentals, the existing investor sentiments in Gujarat are such that any downward movement in the market results in heavy sell-outs.

The state's wary investor expects the downward trend to continue for the next two months. According to Ahmedabad-based stockbroker, Ashish Shah of the Wealth First securities: "Since January, the investor is suffering due to the the downslide in the markets. There was some relief in August, but that did not last long and the markets kept sliding down."

In January, even small investors were on an investing spree on the back of the bull run. But the international factors have washed away much of their wealth. This has made them apprehensive and cautious about investing in the markets.

There was a time when Gujaratis invested heavily in the stock markets in January with the state registering a record demat accounts in the IPO era.

Ahmedabad-based broking houses recorded remarkable intra-day volumes of at least Rs 1 crore per day per terminal. This has come down to a miniscule Rs 5-10 lakh now. According to a broker in Ahmedabad, their earnings have reduced to 30 per cent of what they used to have in January.

K K Mishra, Managing Director of the Ahmedabad Stock Exchange, said: "This is an opportunity to invest in stocks. But the investor is panicky about investing in the uncertain market. The trend will continue till a major positive correction comes through."

It is not just the small investor who is troubled with this uncertain market scenario. The big investor, especially the High Net worth Individuals (HNI) too, has burnt his fingers in the current upheavals in the markets. One such Ahmedabad based HNI, Meet Desai, said the global economic condition is uncertain and so is the market. "Everyone feels that it is beneficial to buy stocks at current levels, but at the same time, it is uncertain to predict the market movements. The feeling of fear has become dominant over the greed to earn more profits," he said.

K Sethuraman, AVP, Alankit Assignments Ltd said: "Some upward movement can be predicted but overall, the slump will continue for at least two months. However, some sectors will yield good results such as power, infrastructure and exports."

Heading: Modi’s return gift: A trainful of relief for marooned Bihar - Indian Express
Content:
The DCB had recovered a plastic bag from the Sidi Saiyed Mosque well, containing a register with details of the police investigation into the Mumbai blasts in Gujarati language, a training manual for terror camps across the country and police interrogation techniques including details about narco test

The report about the Mumbai serial train blasts investigation was originally prepared by one of the accused in Hindi and then translated into Gujarati by Usman Agarbattiwala, an accused in the July 26 Ahmedabad serial blasts, it has been learnt.

The Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) had recovered the report and other incriminating literature from the well of the Sidi Saiyed Mosque Complex in Lal Darwaja area on September 1.

On a tip-off, the DCB had recovered a plastic bag from the well, containing a register with the details of the police investigation into the Mumbai blasts in Gujarati language, a training manual for the terror camps across the country and police interrogation techniques including the details about narco analysis test.

Ashish Bhatia, Joint Commissioner of Police, DCB, said: "The report was originally prepared by Ehtesham Siddiqui, an accused in the Mumbai blasts and a SIMI leader from Maharashtra, during his stay in the Arthur Road Jail. He had provided the same to SIMI ideologue Safdar Nagori."

Bhatia said it is yet to become clear how Siddiqui conveyed the report to Nagori who in turn circulated it among the SIMI cadre.

"The information came to light during the interrogation of the accused who have now been arrested," he said.

Heading: Modi’s b’day special to ferry relief to 50,000 Bihar families - Indian Express
Content:
On his birthday, chief minister to flag off a special train full of relief material

Gujarat Chief Minister Narendra Modi will dedicate his birthday to the flood-affected people of Bihar. He will flag off a train full of relief material for the flood-ravaged state from Surat, as he turns 59 on Wednesday.

"Relief goods will include blankets, sarees, utensils and other daily requirements. It will have virtually everything one needs to start life afresh after the devastation caused by the floods," said a top BJP leader.

The chief minister is increasingly looking at the entire country as his canvas, "a reason why he chose to rush in with relief material for Bihar," said the BJP leader.

He added: "After rebuilding Kutch, the chief minister wanted to help them with disaster relief management while rushing in with additional support, but for now, he will stick to the relief materials."

The recently concluded three-day BJP national executive in Bangalore saw Modi making a detailed intervention on internal security and terror apart from the use of IT in mass communication. With his profile enhanced by several notches, he is also set to make appearances elsewhere for his party.

After Modi makes an appearance alongside party's Prime Ministerial candidate L K Advani for an anti-terror rally in Delhi on Friday, more such appearances are being planned.

The BJP's local unit in Gandhinagar is, meanwhile, organising a "Vaidik Shatayu Abhinandana ceremony" to wish him "a long life of 100 years," while other party MLAs will send postcards to Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and demand the approval of GUJCOC. On his 58th birthday last year, Modi had created an all-tribal district of Tapi in Gujarat.

Some goodies for local schoolkids too
The BJP Yuva Morcha has decided to visit the poor areas of all wards and circles across the state and distribute fruits and biscuits to the government school students on the occasion of Chief Minister Narendra Modi's birthday on Wednesday.

The youth wing has also decided to send postcards to Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, asking him to approve the GUJCOC Bill. In the three-day long programme starting Wednesday, the Yuva Morcha is expected to send about 2 lakh post cards to the PM. Arrangements have also been made to put up hoardings in various parts of the city on the occasion of Modi's birthday.

Heading: Uneasy calm in walled city after stone-pelting - Indian Express

Boy hit by police bullet recalls the tense moments during the riots

The bullet lodged in the body of Class X student Shahrukh Mansuri — who was caught in the police firing during the Ganesh visarjan communal flare-up in Vadodara on Monday morning — has finally been removed. Though he is still in the ICU, doctors say his condition is stable.

His father, Saleem Mansuri, who works in the Vadodara district court, said the doctors have assured him that the boy is out of danger. On the other hand, his mother, Rehana, still finds it hard to believe that her son has undergone such a trauma.

Shahrukh Mansuri's only fault that fateful day was that he had stepped out of his house for the Adani supermarket, unaware of the simmering tension in the Fatehpura neighbourhood.

Narrating the sequence of events, this student of Vigyan School in Vadodara said he had gone to supermarket in Fatehpura Char Rasta on Monday morning, when the police opened fire on the rioters who were looting shops in the area.

Shahrukh said: "I had gone to buy vegetables when I met a friend in the market. While we were still talking, we heard gunshots and saw smoke coming out from a temple." Shahrukh said he wanted to rush home quickly and got into a bylane, but saw stones and bricks flying all over. "I was left with no option but to run towards the policemen, when a bullet hit me on the left hand. I never thought that they would open fire on me," he said.

Heading: Heavy rains lash Junagadh,two killed in house collapse - Indian Express
Content:
Petrochemical complex officials seek help from forest department, which says it has no manpower and equipment to tame the terror

The 1,263 acre Reliance Industries Limited (RIL) petrochemical complex in Vadodara is being frequented by some new visitors these days – an army of about 200 Hanuman langurs.

With three RIL employees already been attacked by the primates, terrorised officials have pressed the panic button and sought the intervention of the Forest Department to handle this Herculean task.

Officials at RIL's safety department fear that the langurs might damage the elevated pipelines, which carry highly explosive sensitive petrochemical products like benzene and acrylonitrile. This could cause a major mishap.

There are some elevated pipelines in RIL manufacturing plants, which the simians can easily access, said R K Desai, Safety Head, RIL Manufactures, Vadodara. Though the RIL safety team made several efforts to drive the langurs out, the situation has remained practically the same. The team has now approached the Vadodara Social Forestry Department to deal with the situation.

The forestry department, on the other hand, is in a fix as it does not have enough experts and equipment to drive out and relocate the apes.

Nayan Desai, Deputy Conservator of Forest, Social Forestry, Vadodara district, said: "The Forest Department lacks experts who can handle the langurs."

Forest Department officials said on condition of anonymity that the department does not have enough tranquilliser guns.

Desai, however, added: "We have begun the process of doing a recce in the RIL manufacturing unit by assigning the work to the local Range Forest Officer (RFO)."

In an official communiqué to the Vadodara Social Forestry Department, R K Desai, said: "Ours is a huge petrochemicals complex. The manufacturing of highly sensitive and hazardous petrochemical products is a continuous process in our plants. Even a slightest tempering with such chemicals may lead to a huge explosion, which might affect the nearby villages also.

He added: "Of late, the population of Hanuman langurs in our complex has increased tremendously. They often enter the highly sensitive and hazardous areas of our plants generally in groups of 30. This can cause serious accidents."

Meet the menace:
The Hanuman langur (Semnopithecus antilus) is mainly found in Bangladesh, Bhutan, Myanmar, China, India, Nepal, and Pakistan. This species can subsist in a variety of habitats, including scrublands, rainforests, and cities. It is a fairly terrestrial animal, inhabiting mostly urban areas. It has been named after the mythological Hindu god Hanuman.

Source: M S University (MSU) Zoology Department

Heading: Head of lawyers’ body threatens to resign - Indian Express
Content:
City areas in grip of civic woes; schools remain closed

Torrential rain threw life out of gear in Junagadh district and claimed two more lives on Tuesday.

The first casualty occurred when the wall of an old house collapsed at Kanaja village near Vanthali town. A 65-year-old man identified as Bachu Nathani was buried under the debris and died. In a separate incident, Ramjibhai Tida, a 55-year-old man died after he was buried under the debris of his house.

Heavy rains also led to the collapse of a two-storey abandoned house at Mendarada town. But no casualties were reported.

According to the district flood control room, Junagadh city and Visavadar received 12 inches (300 mm) of rainfall in the last 24 hours ending Tuesday evening. Other areas in the district that received rainfall are Vanthali 215mm, Talala 163mm, Bhesan 146 mm, Mendarada 133mm, Sutrapada 125mm, Keshod 117mm, Manawadar 100mm, Kodinar 95mm, Una 75mm, Veraval 73mm, Maliya 68 mm and Mangarol 23 mm.

The entire district is experiencing heavy rainfall. Almost all the rivers are flooded, with the dams and the check dams overflowing. Heavy rains in the uphill areas have also led to at least one dozen villages in Ghed being marooned. Out of 19 major dams, 10, namely, Hiran -1, Madhuwanti, Zanzeshri, Machhundri, Hasnapur, Ozat (vanthali), Ozat-2, Mota Gujariya, Aanandpur and Ozat (Shapur) are overflowing while the flood gates in five have been opened. They are Hiran-2, Aambajal, Dharaad, Shingoda and Raval.

Several complaints of water-logging were also reported in Junagadh city. According to sources, water-logging occurred at Timbawadi, Madhuram, Aaditya Nagar and Nehri Nagar society area.

Many of the educational institutions remained closed. The city's main thoroughfares also wore a deserted look as people chose to remain indoors.

Junagadh District Collector Aswini Kumar, said: "Some villages in Ghed area are isolated, but we have taken adequate action to meet any eventuality. The situation is under control and no major incidents have been reported so far anywhere in the district. Besides, the administrative machinery is on an alert now," he said.

Torrential rain has been also reported in the Gir and Girnar Forests. But no loss of life to wildlife has been reported so far. Heavy water flow has been reported from the rivers flowing from the forest area.

Heading: SEBI thinks big for small investors - Indian Express
Content:
Gujarat High Court Advocates Association president Yatin Oza has threatened to resign following allegations made by some senior lawyers that he had incorporated 68 names in the voters' list as associated members who were not eligible to vote as per the constitution of the association.

In a note circulated to the association members recently, Oza said he was ready to contest again once the voters' list was revised. "I will send my resignation to the association's vice-president and general secretary and under no circumstance will it be withdrawn," he declared in a circular. Oza was elected president of the association on April 30, 2008.

Making his position clear in the High Court, Oza said the voters' list used in April 2008 elections was not prepared by him, but by former president of the association K J Sethna. "If at all there was any lapse, it was on his and his team's part," Oza said.

Levelling further allegations against Sethna and his team, Oza said it was a "pre-planned and deliberate action" to include the names of associate members in the voters' list by a committee comprising Y S Lakhani, B B Naik, M D Pandya, J R Nanavati and P V Hathi. "It was done at the instance of advocate K J Sethna," he said.

However, all the junior advocates are eligible to cast their vote as they practice in the High Court, he said.

"It is not my fault if the 'objectionists' do not know the junior advocates and refuse to recognise them sitting in an ivory tower," he said.

When contacted, Sethna said the associate members were included in the voters' list by Oza as secretary of the association. "He is just holding empty threats. Let him resign and re-contest," he said.

According to Sethna, only those practicing lawyers are entitled to vote in the association's election who declare in writing that they have not taken part in any of the association's elections.

Heading: Beijing’s good show galvanises Gujarat - Indian Express
Content:
Small, individual investors no longer need to block their hard-earned money in unfruitful Initial Public Offerings (IPOs) while looking for a more profitable one. As per the circulars issued by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), an investor can keep his money and still subscribe to another IPO. The money in his bank account will be transferred to an IPO account only at the time of actual allotment.

The facility has been made available in 18 districts of Gujarat with effect from Monday in accordance with SEBI's circulars issued on July 30 and August 29.

The IPO investors can now avail the advantage of Application Supported by Blocked Amount facility, while keeping money secure in their bank accounts. "Five banks — IDBI, Axis Bank, State Bank of Bikaner and Jaipur, Bank of Baroda and Kotak Mahindra Bank — having branches in

Gujarat, will become eligible to act as Self Certified Syndicate Banks from September 15," said a SEBI order.

When SEBI issued the circulars, only five banks out of the 57 registered with SEBI agreed to offer the facility. HDFC, SBI and ICICI were the first ones to offer the facility to investors of some of the cities.

Heading: Rajkot water woes end as rains return - Indian Express
Content:
State launches medal hunt for 2012 Olympics

Encouraged by the country's performance in the recent Beijing Olympics , the state govt has launched a multi-pronged programme to ensure its participation in the 2012 London Olympics. The project includes the setting up of a world class sports city and a talent hunt at the grassroots to provide scientific training to sportspersons.

"We visited Punjab and Haryana last week to have a firsthand knowledge of the sports facilities there. We have undertaken simultaneous work of mapping sports activities in all the districts at the school level," said Vipul Mitra, state rural development secretary and president of the state table tennis association.

Mitra was in Kutch to attend the foundation laying ceremony of the indoor stadium of the Kutch District TT Association. Incidentally, the Rs 2-crore-project at Adipur is the brainchild of Mitra, who had thought of this a decade ago, while working as the deputy chairman of the Kandla Port Trust.

He said the port town had seen many national level tournaments and had become the state headquarters of TT. Therefore a need was felt to have an indoor stadium of international standards here. He further said that the Sindhu Resettlement Corporation (SRC) had also allotted land for the purpose.

Mitra said the project will give a boost to sports activities in the border district. He said a sports city will be built on 500 acres of land at a cost of Rs 500 crore on the lines of one under construction in Pune and Dubai. He said the ongoing sports mapping project's aim is to identify areas for a particular sports . "Since the tribals of the state are good in archery, it would be the natural choice in such areas. Similarly the game of choice for Saurashtra would be wrestling because the people here are well-built," he said. He added that after identifying the sportspersons, they will be imparted special training to compete in the national and international sports competitions.

Nirmala Gajwani, SRC Chairperson said more projects were in the pipeline for the modernisation of Gandhidham, which was incidentally developed as a new township for the resettlement of refugees from Pakistan in the aftermath of the Partition.

Anjar MLA Nimaben Acharya said that the stadium will not face any funding problems as the post-quake border district was home to many big industrial houses with love for sports.

Heading: Cong leaders to get lessons in media management - Indian Express
Content:
RMC relaxes cuts in drinking water supply to once after every two days, instead of alternate days

Residents of Rajkot city can heave a sigh of relief as the Rajkot Municipal Corporation has decided to relax the water cuts in drinking water supply this Thursday onwards following good rains in the region.

Last month, RMC has imposed alternate day water cuts due to shortage in water.

However, with the city receiving ample rains in the last spell of monsoon, the water cuts have been relaxed to once after every two days.

"We have decided to ease the water cuts from alternate days to once after every two days. We have received enough stock in the last few days. The Nayri-I and II dams are overflowing with fresh rainwater. We decided to relax the restrictions after several discussions and meetings with RMC engineers," said Rajkot Mayor Sandhyaben Vyas.

Vyas said that at present there is 394 MCFT water available in Aji reservoir, 950 MCFT in Nyari-I and 30.10 feet in Bhadar reservoir situated near Jetpur.

"To work according to the new schedule, RMC requires 260 lakh gallons of water per day to provide water supply for 20 minutes. If we draw 100 lakh gallons from Bhadar, 100 lakh gallons from Nyari and the remaining 60 lakh gallons from Narmada source, we will be able to supply water without any problems," Vyas said.

"Aji reservoir water can be used when there is any interruption in any of these regular water sources," she added.

Heading: AMC chosen for Urban Water Award - Indian Express
Content:
With an eye on LS polls, the party to teach its leaders how to win over scribes to get favourable publicity

During the 2007 Assembly elections, the Congress extended Internet connectivity to all its district offices in a bid to provide fast communication between the state headquarters in Ahmedabad and the districts.

The forthcoming Lok Sabha elections will witness another important development. Over 125 Congress leaders from the state to the district and taluka level will be trained in media management. They will be provided training on how to deal with journalists and what information to dole out to them to ensure maximum favourable publicity for the party as well as the candidates in the fray. The training will be imparted to the Congressmen at a two day workshop being organised by the media cell of the All India Congress Committee at Mumbai on September 19 and 20.

Party spokesperson Jayantilal Parmar has already reached Mumbai to make arrangements for the Gujarat delegation. Arjunbhai Modhwadia, the party's chief spokesperson from Gujarat will also attend the training programme.

Besides Gujarat, Congress leaders from Maharashtra, Goa, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu will also undergo training. In all, 500 men from these states will be imparted with media management skills.

Among those addressing the party workers include AICC media committee chairperson Veerappa Moily and some professionals from the media. The names of media persons have, however, not been disclosed. After the training, the party will set up four regional media centres at Surat, Vadodara, Rajkot and Bhavnagar, besides the state level centres, which is already functional at Ahmedabad. These centres will supply regular materials to the journalists to meet their information requirements with regard to the party. A senior Congress leader said the party has been issuing statements and press notes to the media almost daily from its Ahmedabad headquarter but very little of it has found space in the newspapers, barring the odd press conferences addressed by the leaders.

One of the reasons, he said, could be that the leaders looking after the Congress media cell might not be aware of the needs of the media.

Heading: Court sends 2 blasts accused in 10 days police custody - Indian Express
Content:
The Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC) has been selected for the National Urban Water Award 2008. The award will be handed over to the AMC some time early next year, said Srinivas Chary Vedala, professor and director at Administrative Staff College of India, Hyderabad

The Ministry of Urban Development, Government of India, has instituted the award in partnership with ASCI and the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII). Municipal Commissioner I P Gautam said on Tuesday that the AMC had already been issued the certificate of participation for 'effective water supply management' and 'successful development of a market-based financing system for urban water supply sector'.

Gautam said the award was given to the AMC in recognition of exemplary performance in urban water management contributing to improved quality of life in India. "The award is aimed at identifying and encouraging the initiatives of urban local bodies, water utilities and others for making efforts innovatively and creatively to improve water supply delivery system and share them with others," said the ASCI director's letter to AMC.

Gautam, meanwhile said that the AMC was busy planning improvements in water supply to the 900-odd chawls that house nearly 20 per cent of the city's population, by replacing their old pipelines so that diseases caused by water contamination is avoided. Besides, the civic body was also busy implementing 11 projects of building water tanks in new areas to ease supply and pressure problems. Originally, these projects were listed under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission.

These projects, costing Rs 76 crore, were withdrawn in September 2006 from JNNURM funding because the conditions would lead to inordinate delays in implementation. While JNNURM conditions stipulated 24-hour water supply, this did not match with AMC plans of strengthening the existing system, Gautam said, citing the reason for withdrawal.

Heading: GU flouting UGC norms, allege some faculties - Indian Express
Content:
Umar Kabira and Salim Sipahi were arrested on Monday

The designated Metropolitan Magistrate Court, hearing the pre-trial of the Ahmedabad serial blasts and Surat bomb cases on Tuesday, sent Umar Kabira and Salim Sipahi to 10 days' police custody.

The Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) had on Monday arrested Kabira and Sipahi for their involvement in the Ahmedabad blasts. The two had been arrested for their role in the blasts that took place in Maninagar, including the one at L G Hospital.

In its remand application, the DCB said the police custody of the accused was essential to find their role in the conspiracy and assess their future plans. The remand application also states that a probe is necessary to find out Sipahi's role in teaching bomb making to other SIMI members. Sipahi himself is an expert bomb maker. The DCB further said that it requires time to find out who had imparted bomb-making skills to Sipahi and others things like to which state they belonged to, and other places on the hit list.

The DCB has accused Kabira of being a SIMI member who has organised meetings in his house. He has also been accused of doing a recce in Hindu areas of the city for potential bomb sites.

Appearing for the accused, advocate H M Qureshi contended that the accused were under detention since August 9 and were shown as arrested on Monday. Qureshi said that DCB has had ample time to question the accused and no further remand period was necessary.

Metropolitan Magistrate G M Patel however, accepted the remand application of the DCB. In its order, the court said the accused are involved in offences of grave nature and looking into the complexity of the case it was necessary that the police be given custody of the accused.

Heading: Chalo Dilli: State BJP MLAs to lead party’s dharna in Capital for GUJCOC - Indian Express
Content:
Guides of a few departments offering Master of Philosophy (M Phil) courses in Gujarat University (GU) are not working as per norms, it has been learnt.

The rules provide that at the most four students can be allotted to a guide in a year. This academic year though, the Department of Economics has given regular admission to 20 students.

"There are only three recognised M Phil guides in the department and they have allotted admission to 8 additional students, which is a violation of the university norms," said Pradeep Prajapati, Dean, Faculty of Arts, GU.

K M Bhatt, Head of Department (HOD) of Economics told Newsline: "We had five guides for M Phil until last year. But this year, after the completion of the admission process, one of our guides came to me and confessed that she is not a recognised M Phil guide."

He added: "I have requested the Vice-Chancellor to regulate the norms of allotting five students under one guide in place of four."

The Department of Gujarati has two guides, but this year, they have admitted 20 students out of which, 8 have been allotted admission on regular seats and 12 under the self-finance seats category. As per the authority of the School of Languages, they get visiting faculties to teach students on self-finance seats.

Pradeep Prajapati, a member of the GU Academic Council, however, has a different version on the issue. He said: "How can two guides teach 20 students? This is a violation of the norms. Their point about visiting faculties is completely false."

Manish Doshi, a member of the GU Executive Council said: "The GU itself is ignoring UGC norms and giving excess admissions in M Phil. Ultimately, the students will suffer without enough guides."

The violation of norms is not only in these two departments. The Department of Psychology and the Physical Education Department have also violated a few M Phil norms.

"In the Department of Psychology, M Phil was started last year, but the syllabus on which the students are taught is not passed by the Admission Council (AC) and the Executive Council (EC)," said Prajapati.

But the HOD of Department of Psychology claimed that the AC and EC had passed the syllabus last year.

This year, the guides of Physical Education Department asked their students to submit their viva instead of appearing for one, as part of their M Phil, which is not required. One student has also filed a case against this in the High Court. When asked about the viva issue, the HOD refused to comment. The V-C and the Registrar of GU were also not available to comment on the issue.

Heading: GU employees’ union believe in saying it together - Indian Express
Content:
Day-long protest to culminate with the party's representation to Prez

To mount pressure on the UPA government to approve the Gujarat Control of Organised Crime (GUJCOC) Act, the Gujarat BJP has planned to send all the 117 elected members of the state Legislative Assembly to New Delhi for a daylong dharna. This was decided in the recently concluded national executive meet of the party at Bangalore.

Gujarat BJP President Purshottam Rupala told Newsline that the party has planned for an elaborate agitation programme against the UPA government for getting a clearance on GUJCOC.

"Our MLAs will soon stage a dharna at New Delhi to demand an approval for the same. They will then hand over a representation to the President at the end of the day in this connection," he said. He, however, added that the date for the programme has not yet been fixed. It will be passed on to the state unit of the party by the national leadership soon, he said.

He said the existing laws are not good enough to handle the threats of terrorism. "But unfortunately, the Congress has always equated the issue of terrorism with Islam and is afraid to antagonise the community by clearing a strong anti-terror law. As a party, it has paid the heaviest price to terrorism. It lost two of its top leaders to the menace. It should have been the leader in devising the strong anti-terror mechanism, but instead is all opposed to the Act in a bid to appease the minorities," he added.

Interestingly, the newly formed Mahagujarat Janata Party (MJP), launched by the rebel BJP leaders, has demanded the enactment of the Act.

"Not only do we support the demand for GUJCOC, but we also feel that a stringent federal law must be enacted to deal with the threat of terrorism in India. We need a stronger federal law like POTA to deal with the menace at the national level as the problem is more of an interstate affair," said MJP President Gordhan Zadaphia.

He added: "Apart from playing vote-bank politics, the Congress is also apprehensive of the misuse of such a stringent law as it had done with MISA during the Emergency or with TADA, but that can be no rationale to stop a state from having a law to protect its own citizens."

He said the people of Gujarat cannot be kept waiting for a law to protect themselves, when something exactly similar is in force in neighbouring Maharashtra.

"We will declare our set of programmes on September 25 and the demand for GUJCOC will be one of our key areas," he added.

Heading: Heads riot, tails wrong: Did punters have a hand in Vadodara violence? - Indian Express
Content:
Four major GU unions say yes to merger

On Tuesday, employees of four major employees' unions in Gujarat University (GU) held an hour-long meeting at the Senate Hall and decided to merge all the unions.

The name of the union and its president will be announced on Thursday evening.

The union formed after the merger will have a secretary and a new committee comprising 8-10 members.

At present, there are four major employees' unions — the Gujarat University General Employees' Union, the Gujarat University Annayaya Pratikarak Association, the Gujarat University Press Department Employees Union and the Gujarat University Employees' Association.

Dilip Vaghela, President of the Gujarat University Employees' Association told Newsline: "Over the years, we have realised that we would be better off having a mother body that would take up the cause of all the unions. Earlier, each union had to present its case separately before the Vice-Chancellor, which somehow did not have a positive outcome."

Rashik Kadia, President of the Gujarat University General Employees' Union praised the decision. He said the merging of the unions was a historic step that would benefit all the employees.

He added: "On several occasions earlier, several problems at the GU management-level and the state government-level were not solved on time. This was because all the unions had different agendas and needs. But the situation is very different now and it demands a merger of all the unions. Also, we need to cut down on the monopoly of the GU management."

Vijaysinh Parmar, President of the Gujarat University Annayaya Pratikarak Association spoke about the divisive policies adopted by the GU management. He said: "The GU management always applied the divide and rule policy for the unions. We have now pledged to join hands and solve the problems of our employees."

Heading: Kurien conferred lifetime award for agricultural leadership - Indian Express
Content:
Cops to probe betting angle in communal flare-up

The riots in Vadodara during Ganesh visarjan on Sunday, could well turn out to be a Kafkaesque nightmare — where riots were stage-managed for personal gains.

Even though the Vadodara police has denied the involvement of a betting syndicate in the recent riots in Fatehpura, the arrest of Rajesh Pawar, a history-sheeter with several cases of betting registered against him, speaks otherwise. Joint Commissioner of Police, Pravin Sinha has, however, said the involvement of a betting syndicate is still under investigation.

Pawar was arrested for inciting a mob of 100-150 people and not following police orders during the Ganesh visarjan procession near Champaner Gate.

"He was arrested for inciting a mob and torching shops in Champaner Gate. Though he is involved in several cases of betting, we have arrested him this time for inciting a mob," said Sinha.

It was only recently that the Prevention of Crime Branch, Vadodara under the guidance of Commissioner of Police Rakesh Asthana, had arrested Arvind Valand, the kingpin of the betting syndicate in the city. He was arrested under the Gambling Act for betting on international cricket matches. The police also doubted his role in stage-managing Ganesh visarjan riots in the past by inciting the mobs.

Asthana had then said that not only did Valand bet on riots but also placed his money on the extent of damages during such flare-ups.

Heading: Minister’s mantra: With great profit comes great responsibility - Indian Express
Content:
Verghese Kurien, the father of Operation Flood and former chairman of the Gujarat Co-operative Milk Marketing Federation (GCMMF), was conferred the Lifetime Achievement Award by the National Awards Committee of

Agricultural Leadership Awards, 2008.

The ceremony will be held at New Delhi as part of the Agriculture Leadership Summit under the chairmanship of Prof M S Swaminathan.

The award is given to outstanding personalities for having served the Indian Agriculture system, which had a positive impact on the growth in India's farm sector.

Kurien received the award for providing a lifeline to millions of rural milkmen. His macro management model is known globally as the most significant innovation for socio-economic objectives.

The National Awards Committee is headed by Dr A R Kidwai, Governor of Haryana and has 12 people of national eminence as members. The Agricultural Leadership Awards have been instituted by Agriculture Today, the national agriculture magazine published by the Centre for Agriculture and Rural Development in New Delhi.

Heading: Driver lodges abduction case, owner casts doubt - Indian Express
Content:
Minister of State for Industry Saurabh Patel clarified on Tuesday that the state government believed in social responsibility and the public sector enterprises must spend a part of their profit on projects for the poor and the needy. He was reacting to the controversy by some investors over public sector enterprises being asked to spend 30 per cent of their Profit Before Tax (PBT) on social causes.

"No one should have any objection to the proposal because the money will be spent on educational and other needs of the poorest of the poor of society," he said.
