The PSEs that have been asked by the government to spare 30 per cent of their PBT for social cause are the Gujarat Mineral Development Corporation (GMDC), Gujarat Narmada Valley Fertiliser and Chemical Limited (GNFC), Gujarat Industries Power Corporation Limited (GIPCL), Gujarat State Fertiliser and Chemical Limited (GSFC), Gujarat Alkalis and Chemicals Limited (GACL) and Gujarat State Petronet Limited (GSPL). But after the proposals, the scrips of these PSEs have witnessed a fall at the stock exchange.

Heading: Pandya new chairman of Institute of Engineers - Indian Express
Content:
The driver of city-based activist Kanu Brahmbhatt has lodged an FIR against four unknown people at the Sayajigunj police station on Monday evening for trying to abduct him while he was driving back Brahmbhatt's car home.

Suresh Patel has said in the FIR that the car developed a snag near the Jetalpur underpass while he was returning from the railway station. Four unknown people approached and offered him help.

As soon as the car started, the accused gagged him and forced him to get into the rear seat. The accused drove the car towards Karjan where they rammed the vehicle against a tree.

Investigating Officer, R J Pandor at the Sayajigunj police station said they are trying to ascertain the facts of the case.

Meanwhile, Brahmbhatt, who is now in Mumbai, has cast doubt on the allegation made by Patel.

He said: "The complaint is baseless. The driver came to drop me at the station as I was going to Mumbai on September 12. I had asked him to park the car in a society at Jetalpur Road, which is just a few minutes away from the railway station. My relatives stay there and they had offered him dinner as well, but he refused saying that he had other plans with his friend. The driver might have consumed liquor and possibly rammed the car."

Heading: Police custody of 10 blasts accused extended - Indian Express
Content:
Reader at MSU's faculty of technology, I I Pandya was elected chairman of the Institute of Engineers, Vadodara chapter, here on Monday.

Pandya is also the MSU syndicate member and has 28 research papers and overseas journals to his name. The Institute of Engineers aims at promoting fieldwork as well as practical knowledge among budding engineers.

Pandya has been a member of professional bodies such as Indian Society for Technical Education and Structural Engineering Association. He was also deputed to the Department of Science and Technology in Singapore.

Pandya has been given the new responsibility considering his knack in administration, and efforts in framing policies and amending rules as a syndicate member, said secretary and director general A K Poothia.

Heading: Vadodara Social Forestry Dept plagued with staff crunch - Indian Express
Content:
The designated Metropolitan Magistrate Court extended the police custody by another 14 days of the 10 people accused in the Ahmedabad serial blasts and Surat bomb cases.

The ten accused include Mufti Mohammad Abdul Bashir, the named mastermind of the blasts and Sajid Mansuri, the key SIMI operative. The remand is in connection with the case registered under Khadia police station where three bombs killed five people and injured 45.

Meanwhile, Metropolitan Magistrate G M Patel pulled up DCB officials for not allowing family members of the accused inside the court room. Patel said: "This is an open court room. Nobody should be stopped from coming inside. Only court is the competent authority to issue a direction of such a nature, and so far the court has issued none."

On the other hand, Sajid Mansuri's wife Sajida Bano submitted an affidavit stating that Mansuri was ill-treated by the police. She stated that her husband sustained a fracture in his leg due to physical torture and has demanded that Mansuri be examined by the Magistrate, his statement recorded, and he be given medical assistance.

Heading: Web of wellness - Indian Express
Content:
Overburdened with additional charges and excessive workload for the past one year, Vadodara Social Forestry Department officials are finding it difficult to manage wildlife in the city these days.

While the problem of staff shortage has plagued the Social Forestry Department in the entire state, Vadodara is reeling under the fact that the maximum number of wildlife cases are being filed in the city. In addition, the city department officials have been allotted additional territorial forest duties despite the presence of a separate territorial forestry staff in the district.

The post of Vadodara Range Forest Officer (RFO), which was vacant for one year, was filled by a range forest officer from Savli taluka social forestry, N N Sheikh, three days ago. Sheikh said: "I have sufficient experience in social forestry work, but lack of proper management, no wireless system and dearth of staff will make handling wildlife a major problem".

Most of the RFOs have been given the charge of additional territorial forests even as there is a separate Division Forest Officer (DFO) in place. Nayan Desai, Deputy Conservator of Forest (DCF), Social Forestry, Vadodara, told Newsline: "Generally, the Social Forestry Department is allotted additional charge of territorial forests in case there is no separate division of territorial forest. But, this is not the case in Vadodara district."

Some officials said on condition of anonymity that there are 11 posts for RFO I Vadodara Social Forestry Division. However, four posts in Chhota Udepur, Naswadi, Sinor and Pavi Jetpur ranges have been lying vacant for the last one year.

While sources say there should be at least three vehicles in a division, forest divisions such as Bharuch and Vadodara are operating with just one vehicle. Moreover, vehicles allotted to social forestry officials in Anand and Narmada districts are in a bad state. "The situation remains the same despite sending monthly reports to the Gujarat Social Forestry head office in Gandhinagar," said an official.

M L Sharma, Principal Chief Conservator of Forest (PCCF), Gujarat Social Forestry Department, said: "Around 150 RFO posts have been lying vacant for the last one year. Issues on promotions and transfers will be sorted out. As far as the issue of vehicles is concerned, the Social Forestry Departments are free to hire vehicles on emergency."

Sharma, however, refused to comment when asked about the matter of filling up vacant posts.

Heading: Minor girl says she was gangraped; 3 held from Sector 52 - Indian Express
Content:
Docs in the city are spreading the word on health & fitness via their websites

The barriers of time, place, distance…cease to exist when it comes to gaining good health. As technology gets the world closer, healthy living, treatment options and docs' consultations are just a click away and more accessible than they were ever before. Health websites are the brand-new way doctors are reaching to reach out to people on new disease modalities, cost options, best facilities and cures at hand and to enhance their business. Quick, reliable, simple, just log on to know what's best for you.

Dr Sandeep Jassal, an Integrated Medicine Physician and holistic health consultant conceived LiveLifeMore.com in February 2003 with a vision to help people all over the world, irrespective of age, gender or ethnicity and improve their health and lives through harmonization of the key aspects of healthy living. LiveLifeMore recognizes that health is more than just an absence of disease. A multi-disciplinary approach to medicine provides the maximum therapeutic benefit. LiveLifeMore offers subscription-based online guidance in the essential components of optimal health: nutrition, exercise, attitude and lifestyle modification. The harmonization of these aspects of health is a holistic approach by integrating scientific advancements of medical science and diagnostics, evidence based research in exercise and nutrition with age old wisdom in therapies like ayurveda, yoga and naturopathy as well. It is a holistic, preventive approach which empowers individuals to optimize their health, well-being and vitality. "And this can translate into a state of total health, that is it can add years to lives, add life to years,'' smiles Dr Jassal. By logging on to LiveLifeMore.com, you have access to personalized health information from leading experts 24 hours a day, seven days a week and you can receive personalized meal plans, vitamin and supplement plans, exercise plans, attitude plans and lifestyle modification plans directed to your specific goals and needs. "I and my wife Pallavi, a diet and nutrition consultant coordinate with specialists from nearly all the specialties in LiveLifeMore.com's Cyber Clinic consultations and visiting national and international specialists are a part of CyberClinic of LiveLifeMore.com,'' Dr Jassal says their emphasis is on prevention of illness, early intervention and health promotion and educating people to be aware of the body's requirements and train them to take responsibility for their own health.

It was on a patient's suggestion and insistence that Dr GK Bedi and Dr RS Bedi developed their website ivfbedi.com way back in 2000. A patient from abroad received a successful infertility treatment at their clinic and was blessed with twins and it all began on a positive note, recalls Dr Bedi. "She told us that the treatment here was so affordable and effective and people were desperate for this treatment and needed to know about it and a website was the most effective way to reach out to the far corners,'' Dr Bedi says the website was a hit from the word go, as they received queries and hopeful patients from places like Sweden, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Iraq, Australia, Kenya!

From a basic launch to an active website, which answers all queries of patients, the website is attached to institutes abroad. "Procedure of treatment, duration, patient profile, cost, stay arrangement, it's all here, put simply and clearly,'' assures Dr Bedi.

In today's time and age, when people are discerning, well-read and travelled, have access to information and knowledge, health websites are the need of the hour and the best and most cost-effective way to talk about the USP of a doctor, believes DR KM Kapoor, a leading plastic and cosmetic surgeon. His website, indiaplasticsurgery.com is among the leading websites of the country and the doc's been included in the Google directory too. The tremendous scope for medical tourism in the field of plastic surgery prompted Dr Kapoor to design the website. "It was tough to access foreign clients and via indiaplasticsurgery.com in the last three years I have been able to treat a number of NRIs and patients from abroad,'' Dr Kapoor says the website offers complete details of surgery, the affordable facilities as compared to abroad and also an elaborate photo gallery which displays pre-operative and post-operative pictures. "It's simple and the first page itself gives patients an access to my direct number and mail.''

Dr Nirja Chawla simply loves the process and chance of learning new technology when she uploads, downloads and edits her website www.nirjachawla.com. The wonderful colours and aesthetic design of the website make the well-known gynaecologist proud. "As for the patient, the website, which is linked with endoscopy.co.in, in clear and coherent words, gives people the information that they need, clears many misconceptions regarding endoscopy and other procedures, includes media reports, patient-friendly articles and also some technical matter,'' the doc feels more and more people and docs need to be Net savvy to make the best of technology. Log on to good health!

Heading: Judicial fixers like Ravinder deserve no relief, says Bar - Indian Express
Content:
A 16-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped by three youths after keeping her in confinement for the last six days. The girl from Nehru Colony, a slum area in Sector 52, was thrown outside her house late on Monday night in a semi-conscious state.

All three accused named by her have been arrested and a case of rape and kidnapping registered against them. According to the police, the accused are brothers who lived in the same locality and were known to the girl. Sonu (26), Monu (22) and Nitin (19) were sent to judicial custody on Tuesday. All three worked as sweepers. Their medical tests were conducted, the police said.

Coming from Muzzafarnagar in UP, where her mother lives — her father is no more — the victim had been staying with her grandparents in Nehru Colony for the last one month. She had been missing since September 10. The girl was illiterate and had come to the city in search of a job.

She told the police that she was returning home from Phase 3, Mohali, on foot around noon on September 10, when the three youths came in an auto-rickshaw and asked her join them, on the pretext of drop her home. Instead, they allegedly took her to an unknown place where they confined her and repeatedly raped her, the girl said in her complaint.

According to sources, however, the girl had an affair with Nitin. The police said Nitin had confessed to the crime and further investigations were on.

The girl's uncle, a private security guard, said he returned from duty at 11.30 pm on Monday night and found her lying unconscious outside their house. "I immediately took her to the Sector 16 hospital." He alleged that they had gone to the police ever since the girl was missing, but the latter refused to lodge a missing report. Officers refuted the charges.

On the statement of the girl, DSP (South) Jasant Singh Khaira said, they had registered a case at the Sector 36 police station.

Heading: More dead fish surface in Sukhna Lake - Indian Express
Content:
CASH AT JUDGE'S DOOR n Court reserves orders on his anticipatory bail plea

The District Courts witnessed a war of words between the counsel representing the Punjab and Haryana High Court Bar Association and that for Ravinder Singh, co-accused in the cash-at-judge's-door case. The heated arguments lasted for nearly one and half hour, after which the court reserved its orders on the anticipatory bail application filed by Ravinder.

Taking a dig at the Delhi-based hotelier, who has been evading arrest ever since the scandal came to light, Advocate Anupam Gupta, counsel for the HC Bar, said Ravinder was a "judicial fixer par excellence who was not entitled to any kind of relief from the court".

Gupta demanded his custodial interrogation, terming the case as "more serious than a murder". "It is rape of the judicial system. If custodial interrogation of Ravinder is not allowed, it will be a case of blatant and flagrant miscarriage of justice. Such a shocking case of corruption involving lawyers and judges has happened for the first time," Gupta added.

Ravinder's counsel, meanwhile, objected to the contentions raised by Gupta. Advocate H S Bhullar raised eyebrows on the Bar's "motive" behind moving the application demanding permission to intervene in the case.

"Is the Bar genuinely coming forward to contest the anticipatory bail of Ravinder or they are trying to browbeat the courts in order to get judicial orders in their favour. If that is the actual motive, allowing application of the Bar will set a bad example," said Bhullar.

He added that if the Bar was so much interested in the case, it should ask its representative to approach the CBI and assist it. Bhullar argued that merely sending Rs 15 lakh from Delhi did not constitute any offence against Ravinder. "Moreover, as per statements of Sanjeev Bansal, the packet sent by him was not delivered to any judge," Bhullar submitted.

On the other hand, Gupta said the day the incident took place (August 13), as many as 75 calls, both incoming and outgoing, were made from the mobile phone of Sanjeev Bansal to Ravinder Singh and many others, including a few judges, between 8.30 and 11.30 pm.

"The sheer number of phone calls proves that something had gone wrong," he argued.

Establishing the close relations between Bansal, former Additional Advocate General, Haryana, and Ravinder, Gupta said: "We are not dealing with innocent people here. The two had gone into hiding the day the incident took place."Demanding protection, Bhullar said Ravinder was not confident of surrendering as he feared the CBI might force him to make certain confessions.

"It will be a tragedy if custodial interrogation of Ravinder is not allowed," said Gupta.

The special public prosecutor for the CBI, too, demanded custodial interrogation of Ravinder. The court questioned as to why a custodial interrogation was required since their investigation had not made any headway so far.

"The investigation will remain stranded until Ravinder is arrested and interrogated," Gupta submitted.

Heading: Protests by sugar mill workers turn violent - Indian Express
Content:
Dead fish continued to surface in the Sukhna waters for the second consecutive day. Around 20 more of them were found floating on the lake on Tuesday. Experts reiterated that it fish mortality was not uncommon during the rainy season. But, with this not occurring during the peak of monsoon, the reasons needed to be investigated further, they added. The dead fish found on Tuesday were smaller in size.

The examination of the dead fish on Monday had revealed that deposition of sand in their gills led to asphyxiation, causing their death. Prof M S Johal from the Department of Zoology, who conducted the examination, had said the fish might have gone to an area with more silt, which caused deposition of sand on their gills.

The removal of silt from the lake is a problem that the Administration has been trying to find a solution for. A Rs 72-crore de-silting project is still awaiting approval of the Cente. Silt accumulation has been occurring in the lake since 1958. The slide gates built near the tower had got buried under silt within a year of construction.

Dr G S Dhillon, former chief engineer of the Punjab Irrigation department and an expert on the lake, said there had been initially a plan to build tanks from where the water entered the lake. "The objective was to first let the water enter the tank, giving the silt enough time to settle down. The water would have been released into the lake after that. This would have prevented the accumulation of silt in the water body. But the proposal never materialised. The silt deposited could later be sold off," he said.

The Chandigarh Pollution Control Committee is, meanwhile, testing the water samples to find out the reason behind the fish mortality. The water will be tested for presence of toxins and oxygen content.

Heading: Senate poll contestants go hi-tech to woo voters - Indian Express
Content:
Police use force on protestors after they resort to stone-pelting and threaten to burn themselves

A protest by the Co-operative Sugar Mills Workers Federation, Punjab, went awry when the Chandigarh Police resorted to baton charging the protestors and using water cannons and tear gas shells to disperse the mob.

The protestors were trying to cross the barricades to move towards the Vidhan Sabha. The protestors, hundreds in number, also hurled stones at the police, following which the latter had to use force, officers said.

The incident took place around 3.15 pm.

The police arrested Kashmir Singh Zira, chief advisor of the federation, along with 16 others as preventive action. A case was registered against federation president Karnail Singh Lakhmipur on charges of violating prohibitory orders and assaulting public servants.

The disgruntled sugar mill workers had come to the city to take out a protest march to the residence of Punjab Cooperation Minister Captain Kanwaljit Singh against what they termed as non-acceptance of their demands agreed to by the government in the past.

They threatened to burn themselves if their demands were not met, which made the police act against them, the officers said.

Heading: ‘The WC is something which I have always dreamt of ’ - Indian Express
Content:
While students' polls are over, Panjab University is under the grip of another election — that for the senators of the graduate constituency. The polls are scheduled to be held on Saturday.

Using hi-tech methods for campaigning, the contestants have gone a step ahead.

They are busy wooing prospective voters using latest techniques — Power Point presentations, text messages and emails. Being the largest constituency, the contestants are trying to put their best foot forward and are leaving no stone unturned.

More than 30 contestants are vying for 15 seats. The vote bank consists of all those who have passed out of the university and affiliated colleges.

M L Aeri, one of the contestants and the Director, DAV Management Committee, has every DAV college and school pitching in to campaign for him. In a move to impress the director, schools in the tri-city seem to be competing with each other to become the 'best campaigner'.

Another new face in the elections is S C Gupta, who is busy sending texts to anyone and everyone whom he can ask for votes. Speaking to Newsline, he said: "SMS is the ideal way to get noticed and it serves the purpose of campaigning in the best possible manner. One doesn't have to bother any one by going door to door."

Most of the contestants have shed the traditional ways of campaigning.

On Tuesday, teachers of a DAV school in Mohali and their principal Jaya Bhardwaj went to the Punjab School Education Board, campaigning for Aeri.

Bhardwaj said all teachers were willingly canvassing for the candidate before and after school hours. She said the school had prepared a Power Point presentation. "We are showing this presentation to groups of people to involve them in the democratic process of electing their representative in the Senate elections, also known as the mini-Vidhan Sabha elections of PU," she said.

Heading: After visa clearance, Alam to arrive this weekend - Indian Express
Content:
As Jeev Milkha Singh vaulted his way into top-60 in the world on Tuesday, he now sets his eyes on World Cup

Ten years ago may have been one of those rare times when Jeev Milkha Singh was tempted to make a bold statement. He had just taken part in the Eisenhower Trophy in 1988 and missed a short par putt when he heard someone say, "Playing for the country should be the top priority," and in reply, Jeev had said "Yes, I firmly believe in that." As India's top-ranked golfer returned to Chandigarh on Tuesday after finishing tied 11th in the Mercedes-Benz Championship at Cologne, Germany, he remembered the reference as talk turned to him pairing up with compatriot Jyoti Randhawa in the Mission Hills World Cup to be held in China from November 27 to 30.

"The World Cup is something I have always dreamt of. It's even more special than the Masters, and both Jyoti and I cherish it. I have never played in a World Cup before and I think we have got an excellent chance," he stops for a while and then continues while praising Jyoti. "The last time I played in a team event was during the Royal Trophy between Europe and Asia in the later part of 2006. I have got some fine memories of playing in the Eisenhower Trophy early in my career and I hope this team event will be good for me. Jyoti has been fantastic early this season and we compliment each other well," says Jeev as he takes a look at the latest ranking list released by World Golf Rankings on his newly bought Wi-Fi phone. The 38-year-old golfer vaulted in the top 60 players in the world on Tuesday, a feat which has brought back memories of the 2006 season for him, in which he fetched four wins and

18 top-ten finishes. "I think this year I have been more consistent through out the season and with two wins along with a top-ten finish in the Masters, I guess at least three wins are on the way. I will play in the Singapore Open, Mount Open and HSBC Open Championship before I play in the World Cup in the fourth week of November," shares Jeev. But often amid the celebrations it is forgotten that the Chandigarh golfer has been nursing a right-foot injury which has meant that he missed practice rounds during most of the tournaments.

"According to my doctors, my right foot is in a very bad condition and I need at least four to six weeks complete rest. Last month was the only time after 2000 that I had a break for more than three weeks," Jeev says. "Even during the Masters Championship, I played the 35 holes on the last day while taking eight painkillers. I had a MRI scan in New York last week and it revealed that the foot is healing," And over the last few months, Jeev has set his concentration on setting his record straight in India. "That's the only part which I need to work upon. I will be playing in British Masters Open and Dunhill Open before I play in the Indian Open in October and I need to set my record straight in India. People think of me as a global player but I need to do well in my home country too," feels Jeev as he takes another look at his phone. "And to tell you more, I have also committed for playing in the PGTI BILT Open from December 25 to December 26 which I will be playing after the Volvo Masters," says the 60th ranked player as he tees off at Chandigarh Golf Club.

Heading: ONGC, SBM clash today - Indian Express
Content:
Former Pakistan skipper Intikhab Alam, appointed as coach of the Punjab Ranji team, would arrive in Chandigarh this weekend after his visa documents were cleared by the Indian and Pakistan High Commission. According to top officials in Pakistan, the Legastic Cell of Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) today apprised Alam about the visa clearance.

According to sources in Punjab Cricket Association (PCA), Alam's visa was pending with the government for necessary clearances. "He was scheduled to leave for India on September 1 and watch an inter-district tournament but could not leave due to the visa delay but now the deck is clear for him," they said.

Alam would replace outgoing Punjab coach Gurcharan Singh, who failed to impress in the Ranji Trophy season last year following which Alam was called back for the job. Alam, who had coached and managed the Pakistan team that lifted the 1992 World Cup, was coach of the Punjab team from 2004 to 2006 and guided Punjab into the final of the Ranji Trophy.

Talking to The Indian Express from Pakistan, Intikhab Alam said that he was eager to join the State side as coach, and watch the players in action. "I got a call from the PCB officials today afternoon and they have informed me that the visa clearance has been granted and I would get the documents by the evening or by Wednesday morning", he said.

"It was a long wait and, perhaps too boring as I had to take up the coaching assignment in India and the delay was only due to visa problem," he said. "Inshah allah ab main JP Atray se pehle Punjab pahunch jaunga (by God's grace I would reach Punjab before JP Atray tournament commences," he informed. "I would leave by this weekend for India", he said.

It may be recalled that the Punjab Cricket Association had sent a letter of appointment to Alam requesting him to join by September 1 almost three months back. The Punjab Cricket Association had appointed former Pakistan captain Intikhab Alam as its senior team coach amid reports that the PCB was also trying to appoint him as the national coach. However the PCA was successful to sign Alam for the top job in the state cricket, earlier this year.

PCA Secretary MP Pandove told The Indian Express that the delay would not weigh much on the team and also on its selection as there is an important tournament with big names of Indian cricket still in the offing. "Alam is most likely to be here after the clearance of his visa and would watch the potential Punjab talent in action before the start of the Ranji season", he added.

Heading: Minor ‘tortured’ in police custody - Indian Express
Content:
ONGC, Delhi will take on last year's runners-up State Bank of Mysore (SBM) in the first match of the 15th All India J P Atray Memorial Cricket Tournament for the PEARLS Trophy at Sector 16 Cricket Stadium on Wednesday.

Wicket-keeper Tilak Nayudu will lead the State Bank of Mysore side which also includes the likes of B Akhil, Anand Kati, K N Ramesh and KST Sai. Meanwhile, ONGC boasts of Munaf Patel, Ajay Ratra and Sarandeep Singh in the team. The match will be a 50 overs affair and commence at 9.15 am. Meanwhile, former Indian skipper Sourav Ganguly and speedster Ranadeb Bose will arrive in Chandigarh on Thursday.

Heading: Contractor is king at Kalka bus stand - Indian Express
Content:
16-year-old Vimal admitted in Rajindra Hospital, Patiala, following an attempt to commit suicide

A 16-year-old resident of Nepal was admitted in Government Rajindra Hospital, Patiala, on Tuesday following an alleged attempt to commit suicide after being tortured in police custody.

According to the Kotwali police, Vimal G C was caught red-handed by a resident of Nabha stealing some wires on Saturday afternoon. "We recovered the wires from his possession and a case under Sections 454, and 380 of the IPC was registered against the accused. Now, a case of attempt to murder under Section 309 has been registered against Vimal," said Station House Officer Kotwali, Gurinder Bal, who was waiting outside the Intensive Care Unit.

Sources said the boy was produced at the juvenile trial court on Sunday.

"The boy was brutally tortured at the Kotwali police station in Nabha. The cops were under pressure to recover the stolen material from the accused and used the third degree. Vimal even tried to commit suicide by strangulating himself with his vest in the lock-up," said a source.

SHO Bal admitted to a degree of negligence on part of the staff but denied allegations of torture.

"The boy tried to tear off his vest and strangulate himself. But the on-duty sentry saw his legs shaking and opened the lock up. I was intimated about the incident at 8.40 am today," he said.

When asked why the victim was admitted to hospital at 11.50 am (a delay of three hours) despite Nabha being only a 40-minute drive from Patiala, the SHO had no reply. "The boy was taken to a local doctor before going to Rajindra Hospital. I will look into the matter and ask the on-duty munshi Sarabjeet Singh and sentry Satguru Singh to explain the case. I was out in the field when the incident took place," he said.

Nabha Deputy Superintendent of Police Arshdeep said the sequence of events is still unclear. "Action will be initiated as per the law. An enquiry has been ordered into the matter and no guilty official would be allowed to escape," he said.

Undertrial attacks inspector
Ambala:An undertrial facing charges of murdering a Home Guard at the Ambala Cantonment railway station, attacked an RPF Inspector on Tuesday.

Rakesh, a vendor, was being taken to court when he suddenly pounced on Inspector Anil Kumar, tearing his uniform, before the other policemen present intervened.

A Bihari migrant with a criminal record, Rakesh used to sell cold drinks illegally on trains.

When Home Guard Jai Pal tried to stop him, Rakesh murdered him with a pointed rod used to break ice. Although he escaped, he was arrested in Ludhiana.

The police have registered another case of assaulting a government servant on duty.

Heading: Computer professional turns reiki healer for asthmatic daughter - Indian Express
Content:
Parking one's car at the Kalka bus stand is becoming a cause of harassment for the residents of the area.

The management of the parking place at the bus stand has been allotted to a contractor by the Haryana Roadways but the contractor has been issuing parking slips to visitors in the name of the roadways instead of his own.

According to Meenakshi Sharma, a resident of the area, she had parked her scooter at the parking lot and was given receipt number 4043 in the name of Haryana Roadways.

It was not mentioned anywhere on the receipt slip that extra money would be charged as night charges.

"There is no name or contact number of the contractor on the board put up in the parking lot or on the receipt, which is mandatory as per the contract," added Sharma.

When she went to take her scooter the next day, an employee of the contractor told her that he was a worker and he had been asked to take Rs 10 including night charges.

Parking charges for the whole day, however, is Rs 5. "He also refused to give a receipt for the same," she claimed.

When Newsline asked him why he was charging extra money in the form of night charges, he said, "It is our will and we will charge as per our desire on the receipt of the Haryana Roadways."

K S Kalsan, General Manager, Haryana Roadways, Chandigarh said, "This contract has been given to a private contractor and it is wrong if he is using it in the name of Haryana Roadways. I will look into the matter immediately."

Heading: AIDS control society to set up hospice in city - Indian Express
Content:
Shivi Dua was a computer professional for five years till her daughter was diagnosed with asthma. To help her daughter deal with her ailment she learnt the art of reiki, and is now a professional healer herself.

She went through all levels of learning, practising and teaching the healing processes since 2000 and has now graduated to an advanced form termed as Theta healing.

"Healing, by now, has become a way of life for me. So in 2005, the move to Theta Healing was natural for me. It works by changing negative beliefs in the subconscious to positive ones. I am very happy with the results as my daughter is completely rid of asthma," says Dua.

Dua adds while the physical symptoms of the stress and ailments may be treated in the first session itself, the sub-conscious healing takes time.

She opines: "The scope of this healing work is unlimited and caters to each and every aspect of life such as physical ailments, relationship issues and financial problems," adding that the technique has helped people deal with ailments like back problems, perforated retina, obsessive neurosis, asthma and spondilitis.

Heading: Come Sept 21, cardiac emergency treatment at your doorstep - Indian Express
Content:
Looking for an NGO to run its second hospice in the city for AIDS patients, State AIDS Control Society (SACS) today invited expressions of interest from willing organisations.

The planned hospice will be set up in the southern part of Chandigarh to help patients coming for Anti-Retroviral Treatment (ART).

"The exact location has not been decided upon as yet. But it will be set up near Government Medical College and Hospital (GMCH), Sector 32, so that patient load can be easily shared between the PGI and the GMCH," said Dr Vanita Gupta, Project Director for SACS.

For temporary accommodation of ailing HIV patients, the authorities are planning at least 20 beds in the hospice.

At present , a 10-bed hospice run by the Red Cross is functioning at village Khuda Ali Sher in the northern part of the city, which is in proximity to the PGIMER. "Here, patients are kept for a limited period of time, normally one to two weeks, and are discharged after their condition stabilises. The ART medicines are provided free of charge," she added.

Heading: UT Administrator stresses on strengthening security agencies to avoid terror attacks - Indian Express
Content:
Now, cardiac emergency treatment will be available at the doorstep of residents in Chandigarh, Mohali and Panchkula. Patients can call mobile number — 09915444550 for a cardiac care ambulance, carrying a coronary care response team, which will reach their residence at the earliest.

Part of the Panjab Remote Telecardiology Access Project (PARTAP) and Chandigarh Heart Electronic Tele-Access Kardiogram (CHETAK), the cardiac ambulance will be launched on September 21 by former Director General, Army Medical Forces, General (retd) B N Shahi.

Former Additional Professor of Cardiology, PGI, Dr Anil Grover has teamed up with five other cardiologists to launch the project, which will provide free advice to the patients.

Dr Grover told Newsline: "Any person who has cardiac symptoms can dial the service and avail expert advice or if required, the ambulance will be sent to his/her house."

The ambulance will have an Emergency Medical Technician (EMT), a nurse-cum-EKG technician and an MBBS doctor. The EKG will be recorded and uploaded on the internet at a common mail address —the.heart.in@gmail.com.

The air-conditioned ambulance is equipped with an EKG, scanner, backup, monitor, defibrillator, portable ventilator, oxygen supply, suction apparatus, a laptop and a mobile phone with 5 mega pixel camera for sending MMSes or EKGs through the internet.

Heading: First Comic Standing - Indian Express
Content:
UT Administrator General S F Rodrigues (Retd) today stressed upon revitalising the decision-making bodies and security agencies at the national and state levels to deal sternly with the challenges regarding internal security. He was speaking in a Governors' Conference at Rashtrapati Bhawan in New Delhi.

"India has emerged as a strong and vibrant nation with a buoyant economy with confident and competent people. The world has recognised us as a leading global economy. A pragmatic and constructive approach is required to maintain our growth by focusing on grey areas and taking corrective measures. Issues like drug addiction, female foeticide, cases of AIDS need collective endeavour at all levels, as these are posing a serious threat to our future."

Highlighting the role of education as a primary indicator of national purpose, General Rodrigues advocated the need for introducing innovative professional and skill development programmes in universities and colleges. "It is also essential that our educational institutions focus on the inculcation of proper values, so as to make our children good citizens. We, in Chandigarh, have started a novel programme — Focus: Moral Values and Civic Duties in Education — at primary school level," he said.

Heading: Live it up - Indian Express
Content:
That's Adam Sandler, in line with comedy

Quirky to the core. A complete Mad Hatter who's high on the fun ratings and possesses a finely twisted soul (in a good way) which finds immense pleasure in playing characters that can leave you in a state of shock and disbelief. Often, on the floor, breathless, and rolling in laugh attacks. No wonder his films come with a 'warning' from the health department! Just kiddin' but that's the absolute nonsensical sense actor Adam Sandler makes. And despite all the farting, ogling, squeaking, fooling he pulls off in his films, the Hollywood actor shines on the billboard of comedy giants. Out with his new new film, 'You Don't Mess With The Zohan', we, through an e-mail interview, got to know the man behind the actor, producer, writer and musician and the choices he's made.

"Right from childhood, I was always drawn towards stand-up comedy and everyone thought I was a natural comic. After a short stint in television acting and script writing for Saturday Night Live, I felt I enjoyed acting the most, and decided to focus on that," he types picking comedy as his specialisation. "Making people laugh is the most serious business." However, adds Adam, humor should be in accordance with the class targeted. If it's for masses, it should cover all those aspects. If it's classified, it should specifically portray those fun elements which are specific to the audience who don't have any objection. So, is The Zohan classified? "Well, the film was my idea and at no point I had ever thought that we would pick up a sensitive issue and deal with it in such a comic way. We worked on that because one minor mistake would have made the whole movie controversial, as the subject of the film deals with the tension, between Israel and Palestine." Sandler plays Zohan Dvir, a highly skilled, indestructible counter terrrorist who takes a break from the Army and moves to America to become a hairstylist. "He seems like he enjoys his life. So The Zohan is one character, I really don't mind being him in my real life," clicks Sandler.

We can't help but notice the underdog element in Sandler's works, most of which appears to be inspired from some real life characters and stories. "All of us, at some point in time has been, or has at least, felt like the underdog. The top dog may not always be liked by everyone, but everyone loves it when the underdog makes it big. He just connects with his audience all of us identify with him. The underdog gets into all these tricky situations and has all these funny moments which make up for the comedy in a movie...why would someone want to know the story of a guy who is the best in everything and has everything? It is always more interesting to know about the guy who has to face the odds to reach his goal." As for the real life experiences, Adam says most it is from stories he sees and hears. "Like for Zohan, the idea got better with help from conversations with my hairdresser Yuki. There were so many more people who helped me make Zohan more authentic, like Ronit Ravich-Boss, the script writer from Israel, and she helped me with my accent. Mariah Carey had to be a part of this because during my last trip to Israel, way back in the 90s, I met this cab driver who told me that the men there are absolutely ga-ga over her. So you can see that there are so many small experiences woven in to make a single story!"

He is looking forward to Bedtime Stories and Funny People, is writing and composing, and also looking after his production house, Happy Madison. "I guess each job is interesting and based on each other. I have enjoyed all from writing, composing music to acting and producing films. But would say that I can portray what I write or feel through my acting. So acting is my priority but yeah others are really unavoidable for me. After all it's a God gift to be multitalented. Isn't it? So sorry, I can't be biased towards either gift of God," he hits another one.

It would be a mistake if we say Sandler is all about being happy and funny for he's done his share of serious stuff, like the character in Reign Over Me and Spanglish. For Sandler, comedy might look easy and many critics don't consider it true works of art, but it's a serious business, and not just money-wise. "For it requires the same, sometimes even more dedication than action or drama. Timing is important and developing it is not an easy task. Frankly, I want to be master of all trades rather than just be the jack," punches Adam adding that versatility is one of the finest qualities that an actor can possess. "I could do comedy all my life and for such well thought concepts and issues are portrayed in a light manner, but yeah, in line with comedy, I would love do any role which is appealing and satisfying to me, be it romantic, serious or even negative. It helps me explore my abilities as an actor and set up better credentials. It is not that with my serious films I am trying to break the shackles of comedy type cast...acting is my forte and I want to do whatever I can." Proud of all his films, the actor's pretty excited about entering the horror/thriller genre with Scary Madison. As for Bollywood, he writes he's heard of "the awesome acting and film making talent in India", and regrets he hasn't watched any Indian film so far. "I have heard that comedies and romances are a huge rage in India, and that most of your films are musical. I would definitely not mind working in an Indian film." We are looking forward to that!

Heading: Foot Loose - Indian Express
Content:
Pucker up
Beauty International has launched the international cosmetic brand 'NYX' lip professional collection in India. The professional lipstick covers your lips with dazzling colours while smoothing and moisturizing lips. The delicious collection includes different range of lipsticks, glosses, and treatments. So get ready to highlight that sexy pucker of yours with. Available at all beauty centres and prices start at Rs 500.

Pillow talk
Although you may not think about them too much, pillows are a big part of our lives. Imagine, after a hectic day at work when you reach back home tired and ready to hit the bed but find your pillow missing! A bed without the pillows is so incomplete, but a bed with 'uncomfortable' pillows is as much a pain. Addressing the latter, Hush India is out with 'Super-Soft' pillows designed for the comforting sleep. The pillow range of Hush 'Super soft' is filled with Slow-Release-Fibre. They are made with home blend of imported fibre which has been developed to offer good support and comfort level. The pillows come in an international size offering a three way neck - shoulder - head support. The Hush 'Super Soft' pillow comes in an international size of 20' x 32' and are available with all leading furnishing stores across India for Rs 1,139.

Fresh face forward
We all know heat, pollution, poor nutrition, lack of sleep and humidity damages your skin. But how to deal with it is something we miss out on. Here's announcing Cheryl's Dermalite Face wash with Chamomile & Licorice for normal to dry skin and Cheryl's Dermalite Face wash with Tea Tree Oil for oily skin. Cheryl's Dermalite Face wash - an innovative skin lightening face wash that effectively lifts away dead surface cells, reduces surface melanin (pigment on your skin) & cleanses the skin of accumulated surface oils, debris and impurities without stripping away moisture, making your skin look clean, fresh, fair and radiant. Cheryl's Dermalite face wash comes in a pack of 50 ml for Rs 140 and 180 ml for Rs 400.

Gloss it over
Simply irresistible and lustrous,Lotus Herbals has introduced 'Seduction', a unique high sheen, non-sticky tinted lip gloss. This premium lip gloss is 100 percent vegetarian and free of animal products, making it absolutely safe. It contains botanical extracts of grapes and jojoba that keep your lips soft and moisturized all day long. Its easy grip brush applicator ensures precise and accurate application on your lips. In addition, its long & soft bristles allow you to use the lip gloss as a top coat without affecting your lip colour. The lip gloss comes in five shades that suit every Indian skin tone. It is priced at Rs 175.

Go vertical
DA Milano has introduced its 'Vertical Pleats' collection of handbags for women, as part of its Autumn collection 2008. Crafted by combining patent and croco print leathers, this luxurious collection of handbags makes a bold fashion statement. These ultra sassy handbags, designed with a great attention to detail, feature zippered compartments, comfortable handles and stylized with the Da Milano monogram, in brass. The handbags are ideally sized to carry all your essentials for a high-powered meeting or to flaunt as arm candy on a hot night out. Available in striking metallic shades ranging from purple, red, black, brown, chocolate, beige, white, light grey and silver. The collection is priced at Rs 5,995.

Heading: Present Tense - Indian Express
Content:
Block by block!
This Tuesday saw Fabindia host for the first time an exquisite Block-printing workshop that saw professional craftsman come in from Delhi to display the craft. Also on showcase was the art of gold and silver 'Khari' work along with a select display of the use of vegetables dyes for printing of motifs and designs on dupattas and saris in traditional fabrics like Chanderi, Maheswari and Kota. Customers were able to choose their own motifs and work out a design of their choice to get block printed. Interestingly, the craft of block-printing is very refined, skillful and exclusive in nature. It can take five carvers up to three days to create an intricate design in a block of teak used for printing. The printers may use up to thirty blocks to create a design. Separate pieces of wood are required for each of the colors used in a design and it is not unusual to have four or five colours in a professional design. On the occasion, a Fabindia official remarked, "In an ongoing effort, we constantly aim to showcase and nurture the ancients crafts of India. The block-printing workshop held at our store today was a step in the direction to showcase a traditional craft to the people of Chandigarh."

e-Testing
With most preparation courses for entrance tests going online, even the test preparation industry providing courses for preparation of IIT, CET, IAS and others need a little assistance. And providing it is WiZiQ.com through its seminar on 'Internet Strategies for Test Preparation Businesses'. To be held on September 17 from 3:00 to 7:00 pm at Hotel Sunbeam, here they will provide tips to test preparation institutes on how to reach a wider audience via e-learning. The seminar will incorporate face-to-face and online talks/discussions from a number of national and international experts on various topics related to the test preparation industry. This seminar will be free for all.

Hot spot
Complete with dry Japanese garden, party pool, waterfalls, lush green lawns and perfect landscaping, Sunshine Gardens is the new venue for party organisers. Matured over two years, "it is located on the Chattbir Zoo Road in three acres of area and has a capacity of 800," says proprietor BP Singh, adding that here there's inhouse parking and an AC Hall. What's more, this place is built on the theme of Sun, requires no tents, "as the place is fully-equipped and is designed with functionality in mind," he signs off.

Just in time!
This one was a new lesson for the 25 students from Suru River Valley in Kargil. One which taught them about machine tools and tractor parts. Organized by the Indian Army under its operation Sadbhavana Project, these students were given an opportunity to visit HMT factory, Pinjore, on Tuesday. While the students were acquainted with technologies and processes being adopted in manufacturing, they were also given joy rides on the tractors. "The students also visited St Vivekanand Millennium School during the trip," executive director of HMT Prakash Sharan told us. "The trip has been organized to bring oneness, build bridges of friendship and help local population in remote areas to join the mainstream. For most of these students, this visit is the first one away from their villages," added Major Pushkar Raj of the Indian Army, who coordinated the visit.

Heading: No ban here: Bulls fight at Sair fair - Indian Express
Content:
Art students get scientific on nuclear matters with 'Nuclear Energy Why?'

The exhibits may give the impression that a science fair is under progress but the surroundings bring you face to face with reality. The premise is the Government College of Arts in Sector 10 and on display is a collection of what the Bachelor of Fine Arts final year (Applied Art) students think of the nuclear deal. "We have an opinion and we will express it the best way we know," remarks Dancy. The campaign 'Nuclear Deal Why?' started as a class assignment by the faculty D S Kapoor, "I wanted to give them something different so that they create something unique in a sphere that they normally don't venture into as art students," Kapoor shares.

Under their faculty's guidance the students did a lot of research on the nuclear deal and why the whole hullabaloo. The result? Presentations and posters on the whole issue. "What we have done is compiled all the facts on nuclear energy, as in what it is, how it will effect us, why it is important, what are the pros and cons...all in a very simple manner," shares Kanwalpreet Cheema. Also on display are newspaper clippings of the whole process of the nuke deal. These students believe that it is the responsibility of an artist, especially in the field of advertising, to visually inform and educate the masses. The pull of the campaign is such that one of the special students, Vipin Hero, went ahead to contribute with his pieces despite ill health. But the highlight for sure are the posters wherein students have used various symbols like the money plant, terrorism, the Indian national flag to portray whether or not they support the deal. It's quite interesting to see not only different perspectives but the varied on the same issue.The images are very powerful and have impressed quite many. "In fact, the department of Science and Technology, Punjab, is pondering over the idea of using these images for their publication," adds Kapoor. Way to go guys!

Heading: Early chill causes dip in hydro-power generation - Indian Express
Content:
A bull-fight was organised during the celebrations of traditional Sair Mela today at Mashobra block. Significantly, bull-fighting is banned in the country to stop cruelty to animals.

Speaking to The Indian Express on the issue, from Delhi, animal rights activist and former Union minister Maneka Gandhi said that bull-fighting has been banned. "About ten years ago we had approached Maharashtra High Court against bull-fighting in Goa, when the court had ordered for a complete ban in Maharashtra and Goa." "We will initiate action and make sure that such fights are not organised in future," said Gandhi.

Transport Minister Krishan Kapoor who inaugurated the fair said, "I am not aware of any ban imposed on bull-fighting." He added he was not present during the bull-fighting at the fair. "The bull-fighting did not happen when I was there it may have happened after I came back." As per the tradition which continues to be observed till date in many parts of Shimla and Solan districts the bulls are fed with alcohol to charge them up and are later induced to fight during the fair. The fair is attended by people who watch these animals fight.

Gandhi said such things have not been reported in HP and the government has not paid heed to the demand for constituting institute State Animal Welfare Board.

Heading: Technical snag hits Dhumal’s chopper - Indian Express
Content:
Power generation in all the hydro power projects on Satluj, Beas and Chenab river basins in the state have fallen by five to seven per cent due to early setting in of winters and snowfall in higher reaches in early September this year.

Generation has dipped from 24 million units per day to 20 million units at Satluj Jal Vidyut Nigam's 1500 MW Nathpa Jhakri Power Project at Rampur.

Twenty other projects controlled by the Himachal Pradesh Electricity Board (HPSEB) including 126 MW Larji, 120 MW Bhava, Chamera I and Chamera II have also seen a dip in power generation by five to seven per cent less, according to sources.

The power generation is lean during mid september, but this year due to early snowfall in the higher reached, the water level has fallen at least a week before expected. The power supply to the northern grid has hence fallen. During the peak season the generation per day was 36 million units.

DGM Personnel and Administration V.K. Verma said, "The discharge in river Satluj remains up to 300 cusecs till September 15 but

it fell to 200 cusecs quite early this time, following which power generation has fallen by 4 million units per day at NJPC." However, this would not affect the annual generation target of 6400 million units and supply to the northern grid, as 4500 million units have already been generated in the first six months, he added.

Officials in the HPSEB believe the low discharge in the rivers might be temporary and the water level will pick up once again.

Heading: Guv’s plea to preserve heritage buildings in state - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal completed his journey from Arki to Hamirpur by road today after his helicopter developed a technical snag soon after it landed at Shalaghat near Arki where he inaugurated the two-day district level Sair fair.

Notably, this is the second time in a fortnight when the helicopter developed a snag. Earlier, the Chief Minister had to cancel his visit to Baddi to flag off trucks carrying the relief material to Bihar. The helicopter services have been hired from the Mesco Airlines Company. Besides providing services to the Chief Minister, the helicopter is also used during emergencies. Today's snag raised questions over the safety of the Chief Minister. He was about to take off when thick smoke started emanating from its engine forcing the security agencies to cancel the flight.

According to the sources the contract for the helicopter services had expired on July 31, but owing to some unknown reasons, it was extended up to September 30.

Heading: State highways to be widened - Indian Express
Content:
More than 100 British-era heritage buildings have fallen prey to vagaries of weather in the past two decades.

The remaining, out of which at least 37 fall within Shimla's heritage zone, need urgent restoration.

Taking up the issue at the conference of Governors, Prabha Rau made a plea to to depute a team of national experts to inspect the buildings and suggest measures to maintain them.

One of the prominent buildings include 175-year-old Barnes Court— now state Raj Bhawan where the Peace Accord (1972) between Indian Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and Pakistan PM Zulfikar Ali Bhutto was signed.

Drawing Centre's attention towards immediate renovation of the buildings,

Rau said the restoration work for Raj Bhawan and Town Hall should be sanctioned immediately.

She asked for a financial assistance of Rs 11 crore for renovation of these two buildings.

Rau demanded an increase for the state's quota in the armed forces.

She asked for implementation of one rank one pension scheme for ex-servicemen.

Stressing the need for modernisation of the police force, Rau asked for a grant of Rs 30 crore per annum. She said it is important to fight against the drug menace. Referring to the Pareechu lake threat, Rau said there is a need for monitoring the lake through satellites.

Other issues such as permission of the Centre to allow the state government to levy 10 paisa per unit generation tax on all power projects and implement provision of 12 per cent free electricity for all the power projects commissioned prior to year 1990, beside grant of legitimate share of the state in all the power projects like Bhakra dam, Dehar dam, Pong dam were also raised during the conference.

Heading: Haryana to help realise youth’s dollar dreams - Indian Express
Content:
Road connectivity is expected to see some improvement in the state with the Haryana Public Works Department (B&R) all set to start the widening and strengthening of at least five routes on the state highways 20 and 15A. The project would take one and a half year to complete at an estimated cost of Rs 240.45 crore

"The decision was taken after the observation of heavy traffic on these routes," said P S Singla, managing director, PWD (B&R). Besides the roads, all the bridges and culverts that fall on the routes would also be widened and strengthened, he added.

Sandeep Goyal, manager, PWD (B&R), said, "The project includes five different routes on the state highways 20 and 15A. While the cost of widening and strengthening of the Murthal-Sonepat route is around Rs 27.62 crore, the cost of Sampla-Jhajjar route and Sonepat-Khakhoda-Sampla route is Rs 33.99 crores and Rs 54.06 crore, respectively. The work of shifting of the electricity poles and lines has already started and is expected to get completed soon."

Goyal also added that as some portion of the forest land is also part of the project, the PWD department has applied for clearance from the Forest Department, which is expected soon. "While there would be number of trees that would be cut for the project, the exact number cannot be estimated right now. It has been long since the forest department was asked for the clearance and the go-ahead is expected anytime now," added Goyal.

Heading: Teachers get appointment letters after three-month-long wait - Indian Express
Content:
The Haryana government has come forward to to give legal shape to the dollar dreams of youth of the region. The Overseas Placement Bureau (OPB) of the Haryana government would organise walk-in interviews on September 21 at Panipat to recommend recruitment of technical staff projects in Canada.

Sources said the bureau and Canada-based SNK International Limited entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on July 29 to arrange manpower for Canada. OPB would be floating an advertisement for the interviews soon.

"The initiative is aimed at tackling illegal migration and providing a legal platform to skilled labour to go to Canada," said Krishan Kumar, the OPB member secretary and signatory on the MoU on behalf of Haryana.

"There is a projected requirement of about 3,500 persons in different categories in Canada. We have chosen Panipat because it houses a refinery and we can get the required skilled personnel for the projects in Canada," said OPB executive officer Ashok Sharma.

According to Sukhbir Singh Sidhu, the representative of SNK International in India, they had first approached Punjab government in October 2007, but Punjab did not take any initiative. He said Punjab Finance minister Manpreet Badal was also present in the meeting held to discuss the proposal.

Manpreet, when contacted, said that in his capacity as finance minister, he was "not the right person to talk on the issue". The then secretary (employment generation), NS Kalsi, said that such a proposal was "being considered" when he was posted in Punjab.

Heading: INLD rally on September 25 - Indian Express
Content:
The mental and physical agony of those who qualified for the posts of regular teachers finally subsided today with the process of issuing appointment letters finally beginning. The teachers had been waiting for the last three months to get their appointment letters and be assigned their stations of posting.

In fact, a list of 289 teachers for Hisar division was released on June 29, 2008 and dispatched from the office of Director of School Education in Chandigarh.

The first counseling was slated be held on August 28, 29, and 30, but was postponed. The next date was finalised after a number of visits by teachers for September 3,4, and 5, but again without any success. One more date was given on September 10, 11 and 12 which was against extended to September 13.

The teachers who had come here yesterday for the purpose were forced to wait for more than four hours at the office of the District Elementary Education Officer, but in futility, as the officer did not meet them. "Even drinking water is not available. We are being treated as a third grade citizens," said Vijay Singh, a teacher from Sundar.

The District Elementary Education Officer, Mitter Sen Malhotra, when contacted, said, "The documents were accepted on August 28, 29 and 30 and it takes time for the completion of the scrutiny of documents." He admitted that teachers were asked to come again on September 13 because of "tight schedule"

"The confusion was created by the teachers themselves as it was clearly mentioned on the notice board that the letters will be issued at 3 pm," he said.

Heading: Mewat tops our priority list, says Hooda - Indian Express
Content:
The Indian National Lok Dal (INLD) is making all possible efforts to make the birth anniversary of Devi Lal a huge event and has organised a rally at Bhiwani to mark the occasion. "We promise that this year the INLD rally will be even bigger than last year's rally,'' claimed Ashok Arora, INLD state president.

Almost all top leaders of the INLD have continuously been campaigning for the proposed rally in various parts of the state.

The INLD believes Bhiwani is going to be a power-centre again, with Bhiwani and Mahandergarh becoming a single Parliamentary constituency following delimitation. Ajay Chautala has already declared that he will be recontesting the Lok Sabha polls from Bhiwani.

Heading: The Guardian - Indian Express
Content: Haryana Chief Minister, Bhupinder Singh Hooda today assured that the state government would make every effort for the development of Mewat region and claimed that his government had already initiated projects to meet the water requirements of the area. Speaking at the Iftar Dawat organised at Badkhali Chawk in Mewat on Tuesday, the CM said that it gives him immense pleasure when people from different religions and sections jointly perform Roza Iftar. Roza gives lesson in tolerance, he added. HPCC president Phool Chand Mulana, HPCC executive president Kuldeep Sharma, MP Avtar Singh Bhadana and deputy speaker, Haryana Vidhan Sabha, Azad Mohammad, also addressed the gathering  and thanked the CM for celebrating his birth day with the Rozedars. Earlier, the CM inaugurated the second apparel design and training centre at Rozka-Meo.

Heading: Kareena Kapoor’s birthday plans - Indian Express
Content:
Kewal Dhaliwal is living his dream by bringing back glory to Somtimespassion is enough to make the world go round, and sometimes that is THE thing that makes the world go round. Either ways some people ensure that whether or not they have anything else going their way, they will never fall short of this ingredient. Kewal Dhaliwal is one of those few people. This Amritsar based theatre director was in town for the fifth Gursharan Singh Naat Utsav. "Dreams die without passion, no artist can afford that," smiles Dhaliwal whose theatre group Manch-Rangmanch is a platform for intellectual exchanges, an institution dedicated to social change and a desired destination of artists.

Dhaliwal brought to Chandigarh 'Dhamak Nagare Dee', based on the heroics of Dulla Bhatti - a folk legend of Punjab. "In line with the festival's theme, the play epitomizes social change. Dulla Bhatti lead an agrarian revolution against Akbar by refusing to pay taxes for the land he owned and ploughed. If you look at the current scenario in Punjab, the play is still relevant today where farmers are committing suicides due to burden of taxes et al," explains Dhaliwal who started his career with Gursharan Singh. Though the National School of Drama, Delhi, opened many avenues for him, Dhaliwal chose to stick to his roots and work in Punjab. "I was clear about theatre before I joined NSD. I am not against films but it's theatre that I express through the best."

His biggest challenge has been bringing Punjabi language theatre at par with other regional theatres of the country. "I started theatre activities in Amritsar when terrorism was at full swing. But getting Punjabi theatre the same respect as Marathi or Bengali theatre got proved equally hard. Unlike them we don't have ticket system in our part of the country. Despite that we have moved beyond them. Now not only Manch-Rangmanch, but groups like Punjab Naatshala and Rangmanch Bhawan are flourishing without government aid," says Dhaliwal, happy that Punjabi is gaining popularity nationally and internationally.

Wearing the director's hat for more than 100 plays and acting in more than 150, Dhaliwal looks back with content. His journey so far has been that of freedom with experimentation. He calls it 'total theatre', "meaning that every form is combined in my theatre, be it street, mime, modern, biographies, film scripts or even if a painting inspires me I'll bring it under the arc lights. I believe that when I can create something I should go ahead with it, but it has to sound convincing to the audience too," Dhaliwal points out.

Refusing to be bound by a theme, his plays, however, always leave behind a thought. Hence the recent production 'Main Punjab Bolda Haan', "it's about all that we are losing - kudiyan, chirhiyan, Punjabiyat...it's high time we took care of what's ours." Muse on that.

Heading: State sends team to inspect road project in Amritsar - Indian Express
Content:
If you ask us, we'll tell you she's ageless. But the blithe Kareena Kapoor adds yet another candle to her cake on September 21. As she turns 28, Kapoor insists she will be busy shooting for Raju Hirani's upcoming 3 Idiots in Ladakh.

"I don't intend celebrating my birthday with Saif since I will be shooting with Aamir Khan for my upcoming film," she says of her much-watched relationship with Saif Ali Khan. If only we didn't know the spontaneous Khan better, we'd believe that. It is also rumoured his sister Saba will be designing jewellery for Kapoor's birthday. A fact the actress considers too personal to be discussed.

As we catch up with Kapoor at the opening of a spa, the lass says: "The slimming equipment here is non invasive. Personally, I love yoga and I've controlled my weight by turning vegetarian. I encourage you to do the same," she smiles.

On the movie front, Kapoor has had some disappointments of late with the debacle of her last release, Tashan. But now, Kapoor will lend her voice to an animation film Roadside Romeo, about a spoilt dog roaming Mumbai streets. And as her beau is lending his voice to the film as well, Kapoor can't stop smiling. "I am looking forward to do an animation character. It is nice to know how people associate your voice with a particular character. Since Saif is with me in this project, it's even better," she blushes.

Heading: Good tidings for border farmers - Indian Express
Content:
Acting on the complaint of a few municipal councillors about flaws in the implementation of the much-hyped Rs 100-crore road laying project in the city, the Punjab Government today sent Technical Adviser to the Chief Minister B S Dhaliwal and Director, Quality Control, Harpreet Singh Brar, to inspect the ongoing work.

The officers took samples of the material being used in the laying of roads and also pulled up some of the officials and asked them to ensure quality. The samples would be sent to the laboratory of Mandi Board in Chandigarh and a report would be submitted to the CM, said Dhaliwal.

The project was inaugurated by Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal two months ago. Sources said municipal councillors, led by Sawinder Singh Sultanwind and Amarjit Singh, had met the CM a few days ago and submitted a complaint, alleging that the terms mentioned in the agreement with Rohan and Rajdeep Builders were not being complied with and local machinery was being used.

The CM had also pulled up Municipal Commissioner DPS Kharbanda.

"The workers are untrained and need guidance," Dhaliwal said, adding that there were a few glitches and the officials concerned have been directed to remove them.

Kharbanda, however, said experts had given them tips to deal with the project. He said the work had just begun and care would be taken to ensure that it was properly executed.

Heading: Bathinda resident claims his mobile phone ‘hacked’ - Indian Express
Content:
After a long wait, the Centre has agreed in-principle to give compensation to border farmers, on whose land 11 feet-wide patrolling tracks have been carved out.

The government is mulling Rs 5,000 per acre per annum as distress allowance to the border farmers whose land is beyond the fence. It has also been decided to increase the time of opening and closing the gates at the border and post a women's battalion of the BSF there.

Sources said these decisions were taken in a recent meeting of the Punjab government with the Border Management Wing of the Ministry of Home Affairs.

Besides the panchayat and the government land, about 475 acres were taken from farmers to build the patrolling track. Now, the state government has started identifying the land and its owners, said sources.

An officer said, "The Revenue Department and the deputy commissioners concerned have been told to submit a detailed report, which will be sent to the MHA for the release of compensation. About Rs 100-crore compensation is expected."

Farmers whose land is beyond the fence cannot grow a crop that is over 2.5 feet tall, besides they can work only from 10 am to 5 pm, and are frisked every time they go to their fields. Earlier, no woman could accompany them, as there were only male securitymen at the border. But with the posting of a women's battalion, the trend would change.

There are about 21,000 acres beyond the fence. Sources said the MHA has not agreed fully to the state government's proposal of opening the border from dawn to dusk, but has decided on separate timings for summer and winter.

There are 198 border openings in Punjab, and the State Home Department has written to all the DCs to find out if the villages want these to be opened. But, panchayats would have to pass a resolution for it, after which the state would take up the matter with the MHA.

Highlights
* Compensation for farmers on whose land patrolling tracks have been carved out.
* The government is mulling Rs 5,000 per acre as distress allowance to those whose land is beyond the fence.
* It has been decided to increase the time of opening and closing of the border.
* A women's battalion of the BSF will be posted at the border.

Heading: Son-in-law of Makkar booked, poll deferred - Indian Express
Content:
A Bathinda resident has complained to police the about hacking of his mobile phone.

Anil Jaura claimed that his phone was "misused/hacked" on September 10 and 11 and ISD calls were made to the UK and Australia. Fearing that his mobile phone might have been used for subversive activities against the national interests, Jaura has sought protection for himself and demanded registration of a criminal case against the accused.

Bathinda SSP Ashish Chaudhry said the ASP has been to told look into the matter. "During the investigation, police may seek the opinion of IT experts and the telecom company," said Chaudhry.

In his complaint, Jaura, who is son of BJP's BC cell district president Har Yashpal Jaura, gave time-wise details of the ISD calls, few of which were of more than 40 minutes.

Jaura said he came to know about the "hacking" after his outgoing service was snapped and he was told that his mobile bill had exceeded the credit limit. Saying that he had no acquaintances in the UK and Australia, he claimed that the calls were made during the night when phone is with him.

Jaura said officials of the telecom company told him that the records showed that same IMEI number was reflecting in local calls made by him.

However, an official working at the back-end operations of the telecom service provider in Chandigarh told The Indian Express that the perusal of records of ISD calls made from the number showed a different IMEI number.

However, telecom experts did not rule the possibility of cloning of the SIM.

Heading: Video-conferencing between jails, courts gets President’s approval - Indian Express
Content:
After registration of a case against relatives of Independent candidate Surinder Singh Goga on the complaint of SAD candidate Gulwinder Singh two days ago, the police have booked the complainant.

Case against Gulwinder, who is the son-in-law of SGPC president Avtar Singh Makkar, and 50-60 other unidentified persons was registered on the complaint of Pritam Kaur, a resident of ward number 4. They have been booked for allegedly inflicting serious injuries on Goga and his son and thrashing the presiding officer and the assistant presiding officer.

It was also alleged that Gulwinder, in connivance with a large number of outsiders, got bogus votes polled.

Meanwhile, the Punjab and Haryana High Court, which had deferred the polls till today following the violence on Sunday, directed the District Magistrate and the SSP to file a reply to the notice by September 22 and deferred the election till further orders.

Heading: Patiala most neglected, says Badal - Indian Express
Content:
With President Pratibha Patil giving her assent to a Bill, decks have been cleared for the introduction of video-conferencing between jails and courts in Punjab.

Punjab Jails and Justice Minister Hira Singh Gabria today said the Centre had conveyed this decision to the state government through a communiqué.

This move would not only save money of the Police Department, but also ensure quick and efficient dispensation of criminal justice, he added.

The legislative process required an amendment to Section 167 (3) of the Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC) so that the persons in judicial custody could be produced before the courts either in person or through the medium of video-conferencing, an official release said here.

The Punjab assembly had passed the Bill for the amendment of the Section in December 2007. The Bill was reserved for the assent of the President.

Heading: Passport office staff protest arrest of colleague on graft charges - Indian Express
Content:
Announces Rs 250-cr ultra-modern bus stand and AC vegetable market for city

Terming Patiala as the "most neglected" city of the state, Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal today announced two major projects for it -- a Rs 250-crore ultra-modern air-conditioned bus stand and an air-conditioned vegetable market.

After spending the entire day in Patiala, the hometown and assembly constituency of his bete noire Amarinder Singh , Badal said, "Patialvis have suffered at Captain's hands." Incidentally, this is Badal's second visit to Patiala in three days.

The CM advised Amarinder to thank him for pumping in money in his constituency. "If he had some guts, he should have been thanking me through a telegram," he said.

After listening to the problem of the public in the remaining 15 wards of the city, Badal today doled out liberal grants.

The CM would lay the foundation stone of the first-of-its-kind air-conditioned vegetable market in the city tomorrow.

He said the Rs 250-crore multi-storied AC bus terminal would be set up on the public-private-partnership model, whereby the private player would bear the entire cost of the project and would be allowed to utilise four floors for opening shopping malls and offices. It would also provide Rs 2 crore annually to the PRTC. Badal assured the residents that Patiala would soon become one of the most progressive cities of Punjab.

When commented that he was focusing on Patiala ever since Capt's ouster from the Vidhan Sabha, he said, "I am just doing my job."

He asked the district administration and Municipal Corporation to jointly prepare an action plan to address the civic problems of the residents. He assured that there would be no scarcity of funds.

'Capt insulted Patialvis'
PATIALA:Reacting sharply to the statement of Capt Amarinder Singh that Badal was trying to bribe the people of Patiala, the CM said, "Amarinder has insulted the residents by charging them with accepting bribe." He said such a statement from a former CM for the people who elected him was an insult to them. Badal said Capt should not undermine democracy. His statements were an outcome of frustration, the CM added.

CM 'lights up' Patiala
PATIALA:The presence of Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal in the city proved a boon for the residents, who faced no cuts the whole day despite power shortage. While residents in all other towns in the state sweated for over five hours on Tuesday, Patialvis had their fill of power. However, rural areas in the town faced more than six-hour cuts due to the extra electricity consumed by Patiala.

Heading: State breaks 5-year jinx, gets bumper wheat crop - Indian Express
Content:
The visitors to the Regional Passport Office, Jalandhar, had a tough time as the employees struck work for three hours against the arrest of a clerk on corruption charges by the Vigilance Bureau (VB) yesterday.

They raised slogans against the VB and claimed that the employee was innocent.

"I had come to submit my passport application after changing four buses from my village. But this agitation has spoiled my day," said Nirmaljit Singh of Shahkot in Jalandhar. The employees did not even pay heed to the request of Regional Passport officer AK Mahajan to resume work.
