Notably, clerk Bhupinder Kalia was nabbed by a team of VB sleuths, led by DSP Harpreet Singh Benipal, for accepting bribe from an applicant.

The DSP said they were informed by a local resident that Kalia was seeking Rs 2,000 for sending a letter to the Ministry of External Affairs in his case.

Heading: Students to get packaged mid-day meal, teachers relief - Indian Express
Content:
After yield stagnation for almost five years, the state has finally registered growth. The kharif crop of 2007-08 has crossed the mark of 4,500 kilogram per hectare.

Giving reasons for the bumper crop, experts said while the weather gods were generous throughout the season, investment by the National Food Security Mission, which covers almost 10 districts in Punjab, also paid rich dividends. The districts covered under the mission include Amritsar, Bathinda, Ferozepur, Gurdaspur, Hoshiarpur, Ludhiana, Sangrur, Tarn Taran, Mohali and Barnala.

Notably, the yield crossed the 4,500-kilogram mark in 2000-01, when the average per hectare yield was 4,563, followed by 4,532 kilograms in 2001-02. However till 2007, the per-hectare average yield hovered around 4,200 kilograms.

According to the annual district-wise data collected by the Department of Agriculture, Fatehgarh Sahib has recorded the maximum increase of nearly 10 kilograms per hectare as compared to last year, followed by Ferozepur, Kapurthala, Moga and Muktsar, which recorded an increase of 5 kilograms per hectare.

B S Sidhu, director, agriculture, said, "This increase in the yield calls for more investments in the agriculture sector. While the Centre had pumped in Rs 30 crore for the 10 districts, the state gave a matching grant for the rest. And it has shown results."

Reasons
* Congenial weather
* High MSP
* Investment by the National Food Security Mission, which covers almost 10 districts, paid dividends

Heading: 17 dengue cases confirmed, more suspected - Indian Express
Content:
With the launch of packaged food for the mid-day meal scheme in the district today, the state government eased the burden on schoolteachers. Punjab Education Minister Upinderjit Kaur launched the scheme at a government school in Jadla in the presence of Director General of School Education (DGSE) Krishan Kumar.

Packaged meal would be served to 55,000 students of classes I to VIII in about 450 schools of the district at a cost of Rs 3.2 lakh per month.

About 50 women would cook the meal in a centralised kitchen and 20 vehicles would be used to transport it. The scheme was launched in Tarn Taran yesterday. At present, Nawanshahr, Tarn Taran and Ferozepur have been selected for this pilot project.

Two NGOs, Istri Shakti Sangathan and Indacare, have been engaged to prepare and supply the food.

Heading: Archaic fogging machines become white elephant for MC - Indian Express
Content:
Number of patients admitted to different hospitals in the city has already touched the 200 mark

The number of suspected dengue cases diagnosed in the city is increasing steadily. According to reports, the number of patients admitted to different hospitals in the city has already touched the 200 mark.

The Health department, however, says that all the patients are not confirmed cases of dengue as they have been put to rapid test only and have yet not tested positive for quantitative test like Elisa.

The number of patients at Dayanand Medical College and Hospital (DMCH) who are believed to have contracted dengue has reportedly touched the 125 mark. As on Sunday, the number was 120. Of them, 56 are the residents of the district while the remaining are from other parts of the state.

Meanwhile, the Christian Medical College and Hospital (CMCH) has also registered 64 cases. Of them, 48 are the residents of the district.

Meanwhile, various other hospitals in the city have also admitted patients suspected to have contracted dengue fever. SPS Apollo Hospitals and MD Oswal Cancer Hospital have reportedly admitted 10 patients each for the treatment of the suspected disease so far.

On the other hand, the Health department today confirmed three more patients of dengue. The department has so far confirmed 17 patients of dengue in the district while the confirmatory reports of some other patients are still awaited.

A senior Health department official said hospitals generally go in for rapid test to suggest the presence of dengue. "These hospitals conduct rapid test and therefore the number of suspected patients may be high. But the disease is actually confirmed with the help of quantitative test - Elisa," the official said.

Meanwhile, the Health department has also started a campaign to make the residents aware of the risks of stagnant water in and around their houses.

Heading: Trucker on a hitting spree wreaks havoc, 2 injured - Indian Express
Content:
Rupees one crore is the annual expenditure to run nine obsolete fogging machines by the Municipal Corporation, which excludes the expenditure of fuel and salary of employees. The expenditure crosses more than Rs 3 crore per annum.

A new machine equipped with latest technology costs less than Rs 1.25 lakh. Hence, with an expenditure of Rs 94 lakh, all the 75 wards in the city can get one brand new machine each. However, the corporation is not yet serious about the idea to implement it. Hence, they do not mind spending fat bills on the fogging operations which have little effect in containing dengue and malaria cases in the city.

The fogging operations, which are carried out after every two months, are not effective enough to kill mosquitoes.

The MC, which boasts of 16 fogging machines, has only nine in working order and they too need a lot of maintenance. The municipal corporation records show that to run a fogging machine for an hour, Rs 3,000 is required which involves 60 litres of diesel to run the vehicle and 5 litres of petrol which is mixed in pesticide and used for spraying purposes. "All this has failed to contain mosquito breeding in the city. The corporation must think of buying new machines or can outsource the job," said SAD councillor Jagbir Singh Sokhi.

Interestingly, Sokhi, with his own expenditure, is also buying a new machine for his ward.

For effective results, the Health department recommends the spraying of the mosquito-killing medicine twice a week. However, councillors complain they don't get the machine even after two months.

Sources revealed that since a new fogging machine is available between Rs 40,000 and Rs 1.5 lakh,

the MC is yet to decide on the price range.

Meanwhile, the health wing of the MC said that they are leaving no stone unturned to clean the city. Dr Charanjit Uppal, medical officer health (MOH), "The plan has been chalked out to clean the city.

The fogging is up to the mark in all the wards as per the availability of the machines. "

Heading: Cheque bounce case: Delhi trader gets 1 yr in jail - Indian Express
Content:
Two two-wheeler drivers got injured after a truck hit them near the Cheema Chowk here today. The truck driver has been arrested and his vehicle has been impounded.

The injured have been identified as Amarjit Singh, who has been admitted to the CMC Hospital while one Inderjit Kumar has been admitted to the Civil Hospital. Amarjit Singh was on his motorcycle while Inderjit Kumar was on his scooter when the speeding truck hit them.

According to eyewitnesses, around noon the truck first hit a car near the Cheema Chowk. After hitting the car, the driver sped away. At this, the persons in the car started chasing him. In an attempt to escape, the truck driver accelerated the speed of the truck and hit the vehicles of Amarjit and Inderjit.

From the Cheema Chowk, he sped towards the Dholewal chowk bridge and then went back to the Pratap Chowk.

Angry residents protested outside Division Number 6 police station as the police failed to nab the erring truck driver. Finally, the police swung into action and arrested the truck driver and impounded his vehicle.

Speaking to Newsline, Division number 6 SHO Gurtej Singh said that the truck driver had been booked for rash and negligent driving and putting the lives of others at risk.

The SHO said that the condition of Amarjit Singh was critical and the condition of Inderjit Kumar was stable and out of danger.

Heading: Abandoned briefcase creates panic in Khanna - Indian Express
Content:
The court of judicial magistrate Randhir Verma has sentenced Narinder Gulati, a Delhi- based businessman, to one-year imprisonment in a cheque bounce case. Gulati has also been directed to pay Rs 5,000 as fine.

Baldev Singh of Chander Lok Colony, Basti Jodhewal, had filed a complaint that Gulati had taken loan of Rs 1 lakh from him. He said that Gulati gave a cheque of Rs 1 lakh to him on October 15, 2004, with an assurance that the cheque could be encashed on its presentation. When the cheque was presented for encashment, the same was dishonored by the banker of the accused with the remarks to 'Refer to Drawer' vide memo dated December 21, 2004. Thereafter, a legal notice was served upon the accused requesting him to make the payment of the dishonored cheque, but he failed to make the payment.

On the other hand, the accused pleaded innocence and claimed false implication in the case. In his defence, he also examined two witnesses Rajinder Khanna and Aarti Gulati.

Pronouncing the verdict, the judge held the prosecution guilty in the case.

Heading: Tehabazari operation continues - Indian Express
Content:
Panic gripped the GTB market as an abandoned briefcase and a car with a pistol were spotted in the town. Both incidents happened at the same time as shopkeepers spotted a 'pistol' in the car.

The police were on their heels for over two hours but no bomb was found. Later, the owners came forward to claim their belongings.

The police party led by SP (D) Gurmit Singh reached the spot and cordoned off the area. It was later established that the brief case belonged to a Ludhiana-based businessman Vivek Walia. The case was stolen from his car.

The police impounded the car and found that the pistol in the car was a toy.

The SP told Newsline, "Walia's briefcase was stolen from his car near the bus stand. As the thieves failed to break open the briefcase, they threw it near the GTB market.

He added, "As the police party was enquiring about the briefcase, Walia reached the police station to lodge a complaint about his stolen briefcase."

About the other incident, the SP said, "The owner parked his car in the market and went for shopping. Some shopkeepers panicked after seeing the pistol and reported the matter to the police."

Heading: ‘Save environment’ to be the theme of Kisan Mela this time - Indian Express
Content:
The Tehbazari branch on Tuesday continued with its operations at Ferozepur Road.

The major focus of the team was to remove the structures which had returned after yesterday's operations. Apart from this, encroachments made by Ansal Plaza and few other showroom owners on MC service lane were also demolished.

In addition to this, they also removed a few vehicles from the service lane of Municipal Corporation on Ferozepur Road. However the Tehbazari axe fell only on the two wheelers while four wheelers parked in the service lane were left untouched.

Heading: Blight noticed in paddy fileds - Indian Express
Content:
The two-day Kisan Mela with the theme 'Save environment, save Punjab' will be held at PAU mela grounds on September 18-19. Field demonstrations, display stalls, exhibitions and other activities relevant to the theme of mela will be organised. Dr S.S. Johl, an eminent farm economist, and former Vice-Chancellor will inaugurate the mela.

Stalls by different departments of PAU will be put up on the mela route. In the main pandal, an agro-industrial exhibition will be organised. The programme of the mela will include technical tips by PAU experts. A question-answer session will be organised wherein PAU experts will respond to the farmers' queries. The seeds of different crop varieties will also be put on sale in the mela.

There will be special stalls for the sale of farm literature and enrolment of new members for Changi Kheti and progressive farming monthly magazines. Fruit plants will also be sold. There will be stalls by different departments of College of Home Science of interest to women. Dr Manjit Singh Kang, Vice-Chancellor, PAU, has appealed to farmers and farm women to participate in the mela as it will provide them opportunity to interact with experts and to get an exposure to the latest farm technology.

Dr N.S. Malhi, Director of Extension Education said that on this occasion three farmers namely, Avtar Singh Sidhu (Gunachaur village, Nawanshahar district). Chamkaur Singh (Enna Bajwa village, Sangrur district) and Devinder Singh (Muskabad village, Ludhiana district) will be honoured with the presentation of Dalip Singh Dhaliwal memorial award, Parvasi Bharti Purskar and Ujagar Singh Dhaliwal memorial award, respectively, for their excellence under diversified farming. He said that a progressive farmer and a member of Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices, Mohinder Singh Grewal will also be honoured for his achievements in farming.

According to Dr Jagtar Singh Dhiman, Additional Director of Communication, the proceedings of Kisan Mela will be broadcast live from Dehati Programme of All India Radio, Jalandhar on September 18. According to Dr. Jaswinder Singh Bhalla, Convener of the Cultural Programme Committee, famous folk artists of Punjab including Bhupinder Gill, Neelam, Sukhwinder Sukhi, Ranjit Mani, Nirmal Sidhu, Harpal Pali, Rode Wale Kavisher, Hakam Sufi, etc. will be presenting their programmes on the occasion. Farmers from different parts of Punjab and adjoining states are expected to participate in the mela.

Heading: Tax raids at 3 brick kilns - Indian Express
Content:
According to a survey carried out by PAU team of plant pathologists, incidence of blight has been noticed in paddy fields in different parts of Punjab.

Providing details, Dr H.S. Rewal, Head of the Department of Plant Pathology, said that the disease has been noticed in all varieties of Basmati grown in the areas of Sangrur, Patiala, Hoshiarpur and Ludhiana. He said the disease appeared as yellowish green stripes running from tip downwards and the affected leaf started drying from the margins.

In the severely affected plants, the drying up starts from the top. He said farmers should not spray pesticides to control the disease as these are not effective against it. Since the disease required high humidity for its development, farmers would do well not to allow stagnation of water in the fields, added he.

Dr Rewal advised the farmers to contact experts at PAU, Ludhiana, and its regional stations in case they needed any further clarification.

Heading: ‘Only Rs 2 benefit against promise of full talk-time’ - Indian Express
Content:
The state excise and taxation department today raided three brick kilns and found enough documents pointing towards tax evasion.

A team of excise and taxation officers (ETOs), Manjinder Sidhu and Harshwardhan, inspected Anish Kumar Brick Kiln at Nandpur village in Sahnewal while another team of ETOs — V.P. Singh, Balwant Rai and Arun Thamman —inspected Raj Bricks and Rajgarh Bricks, located at Rajgarh village in Doraha.

The documents seized from the three units will be scrutinized to know the extent of tax evasion, said the officials. The raids were carried out at the directive of the assistant excise and taxation commissioner (AETC), Amrit Kaur Gill.

Heading: Ball badminton tourney to start  from tomorrow - Indian Express
Content:
Though mobile phone users were expecting a good benefit coming out of the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) order to provide full talk time to the consumers, there is only a benefit of Rs 2.

Various telecom companies have only slashed the charges by Rs 2 only. A subscriber of a leading telecom company, who expected to get a good deal for the recharge money, said he only got Rs 87 talk time against Rs 100 while earlier it was Rs 85.

He reacted strongly, saying, "I thought there will be a good increase in the talk-time allotted against the recharge money in the pre-paid top-up, but the things are not much different even today."

Another consumer who got the prepaid top-up on his account with another leading telecom company said, "These companies are fooling us and nothing else. I do not exactly know what TRAI has instructed them to do, but what I know is that I was supposed to get full talk time for the money I am spending on the recharge. There is only a benefit of Rs 2 against the big promise of full talk-time."

Recent directive by TRAI stated the subscribers were entitled to get full talk time on the amount spent on the recharge along with only administrative fee which should not exceed Rs 2 and some other applicable taxes.

On the other hand, Praveen Kumar, divisional engineer (marketing) of BSNL, said the company was already providing full talk time for its subscribers. "We are already providing full talk time though there may be other operators which are not doing so," he said.

A deputy manager with a leading telecom company however said that they had not received any communication in this regard and added that the company was deducting the administrative fees and service tax from the prepaid top-up money.

Heading: We share common areas of concern in agriculture, says Chinese panel - Indian Express
Content:
The Ball Badminton Association (BBA)of Mohali will conduct sub-junior ball badminton championship on September 18 to 19 at BMD Public School-63 in Mohali.

According to Baldev Singhji, president BBA, players from Punjab are expected to take part in the tournament and based on performance, players will be selected to take part in the sub-junior national championship to be held in Amritsar.

Amit to participate in body building meet
Amit Bhatia, a student of KLSD College was selected by Punjab Armature Building Association for the National Body Building Championship to be held from September 24 to 26 at Pune in the 55 to 60 kg category.

Sushil Kumar to be felicitated on Sept 20
Olympian Sushil Kumar will be honoured by Gulzar Wrestling Akhara and Mohali District Wrestling Association on September 20 at 2 pm at Akhara Campus, Zirakpur.

Sushil Kumar made the nation proud by clinching bronze medal at Beijing Olympics.

Badminton tourney from today
Chandigarh Badminton Club under the aegis of Chandigarh Badminton Association will organise XXth Yonex Chandigarh State Badminton Championship from September 17 to 21 at Sports Complex, Sector 42 in Chandigarh.

Heading: GADVASU to hold ‘Pashu Palan mela’ - Indian Express
Content:
A three-member Chinese delegation comprising Dr Wang Qiming, Counsellor (Science and Technology), Dr Cao Jianru, First Secretary (Science and Technology) and Qin Hongming, Second Secretary (Science and Technology), Embassy of the People's Republic of China in India along with officials from Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) of Northern Region, Chandigarh, visited the Punjab Agricultural University today.

They held discussions with the PAU Vice-Chancellor, Dr Manjit Singh Kang in the presence of the deans of the constituent colleges of PAU, dean, postgraduate studies, registrar, coordinators of research and heads of different departments were also present.

Dr Jianru said that it was his desire to visit PAU to learn about its on-going and future programmes and to identify areas in which PAU and Chinese institutes could collaborate in agricultural research and developmental programme. He said that the Chinese Ministry of Agriculture during its parleys with its Indian counterpart had identified some areas that would be further made operative in October.

Dr M.S. Aulakh, Dean, College of Agriculture, Dr P.K. Gupta, Dean, College of Agricultural Engineering, Dr Tejwant Singh, Dean, College of Basic Sciences and Dr S. Jaswal, Dean, College of Home Science, informed the delegates about the educational, research and extension programmes in their respective colleges.

Earlier, Dr Jagtar Singh Dhiman, Additional Director of Communication, while welcoming the delegates elaborated on the mandate of PAU highlighting the research achievements, constraints of Punjab agriculture and efforts being made in the direction of national food and nutritional security. He delved on the growing international linkages of PAU with different globally reputed organizations/institutes.

Deliberating on "Agriculture in China," Dr Jianru said that both India and China had common agricultural concerns. He said that intensive farm management, substantial use of fertilizers and chemicals for grains (273 kg per hectare) and cash crops (441 kg per hectare) and inter-cropping were characteristics of Chinese agriculture.

He said that with total fertilizer use of 56.71 MT (pure nutrient), China was number one in the world. He shared the ways toward rural modernization saying that in 2006 there were 23.14 million township enterprises. Dr Jianru also discussed various measures of agricultural reforms and planned economy.

He said that for building new rural community, increased productivity, improved living standards, civilized rural culture and custom, clean and tidy village, democratic village management were the goals of the national mission for building new rural community. Dr Jianru said that the per capita consumption of grain, vegetables and edible oil was 206 kg, 101 kg and 6 kg, respectively, in 2006 while per capita consumption of meat, poultry and eggs was 26 kg. The per capita consumption of aquatic products was 5 kg. He said that for every 100 farm households, there were 89 TV sets, 43 washing machines, 23 refrigerators and 345 motor cycles. The per capita dwelling space was 31 square meter, he said.

The visiting delegates interacted with PAU experts on various relevant issues. The on-going programmes at PAU were discussed by the scientists with them.

Prof V.K. Sehgal spoke on the research being carried out in the area of enhancing shelf-life of crops, freezing of fruits and vegetables and briquette formation from paddy straw and other waste materials. It emerged that there are many areas such as hybrid rice, vegetables, marketing and trade, fruit and vegetable processing at rural level, etc. in agricultural science and technology where Chinese institutes could collaborate.

Team members were shown around the Museum of Soils, Museum of Water Resources of northern India, Museum of Plant Breeding and Genetics, experimental farms of the Departments of Soil and Water Engineering, and Agronomy where the delegates interacted with the faculty members.

Heading: Chandigarh seize initiative as Satnam’s fiver puts Ludhiana on backfoot - Indian Express
Content:
Guru Angad Dev Veterinary and Animal Sciences University (GADVASU), Ludhiana will organise two-day Pashu Palan mela starting on September 18. Former vice-chairman of Punjab State Planning Board, Dr S.S. Johal will inaugurate the mela while Dr V.K. Taneja, Vice-Chancellor, GADVASU, will be the guest of honour.

Dr O.S. Parmar, Director of Extension Education, GADVASU said that the varsity's elite animals like murrah buffaloes, bulls, crossbreed cows, goats, pigs, rabbits, poultry and fish will be displayed at the event. Books on dairy farming "Package of Practices for Animal Husbandry" will also be made available to the farmers who can register their names for the varsity's training programmes.

The mineral mixture and uromin lick prepared by the university will also be sold at nominal rates. Teat dip practice and acaricide drug applications will be demonstrated and value addition of milk and milk technologies will be discussed. Milk and meat products will also be sold at the mela.

Different departments of the College of Veterinary Science, College of Dairy Science and Technology and College of Fisheries, will arrange exhibitions to display new techniques and practices for the benefit of the livestock farmers and will respond to their queries.

All the departments of the university including Punjab Dairy Development and Fishery Department, Milkfed and Markfed will put up stalls at the exhibition. During this fair, different organisations dealing with production/marketing of animal feed, medicine, vaccines, animal germplasm, animal farm machinery, milk and meat processing machinery, fodder seed, animal sciences and banking institutes will provide valuable information and know-how to the livestock farmers.

Due to increasing popularity of live-stock profession, a number of companies have evinced interest in putting up their stalls in the exhibition pandal but due to shortage of space, the university is unable to accommodate all these companies.

Various associations like Progressive Dairy Farmers' Association, Punjab Piggery Farmers Association, Innovative Fish Farming Association and Punjab Goat Farming Association will also put up their stalls.

Heading: 2-day ball badminton tourney from tomorrow - Indian Express
Content:
Spinning a deadly web around the Ludhiana batsmen, left-arm spinner Satnam Singh emerged as the star of the first day with five wickets in the finals of Katoch Shield Championship being held at PCA Stadium on Tuesday.

The left-arm spinner came up with an inspiring spell to wreak havoc on Ludhiana team to return with a rich haul of five wickets and left the opposition in disarray to reduce them to 141 in 68.2 overs. Ludhiana skipper Ankur Kakkar had an off day as his decision to bat first backfired as his batsmen failed to cope up with the tidy length and line maintained by the Chandigarh bowlers. The fact that Ludhiana lost six wickets for just 30 runs speaks the amount of pressure created by the Chandigarh bowlers. It was a fine sixth wicket partnership of 66 runs between wicket-keeper Gitansh Khera (46) and Bharat Malhotra (35) that somehow revived the fluctuating Ludhiana innings. Skipper Ankur tried to salvage the innings but didn't find any company from the other end. He remained unbeaten on 15 runs.

Replying to Ludhiana's modest total, Chandigarh also didn't start on a bright note and lost wickets in heap to be left tottering at 56 for 4 in 26 overs at the end of the day's play. Medium-pacer Sunny Kumar Malhotra captured three quick wickets and brought back Ludhiana into the match. Gurkirat Singh (16) and Gaurav Gambhir (2) were holding the crease at the end of first day's game.

Brief Scores:

Ludhiana: 141 for all in 68.2 overs (Gitansh Khera 46, Bharat Malhotra 35, Karan Goel 22, Satnam 5 for 35, Naresh Gogian 2 for 38, Gaurav Marwah 2 for 39); Chandigarh: 56 for 4 in 26 overs (Sarul Kanwar 12, Gurkirat Singh 16 no, Gaurav Gambhir 2 no).

Heading: Cong-SP talks on seat-sharing hang in balance - Indian Express
Content:
The Ball Badminton Association of Mohali will conduct sub-junior ball badminton championship on September 18 to 19 at BMD Public School-63 in Mohali. According to Baldev Singhji, chairman of Baba Mal Das Charitable Trust and president of the association, players from Punjab are expected to take part in the tournament. He added, based on performance, players will be selected to take part in the sub-junior national championship to be held in Amritsar.

Caba honours Jerath
Chandigarh in a felicitation function, orgainsed by the Chandigarh Amateur Boxing Association (CABA), the association officials honoured CABA, secretary, DR CK Jerath after he returned from Beijing Olympics as Technical Observer.

Jerath has toured different countries like Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Dubai, Pakistan, Iran, Dubai, Nepal, Germany, Turkey, Germany, Australia and China as boxing official of the Indian team. He was the manager of the Indian squad which grabbed five medals during the Commonwealth Games held in Melbourne in 2006. He was recently re-elected as vice-president of the Indian Amateur Boxing Federation (IABF).

Among those who were present on the occasion included DSP, Chandigarh Police, KIP Singh, and Anu Chatrath, Chandigarh councilor.

Sushil Kumar to be felicitated
CHANDIGARH:Olympian Sushil Kumar will be honoured by Gulzar Wrestling Akhara and Mohali District Wrestling Association on September 20 at 2 pm at Akhara Campus, Zirakpur. Sushil Kumar made the nation proud by clinching bronze medal at Beijing Olympics.

Heading: Maya’s projects remain only on paper - Indian Express
Content:
Seat-sharing talks between the Congress and the Samajwadi Party (SP) have hit a roadblock with the two parties refusing to concede any ground on their claims on about a dozen seats.

After their second round of talks on September 8, the two sides had decided to formally exchange their "final list" of seats, including the contentious ones on which they wouldn't compromise, on September 13 and meet two days later to take a final call on it. Neither has the lists been exchanged, nor has the meeting taken place.

Top leadership of the two parties, including Congress president Sonia Gandhi and SP chief Mulayam Singh Yadav, are now likely to sort out the differences, according to Congress sources. So far, the negotiations have been led by Rahul Gandhi, Digvijay Singh and Rita Bahuguna Joshi from the Congress, while the SP interlocutors include Amar Singh and Ram Gopal Yadav.

In the last meeting, the Congress had floated the idea of "friendly contests" on some seats, but the SP refused. The y include Farrukhabad, Pratapgarh, Moradabad, Kushinagar, Rampur, Gonda, Fatehpur Sikri, and Domariaganj among others.

The Congress, which had initially laid claims on 30 seats, later came down to 26, while the SP, which had initially offered 12 seats, conceded about half-dozen more during the two rounds of negotiations, said Congress sources. The ruling party at the Centre is, however, reluctant to settle for less than 25 seats on the plea that delimitation of constituencies had changed the "ground situation" in favour of the Congress.

While these irritants held up the seat-sharing talks in Uttar Pradesh, Amar Singh declared on Monday that the SP would have no truck with the Congress in Madhya Pradesh because the latter had poached 4 SP MLAs in the state. Digvijay Singh, however, refuted it on Tuesday, saying that the Congress had no role in it.

"They have resigned on their own," he said. Asked if these SP defectors could be considered for Congress tickets, he replied, "May be."

Heading: Minister blames Centre for UP’s ‘health debacle’ - Indian Express
Content:
During the last 18 months, since BSP came to power in Uttar Pradesh — the most backward state of the country — Chief Minister Mayawati announced around a dozen mega development projects worth Rs 130,000 crore. But most of these projects still remain only on paper.

All these projects are related to development of infrastructure in different sectors, like roads, public transport, technical education, health, tourism, power, aviation, urban development.

To project its seriousness to get these projects moving, the state government unveiled a new State Economic Policy in December 2007. It also created a new Department of Infrastructure. But so far, there has been a very little progress.

The only exceptions are the 165-km Yamuna Expressway between Greater Noida and Agra, which is expected to become operational before the 2010 Commonwealth Games in New Delhi, and thermal power projects like Anpara C, Rosa and Meja where work is on currently.

Explaining the delays, a government official said: "These are big projects. We have invited global tenders to give everyone an equal opportunity. This takes time." He also justified frequent changes in the terms and conditions of bidding for the projects.

The industry, however, thinks otherwise. S B Agarwal of ASSOCHAM, UP Chapter, was categorical that "the atmosphere in UP is not congenial and the infrastructure not appropriate for industry."

He said power crisis and political instability were two major factors deterring investors to come to UP.

An uncertain future?
Integrated Urban Rejuvenation Plan
The project envisages improving the urban infrastructural facilities in eight towns — Ghaziabad, Lucknow, Kanpur, Agra, Aligarh, Varanasi, Allahabad and Meerut — to international standards. The project is expected to bring in an investment of Rs 12,000 crores into urban infrastructure.

After extending the last date of bidding for appointing a consultant thrice, the state government has finally selected a consultant. The consultant will help the Housing and Urban Development Department in identifying the PPP component of this plan and will also assist in the process of inviting the investors.

Ganga Expressway
The Rs 30,000 crore eight-lane expressway from Greater Noida to Ballia in eastern UP is proposed to come up on the left bank of river Ganga. The acquisition of land for the main carriageway was scheduled to begin by July-end but the process could not take off due to alignment problem at Narora and Varanasi. Officials now claim that the problem has been sorted out.

Mutli-Speciality Hospitals
Under this Rs 1,150 crore project, seven multi-speciality hospitals were to be set up in Lucknow, Agra, Saharanpur, Amebdkar Nagar, Azamgarh, Bijnor and Jalaun. At present, the government is in the process of selecting a consultancy firm which would assist the Department of Medical and Health in preparing a blueprint for the project.

Public Transport Infrastructure
To meet the increasing demand for public transport and to provide better public transport to people, the government, opened 460 routes for the private players in March. This gave the private players an opportunity to ply their buses on these routes along with Uttar Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation (UPSRTC) buses. In its terms and conditions, the government made it mandatory for each private player to bring in 4,000 or more buses, which the investors found impractical. On failing to attract the investors, the government first brought the number down to 1,000 which has been further reduced to 250 now.

Bara and Karchhana Thermal Power projects
The Rs 15,000 crore projects aim to set up a 2 X 660 MWpower plant at Karchhana and a 3 X 660 MW power plant at Bara. After conducting the bids three times in about last eight months, and changing the terms and conditions several times, the government has now got 23 companies that have shown interest in these power projects.
— ENS

Heading: First came the news of his death, then story of his survival - Indian Express
Content:
The Uttar Pradesh government has blamed the "biased attitude" of the Centre for the occurrence of diseases like polio, encephalitis and measles in the state.

On Tuesday, Health Minsiter Anant Mishra gave a detailed background of how the Centre had allegedly failed to provide adequate equipment and facilities to check such diseases. "The Central government had supplied excess cold storage equipment to Maharastra and only one-fourth of the requirement to Uttar Pradesh," he alleged.

According to the minister, Uttar Pradesh requires around 1,459 lakh doses of polio, JE, measles and other vaccines for routine immunisation. To store this, the Centre had supplied only 652 iceline freezers and 1,183 deep freezers.

But Maharastra, which uses around 578 lakh doses of the vaccines, was supplied with 1,180 iceline freezers and around 3,056 deep freezers.

"They can condemn us. But it is because of them that we are suffering. They neither supply us with vaccines on time and nor provide us with proper amount of cold chain equipment," Mishra said.

Out of the vaccines that have been supplied, the Centre has put a stop on the use of around 5 lakh doses of measles vaccines and around 21 lakh doses of BCG, saying they are not sure whether the particular batch is safe or not, the minister alleged.

"Around a month ago, the JE vaccination drive was to be included in the routine immunisation programme in the high-risk districts. We had demanded around 10 lakh vaccines, but they supplied us with only 4.6 lakh, which were also substandard," Mishra said.

The minister further said that though this is the peak season for the diseases in eastern UP, the state still does not have JE vaccines under the routine immunisation programme. The state had demanded rapid testing kits for diagnosis of malaria and around 2,100 mt of DDT for spraying in the affected areas. While not a single rapid testing kit has been provided, around 500 mt of DDT has been supplied.

"The situation in eastern UP is getting out of hand," he said. This year, 1,363 children have been infected with Acute Encephalitis Syndrome, of which, 234 have died. As many as 1,858 people have been infected with measles and 45 have died.

Central team takes samples of unfit JE vaccines
A two-member Central enquiry team took samples of JE vaccine on Tuesday that was declared unfit for use by the UP Health officials.

Dr Anil Kumar, Assistant Commissioner, Department of Health, Government of India and Dr Jagdish Chandra, CMO in-charge of Government Medical Store Depot at Karnal, however, said that they would be in a position to give a statement only once the test on the vaccine is completed. Four days ago, the state government had received around 4.6 lakh doses of JE vaccine, but during a random check, the vials were found deteriorated due to exposure to heat.

Heading: Strike to protest registration of case against teachers - Indian Express
Content:
Nearly two days after five blasts rocked the national Capital, Santoshi — the wife of autorickshaw driver Moolchand who took the five terrorists to the Gaffar market — came to know about the incident in which her husband happens to be a prime witness.

An illiterate Santoshi, who does not own a television, came to know about the blasts after her husband's friend called from New Delhi informing that Moolchand has become a victim of the blast.

For Santoshi it was an emotional rollercoaster ride. Firstly, she was told her husband had died, then she came to know that he was critically injured.

In spite of making several efforts, Santoshi was unable to speak to Moolchand, who is recuperating at the RML Hospital. While Moolchand's mobile phone has been shut, his friend Manoj failed to arrange a talk due to the high-level of security at the hospital.

"He (Moolchand) spoke to me on Friday night and was planning to come to Allahabad during Navratri," said Santoshi, who has been inconsolable since she came to know about her husband's condition.

A resident of Berkhera village, which is only 35 kms away from Allahabad, Moolchand had gone to New Delhi four years ago to earn his livelihood. His wife Santoshi and two-year-old old son stay in the village.

After the villagers came to know about the incident and Moolchand's injury in the blast, they came forward to help Santoshi with money some money so that she could visit the New Dehli to meet Moolchand.

His brother Santosh, who had rushed to New Delhi after he came to know about the blasts, is expected to return to Allahabad on Wednesday to take Santoshi back. Since Moolchand is one of the prime eyewitnesses who could provide vital clues regarding the identity of the terrorists to the Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS), he was being treated amid tight security in the hospital, Santosh had told Santoshi.

Santoshi has only one prayer in her lips that her husband returns hale and hearty. "His condition is very critical," Santoshi said.

She alson urged the government to provide help to her husband.

Heading: Crack in pipeline, oil spills into Ganga - Indian Express
Content:
Teachers in 21 government-aided degree colleges in Lucknow went on a day's strike on Tuesday, demanding the withdrawal of cases lodged against Lucknow Christian College (LCC) teacher C McFarland and former manager P R Hamlin.

Lucknow University Associated Colleges Teachers' Association (LUACTA) president Maulindu Mishra said: "If the cases were not withdrawn before September 22, we will boycott Lucknow University's special convocation to award DLit to President Pratibha Patil on September 23." A memorandum in this connection was also submitted to the Raj Bhawan.

About a week ago, the police had visited Lucknow Christian College to arrest a student leader, Fakhrul Hasan, following a complaint that he had threatened a teacher. According to the police, McFarland and Hamlin had instigated the students. As many as 142 students, along with McFarland and Hamlin were named in the FIR.

Superintendent of Police (West) Paresh Pandey said: "We have information that McFarland and Hamlin had instigated students to block the road and pelt stones on police officers."

McFarland denied the charges and said that when the incident took place on Friday, he was in a meeting at the principal's office. "The police had behaved irresponsibly and lodged the case without evidence," he added.

Trouble has been brewing at the Lucknow Christian College since the management decided to appoint S W Prasad, a member of the LCC Society, as the college manager some time ago. The teachers had protested against Prasad's appointment.

LUACTA president Mishra said: "The way in which Prasad was appointed was wrong. He had indulged in forgery to get the post. The teachers wanted a manager with a clean image. Prasad had also committed an irregularity to remove Hamlin and occupy the position of the manager."

Prasad, however, said: "I was appointed by the chairman of the Board of Governors of the Lucknow Christian College Society. My appointment was according to the constitution of the college society."

Asked about the step the college authorities were taking to resolve the matter, principal Dr A J Mukherjee said: "It for the management to handle the matter. The principal cannot take any step in this connection."

Chairman of the Board of Governors, Bishop Cyril S Cornelius, was not available for comment. He conveyed that he could give an appointment only after two days.

Heading: Women panel’s helpline goes 24x7 - Indian Express
Content:
A crack in the diesel pipeline of the Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) has led to oil spillage in Ganga.

Early Monday morning, the leakage was reported from Khannapur village in Unnao district.

Though oil supply was immediately stopped, river water between Shaikhpur and Narainpur villages under the Maharajpur police station was affected by the spillage.

Taking a serious note of the incident, Uttar Pradesh Pollution Control Board (UPPCB) on Tuesday collected water samples of Ganga from two locations, which are 25 km away from Khannapur village.

"If the laboratory tests confirm that the pollution level of the river has increased due to the leakage of diesel, a notice will be served to IOC," said Radhey Shyam, Regional Officer, UPPCB.

He claimed preliminary inspection suggests that the situation was not alarming.

The IOC pipeline extends from Allahabad to Lucknow via Kanpur and Unnao. IOC teams have been constituted in these districts to keep an eye on the pipeline.

The teams have been instructed to use oil dispersants at locations where diesel has been found on the river surface.

Senior Operations Manager (IOC) S P Pandey told The Indian Express: "Change in the course of Ganga near the Khannapur village led to the crack in the pipeline."

He said the place where the crack had earlier appeared was around 150 metres away from the river.

"The pipeline was two metres below the ground level, whereas the pipeline passing under the river is more than 20 metres below the river bed," Pandey added.

According to the IOC official, the change in the river course led to the erosion at Khannapur and the pressure on the pipeline was increased.

"The fault was reported on Sunday night. Within a few minutes, the supply through the pipeline was stopped," he said. Repair work was only possible when the water level of the river recedes in Khannapur, he added.

The station officer of Maharajpur police station, Sujit Dubey, said the oil spillage was detected on Monday. Locals were surprised to find a distinct change in the colour of the river water.

"First we were apprehensive of going near the river as it had turned blue, but later it was found the diesel was floating on the surface," said Mahesh Kumar, a resident of Narainpurva village.

"The villagers started to scoop out the diesel form the water surface but soon they found that it was of no use," he added.

"On Tuesday, however, no diesel or any other petroleum product was found in the river," said Sujit Dubey.

Heading: Fire officers ‘beat up’ vendor for asking to pay bill - Indian Express
Content: The Uttar Pradesh State Women's Commission is all set to make its helpline — the toll free number 1800-180-5220 for women in distress — a 24-hour service. In a review meeting of the commission's work on Tuesday, it was decided that the helpline number be extended to 24-hours and officers would be posted for the helpline on the basis of shifts. Abha Agnihotri, chairperson of the commission, said the decision was taken since the commission receives a number of calls from women in distress and as the helpline works only during office hours, many calls from women go unattended.

Heading: LU may change exam pattern - Indian Express
Content:
Demand for your rights and face the consequences. On late Monday night, Lucknow police fire service officers allegedly thrashed a tea vendor. Reason: the vendor allegedly asked them to pay for the tea and biscuits they had at his shop near the Chowk fire station.

The victim, Raju Shukla, was rushed to the civil hospital Balrampur, where his condition was reported to be critical. The medical report of the victim stated that his under garment was soiled with blood and excretion, which indicates that he was assaulted at his private parts, said a senior police officer.

According to the victim's family, when Shukla asked for the outstanding amount from the fire service officers including the fire station officer, they called him inside the fire station premise and beat him up.

The police, however, had a different version. SP (West) Paresh Pandey said: "Shukla was drunk at the time of incident and was fighting with one rickshaw puller who called the fire officials for help. Only one constable Chandra Shekhar Azad had intervened."

Asked as to how the victim got injured, Pandey said: "He sustained injuries while fighting with the rickshaw puller."

An FIR, meanwhile, was lodged by the victim's brother in Thakurganj police station against the seven people including the Fire Station Officer Ramesh Kumar Tiwari.

Chief Fire Officer Aman Sharma said, "Action will be taken if the officials are found guilty in the departmental investigations."

Heading: Officials insist Tatas will stay in Singur - Indian Express
Content:
The Lucknow University (LU) plans to introduce changes in its examination system during the ongoing academic session. The university has constituted a four-member committee to work out strategies where colleges will be exchanged as examination centers.

The team comprises principals of National PG College, Shia PG College, IT PG College and Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Degree College. On Tuesday, a meeting was held between university authorities and the principals of several degree colleges. It was discussed that during examinations on law courses in the previous session when colleges were exchanged as examination centers, the mass copying was curbed. It was decided to set up a college development council at the university level. LU Vice-Chancellor A S Brar asked colleges to submit applications to be granted autonomous status.

Heading: Court allows TC leader to be present during Tata case - Indian Express
Content:
The high-ranking officials of the state government maintained on Tuesday that the small car project will stay in Singur with work resuming in the long run.

This comes in spite of Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee holding a rally and suspension of work continuing at the Tata project site in Singur

Subrata Gupta, MD, West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation, said: "As of now, 85 per cent of the work at the mother plant is over. The engineers who have come from foreign countries on contract, however, have returned. I do not know how long will it take for them to come and join work."

"One must remember that around 11,000 people want work to resume and only around 2,000 are unwilling. Out of this 2,000, we expect a large section to accept the fresh compensation package," he added.

"Though the first Nano may not roll out from Bengal, but there is a definite chance that the Tata plant will stay in the state," an official said.

The state government's hopes have received a boost after the announcement of a fresh compensation package by Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee. Tata Motors has also hailed the new initiative and stated that the company is hopeful that a congenial atmosphere will soon be created in Singur.

"The compensation package will help creating a congenial atmosphere. We are hopeful that Tatas will remain in Singur," said Sabyasachi Sen, Secretary, Commerce and Industries. "I have seen the recent statement issued by the Tata Motors and believe once there is an end to local disturbance, work will resume," he added.

According to sources at the Commerce and Industries Department, Tatas may resume work in the near future if there is no further deterioration in the law and order situation and if the section of unwilling farmers receive the compensation cheques.

In the recent statement, released a day after the chief minister announced the fresh compensation package, Tata Motors had expressed that such initiatives will evoke a positive response from the residents of Singur.

"All stakeholders will contribute to the creation of an environment conducive to the long-term sustained operations of an industrial enterprise," the statement added.

Heading: Bonus criteria: All farmers have to accept compensation first - Indian Express
Content:
The Calcutta High Court allowed the Leader of the Opposition in West Bengal Assembly and Trinamool Congress MLA Partha Chatterjee to take part in the legal proceedings on the petition filed by the Tata Motors calling for restraint on making its deal with the state government public.

Hearing a plea filed by Chatterjee's counsel, Justice Dipankar Dutta allowed the Trinamool leader to be present in the court.

On several occasions, Trinamool chief Mamata Banerjee has demanded disclosure of the agreement between Tata Motors and the state government on the Singur car factory project that was signed on March 9, 2007.

Last week, Tata Motors had filed a petition challenging the move of the West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation (WBIDC) to publish the agreement with the Tatas. Tata Motors had alleged in its petition that the government as well as the WBIDC had violated the provisions of the RTI Act by already disclosing a portion of the deal to the public. Following this, the High Court had issued a stay order last Friday and directed the government and WBIDC not to publish the secret part of the pact within two weeks. The case will come for hearing next Friday.

Heading: US embassy to upgrade visa processing capacity - Indian Express
Content:
The criteria for the compensation to the Singur farmers was laid down by the state government on Tuesday.

The government made it clear that the additional 50 per cent of the amount to be awarded to the farmers will be given only when all the farmers who did not claim the price for their land accepted the compensation.

The West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation paid Rs 120 crore for 997 acres of land at Singur — of which about Rs 91 crore has been disbursed. Of the remaining Rs 29 crore, about Rs 22 crore is lying with the district magistrate of Hooghly.

"Unless that amount is exhausted the government cannot release fresh funds," said Sabyasachi Sen, Principal Secretary, Department of Commerce and Industries.

This means that farmers who have already received price for their land cannot claim the additional 50 per cent unless all the farmers, who did not receive their cheques, accepted the

compensation amount for their land.

The farmers who did not receive their compensation earlier will get 10 per cent of the award amount if they collect it before September 22.

"The amount has already been released. People who have not received the amount earlier can take the 10 per cent of the award amount. If collected after September 22, they will get the compensation but they will not be entitled to the additional 10 per cent of the award amount," Sen said.

The co-ordination committee of the state government employees, meanwhile, blamed the government for the imbroglio in Singur.

"Land acquisition process has totally been mishandled and it is a section of the bureaucrats which is responsible for this,"Ananta Bandopadhyay, secretary of the committee, said on Tuesday.

Heading: Mamata loses five farmers in Singur, but hints at fresh protests - Indian Express
Content:
The US Embassy is planning to gear up the visa processing capacity across India next year. Apart from this, the embassy also has plans to set up a consulate with an investment of $100 million in Mumbai and a new consulate in Hyderabad.

The US embassy has issued about 7.5 lakh temporary visas during the financial year ending September 30, 2008. Two years ago, it had issued 4.5 lakh visas only.

Peter G Kaestner, minister-counselor for Consular Affairs and Consul General, US Embassy, said the embassy is focussed on reducing the backlog time to 14 days from the existing six months wait.

Kaestner said the US was extremely keen to make its visa proceedings easier for students who want to study there. He added that student visa applications were going up by 20 -25 per cent every year and in a survey done in 2007, it was seen that India had sent the maximum number of foreign students to the US.

Heading: Environment development project spells trouble for residents - Indian Express
Content:
The Singur cauldron threw up mixed results for the West Bengal government on Tuesday.

The good news — five previously unwilling farmers turned up at the Hooghly district magistrate's office saying they wanted compensation for their land.

The bad — Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee hinted she might resume the dharna from September 19 and was waiting for Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi to be in town before she took a final decision. She would certainly go ahead if the state government did not honour the Singur agreement, Banerjee told a rally in Singur on Tuesday.

There was some ambiguous news too — Congress leader Subrata Mukherjee hopped on to Banerjee's Singur stage, saying his heart had prompted him to do so. "Please do not read politics in this," he told the farmers. Mukherjee's move could mean two things — he wants to switch camp or that he was state Congress chief Priya Ranjan Dasmunsi's emissary to Banerjee just in case she wanted a Trinamool-Congress tie-up before or after the next general polls.

Though the Congress had earlier kept a distance from Singur, Mukherjee on Tuesday chose to arrive at the rally with Mamata Banerjee and even left with her. When called to speak, he was introduced not as a Congress leader, but by his other portfolio — the party's trade wing president in Bengal. He said: "I have come to protest the breach of trust with Mamata."

On the other hand, the five farmers who want the money are among the 2,250 holding out. The district administration considers this as a breakthrough and feels the others might come forward too. District Magistrate of Hooghly Neelam Meena said: "I have asked these farmers to come to my office on Friday."

They are Bidyut Das, Haradhan Koley, Sambhunath Ghosh, Archibala Ghosh and Manjubala Ghosh. Three of them are from Khaserbheri mouja, a stronghold of Trinamool Congress-backed Singur Krishi Jami Raksha Committee. A total of nine bighas were acquired from these five farmers.

Meanwhile, sub-divisional land reforms officer S K Ghosh has been entrusted with the responsibility of disbursing cheques to farmers. He said the team was ready to process cheques for all those who might accept the government's new package. "The compensation this time will include an additional 50 per cent for the land," Ghosh said.

The local CPM is not sitting idle either. They have started a quiet campaign, trying to convince unwilling farmers. They are going door to door, it is learnt. Party leader Dibakar Das said the people are warming up to the new package. "Many who did not collect their cheques earlier have called now," Das said.

Heading: Air Force officer shot dead by junior in Midnapore - Indian Express
Content:
Lack of coordination between the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) and the Kolkata Environment Improvement Project (KEIP) has set off a crisis over water supply lines and has resulted in huge trouble for the taxpayers.

The KEIP is the nodal agency of the KMC for various developmental work.

The procedure of drainage and sewerage upgradation work, carried out by the KEIP, has triggered several damages in the main water supply lines resulting in the contamination of water supplied to the city.

While carrying out underground drainage and sewerage work, the KEIP is supposed to either ask the KMC for the drinking water pipeline network map or conduct a local survey to track down the location of the network. The KEIP, however, did not opt for any of the options.

"KEIP never consulted the water supply department before carrying out the drainage and sewerage work. Although, we do not have the map of the water supply network of the entire city, we could have provided them with draft maps of the wards. But they never asked for that. They were asked to do a survey by the KMC while carrying out the project, but even that was not done properly by them," said Mrinal Kanti Mondal, Member Mayor in Council, water supply.

While carrying out the project in Behala, ward 128, leakages at 10 places on the AK Paul Road have been found by the KMC water supply department. Since the leakages occurred after the KEIP workers finished their work and moved out of the area, it took three months for KMC workers to detect the leakages.

In another case, a leak was found after 12 days of the work in Jadavpur area, ward 101. The leakage caused water contamination in the area, which is now witnessing large-scale enteric outbreak.

"Detecting seepage in underground water supply line is the most difficult work and it incurs a huge cost as well. The KEIP can minimise the risks of affecting the water supply lines by taking some precautions," said Kushal Das, deputy civil engineer, water supply department of the KMC.

Sometimes, the land — where the underground drainage work has been carried out — caves in after the work gets over. According to a civic engineer of the water supply department, it can be prevented if the span of the compaction is well organised after the work is over. If the span of the compaction on the retaining wall is small then the risk of damaging the water supply lines gets minimised, he added.

The KEIP workers, however, either leave the retaining wall unguarded or do the compaction part in an unorganised way resulting in collapse of the upper layer of soil. And when the upper layer collapses, the fragile joints of the water supply lines break and the outflow starts.

Till date the KEIP's work has caused leakages in the water supply lines at several places including Phoolbagan, (Jadavpur, ward 101), on S C Mallik Road, in Bansdroni (ward 112), ward 113, ward 120, Gardenreach (ward 138).

The KEIP officials, however, denied the allegations. "We always conduct a local survey by digging trial trench with a gap of 50-100 meters. Sometimes some water-supply lines get affected, but we always try to help the KMC in restoring the pipelines. Since we have to work in several diverse situations, it happens," said a senior KEIP official.

Heading: Shopping complex land row: High Court directs govt to return land to owner - Indian Express
Content:
An Air Force officer shot dead his senior on Tuesday morning at the Kalaikunda Air Base in West Midnapore district.

Defence spokesperson Group Captain R K Das said the victim has been identified as junior warrant officer R C Mishra (45). Das said Sergeant B S Rajput (40) was on guard duty at a hangar when Mishra reported for work at 6.30 am.

"What transpired between them or if there was any animosity already existing cannot be said at the moment," said the spokesman.

He added: "The sergeant has been arrested and handed over to the police. He will be tried under civil law. At the same time, we have ordered a court of inquiry to ascertain the reasons behind the incident."

He said both the officers were radio technicians and attached to the air base. They were working in the same department till a month ago.

"Officers of the rank of sergeant and below have to do guard duty by rotation, which is why Rajput had the weapon — a standard 9 mm carbine. He was on duty at the hangar, which was being used for maintenance of routine equipment."

Mishra, who was from Bhopal, was staying with his family at the air base. On the day he was shot his wife was, however, in Kolkata. She has been informed about the incident and is expected to reach Kalaikunda late in the evening. The body, meanwhile, has been kept at the Railway Hospital in Kharagpur.

Heading: JU suspends 24 students for ragging - Indian Express
Content:
Rejecting an appeal filed by the state government, the Calcutta High Court on Tuesday held that the state government should return the land near the Dakshinapan Complex to its owner. The land, measuring 7 katha (about 5,000 sq ft), was acquired by the state government in 1996 to build a shopping complex there.

The Division bench of Justices Pranab Kumar Chatterjee and Tapan Mukherjee asked the state to return the land to 93-year-old Mahamaya Roy Chaudhury immediately.

The case dates back to 1996 when Roy Chaudhury had filed a writ petition in the High Court challenging the notification for the acquisition of the land. After a series of hearing, a single bench of the HC had directed the state to return the land to the owner in 1998 citing the acquisition process illegal. But the government soon moved a petition challenging the order before a Division Bench. The Bench also upheld the order of the single bench and directed the state to return the land to Roy Chaudhury in 2000. The state government, however, did not return the land in compliance with the court's order.

Heading: IT professionals fear that they might lose job - Indian Express
Content:
In an unprecedented move, the authorities of Jadavpur University suspended 24 students and decided to lodge an FIR against six former students on Tuesday for ragging a first-year girl student.

On July 16, the student of the architecture department was allegedly ragged by her seniors. The next day, her father lodged a written complaint to the Registrar of the University, followed by the constitution of a five-member anti-ragging committee comprising the faculties of different departments of the university and the Dean of students.

Based on the report submitted by the committee in the mid-week of August, the decision was taken at Tuesday's Executive Council meeting.

As per the council's decision, three students found directly involved with the ragging have been suspended for four semesters, which is equivalent to two years. Of them, two are girls.

Another 21 students who were present at the site of the incident will be suspended for their "passive" involvement. The university will lodge an FIR against six former students who have already graduated from the university but were involved in the incident. A copy of the FIR will be forwarded to their respective employers. All those found guilty were students of second, third, fourth and fifth years of the same department.

This is the first time ever that Jadavpur University has imposed an academic suspension. In the previous cases, students found guilty of ragging were debarred from staying in the hostels. The Executive Council members were unanimous in their decision on the issue.

"The gravity of the incident forced us to take a strict decision. The students will be given a chance to come up with their defence and explain why such an action will not be taken against them," said Pradip Narayan Ghosh, Vice-Chancellor of Jadavpur University.

Heading: Improve your civic duties to get a good rating for your city - Indian Express
Content:
Kolkata's IT sector has been gripped by fear psychosis a day after Lehman Brothers Holdings declared bankruptcy.

IT employees are apprehensive about losing their jobs, and much of the discussions at the IT offices on Tuesday centred around the health of the US economy.

IT majors like Tata Consultancy Services Ltd, Wipro Technologies, Satyam Computers, Infosys Technologies and HCL Technologies provide services to customers like Lehman and Merill Lynch. TCS, for instance, earns 43 per cent of its revenue from financial services solutions

"Wipro does trim down staff each year but there has been no announcement of any such measure immediately after the US debacle," said a senior employee of Wipro Technologies.

When asked to comment on the possible impact, Tamal Dasgupta, Vice-President of Wipro Technologies, said: "It is too early to comment. We have to be patient and wait for the next two days to see what impact the developments have on the IT sector."

"Any development in the USA or any part of the world is bound to have a ripple effect on the IT sector in India as most of the operations of the IT companies are linked to the firms based in the USA. The BPO and KPO sectors are likely to be worst hit," said an IBM employee.

An employee of a global BPO firm, GENPACT, feels that the fear is unfounded saying, "There are reasons for concern but it is too early to make any assessments."

The TCS authorities refused to comment on its client Lehman's latest financial crisis. But it assured that there would be no drastic measures like trimming down its

workforce.

"There is no question of our employees losing their jobs and our hiring plans for the year are also on track," said a spokesperson for TCS.

Heading: Haldia gets ready for its first IT park - Indian Express
Content:
Waterlogged streets, choked drains or non-installation of water meters — cities will now be rated in terms of their performance in civic issues. The Union Urban Development Ministry has introduced "benchmarks" to assess the performance of cities in civic issues.

A letter has been sent to the Chief Secretaries of all states to "benchmark" services offered in cities with a population of more than four million.

Initially, the benchmarks will pertain to four basic issues like water supply, drainage, sewerage and solid waste management. In future, the transport sector will also be incorporated for benchmarking.

"The state government will have to set a time frame for undertaking works related to issue. They can then analyse their performance based on the benchmarks," said M Ramachandran, Secretary, Union Urban Development Ministry.

The ministry has prepared a series of benchmarks for each of the facilities. For instance, the water supply will have ratings based on the coverage where the benchmark is 100 per cent, the extent of metering of water connection too have the benchmark fixed at 100 per cent, as well as cost recovery in water supply and extent of metering of water connection where the benchmark is 100 per cent in both cases.

It is, however, yet to be decided if the Centre would impose penalties on the state governments if their cities do not score well.

Heading: Woman jumps into Hooghly with her three children - Indian Express
Content:
Soon the state can boast of a new IT park and that too not in Kolkata. The proposed IT park — Haldia One — will be developed by STV Technologies, with an investment of over Rs 100 crore at Haldia.

The park will come up on an area of 3.5 acres housing a 38-storeyed building complex. To lure IT professionals, multiplexes and other amenities will also be built in the complex.

"I don't even foresee Kolkata having such a facility in the near future," said Debesh Das, Minister of Information Technology.

After laying the foundation stone of the park on Tuesday, Siddharth, Secretary (IT), said Kolkata is nearing saturation level and it is important to develop tier II and tier III cities for development of the IT sector.

"We have commissioned a study to identify alternative locations for the development of the IT industry," said Das.

"As per the study, cities like Siliguri, Durgapur, Kalyani, Khragpur and Haldia can be developed as the next IT hubs," added Das.

The nodal agency for the development of the park — Haldia Development Agency (HDA) — has alloted land to 32 companies.

"About 60 companies have applied for the land. But we are facing certain problems with providing land in Haldia," said Lakhan Seth, MP and Chairman of HDA.

To prepare a roadmap for the development of this region, the HDA has asked IIT Kharagpur to prepare a report on the City Development Plan and Mobility Improvement Plan, said Parwez Ahamed Siddiqui, Chief Executive Officer of HDA. The report is expected to reach the agency in another week, said Siddiqui.

Heading: IIMs get their reality check:  those six-figure Wall Street salaries will have to wait - Indian Express
Content:
In an apparent suicide bid, a woman jumped into the Hooghly river along with her three children in Howrah district on Tuesday afternoon. The quick action by a launch passing by and efforts of a bystander, however, managed to save two of the children. The woman and the youngest child were washed away and are presumed dead, police said.

Police said Sutapa Chowdhury (32), a resident of Ahiritola in Kolkata, had taken a launch ride from Babughat to Bandhaghat at around 3.30 pm with her children Chanchal Kumari (7), Sunil (3) and Bugli (1). "After alighting from the launch, she remained standing on the banks.When the high tide came, she jumped into the river with her children," police said.

Luckily, the crew of the Merchant Vessel Bipin Chandra, which happened to be passing by, spotted the children floundering in the river and threw life jackets. Chanchal, the eldest, managed to grab hold of one of the life jackets, but Sunil could not. But thanks to Babuaprasad Jaiswal, a rickshaw-puller who had witnessed the entire episode, Sunil was saved. Police said Jaiswal jumped into the river and rescued Sunil.

Howrah police officials said: "The mother and the infant girl, however, were swept away by the tide. Their bodies are yet to be recovered."

Heading: Iran stonewalling N-weapon probe: IAEA - Indian Express
Content:
Over the weekend, as Lehman Brothers went bust, Merrill Lynch was sold and the world of global high finance shook, hearts broke on Kolkata's IIM campus. For two students of IIM-C's Class of 2009 who had accepted pre-placement offers only a couple of weeks ago, the immediate future was suddenly a void.

"We interned at Lehman's London office only this summer. Work was as usual, no one had any idea that trade was declining," one of them told The Indian Express.

The student could have been speaking for hundreds of fresh graduates at Indian Institutes of Management from Kolkata to Ahmedabad, Lucknow to Bangalore. Firms like Merrill and Lehman have been among the biggest recruiters on campus, and the investment banking and financial services sector has been setting the aspirational benchmark with offers of salaries that have ranged from $120,000 to $360,000 annually. In the 24 hours after what the global media is describing as the blackest day in decades on Wall Street, many aspirations are appearing unreasonable.

The two IIM-C students have received no official word yet from Lehman, but the silence holds only a slim hope. "We put in 12-13 hours a day at the London office and worked on hot sectors like commodities and equity sales. Everyone there was very interested in India," recalled the student.

A third of last year's IIM-C batch of 291 got jobs in the investment banking and financial services sector. For summer placements, Merrill hired 18 students, Morgan Stanley 11, JP Morgan Chase 13 and HSBC Global Investment Banking Division 6. "Both Merrill and Lehman are big players as far as placements are concerned," said IIM-C chief administrative officer Dinesh Varma. "They are good paymasters too. Probably this year we will miss them."

At IIM, Lucknow, the mood was gloomy. Lehman has been making four or five offers every year, and last November, Merrill had shown an interest for the first time. "We were expecting a reduction in the number of offers, but the collapse of Lehman Brothers has come as a shock. Though Lehman made just one summer placement offer this time, we were hoping that would change," said placement cell co-ordinator Rishabh Papardia.

At IIM, Ahmedabad, the Wall Street shock has translated into a gag order on students. "We have been asked not to speak to the media on the Lehman Brothers issue right now as the institute is yet to study the situation completely," said a student.

Mihir Lal, student coordinator of the placement cell of the institute, said: "As a policy, we don't disclose names of individual recruiters and the number of students picked up by a particular company. Our placements are a good six months away and we have a lot of time to evaluate the situation."

Despite the subprime crisis, 133 out of 255 students had joined the investment banking and financial services sector in last March's placements. Besides Merrill and Lehman, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, JP Morgan, Deutsche Bank and Barclays had picked up students from the Class of 2008.

IIM-A students bagged an average international salary of $119,000 last year, with the highest acceptances ranging from $ 280,000 to $ 360,000. (With ENS Lucknow and Ahmedabad)

Heading: US embassy in Yemen hit by car bomb, 1 Indian killed - Indian Express
Content:
UN efforts to investigate allegations that Iran tried to make nuclear arms have run into a dead end, with Tehran steadfastly blocking efforts to probe the accusations, the International Atomic Energy Agency said.

The conclusion was contained in an IAEA report released yesterday to the 35-nation IAEA board and the UN Security Council, which has already imposed three sets of sanctions because of Tehran's nuclear defiance.

"We've arrived at a gridlock," said a senior UN official, describing the document as "a progress report without progress." He demanded anonymity because he was not authorized to discuss the restricted report.

The document also said that through uranium enrichment Tehran now has amassed a third of the amount of enriched uranium it would need to reprocess into the material serving as the fissile core of a nuclear weapon, should it choose to do so.

The US and its allies say Iran wants to develop its enrichment program for its weapons applications. But Tehran insists it seeks the technology only to create nuclear fuel, and IAEA oversight and inspections of the Islamic Republic's known enrichment program has not come up with any evidence that contradict what Tehran says.

The six-page report confirmed that Iran continues to expand its uranium enrichment program in defiance of three sets of UN Security Council sanctions imposed in attempts to force Tehran to mothball such activities.

The document said Iran was now either fully or partially operating nearly 4,000 centrifuges at its cavernous underground facility at Natanz.

Heading: US strike kills at least 4 in Pakistan: Source - Indian Express
Content:
A car bomb targeting the US embassy hit the front gate of its compound in the Yemeni capital, killing 16 people including an Indian.

A senior security official said six guards belonging to Yemen's Interior Ministry and four civilians, including one Indian national, were killed in the car bombing

US embassy spokesman Ryan Gliha told The Associated Press by telephone that a car bomb hit the embassy's gate on Wednesday morning followed by a second explosion. He did not know what caused the second one.

However, the Yemeni security official, who spoke on condition of anonymity because he was not authorised to speak to the media, said the embassy was hit by two car bombs and that heavy gunfire lasting around 10 minutes followed the blasts.

Several nearby homes were badly damaged by the blasts, he said.

Heading: Pak may move World Bank against India over Chenab water - Indian Express
Content:
A US drone aircraft missile attack targeting a militant camp in Pakistan killed at least four people and wounded three, a Pakistani intelligence official in the South Waziristan region said.

Officials said the drone fired four missiles as dusk fell on Baghar, a village in the mountains 55 km (35 miles) west of Wana, the main town in the region.

Foreigners were among the fighters staying in the tents by the spring that runs through Baghar.

US commandos raided the nearby border village of Angor Adda on Sept 3, and another helicopter-borne raid there was aborted on Monday after Pakistani troops and villagers opened fire, according to Pakistani officials.

Heading: US lawmakers fault F16 plan for Pak - Indian Express
Content:
Pakistan will seek arbitration by the World Bank over India's alleged violation of the Indus Water Treaty if New Delhi did not concede the breach of the pact, a report said on Wednesday.

Islamabad had claimed that, in "gross violations of the Indus Water Treaty," India reduced the water flow to fill up the Baglihar dam lake in Jammu and Kashmir, causing to a "loss of agriculture" for farmers in Pakistan.

Pakistan would take up the issue with India on a water commissioner-level meeting likely to be held in New Delhi and would demand compensation for the agriculture loss to it, said a 'Daily News' report on Wednesday.

"We will demand compensation estimated at 0.2 million causes in water loss. If India does not accept the violation, Pakistan will go to the WB for arbitration," official sources were quoted as saying.

India, on the other hand, has clarified that reduced flow in the Chenab river in Pakistan was a result of "very little" availability of water in a lean year.

"There was reduction because the flow was very little this year. We have also explained to the Pakistan High Commission on the situation," Foreign Secretary Shivshanker Menon said in New Delhi on Tuesday.

Pakistan Water and Power Minister Raja Pervez Ashraf, who chaired a high-level meeting, has directed the Pakistani Indus Water Commission chief to hold formal discussions with his Indian counterpart.

He claimed India had stopped 200,000 acre-feet water from August 1 to September 12 to fill the Baglihar Dam lake in Jammu and Kashmir.

Pakistan would ask India to compensate the water loss by releasing water in the Ravi, Sutlej and Chenab rivers and had asked the Punjab Irrigation Department to assess the losses that would be placed before the Indian authorities the meeting, the Daily News said.

Ashraf has directed the concerned authorities to take necessary action, and has directed the Pakistan commissioner to undertake a tour of inspection and hold formal discussions with the Indian commissioner, the sources said.

Pakistan had sought World Bank arbitration after raising objection over the construction Baglihar dam over Chanab river, arguing that it violates the Indus Water Treaty of 1960.
