No organisation has claimed responsibility for the attack so far. Spokesperson of the Catholic Conference of Bishops, Madhya Pradesh, Fr Anand Muttungal said some unidentified men had inquired about the sisters four days ago.

Two guards have now been posted at the school.

Heading: Mamata threatens to restart stir - Indian Express
Content:
In an obvious move to reach out to the Maratha community on the eve of the polls, the state Government has decided to sympathetically consider the community's demand for reservations.

Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh gave this assurance in a meeting with the representatives of the Maratha community co-ordination committee who met him on Tuesday to stress their demands for the inclusion of the community, which comprises almost 30 per cent of the state's population, in the OBC list. Deputy Chief Minister R R Patil was also present at the meeting.

Deshmukh said they were considering how the benefits of reservations could be extended to the Maratha community while adhering to the legal framework. They were seeking information from other states in this regard.

Representatives of Maratha organisations, including NCP leader and former MLC Vinayak Mete, who heads Shiv Sangram that organised an attack on the residence of Loksatta editor Kumar Ketkar, and Purushottam Khedekar of the Maratha Sewa Sangh were present on the occasion.

Heading: With BJP, Prachanda’s temple, Ram diplomacy - Indian Express
Content:
At the Trinamool Congress rally on Tuesday in Singur, party chief Mamata Banerjee hinted that she might again start a dharna after September 19. However, she said a final decision on the issue would be taken only after she meets Governor Gopal Krishna Gandhi, who is currently not in Kolkata.

"The Governor was the convenor at the meeting with the state Government. Hence, I will discuss with him before deciding on the future course of action," she announced. However, towards the end of her speech Mamata said that if the state Government does not adhere to the agreement signed with them, she might decide to restart her agitation.

Meanwhile, Subrata Mukherjee, Congress leader and former Mayor of Kolkata, made a surprise appearance at the rally, triggering speculations about future political formations. So far, the Congress had distanced itself from the Singur agitation. One section of WBPCC leaders interpreted it as a first step by Mukherjee towards switching over to Trinamool. Others said that he was acting at the behest of Priya Ranjan Dasmunshi, the PCC chief, and keeping the Congress's options of a possible tie-up with Trinamool alive.

However, Mukherjee said his sharing the platform with Mamata does not have any "political connotation". "I have come here to protest the breach of trust by the state Government with Mamata," he said.

Heading: Ramadoss advises Buddha to kick the butt - Indian Express
Content:
After inviting L K Advani to visit the Pashupati Nath Temple in Kathmandu during his meeting with the NDA prime ministerial candidate here on Monday, the visiting Nepalese Prime Minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal "Prachanda" in some smart Track II diplomacy broke bread with the brotherhood in saffron here on Tuesday.

Advani — who has never been to Nepal — is reported to have remarked in a lighter vein that "it was probably the wish of Pashupati Nath that he visits Nepal during the prime ministership of Prachanda".

On Tuesday, the visiting Communist dignitary disarmed everyone by using the "Ayodhya-Janakpur" meta-phor when he called on BJP president Rajnath Singh.

As Rajnath said, "India and Nepal share much more than political ties or geographical borders. We share an emotional bond," Prachanda responded by talking about how Ram, who hailed from Ayodhya, married Janakpur's Sita. "There may be ideological and political differences but we have great respect for the cultural heritage shared by the countries," Prachanda said.

Senior BJP leader Murli Manohar Joshi talked of the "spiritual bond", and the Nepalese PM responded by mentioning the "atoot rishta (unbreakable ties)". A former HRD minister, Joshi added that students from Nepal have always been welcome in India, and "this will go a long way in ensuring Nepal's economic prosperity".

Ravi Shankar Prasad, along with Rajnath, raised the Kosi issue with Prachanda, but it was the visiting Communist leader's free-wheeling discussion with his professed ideological adversaries that was clearly the highlight of the meeting.

Former RSS spokesperson Ram Madhav said that the organisation's representatives in Nepal "were as much committed to democracy as anyone else there, but they were also concerned about the Hindu character of the country". Sources say Prachanda looked visibly discomfited at the mention of the RSS presence in Nepal.

Arun Shourie asked Prachanda to ensure that Nepal is not used by forces inimical to the interests of India. Referring to his recent visit to China, Prachanda said that he was there to participate in the Olympics. "Nepal is a poor country sandwiched between two mighty powers -- China and India. It's in India's interests that its northern neighbour prospers along with it," he said.

CPM leaders Prakash Karat and Sitaram Yechury also met Prachanda and invited him to Kolkata.

Heading: Chouhan keeps ear to ground during yatra - Indian Express
Content:
Health Minister Anbumani Ramadoss on Tuesday issued a fresh advice to West Bengal Chief Minister to give up smoking.

"He (Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee) represents the state, where 71 per cent of the men, including the Chief Minister, consume tobacco. He should display leadership and quit smoking first," Ramadoss told The Indian Express.

Ramadoss's appeal to Bhattacharjee came in the wake of West Bengal recently losing millions of foreign aid to its anti-smoking campaign. The Chief Minister's smoking habit made the state lose millions of dollars in international aid.

The World Health Organisation (WHO) applications for aid to the city to curb tobacco consumption and making it smoke free were twice rejected in the last six months by Bloomberg initiative, a global programme to reduce tobacco use in low and middle class countries.

"The agency did not give funds, reasoning that the leadership is not propagation the ill effects of smoking and himself is a smoker," said Ramadoss.

This is not the first time that Ramadoss had urges the West Bengal Chief Minister to kick the butt. Ramadoss, who is a non-smoker, has been urging many other parliamentarians to quit smoking.

"Parliamentarians, celebrities and public figures should set an example. At Nirman Bhawan, where the Union Health Ministry is housed, we fine people who are seen smoking in the premises," added Ramadoss.

According to officials, all major cities in India — Chennai, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Chandigarh and Delhi — have received $1 million each from Bloomberg initiative for reducing consumption of tobacco.

Official figures state that over 70 per cent of the men in West Bengal consume tobacco in some form. In contrast, the figure is 40 per cent for Delhi and Tamil Nadu, 48 per cent for Maharashtra and 33 per cent for Punjab.

While close to 16 per cent women in West Bengal consume tobacco, the figure is less than one per cent in Punjab, 2.8 pc in Tamil Nadu, 3.1 p c in Delhi and 5.2 pc in Andhra Pradesh.

Heading: Modi’s return gift for Bihar victims on b’day - Indian Express
Content:
Far removed from the terror debate that dominated the party's recent conclave in Bangalore, a BJP chief minister is busy playing a different tune as he crisscrosses the rural hinterland in a chariot borrowed from Gujarat. Shivraj Singh Chouhan's Jan Ashirwad Yatra that began in Ujjain on August 28 could as well belong to any other political outfit: there is no mention of terrorism or the Amarnath land row — issues that should ideally occupy any BJP leader's mind, especially someone projected as a chief ministerial candidate.

Instead, the 49-year-old preferred to focus on pro-poor schemes like offering cheap agriculture loans, free school uniforms, cycles and MSP for wheat. He does not offer highways or skyscrapers; not even round the clock electricity.

Even the crowd that turns up to listen to him doesn't seem to expect anything more than basic necessities of life. Not long ago, they saw photographs of Chouhan riding a bicycle to the secretariat and back to the CM's bungalow.

He tells the crowd at Raisen that as the CM he wants to play mama (maternal uncle) to the girls of the state. He elaborates on a scheme wherein the Government spends on the weddings of girls. He also talks about his pet scheme, Ladli Laxmi Yojana, which ensures a cheque of more than Rs one lakh for girls on turning 18. The scheme aims at changing the society's attitude towards the girl child by celebrating her birth. His audience smiles as he tells them that mothers-in-law would apply ghee on chapattis served to daughters-in-law, because they own more than a lakh. Not surprisingly, he draws a loud applause in Geratganj when he tells the largely rustic crowd that the Government gives Rs 80 even for unnatural deaths of poultry.

Ironically, the yatra's theme of Surakshit ghar vikasit pradesh (safe home, developed state) is not reflected in his speeches. If party sources are to be believed the slogan will soon change to "Shivraj ka sandesh (or BJP ka) jeetegi janata, chamkega pradesh."

The third BJP chief minister, after Uma Bharati and Babulal Gaur, since 2003, he never mentions either of them or the achievements of the state Government during their tenures. In fact, he does not even talk of L K Advani or any other senior BJP leader. The BJP has been in power for close to 57 months in the state, but he talks of only the 34 months that he has been the Chief Minister.

He even spins a few yarns. "I have never slept for more than two-and-a-half hours after becoming the CM," he repeatedly asserts and does not bat an eyelid when he says, "Maharashtra CM asked me not to give more bonus to farmers." He seems to have borrowed only aspect from his Gujarat counterpart: he puts up questions before the crowd in order to engage them in a conversation.

Heading: Pak team coming, LoC  trade ready to roll out - Indian Express
Content:
Gujarat Chief Minister Narendra Modi will flag off a train stuffed with relief material from Surat, on Tuesday, his 59th birthday, for flood-ravaged Bihar. "Relief goods will include blankets, utensils and other daily requirements. It will have virtually everything needed to start life afresh," said a top BJP leader.

"The CM is increasingly looking at the entire country as his canvas, a reason why he chose to rush in disaster relief material to Bihar," said the BJP leader. "After rebuilding quake-ravaged Kutch, the Modi wanted to help them with disaster relief management while rushing in additional support, but for now, he will stick to relief material," the BJP leader added.

The recently concluded BJP national executive in Bangalore saw Modi making a detailed intervention on internal security and terror apart from the use of IT in mass communications. With his profile enhanced by several notches, he is set to make appearances elsewhere for his party. After Modi makes an appearance alongside party's prime ministerial candidate L K Advani for an anti-terror rally in Delhi on Friday, more such appearances are being planned.

The BJP's local unit in Gandhinagar is, meanwhile, organising a "Vaidik Shatayu Abhinandana ceremony" to wish him "a long life of 100 years". On his 58th birthday last year, Modi had created an all-tribal district of Tapi in Gujarat.

Heading: Why they don’t want early polls - Indian Express
Content:
India and Pakistan have finally decided to allow cross border trade. A traders group from Pakistan Occupied Kashmir (PoK) is scheduled to visit Srinagar on September 22 to meet traders and the Government before the date for the opening of trade — duty free on either side — is finalised between the two neighbouring countries.

"There is an agreement between India and Pakistan on cross-LoC trade. We are trying to get this star-ted around Eid," a senior official said.

The Government, in fact, is eager to formally announce the opening of cross-LoC trade as soon as possible to calm tempers in the Valley. The list of items was exchanged during a meeting in Islamabad on July 18 this year.

While the Union Ministry of Commerce had approved a list of 23 items from Kashmir on August 27, 2007, Pakistan has sent a list of 26 items.

The items from the Indian side include fruits (fresh and dry), spices, saffron, carpets, rugs, chain stitch, wall hangings, tapestry, crewel embroidery, wollen, shawls, including pashminas and namdas, aromatic plants, medicinal plants, wood carving, cricket bats, black mashroom, green tea, imli, dhania and rajmah.

Although there are several items that are common in the two lists, Islamabad would export onion, garlic, animal and animal hides, wedding dresses, leather and leather products, Peshawari leather chappals and leather shoes, hand woven fabrics, fish and fish products.

According to the J-K Government, Islamabad sent its approval for 11 items for import from the 23 items provided by New Delhi on September 10. In fact, the Government is making final preparations and holding discussions with Kashmiri traders before the arrival of the delegation from PoK which comprises senior office bearers of "Azad Kashmir Chamber of Commerce".

Heading: Police close to first arrest in Bangalore blasts - Indian Express
Content:
At a time when the Election Commission is planning to conduct the Assembly polls in J-K later this year, all political parties with the exception of the BJP have hinted that the timing could be counter-productive, in view of the fact that the Valley is currently churning with massive separatist protests.

Although the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) is the only major mainstream party to openly oppose the elections , there is a growing concern in many others, including the National Conference (NC) and Congress, who fear that rushing into the polls will have serious negative implications.

"The primary concern is that an effort needs to be made to heal recent wounds. The Government both at the Centre and state must reach out to the people immediately," NC president Omar Abdullah told The Indian Express. "We are concerned because we want the election process to be credible. At present, a healthy turnout is very difficult to imagine."

Omar added that he had requested the EC to conduct an assessment of the situation on the ground before taking a decision. When asked if the NC would contest if the EC decides to conduct Assembly polls in November, Omar said that in such an eventuality his party would take a stand after calling a meeting of its working committee.

Former minister and NC's leader of Opposition in recently dissolved Legislative Assembly Abdul Raheem Rather voiced similar views to The Indian Express, asserting that a low turnout would not be in the interests of the party or the country.

Incidentally, the NC had recently called a meeting of all its district presidents from across the Valley for a feedback session. They unanimously told the party leadership that the situation was not conducive and the elections at this juncture would have "disastrous" consequences for the party.

In a surprising twist, however, NC patron and former chief minister Farooq Abdullah came up with a contrary view while speaking at a function held to commemorate the death anniversary of NC founder Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah in Srinagar. Supporting the conduction of Assembly polls in November, he said that even if 4 to 5 per cent people vote, the new government would function for six years. Party sources said that Farooq Abdullah's speech came as a shock to them because it was "not scheduled".

Nevertheless, the leaders admit that nobody in the NC's working committee or the high-level core group dares to question the senior Abdullah who will lead the NC as its chief ministerial candidate in the Assembly elections.

Meanwhile, other parties have also signalled that they would prefer it if the polls were deferred to a later date. Former minister and leader of the Peoples Democratic Forum (PDF) Hakeem Mohammad Yaseen said that there is a need to wait until the present situation is brought under control. "Our party is not against the elections as such, but we feel that at this time it is not an alternative to the resolution of the immediate crisis," he said. "There is a need for some confidence-building measures like opening the Srinagar-Muzaffarabad road for trade, putting an end to the violence here to make the atmosphere conducive for elections." Yaseen's party was part of the coalition government that was formed after the 2002 Assembly polls.

The CPI(M) — which had two legislators in the previous Assembly - is also opposing the polls. "Priority should be given to improving the situation first," said the party's leader and former legislator Mohammad Yousuf Tarigami. "Unless this happens, rushing into elections will not yield the results for which they are held."

The Congress, on the other hand, while not publicly opposing the elections is not accepting them unequivocally either. Pradesh Congress Committee president and Union Minister Saifuddin Soz told the EC that they should make an independent assessment of the situation on the ground and talk to political parties as well as citizens before taking a decision.

Former minister and legislator from Handwara, Ghulam Mohiudeen Sofi had become the poster boy of 2002 Assembly elections. Deemed as a proxy candidate of the separatist Hurriyat-constituent Peoples Conference, Sofi's successful election campaign had become a symbol of a pro-poll change in Kashmir. Sofi too feels that elections in the prevailing situation will be "very, very difficult". He pointed out, however, that political parties in Kashmir have double standards. "They say one thing to them (EC) and a completely different thing here," he said.

Former militant commander and legislator from Bandipore Usman Majeed, on the other hand, said that the decision lies with the Government of India, but "obviously the voter turnout will be low," he said.

Prof Gul Mohammad Wani of Kashmir University's political science department, an expert on elections in Kashmir, said that the ground realities in the Valley are such that elections will not be a credible exercise at all.

"In the Parliamentary elections of 2004 and Assembly elections of 2002, the EC was able to keep the elections outside any controversy. But if they go for elections in November, they will undo everything."

Where the parties stand

•PDP opposes early elections in view of the troubled situation and wants the Centre to apply balm to the "bruised psyche" of the Kashmiris.

•NC is ready to go along with the polls if they are announced, but it wants the process to be delayed to let the situation in the Valley normalise.

•Congress has stopped short of publicly opposing polls, but its leadership is in favour of a postponement in view of the beating the party has taken in the agitation over the Amarnath land issue in Jammu.

•BJP is the only party that publicly supports early elections, because the Amarnath agitation has shored up its support base in Jammu.

•PDP feels the situation is not conducive for elections and believes that the Centre needs to defuse the volatile situation in the Valley with confidence-building measures.

•Panthers Party wants delimitation of the constituencies in the state before elections are held.

Heading: I’m not in demand, all up to leaders: Patil - Indian Express
Content:
Following the SIMI line of investigations, the Bangalore police could be on the verge of announcing its first arrest in the July 25 bomb blasts across the city that left one person dead and eight injured.

A special police team constituted to probe the nine low-intensity blasts that preceded the Ahmedabad blasts of July 26 have been interrogating a 23-year-old student of an arts and architecture college from Bijapur over the past two days.

The police had been looking for Abdul Samee, whose name figured in the interrogations of several alleged SIMI activists arrested around the country, including in the Ahmedabad, Jaipur cases. Sources said Samee was being questioned on his presence in Bangalore around the July 25 blasts and his absence from Bijapur over the weekend of the September 13 Delhi blasts.

The Bangalore police and IB are conducting the questioning.

Samee is believed to be one of the 20 who participated in a SIMI training conclave held on the organisation's foundation day, on April 25, 2007, at Castle Rock on Karnataka-Goa border. It was Adnan alias Hafeez Hussain, a SIMI leader from Karnataka arrested in Indore on March 23 this year with 12 other SIMI functionaries, who reportedly gave his name.

Abdul Subhan Qureshi alias Tauqeer — believed to be a key lynchpin in the blasts that have occurred around the country since July 2006 — Shahbaz Hussain, a key accused in the Jaipur blasts, and Abu Bashar, named as the mastermind of the Ahmedabad blasts, were reportedly all present at this camp.

According to sources, investigations into SIMI activities prior to the Jaipur blasts of May 13 had also thrown up Samee's name and the Karnataka police had even zeroed in on a student of the Malik Sandal Institute of Art and Architecture. But no arrests were made after the police were told that the student's name was Mohammed Samee and not Abdul Samee.

Sources said investigations had returned to the architecture student after his name figured in the interrogation of Shahbaz Hussain in Jaipur.

Samee's family in Bijapur, however, say the arrest is a result of mistaken identity. His father Raj Ahmed Bagewadi has produced college records to show that his son goes by the name of Mohammed Samee Bagewadi and not Abdul Samee.

The investigations surrounding the architecture student show that the Bangalore police is also taking the same line as the Jaipur, Ahmedabad and Delhi blast cases.

Investigations into the Bangalore blasts have until now produced little results. A parallel case of dumping of a large quantity of ammonium nitrate on the outskirts of Bangalore, a day before the blasts, is also being probed.

Heading: Patil’s concern at ‘metro terrorism’ - Indian Express
Content:
"Main daaru peeke baitha hoon (Am I drunk)?" asked Home Minister Shivraj Patil while reacting to questions on media criticism of him, especially his change of three sets of clothes on the night of Delhi blasts on Saturday.

"Main so gaya, main patte khel raha hoon, main daru peeke baitha hoon, main dance club jaata hoon toh aap mujhe dosh dijiye (Blame me if I am sleeping (on the job), playing cards, drinking and whiling my away time and frequenting dance clubs)," he told India TV.

The reporter showed him photos of the three different suits he wore on Saturday evening and wanted to know his reply to the criticism on that account.

A visibly upset Home Minister said, "After 13 hours of work if I take bath and change dress, is that a crime?"

To a question why he was "not on the job" for four hours that evening, Patil said "he was not an inspector to sit in a police station all the time".

He said he was in a meeting of the Congress party where all the leaders, including Sonia Gandhi and the Prime Minister were present. The moment he returned, the situation developed, Patil added.

Earlier, while talking to NDTV news channel, Patil said he would quit if the Congress leadership asked him to go.

"If the leadership is not with me there is no point of staying here. I am not in much demand. I am here just because of them (leadership). I have no group either. It's only that the leadership supports me that I continue to stay here," he said.

Over the criticism on his changing clothes thrice on Saturday, he said, "I will leave it to the people to judge. You judge yourself. Is this the correct way of criticising a politician? You criticise his policies, you don't criticise his clothes."

"If I keep my cool when it is necessary during such incidents, you find fault with me. And if they are doing it, do you expect me to reply to that kind of criticism against me," he retorted.

Heading: 7/11 links to documents seized from Gujarat mosque - Indian Express
Content:
Terming the serial blasts in Jaipur, Bangalore, Ahmedabad and Delhi in the last few months as "metro terrorism", President Pratibha Patil on Tuesday expressed her "serious concern" and called for innovative actions while dealing firmly against the perpetrators to prevent such incidents in the future.

"This emerging phenomenon of metro terrorism has given a new dimension to subversive activities and is a matter of serious concern," Patil said in her address at the Governors' Conference at Rashtrapati Bhawan today. "The state and Central Governments have to deal firmly with those who follow the path and culture of guns."

Addressing the 42nd conference of governors and the first after she took over as the President, Patil called for modernisation of the police force with greater investment in cyber and technical intelligence, communication systems and forensic capabilities. "There is a need for an institutional mechanism to seamlessly share intelligence on real-time basis," she added, suggesting that the help of ex-servicemen could be taken.

In his presentation in the evening, Home Minister Shivraj Patil apprised governors about the challenges in tackling Naxal and communal violence, and also talked about the need to modernise the police force and set up more police stations.

In her address, Patil expressed solidarity with victims of the Kosi flood and and called for the need to go beyond post-disaster management and focus on prevention, mitigation and reduction of such tragedies.

The first woman president of the country, she reminded governors of the urgent need to focus on women's empowerment.

Heading: India-Nepal talks on Kosi by month-end - Indian Express
Content:
A Document on the investigations in the 7/11 serial train blasts in Mumbai, which the Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) officials had recovered from a well inside the Sidi Saiyed mosque complex near Lal Darwaja here on September 1, along with other incriminating literature, was originally prepared by one of the accused of the Mumbai 7/11 blasts in Hindi. It was later translated into Gujarati by Usman Agarbattiwala, an accused of the July 26 Ahmedabad serial blasts.

Joint Commissioner of Police, DCB, Ashish Bhatia, said, "It was originally prepared by one of the accused of Mumbai 7/11 serial blasts and a SIMI leader of Maharashtra, Ehtesham Siddiqui, during his stay in Arthur Road Jail after his arrest in the 7/11 terror strike. He had provided the same to SIMI hardline leader Safdar Nagori."

Bhatia added that it wasn't clear how Siddiqui conveyed the details of the document to Nagori, who, in turn, circulated it among SIMI cadre here. A DCB official said that Usman Agarbattiwala had got the copy of the material, translated it into Gujarati, and circulated it among SIMI members here.

Acting on a tip-off, DCB officials had recovered a plastic bag from the well inside the mosque. The bag contained a register having details of police investigation in the 7/11 Mumbai blasts in Gujarati, a training manual for terror camps across the country, and police interrogation techniques, including details pertaining to narco analysis test.

According to DCB officials, the document carries details about the manner in which the Mumbai police investigated the case, and how they interrogated the accused.

"The information came to light during the interrogation of the accused in the case," Bhatia added.

Heading: At N-E summit, Thailand, Bangladesh promise investments in tourism, power - Indian Express
Content:
In the aftermath of a devastating flood in north Bihar caused by a breah in the emabankment of Kosi at Kusaha, India and Nepal have decided to "revitalise" the engagements on water related issues vis-a-vis rivers emanating from Nepal. As part of the plan, the secretary-level Joint Committee on Water Resources (JCWR) from both sides will be meeting in Kathmandu at the end of this month for the first time since 2004.

Official sources said the decision was taken after discussions between Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and visiting Nepalese Prime Minister Prachanda. They confirmed that expediting the preparation of a detailed project report (DPR) of the Saptkosi High Dam project in Barahkshetra, upstream in Kosi in Nepalese territory, will be high on the agenda during the talks.

During a meeting between the visiting Water Resources Minister of Nepal Bishnu Prasad Poudel and his Indian counterpart Saifuddin Soz on Tuesday, the Nepalese Government assured that it would provide necessary cooperation, including security to the field staff, to complete the preparation of the DPR in the minimum possible time.

For the Kathmandu talks, apart from the Secretary Water Resources, the Indian delegation will comprise senior representatives from the Ministry of Power, External Affairs, Central Water Commission, Ganga Flood Control Commission and those from Bihar, UP and Uttarakhand.

In addition to the Saptkosi High Dam, both sides will also discuss 6,000-MW Pancheshwar Multi-Purpose Project at the Mahakali River at the India-Nepal border in Uttarakhand. The work on the DPR for this project is already in an advanced stage.

In an indication of the mounting political momentum to manage the rivers originating from Nepal, Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar on Tuesday met the visiting Nepalese Prime Minister at the sidelines of a luncheon meeting of the India-Nepal Parliamentary Friendship Forum at the residence of JD(U) chief Sharad Yadav in the Capital.

The meeting holds significance in view of the fact that Kumar came to meet Prachanda aftre he failed to get an invitation from the Centre to participate in the official level talks with the visiting dignitary.

"I had said earlier that if the Centre invites me I would be happy to participate. But what can I do if they did not call me?" Kumar told The Indian Express after the meeting adding, "During my last meeting with our Prime Minister I had raised the need for talking to Nepal. I discussed the same things with the Nepal Prime Minister. There was nothing different. I have to take the initiative since Bihar is the victim."

Heading: Action against cops for not filing FIR: issue goes to larger bench - Indian Express
Content:
Thailand and Bangladesh have promised to come in a big way to the Northeastern region with industry captains and government representatives from both countries identifying power and tourism sectors as the most potential areas for them to come in.

This commitment from the two countries came at the end of the two-day North East Business Summit, the fourth in the series in the past four years that concluded here on Tuesday night. Meanwhile, as many as 247 Expressions of Interest (EoI) were received from 64 companies that are willing to invest in the region.

"We have identified at least six areas of investment opportunities in Northeast India, of which power plants, tourism and the service sectors are the most important. I hope investors from Thailand will soon come into this region," Sakchai Luansathitkul of the Thailand Board of Investment told the media.

Bangladeshi companies on the other hand have already entered into joint venture with Indian companies to set up three units in Tripura, a paper pulp unit, a rubber factory and a fruit processing plant, informed Farooq Sobhan, former Bangladesh foreign secretary.

The Indo-Bangladesh Chamber of Commerce & Industries and the Indian Chamber of Commerce signed an agreement on the sidelines of the summit aimed at strengthening business cooperation between the two countries.

Sobhan, who was part of the Bangladesh delegation, also hinted that the new Government that would take over in Bangladesh after the December elections would make the Chittagong port accessible to India.

The summit, which had delegations from as many as 12 countries, including Thailand, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Cambodia, Laos, Singapore, Malaysia, Brunei, the Arab League, Bhutan and the Czech Republic, also evoked a lot of interest among participants in the tourism sector.

Heading: No Sundays in Valley - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court on Tuesday referred a crucial question — whether punitive action could be taken against cops for failing to register FIRs — for consideration before the Constitution Bench.

Pushed by conflicting views of various benches of the apex court on the issue, the Bench of Justices B N Aggrawal and G S Singhvi directed that matter be placed before a larger bench for disposal.

While issuing the said directions, the Bench remarked that despite strictures passed against several policemen by courts, the government seems to be promoting those officials. "The person becomes a hero. Strictures have become a ground for promotions," the Bench said.

The matter was referred to the larger bench after the court noticed an anomaly that while in some cases the apex court had ruled that the FIR should be promptly registered and investigations launched immediately, in other cases, it had held that the investigative officer should conduct a preliminary inquiry before registering the FIR.

The reference of the issue to a larger bench comes in the backdrop of the bench's earlier direction to the Government to ensure suspension and imprisonment of police officers who fail to register an FIR on receiving a complaint.

The apex court's earlier directions for criminal prosecution of cops was given on a habeas corpus petition filed by Bhola Kamat, father of a 16-year-old UP girl who was abducted by some persons over a land dispute.

Kamat had complained about the UP police's refusal to register an FIR about the kidnap. The local police allegedly threatened Kamat to withdraw the case and enter into a compromise with the accused.

Heading: India, Nepal agree to rethink on 1950 treaty - Indian Express
Content:
With many working days lost to curfews during the Amarnath land agitation, Kashmir will have no holidays on Sundays for a while.

While banks have increased their working hours and will remain open on Sundays, schools and colleges, too, have chosen to hold classes on Sundays till the session ends in October.

Although a September-12 Government order had asked the head of schools and colleges to conduct extra classes, before and after regular classes, most of the educational institutions have chosen to keep the schools open for half day on Sundays.

"Forty working days have been lost (during the Amarnath land row). So in order to compensate for the lost time, the educational institutions have been asked to conduct extra classes over and above their regular classes. How do they do it has been left to their convenience. Some have planned to keep Sundays as working days. Our main aim is that the syllabus should be completed," said Khazir Wani, Director, Higher Education.

The administration has also advised educational institutes to cut down on timings of lunch, morning assemblies as well as physical activity classes. The order also asks heads of institutions to ensure presence of teachers and send a weekly attendance reports to administration. The largest banking chain in Kashmir, J&K Bank, has decided to remain open on Sundays. Other banks like HDFC, too, have decided to follow suit.

"The decision has been taken for the benefit of the people. Everybody knows that four out of seven days are non-working in the Valley. The decision can be revised in case things return to normal in the coming days," said Khurshid Ahmad Pandit, vice-president, Communication, J and K Bank.

Even separatists have expressed support for the open Sundays. Shops and business establishments across the Valley were open this Sunday as a mark of protest following a call for the same by the Kashmir Coordination committee.

Heading: Mortar shell blast kills 2 children in Kashmir - Indian Express
Content:
The Nepal Government on Tuesday showed its willingness to take a fresh look at the 1950 bilateral treaty even as India said it was ready to "update" the agreement to "reflect today's realities".

Nepal's Foreign Minister Upendra Yadav said both sides agreed in-principle to "revise, upgrade and rethink" on the treaty. "If we need a new treaty, there will be one. We are not saying whether it (the treaty) is unequal or equal. But the times have changed, so it needs to be changed for our friendship," he said.

India's Foreign Secretary Shiv Shankar Menon, however, said, "Nepal is keen on a (fresh) look at the 1950 treaty, to update it, we are ready to do so" even as he added, "Updating is pretty big word. We are not trying to limit our options."

Menon said a high-level committee at the level of Foreign secretaries of both countries would discuss the issue.

While Prachanda on Tuesday extended an invitation to Prime Minister Manmohan Singh to visit Nepal, the Foreign Secretary said they also decided to reactivate bilateral mechanisms to take forward the "unique" relations between the two neighbours.

Menon said besides the Foreign secretaries, Home secretaries of the two countries would also meet to review security concerns and other issues.

Heading: Fratricide hits IAF, Sergeant shoots senior - Indian Express
Content:
Two children were killed in north Kashmir's Gurez sector in Bandipore district in a mortar shell blast.

The blast took place close to the Line of Control (LoC) when a group of children were playing with an unattended mortar shell in a maize field. The deaths left the entire neighbourhood scared and a pall of gloom descended in the entire village when the bodies of the children were cremated on Tuesday afternoon.

A police spokesman in Srinagar confirmed the death of two children. "A deafening blast took place at Malangam resulting in the deaths of two children," he said.

The children were identified as Nisar Ahmad Lone, 15, and Sikander Sheikh, 13. Mohammad Yousuf Sheikh 12 suffered injuries.

"The boys were playing in the field when they saw the shell and started playing with it. It exploded with a big bang killing the two boys," he said. "While one of the boys died on the spot another succumbed to his injuries on the way to hospital. Yousuf is undergoing treatment in the hospital. Doctor's said he is out of danger."

The police have registered a case and started investigations are on.

According to sources, the site where the blasts took place near the LoC has seen heavy firing between Indian and Pakistani troops in recent times.

Heading: Jail officials held for letting out lifers regularly - Indian Express
Content:
In a rare case of fratricide in the Indian Air Force, a Sergeant posted on guard duty at the Kaliakunda airbase in West Bengal shot dead his senior officer early on Tuesday morning.

Sources said Sergeant D S Rajput shot Junior Warrant Officer (JWO) D C Mishra early in the morning with his standard machine carbine. The incident occurred at the strategic airbase that houses frontline MiG 27 fighters of the Air Force.

A court of inquiry has been ordered into the incident and Rajput has been arrested. While the COI will bring out details, sources said it does not seem to be a planned murder as the incident occurred at the guard post after Mishra went to check on Rajput. Action will be taken against Rajput as per the Indian Penal Code.

While fragging incidents — usually associated with operational stress — have plagued the Army in recent years, the Air Force has had a relatively cleaner record with one case each occurring in 2004 and 2005. The last fratricidal killing took place in July when a Major posted in Manipur was shot dead by a soldier, allegedly after the officer refused to grant him leave from duty.

Heading: Symonds says he’s sorry, promises to come back a better man - Indian Express
Content:
Manchester United begin their Champions League defence at home to Villarreal on Wednesday and manager Alex Ferguson has set his side the target of becoming the first team to retain the title. AC Milan were the last side to retain Europe's top trophy in 1990 but since the group stage format was introduced in 1992/93 nobody has matched them.

"The fact that no club has won it in successive seasons shows just how hard it is to win in the first place. But I really think we've got a great chance," Ferguson said.

The Scot's optimism is based on the depth of his squad and the different options open to him as he plots a third Champions League success. The arrival of striker Dimitar Berbatov adds greatly to United's attacking threat.

However, they start their challenge from Group E short of the kind of form that helped them dominate last season. The English and European champions have won just once this season and suffered a rare league defeat at Liverpool on Saturday, going down 2-1.

United also lost midfielder Michael Carrick at Anfield with an ankle injury and will be without Paul Scholes, who is suspended after his red card in the Super Cup final. They could though be boosted by the return from injury of Cristiano Ronaldo, who may figure among the substitutes. Coach Manuel Pellegrini is without both his leading scorers from last season — Turkey striker Nihat Kahveci and former United forward Giuseppe Rossi, who both have thigh problems.

Heading: Sixes & seven: Down the order, Aus look frail - Indian Express
Content:
Troubled Australian all-rounder Andrew Symonds expressed remorse on Tuesday over the "gone fishing" scandal and said he wanted to play for his country again.

The 33-year-old was axed from Australia's upcoming tour of India after opting to go fishing rather than attend a compulsory team meeting during their one-day series against Bangladesh in Darwin last month.

It was just the latest drama to engulf him during the past year. He was involved in an on-field dispute with Indian spinner Harbhajan Singh, upset Australian officials by declaring he would not play in Pakistan and was fined for missing a team bus in the West Indies.

There has been constant speculation over whether he will turn his back on international cricket and instead ply his trade in the Indian Premier League, but he insisted he wanted to play for Australia again.

"I'm going through the process of trying to improve and become not only a better cricketer but a better person," he said here in his first comments since the scandal. "I'm looking forward to the challenge of taking up cricket again for my club, state and country, hopefully."

Symonds, who is undergoing counselling, has apologised to his family, his team mates and cricket fans for his behaviour. He said he lived his life "for the moment" but knew he needed to change. "I'm in a position of responsibility, I can't live irresponsibly," he said. "I've realised that and it's probably taken me longer than it should have."

Symonds said his rise from a state player to international superstar had been difficult to cope with. "You get something cast over you which you have no control over. Being recognised is something I deal with well sometimes and at other times not so well," he told reporters. "Hopefully I can come out of this a better person and won't make these mistakes in the future."

It was not clear when he would play cricket again. His first chance to resume his international career would be in Australia's home series against New Zealand, with the opening Test at the Gabba in Brisbane from November 20-24.

Heading: On comeback trail, Tait hits all the right areas - Indian Express
Content:
It will be understandable if Anil Kumble breaks into a smile when he glances down the Australian team list on the morning of October 9, the first day of the first Test against Australia.

Any international captain will understand the relief that comes with the absence of Andrew Symonds and Adam Gilchrist at numbers 6 and 7, especially after the rather intimidating top-order that the Australians possess.

A batting average of 49 at No 7 speaks for itself in Gilchrist's case. And the only reason his retirement — at the end of India's tour Down Under earlier this year — did not leave a big hole in the line-up was because Symonds comfortably stepped into those massive shoes, scoring a pair of 70s in the very first Test after the wicket-keeper's retirement.

The absence of the duo in the Aussie touring party that lands here next week means those slots will be filled by Shane Watson and Brad Haddin. Could this prove to be their Achilles heel, waiting to be exposed?

'Difficult role'

Gilchrist himself shies away from speaking about the 'void', focusing instead on his replacement Brad Haddin's potential. "Haddin is a very experienced first-class cricketer and he has, in the past, forced his way into the one-day team on the strength of his batting alone. I am sure he will be able to do the job for Australia at No 7," he says.

It's only later, when Gilchrist speaks about the complexity of the role, that one understands the magnitude of the task Haddin has in store.

"It's an interesting position to bat. You start your innings with one of the recognised batsmen and then, when you play with the tail, you have to take on a leadership role. Batting at No 7 is something you learn as you go along. You work out how to handle situations and how to be as productive. It has a lot to do with trusting your natural instincts and having faith in them, a case of trusting yourself," he says.

Gilchrist made a living out of stalling several slides to help Australia bounce back after collapses, and while he has bailed the batsmen out time and again, even the bowlers might be sending him 'miss you' messages. Quick runs with a declaration looming were never a problem, after all.

Looking good for India

In contrast, India will be excited about the return of their regular No 7, who was sorely missed during the disappointing Test series against Sri Lanka. MS Dhoni's terrific show in the subsequent one-dayers showed that he has it in him to be a perfect late-order batsman in the Test line-up.

Even Gilchrist was all praise for the wicket-keeper, who was recently crowned ICC's ODI Player of the Year. "He has shown great qualities as a leader. Despite the pressure and expectations, I have been amazed by his calm. I have never seen him lose control of his emotions or let his team get out of control," says the former Aussie wicket-keeper about India's ODI captain.

If this is the kind of impact Dhoni has made on the Aussies, wonder how Ricky Ponting will be feeling when he gets the Indian team sheet on the morning of October 9. After all, Dhoni at No 7 after an intimidating top-order isn't a sight captains around the world would like to see.

Heading: Praveen likes to do things his own way - Indian Express
Content:
It has been quite a turnaround. Burnt out about nine months back, Shaun Tait is back, and he's turning the heat on batsmen just like old times.

On Tuesday, he demolished the much talked-about India A top-order that included Robin Uthappa, Suresh Raina and S Badrinath to guide the visitors to an emphatic win. Batting first, India A reached 207, thanks mainly to Yusuf Pathan's half-century and crucial contributions from the lower order, after being down in the dumps at 55-5 at one stage.

But that was hardly enough as the Australia A batsmen, who had crumbled to 106 against New Zealand A on Monday, got to 168 for one to complete a nine-wicket win by the VJD method in the rain-interrupted match.

Virtually unplayable, Tait said he wasn't bowling with an eye on the speed gun but was focussed on his line and length. "I can't be a Glenn McGrath, but at least I can try to copy his line and length," he said after the match. Except that he was hitting the right areas at over 145kmph.

In the first over, Tait was a bit wayward even as he consistently crossed the 90 mph mark. But the wicket of Uthappa, trapped in front, turned it around. "When I try to bowl fast, it tends to go all over the place. On my comeback, the first thing I wanted to do was bowl a consistent line and length. I knew I didn't have to worry about my pace," Tait told The Indian Express after the match.

He bowled Raina with a delivery that swung in late from a good length spot, while Badrinath edged one while trying to drive without moving his feet. "It is always good to dismiss the top order. It boosts your confidence and I'm looking forward to continuing this way," he said.

While he is smiling now, it was a frustrated Tait who had walked off the field on Monday after going wicket-less against the Kiwis. "The first match against New Zealand didn't turn out well for me. Actually, I was trying too hard to take wickets and bowl fast. But there are certain things I have realised and now I am focussing on those areas."

Brief scores: India A 207 (Yusuf Pathan 54, Abhishek Nayar 30, Praveen Kumar 31; Noffke 4-39, Tait 3-27) lost to Australia A 168 for 1 (Ronchi 108 n.o., Philip Hughes 47) by nine wickets and VJD method.

Heading: Chopra, Kohli put Delhi right back on track - Indian Express
Content:
Praveen Kumar doesn't make a very good first impression with the ball - a medium pace trundler at best, perhaps. But, as one of his team mates points out, he is one of the most street-smart performers on the cricket field.

The 21-year-old Uttar Pradesh pacer knows his strengths and weaknesses, and is fully aware that being fast is not as important as it is made out to be.

And while many a batsmen have already been surprised by the amount of movement he gets with the new ball, even more surprising is his aversion to the use of technology. In an era where video analysis is as much a part of the cricketer's dictionary as the straight drive, Kumar insists he has never sat down to watch tapes of his performances.

"People say do this, do that, your hand should come from here, your hand should come from there — but at the end of the day, I'm the one who has to bowl and I know what I'm doing," he told The Indian Express.

All in the head

Called "bhagad" (bullock) by his team mates, he says his most important asset is not his strength or focus. "My brain is the key," he says, tapping his temples. "All the recipes are in here, I just need to implement them on the ground."

Oddly enough, he doesn't believe in the age-old theory of not bowling to a batsman's strength. "People said that Ricky Ponting is the best player of the pull in the game, but he gets out a lot playing that shot. Even when I bowled to Pakistan's Kamran Akmal, I was told not to bowl short of length, but I got his wicket with a short pitched delivery," he says.

What he hasn't figured out yet, and is desperate to, is how to carry on his his domestic batting prowess into the international arena. "Whenever I have gone out to bat, I have one or two overs left to play," says Praveen, who has failed to make the few opportunities he has got to count. "I'm hoping things fall into place."

Heading: What next for Bangladesh? - Indian Express
Content:
One is hoping for a recall, the other for his first Test call-up. Together, Aakash Chopra and Virat Kohli spent Tuesday evening delivering a discourse on the ideal approach towards the longer format of the game. And, irrespective of how mediocre the opposition attack might have been, especially with the pitch easing up under the harsh sun, their three-hour long effort in endurance had done more for Delhi's charge towards the Mohammad Nissar Trophy than Virender Sehwag's energetic 36 minutes splash-and-dash earlier in the day.

Surprisingly, even at 242 for 1 in the second innings at the end of Day Two, Delhi were not in a commanding position. But after wiping out the huge 132-run first innings deficit, courtesy the unfinished second-wicket run-a-minute partnership of 196, the hosts are now in a position from where they can dictate terms to Sui Northern Gas Pipeline Limited (SNGPL).

Sehwag's flourish

Rocking back and stepping forward, Sehwag slammed the first two balls he faced through the covers. He picked first-innings tormentor Imran Ali for special treatment — spanking him for five of his six boundaries, including a 15-run over that had a six over mid-wicket. He tried to turn a short ball from outside the off-stump, but only managed to direct it to the fielder at fine-leg. It was time to walk back after a 29-ball 37 — while it lasted, there was entertainment for the few standing in the gallery; when it was over, it demoralised those sitting in the pavilion.

Kohli walked in to join Chopra in the middle session and they methodically went about deconstructing the visiting bowlers — anything pitched too short or too full was directed to the ropes, and the strike was rotated at regular intervals. They were neck-and-neck as far as the scoring, and the scoring rate, went, and when stumps were called, Chopra was batting on 93 from 146 balls with ten sweetly timed boundaries while Virat had had 14 thundering hits to the fence in his 91.

In fact, the only reason Delhi didn't end day two right on top was their bowling in the first session, which was sub-standard.

'I've to keep scoring'

Later in the evening, Chopra played all questions thrown at him with as straight a bat as the one he had used through the evening. "I don't need to send a message to anyone. I score runs for personal satisfaction, we are professional cricketers, we get paid for scoring runs," he said.

Ignored by selectors, Chopra said he would continue to be relentless with the bat. "Honestly, I have no option. The fact that you're not getting picked is up to the selectors. If you don't score runs, then it's like shooting yourself in the foot. It's important that I keep presenting my case."

Heading: Cooped up, Mumbai football wants to break free - Indian Express
Content:
After lying low for most of the last six months, the 'rebels' have finally unsheathed their swords again. And all the cuts, for now, are making Bangladesh cricket bleed.

At a glitzy ceremony on Tuesday, the Indian Cricket League paraded four Bangladesh cricketers — Habibul Bhashar, Shariar Nafees, Alok Kapali and Dhiman Ghosh — and announced the names of nine others as they launched their ninth team, the Dhaka Warriors.

With 11 of the 13 players having international experience, it is by far the biggest coup the Zee-bankrolled league has pulled off, and is sure to give a body blow to the game in the south-Asian country, which is anyway struggling to find its feet at the international level.

Be that as it may, Messrs Kapil Dev & Co are not going to lose their sleep over it. Ask them whether this coup would devastate Bangladesh cricket and most react with a shrug of the shoulders.

"Well, it'll certainly have an effect," admits Himanshu Modi, ICL's business head. "How much? I can't really say."

But former skipper Bashar and his mates insisted on Tuesday evening that there was enough talent to replace them.

"It will leave a vacuum, no doubt, for sometime at least," says Bashar, who chose to ignore the Bangladesh Cricket Board summons for a meeting on Tuesday over the ceremony. "But then there's enough depth in Bangladesh cricket."

Shariar Nafees, one of the six players to resign on Sunday, magnanimously looks at the flip side of coin — how his move would actually benefit the up and coming players.

"It actually is an opportunity for the youngsters to come in our place and showcase their talent at the international level," he adds.

The League's Executive board member Kiran More, oddly enough, insists the move is going to harm no one. His logic: "The future of the game is club cricket and not international cricket."

Chairman Kapil sounds more compassionate and wishes that Bangladesh cricket keeps doing fine, but refuses to take the blame if doesn't.

"I hope it doesn't (affect them)," he says. "But if it does, we (the ICL) are not to be blamed.

"You see, we don't have any problems if these guys play the ICL and go back home for their national duties. They've (ICC and BCCI) boycotted us, we've not boycotted them," he adds.

Earlier, while launching the Dhaka Warriors, the ninth ICL team, and announcing start the second season of the league, Kapil took a swipe at "a few people in the ICL" who were not allowing the ICL to be recognised.

"There are only a few people, only a handful of people, who are dividing the game. One man, and I don't want to take his name, is doing all he can so that we remain pariah," he said, making an obvious reference to IPL chief Lalit Modi.

He added that their growth would not stop at the Dhaka Warriors, and that new teams would come up soon.

"Last year, we brought Lahore Badshah into our fold, this year we have the Dhaka Warriors. It is only getting bigger and we are working on bringing teams from other countries next year," Kapil added.

Heading: Kaushik set to return as men’s hockey coach - Indian Express
Content:
It can hardly be called the hub of Indian football, but three clubs from Mumbai will figure in the second season of the I-league beginning on September 28.

But if that figure suggests that football in the city is on the rise, think again.

The three clubs in the fray — Durand Cup champions Mahindra United, newly-promoted Mumbai FC and Air-India — continue to struggle for a proper home ground. The All India Football Federation's (AIFF) approval to the Cooperage as the venue for home I-league matches for yet another season means a series of afternoon games, in unforgiving heat and humidity, in front of a smattering of spectators.

"Playing at 3.30 in the afternoon is like killing yourself. Players can never be at their peak prowess under such conditions," says homegrown striker Abhishek Yadav, who will be representing Mumbai FC this season.

Yadav believes that a player's game goes up by at least 30 per cent when playing on a ground which is in good shape and, more importantly, a ground which he can call home.

Mahindra's coach Derrick Pereira believes it is high time Mumbai got a decent stadium. "We are not asking for something as grand as the Wankhede or even DY Patil for that matter. We need a small facility with floodlights which can at least seat around 10,000 spectators," he says. Pereira adds that the teams lack any kind of home advantage when playing at Cooperage with regards to crowd and ground conditions.

Even the Cooperage is in a bad shape, thanks to litigation issues and the Western India Football Association's (WIFA), which is in charge of the ground, slack attitude.

There was a glimmer of hope when the WIFA said it would install floodlights, even if temporary, this season. But with those plans postponed, that hope has been quashed. Yadav, a former Mahindra player himself, talks of how his team was forced to play their AFC matches in Goa, when the Asian federation termed the conditions at the Cooperage unfit for international matches.

The blame game

All India Football Federation official Col. Gautam Kar said that constructing a stadium is not their prerogative. Mumbai District Football Association secretary Souter Vaz blames bad scheduling which led to further deterioration of the ground. "WIFA organised unnecessary tournaments earlier in the year, especially just before the I-league was about to start," says Vaz.

Some of the matches might be shifted to the swanky DY Patil Staduim this season, but Air-India coach Bimal Ghosh, though, believes there is no need to shift base. "It is a historic venue and I'm sure the stadium will come up in a year or so. Our fan development programme will be finished if they shift," he says.

Ghosh says that more attention needs to be given to facilities for spectators.

"The sport will develop only if more people are attracted to the ground. The players' dressing rooms can be of a sub-standard quality. We spend just around an hour there anyway," he adds.

Heading: Senior statesman Ritwik revels in the hunt - Indian Express
Content:
More than six months after India's Olympic qualifiers debacle, and four months after the Indian Hockey Federation was suspended, the men's team finally seems to have got a coach.

At a selection committee meeting chaired by IOA secretary general Randhir Singh, the decision to appoint MK Kaushik as the chief coach of the national team was taken. Kaushik returns to the post after a 10-year gap.

While no official announcement was made, Kaushik confirmed that he has been informed about the decision. "Yes, I was called in the evening (after the meeting got over) and told about the decision," he said. "But the official announcement will be made only later."

Kaushik was at the helm when India won the Bangkok Asian Games in 1998. Immediately after that, he and seven senior players were unceremoniously sacked by KPS Gill. For the past several years, Kaushik has been with the senior women's team.

Asked if he was willing to take on the responsibility again, Kaushik said he was willing provided he had the necessary clearance from his department (the Haryana government sports board).

"For almost two years, I have not been working properly with the women's team either. Now, the Sports Authority of India have written to my department and agreed to take me on deputation till 2010, allowing me to work full time with the team," he said.

It has also been decided that former junior coach Harendra Singh will assist Kaushik while AB Subbiah will be the goalkeeping coach. Subbiah had earlier worked with Kaushik during his stint with the women's team.

Kaushik's appointment means AK Bansal, who had been in charge of the team since Joaquim Carvalho quit after the Chile Olympic qualifiers in March this year, will be shunted back to the junior team. Bansal had managed to come up with good results with the team, finishing runners-up in the Azlan Shah tournament and winning the junior Asia Cup recently. "No one is questioning Bansal's calibre," said a member of the selection committee. "But we felt that Kaushik has more experience at the senior level.

"We have just one year to prepare for three big tournaments — the World Cup, Commonwealth Games and the Asian Games (all to be held in 2010, the first two in India). So we needed someone someone respected by all."

The selection committee also finalised the list of 48 probables that would form the core of the Indian team till 2010. The list will be made official after being approved by the IOA ad-hoc committee and the sports ministry.

Gill to hold 'AGM' today

KPS Gill is going ahead with the Annual General Meeting of the suspended IHF here on Wednesday. With the IHF suspended, the IOA-constituted ad-hoc committee has been given legal sanction to conduct the affairs of the game. "Gill can have any number of meetings he wants, but he cannot call them the AGM. He has not been provided any relief by the courts, how can a suspended body hold its AGM," questioned ad-hoc committee convenor Mohammad Aslam Khan.

However, with elections to Hockey India — the joint men's and women's body that will replace the IHF — likely to be held by year-end, this could end up being a show of strength for Gill and his supporters.

Heading: Jeev looking forward to taking on the world - Indian Express
Content:
He's barely 28, but already Ritwik Bhattacharya finds himself in the position of senior statesman, often slipping into 'when-I-was...' mode with young greenhorns hanging onto his every word.

Indian squash's first real achiever on the PSA circuit, Bhattacharya is heading into a phase where his contribution to the sport begins to have an impact beyond the number of titles he'll pick, or the seven that he has previously won (still three ahead of the rapidly rising Saurav Ghosal).

But Bhattacharya isn't averse to playing mentor to the burgeoning group of juniors — fresh talent mushrooming in different parts of India.

Sensing the buzz at the Bombay Gymkhana, where 35-40 juniors were bursting with energy as Mumbai looked to get back seriously on the squash-radar, the senior hurriedly agreed to a detour to the city, squeezing the state open in between two scheduled events.

Regularly sought out for coaching clinics, Bhattacharya goes about his job as an advisor diligently. The home-page to his website is peppered with advice and Mumbai junior Mahesh Mangaonkar got an elaborate pep-talk before he started out to Zurich for the World Juniors: Relax, enjoy the event, play as a team with passion...

"I end up learning too, and most times when I'm teaching them, I realise we didn't have these things when I started playing," he states. Wisdom flows, as the pro who has spent close to a decade at the highest level with a top-ranking of 38, plays the guide.

The Delhiite, who has virtually shifted base to Mumbai, believes he has another three-four years of squash in him, at least. He looks fitter, believes his current flexibility makes his past self seem a joke, and attributes it to the serious yoga sessions under Bandra-specialist Mr Vinayak. "Squash is all that I want to do," he says, and taking up the challenge thrown by Saurav Ghosal is something he's enjoying.

"It's not been a great year at all," he says of his indifferent season. "Post-injury, sometimes the game cracks apart, but when it comes together, it's very effective." The man's clearly enjoying the struggle — the climb up from rank 79 and the three lacklustre nationals, where he's gone without the title.

Bhattacharya was around when Ghosal picked his career-best win at France, and says, "If not me, it was good that the winner was another Indian. He's playing better than anyone else in India, and alongwith Sidharth Suchde, they've raised the bar in Indian squash. It's exciting now that I'm not being chased, but doing the chasing."

Heading: Tiger’s niece out to prove it runs in the family - Indian Express
Content:
Ten years ago may have been one of those rare times when Jeev Milkha Singh was tempted to make a bold statement. He had just taken part in the Eisenhower Trophy in 1988 and missed a short par putt when he heard someone say, "Playing for the country should be the top priority," and in reply, Jeev had said "Yes, I firmly believe that."

As India's top-ranked golfer returned to Chandigarh on Tuesday after finishing tied 11th in the Mercedes-Benz Championship at Cologne, Germany, he remembered the reference as talk turned to him pairing up with compatriot Jyoti Randhawa in the Mission Hills World Cup to be held in China from November 27 to 30.

"The World Cup is something I have always dreamt of. It's even more special than the Masters, and both Jyoti and I cherish it. I think we have got an excellent chance," he said. "The last time I played in a team event was during the Royal Trophy between Europe and Asia in the later part of 2006. I have some fine memories of playing in the Eisenhower Trophy early in my career and I hope this team event will be good for me," says Jeev .

The 38-year-old golfer found himself among the top 60 players in the world on Tuesday, a feat which brought back memories of the 2006 season, in which he fetched four wins and 18 top-ten finishes.

"I think this year I have been more consistent. I will play in the Singapore Open, Mount Open and HSBC Open Championship before I play in the World Cup," said Jeev.

Injury worries

The Chandigarh golfer has been nursing a right-foot injury which meant he missed practice rounds during most of the tournaments. "My right foot is in very bad condition and I need at least four to six weeks of complete rest. Last month was the only time after 2000 that I had a break for more than three weeks," Jeev says. "Even during the Masters Championship, I played 35 holes on the last day while taking eight painkillers. I had an MRI scan in New York last week and it showed the foot is healing."

Over the last few months, Jeev intends to set his record straight in India. "That's the only part I need to work on. I will be playing in the British Masters Open and Dunhill Open before I play in the Indian Open in October. People think of me as a global player but I need to do well in my home country too," feels Jeev.

"I have also committed to playing in the PGTI BILT Open after the Volvo Masters," says the 60th-ranked player as he tees off at the Chandigarh Golf Club.

Heading: Two approaches to Wall St: McCain thinks it’s greed, Obama blames lax regulation - Indian Express
Content:
Real Madrid coach Bernd Schuster is already looking beyond the Champions League group stages in his mission to raise the nine-time champions back to the summit of European football.

Madrid's journey to May's final in Rome begins against BATE Borisov, the Belarusians making their Champions League debut. "If we have just a little more luck we can get past the first knockout round without any problems," Schuster said. Defender Fabio Cannavaro could make his first appearance of the season after missing Euro 2008 with an ankle injury.

Group H has gained the "group of death" tag due to the presence of 1996 champions Juventus and Zenit St. Petersburg, who last month added the UEFA Super Cup to the UEFA Cup they won in May.

Two-time champions Juventus will be determined to show the Champions League just what they have missed during their two-year absence resulting from Italy's match-fixing scandal.

Bayern Munich return to the Champions League against Steaua Bucharest in Group F without Franck Ribery. The midfielder is back in training after ankle surgery, but isn't ready for a full match.

Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger isn't relishing the trip to Dynamo Kiev as the prelude to further tricky ties with FC Porto and Fenerbahce in Group G. "It is a difficult group because all the teams are used to playing in the Champions League — and they are all strong at home," Wenger said.

In other matches, Scotland's Celtic take on Danish side Aalborg BK and FC Porto face Turkey's Fenerbahce. French champions Lyon are up against Italian club Fiorentina.

Heading: Time to teach kids a financial lesson - Indian Express
Content:
The crisis on Wall Street will leave the next president facing tough choices about how best to regulate the financial system, and although neither Senator Barack Obama nor Senator John McCain has yet offered a detailed plan, their records and the principles they have set out so far suggest they could come at the issue in very different ways.

On the campaign trail, McCain, the Republican presidential nominee, struck a populist tone. Speaking in Florida, he said that the economy's underlying fundamentals remained strong but were being threatened "because of the greed by some based in Wall Street and we have got to fix it."

But his record on the issue, and the views of those he has always cited as his most influential advisers, suggest that he has never departed in any major way from his party's embrace of deregulation and relying more on market forces than on the government to exert discipline.

While McCain has cited the need for additional oversight when it comes to specific situations, like the mortgage problems behind the current shocks on Wall Street, he has consistently characterized himself as fundamentally a deregulator and he has no history prior to the presidential campaign of advocating steps to tighten standards on investment firms.

He has often taken his lead on financial issues from two outspoken advocates of free market approaches, former Senator Phil Gramm and Alan Greenspan, the former Federal Reserve chairman. Individuals associated with Merrill Lynch, which sold itself to Bank of America in the market upheaval of the past weekend, have given his presidential campaign nearly $300,000, making them Mr. McCain's largest contributor, collectively.

Obama sought to attribute the financial upheaval to lax regulation during the Bush years, and in turn to link McCain to that approach.

"I certainly don't fault Senator McCain for these problems, but I do fault the economic philosophy he subscribes to," Obama told several hundred people who gathered for an outdoor rally in Grand Junction, Colorado.

Obama set out his general approach to financial regulation in March, calling for regulating investment banks, mortgage brokers and hedge funds much as commercial banks are. And he would streamline the overlapping regulatory agencies and create a commission to monitor threats to the financial system and report to the White House and Congress.

On Wall Street's Republican-friendly turf, Obama has outraised McCain. He has received $9.9 million from individuals associated with the securities and investment industry, $3 million more than McCain, according to the Center for Responsive Politics, a watchdog group. His advisers include Wall Street heavyweights, including Robert E Rubin, the former treasury secretary who is now a senior adviser at Citigroup, another firm being buffeted by the financial crisis.

If many voters are fuzzy on the events that over the weekend forced Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc. into bankruptcy and Merrill Lynch & Company to be swallowed by the Bank of America Corporation, the continuing chaos among the most venerable names in American finance -- coming on top of the recent government seizure of mortgage giants Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac and the demise of the Bear Stearns Companies -- has stoked their anxiety for the economy, the foremost issue on voters' minds.

So it was that first Obama and then McCain rushed out their statements before most Americans had reached their workplaces.

Heading: Pink Floyd’s Wright dies of cancer at 65 - Indian Express
Content:
See Sally. See Sally run from the bank. Run Sally run.

In the midst of one of the worst banking crises in decades, the US Treasury Department will launch today a long-planned programme to teach young Americans about credit and other financial matters.

The theme of the campaign: "Don't let your credit put you in a bad place."

Like in bankruptcy court?

Don Iannicola, the department's deputy assistant secretary for financial education, tried to put the best face on the timing of the announcement. "The events unfolding in the last few months can be seen as a national teachable moment," Iannicola said.

Planning for the programme, which cost about $750,000, began last year. Iannicola said Treasury officials didn't consider delaying the launch. "There is no bad time for people to learn about their money and their credit," he said.

The Treasury folks aren't planning a similar programme for heads of financial institutions or regulators.

Iannicola acknowledged that some might detect a contradiction in a Treasury-sponsored education programme being launched at a time when slack government oversight was getting some of the blame for the mortgage market meltdown that begat the credit crunch that led to Monday's financial fallout.

The programme will consist of television and radio spots, web banners and a site (www.controlyourcredit.gov) that has an interactive game called The Bad Credit Hotel.

No word on whether there will be a Lehman Bros. suite or early check-out policy.

Heading: Pak aircraft bomb militants; US drones prowl - Indian Express
Content:
Richard Wright, a founding member of the rock group Pink Floyd, died on Monday. He was 65.

Pink Floyd's spokesman Doug Wright, who is not related to the artist, said Wright died after a battle with cancer at his home in Britain. He says the band member's family did not want to give more details about his death.

Wright met Pink Floyd members Roger Waters and Nick Mason in college and joined their early band, Sigma 6. Along with the late Syd Barrett, the four formed Pink Floyd in 1965.

The group's jazz-infused rock and drug-laced multimedia "happenings" made them darlings of the London psychedelic scene, and their 1967 album, The Piper at the Gates of Dawn, was a hit.

In the early days of Pink Floyd, Wright, along with Barrett, was seen as the group's dominant musical force. The London-born musician and son of a biochemist wrote songs and sang.

The band released a series of commercially and critically successful albums including 1973's Dark Side of the Moon, which has sold more than 40 million copies. Wright wrote The Great Gig In The Sky and Us And Them for that album, and later worked on the group's epic compositions such as Atom Heart Mother, Echoes and Shine On You Crazy Diamond.

But tensions grew between Waters, Wright and fellow band member David Gilmour. The tensions came to a head during the making of The Wall when Waters insisted Wright be fired. As a result, Wright was relegated to the status of session musician on the tour of The Wall, and did not perform on Pink Floyd's 1983 album The Final Cut.

Wright formed a new band Zee with Dave Harris, from the band Fashion, and released one album, Identity, with Atlantic Records.

Waters left Pink Floyd in 1985 and Wright began recording with Mason and Gilmour again, releasing the albums The Division Bell and A Momentary Lapse of Reason as Pink Floyd. Wright also released the solo albums Wet Dream (1978) and Broken China (1996).

In July 2005, Wright, Waters, Mason and Gilmour reunited to perform at the Live 8 charity concert in London — the first time in 25 years they had been onstage together.

Wright also worked on Gilmour's solo projects, most recently playing on the 2006 album On An Island and the accompanying world tour.

Heading: Pak orders troops to stop US raids - Indian Express
Content:
Pakistani aircraft bombed militant strongholds in a northwestern region on Tuesday while US drones prowled the sky over another militant sanctuary on the Afghan border, a military official and residents said.

Pakistani forces launched offensives against al Qaeda and Taliban militants in the northwest in August and the government says hundreds of militants have been killed.

But at the same time, US forces have stepped up strikes on militants on the Pakistani side of the border, angering Islamabad and straining relations between the allies.

Admiral Mike Mullen, chairman of the US Joint Chiefs of Staff, was due in Pakistan late on Tuesday.

Mullen said this month he was not convinced Western forces were winning in Afghanistan and he was looking at a new, more comprehensive strategy that would cover both sides of the border, including Pakistan's tribal areas.

Pakistani aircraft bombed three areas of Bajaur on Tuesday as ground troops searched house-to-house for militants, a military spokesman said.

They have constructed underground bunkers and along with foreign fighters are putting up stiff resistance. Troops are clearing each and every house in these areas, said military spokesman Major Murad Khan.

Heading: Fingers crossed, Petraeus heads out of Iraq - Indian Express
Content:
Pakistan's military has ordered its forces to open fire if US troops launch another raid across the Afghan border, an army spokesman said Tuesday. The orders mark a dangerous escalation in tension between Washington and a key ally in its seven-year war on terror.

Pakistani protests are hardening in the wake of a September 3 incident in which helicopters ferried US commandos into Pakistan for a highly unusual ground attack in a militant stronghold.

The country's civilian leaders, who have taken a tough line against Islamic militants since forcing US ally Pervez Musharraf to resign as president last month, have insisted that Pakistan must resolve the spat with Washington through diplomatic channels.
