Well, the first is that, sure, capital control proponents can be happy that institutional investors losing money with Lehman aren't taking a lot of the money away from us. But our markets are growing: we will have to start worrying about contagion here soon enough. When that day comes, what's partly insulating us now may mean that our system doesn't have the adaptability that others do. The second? Think hard about regulation. It isn't the under-regulated that may fail — perhaps it's the incentives that need to be looked at. The third — we have the chance to build an open, transparent, comprehensible financial system from scratch. Let's not lose it.

mihir.sharma@expressindia.com

Heading: No light at the end of the tunnel - Indian Express
Content:
There are times when the ability and willingness to call a spade a spade matter more than anything else. It is imperative for an elected government to distinguish fact from speculation and act accordingly. Above all, it is mandated to protect the citizens it is responsible for. The attacks on churches across Karnataka would have been mitigated and even stopped had the B.S. Yeddyurappa government treated the issue first and foremost as a law and order problem. Of course, the CM has promised action and the maintenance of peace and harmony. Vacuous as those terms are, we all have a rough idea as to what they signify and why they are so vital to the continuance of civilised life. But the "iron hand" that the CM has promised hasn't quite been manifest as policemen deployed couldn't prevent the Bajrang Dal and VHP activists from running amok, targeting churches. It is an axiom that police personnel act when there is the political will.

Attacks on citizens abiding by the law of the land cannot be obfuscated by ideology and argument. And the government doesn't have the luxury to waste time and words. There are wild people causing havoc and they must be stopped before they do more damage. But Yeddyurappa had initially chosen to preface his comments by stating that forced conversions are inappropriate. The CM doesn't, and should not, hold any brief for a particular community. His job is to ensure that ordinary people attending a prayer meeting do not face violence of any kind. The government's self-congratulatory message on concluding 100 days in office significantly failed to account for the attacks on Christians in Karnataka.

There may or may not be economic reasons behind the attacks. But we do not yet know enough about that. While Orissa's (another state that has witnessed attacks against Christians recently) development story is usually ignored, Karnataka has been treated by the media as a great success. What is happening in the state now is a serious reversal of image, something that no constituent territory of the Indian Union can afford.

Heading: Lalu’s right - Indian Express
Content:
I am desperately homesick after six years of exile from Zimbabwe. Yet [the] power-sharing deal between Robert Mugabe, Morgan Tsvangirai and Arthur Mutambara has not brought me any relief that I can re-enter a new democratic country... What Zimbabwe desperately needs is a complete re-birth. A complete break with Mugabe's political and economic insanity. This required a settlement in which he is not involved. But he remains in the driving seat. You cannot teach an old dog new tricks. At 85, Mugabe has not suddenly transmogrified from a murderous tyrant into a true democrat... His long, incoherent and rambling acceptance speech yesterday confirmed my worst fears. There was nothing in it to exemplify any vision for the reconstruction of his embattled country...

Mugabe remained stuck in his favourite, but hugely irrelevant, subjects: colonialism, blaming Britain for everything wrong in Zimbabwe and eulogising the '70s liberation struggle. Not a word about how to move Zimbabwe forward from the dark dungeon into which he has plunged the country... In [his] own words, the power-sharing deal can only last as long as all the parties uphold certain "salient principles" that he holds dear...

How will Tsvangirai revive Zimbabwe's agro-based economy without reversing Mugabe's destructive land reforms... How will Tsvangirai persuade investors to come, without entirely repealing unsustainable empowerment laws which prescribe majority shareholding by black Zimbabweans in all firms? How will Tsvangirai endeavour to accommodate international donor prescriptions for aid without being accused of compromising on national sovereignty?

Excerpted from a comment by Basildon Peta in 'The Independent'

Heading: Maiden Visit - Indian Express
Content:
Prosecutors in an Italian court Thursday asked the key middleman in the IAF's VVIP chopper deal whether the initials 'AP' in an alleged "budget sheet" for bribes to politicians referred to Ahmed Patel, the political secretary of UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

The middleman, Guido Haschke, who has consistently denied bribing Indian officials or politicians, replied that he did not know who or what 'AP' stood for.

As first reported by The Indian Express, Italian prosecutors had last month produced a handwritten document they alleged was a "budget" drawn up by two middlemen — Haschke and Christian Michel — which purportedly lists initials of Indian politicians and designations of bureaucrats and IAF officers who allegedly had to be "handled" to fix the Rs 3,546 crore deal.

The alleged "budget sheet" detailed how kickbacks of 51 million euros would be divided and under the heading "POL" — Haschke has claimed this referred to Indian politicians — there is a reference to "AP" against which "3 million euro" has been listed.

Another amount of 15/16 million euros was listed against "FAM" which is said to be "Family". Haschke has claimed the note was dictated to him by British consultant Michel during one of their meetings in 2008.

On Thursday, Italian prosecutor Eugenio Fusco asked Haschke during a court hearing in Busto Arsizio near Milan whether "AP" in the note was a reference to Ahmed Patel.

In his reply, the middlemen said he did not know what AP meant when he wrote it down. Haschke also denied any bribes were paid for the contract and said that the "budget sheet" was just an imaginary note drawn up and was never acted upon.

He also said the budget sheet was merely bragging by Michel about his Indian contacts and that Haschke tried to disassociate himself from the Briton.

Strongly denying any wrongdoing in the deal, Haschke also claimed to Indian interrogators in the court that no bribes were paid for the contract and that the money he received from AgustaWestland - in excess of 24 million euros - is justified as fees for engineering consultations.

Italian prosecutors also produced another note in court Thursday - a March 2008 fax by Michel to Peter Hulett, said to be the then head of region, govt sales at AgustaWestland's India office. The fax said that among the politicians who would use the choppers once acquired by India would be UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and her senior advisors, including Ahmed Patel.

However, Sonia is not entitled to use government helicopters. She can use VIP aircraft only when she flies with the PM, President or ministers who are officially entitled to the aircraft. This fax by the British middleman has also been shared by the Italian side with the CBI team that is in Busto Arsizio for the hearing.

Michel has been elusive and no investigative agency has been able to reach him.

Haschke, who is facing a case in Italy for being part of a conspiracy to bribe Indian officials to ensure the AW 101 chopper was picked by the IAF, faced several questions from the Indian side and denied any irregularity.

But the Indian side did not ask Haschke to explain what AP, FAM or any of the other acronyms in the note - "DS", "JS AIR", "AFA", "DG Acquisition", CVC" etc - referred to, source said.

The middleman, who was quizzed about his association with former Air Chief S P Tyagi - named as an accused in the CBI case in the deal - denied that any money had been paid to the retired Indian officer. Haschke, sources said, admitted that he was in regular touch with three cousins of Tyagi who have also been named in the case.

In response to a question from the Indian side, Haschke said he was not aware if any money was paid to S P Tyagi.

The UPA government had come under pressure in connection with the alleged kickbacks last month after The Indian Express report on the budget sheet of the middlemen. The opposition BJP had demanded the government reveal what or who "AP" and "FAM" stand for. The party also said that it wants a detailed discussion in Parliament on "alleged payments to persons close to the ruling establishment" in connection with the controversial chopper deal and has accused the government of "running away from discussions".

The discussion did not take place as the Parliament session was abruptly called off midway.

Heading: I-T raids at outlets of Hot Millions - Indian Express
Content:
Out of their village for the first time, students from Kargil are enjoying the diversity in the city

The roads, the cars, the people, the language... there's nothing that fails to amaze these 25 students from Kargil. Out of their village for the very first time on a holiday, they are a thrilled lot. "This is a whole new world for me," smiles Imtiaas Hussain, a fifth class student, as he gets off the boat at the Sukhna Lake and asks his guide if he could take it back home. The others meanwhile shuffle for their chance for a ride. "We have already been on the Hop On bus and to the Rock Garden, the War Memorial and the Museum," says friend Mohammad, as he gives a low-down on the 14-day trip. "We spent 12 days in Himachal and two here."

This, being the first of its kind trip for them. "From hearing stories about fights and bombs in Kargil to success stories of people and about various job opportunities here, it's quite a drastic change," admits Mohammad Saudika, whose dream have seen a drastic change after the visit. "I wanted be become a driver but now I want to own a car and become a businessman," he says. Organized as a part of the Sadbhavana Project, "This is the second lot of children that we have got to Chandigarh," Major Pushkar Raj tells us that cultural diversity and hospitality of the Chandigarh Tourism Department brings them back here.

Heading: Up, Up & Away! - Indian Express
Content:
Anita Jain gets candid about the husband hunt and about her memoir Marrying Anita

Several failed attempts at finding a suitable boy to marry led journalist Anita Jain to write Marrying Anita (Penguin, Rs 450)— a completely honest and reflective memoir that's already raised eyebrows in book circles around the world.

Sitting at Oxford Bookstore, Jain sips her cold coffee and pointedly tells me that the book is definitely not chick-lit. "Principally, it is a memoir. Every second book in the West is a memoir but nobody in India writes memoirs unless they're public figures," states Jain, 35, who embarked on a "grand experiment to merge the memoir with the travelogue". The experiment has been successful, reviews in the West have been favourable but things might be different in India, Jain feels. "People here are uncomfortable with talking or writing about loneliness. While the West is interested in the whole phenomenon of Arranged Marriage, here the focus of the book has been my honesty," she says.

Jain began writing about her own dating-courtship experiences when she figured out that the New York City romance scene had failed her completely, and after much thought, she boarded a plane for New Delhi giving herself a year to find a husband. As her search for the 'One' became tougher than ever before, Jain found that she was succumbing to the shaadi.com route and even then, things weren't working out.

"Men are basically the same everywhere," states Jain a tad philosophically. "There's as much sexual freedom here as there is abroad," adds Jain.

In 2005, when she came to the capital, the landscape had changed completely to malls, call centre glass offices, new clubs, pubs and jobs. Jain found herself meeting an entirely different community of people who made up the New India. "Nobody talks about the people who've made a journey from the interiors of India to come and work in Delhi. They're in the fringes, ignored and underestimated by the South Delhi social circles. But they're the ones who're responsible for the increase in the GDP every year," says Jain who has consciously given them a voice in her memoir. The book delves into the inter-play of Old and New India and contains a sharp critique of the rigid class structure in North India, while Jain shifts from one situation to another in her never-ending search for a husband.

Jain refuses to comment on her current relationship status. She's not writing another book in a hurry but she is definitely staying back in the country. "This is an exciting time to be India, so much is happening. There are no set rules for anything and it's a great place to find something wonderful to do," says Jain who would like to move to Mumbai soon and try her hand at film production. There, maybe she will get lucky finding that very elusive husband.

Heading: Scratchin’ the surface - Indian Express
Content:
When it comes to parasailing, be prepared to be swept off your feet

Weightless. If you ask me what parasailing is, then it's this amazing feeling of weightlessness, and like they say in books - swept off your feet! Also known as parascending, this aero adventure sport is amongst the safest adventure sport and can also be called as gateway to aero sports. The sheer joy of soaring in the sky, hundreds of feet above without much training, has made this recreational event immensely popular.

The Beginning
Parasailing as a sport began in the 60's when Piere Lamogine attached a parachute to a car. A cheaper way to teach parachuters, they would raise the person to a certain height and then release. This was called Parascending. In the mid 60's, Pioneer Parachute Company started making parachutes under protected name 'Parasail'. Today we know it as a parachute attached to moving transportation medium like a motorboat. The jeep pulls para sailor along with the parasail mechanically. The canopy gets inflated and on further pulling by the transport medium the parachute is made ready to go up in the air and the person attached with it takes three or four quick steps and then jumps up in the air and starts ascending like a glider to an approximate height of 300 feet.

Methods of Parasailing
There are three methods currently being offered around the world. Winchboat Parasailing, Beach Parasailing and Platform Palasailing of which Winchboat is the most popular.
Winchboat Parasailing: Here, the launch and recovery of the parasailor and parachute takes place directly from the boat itself. The boat is equipped with a parasail inflation system and hydraulic winch powered by the main drive engine to launch and retrieve the parasailor from the flight deck, usually located in the rear of the boat.
Beach Parasailing: This sport along an exotic beach may seem fun, but it can also be extremely hazardous, and not approved for even the most experienced parasailors.
Platform Parasailing: Platform parasailing is not as dangerous as beach parasailing but if you intend to use this method, never fly in winds under five or above 15 mph, in rough oceans, poor weather and certainly away from buildings and other objects in close proximity.

The Requirements
A boat of at least 90HP, a parasail canopy, a body harness and a towline are all that you require to start off. A wind speed ranging from 12 mph to 27 mph is recommended. The take off and flight area must be clear of any obstructions, such as trees, ropes and power lines. A skilled driver and observer, a two man ground crew, favourable winds and you're off.
A variety of parasails are available in the market ranging from 24 feet high parasails to 42 feet high. Parasails come in varying capacities, some are for single flyers, others for a two or even threesome. Yet other parasails can be fitted with a sky chair to afford the riders a luxurious view.

In India
Training programs in parasailing are available for tourist in the Doon valley. Apart from Billing in Himachal, the thrill of this parasailing can also be enjoyed on Nilgiri hills in the South India, the Eastern Himalayas in the Darjeeling/Gangtok area, Auli in Uttranchal, and Sansar in Jammu & Kashmir.
Himachal Tourism sponsors training programs and events at various times of the year, in different places. There is an Adventure Sports Hostel at Dharamsala (Kangra) and an Aero Sports Complex at Bir who facilitates parasailing. In Mumbai, Marine Drive Chaupaty is a famous spot.
It is also popular in Rishikesh area. The sport of parasailing is also pursued in Goa, Trivandrum, Orissa, Haryana, the Northeastern states, especially Manipur, and many other places in India.

Safety Tips
* Make sure you parasail with a fully licensed company operating from a well-established location, insured by a licensed insurance company.
* Untrained parasailors should avoid this activity in winds that exceed 15 knots due to difficulties and a complication arises during emergency water landings.
* Never take up parasailing activity in rain, fog or an approaching storm.
* Never fly over 600 feet. This is a maximum recommended altitude for using hand signals and recovery during water landings over open oceans and 300 feet over small lakes or bays.
* Avoid parasailing in close proximately to the shoreline, other boats and objects
* Educate yourself on the different types of parasail equipment, passenger support devices.

The writer owns adventure club, www.clubfootloose.com, and is a city based gemmologist. Mail soli@clubfootloose.com

Heading: Man attempts to set wife ablaze, booked - Indian Express
Content:
DJ Wicked likes to give the turntables a little twist of his own

If we go into the details of when and why, then DJ Wicked would stand attention in the ranks of veterans. "When I started there weren't any CD players or turntables and amazing consoles...there was a cassette and tape recorder," Vicky Arora rewinds to the early nineties, the time of hip hop and psychedelia. "I had cousins bringing in UK-US Top of the charts from abroad and we used to mix them on the this basic cassette player...those were the days," he tells us. Music was of course a huge factor in joining the ranks, the biggest kick was girls. "That's right. I still remember how they went crazy over Akbar Sami's concert in Delhi. I knew instantly that this is what I want to do." He was 19, and he was re-christened DJ Wicked. "Because people think I'm wicked," he twists the turntables to his own and is already out with his debut album, 'Energy Electro & Minimal House'. "House, hip hop, retro, Bollywood, Punjabi pop - give me anything and I'll make the floor dance," DJ Wicked is also member of Buzz Funk, a dhol fusion band which also has inspiration and mentor Sumit Sethi and rapper Paras Sunda. "Dhol is the backbone of music. You check out any group, and they'll have the quintessential beat in their music." Akon, 50 Cents, Nelly Furtado...the Punjabi mix has not eluded any of them. That's true, but aren't these just remixes, where's the originality? "I know there's this whole debate about DJs not being original, that they just lift and play. But that's not true. There was a time when DJs were not considered artists, but now, they are respected as composers, arrangers, producers and musicians. It's because technology has changed, the clubbing scene has changed and we've started experimenting. Picking a song or a tune and adding beats to it is basic. Picking a track and changing the entire mood, the melody and rhythm is what we call composing, and DJs are doing that," Wicked defends his clan and adds why aren't singers who copy songs attacked? "When I change a track, it becomes my composition, I've worked on it so that it sounds different and suits the ambience I'm working in."

All set to release his second album, which will have five original and five remixes, Wicked says he'd rather concentrate on work and stay away from the 'War of the DJs'. "There's no competition for me," he plays on.

Heading: Bull’s ‘murder’ stirs up a hornet’s nest - Indian Express
Content:
A 26-year-old woman and her three-year-old son were admitted in General Hospital, Sector 6, Panchkula, with burns following a minor altercation with her husband on Wednesday morning.

Anjali's husband, Ravinder Kumar, was reportedly inebriated.

A resident of Sector 7, Anjali said: "Last night, Ravinder returned home drunk. In the morning, he started abusing me and made a big fuss over the meal I had cooked. In a fit of anger, he threw the burning stove towards me. He fled when he realised that the sofa had caught fire and the blaze had engulfed the entire room. Then, I cried for help and the neighbours came to my rescue."

Her two sons — Madhur and two-year-old Kartik — were also present at the spot.

A case of attempt to murder under Section 307 of the IPC has been registered against Ravinder.

Inspector Ajaib Singh of Sector 5 police station told Newsline: "Ravinder too received some burns in the process and has been admitted to GMCH, Sector 16, Chandigarh. He will be arrested soon."

Anjali is a caretaker at a play school in Sector 7.

Ravinder, earlier employed as a trainer at a local gym, is currently unemployed.

Heading: The tale of an ‘invisible’ book depot, starring Setia - Indian Express
Content:
The death of a stray bull sparked off a massive public protest near Sector 69, Mohali, on Wednesday evening. Alleging that the animal was beaten mercilessly and strangled to death by the Municipal Council (MC) enforcement staff, the residents of Lambian village resorted to blocking traffic on the road leading from Sector 69-70 lightpoint to Kumbra light point. Later, they gheraoed the MC Bhawan in Sector 68.

Around 4 pm today, the MC staff saw a bull near the bus stand in Phase VIII. "They put a rope around the animal's neck and then tightened the noose. Then the bull was brutally beaten with iron rods, leading to its death," said a protestor. When a crowd gathered, the MC staffers fled leaving behind the dead bull as well as the MC animal-rescue vehicle. Senior police officers reached the spot at 5.30 pm and assured that necessary action would be taken against the guilty.

MC staff, protestors booked
The police have booked the MC staff as well as the protesters on the basis of the counter complaints filed against each other. "While the MC officials have been charged with the animal's murder under Section 429 of the IPC, the residents of Lambian village have been booked under Sections 332 and 353 of the IPC for assault and obstructing officials from discharging their duty," said Station House Officer, Phase VIII, Navneet Kumar.
However, no one has been arrested yet.
The bull's carcass has been preserved and an autopsy will be conducted on Thursday to ascertain the cause of death, added the SHO.

'Gross violation' of Act
As the news spread, activists of various social, religious and animal rights organisations also joined the protest. The Chandigarh Chapter of People for Animals (PFA) condemned the "inhumane" act and sought the immediate arrest of those involved under Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960.
"The incident is a gross violation of the act which bans capture by the sack-and-loop method. It clearly states that animals have to be captured with the help of tranquiliser guns or by any other method, which renders the animal insensitive to pain," said PFA founder trustee Payal Sodhi. "If the authorities do not take proper action, we will launch a mass agitation and will not rest till the administration acts according to the rules," she added.

MC employees angry
Late in the evening, MC employees Ranjit Singh and Piara Singh were admitted to the Mohali Civil Hospital with injuries. Up in arms against the protest, the MC Employees' Union announced an indefinite strike and dharna outside the MC Bhawan. Irked MC employees also met Deputy Commissioner Rahul Bhandari to press him for fulfilling their demand.
"They are demanding that the attackers be arrested and action be taken against the MC president and local MLA who incited the mob," said municipal councillor Harman Preet Singh Prince.
MC president Rajinder Singh Rana and MLA Balbir Sidhu, however, denied the allegations.

Heading: Life in Patiala comes to a halt as rain clogs roads - Indian Express
Content:
Yet another proposal of the UT Education Department has apparently failed to see the light of day.

A year ago, the department had decided to open its own book depot to facilitate the direct purchase of National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) books by students. The proposal was to be enforced in the current academic session.

Now, even though District Public Instruction (Schools) S K Setia says such a depot has been opened, none except him seem to be aware of the fact.

Anujit Kaur, Principal of Government Model Senior Secondary School (Girls), Sector 18, said: "We have purchased our books from the main depot in Sector 18 but I am not aware whether the department is operating one for the students as well."

Agrees Kusum Gupta, Principal of Government Model Senior Secondary School, Sector 20, said: "All the prescribed books are available at the Sector 18 bookshop and we buy our stock from there only."

Earlier local booksellers used to get the supply of books from NCERT but according to this proposal, the department was to keep its own stock.

The department had asked the NCERT for the copyright to print its own books but it was denied.

Setia, apparently tired of Newsline highlighting his follies, said: "Yes, we have opened a depot but I do not wish to talk about it to this newspaper."

Heading: Pbi varsity sets up film, TV studio - Indian Express
Content:
A two-hour shower affected daily life in the city after most of the localities were heavily flooded.

Unfortunately, the Chief Minister, who was in the city till afternoon, missed the downpour and was not privy to the pathetic condition of the roads.

Angry residents complained about the sewer water entering their houses, and expressed their irritation at the government turning a blind eye to the state of the civic amenities.

Heavy water also accumulated in Anardana Chowk, Jattan Walka Chauntra, Chotti Baradari, Lehal colony, Sewak colony and Ragho Majra.

"When the CM was in the city, it was not raining, so he did not see the result. The municipal corporation claims they want to develop Patiala into a modern hub, but the situation in the city is alarming," said a resident of Lehal Colony.

On a more positive note, the rains brought some respite from the high temperatures, which had been bothering the city residents.

"The resulting cool weather will save us from the heat brought on by power cuts and the humid weather," said Anil Jain, a resident of Sunami Gate.

The MC officials claimed that due to the pathetic drainage system, water collects in lower areas and the problem would be solved once the draining facility is improved.

Heading: Uprooted trees play havoc at NH-72 - Indian Express
Content:
Responding to the demands of the film and television industry for more professionals, the Punjabi University's Department of Journalism and Mass Communication received its new TV and Film Studio on Wednesday.

The acoustic soundproof studio and the state-of-the-art equipment, as well as a production control room (PCR) worth approximately Rs 25 lakhs, was inaugurated today by Vice Chancellor Jaspal Singh.

The V-C also announced a grant of Rs 5 lakh for further upgradation so that students are taught every aspect of professional training.

The students of PG Diploma in the Audio-Visual Production course will use the grant to make about 40 ad-films and documentaries.

The V-C also said that a media centre would also be created in the department.

"Our major objective is to upgrade programmes and packages to cope with the quick upsurge in demands of the professionally trained candidates by the electronic media. The new environment will certainly enable our students to quickly adapt themselves to the professional ambience and facilitate their quicker absorption in various electronic media organisations," he added.

Gurmeet Maan, Head of the Department, said the studio will be used to produce talk-shows, panel discussions, interviews and quiz shows for radio and television.

Heading: Welcome to the playground of the Shivaliks - Indian Express
Content:
A head on road collision between an autorickshaw and a trailer near the Baharapur village bus stand (Naraingarh) on Wednesday claimed one life and left five seriously injured. This incident is part of a series of mishaps that have occurred on NH-72, reportedly due to negligence on part of the Forest department who have failed to remove an uprooted tree on the highway.

A motorcyclist had earlier lost his legs in an accident while the victims of another accident are still fighting for their lives in the hospital.

A third accident of similar nature took place near the Shehzadpur sugar mill.

According to Shehzadpur SHO Hardev Singh, the accident could have been averted if the Forest department personnel had removed the fallen tree from the road. The police squarely held the Forest department officials responsible for the accident. The NH-72, they pointed out, had become a mortuary of uprooted trees which were yet to be removed by the department.

Haryana Forest official Chander Mohan, when contacted, stated that the uprooted trees were being cleared from the roads. Though the local people had chopped off the small branches of the tree, the heavy girth remained lying on the road thereby blocking the traffic. The residents have demanded an inquiry into the matter and punishment to the defaulting forest officials.

Heading: MC notice has Mohali powerless, sleepless - Indian Express
Content:
The view is amazing...the beautiful Shivaliks in the distance, Sukhna alongside and the clean air. The Lake Sports Complex, set up in 1961, is an ideal place for sport buffs.

Earlier known as the Lake Club, the 10-acre clubhouse boasts of an impressive membership. "We have IAS officers from Haryana and Punjab coming here," says Reet Mohinder Singh, general manager of the complex.

But an interesting nugget of information — the clubhouse was designed by Le Corbusier. The idea to create a complex on the lake was a brainchild of A L Fletcher (the then Financial Commissioner Development, Punjab). "Corbusier designed the building in a way that it is invisible from the road and does not obstruct the view of the lake and the hills," says Singh adding that the original drawings by Corbusier are still with the complex.

Till 1966, the complex functioned under the aegis of Punjab Sports Department. After Chandigarh acquired the status of a Union Territory, the complex became part of the UT Education department. The complex was inherited by the Department of Sports after its inception in 1984. In 1997, the management and administration of the complex was transferred to the Chandigarh Sports Council.

At the time, the complex had just 500 members and offered rowing, canoeing, kayaking and sailing. "Today, we have about 800 members and the complex is one of the best in the region. We have the only glass squash court in the city. Our rowing training centre is also the best, recently made famous by Manjit Singh, the Olympian," smiles Singh.

The two-kilometre long rowing course was the venue of the 1989 Senior Asian Rowing Championship and the 1994 Junior Asian Rowing Championship. Many national-level tournaments have been organised here besides rowing, canoeing, kayaking and sailing events.

The main emphasis, he adds, is now on the multi-purpose hall with indoor facilities like a gymnasium, judo and wrestling rings, badminton, table tennis and volleyball courts.

Heading: Employees, local leaders hold dharna at Mohali DC office - Indian Express
Content:
Residents asked to remove generators from outside homes; daily powercut of up to 8 hours makes life tough

 

The 'powerless' residents of Mohali are in for more trouble. If the ongoing power crisis was not enough to throw normal life out of gear, the residents have been asked to remove generator sets from outside their homes.

In the wake of unscheduled powercuts stretching up to 8 hours daily, most of the residents were forced to use generators as an alternate source of power supply. It can be no longer be the solution as the Mohali Municipal Council (MC) has served notices to the residents whose generator sets were set up in the front or rear sides of their buildings.

With the MC notices asking them to immediately remove generator sets to avoid them being impounded, the aggrieved residents are up in ante.  "Where do we put our generators," asked a local resident while reasoning that they were forced to use generators after inverters failed to work due to long and routine powercuts. They argue that since the generators cannot be placed inside the buildings and multi-storey houses and shops, the only place to put them was in the front or rear of a building.

The civic body, however, is in no mood to reason. The MC Executive Officer, in the notices, has asked the residents to immediately remove their generators otherwise the MC enforcement staff will take them away and legal action be taken against the defaulters. Notices cite air and sound pollution as the reason behind the action. Besides, the MC also claims to have received several complaints from some residents in this regard.

The notices have met widespread resentment and anguish. Aarushi, a housewife in Phase 3B2 said: "With long and unscheduled power cuts becoming a norm, generators are the only alternate to survive. How can the MC be against this?  They should only suggest some alternative."

"We are not using the generators for fun. Besides extra investment on its purchase, we bear expensive costs to generate power," reasoned a Phase V shopkeeper, Sukhjeet Singh. A perturbed Phase IV resident, Neena Singh asked the MC to first ensure uninterrupted power supply before acting against the use of generators.

The power situation, meanwhile, is becoming grimmer with each passing day. Besides long powercuts all through the day, the most trying hours for the residents are midnight. "At least nights should be spared from powercuts so that one gets the luxury of an eight-hour sleep," said a Kharar resident, Neelam.

Mohali and Kharar areas are facing daily power cuts ranging between 6-8 hours besides frequent tripping and voltage fluctuation. At times, the voltage goes so low that even the tubelights and fans fail to run.

The Punjab State Electricity Board (PSEB) officials attribute the problem to orders of Power Controller in Patiala and shrug off the responsibility of giving advance powercut schedule while claiming that they receive daily or instant call to shut power supply.

Heading: Your car’s at risk: Motor theft up by 50 % - Indian Express
Content:
Employees of different government departments, panches and sarpanches from different parts of Mohali district on Wednesday staged a massive dharna outside the Deputy Commissioner's office.

Under the banner of the Joint Action Committee (JAC), the five different bodies of the Rural Development and Panchayats Department comprising panches, sarpanches, junior engineers, panchayat officers, secretaries and gram sewaks protested against the non-fulfillment of their long-pending demands.

Speaking to Newsline, JAC president Harminder Singh Mavi threatened that all the protesters will go on pen down strike across the state if the government failed to fulfill their demands.

Their demands include regularisation of 909 contractual panchayat secretaries, withdrawal of flying squads to check old works in the department, withdrawal of chargesheets filed against employees and sarpanches and implementation of 73rd amendment of the Constitution.

The JAC submitted a memorandum of its demands to the DC for forwarding it to Punjab Chief Minister for consideration.

Heading: ICICI Lombard directed to pay up Rs 1 lakh as punitive damages for denying claim - Indian Express
Content:
Cases of rioting, rape, human injury has declined in 2008

The property-related crime graph in the city has experienced an ascent over the last year.The number of motor vehicle thefts that tops the chart has witnessed a 50 per cent increase this year with 756 cases being reported this year.

The corresponding figure of motor vehicle thefts at this time last year was 505.

The figures were revealed by SSP S S Srivastava on Wednesday after a crime review meeting with the senior officers.

The recovery rate of motor vehicles remains poor as a mere 128 of the stolen vehicles have been recovered so far. The SSP, however, said the figure does not include the large number of vehicles that were found abandoned and thus the actual recovery rate would be much higher.

The city has also witnessed a huge increase in snatching and robbery cases. As compared to 121 cases reported at this time last year, nearly 152 cases have already been reported this year. The good news is, said the SSP, that 50 per cent of the snatching cases have been solved.

While 15 murder cases were reported till August 31 last year, this year has seen a total of 12 murders - two of which still remain unsolved.

While cases of human injury have declined from 51 last year to 47 this year, the riot cases have however increased.

From 38 till August last year, this year a total of 60 cases of rioting have been reported. The cases of rape have also declined from 23 in the corresponding month last year to 17 this year.

While the proposal to install CCTV cameras is yet to be implemented, the SSP said they have mooted a plan for sealing the periphery of some sectors during night hours and carrying out thorough searches to prevent the rising motor vehicle thefts.

The SSP urged for public cooperation at all levels to prevent the petty crimes.

Heading: More city women are falling prey to AIDS, says survey - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Forum has directed ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company to pay Rs 1 lakh as punitive damages after they submitted false evidence before the consumer forum to justify their repudiation.

While Rs 25,000 out of this goes to the complainant as compensation, Rs 75,000 will be deposited with the State Legal Services Authority. The forum has also asked the company to pay Rs 5,500 as costs of litigation and to settle the claim as demanded by the complainant.

While the company claimed to have paid Rs 25,204 on September 2, 2008, they are liable to pay the rest at an interest rate of 8 per cent per annum on the amount of Rs 41,204 from February 25, 2006 (the date of surveyor's report) till September, 2008. It has also been directed to pay interest on the same rate on the remaining amount from September 2008 till realisation.

The complainant, Nishchai Trehan, got his Ascent Viva Car insured with the ICICI Lombard General Insurance, which was valid from February 15, 2005 to February 14, 2006 against a premium of Rs 22,850.

The car met with an accident on January 17, 2006. The complainant claimed that he had spent Rs 41,409 for repairing the claim and submitted all relevant documents to company. But the company failed to settle the claim, following which he moved the forum.

ICICI Lombard, in its reply, stated that they have offered Rs 25,204 as assessed by the surveyor but the complainant refused to accept it.

They admitted that while issuing the insurance policy, the premium was paid through cheque drawn by the Syndicate Bank, Panchkula. But later, the cheque was not shown as cleared or paid in their records and therefore, the policy was cancelled.

The forum said the company has not produced the copy of their bank account to prove whether they received the amount from the bank.

"It is unbelievable that for more than a year the company was not aware that the cheque received as premium was not honoured and the amount was not credited to their account," said Jagroop Singh Mahal, President, District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum.

Heading: Fire engines to be equipped with GPS - Indian Express
Content:
The number of women suffering from AIDS in the city has experienced a constant rise over the last eight years. From a mere 18 women diagnosed with the illness in 1999, the figures rose to 245 in 2007.

The statistics computed will July this year has already listed 120 women detected with AIDS.

It is not only the absolute numbers that has risen, even the proportion of women in the total pool of AIDS patients has grown over three fold.

While in 1999, women comprised 13 per cent of the total 137 cases, the figures in 2007 rose to 34 per cent of the total cases. For the ongoing year, women comprise 37 per cent of the total cases.

With the grip of AIDS increasing by nearly 15 times since 1999, the authorities attribute the rising

detection cases to better diagnostic facilities available in the city.

"We have witnessed a huge jump in the number of detection among women patients coming for tests in Chandigarh. The reason could be that now all the pregnant women have to undergo a mandatory test when they come to the hospitals and a majority of the cases are generated from these cases," says Project Director of State AIDS Control Society (SACS), UT, Dr Vanita Gupta, while talking to the Newsline.

Pooja Thakur, the president of the Chandigarh Network of the People Living with the HIV/AIDS says that her "drop-in counseling" is now thronged with women, unlike the case a few years ago.

"Of the nearly 150 registered patients who come for regular counselling, more than 80 are women alone. The number of new cases among women has risen tremendously in the last few years. The women come out of the closet and get themselves tested either after the death of their infected husbands or at the time of pregnancy," says Thakur.

Of the 80 women who are a part of the Network in Chandigarh, nearly 30 are widows who have lost their husbands to the same disease.

"As compared to men, women still lack awareness and access to fight the infection. We counsel several sex workers who are aware of their high-risk behaviour but do little to save themselves from the infection. If it is not for the mandatory testing at the time of pregnancy, majority of the cases among women would not surface even today," adds Thakur.

Heading: PGI doctor’s book on gastro infections a big draw even in global market - Indian Express
Content:
Training programme for building, pump, cinema hall owners soon

The fire brigades in the city would soon be equipped with the Global Positioning System (GPS). The decision was taken during a meeting of the Fire and Emergency Committee of the Municipal Corporation held under the chairmanship of councillor MPS Chawla.

The committee also decided to seal those buildings that have been served notices for violating fire safety norms if requisite changes were not made.

The members also sought to have training and awareness programmes to impart fire safety training through some specialised agency to the owners of buildings, petrol pumps, gas agencies, hotels and cinema halls.

They will be trained to use the installed fire fighting equipment. As many as five thermal imaging cameras would be purchased to meet any exigency caused by fire.

The committee has also decided to conduct a survey of rehri markets to assess its fire safety after reports of encroachments on the external walls of the shops in various rehri markets came up.

The committee has also approved a study tour of the members of the Fire and Emergency services committee and Fire Officers to Ahmedabad, Mumbai and Delhi where the fire offices are well-equipped with modern fire fighting equipments.

Heading: Industrial Area devoid of basic civic amenities - Indian Express
Content:
Dr Chetana Vaishnavi, Additional Professor, Department of Gastroenterology, PGIMER, has edited and produced a book on Gastrointestinal Tract Infections, that was showcased today at the PGI.

The book has been recently released by Professor B N Tandon, a leading figure in the field of gastroenterology, on the occasion of the international congress of the Asia Pacific Digestive Week at New Delhi.

"The demand for the book was instantaneous, both from the Indian and the international community. This book is the first of its kind in the country. Globally, only a couple of books on this subject could be traced," said Dr Vaishnavi. According to the doctor, gastrointestinal tract infections constitute a large and important proportion of clinical practice and medical science has made great strides in mitigating the sufferings of humanity.

"With the advancement in the field of GI infections comprising of bacterial, viral, parasitic and fungal organisms, it was very important to produce a book that covers all aspects of these infections. Undertaking the production of this book was an incredible challenge. The most daunting tasks were to provide the readers with comprehensive materials," added the doctor.

The highlight of the book is the fact that epidemiology, clinical manifestations, diagnosis and treatment have been discussed in detail with emphasis on the basic aspects as well as clinical and evidence based medicine.

Participation of experts in the field from all over the country has been included. Prominent among these are Professor M P Sharma, Professor P Kar, Professor A K Jain, Professor Atul Sachdev, Professor V Balakrishnan, Professor Ajay Wanchu, Dr Pallab Ray and Dr Mamatha Ballal.

Heading: PU grants ‘special chance’ to students to clear exams - Indian Express
Content:
Industrial Area — the business hub of the city — lacks basic civic amenities and speaks loudly of the poor management by the Municipal Corporation authorities.

No parking space, pathetic condition of roads, poor drainage system, non-maintenance of parks and non-functional streetlights — the list is endless.

The traders complain about the pathetic condition of roads, especially after the rains which gave way to deep potholes. The poorly-lit roads only compound the problem.

Jarnail Singh, chairman of Chandigarh Industries and Traders Federation, blames the unclear policies of the UT Administration for various problems. "The Administration is unclear about its conversion policy. They keep modifying it time and again. Consequently, there is no clarity," he says.

The members had earlier raised other demands including building of a community centre in the area to hold meetings and functions. They had alleged that the transfer policy of the Administration is not clear with regards to allottees and GPA holders among others.

Many traders say the small units have an important role to play in the development of the city for they provide employment to a large number of people. But these units are largely feeling neglected with the Administration freely giving sops to the upcoming malls in the area. The coming of new malls has also worsened the lack of parking space.

Councillor M P S Chawla says during a meeting of the representatives of various organisations with Finance-cum-Home Secretary Sanjay Kumar, they were assured the facilities would be upgraded.

Eyebrows were also raised after the Municipal Corporation started re-carpetting roads.

The issue was debated in the House Meet also where questions were raised if the MC should spend funds on development of the Industrial Area since the Administration has not released any money for the same.

Heading: Senate polls: Ojha, Tiwari win from professor constituency - Indian Express
Content:
At the culmination of the diamond jubilee celebrations, the Panjab University has granted one "special chance" to students to clear or reappear for their compartment exams in all the courses. The candidates can avail of this chance in September 2008 or April and September 2009.

Even those students who have missed a paper due to medical or service exigencies in April 2008 examinations will be given a chance.

Those who have already submitted their examination forms for the supplementary examinations (September 2008) but were declared ineligible, will have to pay the balance fee and also submit their original DMCs by September 23 (5 pm).

It is incumbent upon such candidates to collect their PUPIN/Roll Numbers personally from the Panjab University Administrative Office during working hours on September 23.

In case of the candidates, whose applications have been rejected due to one reason or the other but are, otherwise, eligible under the special chance category can submit their examination forms with the requisite fee by September 23 (5.00 p.m.) if they wish to appear in the September 2008 exams.

Candidates who wish to appear in April 2009 or September 2008 examinations under this special chance would have to submit the fresh examination forms as per the University schedule applicable then.

One special chance for improvement in performance, admission in the concerned examinations, will also be given in April or May 2009. Students can visit the website link www.puchd.ac.in/news/special chance1.pdf for detailed information on the subject.

Heading: PU, PGI sign agreement for research programme - Indian Express
Content:
The results for the Professors' Constituency in the Senate elections, held on September 15, were declared on Wednesday. The results revealed the names of two professors — Prof N K Ohja from the Arts faculty and Prof Rupinder Tiwari from the Science faculty — who have secured their seats in the Senate.

While Prof N K Ohja defeated Prof V K Mahajan by securing 68 votes followed, Prof Rupinder Tiwari from the Science faculty won against Prof A S Ahluwalia and K P Singh by securing 72 votes.

The winners have secured a seat for themselves in the Senate for the coming four years. Talking to Newsline, Prof Ohja said, "I was always certain of my victory. I will work for the upliftment the teachers and students and promise my complete support to both."

Expressing joy and surprise on his victory, Prof Tiwari said that the results came as a pleasant surprise. While speaking to Newsline, he said, "The results have shown that people still vote for individuals and not for any party. I do not belong to any party and shall put in all my efforts to do the best for both teachers and students."

Heading: Centre is killing Punjab farming: CM - Indian Express
Content:
An Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between PGIMER and Panjab University was signed on Wednesday allowing Phd research students of the university to enroll or register at PGI and vice versa.

The Chief Supervisor for this project would be appointed from the parent University Teaching Department that is from Panjab University and the Co-Supervisor/Supervisor from the PGI.

Students will not be supervised by their own professors but by those from the corresponding varsity.

A candidate from PGI will be supervised by a professor from Pnjab University and vice versa.

The rules and regulations of the concerned Institute would be applicable on the candidate wherever he/she is enrolled/registered.

The MoU was signed by Dr. KK Talwar, Director, PGIMER on behalf of PGIMER and Prof R C Sobti, Vice-Chancellor, on behalf of the Panjab University.

Heading: SAD members walk out of Amritsar MC House in protest - Indian Express
Content:
Lays foundation stone of air-conditioned Veg Market, seeks Rs 100 crore for PAU

While laying the foundation stone of a modern air-conditioned vegetable market here today, Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal charged the Centre with killing Punjab farming through 'slow poisoning'.

Addressing a gathering at the Grain Market, Badal claimed the Centre was not giving Punjab its due, as all its schemes were aimed at harming the farmers and farming in Punjab.

The chief minister said that even though Punjab filled the nation's food basket, the Centre did not recognise the contribution made by the farmers of the state, and instead meted out a step-motherly treatment towards the state.

The CM urged the farmers to adopt modern techniques for increasing their produce, especially for growing off-season crops. He also called for introducing modern techniques for proper marketing of fruits and vegetables.

Badal said the new mandi will cover 16.5 acres. It will be constructed at a cost of Rs 23 crore, and will be completed in 15 months' time. The CM said that the mandi will have vegetable grading facilities, and also cold storages for preserving fruits and vegetables. He added that new scientific ways of ripening fruits will also be made available here.

Badal called upon Agriculture Minister Sucha Singh Langah to create green houses within the mandi.

Badal urged the Centre to release a grant of Rs 100 crore for Punjab Agricultural University. He said the grant had been promised by the Prime Minister, and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram had announced it in his budget.

Heading: 17 corporates give assent - Indian Express
Content:
The members of Shiromani Akali Dal (Badal) including Senior Deputy Mayor Ajaybir Pal Singh Randhawa and Deputy Mayor Kashmir Singh today staged a walk out during a meeting of the Finance Committee of the Amritsar Municipal Corporation.

The SAD members were protesting the allotment of a solid waste management project to a private company. Randhawa and Kashmir Singh alleged that SAD (B) was not consulted before giving work to private builders. The duo have warned of approaching the party's senior leaders and BJP Lok Sabha MP Navjot Singh Sidhu too.

Randhawa stated that there were two options before the Municipal Corporation. One was to buy the machinery themselves, which he claimed would have been less costly. Randhawa said the other option was to let the firm, to whom the work is allotted, buy the machinery, which was likely to cost more.

The Senior Deputy Mayor added that SAD (B) was not consulted in this regard, and the work was given to a Mumbai-based company. "We will not allow the Mayor to waste public money, and will ensure that every penny is spent judiciously," he said.

When contacted, Mayor Shawet Malik said MC was committed to providing the best facilities to the city residents. He denied charges of ignoring the SAD (B) members in taking the decision. Malik added that all decisions would be in the interest of the public.

Heading: Amritsar land scam: VB grills accountant of builder - Indian Express
Content:
After a slow start, Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal's pet project of Adarsh Schools in Punjab has taken a leap forward. The state government has received final confirmations from 17 corporate players who are willing to pitch in for the project. At least eight others also evinced interest at a board meeting held in New Delhi recently, said sources.

The corporate list for the project, which will function on the private-public partnership model, is also getting bigger. Official sources said construction major Ansals, DLF and Emaar MGF too were likely to participate in setting up of the schools.

The government has also set in motion the process of transferring land for schools from panchayats. An official said, "The process will be completed in the next about two weeks. The laying of foundation stones for all the 17 schools is planned in October."

A Delhi-based private architecture firm has been engaged to suggest a uniform design for schools, each of which would be spread over 10 to 15 acres. Three designs have been shortlisted, sources said.

At present, Rakesh Mittal's Bharti Group leads the list with confirmation for at least six schools and another five expected for the next phase, while Ranbaxy has given consent for five.

Career Launchers will set up two schools, Khalsa Diwan Society three and Educom one.

Rajya Sabha MP Naresh Gujral told The Indian Express that Trident, Oswal and some other companies have also shown keenness. "The board has decided to run the project on first-come-first-serve basis. Our target is 108 schools," Gujral said.

Earlier, the response to advertisement for the project was not encouraging, and the last date for submission of requests had to be extended.

At present, about eight schools are being run by the Punjab School Education Board.

The idea is to have quality schools for the poor students in rural areas.

On the 14-member board of the Adarsh Schools are corporate heads, including Sunil Munjal of Hero Honda, Arun Kapoor, Director of India Today Education Trust, Harpal Singh, Chairman of Ranbaxy, Rakesh Mittal, Joint Managing Director of Bharti Group, and Vice-Chancellor of Punjabi University Jaspal Singh. Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal heads the board.

Heading: No solution to mealy bug, new Bt cotton variety next year - Indian Express
Content:
The Vigilance Bureau (VB) sleuths today questioned a Chartered Accountant of Veer Enclave in the Amritsar land scam in which the House panel had indicted and later expelled former chief minister Captain Amarinder Singh.

Jatinder Arora was questioned by a team led by SP Chaman Lal Sharma at the office of the private builder. Sources said the VB also acquired some of the records from Arora.

The role of the officials of the Amritsar Improvement Trust involved in the grant of approval for exemption of the 32 acres too has come under the scanner and they would also be questioned.

Sources said the officials, including PA of the former chairman of the Trust and a few others, slipped away when the VB team from Chandigarh visited the office to scan the records.

Meanwhile, there were reports that the sleuths found the records tampered with, as some of the items, including the exemption of 32 acres, were included after a meeting of the Trust, in which 21 items were passed by the trustees.

Sharma said, "We have questioned Arora, but can comment only after examining the records."

Heading: Anticipatory bail granted to Moga MLA, others - Indian Express
Content:
Certain reports have raised doubts over biotech crops, but they are as safe as conventional ones and the success of Bt cotton can be replicated in other crops. This was stated by the All-India Biotechnology Association at a press conference here today.

Representing the interests of 13 leading corporate houses in agriculture biotechnology, including multinationals like Monsanto, the association, while allaying fears about the safety of Bt crops, said the industry was aware of the mealy bug problem and scientists were working to find a solution. "The field trials of the new Bt cotton seed variety have been successful and will be introduced for commercial use next year. Unlike the prevailing varieties, which have to be replaced every year as they lose effectiveness due to segregation of gene traits that affects the yield, this variety has to be replaced only after three to four years and will be within the reach of even small farmers," association director Sanjiv Anand said. And the Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI) was by its side to substantiate the claims on safety of biotech crops, he said.

Dr KC Bansal, a scientist with IARI, said introduction of Bt cotton has decreased the usage of insecticides by up to 50 per cent, increased yield and farmers' incomes, besides, it has the potential of withstanding climatic changes and water scarcity, thereby decreasing dependence on monsoon. "It is also resistant to viral disease, has a longer shelf life and is able to withstand salt stress. Most importantly, it is introduced only after undergoing stringent tests on safety, nutrition and productivity," he added.

He said the introduction of Bt cotton has made the country the second largest producer and third largest exporter of cotton. Bt brinjal would be introduced next year, while biotech varieties of okra, cabbage, cauliflower, chickpea, rice and pigeon pea were also in the pipeline, he added.

Heading: BSF adds sheen to Retreat Ceremony at Attari border - Indian Express
Content:
Justice Arvind Kumar of Punjab and Haryana High Court has granted anticipatory bail to Moga Congress MLA Joginder Pal Jain, Harnek Singh, former sarpanch of Ramoonwala, and eight others.

Earlier, the anticipatory bail plea of these persons was rejected by Moga Additional Sessions Judge Amarjot Bhatti. The case was registered against these persons by Mehna police, on the complaint of Guriqbal Singh of Ramoonwala.

Guriqbal had stated that on the day of the Gram Panchayat poll on May 26, these persons had fired on him near the polling station. Guriqbal had stated that these persons were carrying fire arms and lethal weapons, and created terror among the electorate. Guriqbal said that he had received bullet injuries too.

The accused MLA and others pleaded that registration of cases against them were politically motivated. In this regard, the court has issued notice to Punjab government for November 10.

Heading: Rahul Gandhi to visit Punjab - Indian Express
Content:
The soft tones that had become normal at the Retreat Ceremony at the Attari border have once again become high-pitched, with the BSF once again resorting to shrill gestures for the show.

With this, the BSF soldiers have again perked up the ritual for visitors to the border, who have hailed the reversion. The aggressive display of strength is being attributed to the unwillingness on the part of the Pak Rangers to tone down their drill. Hence the corrosive stares and gestures are back again.

This is much to the delight of the spectators, who had been missing the excitement. Spectators prefer some punch in the drill, which had been mellowed in 2007 by BSF IG Arvind Ranjan. At that time, the aggressive shaking of head arms, and violent clicking of heels, had been replaced with softer gestures and tones.

Rajwinder Singh, a visitor, said that again, the visitors can look forward to some excitement in the drill. BSF officials stated that the exercise at other borders too had been mellowed down by the Indian contingents, but the Pak Rangers remained persistent in the display of aggression.

DIG Border Security Force Mohammed Acquil said that the change had been made a month ago, seeing the unwillingness of the Pak Rangers to relent.

Heading: Paddy arrives in mandis - Indian Express
Content:
General Secretary of All India Congress Committee (AICC) Rahul Gandhi will begin his three-day visit to the state from September 22. This was stated by president Youth Congress Ashok Tanwar here today, while talking to mediapersons.

Tanwar said Rahul Gandhi will address a youth rally in Bhatinda on September 23, a Scheduled Caste Convention in Jalandhar, and a convention for girls in Gurdaspur.

Rahul will start his visit from Mohali. He will visit Ropar, Fatehgarh Sahib, Patiala, Sangrur and Mansa districts on the first day. On the second day, he will address a youth rally at Bathinda in the morning, before visiting the Muktsar, Faridkot, Ferozepur, Tarn Taran, Amritsar and Gurdaspur districts,

Tanwar said.

Heading: Fresh bids for CFL bulbs invited - Indian Express
Content:
The early-maturing variety of paddy has started pouring in the mandis. Phillaur grain market today received 27 tonnes of paddy, while Jalandhar got almost its double.

Due to good rains throughout the season, the crop matured at the right time. The farmers are getting Rs 880 per quintal even for the common variety, which is a little more than the maximum support price (MSP).

Nirmaljit Singh, a farmer from Kadian village, said, "The early-maturing variety can be harvested in 60 to 70 days. I am very happy that I am getting a good price even for the common variety." District Food and Supply Officer Dr Rajat Oberoi said though the arrival was slow, the quality of grain was good due to which farmers were getting a good price. He added that notwithstanding the floods this year, they were expecting a bumper crop.

Heading: Waste management campaign in public domain - Indian Express
Content:
According to HPSEB, only 0.85 PF CFL bulbs will be purchased

Clearing the controversy around the order for purchase of 72 lakh Compact Fluorescent (CFL) bulbs under Atal Bijli Bachat Yojana —-an energy saving scheme, Himachal Pradesh State Electricity Board (HPSEB) has decided to invite fresh bids.

HPSEB today also made it clear that only 0.85 Power Factor (PF) CFL bulbs will be purchased for distribution under the scheme, resulting in a set back for the manufacturers of 0.05 PF bulbs. A circular from the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) said only 0.85 PF CFL bulbs will allowed to be sold in the markets.

Companies claiming to supply 0.05 PF bulbs at a lower cost will be required to file their bids for 0.85 PF bulbs only.

The supply orders for purchase of 0.85 PF CFL bulbs were earlier placed with four leading CFL manufacturers. The orders, however, were put on hold following complaints of the rival firm, which offered to supply 0.05 PF bulbs at much lower price.

After last evening's decision of the HPSEB to go for fresh tenders, the orders finally stand cancelled.

The HPSEB Chairman R.K.Jain, who took over the charge few days back, has posted Vijay Kaprate, Chief Engineer (commercial) in place of Surya Kant, HPSEB's Chief Engineer (marketing management).

Kant was one of the officials associated with the tendering process during the tenure of the previous chairman Ajay Mittal. Kant has been posted as Chief Engineer (system planning) .

Chief Secretary Asha Swaroop who had asked the HPSEB's chairman to get the CFL bulb issue examined afresh has favoured cancellation of the earlier bids.

A meeting of the full-time board members has already been convened for tomorrow to pass final orders on scrapping of the supply orders. Advertisements, inviting fresh bids have already appeared in the leading newspapers.

The last date for the receipt of tenders is September 29 and a decision on fresh orders is expected next month. Under the scheme all 16.5 lakh domestic consumers in Himachal Pradesh will be provided four CFL bulbs free of cost.

Heading: Snapped cables disrupt broadband connectivity - Indian Express
Content:
Taking the anti-dumping and garbage management campaign in Shimla to the public domain, the government today involved Municipal Councillors and the Mayor of Shimla Municipal Corporation to tackle the problem at local level.

In a first of its kind meeting organised by the Department of Environment, Science and Technology, senior government officials discussed the environmental issues of garbage and muck management.

During the meeting, Forest and Environment Minister J.P. Nadda, emphasised the need for having micro-level plans for solid waste management in Shimla. "Segregation of waste should be done at the source to carry out solid waste management in a more scientific, professional and eco-friendly manner," said Nadda as he stressed the need for introspection and social audit by everyone to see whether they were disposing the waste in a scientific manner.

He directed the staff for regular field inspections by the departments to ensure cleanliness in the town.

Officials of Pollution Control Board highlighted the prevailing situation in Shimla and 37 spots were identified with alarming environmental degradation. Flaws in current garbage management practices followed by MC Shimla were also pointed out.

While the councillors appreciated the idea of their involvement in the process, the issue of shortage of manpower and funds was also raised. Mayor Narender Kataria said earlier 1,000 employees worked for a population of 50,000, today the population in Shimla has increased to about 2.5 lakh but the manpower has gone down.

Heading: Baddi belt master plan to be highlight of LS elections - Indian Express
Content:
Frequent digging up of Kalka-Shimla highway for repair work and widening has been leading to snapping-off of the optical-fibre cable, disrupting the broadband connectivity in the state.

The subscribers have been facing the problem of unstable network for the past four months. The BSNL Himachal has linked with a standby network in Dehradun to maintain the connection even if the link is cut off from the main server at Chandigarh.

Despite repeated communiques sent by BSNL to National Highway Authority of India (NHAI) and PWD departments, the problem continues as the work of digging is allotted to contractors without giving any notice to the BSNL about the potential damage involved in the process.

"If we are informed before hand our technical staff can be present on the spot to repair the damage immediately and the link with Chandigarh server can be restored immediately," said Chief General Manager Anil Kaushal.

"We are in the process of linking Himachal with a server at Dehradun that will be a backup arrangement. The equipment would be set up in Himachal within next four months,"

said Kaushal. BSNL is the largest broadband service provider in Himachal.

Heading: CBI team in Sirsa, perusing records of Chautalas’ assets - Indian Express
Content:
The decision of ruling Bhartiya Janta Party government to implement the proposed master plan in Baddi- Barotiwala and Nalagarh industrial belt covering large number of villages may cast its shadow on the coming parliamentary elections.

Protests by the public representatives, along with villagers, to concede their demand of excluding villages and making amendments in the draft proposal of plan is giving sleepless nights to the frontline leaders of the Doon and Nalagarh constituency.

"This particular issue is virtually throwing cold water on the rank and file of Bhartiya Janta Party besides giving an political issue for Congress to raise," said a BJP leader on the condition of anonymity.

Over 20 pardhans of panchayats, along with villagers and members of Panchayati Raj Institutions and Baddi and Nalagarh civic bodies have submitted a memorandum to the Chief Minister and authorities of Baddi-Barotiwala-Nalagarh Industrial Development Authority (BBNIDA) to exclude the villages from the lists of Town and Country Planning (TCP) department and Special Area Development Authority (SADA).

Under the plan, the government had proposed total width of internal roads from five to 15 meters, 24 meter of main roads, 45 meters of state highways and 60 meters of national highway. Besides other measures to create more infrastructure in the towns and villages were also included in the plan. The government after finalising and approving the plan had invited the objections of the general public.

"The BJP leaders had announced during the Assembly elections that all the villages would be excluded from the lists of the master plan if the party was voted to power. Now the sitting BJP legislators of Doon and Nalagarh constituency are silent over the issue," said former Congress Parliamentary Secretary Lajja Ram.

He said the implementation of plan without involving the elected representatives of Panchayati Raj

Institutions and villagers is an indication that government is siding with the industrialists.

"The implementation of plan would certainly defeat the very purpose of empowering the gram panchayats to carry out developmental activities in accordance with the 74th amendment in Panchayati Raj Act," said Chairman of Solan Zila Parishad Ram Kumar.

He said Congress would definitely take up this issue in the coming Lok Sabha elections. President of Kisan Sangarsh Samiti Avtar Singh Khera said the farmers and public

representatives would hold a protest rally at Nalagarh again to protest against the decision of the government.

A senior leader of BJP Balbir Thakur said the farmers are not against the planned growth of the region but the manner in which the draft plan has been prepared has agitated them.

Heading: Karnal MP strikes note of dissent - Indian Express
Content:
A two-member CBI team today landed in Sirsa to conduct raids and start perusal of the revenue records of the properties belonging to former Haryana chief minister Om Parkash Chautala and his family.

Sources revealed that the team, led by ASP Jagroop of CBI's Special Crime Bureau (SCB), first obtained the revenue records pertaining to properties believed to be owned by the Chautala family, before recording the statements of revenue officials (patwaris) of Sirsa, Khairpur, Vaidwala, Bajekaan and Bhamboor.

The CBI team would also be examining the revenue records of properties in Chautala, Teja Khera, Lambi and Baru Khera in the next couple of days. Notably, Chautala family has a plush farm house at Teja Khera village.

Even as officials remained tight-lipped on the issue, today's CBI raids are believed to be associated with the case against Chautala, his family members and some other persons for allegedly amassing assets disproportionate to their known sources of income, from July 1999 to March 2005. CBI had registered the case on April 3, 2006 after the Centre issued a notification in response to a request made by the Haryana government. It was alleged that a wealth of Rs. 1400 crore had been amassed by them.

Following the registration of case, the CBI, in May 2006, had raided a number of places in six states and union territories, where Chautala and his family members, among others named in the case, were believed to own properties.

"The CBI team had sought the revenue records from us of the properties of Chautala family in some places in the region. As required by them, the record was made available to them," Sirsa SDM H C Bhatia told The Indian Express. He confirmed that CBI team would be examining the records of properties of the family at other places as well.

Heading: Tourism complexes to be handed back to original owners - Indian Express
Content:
The recent attack on the Congress party and the state leadership by Karnal MP Dr Arvind Sharma has led to speculation that he may be thinking of quitting the Congress.

Sharma is organising a Sarvjateeya Mahasammelan in Karnal on November 30. Sources say the meeting may decide his future course of action. Sharma plans to seek party workers' and the people's advice on whether to remain in the Congress party or not, say sources.

Dr Sharma had created a furore in the party before the recent trust vote in Parliament, with his outburst against the leadership and had praised BSP supremo Mayawati.

At that time Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda and other leaders of the Congress had managed to curb his rebellious tendencies with some promises and he had even voted in favour of the UPA government.

After lying low for some time, Dr Sharma has again attacked the leadership of Hooda. He severely criticised the party leadership during the recent police firing on agitating teachers in Rohtak and also on the removal of the ban on export of PUSA 1121 variety of rice. He also flayed the government on the issue of construction of a medical college for Karnal, besides a couple of other such instances.

When contacted, HPCC president Phool Chand Mullana said, "We have informed the party high command of his actions. If leaders have any problem they should discuss in the party fora and not rush to the press."

Heading: Maruti concession to cost state Rs 70 crore - Indian Express
Content:
Finally turning attention towards the almost-defunct tourist complexes, the Haryana Tourism Department has found a way to rescue these complexes. It has now offered these complexes, 10 in number, to the original owners to be maintained as guest houses at various places.

Eight such tourist complexes have been handed back to the government or to the departments which own these complexes, so that these can be maintained as guest houses. These include the complexes at Hathni Kund, Charkhi Dadri, Ottu, Aboob Shehar, Nasibpur Narnaul, Meham and Shakore in Sonepat.

The previous INLD government's idea to bring in private players to rescue these complexes had been given the cold shoulder by the private entrepreneurs. By the time the government could convince the private players, it was sent packing. The main reason behind the failure was that the government offered only those complexes for private management which were remotely located and loss-making.

Ironically, things have gone from bad to worse now with even The Oasis in Karnal in the red. Though the government is maintaining that Oasis, termed the pioneer complex of highway tourism in the state, is doing well, things are different on the ground and the deserted parking lot of the once packed-to-capacity complex reveals the real story. Evidently, this tourist complex on the Chandigarh-Delhi national highway has failed to stand in competition with the private complexes developed in its surroundings.

The exercise to hand over these complexes as guest houses started from Narwana complex. "Now we are surrendering these complexes to their respective departments or the government so that these can be used as guest houses, as competition has made life extremely difficult for most of these complexes," said a senior official of the tourism department.

Heading: Dairy industry to go hi-tech in state - Indian Express
Content:
As A result of the concession given to auto giant Maruti Suzuki India Ltd (MSIL), the Haryana government stands to lose Rs 70 crore this financial year. It is a result of the government deciding in principle to reduce the Central Sales Tax (CST) on inter-state sale of MSIL vehicles from the existing 2 to 1 per cent from November 1.

The state government, however, is not unduly worried about the loss of revenue though. "The Haryana Excise and Taxation Department will certainly achieve the annual target of 11,808 crore revenue for the financial year 2008-09," claimed Apoorva Kumar Singh, commissioner, Excise and Taxation Department.

"No doubt we are giving one per cent concession to the Maruti this year. But the concession would be effective from November. And anyway from April 2009 we would have had to reduce the CST by 1 per cent under the CST phasing-out programme of the Central government," he elaborated.

MSIL has been one of the regular investors in Haryana for decades. Since 1984, it has given 5500 crore in tax to the state. "We had to provide a level playing field to Maruti. Tamil Nadu for example has given tax exemption to the Hyundai and TVS companies for years together. MSIL has also promised to invest Rs 9,000 crore more in Haryana in the near future," added Apporva.

Heading: HOW CHARMING! - Indian Express
Content:
In a bid to organise the dairy farming sector to enhance milk production in the state, the Haryana Animal Husbandry and Dairy Department is all set to facilitate setting up of 500 high technology dairies all over the state under the high-tech dairying project.

The first and the largest dairy under the project is being set up at Bohatwala village in Jind. Presently, around 99 per cent of the milk production in the state is being done through unorganised dairy farming. "We aim to change the entire unorganised sector into organised form so that not only can the state maximise its milk production but also the best quality of milch animals can be bred."

"We have tied up with banks who would provide loan facilities on subsidised rates to the farmers under the scheme," said Dr KS Dangi, director general, Haryana Animal Husbandry and Dairying Department. He added that it is through the small farmers that the government aims to set up as many as 500 high technology dairies in the entire state.
