Heading: 43 cameras in NDMC areas - Indian Express
Content:
Four days after the serial blasts, and the blame game is on. While Delhi Police has blamed central intelligence units for not giving adequate inputs, the Home ministry plans to hold the city police accountable for its failure.

Sources said that in a meeting with the Ministry of Home Affairs, the top brass of Delhi Police, including Commissioner Y S Dadwal, were asked why the city police failed to prevent the blasts despite the country being on alert since recent blasts in Jaipur and Ahmedabad.

According to sources, Delhi Police told MHA officials that the blasts were a result of intelligence failure. Sources said the Intelligence Bureau (IB) had warned the city police about possible attacks at religious sites immediately after blasts in Jaipur on May 24. The input was "strengthened" after the blasts in Bangalore and Ahmedabad.

Police sources said security was tightened at Jama Masjid, Akshardham Temple and other religious sites following these inputs.

A senior MHA official said: "The blasts occurred due to failure of two wings of the government: the IB and the police. The Bureau's inputs turned out to be faulty, and IB officials said that their inputs were based on interrogation of blast suspects in Ahmedabad.

"(But) after serial blasts (in other cities), a red alert was sounded and it was Delhi Police's responsibility then to strengthen security." The official said the situation is being reviewed to fix accountability. Home ministry MHA sources indicate that the Centre has expressed its "unhappiness" with the blast investigations.

Special Cell officers could not be contacted despite repeated attempts.

Heading: South Delhi builder held for killing daughter, wife - Indian Express
Content:
The New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) had been sitting on the proposal since June, 2007 — for far too long. But Saturday's blasts saw the municipal body reaching for the file on surveillance cameras in four days flat. It will now install 43 Internet-Protocol (IP) cameras in Palika Kendra, Central Park, Palika Bazar and its parking. In the next six months. These sophisticated cameras can feed its footage directly into the Internet. They will work all hours for 15 days at a stretch and will be set up at strategic corners. The plan was cleared last June after an extensive survey, but the final tenders got the nod on Wednesday. The cameras will cost Rs 1.2 crore.

The traders' association at Palika Bazar had prodded the Council for the last four years to strengthen electronic surveillance in the market. General Secretary Dinesh Walia said, "It is about our security. We have asked the NDMC for long to clear the tenders."

Meanwhile, the dustbins that were overturned following Saturday's blasts continue to remain that way as there is still no plan on what to do with them.

While garbage piles up atop, it was learnt that the order to put them upside down first came from District Commissioner of Police, New Delhi, Anand Mohan — soon after the blasts.

Mohan said, "Minutes after the blasts at Barakhamba and Central Park, we realised they had put the bombs in dustbins this time. I flashed a message to all posts to check dustbins for more bombs." Mohan had also alerted NDMC officers.

Police officers on the beat asked ragpickers and vendors to go through the garbage.

Heading: HC slams govt’s ‘abysmal’ efforts rescuing children from bonded labour - Indian Express
Content:
Syed Mohammed Abbas, the Maharani Bagh-based builder who allegedly attempted suicide after killing his wife and daughter in what he claimed was a "suicide pact", was arrested on Wednesday for the duo's murder.

The police said Abbas was reportedly under immense pressure to repay loans and, therefore, asked wife Neelam to write a joint suicide note. Deputy Commissioner of Police (South) H G S Dhaliwal said, "After she wrote it, Abbas smothered Neelam and daughter Zenab with a pillow and later attempted suicide by injuring himself with a knife and some blades. He ended up unconscious."

Abbas was admitted in AIIMS and recuperated there. The bodies were found on September 4.

The police suspect he killed his wife to get the money from life insurance companies to repay the debt. "Though he confessed to having committed the crime, he is not medically fit yet," an officer said. "He would undergo more interrogation later."

According to the officer, Abbas told police that he had to take this step since he could not go back to his own family — he had reportedly split from his family in 1990 and teamed up with one Dr Shivnath Singh and joined his shoe business. Neelam was Singh's daughter — the two eloped to get married in 2005.

Abbas, 38, has told police he thereafter got into manufacturing tiles and stones and the initial success later set up his construction company with a partner, one Anupam Pandey. According to police, they bought land in Nangla Charan Das village, Noida Phase II, for Rs 15 crore but failing to call in investment from pre-booking of flats, the business went downhill, sharply.

As his debts increased, Abbas felt the only way out was to kill his wife and claim the insurance money.

A case is already registered against Abbas at New Friends Colony police station.

Heading: High Court, city court gore civic agency over moo menace on city roads - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi High Court on Wednesday said that efforts of the government to rescue children from bonded labour are "completely abysmal", with only 600 rescued in a city where around 60,000 minors work under abusive conditions.

"Just look at the work of your officers. They have no idea what rehabilitation is. About 600 children were rescued in the past two years in a city where 60,000 children work," a Bench led by Chief Justice A P Shah made this scathing remark on the Social Welfare Department's inability to rescue and rehabilitate children from bonded labour.

"Efforts towards their rescue are completely abysmal. We are dissatisfied. Till 2007 there were no rescue operations at all," noted the court.

The court wondered aloud how sweatshops employing child labour could still continue to operate, and asked the government if sealing the factories will help address the problem.

"Most of these factories are functioning from rented premises. Sealing the premises would only mean that the owners will open the establishments at some other place," briefed government counsel Mukta Gupta.

The court has now made clear its intention to set up an independent committee to look into the welfare of children rescued from bonded labour.

It went on to issue notices to the secretaries of Labour Department and the Social Welfare Department, Delhi Police, National Child Rights Commission and the Education Department for their response in this regard.

In an earlier hearing, the Bench had observed that children rescued from bonded labour often find their way back to other sweat shops without access to a better life or education.

The court had also sought information on the extent to which the government was adhering to the provisions of the Bonded Labour (Abolition) Act as far as payment of compensation to the rescued children was concerned.

Each child is given a 'release certificate' by the Union Labour Ministry, aimed at making the government liable to pay compensation to these children for their time spent in bonded labour.

Heading: Railway station completes change to new routing system - Indian Express
Content:
MCD excuse: Cattle owners' backing; HC 'surprised'

Think twice before you shoo off 'stray' cattle on Delhi roads. According to the MCD, the men who own them have "political backing".

After eight years of litigation and three time-bound orders from the Delhi High Court to remove stray cattle later, this is how the MCD explained its inability to rid the Capital's roads of bovines bit by wanderlust. Even worse is the civic agency's experience, as narrated before a division bench comprising Chief Justice A P Shah and Justice Muralidhar on Wednesday, during its attempts to "re-locate" dairy farms in the city. "Dairy owners beat up our (MCD) officers," a senior panel lawyer for MCD said. "We have 21 FIRs for assault and other criminal charges registered against these dairy owners.

"These people have political backing."

In 2002, the High Court had given MCD six months to remove all stray cattle from the Capital's roads. The order was repeated in 2005 and late 2007 following complaints that the civic agency had not acted in response.

Meanwhile, the MCD's submission about "practical difficulties" in rounding up cattle from the city thoroughfares took the court by surprise. The Chief Justice said, "I have never seen any statutory authority behave like this."

The civic body's counsel reacted, "I have only tried to apprise this court of the problems faced by the agency. We need help of other government agencies to remove these cattle and relocate dairies."

To this, Justice Muralidhar retorted: " (Do) you want the court to run the administration for you? Officers now find it very convenient to say that they will not talk to other government departments. They expect the court to do it."

Meera Bhatia, counsel for Common Cause, the NGO which had drawn court's attention to the problem, said: "The various departments continue to pass the buck from one to the other. The MCD's stand is actually in contempt of the court orders."

The civic agency, however, defended itself by claiming to have removed "18,838 cattle in the past two years". The MCD counsel said, "We just need nine more months to remove all of them — 60 per cent of our work is over; only 40 per cent is left."

The court directed all government agencies, including MCD, NDMC and Delhi Police, to file a joint status report on cattle menace within the next two weeks.

Heading: MCD told: Pay for death due to bovine interference - Indian Express
Content:
The New Delhi Railway Station's conversion to the new route relay interlocking system has been completed in record time. Closed for all operations on September 5, the station was able to handle limited traffic starting September 13 and was functioning in full capacity by Tuesday morning.

"Not only did we finish work on the route relay interlocking system two days ahead of schedule but we were also able to operationalise two new platforms at the station," Geetanjali Kame, public relations officer for the station, said.

The transfer was, however, not as smooth as the Railways would have liked us to believe. Most trains headed to the station were delayed by anywhere between a few minutes and a few hours. "Fact is that we managed to get work done in record time. Obviously, there were a few minor glitches that took time to be sorted out. We are confident the system will function perfectly by the end of the week," a railway official said.

For the record, Northern Railways has laid 1,278 routes — being touted as the largest in the Indian Railways network so far — in nine days. A total of 3,000 gangmen worked on the system in order to ensure that it was completed in record time. Over 740 trains had to either be diverted or cancelled for the purpose.

Many passengers assumed the change in the interlocking system had something to do with modernising basic facilities at the station. "It has been bought to my notice that many passengers confused the change in signal systems with the larger world class railway station programme we hope to implement soon," a senior railways official said.

"The system ensures that when one train has been cleared to leave or approach the station, another train does not come in its way. It was of utmost importance to modernise this system in order to reduce dependence on manual patrolling, thereby making our operations safer," the official said.

"We had space for four new platforms but that is about it," an official said.

Heading: Bail hearing on BMW case today - Indian Express
Content:
Why have you not removed stray cattle from the Capital's roads, a city court recently asked the civic body, at once ordering it to pay Rs 2 lakh as compensation to the relatives of a man who had died from a fall in 2006 — while trying to maneuvre his scooter around a wandering cow.

Additional District Judge Kamini Lau said it was the municipality's "statutory obligation" to keep bovines off the road. "Presence of large animals on the road, particularly cattle, is also the failure of the corporation to effectively discharge its duties," the judge said. She said the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) had been "careless and negligent" in tackling the menace of stray cattle despite several time-bound orders from the High Court on this.

The High Court had directed the civic body thrice to impound stray animals and to relocate illegal dairies from urbanised villages to the Ghoga Dairy Colony. But the municipality had dallied, putting forth various reasons. Judge Lau said: "It can definitely be done... if officers have the will to do so and are more vigilant and sensitive to the problem." She said the corporation should be held guilty if anyone is harmed by the strays.

The court's observation was provoked by the petition of one Rukmani Devi. Her husband Raj Kumar had fallen off his scooter when the vehicle collided with a cow which had wandered in its path.

Rukmani Devi had sought compensation for her three minor children, arguing that her husband had died because of the corporation's recklessness.

The civic body had fought back, saying Raj Kumar was wearing improper head gear and that his two-wheeler was not fit for driving. It had also said that the cow had jumped onto the road from a divider, and construction of dividers were not within its jurisdiction.

The judge admitted the victim might not have driven cautiously but that did not absolve the civic body of its duties. She also ordered the corporation to pay Rukmani Devi's legal expenses.

Heading: Cops mislead accident victim’s family, suspended - Indian Express
Content:
A city court is expected to decide on Thursday the anticipatory bail plea of Utsav Bhasin, whose bail was cancelled after the police booked him under a stringent penal provision for allegedly mowing down a man with his BMW. Additional Sessions Judge Brijesh Garg adjourned the hearing on the plea of the Haryana-based industrialist's son after the parties failed to produce the High Court's order giving permission to the police to re-arrest Bhasin if required.

The police had added Section 304 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) to the FIR lodged in the case, after the accident victim Anuj Singh, a BPO employee, succumbed to his injuries on Saturday.

The 21-year-old youth was allegedly at the wheels when his car hit two motorcycle-borne men around 2.40 am on September 11 near the Moolchand flyover in South Delhi.

Heading: Former city BSP chief, 23 others join Cong - Indian Express
Content:
The Noida police suspended five personnel on Wednesday for carelessness in performing their duty. A protest was held at the office of the SSP, after police personnel allegedly misled the family of a 55-year-old man, who died in a road accident on Tuesday.

"We have suspended chowki-in-charge, Hardola, Ompal Sharma, Pawan Malik and chowki-in-charge, Sector-24 Hari Darshan along with two constables, Balkrishan and Gajender Singh, of Sector-24 for not fulfilling their duties. The family should have been informed as the police had information about the deceased," SP (city) Ashok Tripathi said.

Pundev Singh, a resident of Sector-4 in Noida, had gone to buy groceries on Tuesday morning when he was allegedly crushed by a tractor near Sector-5. His family contacted the police and several hospitals in the area in a bid to find him.

"We lodged a missing persons FIR but the police kept us in the dark about his whereabouts. This morning, they told us he was cremated after he succumbed to his injuries," Ram Udeshya Singh, son-in-law of the deceased, alleged.

When the family went to the spot of the accident, eyewitnesses told them the driver of the tractor took the almost dead Singh to Hardola. "And soon after, the police arrived. They knew about the accident but no action was taken till this morning. And they did not wait for us to claim the body and cremated it. He was the sole bread winner of the family," Gopal Kumar, a neighbour, said.

The Noida police have arrested the tractor driver, Sanjeev Kumar, who has been booked for causing death due to rash and negligent driving.

Heading: 19 new dengue cases reported as MCD tackles worker strike - Indian Express
Content:
Former president of BSP's Delhi Unit Jageram Bhati, along with 23 other BSP office-bearers, joined the Congress at a function at CM Sheila Dikshit's official residence on Wednesday.

A beaming Dikshit claimed that this move comes as a jolt to BSP's plans in the Capital. "BSP had been claiming that they would emerge as strong competition during the coming Assembly elections, but it does not seem to be likely any longer," Dikshit told reporters.

Dikshit also announced that Sonia Gandhi's rally, which was initially scheduled for September 17, will now be held on October 4. The rally, in which the Congress president was to distribute provisional regularisation certificates to the Capital's unauthorised colonies, was postponed in the wake of Saturday's blasts.

Bhati had been removed from the post of president of the Delhi unit on August 30 by BSP supremo Mayawati for indiscipline and lack of work at the ground level. BSP sources said that Mayawati was also unhappy with the list of final candidates prepared by Bhati for the Assembly elections. Bhati was replaced by Brahm Singh Bidhuri, the candidate from the Okhla seat. Mayawati even refused to give Bhati a ticket for the Assembly elections.

Bhati had quit Congress in 2003 to join BSP for the very same reason. "We were the ones who established BSP in Delhi. Mayawati nevertheless decided to give a ticket to those who paid her a higher rate," Bhati said.

Interestingly, earlier he had said that he would abide by Mayawati's decision and continue to work for the party after he was removed from the president's post.

Even Dikshit has not made it clear whether Bhati would be given an Assembly ticket or not. Those who quit BSP include Ashwini Bhargava, the in-charge of Northwest Lok Sabha constituency and Mohammad Arif, BSP Muslim front chief.

Interestingly, other than the State Urban Development Minister Raj Kumar Chauhan, no other Congress leader was present at the function. DPCC chief Jai Prakash Aggarwal and AICC general secretary in-charge Ashok Gehlot were conspicuous by their absence.

Heading: Mid-week rain, waterlogging bring city traffic to standstill - Indian Express
Content:
Nineteen fresh cases of dengue were reported in the city on Wednesday, taking the number of people infected with the virus to 293 this season.

"Nineteen more patients have tested positive for the virus, taking the number of dengue-afflicted persons to 293," MCD Public Health Committee Chairman V K Monga said.

Adding to the MCD's woes, around 2,500 domestic breeding checkers (DBCs), employed with the MCD on a contract basis, are on strike demanding regularisation of their jobs.

The strike and a relay fast organised by the DBCs from Wednesday at the Town Hall has sparked off a controversy over their removal and new appointments. With the contractual employees on strike, the civic body is planning to hire another 420 workers to fill in.

"Out of 3,200 DBCs, only 750 are reporting for work. We had, however, recently advertised for 420 vacant posts, for which we have received 6,000 applications," MCD Public Health Committee Chairman V K Monga said.

"If the strike is not resolved within two to three days, we may even think of taking in more people and effectively end the contract of the workers on strike," he said. MCD officials said September-October is the peak season for dengue cases and the strike is merely a "blackmailing tactic".

The ruling BJP in MCD accused the Congress "Opposition lobby" of "instigating" the protestors, as the Congress has openly come out in support of the DBCs holding the BJP responsible for the situation.

The deadlock notwithstanding, dengue cases are increasing rapidly in the Capital. Delhi has reported 274 cases and one death so far this year. Officials say that the number of cases is not expected to decline at least till September-end. The civic body also refuted allegations of the Opposition that medicines being used for treating the disease have crossed expiry dates.

Heading: Sheila for more stringent terror laws - Indian Express
Content:
As the skies opened up on Wednesday evening, peak hour traffic came to a standstill at several places due to waterlogging. With 37.44 mm rainfall, the minimum temperature dipped to a pleasant 25.5 degrees Celsius.

The MCD received 21 complaints of waterlogging from various places. All major arterial roads in the Capital, including Mathura Road, Mehrauli-Badarpur Road, Bhairon Road T-point, under Dhaula Kuan flyover, under Mayapuri flyover, ITO-junction, Rajghat, Rao Tula Ram Marg, Vikas Marg and Chilla Chowk in Gazipur were choked due to waterlogging.

"It took me nearly two and a half hours to reach ITO from New Friend's colony. Several vehicles broke down due to the waterlogging," said Ankit Jain, a bank employee.

Vipul Agarwal, who works in a software firm in Greater Noida, said "It took me nearly an hour to reach ITO from the border."

At 10 in the night, the Ring Road was completely jammed due to waterlogging in several parts. Between Yashwant Place underpass and Vinay Marg, traffic came to a standstill due to waterlogging. With the Dwarka roundabout close to the airport completely submerged in water, traffic was stuck till the Rao Tula Ram flyover.

The weather forecast over the next two days indicates yet more rainfall. "The minimum temperature is likely to remain low and the next two days will see thunderstorms with the possibility of rain," an officer on duty at the Safdarjung Met department said.

Heading: No checks: security terminates at ISBTs - Indian Express
Content:
In stark contrast to UPA government's stand, Delhi Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit on Wednesday strongly advocated the need for "most stringent" legislation to deal with terrorism in the wake of Saturday's blasts that left 28 people dead and nearly 130 injured.

"I am in favour of most stringent laws to deal with such kind of things (terror acts)...The law should be such that they become a deterrent," Dikshit told reporters after a meeting with city traders here.

She said it is for the Parliament and the central government to decide on the content of the legislation. The Chief Minister also said that even though she had no role to play in police activity or security management of the city, she would voice the concerns of the people.

Her comments came a day after the Administrative Reforms Commission felt that existing laws were not enough to deal with the menace and recommended a comprehensive anti-terror law, in contrast with the central government's view.

The UPA government has been of the view that the existing laws were adequate to deal with terrorism and crimes having inter-state links. After reviewing the security scenario in the city at a Cabinet meeting yesterday, Dikshit said it has decided to intensively involve RWAs and market associations to create awareness on terrorism.

Heading: Purana Qila, ruins or not, old is gold - Indian Express
Content:
11 am
Sarai Kale Khan Inter-State Bus Terminus (ISBT) in South Delhi has at least 1,500 persons within its premises. Waiting to catch a bus connecting the Capital with several states — Haryana, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan — as also DTC buses on some city routes.

Amid the milling crowd the absence of policemen, in and around the bus station, is stark, keeping in mind it's just four days since serial blasts ripped apart the Capital. There is neither any CCTV camera nor any door frame metal detector installed in the terminus.

Entry and exit are a free for all.

Radheshyam Khokhar, about to take a bus to Rewari in Haryana, says, "I was not checked, my bags were not frisked, and I could not see a single policeman anywhere."

It's just before noon, and private security guards man the entry points as cops at the police post sip chai. "The security will be beefed up soon," a policeman says.

DCP (South) H G S Dhaliwal could not be contacted for his comments on the post-blast bandobast, or the apparent lack of it.

12 noon
There are close to 2,000 people at Anand Vihar ISBT in East Delhi. This terminus caters to many routes of UP, Uttarakhand and many city routes of DTC.

The CCTV cameras are all out of order here. There is, however, a good presence of policemen in and around the ISBT; the door frame metal detectors, too, are working. There is no frisking, and baggage is never scanned.

"We have had a meeting with all bus drivers and people who work in and around this ISBT. They have been briefed about identifying suspicious packets and other such issues," DCP (East) Ajay Chaudhary says. As for baggage scanners, Chaudhary says, "We will procure them if requirement arises."

He adds that continuous "announcements are being made through speakers installed at the ISBT".

1 pm
Kashmere Gate ISBT is the Capital's largest, oldest and busiest bus terminus. There are more than 3,000 people, waiting for buses to all north Indian states — Haryana, UP, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Rajasthan, Jammu & Kashmir, Rajasthan, and Madhya Pradesh.

The door frame metal detectors are up at all entry and points points, and there is a good presence of the men in khaki and private security guards.

No one, though, is frisked; no bag is checked. A guard at one of the entry points says they "do frisk people and check their bags, sometimes".

DCP (North) Sagarpreet Huda says, "All the CCTV cameras are functional and there are constant announcements for public awareness."

Heading: IIM-A expresses solidarity with Lehman Brothers, Merrill Lynch - Indian Express
Content:
Students of Blue Bells School International, Kailash Colony, take part in the heritage walk at Purana Qila conducted by The Indian Express in association with INTACH and ASI

A schools' initiative from The Express Group
Quest is a project conducted by The Indian Express in schools in and around Delhi. It covers more than 50 schools in Delhi and NCR.

Quest aims at stirring awareness and opinions. Today, when all that children see are shopping malls and cineplexes, we at The Indian Express want to show a completely different picture of this city to them. Delhi has changed beyond nostalgia and recognition since Independence. How many of these kids know of the 'Seven Cities' of Delhi or the stories of the pigeon fliers of Old Delhi?

The idea behind such an activity is to create awareness about the various structures and monuments that the students do not know about. This is a specially designed programme, which will help the students appreciate the rich culture and background of this city. In association with INTACH and ASI, this is a small effort on our behalf to depict a phase of our national life and the decay of a whole culture, a particular mode of thought and living. The visit is followed by the students sending in articles, pictures, poems, paintings, and collages to express their experiences about the heritage walk.

A fusion of indian, islamic architecture
On Friday, September 12, I went for a heritage walk at the Purana Qila, organised by The Indian Express in collaboration with the Archaeological Survey of India and INTACH, along with other students of Blue Bells School International. Though we all have been to monuments like the Red Fort and Humayun's Tomb, this was the first time we got a chance to know in depth about a monument. It was totally different because we had guides from INTACH helping us in getting to know our own heritage.

The Purana Qila is believed to date back to the times of the Pandavas; when they lived here and the city around them was called Indraprastha. It is said the area around Purana Qila was earlier a barren land known as "Khandaprastha" but then Lord Indra's architect, "Vishwa Karma", made the barren land fertile. From then on it was called Indraprastha — The Land of Indra.

Excavations providing evidence of the Mauryan kingdom were also found here.

The Purana Qila was built by Humayun in 1533 and shows the fusion of Indian and Islamic architecture . This fort was then conquered by Sher Shah Suri, who built a mosque, Qila-e-Kona, before handing the fort over to his son, Saleem .

It was only a couple of hours long but we learned a lot during the walk. I am grateful to my teachers and the organisers for this excursion.
— Surashree Bhattacharjee, IX B

A past worth revisiting
A walk on the wilder side of history! If a sentence had to sum up our trip to the Purana Qila, nothing would have been more apt than the above sentence.

Interspersed with forest and the city, were the quite well-maintained ruins of the city of Dinpanah. A sprawling complex, with many remnants of the glorious past still around, one can't help but get a feeling of what could have been, had Humayun not taken that unfortunate tumble and attention not shifted from the city.

With the forest and greenery around us, urban living must have had a different meaning back then. The fort is full of mosques, observatories, libraries and wells that were used to pull water from the Yamuna.

The architecture and calligraphy are brilliant works of art and make one marvel at the knowledge that has been lost.

To conclude, the trip was enlightening, engrossing, interesting, fun and quite tiring.
— Uday mishra, IX D

Walking in for fun, walking out with information
Antiquity and history always fascinates me and I have always admired the creations of the pre-Mughal and Mughal eras. I was excited about the visit to the Purana Qila and the uphill walk towards the un-ostentatious yet imposing gateway had an overwhelming effect on me. History does not stimulate the majority of us and spending some quiet time reading is an activity scoffed at. However, such heritage walks are fun and help in absorbing knowledge, and are also meaningful time spent with friends.

We had well-informed guides from INTACH and The Indian Express showing us around. Something that really caught my attention was the simplicity of the mosque, the beautiful carvings on the western wall, and the difference of style of the five arches of the mosque.

The Sher Mandal was built for the purpose of leisure and also for keeping watch over the entire area. Emperor Humanyun died a most tragic death; he is believed to have been in his private library trying to spot Venus when he heard the azaan. He tried to make haste, tripped and fell off the stairs. In those times, the stairs were built in such a manner that they were kept tucked away, were narrow and offered a steep climb, keeping in mind the threat from intruders.

There are many such interesting facts waiting to be discovered and appreciated. Such walks are fun and educative.
— Priyadarshini Bhattacharya, xii c

Breath of fresh air
The heritage walk to Purana Qila was indeed an interesting activity to undertake on a September morning.

Students study architecture as a necessary component of history. A few visuals of monuments in the classroom during lessons, the giving out of factual information like who built the structure, when, material used, dimensions etc, reduce a very interesting topic to an utterly boring one.

Walks, such as these, organised once in a while, come as a breath of fresh air. Indeed, teaching history is greater fun in an ambience like that. Questions do not have to be asked by the teacher, they instead come from the students. "Ma'am, why grey blocks of stones here and red sandstone there; how is the prayer done; why only calligraphy, why not human representations; where is the king's palace, the common people's habitations?" And there you have a teacher truly satisfied that the students have learnt, for they have thought.

We wish to extend our sincere thanks to The Indian Express and INTACH for organising a walk for us with enthusiastic facilitators, who gave us not only historical information about the monument but also anecdotal inputs relating to it, which obviously had the students so much more interested. This walk has left us greedy for more.

A follow-up session in classrooms has students more animated and charged, as each wants to share his/her own experience or, should I say, interpretation. Constructing knowledge — is that not what we aim at?
— Smita Sahay Bhattacharya, Senior History Teacher

When history came alive
Turning the pages of a history text book doesn't interest any body. But what happens when those very pages of history come alive! I, along with other students of Blue Bells School International, Kailash Colony, visited the famous Purana Qila on Friday, September 12. We were very excited and hoped the day ahead would be fun filled. When we reached the Purana Qila, we were given a small introduction about the monument and other neighbouring structures.

We entered the monument only to be amazed by this magnificent piece of architecture. From the huge domes decorated with intricate carving, to the colossal halls, to the wide expanse of greenery all around — it was so beautiful.

We have been studying about these famous monuments for so long but when we see them with our own eyes, we tended to understand them better and with a lot more interest. I am sure that visits such as these would make history lessons more fun. When knowledge does not limit itself to the pages of a book and moves beyond, it attains a new life.

We feel proud of such a great legacy, such a great cultural heritage. We hope we can sustain these symbols of glory even for the future generations to cherish.
— Ananya Pathak, XII C

We invite schools to be a part of this Express Group initiative. For queries mail to heritagewalks@expressindia.com

Heading: Special courts to deal with cheque bouncing cases - Indian Express
Content:
The Indian Institute of Management-Ahmedabad on Wednesday expressed solidarity with Lehmann Brothers and Merrill Lynch, US firms now in the eye of the global stock market crash.

In a statement, IIM-A said: "We would like to express our solidarity with two of our longstanding recruiting partners and we wish them well in their hour of distress."'

IIM-A, however, remained non-committal on the fate of its alumni now employed in these giants. In the last two years, 59 students from IIM-A have made it to the two institutions.

IIM-A said that given the diversity of their student pool, those looking for a long-term career in finance will continue to have a preference for the sector and they are unlikely to base a long term career decision on a short term view of the market.

Saral Mukherjee, Placement Chairman, IIM-A said: "Though there is a lot of speculation following the recent events at the Wall Street, but the events are definitely not conclusive in nature. Nevertheless, future hiring by these two companies is uncertain at this point though how these events have impacted our alumni and interns cannot be commented on at this moment. With our diverse pool of recruiters, the placements are unlikely to be affected."

An IIM-A official further said that the combined number of PGP students hired by these two firms was 11 last year, while the numbers for previous years are 28 (2007) and 20 (2006).

He added that the crisis was unlikely to have an impact on the IIM-A students working at these places.

Heading: SIT arrests 7 in connection with Gulberg Society massacre - Indian Express
Content:
Starting mid-October, these will be the first of their kind in India

Starting next month, Ahmedabad will have eight metropolitan magistrate courts to deal exclusively with cheque bouncing cases under the Negotiable Instruments Act. Once set up, these will be the first of their kind in the country. The additional courts will be set up within the premises of the old collectorate compound.

Initially, exclusive courts to dispose pending cheque bouncing cases are being established in Ahmedabad on an experimental basis. Later, such courts are likely to be opened at other centres.

According to High Court sources, there are approximately two lakh cheque bouncing cases all over the state, with the majority of them (84,000 cases) in Ahmedabad, followed by Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot. Apparently it was because of such a huge number of cases that prompted the High Court to come up with the idea to open additional courts to deal with such type of cases.

Law Secretary M H Shah said a large number of cases under the Negotiable Instruments Act were pending. As such, the government went ahead to set up the exclusive courts as part of a special drive to dispose these cases and reduce the burden from regular courts so they could be handle other cases. The state government, only recently, cleared the setting up of these courts on an initiative by the Gujarat High Court.

Chief Justice K S Radhakrishnan, who recently assumed office, said the exclusive courts will provide relief to the people whose cases were pending in different courts for a long time.

Advocate Kamal Shah, a criminal case practitioner, said that litigants had to wait for long for disposal of their cheque bouncing cases because regular courts were busy with other serious cases. An exclusive court for cheque bouncing cases will dispose such cases effectively and fast. Another criminal lawyer said that the new courts will benefit people in the long run, much like the fast track courts which have helped reduce the pendency of cases.

A senior High Court official said that the large number of cheque bouncing cases indicated an increase in white collar crimes in economically and financially strong Gujarat, but, it also showed the reliance of the people for justice. An increasing number of people were moving the court to seek justice in cheque bouncing cases, the official added.

According to Registrar General Pradeep Bhatt, the new courts will be formally inaugurated by Chief Justice K S Radhakrishnan on October 18. After this, courts will begin functioning and handling the cases.

Bhatt added that the attendant staff for the eight courts has already been appointed. At present, the premises where these courts will be set up are being redone, and they will be complete within two week.

Heading: Man uses family album to dupe cousin - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court appointed Special Investigating Team (SIT) on Wednesday arrested seven people in connection with the Gulberg Society massacre during the post-Godhra riots of 2002.

The total number of people arrested in the case now stands at 54.

Those arrested include Naran Tak (46), Manish Patil (25), Raju Tiwari (32), Dashrat Patni (28), Nagin Patni (29), Lakhansinh Chudasma (29) and Dharmesh Shukla (28). The accused have been booked on charges of murder, arson and rioting.

J M Suthar, DySP, SIT said: "These arrests were made on the basis of statements of nearly 160 witnesses that we recorded during the investigation of this case. Some more people have been named and they will be arrested soon.

At least 37 people, including Congress MP Ehsaan Jaffri were killed in the infamous massacre at Gulberg Society. The incident took place on February 28, 2002. A total of 47 persons accused in the case are already behind bars.

The seven are likely to be produced before a city court on Thursday.

Heading: 10 post-Godhra riot accused gets 5-day police remand - Indian Express
Content:
A man allegedly used a family album to forge documents and transfer the power of attorney of the family land under his name, thereby duping his cousin of the claim.

On Wednesday, Salim Qazi (45), the victim, lodged a complaint against his cousin Moinuddin Qazi at the Dahod Rural Police station in this regard.

Sub Inspector K V Jhala said: "We are still investigating the matter. It looks like the accused stole a family album, then allegedly used the photographs using computer software, to make passport-size portraits, and sold off the property worth Rs 30 lakh."

Moinuddin is related to Salim from his father's side. Salim said: "He is the son of my father's sister. We have some ancestral land, which was shared by my father and my aunts. But, in connivance with the buyers, Moinuddin stole our family album, forged the papers and also involved a notary of the Dahod District Court in this."

Besides Moinuddin, Qazi has named buyers Avinash Shah, Satishchandra Shah, Bakul Shah, Babulal Shah, Amisha Parikh, Neha Parikh and the notary P B Joshi in his complaint.

He has also alleged that some of the local police officers are involved in the case.

Apparently, after his complaint was not entertained at the Dahod rural police station for almost a month, he wrote a letter to Deputy Superintendent of Police H R Chaudhary on September 8.

Salim is now staying in the ancestral land and earning a living through carpentry.

"Sometimes, I get work. My family is known in the city, so something or the other always works out. I do not care about Rs 30 lakhs, but why did he use the family album?" said Salim.

As proof of ownership of the land, he also showed the receipts for the revenue he had been paying for the land over the couple of years. The police said they were looking for Moinuddin, but are yet to find him.

Heading: BJP demands 70% BMC jobs, contracts for Marathis - Indian Express
Content:
A Metropolitan Court on Wednesday placed 10 people under 5 days police remand in two different post-Godhra riot cases.

The Supreme Court appointed Special Investigation Team (SIT) arrested Ashok Purani, Vijay Chchara, Ramesh Bidawala and Kishan Marathi on Tuesday for their role in the Naroda Patiya killings, which left 86 dead.

The other six accused, Mukesh Vyas, Rakesh Vyas, Sanjay Vyas, Bhikhabhaui Patel, Mahesh and Manilal Thakor were arrested by the SIT on Sunday for their alleged involvement in the Naroda Gam case, which had left nine dead. The six were sent for a three-day remand on Monday, which was extended to another five days on Wednesday.

The SIT has asked for the remand to further question the accused for information about other people still at large in connection with the two cases and also the involvement of leaders of organisations and political parties in the riots.

The SIT's remand application also says that more time is required to find out more about the goods looted during the riots.

Heading: On his 59th birthday Modi takes to blogging - Indian Express
Content:
Party corporator moves notice of motion in municipal body's GB, says he wants to put an end to Sena-MNS tug-of-war for Marathi manoos

For the last eight months, as the Raj Thackeray-led Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) and cousin Uddhav Thackeray-led Shiv Sena battled it out on the streets "for the cause of Marathi manoos", their ally the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) chose to remain a quiet spectator. But now it has ended its silence and jumped onto the bandwagon — and is claiming that it will put an end to the "tug of war between the two Senas".

In the latest development, the BJP has demanded priority for the Marathi population for jobs in the country's richest civic body, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), as well as for BMC contracts and projects. Party corporator Vishwanath Maske has moved a notice of motion in the BMC General Body (GB), demanding that the civic body make a compulsory "priority" of 70 per cent for Marathi manoos for all jobs with the BMC, its contractors and its various outsourced projects.

"Hoards of migrants are coming into the city every day, due to which locals are being deprived of job opportunities," he said. Maske's notice is expected to be discussed in the coming days. If it is approved by all 247 members, then Municipal Commissioner Jairaj Phatak will have to submit a report on its implementation in a month.

Maske has asked the BMC to give priority to the Marathi population while recruiting staff for the commercial capital's civic administration as well as for other bodies like BEST, distribution of stalls in civic markets and even contractors who are appointed for various projects.

The civic body, with a budget of Rs 16,000 crore, awards numerous infrastructure projects on contract basis. Many of the current contractors as well as labourers are "outsiders".

Maske told Newsline that he wants to put an end to the Shiv Sena-MNS tug-of-war for Marathi manoos. "Both the parties are screaming and running riot in the name of Marathi manoos. Who benefits from all this? No one. It only results in losses," he said. "The main problem will not get solved by displaying signboards in Marathi. The locals need jobs and better financial conditions. Job priority and reservation is the final and only solution," he asserted.

Maske's party colleagues in the BMC are backing him. BJP leader Bhalchandra Shirsat said it is the party's duty to demand that jobs be reserved for locals.

"We support the issue of sons of the soil and there is nothing wrong with it," he said, adding that along with contractors, priority and reservation should also be applicable to contract labourers. "If the project and money are from Mumbai, Maharashtra, then why shouldn't the labourers too be from here? Why bring outsiders?" he asked.

The Shiv Sena, which is the ruling party in the BMC along with its ally the BJP, pointed out that it has been demanding job reservations from the very beginning. "Apart from reservation for staff recruitment, priority should also be given to Maharashtrian contractors if they fit the eligibility criteria," opined Standing Committee Chairman Ravindra Waikar.

While the MNS leader in the BMC was not reachable, the party's general secretary Shirish Parkar said that the demand is an indication of how all parties are slowly uniting on the issue of "sons of the soil". "It is a victory of solidarity and unity for the Marathi manoos. We do not mind if the BJP too supports the cause. If they want to take credit, then let that be. The important aspect is that all this is for the sons of soil," he said.

Heading: Modi flags off relief train for Bihar on his birthday - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister Narendra Modi is to take to blogging on his revamped personal website www.narendramodi.in, where he will share his views with others. After having reported a conversation at the Tarnetar Mela wherein Modi was reportedly referred to as "a god with beard," the Gujarat Information Department briefed the changes in Modi's personal wesbite on the occasion of his 59th birthday.

Relaunched today, the website is now an interactive portal aimed at creating a platform for building a golden Gujarat.

The new-look website is loaded with Modi's ring-tones, wallpapers and screen savers and a special section exhorting everyone to participate in Gujarat's golden jubilee function in 2010.

There is also a section which has him answering queries for children and others in both text and video format. Besides, there is also a section dedicated to the common man — "I am available" — which provides an option to interact with the CM. Visitors can ask questions to Modi through this section. Visitors can also have access to Modi's speeches, photographs, his publications and his take on good governance on the website.

Compensation for Vadodara resident killed in Delhi blast
The state government has announced a compensation of Rs 1 lakh for the family of Kamini Nisarata, a Vadodara resident who died in the serial bomb blasts in New Delhi. A press release issued by Health Minister Jaynarayan Vyas and Industries Minister Saurabh Patel also said that compensation will also be given to Kashyup Ravat who got injured in the bomb blast.

Heading: Proved: Civic body negligent, but will it own up? - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday celebrated his 59th birthday by flagging off a relief train with materials worth Rs 5.27 crore to the flood-affected districts of Bihar

For the first time, the welcome accorded to Modi at the Surat Railway Goods train yard was simple, without any folk music or garland ceremony.

Apparently Modi had informed the district administration officials that the programme should be simple given that lakhs of people in Bihar are starving and trapped in the flood waters.

Modi said Surat was once trapped under flood and the people of the city know the hardships others face under similar circumstances.

"The people of Surat had then experienced the importance of relief materials as everything else was submerged under water and there was nothing to eat or drink. After learning about the floods in Bihar, we had sent a team of five officials to collect information about the relief package. Later I had appealed to the people of Surat and elsewhere in south Gujarat to collect donations for the flood-affected people," he said.

He said for the first time in the country, a train carrying relief materials like sarees, clothes, milk powders, kitchen kit, stoves was being sent to Bihar.

He added: "We regularly read in the newspapers about floods and other natural calamities in Bihar, but this is the first time in the history of the state that 2,500 villages in the state have been affected."

At the function, Modi declared that a second train containing relief materials worth Rs 8 crore will be sent to the flood affected villages on October 12 from Ahmedabad. He added that the government has planned to send in relief worth a total of Rs 20 crore to Bihar.

Modi was accompanied by state BJP President Purshottam Rupala, Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Anandi Patel, Tribal Development Minister Mangu Patel, Rural Development Minister Narottam Patel, Surat Mayor Ranjeet Gilitwala and MLA Kishor Vankawala.

Heading: Open drains expose slack civic body - Indian Express
Content:
It was a clear case of death due to negligence on part of the civic administration.

On Wednesday night,Jivaji Marwadi was pulling the string to propel the engine of his auto-rickshaw when he slipped and fell into a deep drain exposed by an open crater at Guptanagar on Sarkhej Road.

Local residents say their complaint about the open crater was left unattended for one week. After the unfortunate incident, "barriers have been placed around the 10-feet deep crater and work to close it is going on a war-footing," said a local shop owner, who saw Jivaji fall into the drain.

Jivaji's body was fished out after a long search operation on Thursday morning, from the Pirana sewage water treatment plant where the pipeline ends, fire brigade officials said.

Jivaji made a living by plying an auto-rickshaw (GJ7-TT-5399), which he had purchased through private finance. While he had cleared Rs 70,000 of the loan, Rs 10,000 is still to be paid.

Father of three children, two of them school-going, Jivaji lived in a rented room paying Rs 500 a month and had difficulty making both ends meet, say his neighbours.

Whether the AMC will give him family compensation or not is unclear, but there is a precedent of the civic body offering job to the widow of a man who died at Saijpur Bogha pumping station, on compassionate ground despite the man not being a civic employee. Of course, it was done under tremendous public pressure, as people had refused to perform the last rites of the deceased until the matter was settled.

The AMC is still to take a decision on the responsibility it will take in another case of death caused by negligence at a skating ring in Paldi area where a girl died after coming in contact with an exposed live wire of a nearby electric pole.

When contacted, municipal commissioner I P Gautam ruled out any compensation saying it was a case of accidental death wherein the AMC had no role to play. "However, looking at his poor economic condition, we are trying to help out the family in some other way," he said.

Heading: Metropolitan Court admits complaint against Bukhari - Indian Express
Content:
On june 25, three-year-old Akash Salat went missing after he drowned in storm water drain near Sardar Estate crossroad on Ajwa Road. The fire brigade personnel's 30-hour search operation went in vain.

In August, two days of heavy shower came as a surprise for all. During a surveillance of the city, Mayor Balkrishna Shukla himself fell into a 10-feet ditch in Manjalpur area in an attempt to rescue a local photographer.

Come monsoon, cases of drowning in open ditches and storm water drains are inevitable, as efforts to close open drains are nowhere in sight. While a few drains have been partially barricaded, the massive storm water drains near Ajwa are still left open. Here, wooden planks have been dangerously kept on the open drain to allow people to cross over.

However, executive engineer of storm water drainage system P M Patel said: "The whole process has been completed and the stretch barricaded. Incidents of falling into drains happen when people try to become acrobatic".

Heading: GU spending crores of public money illegally, allege senate members - Indian Express
Content:
The Metropolitan Court on Wednesday admitted a complaint against Ahmed Bukhari, the Shahi Imam of Jama Masjid, Delhi, accusing him of using language hurting the religious Hindu sentiments.

He has also been accused of using provocative language that could lead to riots in connection with the Ahmedabad serial blasts.

The Court has slotted the next hearing of the case to September 30 and said that it will initiate an inquiry under section 202 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to find out whether there are sufficient grounds for proceeding in the case.

The complaint has been filed by Bachchu Randhya, a social worker and a self-confessed gau rakshak, who runs the Geeta Sena, an organisation that aims to prevent cow-slaughter.

The complaint against Bukhari is based on some statements given by him on August 21, which were printed in a vernacular daily in the city on August 22. In the newspaper, Bukhari is attributed to have said that organisations such as SIMI are not responsible for terrorist acts in the country. Rather, it was Hindu organisations such as RSS, VHP and Shiv Sena, which were responsible for the bomb blasts.

The newspaper article has been cited to show Bukhari as saying that Abdul Bashir, who has been named as the mastermind of the Ahmedabad serial blasts by the police, is innocent and should be released. He has also been quoted saying that if police do not release Bashir, then Muslims across the country will start a movement much like the one that took place in 1947.

Heading: GCA denies sacking coach Vijay Patel - Indian Express
Content:
Accusing Gujarat University (GU) administration of flouting the provisions and rules of GU Act 1989, five GU senate members submitted a request letter to Gujarat Governor and Chancellor of GU Nawal Kishore Sharma, seeking the varsity's financial and social audits for the last five years.

In their letter, the senate members have mentioned that GU authorities have been violating university rules for the last few years. Pankaj Shrimali, one of the senate members, told Newsline: "GU has not been following the provisions and rules laid down in the GU Act 1989. There has been a complete violation of the act, in letter and spirit, at each and every level. Almost all the academic, administrative, and financial decisions have been taken only by the Vice-Chancellor (V-C) and not by any statutory authority of the university."

The senate members have alleged that GU authorities have illegally spent crores of public money for their personal benefit by keeping higher authorities in the dark.

"This request is neither for our personal benefit, nor are we against any particular person. We just want GU to function in a proper and legal manner. We also want the current V-C to start concentrating on the development of GU," Shrimali said.

Digvijaysinh Gohil, another senate member, said: "We need to launch a probe into the contracts given out by GU, including building constructions, renovations, security contracts, printing, canteen etc."

Pradeep Prajapati, Dean, Faculty of Arts, GU, said: "More than 250 regular and permanent appointments are made in GU. All of these appointments are illegal and according to media reports, political. The names of such appointees and their political relations have appeared in the media. Despite this, university authorities have not taken any action."

When contacted, GU V-C Parimal Trivedi said that he is not aware of the request letter submitted by the five senate members.

Heading: GSRDC plans three new road corridors for state - Indian Express
Content:
The Gujarat Cricket Association (GCA) has stated that it has not sacked Vijay Patel. On the contrary, the coach himself refused to render his services to the association, it said. "Not just Vijay, we had asked other coaches also to tell us whether they were willing to provide their services, but they did not turn up. So we assumed that they were unwilling," said Hitesh Patel, GCA joint secretary.

He added that Vijay Patel even went to the NCA in Bangalore on behalf of the GCA at the Association's expense for his refreshment course.

When asked whether the GCA had asked the NCA to take Vijay Patel's name off the NCA register, Hitesh said: "We told them that the following people are not with us anymore. As far as the Vadodara assignment is concerned, we will obviously try to stop anyone who looks to bypass authority and directly interacts with the higher-ups."

Hitesh further said that Vijay and the others had turned rebels due to their proximity with the rival group.

"I see Vijay's pictures in the newspapers and also on television where he is in close contact with the rival faction. So you can draw your own conclusion. But at the end of the day, all this is only harming cricket," Hitesh added.

Heading: Rains throw rail route out of gear - Indian Express
Content:
The Gujarat State Road Development Corporation (GSRDC) signed a concession agreement with M/s Larsen and Toubro (L&T) on Wednesday for construction of three 'road corridors' in the state. The total length of the road corridors will be 485 km and the project cost will come to around Rs 4,308 crore. The agreement was signed in the presence of state Roads and Building Minister Anandiben Patel.

The three corridors will be developed into four-lane roads on build, operate and transfer (BOT) basis under the Viability Gap Funding (VGF) of Public Private Partnership (PPP) model of the Government of India.

According to an official statement, the three corridors to be developed on the BOT basis are the: Rs 1,669 crore, 188 km long Ahmedabad-Viramgam-Maliya Road (SH-7 and SH-17); Rs 1,217 crore, 131.65 km long Rajkot-Jamnagar-Vadinar Road (SH-25) and Rs 1,422 crore, 173.06 km long Halol-Godhra-Shamlaji Road (SH-5).

Officials said that the concessionaire will develop the four-lane roads by constructing two additional lanes and will also provide the best traffic measures, road furniture, retro-reflective sign boards, thermo plastic road markings and service roads wherever required.

The three road projects are to be completed in two-and-a-half years.

The concession period fixed for Ahmedabad-Viramgam-Maliya Road is 22 years, and 20 years for the other two road corridors.

The statement said that as per the bids received, the concessionaire M/s L&T will give a premium of about Rs 6,000 crore over a period of 22 years to the state government.

All pre-construction activities like land acquisition, forest clearance and electrical poll shifting have been completed, it added.
